## Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:EditsOneRowPerRecordAndRereads

Fixture: one record per signature. SNDR records 0x800 and 0x808 and TRNS records 0x809 and 0x80A are the link targets. Each item edits one scalar row, one MODL string and one link row. The SNDR links (ACTI, CONT, DOOR, MSTT, TACT) retarget from 0x800 to 0x808; the FURN and TERM PreviewTransform (PTRN) links retarget from 0x809 to 0x80A. After re-read the test checks the stored bytes directly: scalar bytes against `encode_scalar`, the string against zstr, and the link subrecord data against the raw u32 of the target (`u32_bytes(raw_id(...))`). It does not go through `collect_form_links`. The TACT fixture lists PNAM (4 zero bytes) before SNAM and FNAM (2 zero bytes) after it; the FURN and TERM fixtures put PTRN directly after OBND. `FixtureLinksStartOnTheirFirstTarget` checks the starting bytes first.

## Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records_real.cpp:RowsDecodeAndAuthoringLimitsHold

Over the seven official masters (`FO4_DATA_DIR`): every scalar row's payload size and decode, every FormLink row's payload size, every authoring minimum and maximum, and the authoring order rule (a listed subrecord's authoring index never goes down within a record). The order check looks only at listed rules; unlisted subrecords are skipped. The test checks each record inside the `visit_records` callback, on the record it is given, so it makes no (plugin, key) lookups and needs no sampling. A post-fix re-run of the order check over CONT (635), FURN (783), TERM (1074) and TACT (74) found no violations.

## Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupDescriptor

A repeating subrecord group. The leader is the first member that is not `leading`, which must be required and non-repeatable and starts each run; `leading` members come first in `members`, are optional and non-repeatable, and belong to the run of the leader that follows them; the other members may be required, optional or repeatable. `count_subrecord` names the whole-payload u32 row that stores the run count, and codegen requires it. `successors` lists the subrecords that follow the group in the record, from `build/xedit/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` @01a11729 (for CONT, the successor list in `fields.json`). `SubrecordGroupMemberDescriptor` carries the signature, `required`, `repeatable`, `payload_size` and the `default_payload` that insert writes. The only source of these descriptors is the generated `k_subrecord_groups` table. `schema_codegen.py` enforces the rules; `field_writer.cpp` relies on them and also checks each record it touches.

Not supported yet:

- Insert creates only the required members. It never creates an optional member such as COED, so a run keeps COED only when it already had one.
- Insert creates the count subrecord only for a record with no count and no runs. A record with runs but no count returns `subrecord_missing`.
- Only `existing_only` insertion is accepted. Runs cannot be reordered, and a repeatable leader is rejected.
- Only CONT is generated. The LVLI leveled-list entries use the same COED shape in vanilla (see `generated_scalar_fields.inc:k_subrecord_groups`) and are not wired.
- This change adds no C API or editor entry point for groups; insert and remove exist only as C++ functions in `mutation.hpp`.
- The group check covers only the `field_writer.cpp` entry points, scalar and FormLink writes through the `scalar_slots` and `formlink_slots` helpers, and the `field_writer_containers.cpp` entry points insert, remove and `subrecord_group_spans`. `formlink_list_read.cpp`, `src/schema/formlink_slots.cpp` and `preflight` do not run it yet.

## Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:subrecord_group_for_member

Returns the first group in the generated table, within the record's own groups, whose members name the subrecord. The codegen rejects a member declared by two groups in one record, so the first match is the only match. `is_subrecord_group_count_subrecord` answers whether a subrecord is a group count in its record, and `write_scalar` consults it to refuse plain writes.

## Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans

Splits a record's subrecords into runs. A run starts at a leader and continues while subrecords are members of the group, stopping at the next leader or the first non-member. It throws `SubrecordGroupError` for a member outside a run (an orphan), a member out of order or repeated when its descriptor is not repeatable, a run missing a required member, and a member whose payload size differs from its descriptor. A run member met where the outer scan expects a group member throws `count does not match its nested runs`, so a nested run that states too low a count fails closed instead of leaving orphan tuples for insert or remove. The outer `count_subrecord` itself is not checked. Scalar and formlink reads and writes reach it through `scalar_slots` and `formlink_slots` and convert the error to `ScalarError` or `FormLinkFieldError`, so a broken run fails closed for member access. A count that disagrees with the run count can still be read and written at member level, as counted arrays allow; insert and remove refuse it through `group_counter`.

## Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_counter

Finds the one `count_subrecord` in the record, requires four bytes, and requires its value to equal the number of runs. A duplicate, a wrong size or a mismatch throws `SubrecordGroupError`. Codegen makes the count mandatory, so there is no count-less path. A missing count subrecord returns nullopt. Insert then creates it only when the group has no runs; otherwise insert and remove report `subrecord_missing` without changing the plugin.

## Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:subrecord_group_spans

Enumerates the runs as `SubrecordGroupSpan{first, end, runs}`, half-open indexes into `Record::subrecords`, where `runs` holds the nested tuple spans inside each outer run. It reports structure only. The outer `count_subrecord` is not compared, so a record whose outer count disagrees still enumerates; insert and remove are the calls that refuse it through `group_counter`. A nested count is compared here: too few tuples, a tuple without its leader, or a run member past the stated count throws `SubrecordGroupError`.

## Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_subrecord_group

Inserts run `index`. The new run goes before run `index`, or after the last run's end when `index` equals the run count. An empty group whose count is present takes the run straight after the count. When the count is missing and there are no runs, insert creates a count subrecord of 1 followed by the new run, placed before the first present successor (`first_successor_index`), or at the end when none is present. Each required member is created with zero bytes and then its default bytes are copied in. Optional members are never created. All checks run before the subrecords change. The count is written after the insert, at its index shifted past the new subrecords, so a throw leaves the plugin untouched. An `index` above the run count returns `index_out_of_range`. For CONT, the CNTO default `00000000 01000000` is item 0 with count 1, from xEdit's `wbCNTO` (`build/xedit/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` @01a11729, lines 3300-3313): the item form ID at offset 0 and `wbInteger('Count', itS32).SetDefaultNativeValue(1)` at offset 4. xEdit creates the count when items go above zero (`build/xedit/wbImplementation.pas` @01a11729, lines 21144-21172), which is why an item-less CONT gets COCT=1 here.

## Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:remove_record_subrecord_group

Erases the run's subrecords, its optional and repeated members included, and writes count-1. Removing the last run keeps the count subrecord at zero rather than deleting it, so a later insert does not have to create it.

## Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group

Validates one `subrecord_group` row and returns `(group, rows, links)`. Member scalar rows become scalar rows with `repeated: true` on their member subrecord, so they pass through the existing scalar loop and get its alignment, payload and overlap checks. Member FormLink rows come back as links, and `formlink_schema_codegen.load_lists` appends them to the record's FormLink rows. `count_subrecord` is required and must be four printable ASCII characters. `successors` is an optional list of distinct four-character signatures that may not name a member or the count. Rejected: a leader that is optional or repeatable; a member signature repeated or equal to the count subrecord; member keys outside `GROUP_MEMBER_KEYS`; link keys outside `GROUP_LINK_KEYS`, which refuses `payload_sizes` on a link; rows on an optional or repeatable member; a row that does not fit its member, where a whole-payload row must match the member size; a default whose length differs from the payload size; unknown group keys; a path not qualified by the record; an insertion policy other than `existing_only`; and any `leading` run member. Run members cannot be leading because `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` treats `run.members[0]` as the nested leader and breaks a nested run on `*inner == 0`, so a leading run member would be mis-parsed at runtime. The rule that `run.members[0]` is required and non-repeatable is checked here as well. Test: `Radicle/tools/test_subrecord_group_codegen.py:LeadingGroupMemberTests.test_subrecord_group_run_members_cannot_be_leading` fails if codegen again accepts a leading run member, which the old first-non-leading leader pick allowed.

## Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:load_lists

Appends each group member link to the record's FormLink rows before the usual checks, so a group link gets the same path, offset, target and overlap rules as an ordinary FormLink field. The FormLink/scalar overlap check runs over the expanded group scalars too, so a link and a member scalar in one CNTO payload are checked together.

## Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:render

The two tables that grow with the schema outgrew one header. `k_generated_formlink_field_targets`, `k_generated_formlink_list_anchors` and `k_generated_formlink_fields` now emit their rows into shard files, `render_shard` names each one `generated_formlink_lists_<table>_shard<NN>.inc` and declares the header of its own record span on line three. `chunk_entries` groups rows by record and packs whole records until `SHARD_ENTRY_LIMIT` (600) rows would be exceeded, so a shard never splits one record's rows and no generated file reaches the 750-line source limit; `render_shard` raises if a shard still would. The parent keeps a single array per table and pulls the shards in with `#include "<shard>"` inside the braces, in order, so `first_target`, `first_anchor` and `first_segment` stay plain offsets into one array and no descriptor changed. The include names are bare file names, which resolve against the including file's own directory, so the parent cannot be relocated in the tree without regenerating. Shards are written next to `--output`, `main` drops a shard left over from a larger schema, and `--check` reports a stale or orphan shard as well as a stale parent. Read with the shards expanded, the output is identical to the single-file version apart from these header comments. `render` returns the parent text and the shard texts, and its shard-name stem defaults to `generated_formlink_lists` (`formlink_schema_codegen.py:render`), so the codegen tests still call it with four arguments and assert that a small schema shards nothing. Test: `Radicle/tools/test_formlink_list_storage.py:FormLinkListStorageTests.test_render_shards_whole_records_below_the_line_limit` renders two records of 400 targets, checks the two shard names and their order in the parent, checks each shard header names one record and holds all 400 of its rows, and checks `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:render_shard` accepts 750 lines and raises past that; a chunker that splits a record across shards, renames a shard out of include order, or loses the line cap fails here. `Radicle/tools/test_formlink_list_storage.py:FormLinkShardCheckTests` covers the same check against the written files: a drifted shard reports its own path and exits 1, an orphan `generated_formlink_lists_formlink_list_targets_shard02.inc` reports as an orphan, and the writer repairs the drift and deletes the orphan so the next `--check` is clean.

## Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py:formlink_rows

Expands group links through `parse_subrecord_group` as `load_lists` does, so the FO4_PARITY FormLink counts and kind table include group links.

## Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc:k_subrecord_groups

The CONT `CONT\Items` group. Leader `CNTO` is required, 8 bytes, with default `0000000001000000`. Optional `COED` is 12 bytes with no rows. Count `COCT` is the whole-payload u32 row `CONT\ItemTotal`. Member scalar row: `CONT\ItemCount`, CNTO offset 4, i32, repeated. Member link: `CONT\ItemObject` in `generated_formlink_lists.inc`, CNTO offset 0, targets `sigBaseObjects`, nullable. NULL is item 0, which insert writes, and xEdit's `sigBaseObjects` includes NULL (`build/xedit/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` @01a11729, line 75) and CNTO uses it (line 3303). `successors` is DEST, DAMC, DSTD, DSTA, DMDL, DMDC, DMDT, DMDS, DSTF, DATA, KSIZ, KWDA, FTYP, NTRM, PRPS, SNAM, QNAM, TNAM, ONAM.

xEdit citations are to `build/xedit/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` @01a11729. `wbCOED` is at 3290 with the owner form ID at offset 0, a global-or-rank union at 4 and a float at 8, so 12 bytes. `wbCNTO` is at 3300-3313, `wbCOCT` at 3315 and `wbCNTOs` at 3316, which sets `SetCountPath(COCT)`. The CONT record at 6176 lists `wbCOCT` before `wbCNTOs`, then `wbDEST` and `DATA`. COED sits in the same repeated struct as CNTO, so a run is CNTO plus its optional COED.

Vanilla survey, read-only over the seven local masters under `D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Fallout 4/Data`: 635 CONT records, 476 with items. In those 476, COCT is the subrecord directly before the first CNTO, is four bytes, and equals the CNTO count in every record (476 of 476). The other 159 have no COCT and no items, so insert gives them COCT=1 with the new run before the first successor. All 4579 CNTO subrecords are 8 bytes. No CONT record has a COED (0 of 4579 items), no record has more than one COCT, and no non-member subrecord sits inside an item run. Item targets resolve to ALCH 322, LVLI 1558, MISC 1521, ARMO 501, KEYM 31, BOOK 314, WEAP 151, NOTE 168 and AMMO 13, all in `sigBaseObjects` (4579 of 4579). COED has no CONT sample. The only vanilla COED is in LVLI leveled-list entries: 66 subrecords, all 12 bytes, where xEdit's LVLI array is at `build/xedit/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 10021-10027 with `wbCOED` at line 10024. The CONT COED member therefore rests on the xEdit layout and the LVLI samples, not on CONT data.

The `NPC_\Spells` group is the same shape over the actor-effect list, and it is a row conversion: `NPC_\Spell` left `formlink_fields` and became the one member link of a new group, and the `SPCT` count gained the whole-payload u32 row `NPC_\SpellCount` that `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:load_schema` requires for a `count_subrecord`. Member `SPLO` is required, non-repeatable and 4 bytes with no default, so an inserted run starts as a null form ID that `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field` then points at a `SPEL` or `LVSP`; the member stays non-nullable, as the row was. The link keeps its path, subrecord, offset, target list, nullability and `repeated` flag, but it no longer carries `payload_sizes`: `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` refuses that key on a group link (`GROUP_LINK_KEYS`) and the 4-byte rule moves to the member descriptor, which `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` enforces inside `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots` and `scalar_slots`, so a read or a write on a wrong-sized `SPLO` still fails closed. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:is_subrecord_group_count_subrecord` now reports `SPCT` as a group count, so `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` refuses a plain write to `NPC_\SpellCount` and insert and remove stay the only count writers. `successors` is the NPC_ tail after `SPLO`, in the order of the `authoring.subrecords` list in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` and of `Radicle/src/forms/npc.cpp:k_order`: DEST, DAMC, DSTD, DSTA, DMDL, DMDT, DMDC, DMDS, DSTF, WNAM, ANAM, ATKR, ATKD, SPOR, OCOR, GWOR, ECOR, FCPL, RCLR, PRKZ, PRKR, PRPS, FTYP, NTRM, COCT, CNTO, COED, AIDT, PKID, KSIZ, KWDA, APPR, OBTE, OBTF, OBTS, STOP, CNAM, FULL, SHRT, DATA, DNAM, PNAM, HCLF, BCLF, ZNAM, GNAM, NAM5, NAM6, NAM7, NAM4, MWGT, NAM8, CS2H, CS2K, CS2D, CS2E, CS2F, CSCR, PFRN, DOFT, SOFT, DPLT, CRIF, FTST, QNAM, MSDK, MSDV, TETI, TEND, MRSV, FMRI, FMRS, FMIN, ATTX. ATKE, ATKW, ATKS and ATKT are left out because they are `wbAttackData` members that always follow ATKD, which is listed. xEdit declares the list at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3283-3285` (`wbSPCT := wbInteger(SPCT, 'Count', itU32, nil, cpBenign)`, `wbSPLO := wbFormIDCk(SPLO, 'Actor Effect', [SPEL, LVSP])`, `wbSPLOs := wbRArrayS('Actor Effects', wbSPLO).SetCountPath(SPCT)`) and places `wbSPCT` directly before `wbSPLOs` in NPC_ at `:10371-10372`, which is why `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` starts scanning a counted group after its count subrecord. `RACE` uses the same xEdit shape at `:11062-11063` and is unchanged: it keeps its `RACE\ActorEffects` `formlink_fields` row with no count. The `NPC_\Spells` row therefore adds no schema kind, no generator branch and no runtime path.

Vanilla survey of the `NPC_` actor-effect list, read-only over the same seven masters on 2026-10-19: 4369 NPC_ records, 476 with an `SPCT`. All 476 have `SPLO` too, `SPCT` is 4 bytes, and it sits directly before the first `SPLO` in every one (476 of 476), so `group_spans`' "a counted group's runs follow its count subrecord" start is the vanilla layout and not an assumption. `SPCT` equals the `SPLO` count in all 476, no record carries two `SPCT`, no record has an `SPLO` without an `SPCT`, and no non-member subrecord sits between the first and last `SPLO` of a record, so the run is contiguous in every case. All 630 `SPLO` subrecords are 4 bytes, and the largest list holds 3. `Radicle/tests/test_npc_real.cpp:NpcReal` decodes the new `NPC_\SpellCount` row on the same masters.

## Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_formlink_lists.inc:k_generated_sig_base_objects

The 44 signatures of xEdit's `sigBaseObjects` union (`build/xedit/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` @01a11729, lines 75-82). ENCH was added last, at line 82, so `is_sig_base_object(ENCH)` is true, as `tests/test_kwda_formlink_lists.cpp` expects. Leveled-list entries do not read this table: `src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:k_lvli_targets` keeps its own list, which already had ENCH.

## Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_group.cpp:SubrecordGroup

The fixtures build a CONT record and use the generated group, so the vanilla shape is tested directly. A hand-built descriptor (`custom_group`) covers the leader, required, repeatable, order and payload rules, which the generated table does not express. The remap test uses the same three-master header as `FormLink.CntoRemapsItemLeavesCount` in `test_formlinks.cpp` and leaves COED out, so it checks only the two CNTO item IDs; each one must move to master index 1 exactly once.

## Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:SubrecordGroupSpan

`SubrecordGroupSpan{first, end}` is the half-open range of one run in `Record::subrecords`. `SubrecordGroupMutationStatus` mirrors `CountedArrayMutationStatus` with `updated`, `record_missing`, `index_out_of_range` and `subrecord_missing`. Structural failures are `SubrecordGroupError` throws instead of statuses.

## Radicle/src/schema/form_link_schema.cpp:schema_formlink_offsets

Schema FormLink rows (`k_generated_formlink_fields`) that the global table cannot reach, such as WEAP DNAM with 132-byte payloads, are resolved here with `resolve_field_slots` and returned as byte offsets per subrecord. The global table applies only to 4-byte payloads (see the `is_listed_formid_signature` checks in `src/schema/form_links.cpp`). A slot is kept only when it is valid, its payload size matches the row's `payload_sizes` (any size when `payload_sizes[0]` is zero), and the subrecord is not deliberately non-form ID. Slots on subrecords that `struct_payload_formid_offsets` or `mixed_formid_offsets` own (EXPL DATA, PROJ DNAM and HAZD DNAM among them) are dropped, so those handlers keep their malformed-size rejection. INFO returns nothing because `visit_info_link_offsets` in `src/schema/form_links.cpp` owns that record. NAVI NVMI slots are valid only when the navmesh mixed-offset parse succeeds and NVER is 4 bytes. PACK and IDLE rows also pass the behavior payload rules inside `resolve_field_slots` in `src/schema/field_address.cpp`. Callers compute this once per record, so the row scan is not repeated for each subrecord.

## Radicle/src/schema/form_link_schema.cpp:deliberate_non_formid_subrecord

Excludes subrecords that are deliberately not form IDs from the schema path: any `XXXX` subrecord, RACE `SRAF`, the QUST signatures in `qust_non_formid_signature`, and the corpus rules in `corpus_non_formid_slot` (PACK `CNAM` after `ANAM`, SCEN action scalars, and the static pair list). Without this predicate the schema path would revive links that the existing visitors reject on purpose.

## Radicle/src/schema/form_link_schema.cpp:qust_non_formid_signature

Signatures that QUST reuses for scalar or string data although they are form ID signatures in other record types: DNAM (General quest data), NAM2 (stage note), CNAM (stage log-entry text), FNAM (objective/alias flags), ANAM (next alias ID), NNAM (objective text or quest description), and SNAM (SWF filename). They must never reach the global signature-only form ID table. The list is unchanged from the former `qust_non_formid_signature` in `src/schema/form_links.cpp`.

## Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:visit_formlink_offsets

Wraps `visit_link_offsets` and merges in the schema offsets for the same subrecord. Subrecords with no schema offsets skip the buffer and go straight to `visit_link_offsets`. Otherwise the union is sorted and deduplicated before the callback runs, so a link that both the global table and a schema row list, such as FACT VEND with a 4-byte payload, is visited once (`tests/test_form_link_schema_remap.cpp:LinkAlsoListedByGlobalTableIsVisitedOnce`). Strict mode passes through unchanged. Sorting can reorder output from a handler that did not emit ascending offsets; the remap and rekey callbacks do not depend on order.

## Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:editable — coupled count subrecords

Count subrecords are marked `coupled` in `schema/fallout4/fields.json` (NPC_ SPCT, DEST, PRKZ, COCT, KSIZ, KWDA, OBTE, CS2H; LVLI and LVLN LLCT; FACT CITC; LIGH KSIZ and KWDA). Older records mark KSIZ and KWDA together and DEST alone, and `editable` reads the flag, so an unmarked count with minimum 0 could be removed while its entries stay. The entries the counts describe (PRKR, CNTO, LVLO, CTDA, SPLO, OBTF, OBTS, CS2K) are repeated without `uncounted`, so `editable` already refuses them.

LVSP LLCT (minimum 1) and SMBN, SMEN and SMQN CITC (minimum 1) are not coupled. Removal already stops at the minimum and add stops at the maximum. Coupling them would make `create_with_rules` refuse those records, because it requires every minimum-1 rule to be editable, and `tests/test_c_api_authoring.cpp` creates an LVSP through that path.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_ — NAM7 minimum 0

NPC_ NAM7 has minimum 0 (it was 1). xEdit marks it required (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10424`, `wbFloat(NAM7, 'Unused', cpNormal, True)`), but the audit count found it on none of the 3015 vanilla NPC_ records, so the minimum follows the corpus. This is a deliberate deviation from the xEdit flag.

## Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:check_links — DLBR SNAM with a missing target

`check_links` skips a DLBR `SNAM` whose target is in no loaded plugin. Before this, that link also got an `unresolved_link` finding, a warning because the DLBR `SNAM` slot has no schema proof, next to the `branch_starting_topic_not_dial` error from `check_dialogue_links`. The dialogue rule is kept because it names the requirement (a loaded DIAL). Deleted targets still come from `check_links`. Test: `tests/test_check_errors.cpp:MissingBranchStartingTopicIsReportedOnce`.

## Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:check_links — RFGP RNAM with a missing Fallout4.esm target

`check_links` skips an RFGP `RNAM` (Reference, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12585`) whose target is a Fallout4.esm form found in no loaded plugin. #594 made the slot proven (`generated_formlink_lists.inc` `RFGP\Reference`), so these links became `unresolved_link` errors, and vanilla Fallout4.esm ships 19 of them (for example 23AF81, 2079CE, 04ED0B), which failed `VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings` on c1a305ba4. The bytes are vanilla data, not a decode fault. A missing target owned by any other plugin is still an error, and a loaded target of the wrong type is still `wrong_target_type`. Tests: `tests/test_check_errors.cpp:MissingGameMasterReferenceGroupTargetIsNotAnError`, `MissingModReferenceGroupTargetIsStillUnresolved`, `VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings`.

## Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:check_links — REGN WNAM with a missing Fallout4.esm target

`check_links` skips a REGN `WNAM` (Worldspace, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11876`, `wbFormIDCkNoReach`) whose target is a Fallout4.esm form found in no loaded plugin. The REGN authoring entry (#602 C-33, `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` `REGN\Worldspace`) made the slot proven, so these links became `unresolved_link` errors and `VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings` failed on bf7e2e66. Fallout4.esm has 106 REGN records, 68 of them carry a WNAM; 5 of those (00200046, 001D1CED, 0017162A, 001A65EF, 00001171) name worldspace 01D1D0, which no master defines (checked against Fallout4.esm and the six DLC masters), while the other 63 resolve. xEdit does not reach into this link, the same fact `src/graph/reachability.cpp:no_reach` already encodes for `{REGN, WNAM}`. A missing target owned by any other plugin is still an error, and a loaded target of the wrong type is still `wrong_target_type`. Tests: `tests/test_check_errors.cpp:MissingGameMasterRegionWorldspaceIsNotAnError`, `MissingModRegionWorldspaceIsStillUnresolved`, `VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings`.

## Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:npc_formid_offsets — NPC_ SNAM and PRKR

NPC_ `SNAM` (faction) is 5 bytes: form ID u32 at 0, rank s8 at 4. NPC_ `PRKR` (perk) is also 5 bytes: form ID u32 at 0, rank u8 at 4. Both layouts are exact, so any other size throws under strict remap and is skipped otherwise. The sizes match `encode_factions` and `encode_perks` in `src/forms/npc.cpp`, which write 5 bytes, and `decode_npc_factions` and `decode_npc_perks`, which require 5. xEdit defines the perk struct at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10386-10388`. Before this layout, the generic `SNAM` entry in `formid_subrecords.inc` remapped only 4-byte payloads, and `PRKR` was in no remap table, so the perk form ID was never remapped. Tests: `tests/test_packed_formlink_arrays.cpp:NpcFactionSnamRemapsFormIdAndKeepsRank` and `NpcPerkPrkrRemapsFormIdAndKeepsRank`.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:PRPS rows (#602 WP-9)

- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACTI, CLAS, CONT, FLOR, FURN, LIGH, MSTT, NPC_, RACE, STAT and TERM `PropertyActorValue` and `PropertyValue` rows (#602 WP-9 PRPS). xEdit `wbObjectProperty` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5266-5270) is `wbStructSK([0], 'Property', [wbActorValue, wbFloat('Value')])`, so each PRPS element is 8 bytes: Actor Value form ID at offset 0 and f32 Value at offset 4. `wbActorValue` is `wbFormIDCkNoReach('Actor Value', [AVIF, NULL])` (:3288), so `<SIG>\PropertyActorValue` is a formlink to AVIF, nullable true, offset 0, stride 8, existing_only, and `<SIG>\PropertyValue` is an f32 scalar at offset 4, stride 8, existing_only. Precedent: LVLI/LVLN `LLKC` rows (`LVLI\FilterKeyword`, `LVLI\FilterChance`). The eleven records are the xEdit PRPS users (`wbPRPS` uses at ACTI 5644, CLAS 6107, CONT 6207, FURN 6869, MSTT 7091, LIGH 9885, NPC_ 10394, RACE 11067, STAT 12073, FLOR 12176, TERM 12687), and each already had a record entry. ACTI, CONT, FURN, MSTT, RACE and TERM authoring lists omit PRPS, so generic add does not create it. Corpus (seven masters, read-only scan, 2026-10-15): 6651 PRPS subrecords (NPC_ 4369 of 4369 records, STAT 1407 of 23579, ACTI 463 of 2196, FURN 144 of 783, RACE 110 of 110, CONT 52 of 635, FLOR 45 of 64, CLAS 32 of 32, LIGH 18 of 1065, TERM 9 of 1074, MSTT 2 of 1106); every payload is a multiple of 8, 51629 entries in all; no zero links; 49100 links resolve to AVIF; 2529 point at Fallout4.esm local IDs below 0x800 that no master defines (engine-hardcoded actor values), which `Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:check_links` skips through `k_first_non_hardcoded_id`; no wrong-type target; values -240 to 111100, all finite. 2013 subrecords are sorted by actor value and 4638 are not, so the xEdit sort key is not a file invariant and insertion stays existing_only. Double count: every PRPS is owned by `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_repeated_struct_layouts`, so `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_schema.cpp:schema_formlink_offsets` skips it (`struct_or_mixed_handler_owns`) and remap and `collect_form_links` still see each link once. The new rows add only the `check_errors.cpp:slot_targets` AVIF check, which had no PRPS target before. Open: the 2529 hardcoded references have no AVIF record to check against, and six records lack PRPS in authoring. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_prps_rows.cpp:WP9PrpsRows`.

## Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:leveled_list_formid_offsets — LVLI and LVLN LLKC

LLKC is an uncounted array of 8-byte structs: keyword form ID u32 at 0 and a u32 chance at 4 (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9979-9984`, `wbArrayS` with `wbStructSK([0], ...)`). The layout is non-exact, `size % 8 == 0`, like `XPOD` in `k_placed_reference_layouts`. Reason: the shipped byte check found 8, 16 and 24 byte payloads, and xEdit accepts any element count. The chance is not remapped. Tests: `tests/test_packed_formlink_arrays.cpp:LeveledListLlkcKeywordsRemapAndKeepChances` and `WrongSizedFixedLayoutPayloadsFailClosedUnderStrictRemap`.

## Radicle/src/forms/npc.cpp:require_local_target — typed NPC_ targets

`add_npc_faction` and `set_npc_faction` require a local SNAM target to be FACT. `add_npc_perk` and `set_npc_perk` require a local PRKR target to be PERK. A local key that does not resolve throws `NpcError`. Foreign keys are not resolved here and are not checked, the same rule as `validate_local_entry_targets` in `src/forms/leveled_spell_creation.cpp` and `validate_entry_target` in `src/forms/leveled_list.cpp`. xEdit uses `wbFormIDCk('Faction', [FACT])` for SNAM and `wbFormIDCk('Perk', [PERK])` for PRKR (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10387`). Test: `tests/test_npc_lists.cpp:LocalFactionAndPerkTargetsMustHaveTheirSignature`.

## Radicle/src/forms/faction.cpp:require_relation_target — FACT XNAM targets

`add_faction_relation` and `set_faction_relation` require a local XNAM faction to be FACT or RACE, before the plugin is copied. A local key that does not resolve throws `FactionError`. Foreign keys are not checked, as in `require_local_target` (`src/forms/npc.cpp`). xEdit defines the relation struct with `wbFormIDCkNoReach('Faction', [FACT, RACE])` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8818-8819`). Test: `tests/test_faction.cpp:RelationTargetOfThisPluginMustBeFactOrRace`.

## Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:set_leveled_list_settings — LVLF bits

LVLF flags may use only bits 0x01, 0x02 and 0x04 (mask 0x07). `set_leveled_list_settings` applies the same check as `create_leveled_list`, before any read or write, so a rejected call leaves the plugin unchanged. Test: `tests/test_leveled_list.cpp:SettingsRejectFlagBitsOutsideTheDefinedMask`.

## Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_weapon_layouts — WEAP embedded form ID slots

WEAP DNAM (132 bytes), FNAM (41) and CRDT (12) are fixed-size structs with no version condition in xEdit (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` WEAP record, lines 12877-13032; the DNAM struct is at 12911). Slots: DNAM Ammo @0, Skill @40, Resist @44, eight Sound slots @73 to @101 (lines 12912, 12922, 12923, 12978-12985); FNAM Override Projectile @29 (line 13004); CRDT Crit Effect @8 (line 13016). Sizes are exact, so a payload of another size fails closed under strict remap. The layouts are interpreted by `fixed_stride_formid_offsets`, like the FACT XNAM and NPC_ SNAM layouts.

## Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:faction_plvd_formid_offsets — FACT PLVD location slot

xEdit `wbPLVD` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 4200-4221) is a struct whose first field is a s32 Type that selects the union member at @4. Types 0 (Reference), 1 (Cell), 4 (Object ID) and 6 (Keyword) hold a form ID; the others (2 and 3 byte arrays, 5 Object Type, 7 unused, 8 to 14 aliases and targets) do not. Collection Index is optional from member 3 (`SetOptionalFrom(3)`), so the payload is 12 or 16 bytes. `Radicle/src/graph/reachability.cpp` checks PLVD types 0, 1 and 4 only; this remap includes type 6 as xEdit lists it. The PACK PLDT decider in `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp` uses the same four types as this function.

## Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:zeroes_chance_none — LVLO chance on form versions below 69

`decode_leveled_list` reports entry chance none as 0 and `replace_leveled_list_entries` writes 0 for LVLI and LVLN records whose `header.form_version` is below 69. xEdit's `wbLLEAfterLoad` zeroes the entries' Chance None under the same condition (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:2215-2250`), attached to LVLN (10007) and LVLI (10031) only. LVSP has no after-load (10044-10049), so LVSP chance is decoded as stored. Unedited records are not rewritten. Tests: `tests/test_leveled_list.cpp:LegacyFormVersionReportsZeroChanceNoneForLvliAndLvln`, `LegacyFormVersionEditsWriteZeroChanceNoneAndNoOpStaysIdentical`.

## Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:sorted_entries — LVLO order for typed writes

Typed writes store LVLO entries in xEdit's order. The entry struct's sort key is Level, then the reference, then Count (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8788-8802`, the extended key from `wbStructExSK([0, 2], [3])`). The reference is compared as the raw form ID in this plugin's context, which matches load order for the plugin's masters. Keys are compared as fixed-width hex strings, so the order is numeric. `Core/wbImplementation.pas:2151-2175` (`CompareSortKeys`) and `:20916` (`TwbSubRecordArray.DoInit`) sort the array. `std::stable_sort` keeps the caller's order for equal keys. The sort runs in `replace_leveled_list_entries`, so insert, set and remove all write sorted lists. A list that is already sorted is still a no-op when the caller's entries equal the decoded entries.

Index meaning: `insert_leveled_list_entry` and `set_leveled_list_entry` take an index into the list as decoded before the call. The new entry lands at that index first, and then the list is sorted, so its final index is set by its key. Among equal keys, the index decides the order. Tests: `tests/test_leveled_list.cpp:EntriesSortByLevelThenReferenceAfterTypedEdits`, `EqualSortKeysKeepTheirOrderAndSetResortsTheEdit`.

## Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:replace_leveled_list_entries — LVSP COED refusal

An LVSP entry with `extra` is refused before any write. xEdit's LVSP entry is LVLO only (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10044-10049`). A COED-carrying LVSP entry from a file is still decoded, and any write that carries it is refused. Test: `tests/test_leveled_list.cpp:SpellListEntriesRefuseExtraData`.

## Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:zstring — editor ID NUL

`create_leveled_list` refuses an editor ID with an embedded NUL before the plugin is copied. A NUL would write an early terminator into the zstring. The same local check is in `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:zstring`. The LVSP creator takes no editor ID, so it has no check to match. Test: `tests/test_leveled_list_creation.cpp:RefusesEmbeddedNulInEditorId`.

## Radicle/src/forms/faction.cpp:zstring — FACT editor ID and full name NUL

`create_faction` refuses an editor ID or full name with an embedded NUL. The local check matches the one in `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:zstring`. Test: `tests/test_faction.cpp:RefusesEmbeddedNulInEditorIdOrFullName`.

## Radicle/src/forms/npc.cpp:k_order — NPC_ run boundaries

`insertion_index` places a missing run after the last known subrecord that orders before the anchor. An unknown subrecord between two known ones can therefore be split off. The order table lists each group's members in xEdit's `NPC_` definition order: `wbDEST` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4275-4300`: DEST, DAMC, DSTD, DSTA, DMDL, DMDT, DMDC, DMDS, DSTF), `wbAttackData` (`:4073-4121`: ATKD, ATKE, ATKW, ATKS, ATKT), and the SPCT count before SPLO (`:3283-3285`). Without the full groups, a new PRKZ or COCT run landed between DEST and DSTD, or between ATKD and ATKE. Test: `tests/test_npc_lists.cpp:InsertedRunsStayOutsideTheDestAndAttackGroups`.

## Radicle/src/forms/npc.cpp:require_local_base_object — CNTO item targets

`add_npc_inventory_item` and `set_npc_inventory_item` require a local CNTO item to be a base object, using `schema::is_sig_base_object` (the generated xEdit `sigBaseObjects` list, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:74`). Foreign keys are not checked, as in `require_local_target`. Test: `tests/test_npc_lists.cpp:InventoryItemsMustBeBaseObjectsAndCoedOwnersNpcOrFact`.

## Radicle/src/forms/npc.cpp:require_local_coed_owner — COED owner targets

A local COED owner must be NPC_ or FACT, as xEdit's `wbCOED` owner (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3291`, `[NPC_, FACT, NULL]`). A null owner is allowed. Foreign keys are not checked. Test: `tests/test_npc_lists.cpp:InventoryItemsMustBeBaseObjectsAndCoedOwnersNpcOrFact`.

## Radicle/src/forms/npc.cpp:encode_perks — count kept at zero

`encode_perks` and `encode_inventory` always write PRKZ or COCT, including 0 when the last entry is removed. xEdit's `TwbSubRecordArray.BeforeActualRemove` sets the count element to 0 and keeps it (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:20774-20797`). Test: `tests/test_npc_lists.cpp:RemovingTheLastEntryKeepsItsCountSubrecordAtZero`.

## Radicle/src/forms/npc.cpp:replace_run — NPC_ SNAM, PRKR and CNTO keep append order

`replace_run` writes the caller's order and does not sort. This deviates from xEdit, which declares the CNTO array with `wbRArrayS` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3316`). The reason is shipped-corpus evidence: vanilla Fallout4.esm stores 1,011 SNAM, 1,468 CNTO and 127 XNAM lists unsorted, so a sorted write would reorder records that Bethesda stored in another order. LVLO is sorted (see `sorted_entries`).

## Radicle/src/forms/faction.cpp:add_faction_relation — FACT XNAM append order

`add_faction_relation` inserts after the last XNAM and does not sort. The reason is the same shipped-corpus evidence as `replace_run`: a byte scan of the shipped Fallout4.esm found 127 unsorted XNAM lists in Fallout4.esm.

## Radicle/src/forms/faction.cpp:require_editable — undecodable refusal before index checks (GT-276)

The index-based FACT, NPC_ and LVLI/LVLN edits (`set_faction_relation`, `remove_faction_rank`, `set_npc_perk`, `remove_leveled_list_entry` and the other set/remove entry points) call `require_editable` before any index check or decode. `Radicle/src/forms/faction.cpp:require_editable`, `Radicle/src/forms/npc.cpp:require_editable` and `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:require_editable` call `require_decodable` on the target record. The reason: an undecodable record has empty `subrecords`, so the decoders return empty lists and the old check reported "index is out of range" instead of the undecodable refusal.

The whole-record write points also refuse, so add, replace and settings edits do not write into an undecodable record: `Radicle/src/forms/faction.cpp:mutable_faction`, `Radicle/src/forms/npc.cpp:replace_run`, and `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:replace_leveled_list_entries`, `set_leveled_list_settings` and `reset_leveled_list`. Before this change an empty `replace_leveled_list_entries` on an undecodable LVLN returned true without touching the record, because both sides decoded to no entries. The `decode_*` readers are unchanged, so reads of an undecodable record behave as before. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_undecodable_edit.cpp:FactionIndexedEditsRefuseUndecodableRecord`, `NpcIndexedEditsRefuseUndecodableRecord`, `LeveledListIndexedEditsRefuseUndecodableRecord` and `LeveledListWholeEditsRefuseUndecodableRecord`.

## Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_edit.cpp:set_placed_reference_record_flags — Deleted bit kept

`set_placed_reference_record_flags` keeps the record's compressed, persistent and Deleted bits and takes the other bits from the caller. Deleted is never set or cleared here, because deleting needs the content stripped (xEdit `SetDeleted` in `Core/wbImplementation.pas`). Reason: #602 D-6. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_environment_ref_fields.cpp:RecordFlagsNeverToggleDeleted`.

## tools/schema_codegen.py:min_form_version (#602 WP-11)

A scalar row may carry `min_form_version`. Its gate is enforced once, in `src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots`, which every scalar reader and writer goes through: `src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots` (write, `set_record_scalar` and `record_field_count`) and `src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` (read). `scalar_field_shape` copies the value into `FieldShape::min_form_version`, and `resolve_field_slots` treats a record below it as `sized == false`, the same as a payload shorter than `minimum_payload_size`. So the row is not valid and not misfit, nothing is read, and a write returns `subrecord_missing` with the bytes unchanged. `scalar_field_bytes` and `patch_scalar_field` take only a payload, so they carry no version; no src caller uses them, only tests. Reason: xEdit `EXPL DATA` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7350`, `wbFromVersion(97, wbFloat('Inner Radius'))`) sits mid-struct, so below 97 every later member is 4 bytes earlier than the rows. The 13 rows from `EXPL\InnerRadius` (offset 32) to `EXPL\ProjectileCount` (80) carry `"min_form_version": 97` in `schema/fallout4/fields.json`. Those rows are hidden below 97 even though their bytes exist there at 4 bytes earlier; a versioned row would expose them but the brief forbids duplicate rows. The `Spawn` rows at 64-80 could use 112 to match xEdit exactly, since v97-111 has no Spawn struct; left at 97. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_scalar_embedded.cpp:InnerRadiusIsGatedByFormVersion97` (84-byte DATA at 96 and 97). Codegen test: `tools/test_field_address_codegen.py:test_min_form_version_gates_a_row_and_rejects_bad_values`.

Scan of the 24 xEdit `wbFromVersion` uses in `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` for a gated member followed by ungated members: `EXPL DATA` (fixed above) and `RACE DATA` (gated since #602 C-25, below). `RACE DATA` has two (`Male Default Weight` and `Female Default Weight` at 109, `Beard Biped Object` at 124, lines 11072-11128) with ungated members after them, and the 37 `RACE DATA` scalar rows of #602 C-25 (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\MaleHeight` through `RACE\OrientationRoll`, the two `RACE DATA` sections below) carry the gates: their offsets sum to the 200-byte form version 131 layout, so every row from `RACE\MaleWeightThin` on carries `"min_form_version": 109` and every row from `RACE\BeardBipedObject` on carries 124, which hides a member whose bytes sit 4, 24 or 28 bytes earlier on an older record instead of reading them. `RACE\MaleHeight` and `RACE\FemaleHeight` carry no gate, their offsets being version-independent. `RACE\OrientationPitch` and `RACE\OrientationRoll` also carry `minimum_payload_size` 196 and 200, so a shorter payload hides them. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_race_data_rows.cpp:RowsMatchXEditOffsetsStorageAndGates`, `Radicle/tests/test_race_data_rows.cpp:ShiftedMembersAreHiddenBelowTheirFormVersionGate` and `Radicle/tests/test_race_data_rows.cpp:OrientationRollNeedsTheFull200BytePayload`. The rest are trailing: `wbSNAMMarkerParams` (5321-5331), `wbAIDT` (6229-6230), EXPL after Inner Radius (7369-7377), IMAD (7523-7525), NAM5/NAM6 (7543-7544, separate subrecords), MATO DATA (9387-9389), QUST QSTA Keyword (10787), RACE OnCripple and its successors (11182-11192) and WTHR Wind Turbulance (13086). Trailing gated members need no gate because short payloads already hide them, except the RACE `OnCripple`, `Explodable - Subsegment Explosion` and `Orientation Limits` rows of #602 C-25, which carry `"min_form_version": 124` because their offsets are the same 131 layout and a version 96-to-123 record holds them 4 or 28 bytes earlier.
## tools/schema_codegen.py:max_form_version (#602 WP-9)

- A scalar or FormLink row may carry `max_form_version`, an exclusive upper bound: the row applies only when the record's form version is below it (0 or absent is no bound), the counterpart of `min_form_version`. `tools/schema_codegen.py` and `tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py` reject a value that is not a 16-bit positive integer, and a scalar whose value is not above its `min_form_version`. The scalar gate is `src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` through `FieldShape::max_form_version`, which `src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_shape` copies. The FormLink shape is built in `src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots`, `src/schema/formlink_slots.cpp:formlink_field_at` and `src/schema/form_link_schema.cpp:schema_formlink_offsets`. Only the WEAP DAMA rows use it, so form version 152 and up is not rowed (xEdit `wbFromVersion(152, ...)`, Common 8454-8463).

## src/schema/form_links.cpp:is_listed_formid_signature (generator gaps, #602 WP-3)

Each row below was read in xEdit at pin 93cc0bc5 (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` and `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas`) before coding, and every definition of the signature in both files was checked. Tests are in `Radicle/tests/test_generator_gap_remap.cpp` (`GeneratorGapRemap.*`). The static deny pass (`non_formid_slots.py --check-static`) reports no scalar pair for any added signature, so `XEDIT_DENIED` is unchanged.

Global signatures (`formid_subrecords.inc`, 4-byte payload, any record):
- EITM: the only definition is `wbEnchantment` (`wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8486-8489`, form ID when not TES4). Used by ARMO (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5798`), EXPL (:7339) and WEAP (:12891).
- CS2K and CS2D: NPC_ sound pairs in `wbActorSounds` (`wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8399-8405`), used at `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10434`.
- PLYR: the PLYR record's own subrecord, `wbFormID(PLYR, 'Player')` (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12131`).
- HEAD: `wbHeadPart` (`wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8583`), used only for RACE head parts (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11274` and :11292). No other record defines HEAD.
- MDOB: `wbMDOB` (`wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8877`), used only by MGEF (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10056`).

Keyword array (`is_formid_array_signature`):
- APPR: `wbArrayS(APPR, ..., wbFormIDCk('Keyword', [KYWD]))` (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5275`), used by ARMO (:5841), FURN (:6916), NPC_ (:10404), RACE (:11068) and WEAP (:12901). Every element is a keyword form ID.

Record-qualified (`packed_formid_array_offsets`, not global, because MODL and INDX are not form IDs in other records):
- ARMO MODL: the Armor Addon form ID inside the Models struct (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5823-5825`, after INDX).
- ARMA MODL: one RACE form ID per repeated subrecord (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5885`).
- MODL is a model path string through `wbGenericModel` (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:1034`). ARMO and ARMA do not use that helper: its users between lines 5786 and 5890 are none, and ANIO (:5782) and BOOK (:5897) sit outside that range.
- NPC_ TPTA: 13 form IDs, 52 bytes (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10353-10366`, entries from `wbNPCTemplateActorEntry`, `wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8274-8277`).
- OVIS INDX: `wbFormIDCk(INDX, 'Object', [STAT])` (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12550`). INDX is an integer in NOCM (:12462) and in other records.

Structured slot (`structured_formids.inc`, any record, payload at least 12 bytes):
- ATKD attack spell at offset 8: `wbAttackData` (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4073-4119`), two floats, then the Attack Spell form ID, then attack flags. The struct is 44 bytes by its member sizes. Used by NPC_ (:10377) and RACE (:11211). ATKD is defined only in `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas`.

Schema formlink rows (`schema/fallout4/fields.json`) hold none of these signatures as remap fields; they appear there only as authoring rows. `visit_formlink_offsets` also dedupes any overlap, so no offset is visited twice.

## Record flags and delete as a flag (#602 WP-12 D-6, D-28)

`set_record_flags` and `mark_override_deleted` are declared in `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/record_flags.hpp` and defined in `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp`. Both look the record up by form key across all groups, after `assign_record_form_keys`. A TES4 header key is checked against `plugin.tes4.form_key` first, which is the default key, so only an empty form key ever reports `header_record`.

- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:set_record_flags` bit rules: the master bit (bit 0) is dropped on every non-TES4 record, matching the xEdit `Record Flags` setter (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:24790-24836`, `if Flags.IsESM then ... SetESM(False)`). Compressed and partial form keep the record's current bits whatever the caller passes. The writer compresses from `Record::compressed` (`src/plugin/writer.cpp:write_record`), so the header bit and that field must agree, and a caller cannot toggle them here.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:set_record_flags` Deleted: a change to the Deleted bit returns `deleted_bit` and writes nothing. xEdit routes Deleted through its own setter (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:24790-24836`, `Flags.IsDeleted <> ... ToggleDeleted`), and a delete has to strip content, so only `mark_override_deleted` sets it. On a deleted record the persistent bit keeps its current value, because xEdit applies Persistent and VWD only when the record is not deleted (same setter).
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:set_record_flags` relocation: when the persistent bit changes on a record sitting in a bucket of type 8, 9 or 10 under a `cell_children` GRUP, the record moves to the bucket matching its new persistence. xEdit does the same in `SetIsPersistent` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14231-14243`, calls `UpdateCellChildGroup` when `CheckChildOfCell`), and `UpdateCellChildGroup` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14489+`) picks type 8 when persistent and 9 otherwise. On an interior reference, a record already in the target bucket is not moved. That matches xEdit's early exits: `Core/wbImplementation.pas:14525` for types 8 and 10 (`CorrectGroupType <> 9`), and `:14543` for any type on an interior CELL (`not IsExterior`). An exterior reference in a type 8 bucket is skipped on Set (the same `:14525` exit), but a Clear always resolves its grid CELL by position; see the exterior relocation bullet below. The new bucket comes from `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp:ensure_reference_bucket` (declared in `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy_internal.hpp`), which places it before the first later-typed group, so type 8 precedes type 9. The interior path and the exterior path share it. The old bucket is erased when it is empty.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:set_record_flags` VWD: type 10 is accepted as a source bucket but is never a target. xEdit's target is 10 only when `wbVWDInTemporary` is false (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14489+`, `CorrectGroupType`), and FO4 sets it true (`xEdit/xeInit.pas:1093-1094`). So on FO4 a visible-when-distant reference never lands in a type 10 group after a change. A visible-distant toggle never moves a reference here. xEdit's `SetIsVisibleWhenDistant` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14251-14253`) does call `UpdateCellChildGroup`, which would move a type 10 reference to type 9; Radicle leaves that alone, as the brief asks, and on FO4 no reference should be in type 10.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:set_record_flags` exterior relocation (D-28): when the persistent bit changes on a reference in a `cell_children` bucket, `relocate_reference` runs for exterior and interior references alike. It works on a copy of the plugin and assigns it back only on success, so the flag change and the move commit together and a throw leaves the plugin untouched. The owning CELL is the record before its children GRUP. The worldspace comes from `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy_internal.hpp:worldspace_record`, and the owning GRUP must be a world-children or exterior sub-block GRUP. Set: the target is the worldspace's persistent CELL (`Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:find_persistent_exterior_cell`) in its type 8 bucket. A reference already in a type 8 bucket is left in place (`:14525`), with only its flag written. xEdit: `CELL[P]` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14558`), keeping the group when the old cell is already in the world-children GRUP (`:14565`). Clear: the target is the grid CELL for the DATA position (`exterior_grid_in_range` and `grid_coordinate` from `placed_reference_copy_internal.hpp`, looked up with `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:find_exterior_cell`) in its type 9 bucket, wherever the reference sits now. xEdit: grid branch `:14570-14593`, same-grid early exit `:14576-14578` (taken only when the bucket already has type 9), and the cell is kept on a matching grid (`:14579`). A destination equal to the source CELL changes bucket in place with `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp:move_reference_to_bucket`, or only writes flags when the bucket already has the target type. The group move is `:14604-14623`. The persistent bit reaches `UpdateCellChildGroup` through `SetIsPersistent` (`:14231-14240`) from the Record Flags setter (`:24816`, `:24837-24838`).
  Deviations: (a) xEdit's `CELL[P]` and `CELL[x,y]` lookups (`:16882`, `ChildBySignature['CELL']` and `ChildByGridCell`, over `MainRecords` from `AllVisibleForFile`, so masters count) copy a match from another file as an override (`wbCopyElementToFile`, `:16891`), and create the CELL when none matches (`:14558`, `:14587`). Radicle searches only this plugin and returns `target_cell_missing` with no change, because callers create cells first (D-29). (b) A CELL whose DATA is missing or empty commits the flag only, with no move and no throw. xEdit exits there (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14533-14537`) after the flag is applied by the Record Flags setter, so nothing moves. Radicle's `relocate_reference` is the place where this is decided. (c) `find_persistent_exterior_cell` takes the first CELL directly beneath the WRLD children GRUP, as xEdit's `ChildBySignature['CELL']` does (`:16882`). Out-of-range positions return `target_cell_missing` (D-29 deviation d).
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:mark_override_deleted` xEdit parity: `TwbMainRecord.Delete` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:10321-10373`) sets Deleted, clears Compressed and, where the definition allows it, Partial Form, releases all elements, and on FO4 re-adds the base record (NAME) for placed references. It does not touch child GRUPs. Radicle keeps only the first NAME for the ten placed-reference signatures (`is_placed_reference_signature`, `src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp`) and drops every other subrecord. Partial Form is cleared only where the definition can be partial, as xEdit does (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:10341-10342`, guarded by `mrDef.CanBePartial`): `TwbMainRecordDef.GetCanBePartial` (`Core/wbInterface.pas:10542-10544`) is true when the record's Record Flags definition holds a flag named 'Partial Form' (`Core/wbInterface.pas:10063-10070`), and on FO4 those records are CELL (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5957`), DIAL (`:6311`), QUST (`:10686`) and WRLD (`:13112`). LCTN's bit 14 is named 'Unknown 14' (`:8042`), so LCTN cannot be partial and its bit is left alone. `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/container.hpp:can_be_partial` holds that four-signature list, and `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/container.hpp:is_partial_form` now calls it. Compressed is still cleared for every signature (`:10343`). It leaves child GRUPs and the record's position alone, as xEdit does.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:mark_override_deleted` locality: a record whose form key owner is this plugin returns `local_record`. Those are removed with `delete_local_record`, which takes the child GRUP with the record. The deleted check comes after the locality check, so an already-deleted local record reports `local_record`.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:set_record_flags` relocation scope: only the ten placed-reference signatures move, following `CheckChildOfCell` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:9964`). NAVM and LAND records in cell buckets (781 interior and 7,113 exterior NAVM, 37,020 LAND in Fallout4.esm, all in type 9) keep their group and only get the new bit. Test `RecordFlags.PersistentChangeOnInteriorNavmeshKeepsItsBucket`.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_record_flags.cpp` and `Radicle/tests/test_record_flags_deleted.cpp` (`RecordFlags.*`). Refusal tests compare `Radicle/tests/plugin_bytes.hpp:plugin_state` before and after the call, not only the written bytes. `Radicle/src/plugin/writer.cpp:write_record` copies the original bytes whenever `Record::original_range` is set, so an in-memory edit made without `mark_record_modified` still writes identical bytes. `plugin_state` catches that edit through subrecords, header flags and `original_range`.
## Undelete and disable references (#602 WP-12 D-5)
`UndeleteStatus undelete_and_disable_reference(Plugin&, const env::Environment&, const FormKey&)` is declared in `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/record_flags.hpp`. The xEdit reference is `TfrmMain.mniNavUndeleteAndDisableReferencesClick` at xEdit commit 93cc0bc5 (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:11803-11990`). The load order is the `env::Environment` the caller already holds, the same way `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:resolve_water` reads the winning record; no separate master table is built.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` filter: xEdit acts only on deleted REFR, PGRE, PMIS, ACHR, ACRE and PARW, PBAR, PBEA, PCON, PFLA, PHZD (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:11925-11940`; FO4 defines these at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5944-5951`, though the xEdit source comment tags them Skyrim). NAVM is in that list, but `canUndelete` refuses it (`xeMainForm.pas:11830-11833`). Radicle's filter is `is_placed_reference_signature` (`src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp`), which omits ACRE. ACRE is not an FO4 record (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` defines none), so this matches xEdit on FO4.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` skips: xEdit refuses an injected record and a record with no resolved base (`xeMainForm.pas:11828`, `11835-11838`). `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:is_injected` implements the first: the record's form key owner is not this plugin and no version of that key in the load order belongs to the owner file, which is `GetIsInjected`'s `not Assigned(mrMaster)` together with the form ID not being new to the file (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:11985-12000`). It returns the new `UndeleteStatus::injected_record` and writes nothing. The base check is still a proxy: the function requires NAME and DATA to be present, where xEdit resolves the NAME link through `MasterOrSelf.BaseRecord`. The load order now allows that resolution through `resolve_plugin_form_id`, and it is not implemented. The owner plugin must be in the load order, though not because `versions` is keyed by owner: `Radicle/src/environment/environment.cpp:Environment::versions` is keyed by record key and returns a version for any loaded plugin that holds that key. `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:is_injected` is true when no loaded plugin whose key equals the record's owner holds a version of that key, so an override owned by a plugin outside the load order is refused as `injected_record` even when its own NAME and DATA are present, and even when another loaded plugin such as a patch also overrides the same key. `RecordFlags.UndeleteTreatsOverrideWhoseOwnerIsNotLoadedAsInjected` pins that empty-environment behaviour, with no write.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` content restore: `TwbMainRecord.SetIsDeleted` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14010`) resets required members (`:14052-14054`) and then assigns content from the master chain (`:14075`, `:14082`). `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:winning_master_content` walks `env::Environment::versions` from the highest priority down, skipping this plugin, versions whose plugin is not in `plugin.header.masters` (`:14074`), deleted versions and partial forms (`:14071`), and returns the first match. That is xEdit's walk from `Pred(SelfIndex)` down (`:14070-14079`) plus its master fallback (`:14081-14082`). When NAME or DATA is missing the function replaces the record's subrecords with that version's, so a stub from `mark_override_deleted` gets the master's content. A record that still has its own NAME and DATA keeps its own content, which may differ from xEdit's result, and a record with no such version in the load order is still refused as `incomplete_reference`. The walk also skips a version whose `Record::undecodable` is set, because `Radicle/src/plugin/reader.cpp:read_record` leaves its subrecords empty after a failed inflate, so a corrupt master REFR supplies no content. After the copy the function re-checks NAME and DATA on the restored subrecords and returns `incomplete_reference` while either is missing, so no REFR is committed without NAME and DATA and `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference.cpp:decode_placed_reference` cannot throw `PlacedReferenceError` out of this status-returning function for a missing NAME or DATA; a present-but-wrong-size NAME, DATA or XSCL still throws from `decode_placed_reference` (known residual, non-persistent overrides only, because the decode at `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:290` is skipped for persistent overrides). The copied subrecords are not usable as raw bytes: their FormIDs are encoded in the source plugin's master-index space, and a source self-index can land on a different master in the destination. `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` therefore copies the `Record` behind the `env::RecordRef` that `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:winning_master_content` returns, runs `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:remap_record_form_links` in strict mode from `plugin_form_id_context` of the plugin that holds that version into `plugin_form_id_context(next)`, with that plugin as `type_source`, and moves only the remapped subrecords into the override. A strict-remap throw (unsupported VMAD or mixed NAVM/NAVI payload, malformed structured payload, or a form ID whose owner is absent from the destination master table) leaves the plugin unchanged and returns `UndeleteStatus::incomplete_reference`, like the missing-NAME/DATA path. Without the remap, a NAME of `0x0100xxxx` inside a plugin that masters only Fallout4.esm (index 01 is itself) copied into a plugin whose master table is [Fallout4.esm, DLCCoast.esm, DLCRobot.esm] would resolve index 01 to DLCCoast.esm. `Radicle/tests/test_record_flags_deleted.cpp:RecordFlags.UndeleteRemapsMasterFormLinksIntoTheTargetMasterSpace` pins the two-level case.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` Deleted: xEdit's `IsDeleted := True; IsDeleted := False` (`xeMainForm.pas:11945-11946`) clears the Deleted bit (`SetDeleted(False)`, `Core/wbImplementation.pas:14033`; Deleted is 1u << 5 in `Radicle/include/fo4/flags.hpp`). On an already-deleted record `IsDeleted := True` is a no-op (`SetIsDeleted` returns when the value is unchanged, `Core/wbImplementation.pas:14021`), and the undelete branch clears only the Deleted bit; the flags word is not copied from the master (see the group bullet), so Compressed is kept, as the function does.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` group: xEdit moves a record in `SetIsPersistent` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14231-14242`) and `SetIsVisibleWhenDistant`, not in `SetIsDeleted`. When the override has a non-deleted master, xEdit then copies the master's content with `Assign(wbAssignThis, Master)` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14075`, `14082`), which copies the whole flags word (`:9371`) and the form version (`:9374`), so Compressed and Persistent come from the master, and calls `UpdateCellChildGroup` (`:9411`), which can move the record. The function copies the master version's subrecords only, so Compressed and Persistent stay the override's own and the record does not move: that is the remaining deviation from `Assign` here. A deleted reference keeps the persistent bit that matches its bucket (see `set_record_flags` above). A file that already has the persistent bit in the temporary bucket is not repaired.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` Initially Disabled: `IsInitiallyDisabled := True` (`xeMainForm.pas:11965`) is not gated on persistence. Initially Disabled is 1u << 11 in `Radicle/include/fo4/flags.hpp`.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` Z: `wbUDRSetZ` is True and `wbUDRSetZValue` is -30000 (`Core/wbInterface.pas:321-322`). The FO3/FNV override (`xEdit/xeInit.pas:995-997`) does not apply to FO4. Z is written only when the reference is not persistent (`xeMainForm.pas:11958-11962`).
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` XESP and XTEL: xEdit removes "Enable Parent" and XTEL (`xeMainForm.pas:11963-11964`), then adds XESP with Reference set to `$14` and Flags set to 1 (`xeMainForm.pas:11966-11968`). Flag bit 0 is "Set Enable State to Opposite of Parent" in the FO4 `wbXESP` struct (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4330-4335`). The function erases both subrecords and calls `forms::set_placed_reference_enable_parent` with the FormKey `000014:Fallout4.esm`, the player in the load-order ID space that xEdit's `$14` names (#705, GT-294). Resolving raw 0x14 through the plugin's own MAST table pointed at local object 0x14 of master 0, which is the player only when Fallout4.esm is master 0. A plugin that lacks Fallout4.esm as a master gets it added as master 0 through `remap_plugin_masters`, which remaps every form link in the plugin, before the XESP is written; the setter's `encode` refuses a parent that is not a master. This deliberately differs from xEdit's bytes: xEdit hardcodes ids below `$800` (`Core/wbInterface.pas:22206-22208`, `Core/wbImplementation.pas:5124-5128`) and writes raw `0x00000014` with no added MAST, whereas Radicle adds the master and writes `0x0N000014` when Fallout4.esm is master N (`0x00000014` when it is master 0, which is byte-identical to xEdit). Static RE of the OG, NG and AE executables (#783 comment 20663) found the reserved range `0x1`-`0x7FF` skipped by the load-order remap and the enable-parent loader storing the file dword unchanged; whether a `0x0N000014` value is converted elsewhere was not found within that scope, and nothing was run in game. Raw `0x00000014` with resolver support for ids below `0x800` is the follow-up (option B). Test: `Radicle/tests/test_record_flags_deleted.cpp:RecordFlags.UndeleteParentsToTheLoadOrderPlayerWhenFallout4IsNotAMaster`. A plugin the master prepend cannot re-encode (an undecodable record elsewhere, or 253 masters (`k_max_plugin_masters`)) makes the function return `incomplete_reference` and leave the plugin untouched, so a Clean over many references does not abort. `UndeleteKeepsMasterOrderWhenFallout4IsANonZeroMaster` pins that a present Fallout4.esm master is never moved. The prepend types COED owners through the plugin first and then the load-order winner, so an owner that is an NPC_ or FACT in another master does not make the remap throw; `UndeletePrependsPlayerMasterWhenACoedOwnerIsTypedByAnotherMaster` pins that.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` scale: `wbUDRSetScale` is False on FO4 (`Core/wbInterface.pas:319`), so XSCL is left alone (`xeMainForm.pas:11971-11976`).
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` MSTT: `wbUDRSetMSTT` is True, but the branch needs `wbIsFallout3` (`xeMainForm.pas:11978`), so the function does not swap NAME to MSTT on FO4.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` non-deleted: xEdit skips them silently (`xeMainForm.pas:11925`). The function returns `not_deleted` and writes nothing.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` atomicity: the function works on a copy and assigns it back only on success, because the placed-reference helpers can throw after an earlier write.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_record_flags_deleted.cpp` (`RecordFlags.Undelete*`). `RecordFlags.UndeleteRestoresStrippedContentFromTheWinningMasterVersion` undeletes a NAME-only stub whose master carries NAME, DATA, XESP, XTEL and XSCL, and asserts the restored subrecords, the flags, the Z value taken from the restored DATA, and a byte-identical save/reload round trip. `RecordFlags.UndeleteRefusesInjectedReferenceWithoutChange` covers a complete override whose owner master lacks the record. Regression: without the injected check, Clean would restore and re-enable a reference that the master never defined, and the bytes would change. `RecordFlags.MarkOverrideDeletedClearsPartialFormOnlyWhereItCanBePartial` covers the Partial Form rule above. Regression: clearing bit 14 on every signature would strip a bit that is not Partial Form on a REFR, and never clearing it would leave a deleted CELL partial. The plugin builders shared by these tests are in `Radicle/tests/record_flags_fixture.hpp`; `record_flags_fixture.hpp:load_order` writes the master first and the patch second, the lowest-priority-first order `env::Environment::load` takes. In `record_flags_fixture.hpp:CellPlugin` the patch's CELL keeps index byte 1, which is past its single master, so that CELL resolves to the patch itself while the REFR (index byte 0) resolves to the master; the master's own CELL and REFR both resolve to the master, so the REFR keys match across the two plugins and the CELL keys do not. `RecordFlags.UndeleteRefusesUndecodableMasterVersionWithoutChange` detects a restore from a master version whose inflate failed, which would commit an empty record. It writes a master REFR that is compressed and fails to inflate (`record_flags_fixture.hpp:load_order_with_undecodable_reference`, the corrupt stream `Radicle/tests/test_undecodable_record.cpp` also uses) with a deleted NAME-only override in the patch, temporary and persistent, and asserts `incomplete_reference` with unchanged bytes. `RecordFlags.UndeleteRefusesMasterVersionWithoutNameOrDataWithoutChange` detects a record committed without NAME and DATA, which `decode_placed_reference` would then throw on forever. It does the same against a decodable master version that carries only XSCL, which pins the post-restore NAME and DATA re-check. `RecordFlags.UndeleteRemapsMasterFormLinksIntoTheTargetMasterSpace` detects a restore that copies master subrecords without remapping their FormIDs, which would point NAME at the wrong plugin whenever the patch's master order differs from the master's. It uses `record_flags_fixture.hpp:two_level_master_plugin` (Machine.esm, which masters Fallout4.esm, so its own NAME form ID uses index 01) and `record_flags_fixture.hpp:two_level_patch_plugin` (Patch.esp with masters [Fallout4.esm, Coast.esm, Machine.esm], so Machine.esm is index 02), undeletes the deleted override, and asserts that the restored NAME still resolves to its source key `000801:Machine.esm`; the copied raw `0x01000801` would resolve index 01 to Coast.esm if the remap were skipped. `record_flags_fixture.hpp:load_order` also has an `std::initializer_list<CellPlugin>` overload that writes the plugins in the order given, `record_flags_fixture.hpp:form_id_of` reads a 4-byte form ID payload, and `record_flags_fixture.hpp:resolved_link` resolves it through a plugin's context. `RecordFlags.UndeleteTreatsOverrideWhoseOwnerIsNotLoadedAsInjected` detects a Clean run with an empty or incomplete load order silently undeleting a complete reference, instead of refusing it as `injected_record` with unchanged bytes.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` callers: outside the tests the only caller is the PluginEditTool native backend. `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginMaintenance.cpp:invokeLegacyBackend` calls it once per deleted placed reference during `CleanPlugin`, with a load order built from the backend's own loaded plugins through `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/environment.hpp:Environment::from_plugins`, and turns `injected_record` and `incomplete_reference` into the refused counts in the result string. The detail is in `docs/code-notes/GARDEN-TOOLS.md`.
- `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginMaintenance.cpp:invokeLegacyBackend` status mapping: a deleted reference whose owning master is absent from the load order built by `Environment::from_plugins` is refused by `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:is_injected` with `UndeleteStatus::injected_record`, and the backend reports it in the "refused N injected" count. That wording covers both a genuinely injected record and an override whose owner plugin is simply not loaded. `UndeleteStatus` has no distinct owner-missing value; adding one would change `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/record_flags.hpp:UndeleteStatus` and every switch over it, and no consumer needs the distinction today, so the mapping is left as is. `RecordFlags.UndeleteTreatsOverrideWhoseOwnerIsNotLoadedAsInjected` pins the empty-load-order behaviour.
## Localized subrecord gaps (#602 WP-10)

Anchors: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` (per-record `localized_subrecords`) and `Radicle/src/schema/localized_fields.cpp:is_localized_field`. The lists feed `Radicle/tools/lstring_schema_codegen.py`, which writes `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_lstring_fields.inc`. `is_localized_field` reads that table, keyed by (record, subrecord).

Each pair was checked in xEdit at pin 93cc0bc5 (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas`). The subrecord is declared as `wbLString` or `wbLStringKC`, directly or through the `wbFULL`, `wbFULLReq`, `wbDESC`, `wbDESCReq` (:3692-3695) and `wbATTX` (:5277) macros. Every other use of that signature inside the same record is also a localized string.

Added:
- QUST FULL: `wbFULL` (:10690).
- PERK FULL and DESC: `wbFULL` and `wbDESCReq` (:7588-7589). EPF2: `wbLString(EPF2, 'Button Label')` (:7662), the only EPF2 definition. It is always a localized string in xEdit, whatever EPFT holds, so the table keys it unconditionally.
- SCOL FULL (:12645), WRLD FULL (:13118), MISC FULL (:10221), REGN RDMP (:11904).
- TERM BTXT (:12717), ITXT (:12729), RNAM (:12730) and UNAM (:12751), all `wbLStringKC`. TERM NAM0 and WNAM were already listed.
- RACE TTGP (:3102, `wbTintTemplateGroups`), MPPN (:3140, `wbMorphGroups`) and FMRN (:3176, `wbFaceMorphs`). Only RACE calls these helpers (:11279-11299), so no other record gets the pairs.
- NPC_ FULL (:10407), SHRT (:10408, `wbLStringKC`) and ATTX (:10488, `wbATTX`).
- OMOD FULL and DESC (:12507-12508).
- INNR WNAM (:12352, `wbLStringKC`).
- BPTD BPTN (:7698), CELL FULL (:5965), COBJ DESC (:10271) and FLST FULL (:7576). A master scan found all four always 4 bytes, in every localized master.

No candidate was rejected.

PERK, SCOL, WRLD, REGN, MISC, OMOD, BPTD, CELL and COBJ had no `fields.json` entry. Each got a minimal entry (`fields: []`), as QUST already had. The other codegen scripts accept an empty `fields` list, and `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py --write` refreshed `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` for the new localized counts.

Effect: in a localized plugin these subrecords now read as string IDs through `read_localized_string`. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp` refuses inline text for them, `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:default_usable` drops their defaults, and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp` skips the size-4 zstring check. No top-level scalar row in `fields.json` uses these pairs, and no shipped reader calls `read_localized_string` for them yet. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_localized_fields.cpp:Wp10LocalizedPairsAreMembers` and `Wp10NewPairRoundTripsAStringId`.
## src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:mixed_formid_offsets (unions and deciders, #602 WP-4)

Each rule below was checked against the xEdit source at pin 93cc0bc5 (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas`) before coding. Strict remap throws `FormIdError` on a malformed size; lenient remap returns no offsets. Tests are in `Radicle/tests/test_union_payload_remap.cpp` (`UnionPayloadRemap.*`).

Decider unions (`book_teaches_formid_offsets`, `omod_data_formid_offsets`):
- BOOK DNAM (`book_teaches_formid_offsets`): 13 bytes. Flags u8 at 0 decides the u32 at +1 (`wbBOOKTeachesDecider`, `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:1618-1636`; union `Teaches` at :5918-5923). Flags bit 0x01 (Advance Actor Value) is an AVIF, 0x04 (Add Spell) a SPEL, 0x10 (Add Perk) a PERK; with none of those the value is unused and not remapped. Test `UnionPayloadRemap.BookTeachesRemapsOnlyWhenFlagsSayFormId`.
- OMOD DATA (`omod_data_formid_offsets`, layout in `omod_data_layout_offsets`): `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12510-12537`. Header: Include Count u32 at 0, Property Count u32 at 4, Form Type u32 at 10 (an enum, never remapped), Attach Point form ID at 16. Then a u32 count and 4-byte KYWD slots (Attach Parent Slots), a u32 count and 8-byte items (no FormIDs), I rows of 7 bytes (Mod form ID at row +0), and P rows of 24 bytes. Property Value 1 at row +12 is a form ID when the value type byte (row +0) is 4 or 6 (`wbOMODDataPropertyValue1Decider`, `:2382-2406`). The total must equal the sum of the parts, otherwise the payload fails closed. Test `UnionPayloadRemap.OmodDataRemapsAttachSlotsIncludesAndFormValueTypes`.

Property rows on OBTS (`obts_formid_offsets`): the same 24-byte rows follow the includes. Value 1 at row +12 is remapped under the same value-type rule. Property union at `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5479`, `wbObjectModProperties` at :5458. Test `UnionPayloadRemap.ObtsPropertyValueRemapsOnlyFormIdValueTypes`.

MGEF DATA (`mgef_assoc_item_formid_offsets`, called from `form_links.cpp:visit_link_offsets`): the Assoc. Item union at DATA +8 is a form ID when the Archetype u32 at DATA +64 (`:10124`) is 12, 17, 18, 25, 34, 35, 36, 39, 40, 45 or 46 (`wbMGEFAssocItemDecider`, `:1367-1389`; Assoc. Item union at :10096-10110). The rule applies only to 152-byte payloads, the size the schema rows require, and other sizes are left unchanged. It is non-owning on purpose: `mixed_formid_offsets` returns nothing for MGEF DATA, so `form_link_schema.cpp:schema_formlink_offsets` keeps its 18 DATA rows (offsets 16 to 136). `visit_formlink_offsets` merges the extra offset with those rows. Test `UnionPayloadRemap.MgefAssocItemFollowsArchetypeAndKeepsSchemaRows`.

Form-version gates (`k_record_stride_layouts`):
- DMGT DNAM at form version 78 or later: an {AVIF, SPEL} 8-byte pair per entry, slots 0 and 4 (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12313-12320`). Below 78 the payload is a u32 index array, and an empty 4-byte row claims it so the global 4-byte `formid_subrecords.inc` table does not remap a single index. Test `UnionPayloadRemap.DamageTypeAndRaceBipedRemapByFormVersion`.
- RACE RBPC at form version 78 or later: one AVIF form ID per 4-byte entry, slot 0 (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11011-11022`). Below 78 the entries are integers and not remapped. Same test.
