- EFSH DNAM (`wbFormVersionDecider(106)`, `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6519-6722`): at form version 106 or later the flat Data arm is 157 bytes and its Ambient Sound SNDR is at 108 (members counted from :6652-6722; the same 157-byte size is in the Radicle.md EFSH note). Below 106 the old-format arm is 395 bytes, with Addon Models DEBR at 241 (:6582) and Ambient Sound SNDR at 305 (:6598). Both sizes match the corpus counts in the EFSH note above. Test `UnionPayloadRemap.EfshAmbientSoundFollowsFormVersionLayout`.
- Malformed size on any of the above fails closed in strict mode. Test `UnionPayloadRemap.MalformedUnionPayloadsFailClosedWithoutMutation`.

## src/schema/form_link_records.cpp (struct payloads part 2, #602 WP-2)

Each rule below was checked against the xEdit source at pin 93cc0bc5 before coding. Strict remap throws `FormIdError` on a malformed size; lenient remap returns no offsets. Tests are in `Radicle/tests/test_record_struct_remap.cpp` (`RecordStructRemap.*`). `record_struct_formid_offsets` is called from `form_link_mixed.cpp:mixed_formid_offsets`. Fixed-stride rows reuse `fixed_stride_formid_offsets` and `FixedStrideLayout` from `form_link_mixed.cpp`, declared in `form_link_mixed.hpp`.

None of the subrecords below has a `fields.json` formlink row, so claiming them drops no schema offsets.

Fixed-stride rows (`k_record_fixed_layouts`):
- LCTN ACPR and LCPR: 12-byte {Ref, World/Cell, Grid Y, Grid X}, slots 0 and 4, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 8045-8164. Test `RecordStructRemap.LctnEntriesRemapFormIdSlotsOnly`.
- LCTN ACUN and LCUN: 12-byte {NPC, Actor Ref, Location}, slots 0, 4 and 8. Same lines and test.
- LCTN ACSR and LCSR: 16-byte {Loc Ref Type, Ref, World/Cell, Grid Y, Grid X}, slots 0, 4 and 8. Same lines and test.
- LCTN ACEP and LCEP: 12-byte {Ref, Enable Parent, Flags, 3 unused}, slots 0 and 4. Same lines and test.
- LCTN RCPR, RCUN, RCSR, ACID and LCID: one 4-byte form ID per entry, slot 0. Same lines and test.
- BPTD BPND: exact 101 bytes (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 7703-7771, record at 7693). Slots 4 and 8 (Explodable Debris, Explosion), 16 and 20 (Severable Debris, Explosion), 52 and 56 (Severable and Explodable Impact DataSet), 67 (Actor Value, unaligned), 79, 83, 87 and 91 (On Cripple Art Object, Debris, Explosion, Impact DataSet). Test `RecordStructRemap.BodyPartNodeRemapsElevenSlots`.
- CELL XPRI: packed 4-byte array of placed-reference form IDs, slot 0, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` line 6087. Test `RecordStructRemap.CellPrevisAndCombinedIndexRemap`.
- IDLM IDLA: packed 4-byte array of IDLE or NULL form IDs, slot 0, `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas` lines 8651-8652 (`wbIdleAnimation`, used by IDLM at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` line 7098). PACK IDLA stays in `behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_formid_offsets`, which returns nothing for IDLM. Test `RecordStructRemap.IdleMarkerAndLandLayersRemap`.
- LAND BTXT and ATXT: exact 8 bytes {LTEX, quadrant u8, unused u8, layer s16}, slot 0, `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas` lines 8722-8748 (`wbLandLayers`, LAND at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` line 9846). Test `RecordStructRemap.IdleMarkerAndLandLayersRemap`.
- RACE TTEC: 14-byte tint template colors {CLFM, float, u16, u32}, slot 0, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 3064-3128, used at lines 11279 and 11297 inside RACE. Test `RecordStructRemap.RaceDataAndTintTemplatesRemapByFormVersion`.
- REGN RDOT: 52-byte objects, slot 0. RDGS: 8-byte grasses, slot 0. RDWT: 12-byte {Weather, Chance, Global}, slots 0 and 8. RDSA: 12-byte {Sound, Flags, Chance float}, slot 0. `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 11909-11954, and `wbRegionSounds` at `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas` lines 9172-9185. Test `RecordStructRemap.RegionEntriesAndStagTnamRemap`.

Custom rules:
- LCTN ACEC, LCEC and RCEC (`worldspace_cells_offsets`): World form ID at 0, then 4-byte cell coordinates to the end. The payload must be at least 4 bytes and a multiple of 4. `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 8045-8164. Test `RecordStructRemap.LctnEntriesRemapFormIdSlotsOnly`.
- CELL XCRI (`combined_reference_offsets`): u32 mesh count at 0, u32 References Count at 4, then count u32 mesh IDs at 8, then 8-byte {REFR, mesh} entries. xEdit halves the References Count (`wbCELLCombinedRefsCounter`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 2429-2438), so the field counts u32 words. The REFR form ID sits at 8 + 4M + 8i. The size must equal 8 + 4M + 4 × count, and an odd count fails closed. `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 6087-6100. Test `RecordStructRemap.CellPrevisAndCombinedIndexRemap`.
- RACE DATA (`race_data_offsets`): offsets from summing member sizes, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 11069-11195. Weights add 24 bytes from form version 109, so Flags starts at 32 (8 below). Severable Explosion, Debris and Impact DataSet, then Explodable Explosion, Debris and Impact DataSet, start at Flags + 114 from form version 124 (+110 below). OnCripple (from 96) has Explosion, Debris and Impact DataSet at +6, +10 and +14 of its 18-byte struct. Subsegment Explosion (from 118) follows. Pitch (98) and Roll (101) are scalars. Expected sizes are 200 at version 131 and 164 at version 100. Test `RecordStructRemap.RaceDataAndTintTemplatesRemapByFormVersion`.
- STAG TNAM (`stag_tnam_offsets`): one {SNDR, zstring} entry per subrecord, slot 0, size at least 4, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 12663-12666. The zstring is not validated. Test `RecordStructRemap.RegionEntriesAndStagTnamRemap`.
- WRLD RNAM (`large_reference_offsets`): Y s16 at 0, X s16 at 2, u32 count at 4, then 8-byte {REFR, Y, X} entries. Slot is 8 + 8i. The size must equal 8 + 8 × count. `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas` lines 9737-9760, WRLD at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` line 13110. Test `RecordStructRemap.WorldLargeRefsAndNvnmOutsideNavmesh`.
- NVNM on ACTI, FURN and STAT (`nvnm_outside_navm_offsets`): same struct as NAVM (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 4360-4366, `wbNVNM`). Hosts are ACTI at line 5669, FURN at 6918 and STAT at 12082. NAVM at 7220 already uses `navmesh_mixed_formid_offsets`. Same gates as NAVM: form version 128 or later, Version u32 15, and `nvnm_formid_offsets` must accept the payload. Test `RecordStructRemap.WorldLargeRefsAndNvnmOutsideNavmesh`.

Skipped on purpose:
- REGN RDAT is an 8-byte header {Type enum, Override, Priority, unused}, with no form ID (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 11880-11887).
- RACE TETI, TTEF, TTGE and TTEB have no form ID. Template conditions stay on the CTDA path.
- REGN RDMO and WNAM are unchanged.
- Malformed sizes on every rule above fail closed in strict mode. Test `RecordStructRemap.MalformedSizesFailClosedWithoutMutation`.

## EXPL DATA version gate (#602 WP-11 D-27)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:EXPL`: xEdit DATA layout by record form version, from `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` lines 7341-7384. `wbFromVersion` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:6423`) is a union on `wbFormVersionDecider`, which picks the member when the record `Version >= gate` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:5542-5562`). Ungated, offsets 0-31: Light, Sound 1, Sound 2, Impact Data Set, Placed Object, Spawn Projectile, Force, Damage (lines 7342-7349).
- Gated members: Inner Radius only at 97 and up (line 7350, offset 32). Outer Radius, IS Radius, Vertical Offset Mult, Flags and Sound Level (lines 7351-7367) are unconditional, so they sit at 36-52 from 97 on and at 32-48 below 97. AutoFade from 70 (line 7369), Stagger from 91 (lines 7370-7376), Spawn struct of 20 bytes from 112 (lines 7377-7383).
- Vanilla DATA sizes by form version: below 70 is 52, 70-90 is 56, 91-96 is 60, 97-111 is 64, 112 and up is 84. These match the 52/56/60/64 truncations named in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp` (`ScalarDescriptor::embedded`).
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:EXPL`: the 8 rows from `EXPL\InnerRadius` (32) to `EXPL\StaggerMagnitude` (60) carry `min_form_version: 97` and the 5 Spawn rows (64-80) carry 112, as xEdit gates them. Below 97 all 13 are hidden, including Outer through Sound Level, which xEdit shifts but does not gate at 97. The fixed row offsets are only right at 97 and up. The Force, Damage and formlink DATA rows (0-28) are the same at every version and stay ungated.
- `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots`: a record below `shape.min_form_version` is `sized == false`, so the row is neither valid nor misfit. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` then returns `subrecord_missing` before encoding, so the bytes do not change. `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` uses the same resolver for reads.
- At 97-111 the 64-byte DATA hides the Spawn rows at 64-80 by size (`resolve_field_slots` misfit or short payload), while Placed Object Fade Delay (56) and Stagger (60) stay readable.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:EXPL`: from 97 to 111 a DATA longer than 64 bytes (not produced by vanilla) still hides the Spawn rows, because xEdit reads that tail as unused rather than Spawn.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_scalar_embedded.cpp:ExplDataFullLayoutReadsAndWritesLaterMembersFrom112` (84-byte DATA at 111 refuses ProjectileCount; at 112 later members read, ProjectileCount written and read back), `ExplDataOlderLayoutsHideGatedMembersWithoutMutation` (52, 56 and 60-byte DATA at 69, 90 and 96, refused with DATA unchanged), `ExplData64BytesFrom97ExposesStaggerButNotSpawnRows` (64-byte DATA at 100). The fixture `Radicle/tests/test_scalar_embedded.cpp:expl_plugin_at` takes the DATA length.
## Listed form ID signatures with other sizes (#602 R-1)

- `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:visit_link_offsets` remaps a signature from the global table only when the payload is exactly 4 bytes; any other size falls through silently, in strict mode too. A survey of the seven masters (2,192,237 records, 179 listed signatures) found 1,535 (record, subrecord, size) combinations that no handler claims, in 144 (record, subrecord) pairs. Most of those pairs hold strings, flags, scalars or float structs (for example STAT MNAM, NPC_ DNAM, the IMAD and IMGS blocks, WRLD DNAM), so the fall-through is right for them.
- `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp:record_fixed_layout_offsets` MUST SNAM: the Tracks array of MUST form IDs (xEdit `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8816`), 41 vanilla payloads of 28 to 248 bytes. The generated MUST SNAM list row (`include/fo4/schema/generated_formlink_lists.inc`) already remapped well-formed payloads through `schema_formlink_offsets`; the stride-4 rule moves ownership into the mixed path, which drops that schema row, and makes strict mode throw on a size that is not a multiple of 4. Tests `RecordStructRemap.MusicTrackListRemaps` and the MUST SNAM case in `RecordStructRemap.MalformedSizesFailClosedWithoutMutation`.
- `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp:transient_type_offsets` TES4 TNAM: Transient Type, a u32 form type (78 DIAL, 126 SCEN) then an array of DIAL or SCEN form IDs (xEdit `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12114-12125`), 11 vanilla payloads of 8 to 14,276 bytes. The form type word is never remapped. `visit_records` reaches the TES4 header (`include/fo4/plugin/visit.hpp`). TES4 has no schema rows and TNAM is not in the global table, so this was a real gap. Test `RecordStructRemap.HeaderTransientTypesRemapReferencesNotFormType`, which also checks that a 6-byte payload throws in strict mode without mutation.
- AMMO DNAM (16), CPTH ANAM (8), STAT DNAM (8 and 16) and ZOOM GNAM (24) also fall through `visit_link_offsets`, but `src/schema/form_link_schema.cpp:schema_formlink_offsets` remaps their form ID slots from the generated field rows, so they are covered.
- Not done: a strict-mode throw on the remaining fall-through. Every strict caller scans the whole plugin (`rekey_form_links` from delete and renumber, `remap_form_links` from master changes and save, `remap_record_form_links` from copies), and STAT DNAM alone occurs 23,579 times, so a throw without a (record, subrecord, size) allow-list of the 137 non-form-ID pairs would break almost every plugin. The allow-list and the choice between throwing and only reporting are open on #602.

## Magic effect lists (#602 WP-6)

- `Radicle/src/forms/effects.cpp:decode_effects` xEdit effect struct: `wbEffect` is a `wbRStruct` of EFID, EFIT and Conditions with summary key [0,2] (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5599-5606`), and `wbEffectsReq` is a required `wbRArrayS` (`:5608-5609`). An effect starts at each EFID and runs to the next EFID or the end of the record.
- `Radicle/src/forms/effects.cpp:decode_effects` EFID is a 4-byte form key to MGEF (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5114`). EFIT is 12 bytes: f32 magnitude, u32 area, u32 duration (`:5116-5121`, required). The condition run after EFIT is CTDA with optional CIS1 and CIS2 (`:5183-5251`, CITC count via `SetCountPath(CITC)` at `:5254`), read by `read_ctda_conditions_in` and written by `serialize_ctda_run`.
- `Radicle/src/forms/effects.cpp:set_magic_effects` block position: ALCH `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5738` (after DNAM at :5737), ENCH `:6749` (after ENIT), INGR `:9820` (after ENIT), SPEL `:12038` (after SPIT). In all four the effect list is the last member, so the block is appended at the end when the record has no EFID.
- `Radicle/src/forms/effects.cpp:set_magic_effects` order: `wbRArrayS` sets the array sorted (`Core/wbInterface.pas:8482`), and the xEdit GUI turns on `wbSortSubRecords` (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:5160`; core default False at `Core/wbInterface.pas:150`), which merge-sorts effects by `CompareSortKeys` on add and init (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:20767`, `:20914-20917`). The CK does not store them sorted: in the seven masters 550 ALCH, ENCH, INGR and SPEL records hold more than one effect, 225 of them not in ascending EFID order and 178 with a repeated EFID. Sorting would reorder vanilla data, so the function writes the caller's order.
- `Radicle/src/forms/effects.cpp:block_is_contiguous` layout: `wbConditions` can carry a CITC count (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5254`), but a CITC or any other non-effect subrecord inside the block is refused (`set_magic_effects` returns `unexpected_layout`; `read_magic_effects` throws). In the seven masters every one of the 2,701 effects on these four records sits in one contiguous block at the end of its record, with no CITC, and every EFIT is 12 bytes, so the rule refuses no vanilla record.
- `Radicle/src/forms/effects.cpp:set_magic_effects` refusal order: record missing, unsupported type, then the contiguity check. All entries are encoded before the erase and insert, so a throw leaves the subrecords unchanged. The only content write is `detail::mark_record_modified`. `assign_record_form_keys` runs first and changes only the form key cache.
- `Radicle/src/forms/effects.cpp:encode_effects` an effect whose owner is neither this plugin nor a master throws `MagicEffectError`, not an enum value, because the encode step (`encode_plugin_form_id`) throws. Sibling writers throw the same way (`Radicle/src/forms/components.cpp:set_record_components`).
- `Radicle/src/forms/effects.cpp:decode_effects` a condition run must begin with CTDA and may not hold EFIT; a stray CIS before the first CTDA would otherwise be dropped silently by `read_ctda_conditions_in`, so it is refused first.
- `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:effect_element_ranges` already models the same EFID/EFIT/CTDA region; the contiguity rule matches it.
- Not done: a strict-mode throw on the remaining fall-through. Every strict caller scans the whole plugin (`rekey_form_links` from delete and renumber, `remap_form_links` from master changes and save, `remap_record_form_links` from copies), and the 137 non-form-ID pairs account for 185,405 vanilla payloads, so a throw without an allow-list would break almost every plugin. Nomad chose report only (#602 decision, option 2).
- `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:collect_form_links_detailed` report only: a payload is listed in `FormLinkCollection::unclaimed_link_payloads` when its signature is in the global table, its size is not 4, no handler in `visit_link_offsets` claimed it (the function returns false only on the final fall-through), no schema row covers it (`visit_formlink_offsets` returns true when it has schema offsets), and the (record, subrecord) pair is not in `include/fo4/schema/unclaimed_link_allowlist.inc`. Nothing throws. `scan_master_usage` copies the count to `MasterUsage::unclaimed_link_payloads`, which does not change `complete()`.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/unclaimed_link_allowlist.inc`: the 137 (record, subrecord) pairs from the R-1 survey of the seven masters whose unclaimed payloads hold strings, flags, scalars or float structs per xEdit 93cc0bc5 (for example STAT MNAM, NPC_ DNAM, the IMAD and IMGS blocks, WRLD DNAM). Keyed by pair, not size, because the string members vary in length. SCEN HTID and SNDR BNAM hold a form ID only at size 4 (`wbFormIDCk` Play Sound and the Base Descriptor union member), which the report skips anyway; their other vanilla sizes are s32 arrays or structs. A Sonnet port of the dispatcher at this commit reports 0 of 2,192,237 vanilla records. TES4 TNAM and MUST SNAM are left out because #612 gives them rules. Test `RecordStructRemap.CollectReportsUnclaimedListedPayloadsOutsideTheAllowList`.

## ITM comparison (#602 WP-13 D-4)

- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:ItmScan::identical_previous` partner: the defining owner (`ItmScan::owner_index`, the earliest plugin in load order that matches the record's owner key), not the nearest earlier version. xEdit 93cc0bc5 compares each override with its master: the node list is `[Master] + Overrides` in load order (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:15060-15153`, `TfrmMain.NodeDatasForMainRecord`), and the master is `TwbMainRecord.GetMasterOrSelf` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:12140`). The former nearest-version rule reported C in `[A v1, B v2, C v2]` as ITM; xEdit compares C with A, which differs, so C is not ITM.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:ItmScan::identical_previous` winner chain: a record is reported when a later plugin still holds it (`held_after`), because it is then not the winning node. When it is the last holder, every plugin between the owner and it must hold the owner's version (`ItmScan::same_version`), otherwise the record is not ITM. xEdit turns the last node into `ctIdenticalToMasterWinsConflict` when another node differs (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2723-2746`, `TfrmMain.ConflictLevelForNodeDatas`), and that verdict is not removable unless partial forms are allowed (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:12238`, `wbAllowMakePartial`). So `[A v1, B v2, C v1]` keeps C. `[A v1, B v2, C v1, D v1]` reports C only when the caller passes the full load order, so `held_after` sees D. `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginCheck.cpp:RadiclePluginBackend::lootCleaningReport` (lines 92-98) and `Radicle/tools/inspect/main.cpp:print_itm` (line 311) pass the full order. The removal path (`PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginMaintenance.cpp:RemoveIdenticalToMaster`, lines 443-447) and the C API (`Radicle/src/c_api_maintenance.cpp:radicle_env_identical_to_master`, lines 41-44) pass only the order up to and including the plugin, so `held_after` is always false there and C is kept, because B v2 intervenes. The truncation is the conservative choice: a removal must not depend on a later plugin that the user can disable or reorder. The truncated set is always a subset of the full-order set. The LOOT `itm` count is full-order and feeds `dirty` (`lootCleaningReport`, line 104), so the dirty flag can stay set after cleaning.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:ItmScan::scan` verdicts: the per-slot compare is against the first node (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2650-2669`), and a record's verdict is the maximum over its children (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:4878-4930`, `TfrmMain.ConflictLevelForChildNodeDatas`), so any differing subrecord keeps the record. An undecodable record, owner or intermediate holder, or a remap error in `remapped_into`, yields no ITM.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:same_record` compares the signature, the raw header flags (`Radicle/include/fo4/flags.hpp:RecordFlags`, deleted 0x20 and compressed 0x40000) and the comparable subrecords in stored order. Data size, version-control info and form version are not compared, as xEdit's record header marks them `cpIgnore` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8295`, `:8298-8303`). xEdit compares the Record Flags element at normal priority (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8296`), and a deleted or partial record only changes that element to `cpNormalIgnoreEmpty`, which still compares it (`Core/wbInterface.pas:14503-14513`). Its flag lists name bit 18 'Compressed' (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5959`), so the raw compare is at least as strict.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:ItmScan::same_version` placement: `record_placements` gives the group type and the parent, where parent groups of types 1, 6 and 7 set the parent (`Radicle/src/plugin/placement.cpp:place_group`). xEdit's record compare keys on the form ID alone (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:12525-12528`, `TwbMainRecord.GetSortKeyInternal`), so this check is stricter: a record moved to another parent or group type is never reported.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:k_itm_ignored_subrecords` holds 10 whole-subrecord entries. Each is a `cpIgnore` leaf in `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` whose own definition carries the priority (the signature constructors pass it to the value definition as well, `Core/wbInterface.pas:7880`, `:7931`, `:7986`, `:8769`, `:9041`), so `TwbDataContainer.GetConflictPriority` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:23876-23893`) returns `cpIgnore` and the slot stays out of the verdict (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2619`): TACT PNAM (`:5685`) and FNAM (`:5687`), CSTY CSMD (`:6252`), DIAL TIFC (`:6472`), PROJ DATA (`:7121`), PERK PRKF (`:7689`, an empty end marker inside each effect), MESG INAM (`:8183`), MATO DNAM (`:9379`, repeated), REFR XMBP (`:11515`) and WRLD NNAM (`:13170`).
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:is_itm_ignored` does not ignore CELL XCLW, although xEdit's `wbCELLXCLWGetConflictPriority` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:2090-2122`, exit on a deleted record at `:2109`, `cpIgnore` for an interior cell at `:2119-2121`) was written for it. The getter is attached with `SetGetCP` to the XCLW subrecord definition (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6045`, `Core/wbInterface.pas:10977-10984`), but `TwbDataContainer.GetConflictPriority` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:23876-23893`) reads the subrecord's value definition first, the unnamed float definition (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:15756-15758`), which has no getter. The getter therefore never runs, and xEdit 93cc0bc5 compares XCLW in every cell. Ignoring it would keep a false ITM for an interior cell whose water height alone changed, so Radicle keeps it.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:k_itm_ignored_subrecords` not ignored, so Radicle stays stricter (never a false ITM): field-level or conditional `cpIgnore` and `cpNormalIgnoreEmpty` members inside structs, which need a field decoder: NAVM PLDT, PLVD and Target Data fields (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4182-4245`), NAVM Edge Link (`:4406-4411`, conditional through `wbNAVMEdgeLinksGetCP`), ACHR EFIT and CTDA (`:5127`, `:5130`, `:5212`), PERK Perk Condition Tab Count (`:7640`) and DOBJ (`:8622-8624`). `cpBenignIfAdded` XLRL (`:3260`, `:4580`, `:11683`) is not modeled: xEdit treats an element the master lacks as benign when it is the last override (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2655-2662`), while Radicle counts it as a difference. `PACK PFOR` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10634`) carries `cpIgnore` on the `wbRArray` wrapper. `TfrmMain.InitNodes` (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:7701-7702`) marks a child missing under a present `cpIgnore` wrapper as `vnfIgnore`, and the slot compare drops that node (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2526-2535`). A slot takes the multi-node compare only when two or more records have the entry (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2537-2550`); a lone entry is `caOnlyOne`, which ranks below `caNoConflict` (`Core/wbInterface.pas:491-499`). The lone entry still sets `ctOnlyOne` on the record that has it (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2545`, propagated by `TfrmMain.ConflictLevelForChildNodeDatas`, `:4878-4935`). `ctOnlyOne` ranks above `ctIdenticalToMaster` (`Core/wbInterface.pas:506-518`), so the removal test (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:12231`) fails for an override that adds a trailing entry. An override that drops a trailing master entry leaves `ctNotDefined` and can still pass that test. Radicle compares every entry in stored order, which is stricter. No order-insensitive arrays are implemented.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:same_record` deleted records: a deleted override matches only a deleted master, through the flag compare. `count_deleted_records` is a separate read-only count and is unchanged.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:ItmScan::scan` child groups: a record is reported only when its owned child group is emptied by the same scan, so an identical cell with a changed reference is kept (`Radicle/tests/test_maintenance_nested.cpp:MaintenanceNested.ChangedReferenceKeepsItsIdenticalCell`).
- `Radicle/src/plugin/placement.cpp:place_group` persistent and temporary cell children: groups 8 (`cell_persistent_children`) and 9 (`cell_temporary_children`) do not set a parent, so their records take the CELL from the enclosing type 6 group. A record moved between them is not reported, under the placement rule above.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:k_itm_ignored_subrecords` NAVM: no whole-subrecord entry, so a navmesh is compared raw. Its ignored members are field-level (see above), so an override that differs only there is kept.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:find_identical_to_master` vanilla impact (measured with a scratch script outside the repo): for each vanilla DLC, overrides with raw top byte 0 that are byte-identical to Fallout4.esm with the same flags and placement, before and after the ten-entry table. DLCRobot 36 to 36, DLCworkshop01 1 to 1, DLCworkshop02 0 to 0, DLCworkshop03 7 to 7, DLCCoast 37 to 38, DLCNukaWorld 39 to 40; totals 120 to 122 of 2368 overrides. One DLCCoast NAVM override has no Fallout4.esm record and is excluded. The table adds two DIAL records, 001CF636 (DLCCoast) and 0006B8AE (DLCNukaWorld), both differing only in TIFC. No other entry adds a record. Caveat: link bytes are compared raw. That is exact here because Fallout4.esm has no masters and every DLC lists it as master 0, but each override is compared with Fallout4.esm only, without the later-holder or intermediate-holder checks.
- `Radicle/tests/test_maintenance.cpp:OverrideIdenticalToMasterIsItmWhileALaterOverrideStillHoldsTheRecord` and its neighbors: `IgnoredSubrecordDifferenceStillIdenticalToMaster`, `RealFieldDifferenceIsNotIdenticalEvenWithIgnoredSubrecord`, `CellWaterHeightIsComparedForInteriorAndExteriorCells`, `OverrideIdenticalToMasterIsNotItmWhenAnInterveningOverrideDiffers` and `OverrideIdenticalToAnInterveningOverrideIsNotItmWhenItDiffersFromMaster`. Expectations unchanged under the owner rule: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_maintenance.cpp:CApiMaintenance.ReportsItmDeletedAndUnusedMasters`, `Radicle/tests/test_undecodable_edit.cpp:UndecodableEdit.FindIdenticalToMasterSkipsWhenMasterRecordIsUndecodable`, `Radicle/tests/test_maintenance_nested.cpp:MaintenanceNested.ItmReferenceAndItsCellAreBothFoundChildFirst`, and the PluginEditTool tests `RadiclePluginItmNestedTests.cpp`, `RadiclePluginMaintenanceTests.cpp` and `RadiclePluginAddMastersTests.cpp`, each with a single override.
## Placed reference relocation on move (#602 WP-13 D-29)

- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` trigger: xEdit's `UpdateCellChildGroup` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14489-14623`) has four callers: a DATA position change (`TwbMainRecord.DoAfterSet`, `:9538-9559`, call at `:9557`), a persistent-flag toggle (`SetIsPersistent`, `:14231-14242`, `:14240`), a visible-distant-flag toggle (`SetIsVisibleWhenDistant`, `:14244-14255`, `:14253`), and a bulk assign (`:9410-9411`). `move_placed_reference` handles only the position trigger; the persistent toggle is WP-12's `set_record_flags`, and the visible-distant toggle is not handled. On the position trigger, `DoAfterSet` calls `UpdateCellChildGroup` for a record that `CheckChildOfCell` accepts (`:9964-9982`: REFR, PMIS, PGRE, ACRE, ACHR, PARW, PBEA, PFLA, PCON, PBAR, PHZD) when the position element is modified and its generation changed (`:9553-9555`). Radicle writes DATA first through `set_placed_reference_transform`, then decides relocation from the new position.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` bucket choice: a persistent reference (record flag `0x00000400`, xEdit `Core/wbInterface.pas:20455-20458`) takes CorrectGroupType 8 (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14518-14519`) and every other record takes 9 (`:14522-14523`). xEdit's type 10 arm (`:14520-14521`) needs a visible-when-distant flag and `wbVWDInTemporary` false (`Core/wbInterface.pas:171`), and FO4 sets that true (`xEdit/xeInit.pas:1093-1094`), so on FO4 the target type is 8 or 9 only. Radicle computes the same `wanted_bucket` from `Record::header.flags.is_persistent()` (`placed_reference_move.cpp:83-85`) and never builds a type 10 target. xEdit exits when the record already sits in a persistent group (`:14525-14526`, `CorrectGroupType <> 9`), and for an interior CELL (CELL DATA bit 0, `:14540-14544`) when the bucket already matches (`:14543`); Radicle returns `moved` in both cases (`placed_reference_move.cpp:87-89`, `:91`). A record in a type 8 bucket whose persistent flag is clear is no longer exempt from that decision: it re-buckets (deviation (h) below).
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy_internal.hpp:grid_coordinate` grid math: `wbPositionToGridCell` (xEdit `Core/wbInterface.pas:5339-5347`) takes floor(position / `wbCellSizeFactor`) on each axis, with `wbCellSizeFactor` = 4096.0 (`wbInterface.pas:300`). `grid_coordinate` applies the same floor with `k_exterior_cell_span` and throws for a non-finite or int32-overflowing grid, as create does. Deviation (d): `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:exterior_grid_in_range` checks that floor against `Radicle/include/fo4/forms/cell.hpp:k_exterior_cell_min_coordinate` and `k_exterior_cell_max_coordinate` before `grid_coordinate` runs, so an out-of-range finite position returns `target_cell_missing`. A NaN or infinite position never reaches it: `set_placed_reference_transform` refuses it first with `PlacedReferenceError` (see "Placed reference transform refuses non-finite values (#657)"). xEdit has no range limit (`wbPositionToGridCell` has no clamp). `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:exterior_cell_grid_layout` throws `CellError` outside -110..110 (`:249-250`), which is why the move checks first.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` same grid: xEdit keeps the reference in its cell when the grid matches and the group type already matches (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14576-14578`), and when the grid matches but the type differs it keeps the CELL and only re-buckets (`:14579`; the record then lands in `CorrectGroupType` through `:14604-14617`). Radicle compares the `find_exterior_cell` result with the source CELL form key (`placed_reference_move.cpp:117-121`, `:124`) and, on a match, calls the same re-bucket helper when the bucket type differs, then returns `moved` (`:124-127`). A same-CELL move whose bucket already matches changes nothing but DATA, which `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_move_exterior.cpp:PlacedReferenceMoveExterior.SameCellMoveWithAMatchingBucketWritesOnlyData` pins byte-for-byte against `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference.cpp:set_placed_reference_transform` alone.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` persistent world cell: xEdit skips the same-grid test when the old CELL is persistent (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14573`) and relocates the temporary reference to CELL[x,y] (`:14583-14588`), so a temporary reference in the persistent cell does relocate. Radicle's `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:find_exterior_cell` never returns a persistent CELL (`cell.cpp:301-302`), so the target never equals the source and the reference relocates.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` deviation (c), missing target: xEdit calls `WorldSpace.Add('CELL[x,y]')` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14587`), with `aSilent` defaulting to True (`Core/wbInterface.pas:1445`). That lookup copies a visible master CELL into this file as an override (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:16880-16893`), or creates a new CELL with a new form ID and the grid set (`:16896-16951`). Radicle returns `target_cell_missing` and leaves the plugin unchanged. Creating or overriding a CELL is out of this change's scope, so the caller does it first. `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:create_exterior_cell` needs its WRLD in the plugin, and `find_exterior_cell` searches this plugin only.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` group placement: xEdit ensures the CELL child group (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14593`, `TwbMainRecord.EnsureChildGroup` at `:9852-9882`) and the temporary bucket (`:14604-14606`). Radicle reuses `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp:ensure_cell_children_group` and `:ensure_reference_bucket`, which insert the child group after the CELL record and the bucket in type order. The target bucket is the one `wanted_bucket` picks (`placed_reference_move.cpp:143-144`), so a persistent reference lands in type 8 and every other record in type 9.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_edit.hpp:erase_if_empty` cleanup: xEdit removes an emptied old bucket and an emptied old child group (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14611-14622`). Radicle does the same. The shared helper matches the group by type and label, so with a duplicate header in one parent only the first match is checked. A valid plugin has one group per type and label under a parent, so there it removes the group xEdit removes.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` deviations from xEdit, in order: (a) visible-distant relocation throws, (b) a persistent reference under a grid CELL moves to the worldspace persistent CELL, (c) a missing target returns `target_cell_missing`, (d) a finite grid outside -110..110 returns `target_cell_missing` (a non-finite position is refused earlier, see the #657 section), (e) malformed containment throws, and a CELL without DATA is treated as exterior, (f) a same-cell bucket mismatch is re-bucketed, (g) the record is appended, not sorted, (h) a type 8 bucket record with a clear persistent flag is re-bucketed. (b), (f) and (h) were closed by #602 WP-13 D-29; (g) is still open, with the reason recorded in its bullet. Each one has its own bullet below. The signature scope (every placed-reference signature) matches xEdit's CheckChildOfCell list in the trigger bullet and is not a deviation.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` deviation (a), visible-distant: a type 10 bucket does not occur in FO4. xEdit's CorrectGroupType is 10 for flag `0x00008000` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14520-14521`, `Core/wbInterface.pas:20460-20463`) only when `wbVWDInTemporary` is False (default at `wbInterface.pas:171`). FO4 sets it True (`xEdit/xeInit.pas:1093-1094`), so FO4 keeps visible-distant references in type 9. Radicle accepts a type 10 source bucket (`placed_reference_move.cpp:63-67`) and re-buckets a move within the same CELL into type 9 (`:124-127`). A move to another CELL out of a type 10 bucket throws `PlacedReferenceError` (`:128-130`). That refusal exists only because `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp:ensure_reference_bucket` accepts types 8 and 9 (`:171-175`), so the move cannot build a type 10 target. The refusal is fail-closed: the move commits only on success, so the caller's plugin is unchanged.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` deviation (b), persistent reference under a grid CELL (closed by this change): xEdit moves it to CELL[P], the worldspace persistent cell (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14553-14565`; `WorldSpace.Add('CELL[P]')` at `:14558`), and keeps the old child group when the owning group is already the world-children GRUP (`:14564-14565`). Radicle resolves the target with `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:find_persistent_exterior_cell`, the lookup `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:relocate_reference` already uses (`record_flags.cpp:117`), and relocates the record into that CELL's type 8 bucket (`placed_reference_move.cpp:106-111`); no new lookup was added. When the owning group is the world-children GRUP the target is the source CELL, so the record only re-buckets (`:124-127`). A worldspace with no persistent CELL returns `target_cell_missing` and leaves the plugin unchanged, where xEdit creates the CELL (`:14558`; deviation (c) below). That refusal is caller-visible and new in this change: a patch plugin that overrides a grid CELL but does not carry the worldspace's persistent CELL — what `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp:copy_placed_reference_as_override` produces — now fails a move of any persistent reference in it, where the base commit wrote DATA and returned `moved`. `Radicle/src/c_api_writeback.cpp:radicle_plugin_move_placed_ref` reports it as `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` with "plugin has no exterior CELL at the new position; create it first" (`c_api_writeback.cpp:198-199`), so the caller must create CELL[P] first. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_move_exterior.cpp:PlacedReferenceMoveExterior.RefusesAPersistentReferenceWithNoPersistentCellInTheWorldspace`. The source CELL keeps its other references, and the move round-trips through `Radicle/src/plugin/writer.cpp:write_plugin`: `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_move_exterior.cpp:PlacedReferenceMoveExterior.PersistentReferenceUnderAGridCellMovesToThePersistentCell`.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` deviation (f), bucket mismatch in the same cell (closed by this change): xEdit exits only when the group type already matches (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14577-14578`), and otherwise re-buckets within the same CELL (`:14579`). Radicle does the same on both same-CELL paths: the grid branch re-buckets when the bucket type differs (`placed_reference_move.cpp:124-127`) and the `wanted_bucket == 8` branch re-buckets a persistent reference out of a type 9 or 10 bucket of a CELL that already sits beneath the world-children GRUP (`:106-111`, `:124-127`). A move whose bucket already matches commits without touching the hierarchy. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_move_exterior.cpp:PlacedReferenceMoveExterior.SameCellMoveFromTheVisibleDistantBucketRebucketsToTemporary` and `...SameCellMoveWithAMatchingBucketWritesOnlyData`.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` deviation (e), malformed input: no WRLD above the CELL group, an owner group that is neither type 1 nor type 5, or a CELL that is not directly before its child group all throw `PlacedReferenceError`. xEdit exits silently (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14528-14530`, `:14549-14552`, `:14585-14586`). Radicle throws so that the caller sees the refusal, and the plugin is unchanged because the move commits only on success. A CELL with no DATA subrecord is a sub-case: `Radicle/src/plugin/record_edit.hpp:is_interior_cell` returns false when DATA is absent, so Radicle treats the CELL as exterior (`placed_reference_move.cpp:90`). In an interior sub-block (owner type 3), the owner check at `:96-99` throws, where xEdit exits silently (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14533-14537`). Under an exterior owner (type 1 or 5), Radicle applies the grid move (`:112-122`, relocate at `:132-146`), where xEdit exits at `:14533-14537` and leaves the reference in place. xEdit reads the highest override visible to the file (`:14534`), and Radicle does not resolve overrides, so a CELL whose own record has no DATA is treated as exterior even when an override supplies DATA.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` deviation (g), append without sort (still open, kept on purpose): xEdit adds the record and then sorts the target group (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:14616-14618`; `TwbGroupRecord.Sort` at `:18441-18807`). For a group that is not type 7 the sort is `wbMergeSortPtr` over `CompareGroupContents` (`:18793-18794`, `:18311-18435`), whose record key is `SortPriority` (`TwbMainRecord.GetSortPriority`, `:12530-12538`: ROAD and LAND -2, CELL, PGRD and NAVM -1, everything else 0), then the load-order or fixed form ID (`:18398-18401`), then `ElementID` (`:18403`). No in-repo sort key exists for a cell bucket: `Radicle/src/plugin/writer.cpp:write_group` writes children in vector order (`writer.cpp:148-155`), `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_create.cpp:create_placed_reference` appends (`placed_reference_create.cpp:142`), the copy path appends too, and Radicle models neither `SortPriority` nor a form-ID order for bucket records. `Radicle/src/forms/cell_create.cpp:insert_cell` does keep CELL records ascending by form ID inside an exterior sub-block, but that rule is for CELL records, not for the records inside a cell bucket. The record is therefore still appended with `emplace_back` (`placed_reference_move.cpp:145`, `:36`), which keeps create, copy and move in one order, and the reason is recorded here rather than inventing a key.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` deviation (h), type 8 bucket with a clear flag (closed by this change): xEdit chooses CorrectGroupType from the record's own flag (`GetIsPersistent`, `Core/wbImplementation.pas:14518`), picks 9 (`:14522-14523`), and re-buckets the record: within the same CELL when the CELL is not persistent and the grid cell is unchanged (`:14576-14579`), otherwise into the grid CELL at the new position (`:14583-14588`); for an interior CELL it moves the record into the same CELL's type 9 group (`:14595-14596`, `:14601-14617`). The old exemption returned `moved` for every record in a type 8 bucket, whatever its flag. Radicle now decides from the flag (`placed_reference_move.cpp:83-85`), so a type 8 record with a clear flag takes the type 9 path: an interior CELL re-buckets in place (`:90-94`), an exterior CELL whose grid still matches re-buckets in place (`:124-127`), and a position in another grid cell relocates the record (`:132-146`). A type 8 record with the flag set still returns `moved` (`:87-89`). A type 8 record with a clear flag whose new position lands in a grid cell the plugin does not carry now also returns `target_cell_missing` instead of the base commit's `moved`, because it takes the type 9 path and the target lookup runs (`:112-122`; deviation (c) below). That refusal is caller-visible in the same way as (b): `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` with "plugin has no exterior CELL at the new position; create it first" (`c_api_writeback.cpp:198-199`). Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_move_exterior.cpp:PlacedReferenceMoveExterior.PersistentBucketWithAClearFlagRebucketsToTemporary` and `...RefusesAClearFlagRecordInAPersistentBucketWithNoGridCell`.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp:move_reference_to_bucket` (declared in `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy_internal.hpp`): the same-CELL re-bucket used by `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` for deviations (f) and (h), and by `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:relocate_reference` for its same-CELL bucket change. It moves the record out of its bucket, calls `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp:ensure_reference_bucket` with the old bucket's header retyped, which finds or creates the target bucket in the same `cell_children` group, and erases the old bucket when it is empty (`Radicle/src/plugin/record_edit.hpp:erase_if_empty`). Both callers share this one helper. `ensure_reference_bucket` itself was not changed: the target bucket is type 8 or 9, both of which it already accepts, so every existing caller's behaviour is byte-identical. One reachable difference from the base remains, left as is: the retyped header keeps the source bucket's label, and `ensure_reference_bucket` remaps it through `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp:remap_group_header`, which throws `PlacedReferenceError` for a null label. A same-CELL re-bucket out of a bucket whose label is 0 therefore throws where the base commit returned `moved`. That is malformed input only (a valid plugin labels a cell child bucket with its CELL's form ID), fail-closed, and untested. Closing it means passing the CELL key instead of reusing the source label, which is a parameter on both call sites of `move_placed_reference` and a behaviour change on that malformed input; the `record_flags.cpp` caller reuses the label the same way, so the fix belongs in this shared helper. The relocate path cannot reach it, because it always encodes a fresh label.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` status: `moved` means the record stayed in the same CELL and only DATA or the bucket changed; `relocated` means it changed CELL (`placed_reference_move.cpp:88`, `:93`, `:126`, `:146`). A same-CELL re-bucket is therefore `moved`, which keeps `Radicle/src/c_api_writeback.cpp:radicle_plugin_move_placed_ref` reporting `RADICLE_PLACED_MOVE_MOVED` for it (`c_api_writeback.cpp:201-203`), as `Radicle/tests/test_environment_writeback.cpp:WritebackTest.CApiMoveWithinACellReportsMoved` expects.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` transaction: the move works on `auto next = plugin;` and assigns `plugin = std::move(next)` only on success, so `reference_missing`, `target_cell_missing` and every throw leave the caller's plugin unchanged. The setter clears the moved record's `original_range` and `decompressed_payload`, and the move clears `next.original_range`. `Radicle/src/plugin/writer.cpp:write_plugin` then rebuilds the bytes instead of returning the original range (`writer.cpp:323-326`), and the structure fingerprint change recomputes the HEDR record count (`writer.cpp:337-342`).
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_edit.hpp:locate_in_group` and `find_mutable_location` (with `MutableLocation`): the record-tree locator has one definition, shared by `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:set_record_flags` and the move. `Radicle/src/plugin/record_edit.hpp:is_interior_cell` (CELL DATA bit 0) is shared by `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:cell_is_interior` and the move. `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy_internal.hpp:group_header` and `grid_coordinate` (with `k_exterior_cell_span`) are shared with `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_create.cpp`.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/forms/placed_reference.hpp:move_placed_reference`: the `PlacedReferenceMoveStatus` enum and the declaration. The callers of `set_placed_reference_transform` still get DATA-only behavior, and the setter now refuses non-finite values (see the #657 section).
- `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_move.cpp` covers the same-cell move, the cross-cell move with a write and read round trip (`PlacedReferenceMove.CrossCellMoveRelocatesIntoTemporaryGroupAndRoundTrips`), the persistent exterior and interior references, the source CELL keeping its other references (`PlacedReferenceMove.SourceCellKeepsItsOtherReferencesAndBucket`), a type 9 bucket added after a persistent bucket in a grid CELL (`PlacedReferenceMove.TemporaryBucketIsAddedAfterPersistentBucketInGridCell`), a temporary reference in the persistent CELL (`PlacedReferenceMove.TemporaryReferenceInPersistentCellRelocatesToGridCell`), a Y-axis-only move (`PlacedReferenceMove.YAxisOnlyMoveRelocatesIntoNorthCell`), the missing target (`PlacedReferenceMove.MissingTargetCellLeavesPluginUnchanged`), and the negative floor grid (`PlacedReferenceMove.NegativeCoordinatesUseFloorGrid`). That file is at 655 lines and the 750-line guard applies, so the exterior bucket cases are a second translation unit, `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_move_exterior.cpp` (registered in `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt`): a type 8 bucket record with a clear flag re-bucketed into type 9 with its NAME and DATA intact and a write/read round trip (`PlacedReferenceMoveExterior.PersistentBucketWithAClearFlagRebucketsToTemporary`), a same-CELL move out of a type 10 bucket re-bucketed into type 9 (`...SameCellMoveFromTheVisibleDistantBucketRebucketsToTemporary`), a same-CELL move whose bucket already matches writing only DATA, checked byte-for-byte against `set_placed_reference_transform` alone (`...SameCellMoveWithAMatchingBucketWritesOnlyData`), a persistent reference under a grid CELL moved to the worldspace persistent CELL with the source CELL keeping its other reference and a write/read round trip (`...PersistentReferenceUnderAGridCellMovesToThePersistentCell`), and one negative case for each refusal that survives in that file: a record that is not inside a cell bucket, one that is not beneath a cell-children group, one whose CELL record is missing from its parent, an exterior CELL whose owning group is neither a world-children nor an exterior sub-block group, and an exterior CELL with no WRLD record (`PlacedReferenceMoveExterior.Refuses*`). Each of those five asserts the throw and that the serialized plugin is unchanged. Two more pin the `target_cell_missing` status the (b) and (h) paths can now return, where the base commit returned `moved`: a persistent reference in a grid CELL whose worldspace carries no persistent CELL (`...RefusesAPersistentReferenceWithNoPersistentCellInTheWorldspace`) and a clear-flag record in a type 8 bucket moved to a grid cell the plugin does not carry (`...RefusesAClearFlagRecordInAPersistentBucketWithNoGridCell`); both assert the status and that the serialized plugin is unchanged.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_writeback.cpp:radicle_plugin_move_placed_ref`: the C export of `move_placed_reference`, declared in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h` with `radicle_placed_move_status`, ABI 41 on `nomad/602-remaining` (`nomad/dev` used 41 for the asset list exports). `radicle_plugin_set_placed_transform` still never relocates; it rewrites only DATA. The move export is the one that covers relocation into another exterior CELL. `moved` and `relocated` return `RADICLE_STATUS_OK` with `RADICLE_PLACED_MOVE_MOVED` or `RADICLE_PLACED_MOVE_RELOCATED` in the optional `out_status`, which is written only on success. `reference_missing` returns `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` ("plugin has no such record") and `target_cell_missing` returns `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` ("plugin has no exterior CELL at the new position; create it first"). Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_environment_writeback.cpp:WritebackTest.CApiMove*`, and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/WritebackTests.cs:MovesAPlacedReferenceWithinItsCellAndRefusesAMissingTargetCell` for the managed `PluginFile.MoveTransform`.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_writeback.cpp:radicle_plugin_set_placed_transform` follow-up, not done: `move_placed_reference` does have a C ABI export, `Radicle/src/c_api_writeback.cpp:radicle_plugin_move_placed_ref` (`c_api_writeback.cpp:180`, declared in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h:565`, mirrored in the generated `bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs`), with the `target_cell_missing` status mapping described above.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:create_record` then `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:create_exterior_cell` compose for a worldspace this plugin creates itself (the open half of D-29): `create_record` files the WRLD in a top group through `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:find_or_create_top_group` (`Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:create_local_record`), which is what `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:locate_worldspace` requires, and `create_exterior_cell` then adds the `world_children` group through `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:ensure_worldspace_children`, labelled with the new worldspace's form ID, plus the block and subblock groups. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_exterior_cell_creation.cpp` (`ExteriorCellCreation.CreatesAnExteriorCellInAWorldspaceMadeByCreateRecord`), on a header-only plugin: the same call before the worldspace exists throws `CellError` and consumes no form ID (negative control), the created WRLD takes `000800`, the exterior CELL takes `000801` at x 5, y -7, the `world_children` group carries label `0x00000800`, `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:find_exterior_cell` finds the cell, and the WRLD and the cell both survive a write and read. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).
## Placed reference transform refuses non-finite values (#657)
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference.cpp:set_placed_reference_transform` refuses a NaN or infinite position or rotation with `PlacedReferenceError` ("placed-reference values must be finite"). The check runs after the missing-record (`false`), signature and `require_decodable` checks, and before any DATA write. The write works on a copy that is assigned back only on success, so a refusal leaves the caller's plugin unchanged.
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_move.cpp:move_placed_reference` calls the setter first, so a non-finite position throws before the grid logic and never reaches deviation (d).
- `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_create.cpp:create_placed_reference` calls the setter on its copy after the new REFR is staged, so the throw leaves the plugin unchanged.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_writeback.cpp:radicle_plugin_set_placed_transform` maps the throw to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` through `placed_error`.
- `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginCell.cpp:RadiclePluginBackend::setPlacedReferenceTransform` reports it as `PlacedTransformWriteFailed`, and `RadiclePluginBackend::createPlacedObject` as `PlacedReferenceCreateFailed`. Both catch `std::exception` and stage the mutated plugin only after the call returns.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:undelete_and_disable_reference` re-sets the transform decoded from a deleted reference's stored DATA (`:176`). A non-finite x, y, rx, ry or rz in that stored DATA now throws `PlacedReferenceError` on undelete, where it used to be rewritten. `z` is replaced with `k_undelete_z` first, so a non-finite z alone is still accepted. The plugin is unchanged, because `plugin = std::move(next)` is the last step.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_move.cpp:PlacedReferenceMove.RefusesNonFiniteTransform` (NaN and infinity in x, plugin bytes unchanged), `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_create.cpp:PlacedReferenceCreate.RefusesNonFiniteTransform`, and `PluginEditTool/native/tests/unit/RadiclePluginExteriorCellTests.cpp:PluginEditTool createPlacedObject refuses malformed arguments without staging` (its `1e39` row, an interior CELL, so the setter check is what refuses it). No test pins the undelete refusal.
## Record-level checks (#602 WP-13 D-15)

- `Radicle/src/graph/check_errors_records.cpp:check_record_levels`: per selected plugin, appended to `check_load_order` after `check_preflight`. It follows xEdit `TwbMainRecord.GetCheck` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas` at `93cc0bc5`, lines 11054-11138), which returns one message per record, so the first matching rule wins in this order: light overflow, master index past the table, deleted content, partial-form content. Severity is per finding; xEdit has no severity levels except its `Warning:` prefix.
- `deleted_record_content` (error, `Record marked as deleted, but contains: ...`): xEdit lines 11101-11118 skip the header element and, for `IsReference` definitions (`wbInterface.pas`, `rdfIsReference`; FO4 set is ACHR, REFR and the eight `ReferenceRecord` rows at `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5944-5951`), any NAME (`ksrBaseRecord`). `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:is_placed_reference_signature` is the same ten-signature set. The base-record rule matches `Radicle/src/plugin/record_flags.cpp:mark_override_deleted`, which keeps NAME only for placed references, and `xEdit TwbMainRecord.Delete` (`wbImplementation.pas:10321-10373`). Error, as in xEdit. The shipped DLC masters carry three such records in `DLCCoast.esm` (one CELL, one REFR, one PKIN), which xEdit also reports; `Fallout4.esm` has none.
- `partial_form_content` (error, `Record is Partial Form, but contains: ...`): xEdit lines 11121-11138 allow only EDID, the header element, and any def flagged `dfDontSave` (line 11130). The allowed set is `Radicle/src/graph/check_errors_records.cpp:k_partial_allowed` (EDID, INOM, INOA). In FO4 the only `dfDontSave` defs that can sit in a partial-capable record are INOM and INOA, members of DIAL (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6473-6474`, defined in `wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8604-8626`, flag at 8610 and 8621). No CELL, QUST or WRLD member carries the flag. Other `dfDontSave` uses in the pinned source are Starfield-only (`wbDefinitionsSF1.pas:5643, 12408, 18335`). Flags inherit upward (`wbInterface.pas:731`), but INOM and INOA are direct members of DIAL, so nothing else picks the flag up. Partial-capable records are `CELL`, `DIAL`, `QUST`, `WRLD` (the `Partial Form` flag at `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5957, 6311, 10686, 13112`, and `TwbMainRecordDef.CanBePartial` at `wbInterface.pas:10542`). That set matches `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/container.hpp:is_partial_form`, and bit 14 (`0x4000`) matches `Radicle/include/fo4/flags.hpp:RecordFlags::partial_form` and `TwbMainRecordStructFlags.IsPartialForm` (`wbInterface.pas:20450`). Error, as in xEdit. The shipped DLC masters carry six QUST records with the flag and a VMAD: one in `DLCRobot.esm`, one in `DLCCoast.esm`, four in `DLCNukaWorld.esm`, which xEdit also reports; `Fallout4.esm` has none. A deleted record is never checked for partial content (xEdit's deleted branch returns first).
- `light_object_id_overflow` (error, `ObjectID 001000 is invalid for a light module`): xEdit lines 11087-11090 flag `ObjectID > $FFF` when the plugin has the light flag and the record's fixed file ID is this plugin. The flag is TES4 bit `0x200` (`wbInterface.pas:TwbMainRecordStructFlags.IsLight`, 20415, FO4 uses bit 9; `Radicle/include/fo4/flags.hpp:RecordFlags::small_file`). The ObjectID limit is `k_light_local_mask` (`0xFFF`, as used by `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:local_form_id_range`), the ceiling in the light-plugin range note under `Radicle/docs/`. The check uses the stored 24-bit local, as xEdit's object ID getter (`wbInterface.pas`, `GetObjectID`, line 22170) does for a non-light-slot ID. Vanilla: 0 findings across the nine shipped `.esl` plugins (every own record checked by survey).
- `internal_form_id_mismatch` (warning, because xEdit prefixes this message with `Warning:`, `Core/wbImplementation.pas:11093`): xEdit's `HITME` branch (lines 11092-11093), with the fixed-ID routine (`wbImplementation.pas:9759`) mapping a stored master index at or past the MAST count to this plugin's own file ID. Radicle implements only the case where the stored index is above the master count: `resolve_plugin_form_id` throws for it, so `Radicle/src/plugin/reader.cpp:assign_record_form_keys` leaves the record key empty. The finding names the plugin's own key. Vanilla: 0 across the seven masters and nine `.esl` plugins. Not reproduced: xEdit's second `HITME` path, where an ID below `0x800` in a plugin without the hardcoded range (`TwbFile.GetAllowHardcodedRangeUse`, lines 4070-4090) gets a null file ID, so a non-zero stored index reads as a mismatch. Radicle's `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:allows_hardcoded_range` covers the record-allocation side, not this warning.
- Not implemented, update-module new records: xEdit gates `TwbFile.GetIsUpdate` and `TwbMainRecordStructFlags.IsUpdate` (`wbInterface.pas:20425`) on `wbIsUpdateSupported` (`wbInterface.pas:5288`), which is false for FO4. `wbHasAddedUpdateSupport` is set only for FO4VR with the VRESL DLL (`xEdit/xeInit.pas:1100-1103`), and `-PseudoUpdate` (`xeInit.pas:1443`) is a debug switch. Radicle has no update-flag reading to match, so this rule does not fire for FO4 in xEdit and is not implemented. Medium: `wbIsMediumSupported` (`wbInterface.pas:5278`) is false for FO4, so no medium ObjectID check.
- Not implemented, internal versus fixed for Starfield or Morrowind: `wbIsMorrowind` and the complex FileFileID mode (`xeInit.pas:1116`, SF1 only) do not apply to FO4, so the HITME rule is taken as FO4 only.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_check_errors.cpp:DeletedRecordContentIsFlaggedExceptReferenceBaseRecord`, `PartialFormContentOtherThanEditorIdIsFlagged`, `LightPluginObjectIdAboveTwelveBitsIsInvalid`, `MasterIndexPastMasterTableIsInternalMismatch`, `CodeNamesAreStable`. Each new check has a positive and a negative record in its test. The existing `VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings` runs only on `Fallout4.esm`, which has no findings of the new kinds.
- Consumers of `CheckCode` checked with the four new values: `Radicle/src/c_api_check.cpp` and `Radicle/tools/inspect/main.cpp` use `check_code_name` only; `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginCheck.cpp` uses `check_code_name` only; `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginAnalysis.cpp` names two codes. There is no `switch` over `CheckCode` outside `check_code_name`, so `-Wswitch` covers its new cases only through that switch.
## Create defaults (#602 WP-9)

`create_with_rules` (`Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:create_with_rules`) walks the rules in order and stops at the first failure: a minimum-1 rule that is not `editable` returns `not_authorable`, and one with no usable default returns `no_default`. Before this batch the first failing rule was NPC_ RNAM, HAZD OBND, IMAD DNAM, ADDN DNAM, DOBJ DNAM, MESG DESC and LSCR DESC (all `no_default`), or DEBR DATA (`not_authorable`: maximum 65535 without `uncounted`). HAZD MODL and MODT are minimum 0 (see the HAZD OBND, MODL, MODT bullet below), so HAZD create no longer stops there and succeeds. Defaults follow the repo rule: xEdit native or edit defaults where xEdit declares them (`SetDefaultEditValue` and `SetDefaultNativeValue`), otherwise zero bytes at the xEdit size. Corpus counts come from a read-only scan of the seven official masters at form version 131 unless marked otherwise. Localized DESC keeps refusing defaults in localized plugins (`Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:default_usable`).

- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_ RNAM and CNAM: `00000000` each, a null form ID. xEdit `form-link (RNAM, 'Race', [RACE]).SetRequired` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10370) and `form-link (CNAM, 'Class', [CLAS], ...)` (:10406) have no default. Corpus 4 bytes in 4369 of 4369. A null required link is the existing MESG INAM convention (`form-link (INAM, 'Icon (unused)', [NULL]).SetRequired`, :8182, default `00000000`). A created NPC_ has no race or class until the author sets one.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_ NAM6 and NAM8: `00000000` each (f32 0.0 and u32 sound level 0). xEdit `wbFloat(NAM6, 'Height Min')` (:10423) and `wbInteger(NAM8, 'Sound Level', itU32, ...)` (:10431) have no default. Corpus 4 bytes in 4369 of 4369.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_ NAM5: `0000`, 2 bytes. xEdit `wbUnknown(NAM5, cpNormal, True)` (:10422) has no size or default. Corpus 2 bytes in 4369 of 4369.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_ DATA: empty (0 bytes). xEdit `wbEmpty(DATA, 'Marker', cpNormal, True)` (:10409) is a required marker with no payload. Corpus 0 bytes in 4369 of 4369. It needs a zero-length default, which the codegen and `has_default` now accept (see the last two bullets).
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:HAZD DNAM: 52 bytes, Target Interval f32 0.3 at offset 16 (`9a99993e`), all else zero. `wbStruct(DNAM, 'Data', ...)` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7186, `SetRequired` at the end of the struct) has Limit, Radius, Lifetime, Image Space Radius, Target Interval (`SetDefaultEditValue('0.3')`, :7191), Flags, Effect, Light, Impact Data Set, Sound and three taper floats. Radicle's rows reach offset 48. Corpus 52 bytes in 78 of 78.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:HAZD OBND, MODL, MODT: OBND 12 zero bytes (`wbObjectBounds`, corpus 12 in 78 of 78). MODL and MODT are minimum 0 because xEdit's `wbGenericModel` is not required for HAZD: HAZD calls it with no argument (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7184), and its `aRequired` parameter defaults to False (:1030-1046). MODL stays `coupled`, so `editable` is false and no path adds or removes it. MODL has no default, since create skips minimum-0 rules and add is refused for a coupled rule. MODT keeps its empty default (0 bytes, zero texture hashes; `wbModelInfo` at Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8918 is variable-size) because add of MODT still reads it. Corpus (seven masters): 78 HAZD records, all 78 with MODL and all 78 with MODT, so the corpus does not show the absent case and the minimum rests on the xEdit definition. HAZD create now succeeds with EDID, OBND (12 zero bytes) and DNAM (52 bytes), pinned by `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:HazdCreateAuthorsEdidObndDnamWithoutModel`. ANIO's MODL stays coupled (ANIO entry).
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD DNAM: 252 bytes at form version 131 (`wbFromVersion(116, ...)` on Vignette Radius and Strength, Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7523-7525). Corpus: 252 bytes at every form version 116 and up (50 records at 131) and 244 at 109 and 113 (49 records). Kept from the xEdit edit defaults: Duration 1.0 at offset 4 and Radial Blur Center X and Y 0.5 at offsets 204 and 208. Tint Color (176) and Fade Color (236) are 2, matching the two-element TNAM and NAM3 created by default. Deviation from xEdit's edit defaults: xEdit gives every other count 2 (Blur Radius 180, Double Vision 184, Radial Blur Strength 188, Ramp Up 192, Start 196, Ramp Down 228, Down Start 232, Motion Blur 240, Vignette Radius 244, Vignette Strength 248). These are 0 here, because the arrays they count (BNAM, VNAM, RNAM, SNAM, UNAM, NAM1, NAM2, NAM4, and the optional NAM5 and NAM6 at Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7543-7544) are optional and not created, so a count of 2 would describe two elements that do not exist. Corpus evidence (read-only scan, 269 IMAD records): each of BNAM, VNAM, RNAM, SNAM, UNAM, NAM1, NAM2 and NAM4 is present in 269 of 269 records, and its count equals its element count (8-byte pairs) in 269 of 269. NAM5 and NAM6 are present in 217 of the 220 records that carry the field, with the count equal to the element count in 217 of 217. In the other 3 records NAM5 or NAM6 is absent but the count is nonzero, so the corpus does not show a 0 for an absent array in every case. Depth of Field (212, 216, 220) and the HDR and Cinematic pairs (8 to 172) have no xEdit default and are not checked here; they stay 0.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD TNAM and NAM3: two zero-filled color interpolators of 20 bytes each, 40 bytes per list: time 0 and time 1, RGB 1, A 0 (`000000000000803f0000803f0000803f000000000000803f0000803f0000803f0000803f00000000`). `wbArray(TNAM, 'Tint Color', wbColorInterpolator).SetRequired` and `wbArray(NAM3, 'Fade Color', ...)` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7530-7531) have no xEdit default. `wbColorInterpolator` (Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8199) is an f32 Time plus four f32 RGBA values, 20 bytes per element. The two-element form is a corpus majority, not an xEdit default: TNAM equals these 40 bytes in 164 of 269 records and NAM3 in 216 of 269. Corpus Tint Color (176) equals TNAM/20 in 269 of 269 records, and Fade Color (236) equals NAM3/20 in 269 of 269. The test `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:CreatesRecordsWhoseRequiredSubrecordsHaveAuthoredDefaults` expects 40 bytes for both.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LSCR DESC: `00`, 1 byte. `wbDESCReq` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9952) is localized, so the default applies only in a non-localized plugin (test `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:LocalizedDescriptionsStillRefuseCreateDefaults`). An empty zstring is one byte, the same as BOOK DESC `00`. Corpus 4 bytes (string ID) in 448 of 448 records.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MESG DESC and DNAM: DESC `00` (localized, as LSCR). DNAM `00000000`: u32 flags, `wbInteger(DNAM, 'Flags', itU32, wbFlags(...))` (:8184-8189) has no default and is required. Corpus 4 bytes in 1990 of 1990 for both. MESG INAM already had `00000000`.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ADDN DNAM: `00000000`, 4 bytes (u16 cap, u16 flags). `wbStruct(DNAM, 'Data', ...)` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7805, `SetRequired` at :7813) has no default. Corpus 4 bytes in 369 of 369. ADDN DATA keeps its existing xEdit default `1c010000` (284, `SetDefaultEditValue('284')` at :7802).
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:DEBR DATA: `000000` (3 bytes) and `uncounted: true`. `wbRArray('Models', wbDebrisModel(...))` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7390) repeats a DATA struct (Percentage u8, Model FileName zstring, Has Collision u8; Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8466-8478) with no count subrecord, which is what `uncounted` marks. Without it `editable` is false and create returns `not_authorable`. The zero default is one `00` byte percentage, an empty zstring, and a zero collision flag. Corpus DATA entries are 40 bytes (23 entries) or 33 bytes (8 entries) across the five DEBR records, with 4 to 11 entries in each record.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:DOBJ DNAM: 8 zero bytes, one `Use` u32 plus one `Object ID` form ID, which is one element of `wbArrayS(DNAM, 'Objects', wbStructSK([0], ...))` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8620, `SetRequired` at :8626). xEdit has no default. Corpus has one record with 3168 bytes (396 elements of 8). One zero element matches the existing unit fixture (8 zero bytes).
- Radicle/tools/record_schema_codegen.py:parse_default and render: an empty `default` string is accepted and rendered as a one-byte array `[1] = {0x00}` with size 0, because C++ has no zero-size array. Used by NPC_ DATA and HAZD MODT, both zero-length.
- Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:SubrecordAuthoringConstraint::has_default: now `default_data != nullptr`, so a zero-byte default counts as present. Rules without a `default` still get `nullptr` from the generator, so the existing defaults (FACT, FLOR, KEYM and others) keep their behaviour.
- Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:remove_with_rules: the guard returns `unknown_order` only when the target is a repeated entry (`rules[*target].maximum > 1`) and some existing subrecord has no authoring rule. It runs after the `absent` and `below_minimum` checks and before the erase. Reason: DEBR DATA is `uncounted` (so `editable`) and repeated, and each DATA is followed by a MODT with no DEBR rule (corpus DATA entries 4 to 11 per record), so erasing one DATA would leave its MODT on the previous entry. A singleton removal cannot orphan a sibling and stays allowed: INFO ONAM, ALFA, GREE, TIQS and INCC and SCEN VNAM, XNAM and NNAM are all singletons. INFO response groups and SCEN groups stay unlisted on purpose. Test `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:RemoveRefusesDebrDataWhoseModelTextureHasNoRule`. Not run: the real-data sound test `Radicle/tests/test_sound_writer_real.cpp` (repeated ANAM removal) if it picks one of the 24 corpus SNDR records with unlisted FNAM, INTV, ITME and ITMS.
- Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/subrecord_authoring.hpp:SubrecordRemoveStatus: `unknown_order` is appended last so the existing values keep their numbers. Consumers updated: `Radicle/src/c_api_authoring.cpp:radicle_plugin_remove_subrecord` (maps to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, as the add mapping does) and `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginElement.cpp:authoringStatusError` (`ElementUnknownOrder`). No C ABI enum mirror or managed mirror of this enum exists in the worktree; the C ABI reports status codes, not this enum.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD RStructs: xEdit marks the Radial Blur, Depth of Field, HDR and Cinematic groups `.SetRequired` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7538 for Radial Blur, which spans 7532-7538; :7545 for Depth of Field, 7539-7545; :7565 for HDR, 7547-7565; :7571 for Cinematic, 7566-7571). Our IMAD authoring rules keep their members at minimum 0: RNAM, SNAM, UNAM, NAM1 and NAM2 in Radial Blur, WNAM, XNAM and YNAM in Depth of Field, NAM5 and NAM6 (optional Vignette lists, :7543-7544), and the HDR and Cinematic `@IAD` lists. A created IMAD omits all of them, so xEdit may report it as incomplete. Corpus (269 IMAD records): WNAM, XNAM, YNAM, RNAM, SNAM, UNAM, NAM1 and NAM2 are each present in 269 of 269, and the Radial Blur set of five and the Depth of Field group are complete in every record. Not changed: raising these minimums would need a default for each member and is a lead decision.

## Version-gated IMAD, MOVT and ENCH rows (#602 WP-11)

- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD\VignetteRadius and IMAD\VignetteStrength: u32 rows at DNAM offsets 244 and 248 with `min_form_version` 116, from `wbFromVersion(116, ...)` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7523-7526). Corpus: DNAM is 244 bytes in 49 records at versions 109 and 113, and 252 bytes in all 220 records at 116 to 131. The rows are hidden at 113 and readable and writable at 116. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_scalar_embedded.cpp:ImageAdapterVignetteRowsAreGatedByFormVersion116`.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD (the 58 fixed DNAM rows, offsets 0 to 240): every offset and storage type matches the struct at Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7468-7527. `wbIMADMultAddCount` is two u32 values, 8 bytes (Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8208-8222). HDR (:7471-7489, 17 pairs) therefore runs from 8 to 144, Cinematic (:7490-7495, 4 pairs) from 144 to 176, Tint Color is at 176 and Motion Blur Strength at 240. No row sits past 244 without a gate.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD\HDR<Member>MultInterpolators, IMAD\HDR<Member>MultTime, IMAD\HDR<Member>MultValue and the four IMAD\Cinematic<Member>Mult* rows: 63 rows (21 counted arrays, each with a Time and a Value member) over the 21 control-byte subrecords `\x00IAD` to `\x14IAD`. xEdit declares one mult count pair per slot in the HDR struct (17 slots, Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7471-7489, eight named and nine `Unused`) and in the Cinematic struct (4 slots, :7490-7495), each `wbIMADMultAddCount` = two u32 counts, 8 bytes (Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8208-8222). Slot order is the struct order, so the named rows are Eye Adapt Speed 0x00, Bloom Blur Radius 0x01, Bloom Threshold 0x02, Scale 0x03, Target Lum Min 0x04, Target Lum Max 0x05, Sunlight Scale 0x06, Sky Scale 0x07, 0x08 to 0x10 unused, then Saturation 0x11, Brightness 0x12, Contrast 0x13 and Unused 0x14. Each row is stride 8, Time f32 at 0 and Value f32 at 4, with `insertion: existing_only` because the count lives in the DNAM pair and a count of 0 already means "use the add list", so a row must not create the subrecord. Previously unexpressible: `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:valid_signature` and `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:valid_signature` rejected any signature byte below 0x20, and both generators rendered every signature through `Signature::from_string`. `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:cpp_signature` now renders a non-printable signature as `Signature::from_bytes(0x44414900u)`, while the length and byte-range checks stay, so a short or over-0xFF signature is still rejected (`Radicle/tools/test_field_address_codegen.py:ControlByteSignatureTests`). Corpus (Fallout4.esm, read by the test): 247 IMAD records, every one carrying `\x00IAD` with 2 elements, 494 in total, counts equal to element counts. The record at 0x24A3C4 decodes Time 0 and Value 1. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_image_fx_records.cpp:ImageFxSynthetic.HdrMultInterpolatorRowsDecodeAndEditOneStrideElement` (2 elements decoded, one value written at index 1 and re-read, index 2 and an absent subrecord both `subrecord_missing` with the plugin bytes unchanged, the neighbouring `@IAD` add list untouched) and `Radicle/tests/test_image_fx_records_real.cpp:ImageFxRecordsReal.EveryImadRecordDecodesTheHdrMultInterpolatorRows`. Regression caught: before these rows every IMAD\HDR*Mult* path was unknown, so a plugin that edited an add list left the mult list of the same pair unreadable and uneditable.
- Element-count source and names for the IMAD mult rows, re-checked against the pin: the count of each bank is the DNAM pair, not a field inside the subrecord. `wbIMADMultAddCount` is `wbStruct(aName, [wbInteger('Mult Count', itU32), wbIntegeR('Add Count', itU32)])` (Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8208-8222), so the mult count is the low word of each 8-byte slot and the add count the high word. The pair order is the struct order: HDR slots 0x00 to 0x10 at Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7547-7564 and Cinematic slots 0x11 to 0x14 at :7566-7570, each `wbTimeInterpolatorsMultAdd(sigMult, sigAdd, name)` (:9282-9302), and each bank is `wbTimeInterpolators` = `wbArray(..., wbTimeInterpolator)` of `wbStructSK([0], 'Data', [wbFloat('Time'), wbFloat('Value')])`, 8 bytes (Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8312-8338). The names are xEdit's: Eye Adapt Speed, Bloom Blur Radius, Bloom Threshold, Scale, Target Lum Min, Target Lum Max, Sunlight Scale, Sky Scale, then nine `Unused` slots and Saturation, Brightness, Contrast, Unused. The rows spell `Scale` as `HDRBloomScale` and the unused slots as `HDRUnused8` to `HDRUnused16`, because the add-bank rows of #623 already used those paths and renaming them would break callers. Measured over the seven official masters (read-only scan, 269 IMAD records): every record carries all 21 mult subrecords and all 21 add subrecords; every Mult Count equals its mult subrecord's element count and every Add Count its add subrecord's, 269 of 269 records for all 21 slots, 0 mismatches, and no subrecord size is a non-multiple of 8 (mult totals run 538 to 577 elements per slot, add 538 to 670). Test: `Radicle/tests/test_image_fx_records_real.cpp:ImageFxRecordsReal.ImadMultAndAddCountsMatchTheDnamPairs` asserts the agreement for every slot of every `Fallout4.esm` IMAD record (247 records, 5,187 pairs, 0 missing, 0 odd sizes, 0 mismatches) and the 494 elements of slot 0x00. Unverified: that the nine HDR `Unused` slots and the Cinematic `Unused` slot have no engine meaning (xEdit names them `Unused`, and their counts match slot 0x00's 538 elements, which is consistent but not proof), and that the two floats are consumed in Time-then-Value order by the renderer (xEdit's member order only).
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD authoring DNAM default (252 bytes): not changed. xEdit sets default '2' on Blur Radius (:7497), Double Vision (:7498), Radial Blur Strength (:7499), Ramp Up (:7500), Start (:7501), Ramp Down (:7519), Down Start (:7520), Motion Blur (:7522) and both Vignette rows (:7524, :7526). The default has 0 at offsets 180, 184, 188, 192, 196, 228, 232, 240, 244 and 248, while Tint Color (176) and Fade Color (236) are 2. Defaults are authoring policy, so this is a lead decision.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MOVT\DirectionalThreshold, MOVT\MovementSpeedThreshold and MOVT\RotationSpeedThreshold (INAM at 0, 4, 8), MOVT\FloatHeight (JNAM 0) and MOVT\FlightAngleGain (LNAM 0): offsets match xEdit (`wbStruct(INAM)` at Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9397-9401, `wbFloat(JNAM)` :9402, `wbFloat(LNAM)` :9403), and xEdit has no version condition on any of them. Corpus: INAM is 12 bytes in 21 records at versions 31 to 102 and absent in 82, including every record from 105 on. JNAM is 4 bytes in 95 records (67 to 131) and LNAM 4 bytes in 88 (98 to 131). Absence already reads as `subrecord_missing`, so no gate was added.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MOVT (SPED has no rows): `wbSPED` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9147-9355) is chosen by `wbFormVersionDecider([28, 60, 104])` (Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:5590-5612): arm 0 below 28, arm 1 for 28 to 59, arm 2 for 60 to 103, arm 3 from 104. The arms are 40, 44, 68 and 112 bytes, because `wbUnused` is zero-size (Core/wbInterface.pas:7951-7956, `wbEmpty` with `TwbEmptyDef.GetSize` at :20335-20338).
