Corpus: 40 bytes in 1 record (v24), 44 in 5 (v31 to 55), 68 in 16 (v60 to 102), 112 in 81 (v105 to 131), 103 MOVT records in all. Left Walk is at offset 0 in arms 0 to 2 and at 4 in arm 3, which also adds Standing and Sprint. Per-arm rows would be new coverage, so SPED is deferred.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ENCH\Cost, ENCH\Flags, ENCH\CastType, ENCH\Amount, ENCH\TargetType, ENCH\EnchantType and ENCH\ChargeTime: `payload_size` 36 became `minimum_payload_size` 28. xEdit's ENIT (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6730-6747) holds these seven scalars at offsets 0 to 24, which end at 28. xEdit has no version condition on ENIT. Corpus: ENIT is 36 bytes in all 416 records, at versions 54 to 131 (357 at 131). Test: `Radicle/tests/test_scalar_embedded.cpp:EnchEnitShortFormsReadOnlyTheMembersXEditReadsCleanly`.
- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ENCH\BaseEnchantment: `payload_sizes` went from [36] to [32, 36]. `SetOptionalFrom(8)` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6747) makes only member 8, Worn Restrictions (offset 32), optional. Base Enchantment is member 7 at offset 28 and is required, so the shortest ENIT xEdit reads cleanly is 32 bytes. A 28-byte ENIT is not that form, because the required member runs past the payload (Core/wbImplementation.pas:22588-22603 marks only members from the optional index as missing). What xEdit shows for 28 bytes is not verified, since no xEdit run was made. ENCH\WornRestrictions stays at [36]. A link write on a payload whose size is not in `payload_sizes` throws `schema::FormLinkFieldError` (`Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots`, throw at :132) instead of returning `subrecord_missing`, so a 28-byte ENIT throws for both links and a 32-byte ENIT throws for Worn Restrictions. The target-type check in `set_record_formlink_field` (:399) runs before it, so the test writes Worn Restrictions with a local FLST target and checks the message names the payload size. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_scalar_embedded.cpp:EnchEnitShortFormsReadOnlyTheMembersXEditReadsCleanly`.
- Radicle/tools/record_schema_codegen.py:parse_default: an authoring default is checked against each subrecord's `payload_size` (exact) and now also against the largest `minimum_payload_size` of its rows. Without this, the ENIT default (36 bytes) would no longer be checked once the ENCH scalars moved to `minimum_payload_size` 28. A default shorter than that minimum is rejected.
- Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:main and Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:main regenerated `include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc` and `generated_formlink_lists.inc`. Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py:main regenerated `docs/FO4_PARITY.md` (IMAD scalar rows 58 to 60).

## NIF geometry, skin and shader C ABI

- Radicle/include/fo4/nif/nif.hpp:Shape: gained `weights`, `bone_indices`, `bones`,
  `material` and `textures`; `bitangents` is now filled instead of empty. `Bone` holds
  the name plus the `BSSkinBoneTrans` fields in storage order, and `Shader` holds the
  property block, its shader type, its name, its texture set reference and the set's
  slots. `read_shader` and `read_bones` are the two new entry points; `docs/NIF.md`
  pins both layouts and the evidence for them.
- Radicle/src/nif/geometry.cpp:read_vertex: the byte layout follows
  `nif.xml:BSVertexData`, so the two bytes the reader used to skip after a position are
  Bitangent X (float at full precision, `hfloat` at half precision) and the fourth byte
  of the normal and tangent fields are Bitangent Y and Z. The bitangent is stored, not
  reconstructed, and is emitted only when bits 3 and 4 are both set, which keeps it at
  exactly three floats per vertex. `read_shape` now follows the shader reference and the
  skin reference; both are range-checked and an out-of-range reference is a
  `parse_error`, while a reference to a different block type is tolerated the way
  `NifShape.cs` tolerates it.
- Radicle/src/nif/shader.cpp:read_shader: reads only `BSLightingShaderProperty` and stops
  after the texture set reference. The leading u32 is read as `Shader Type` because the
  shader-type tail follows it, even though `nif.xml`'s version condition for that
  NiObjectNET field excludes BS 130; the corpus decides, and all 1,111,752
  material-bearing vanilla shapes read a `.bgsm` name at the offset that implies. The
  conditional tail is deliberately not read, so no format guess there can fail a file.
- Radicle/src/nif/skin.cpp:read_bones: `BSSkin::Instance` then `BSSkin::BoneData`, 68
  bytes per `BSSkinBoneTrans`. The tolerance rules match `NifShape.cs:ReadSkin`: an
  absent or mistyped data reference keeps the names and leaves the transforms at their
  defaults, while a bone count that disagrees with the skin's bone count is a
  `parse_error` (skin.cpp:read_bones, see the skin entry under NIF node hierarchy,
  stricter skin and DDS edges). Bone names go through a tolerant name lookup equivalent
  to `NifFile.cs:NameOf`, so a stale node reference yields an empty name instead of a
  parse error.
- Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_nif.h and Radicle/src/c_api_nif.cpp: the `radicle_nif_*`
  surface. A handle is opened from bytes because assets arrive through GameData and the
  resolver. Shapes are decoded once at open. Empty arrays are `OK` with a NULL pointer
  and a count of 0, floats come back with `radicle_free_floats`, triangle indices with
  `radicle_free_triangles`, and every byte array with `radicle_free_bytes`.
- Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/NifFile.cs: `NifFile.FromBytes` snapshots every
  shape into managed arrays and destroys the native handle before it returns, so the
  wrapper holds no native state and cannot leak. `Radicle.Interop` declares its own
  `Vector3` record for record payloads, so the geometry types are reached through a
  `Numerics` namespace alias; the exposed types are `System.Numerics` ones, which is what
  BGS's `NifShape` uses.
- Verified: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_nif.cpp` (ten tests over `tests/nif_fixture.hpp`) and
  `Radicle/tests/test_nif.cpp` cover the fixture, `Radicle/tests/test_nif_corpus.cpp` covers
  the vanilla corpus (226,454 NIFs, 1,207,017 shapes, 23,595 skinned shapes, 169,498 bones,
  0 parse failures, every weight count and every bone index in range), and a throwaway
  harness outside the repository compared BGS's `NifGeometry` against `NifFile.FromBytes`
  on `MaleBody.nif`, `FemaleBody.nif`, `1stPersonFemaleBody.nif` and `RadRoach.nif`: all 8
  skinned shapes agree on the skinned verdict, every bone name, every bind matrix, every
  weight and every bone index.

## DDS pixel decode

- Radicle/src/texture/bcn.cpp is PluginEditTool's bcdec port, moved unchanged apart from
  its namespace, its two entry points and a thrown `dds_error` instead of a returned one.
  Radicle/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md carries the attribution. PluginEditTool still holds its
  own copy; pointing it at `fo4::texture` is the follow-up recorded in that file.
- Radicle/src/texture/dds_codec.cpp parses the container (legacy FourCC and DX10) and
  sizes mips; Radicle/src/texture/dds.cpp decodes one mip into RGBA8, unpacks the
  uncompressed layouts and reconstructs Z for BC5. `docs/TEXTURES.md` lists the formats,
  the header fields and the evidence.
- Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_dds.h exposes `radicle_dds_decode_rgba` and `radicle_dds_info`;
  `DdsImage` is the managed wrapper.
- Radicle/src/c_api_dds.cpp:map_dds_error: every `dds_error` except `TooLarge` maps to
  `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR`, so a caller cannot tell an unsupported format (BC6H,
  BC4/BC5 SNORM, an unknown DXGI code) from a corrupt file except by the message text.
- Radicle/src/texture/dds_codec.cpp:DdsInfo::mip_offset: mip N of a volume texture is not
  supported correctly. DDS stores every depth slice of a mip in turn, but `mip_size` and
  `mip_offset` count one slice, so the offset of mip 1 and up is wrong when depth is above
  1, and mip 0 decodes only the first slice.
- Radicle/src/texture/dds_codec.cpp:DdsInfo::mip_size and Radicle/src/texture/dds.cpp:decode_dds_rgba:
  the mip shift is clamped to 31 because `read_dds` accepts up to 255 mips and a shift of 32
  or more is undefined. A 16-bit dimension is already 0 after a shift of 16, floored to 1, so
  the clamp changes no size.

## NIF node hierarchy, stricter skin and DDS edges

- Radicle/include/fo4/nif/nif.hpp:Node and NifFile::nodes: every node block the
  reader understands is kept once, in block order, with its block index, block type,
  `NiObjectNET` name, parent as a node-list index (-1 for a root), children as the
  block indices the file stores, and its local `NiAVObject` transform.
  `NifFile::node_for_block` maps a block to that list (or -1), and
  `fo4::nif::shape_parent_node` gives a shape's nearest node ancestor.
  `Shape` gained `parent_node` and `warning`.
- Radicle/src/nif/nif.cpp: the node loop that already read the child lists now also
  fills `nodes_` and the block-to-node map, and resolves each node's parent through
  it. The prefix is the one `nif.xml` gives BS 130: `NiObjectNET` name, extra-data
  list, controller; `NiAVObject` flags as a u32 (`#BSVER# #GT# 26`), translation,
  3x3 rotation, scale, collision reference; then the children list. `Effects` is
  gated on `#NI_BS_LT_FO4#`, so FO4 has none, which the corpus confirms: all
  896,993 node blocks of 226,177 vanilla NIFs end exactly at the children list.
  The sixteen-entry node allowlist is unchanged and now proven by the corpus
  histogram in `docs/NIF.md`; `BSFurnitureMarkerNode` is the only vanilla block
  whose name contains `Node` and is not one, and `nif.xml` says why
  (`inherit="BSFurnitureMarker"`), as does its own bytes.
- Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_nif.h, Radicle/src/c_api_nif.cpp: `radicle_nif_node_*`
  (count, block, type, name, parent, children, transform, for-block) plus
  `radicle_nif_shape_parent_node` and `radicle_nif_shape_warning`, and
  `radicle_free_node_refs` for the child array. Children are block indices because
  the file stores those and a child may be a shape; `node_for_block` turns one into
  a node index when it is a node. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` took 52 (#706), bumped from 51.
- Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/NifFile.cs: `NifNode` with
  `ParentIndex`/`Parent`, `ChildBlocks` and `Children` (null where a child is not a
  node), `LocalMatrix` and `WorldMatrix`, `NifShape.ParentNodeIndex`/`ParentNode` and
  `NifShape.Warning`. `RadicleNative.g.cs` and `abi_layout_probe.cpp` were
  regenerated; no struct layout changed, so the probe is byte-identical apart from
  the new function bindings.
- Radicle/src/nif/geometry.cpp: a `BSLightingShaderProperty` or
  `BSShaderTextureSet` that does not parse now leaves the material and texture slots
  empty and records `Shape::warning` instead of failing the file; the geometry, skin
  and transform still read. A bone index past the end of the skin's bone list is a
  `parse_error`.
- Radicle/src/nif/skin.cpp: a `BSSkin::BoneData` whose count disagrees with the
  skin's bone count is a `parse_error` rather than a silent identity transform. The
  absent or mistyped data reference keeps names with default transforms, which is
  what the file holds.
- Radicle/src/texture/dds_codec.cpp: the DX10 array size and, for a volume texture,
  the depth are refused above 65535, and `DdsInfo::payload_size` multiplies unsigned
  with an overflow check, so a header that claims a wrapped byte count is
  `InvalidDds`.
- Radicle/src/texture/dds.cpp: `reconstruct_z` is refused with
  `std::invalid_argument` unless the format is unsigned BC5 (82 or 83). BC5 SNORM,
  BC1 and the uncompressed layouts no longer get a blue channel built from red and
  green. `radicle_dds_decode_rgba` maps that to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- Radicle/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md: the full bcdec MIT and Unlicense text, not just a
  reference.
- Verified: `Radicle/tests/test_nif.cpp` (node tree, furniture-marker blocks, shader
  warning, skin count mismatch, bone-index refusal, a skin the indices stay inside),
  `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_nif.cpp` (the node accessors, the shape's parent node, the
  warning accessor, out-of-range arguments), `Radicle/tests/test_dds.cpp` (the
  reconstruct-z refusals, the array and depth bounds, the payload overflow, the C ABI
  status for a refused reconstruct) and `Radicle/tests/test_nif_corpus.cpp`, which now
  reads the node tree of all 226,177 vanilla NIFs - 896,993 nodes, every node's
  parent and child edge consistent, 1,206,190 of 1,206,190 shapes with a node parent,
  0 parse failures, 0 shape warnings. The managed suite mirrors the fixture and
  covers the node tree, the composed world matrix and the shader warning in
  `NifTests`, and the DDS edges in `DdsImageTests`.

## Record condition lists C ABI (#602 WP-7 XA-2)

- `Radicle/src/c_api_conditions.cpp:radicle_plugin_set_conditions`: writes the root list (`fo4::set_record_conditions`) when `scope_path` is NULL or empty, otherwise a scoped list (`fo4::schema::set_record_scoped_conditions`). The scoped path is resolved by `fo4::schema::scoped_condition_path` against the record's own signature, found with `fo4::find_record` after `fo4::assign_record_form_keys`, so a path cannot name a list on another record type. Root statuses `updated`, `unchanged`, `no_condition_list`, `multiple_lists` and `alias_structure_invalid` map to `RADICLE_CONDITION_UPDATED`, `UNCHANGED`, `NO_LIST`, `MULTIPLE_LISTS` and `ALIAS_STRUCTURE_INVALID`. Scoped `container_index_out_of_range`, `element_not_conditioned`, `alias_structure_invalid`, `multiple_lists` and `unrepresentable` map to `SCOPE_INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `ELEMENT_NOT_CONDITIONED`, `ALIAS_STRUCTURE_INVALID`, `MULTIPLE_LISTS` and `UNREPRESENTABLE` through the out status with an OK return. A missing record is `NOT_FOUND`. A record type that does not match, an unknown scope path, a parameter string that `fo4::text::utf8_to_windows1252` cannot convert, and `rows == NULL` with a nonzero count are `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. An undecodable record is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` too: `fo4::require_decodable` throws `std::invalid_argument`, which the export maps, and the check runs before the comparison, so an empty write to such a record is refused. The core reports `replaced` for identical rows, so the export first compares the readable current list (`matches_current`, over the fields `radicle_condition` carries; `padding` is not compared) and returns `UNCHANGED` without writing. A list that cannot be read (multiple, alias-invalid or unrepresentable) skips the comparison and is written. Written `padding` is zero. The reader `Radicle/src/c_api_conditions.cpp:radicle_record_conditions` reads the root list (NULL or empty path, `fo4::schema::read_root_conditions`) or a scoped list (`fo4::schema::read_scoped_conditions`). A record with no list is OK with count 0. A failed read is an error: an out-of-range index is `NOT_FOUND`, an element that cannot carry conditions or an unknown path is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and multiple, alias-invalid or unrepresentable lists are `PARSE_ERROR`. The result is a caller-freed `radicle_condition_list` holder: `ConditionListHolder` owns the rows vector and a deque of UTF-8 strings, the same shape as `Radicle/src/c_api_behavior.cpp:PackageHolder`, and `radicle_condition_list_free` releases it and is NULL-safe. A record from another environment is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and a root list with more than one list is `PARSE_ERROR`. Root list creation is table-driven in `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:root_insert_anchor` (see `Record-level root condition lists (#602 WP-7)` below); a record outside that table, such as SPEL or ENCH, with no list returns `NO_LIST`. Strings can only be authored on a CTDA row, so a bare CIS1 or CIS2 cannot be written. MGEF carries a record-level list, created through `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:root_insert_anchor` and not through a scope descriptor; MESG's list is nested per menu button and comes from the `message_button` descriptor (`Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:message_button_ranges`). `UNREPRESENTABLE` is returned by the read side of the core only; no write path returns it today.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:CELL authoring rows

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:CELL` carries an `authoring` block: 32 signature rules in xEdit's record order (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5953-6100`), the same shape as the WRLD block below. That record is `.SetUnordered` (`:6100`), which is why it had no block and why every CELL subrecord answered `not_authorable`. `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:remove_with_rules` now accepts `XCWT`, so clearing a cell's water no longer depends on a zero write that `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field` refuses, and `RadiclePluginElement::removeElement` reaches the same rows.
- Placement is `cell_block`, not `top_level`, so `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:create_with_rules` still refuses to synthesise a CELL and `describeElement` keeps `canCreate` false. Cells are created through `Radicle/include/fo4/forms/cell.hpp:ExteriorCellCreation` and PET's worldspace branch, neither of which reads these rows. Known gap closed: `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` now reads the `cell_block` placement described below, which admits every accepted CELL parent, so the valid CELL shapes are no longer flagged. No production caller (`Radicle/src/forms`) preflights a CELL today.
- Minimums are 0. xEdit marks the XWCU array `SetRequired` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6060`); Radicle does not carry that, because a cell without water currents has neither subrecord. XCLR and XPRI are `wbArrayS` arrays with implicit counts, so they are `maximum 65535, uncounted: true`. XWCU is counted by XWCN (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6052-6059`, `SetCountPathOnValue`), so it keeps `maximum 65535` without `uncounted` and `editable` refuses a per-entry add or remove instead of desynchronising the count. XWCN is `coupled`, so `editable` refuses a generic remove that would leave XWCU without its count (`Radicle/tests/test_cell_rows.cpp:CellRows.WaterCurrentCountIsRemovedOnlyWithItsArray`). An equal-count `paired_with` was not used because XWCN counts entries, not subrecords. Every other rule is `0..1`.
- No defaults are declared, so `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:default_usable` answers `no_default` for a generic add. The block restores removal without enabling insertion of payloads Radicle would have to invent.
- Proof from the local MSVC build: before the rows `fo4::remove_record_subrecord` returned `not_authorable` (4) for `XCWT`; after them `Radicle/tests/test_cell_rows.cpp:CellRows.LinkWritesRefuseNullExceptOnTheLightingTemplate` removes the `XCWT` that holds `0x00000A21`, sees it gone, and reads it back absent after `fo4::write_plugin`. `fo4_tests` stayed at 2781 passed and 0 failed of 3179, and the four generated-schema `--check` targets stayed current.

## Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record — CELL `cell_block` placement

`Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` gives CELL its own `cell_block` placement (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:RecordPlacement`, emitted from `"placement": "cell_block"` in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json`), because a CELL record is never a child of a cell children GRUP. The accepted parents are a direct child of the matching top-level `CELL` GRUP (type 0 with label `CELL`), a world children GRUP (1), or an interior cell block (2), interior cell subblock (3), exterior cell block (4) or exterior cell subblock (5) GRUP. The rule is deliberately permissive across interior and exterior: `Radicle/src/forms/cell_create.cpp:create_interior_cell` writes top GRUP `CELL` -> type 2 -> type 3 -> CELL, `Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp` writes exterior cells under a `WRLD` top GRUP -> type 1 -> type 4 -> type 5 -> CELL, and a worldspace top cell sits directly under the world children GRUP (`Radicle/src/forms/cell.cpp:find_persistent_exterior_cell`, `Radicle/tests/test_environment_world.cpp`), so one placement value has to admit all six parents and none of them is rejected. A CELL that sits anywhere else, for example inside a cell children (type 6) GRUP, still reports `record_placement_invalid`. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_preflight.cpp:AuthoringPreflight.CellPlacementAcceptsInteriorAndExteriorCellBlocks`.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:WRLD authoring rows (#602 C-55)

- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:WRLD carries an `authoring` block now: placement `top_level` and 35 signature rules in xEdit's record order (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:13110-13177` with the helpers at `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9682-9950`). This supersedes the "No authoring block" sentence in the #651 bullet above. `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:create_with_rules` and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` read those rows, so `fo4::create_record` with the `WRLD` signature now builds a worldspace; the legacy-read preflight is a separate function (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/preflight.hpp:preflight_record`) and is unaffected.
- Minimums follow the seven-master corpus bullet above where it agrees with xEdit's `SetRequired`: ONAM 1 (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9849`), NAMA 1 (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:13154`), DATA 1 (`:13166`), NAM0 and NAM9 1 (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9922`, `:9936`) -- all five are in 18 of 18 WRLD occurrences. Every other rule is minimum 0: NAM4 and PNAM are `SetRequired` inside an optional xEdit struct (LOD Data `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9717`, Parent Worldspace `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:13124-13136`) and the corpus has them in 12 and 7 of 18.
- RNAM is the only repeated rule: xEdit `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9741` `wbWorldLargeRefs` is a `wbRArray`, so a worldspace carries one RNAM per large-reference cell, which is why the corpus note calls them repeated. It is declared `minimum 0, maximum 65535, uncounted: true`, the same shape as the GNAM rule in Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json. A maximum of 1 would have made `preflight_authoring_record` reject every worldspace with more than one, and `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:editable` would have refused every add. RNAM has no default, so the generic add answers `no_default` instead of writing an empty large-reference block.
- WLEV stays `minimum 0, maximum 2` and not `uncounted`, matching the two members described in the note below: xEdit writes the dimension struct and the cell blob once each, so `editable` refuses an add.
- Defaults are xEdit's native defaults where they exist -- DNAM land height -2048 and water height 0 (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9726-9728`), NAMA 1.0 (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:13153`), DATA 1 = 'Small World' (`:13165`), ONAM world map scale 1.0 then three zero offsets (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9836`) -- and zeros where xEdit has none (WCTR, MHDT, MNAM's 16 bytes, NAM4). NAM0 and NAM9 get eight zero bytes each: the FO4 branch is a `1/4096`-scaled `wbFloat` whose only default is `SetDefaultEditValue('Default')`/`('Min')` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9912-9913`, `:9926-9927`), and the SF1-only `SetDefaultNativeValue(1073741824)`/`(-1073741824)` would place the required minimum above the maximum. The bounds are present and cardinality-checked but zero-sized until the CK recomputes the map; that deviation is deliberate.
- The eight form-link rules (LTMP, XEZN, XLCN, WNAM, CNAM, NAM2, NAM3, ZNAM) carry no default on purpose: xEdit's `SetDefaultNativeValue` for LTMP (196834), CNAM (351), NAM2 (24) and NAM3 (24) are Fallout4.esm form identifiers and `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:default_usable` would write them into a plugin whose masters may not resolve them. Creation leaves those subrecords out and they stay reachable through the `existing_only` rows.
- Tests (Radicle/tests/test_wrld_rows.cpp, not compiled locally; CI is the compiler): `AuthoringRowsFollowXEditOrderAndRepeatRules` pins the 35 signatures in order plus the RNAM, WLEV, NAM0, NAM4 and PNAM cardinalities; `CreatesAWorldspaceFromTheAuthoringDefaults` creates a worldspace and asserts the stored order and bytes (EDID, ONAM 1.0 then zeros, NAMA 1.0, DATA 0x01, NAM0 and NAM9 eight zero bytes), a clean `preflight_authoring_record` and a write-reread; `AuthoringPreflightReportsMissingNamaAndTheOutOfOrderTail` is the negative case (the #651 test plugin has no NAMA and its MHDT and WLEV tail sits after ONAM, so `required_subrecord_missing` at `WRLD\NAMA` and `subrecord_order_invalid` are both expected); Radicle/tests/test_wrld_rows.cpp:`AuthoringRefusesWlevAndRnamBecauseNeitherHasADefault` expects `not_authorable` for WLEV and `no_default` for RNAM, the same answer the generic `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_with_rules` gives when a rule carries no `default` (RNAM is repeatable in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` WRLD authoring but still has no default payload, so it cannot be added by signature alone). Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md is regenerated: WRLD moves to `yes` in the Authoring column.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:WRLD MHDT and WLEV rows (#602 C-56)

- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:WRLD adds four MHDT and four WLEV scalar rows on top of the #651 set; typed by Radicle/tests/test_wrld_rows.cpp. This supersedes the "not covered, deliberately" bullet above for MHDT, WLEV and FULL; OFST and CLSZ stay unrowed (below).
- MHDT: xEdit `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9852` `wbWorldMaxHeight` is one `wbStruct(MHDT, 'Max Height Data')` of a Dimensions struct (Min X, Min Y, Max X, Max Y, each `itS16`) and then a variable Cell Heights array. Rows `WRLD\MaxHeightMinX`, `MaxHeightMinY`, `MaxHeightMaxX`, `MaxHeightMaxY` sit at offsets 0, 2, 4 and 6 with `minimum_payload_size: 8`, no `payload_size`: a payload longer than the eight dimension bytes (the corpus max-height grids in the seven masters, up to 26900 bytes) still exposes all four, and the Cell Heights tail stays unrowed because its row and column counts are the grid dimensions.
- WLEV: xEdit `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9765` `wbWorldLevelData` has two members sharing one signature, a 4-byte 'Dimension' struct (`wbInteger` itS8 X and Y for the NW cell, itU8 Width and Height) and then a `wbByteArray` cell blob. A second candidate for one signature makes the generic resolver report `duplicate` (`Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots`), which `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots` turns into a refusal and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` into a `duplicate_scalar_subrecord` error, so every vanilla WRLD with both members would have failed preflight. The four rows (`WRLD\LevelNwCellX`, `LevelNwCellY`, `LevelWidth`, `LevelHeight` at offsets 0 to 3) are therefore `repeated: true` with `payload_size: 4`: `repeated` skips the duplicate guard, and the exact four-byte requirement accepts the dimension member while rejecting the cell blob (1089 or 3844 bytes in the corpus). Ceiling: a worldspace whose cell blob happens to be exactly four bytes long exposes a second element, and index 0 is still the dimension because it is the first WLEV in record order. i8 for the NW cell follows xEdit `itS8`; Mutagen's `WorldDefaultLevelData.NorthwestCellCoords` is the same byte pair named unsigned.
- FULL: still no row. WRLD lists FULL in `localized_subrecords`, and `Radicle/src/environment/environment.cpp:decode_record_name` already reads it for every record, returning `NameKind::string_id` in a localized plugin; a plain zstring row would decode a four-byte string id as text. The coverage is Radicle/tests/test_environment_strings.cpp, and Radicle/tests/test_wrld_rows.cpp:LocalizedWorldKeepsItsStringIdAndStillWritesLevelRows re-asserts the id survives a write.
- OFST and CLSZ are still unrowed: in non-simple mode xEdit reads them as arrays of rows of `itU32` cells and hides its own elements (`dfNotShow(wbNeverShow)` at `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9682` CLSZ and `:9946` OFST), so there is no field to expose; the seven-master corpus has OFST between 256 and 148996 bytes. RNAM and NNAM are unchanged.
- Tests (Radicle/tests/test_wrld_rows.cpp, not compiled locally; CI is the compiler): the row table now carries `payload_size` and `repeated`; `ReadsMaxHeightAndLevelRows` asserts the bytes and decoded text of MHDT and WLEV; `WritesLevelAndMaxHeightWithoutTouchingTheCellDataBlob` writes two level fields, one MHDT field, re-reads and proves the second WLEV subrecord is byte-identical; `PreflightAcceptsTwoWlevSubrecordsAndLeavesTheCellDataBlobAlone` is the negative case (a WLEV payload that is not four bytes yields `subrecord_missing`, not a value read out of the blob); `LocalizedWorldKeepsItsStringIdAndStillWritesLevelRows` covers the localized header. docs/FO4_PARITY.md regenerated by Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py; WRLD rows go 22 to 30.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:CPTH, DOOR, EQUP and LVSP rows (#602 WP-9 A-26, A-39, A-43, B-37)

- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:CPTH\CameraShots (SNAM), DOOR\RandomTeleportDestinations (TNAM) and EQUP\SlotParents (PNAM, `storage: packed_array`) are formlink_lists rows, `appendable`, not nullable; the CPTH and DOOR rows are per-subrecord lists targeting CAMS and CELL/WRLD (xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7947 `wbRArray` and :6507 `wbRArrayS`, each wrapping a checked link), and authoring SNAM and TNAM went to 0 to 65535 after DATA and CNAM, as KSSM KNAM is addable. EQUP PNAM is one packed array subrecord (:8837 `wbArray`), so its authoring stays 0 to 1. Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:load_lists now accepts `storage` for formlink_lists rows; before, only keyword rows emitted `packed_array`. It also accepts an optional `anchor_predecessors` list of signatures on a formlink_lists row, which replaces the sibling-derived anchors for that row (successors empty). EQUP\SlotParents needs it: EQUP has no sibling list, so without the key an appendable packed PNAM would append after DATA and ANAM, while authoring order is EDID, PNAM, DATA, ANAM; `"anchor_predecessors": ["EDID"]` places the created PNAM after EDID. Its counter is empty (no count subrecord), so `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:reconcile_counter` returns early on an empty counter, and `insert_packed_element` skips the counter lookup for it; without that guard an insert or a partial removal would write an empty-signature subrecord before PNAM. LVSP\ChanceNone, LVSP\MaxCount and LVSP\Flags are existing_only u8 scalars on LVLD, LVLM and LVLF, copied from the LVLI rows (:10036-10038). The generic scalar write checks only the storage range, so `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginScalar.cpp:RadiclePluginBackend::setFieldValue` routes these three paths to the typed LVSP branch in `RadiclePluginMutation.cpp:RadiclePluginBackend::setField`, which refuses flag bits outside 0x01, 0x02 and 0x04 (xEdit `wbFlags` at :10038-10041) with InvalidFieldValue. Corpus over the seven masters: CPTH SNAM is 824 entries of 4 bytes in 329 of 447 records (1 to 17 per record), all resolving to CAMS through each file's master list; EQUP PNAM is in 29 of 47 records (4 bytes in 3, 8 in 23, 12 in 3), 58 lanes, all EQUP; DOOR has no TNAM in any of its 444 records, so the TNAM row is xEdit-only and its targets are unproven; LVSP has no records. EQUP ANAM (:8844, `[AVIF, NULL, FFFF]`) is deliberately not a row: of 44 ANAM, 30 are null or 0xFFFFFFFF, 2 are AVIF, 11 name forms absent from their owning master (Fallout4.esm 0x2CA, 0x2CB, 0x2CF and 0xB2 to 0xB5; DLCRobot 0x2CB, 0x2CF and 0x373, which are absent from Fallout4.esm), and 1 is a CONT (Fallout4.esm 0x0E). A checked row would report unresolved_link errors on vanilla records and wrong_target_type on one, against `CheckErrors.VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings`. Open: no corpus instance proves the DOOR TNAM targets, and the dangling ANAM values need RE or CK evidence before a row can be decided. Tests: Radicle/tests/test_wp9_list_rows.cpp; docs/FO4_PARITY.md regenerated by Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py.

- Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:COBJ: rows and authoring for xEdit `wbRecord(COBJ` (Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10266-10284). xEdit order is EDID, YNAM, ZNAM, FVPA, DESC, CTDA, CNAM, BNAM, NAM1-3 (unused), ANAM, FNAM, INTV, and the authoring block follows it. CNAM (:10273) is the 4-argument checked link helper (Core/wbInterface.pas:4283) over `sigBaseObjects` (:74-82), which includes `NULL`, so it is nullable and targets the `sigBaseObjects` union without NULL. BNAM (:10274, the no-reach checked link helper, Core/wbInterface.pas:4300, KYWD), ANAM (:10278, ARTO), YNAM (:5261) and ZNAM (:5262, both SNDR) are not nullable. FNAM (:10279) is `wbArrayS`, one subrecord holding a packed keyword array (Core/wbInterface.pas:8444-8452), not the one-subrecord-per-keyword `wbRArray` of KSSM KNAM (:12393), so it is a `packed_array` list with no counter, anchored by `anchor_predecessors` and `existing_neighbors` so an append never lands after INTV. INTV (:10280-10283) is a struct: Created Object Count (u16 at 0, default 1) and Priority (u16 at 2); `SetOptionalFrom(1)` makes Priority optional, so its row has `minimum_payload_size` 4. FNAM: 1542 records, one subrecord each, 1532 at 4 bytes and 10 at 8 bytes, all keywords, none zero. INTV: 4152 records, 3991 at 4 bytes and 161 at 2 bytes; counts 1 (4147), 2 (4) and 5 (1). Authoring: FVPA is `coupled` (typed `src/forms/components.cpp`, like ARMO MOD2); CTDA is an order entry only (0 to 65535, the CLFM shape), so generic add and remove on conditioned COBJ records do not return `unknown_order`. ## Radicle/src/forms/copy_as_new.cpp:copy_record_as_new — copy any top-level record as new with editor ID options (#602 D-11)

Public surface: `Radicle/include/fo4/forms/copy_as_new.hpp` (`RecordCopyNewOptions`, `RecordCopyNewStatus`, `RecordCopyNewResult`, `copy_record_as_new`). The top-level branch is the algorithm that used to live in PET as `copyRecordAsNewLocked` (`PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginMaintenance.cpp:copyRecordAsNewLocked`), moved here unchanged except for the editor ID step: masters for the source's form links are added, the record is allocated with `create_local_record`, copied, remapped with `remap_record_form_links`, and the editor ID is applied last. A top-level key that is not found is checked against contained records: INFO goes to `copy_info_as_new`, any other contained record goes to `copy_placed_reference_as_new` (REFR/ACHR only, the rest return `unsupported_signature`). Those delegations keep their own statuses and throw types.

`Radicle/src/forms/copy_as_new.cpp:copy_top_level_as_new` (and `copy_record_as_new`, which takes a trailing `FormLinkTypeLookup type_lookup = {}`) remaps with a lookup. An empty lookup becomes `composed_type_lookup`: the source plugin's `plugin_type_lookup` first, then the destination's, so a COED owner that the source or destination defines is typed (NPC_ remaps the union GLOB, FACT leaves the rank alone), and an owner neither plugin defines still throws `FormIdError` (strict mode unchanged). It is passed to both `remap_plugin_masters` and `remap_record_form_links`. Owners that live only in a master (for example an NPC_ in Fallout4.esm) are still unknown to this composition and still throw unless the caller supplies a load-order lookup. The master remap copies the destination (`remap_plugin_masters(destination, ...)`) instead of moving it, because the lookup reads the destination during the call and a moved-from plugin is empty. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_copy_as_new.cpp` `CopyAsNewRecord.CopiesAContainerWhoseCoedOwnerIsAnNpcAndRemapsTheGlobal`, `CopyAsNewRecord.CopiesAContainerWhoseCoedOwnerIsAFactionAndKeepsTheRank`, `CopyAsNewRecord.RefusesACoedOwnerThatNoPluginDefines`.

Refused signatures: PLYR and NOCM return `unsupported_signature`. xEdit marks both `dfInternalEditOnly` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12129-12132` PLYR, `:12453-12457` NOCM), and the copy menu tests `MainRecord.CanCopy` before copying (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:10537`; the group check is `TwbGroupRecord.CanCopy`, `Core/wbImplementation.pas:17650-17656`, and the element check `:19171-19185`). CELL, WRLD, DIAL and NAVM are not refused by xEdit and are not refused here. TES4 is never reported as a refusal: the header is not a record in any group, so both the top-level scan and `find_record` exclude it and it returns `source_missing`. A GRUP label is not a record key and also returns `source_missing`.

Editor ID options (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:16957-16972` for RemovePrefix and RemoveSuffix, `:17084-17091` for the deep-copy rule). `editor_id` set: the EDID is replaced with it, and that wins over everything else. Otherwise, when the source record is not deleted and has a non-empty EDID, the new EDID is prefix + (source EDID with the remove prefix stripped, then the remove suffix stripped) + suffix. Each strip applies only when the source text starts or ends with it, compared case-insensitively. xEdit uses `SameText`, which also folds non-ASCII letters; this port folds ASCII only, which is a known gap. A record with no EDID gets no EDID from prefix or suffix, because xEdit's rule requires a non-empty source EDID. xEdit's single-record prompt (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:3054-3075`) is the `editor_id` path; its multi-record prompts (`:3090-3098`) are the prefix and suffix path. Those prompts carry the four strings, and all four reach `wbCopyElementToFile` at `:3202`, `:3237` and `:3242`.

Known cost: link collection scans the whole source plugin with `collect_form_links` and filters by the record, because Radicle has no per-record form link collector (`visit_formlink_offsets` is internal to `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp`). Each copy therefore costs one pass over the source plugin.

Destination is edited in place, so a caller that needs all-or-nothing works on a copy. The C ABI does that (below). Undecodable sources throw `std::invalid_argument` from `require_decodable`, and an unrepresentable EDID throws the stored-text error that `set_record_editor_id` raises through `stored_editor_id`; both propagate, as before. `set_record_editor_id` returns false only when the record is absent, and it returns true for an unchanged EDID. A false on a record the copy just placed therefore means a broken invariant, and it throws `std::logic_error`.

C ABI: `radicle_plugin_copy_record_as_new` in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h`, implemented in `Radicle/src/c_api_writeback.cpp`. It takes destination and source plugin handles, the record key, and nullable `editor_id`, `remove_prefix`, `remove_suffix`, `prefix` and `suffix` strings, then writes the new key to `out_key`. It follows `radicle_plugin_copy_placed_ref_new` in having no status out-parameter. Unsupported signatures map to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and missing source and missing parent CELL or DIAL map to `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`. It copies the destination plugin before the call and assigns the copy only on success. This adds `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` 43 to 44 in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h`; the pin was `CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsFiftyTwo`, and the current pin is `CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSeventySeven`, and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` was regenerated with `bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py include <cs out> <probe out>`. The layout probe did not change. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_copy_as_new.cpp`.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:SCOL (#602 WP-9 C-37)

xEdit SCOL is `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12620-12648`: EDID, OBND (required), PTRN, the model group, FULL, FLTR, then `Parts` (required, sorted by ONAM). A part is ONAM (`Static`, non-nullable, 13 targets: ACTI, ALCH, AMMO, BOOK, CONT, DOOR, FLOR, FURN, MISC, MSTT, STAT, TERM, WEAP) followed by DATA (`wbStaticPartPlacements`, `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9223-9233`, required array of 28-byte placements: position, rotation, scale). Rows: six OBND i16 scalars `SCOL\BoundMinX` to `SCOL\BoundMaxZ` (offsets 0 to 10, payload 12), `SCOL\Model` (MODL), `SCOL\Filter` (FLTR), `SCOL\PreviewTransform` (PTRN, TRNS, not nullable; corpus 13 of 13 resolve to TRNS) and `SCOL\PartStatic` (ONAM, repeated, not nullable, the 13 targets). No DATA row: parts are a repeated group and go through `Radicle/src/forms/static_collection.cpp`. FULL needed no row: it is in `localized_subrecords` and `generated_lstring_fields.inc` already. Authoring follows xEdit order: EDID 0..1, OBND 1..1 with a 12-byte zero default, PTRN, MODL 0..1 coupled, MODT, MODC, MODS, MODF, FULL and FLTR 0..1, ONAM and DATA 1..65535 coupled, so generic create returns `not_authorable` and generic add or remove of ONAM, DATA or MODL is refused. No `ONAM` precedent with a DATA pair exists in fields.json, and the layout check in `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:local_layout_valid` is monotone in rule order, so 2 or more parts are out of order for it. The only defaulted rule is OBND, which every vanilla record has, so no current generic add reaches that check. Generic add of an absent non-coupled subrecord returns `no_default`, OBND returns `already_present`; remove of FULL, MODT, MODC, MODS, MODF, FLTR or PTRN succeeds, and remove of OBND returns `below_minimum`. Double count: no SCOL handler exists in `Radicle/src/schema/form_link*.cpp`, so the ONAM row is the only counter. Corpus (seven masters, 3513 SCOL records: 2617 Fallout4.esm, 152 DLCRobot, 3 DLCworkshop01, 219 DLCworkshop03, 235 DLCCoast, 287 DLCNukaWorld): OBND in all 3513, MODL in 3512, PTRN in 13, FULL in 124 (Fallout4.esm) plus 21, 3, 198, 33 and 1, FLTR in 2244 (Fallout4.esm) plus 106, 3, 3, 136 and 211. 20 records have no parts (9 in Fallout4.esm). 22713 ONAM, each followed by exactly one DATA; every DATA is a non-empty multiple of 28 bytes. Every ONAM resolves through its own master list; zero or unresolved ONAM: 0, so the non-nullable row raises no CheckErrors finding. Fallout4.esm targets: STAT 15674, MISC 129, MSTT 21, BOOK 14, ALCH 19, ACTI 5, DOOR 5, CONT 4, AMMO 3, FURN 3, WEAP 1, all inside the list. Parts are not sorted by raw ONAM: 235 of 2581 Fallout4.esm records with two or more parts ascend; across the six DLC masters 89 ascend and 754 do not. Placement arrays are not sorted either (xEdit `wbArrayS` has no sort key): 2614 of 8317 arrays with two or more placements are sorted by position. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_scol.cpp`; pin `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:SubrecordAuthoring.GeneratedSchemaMarksSiblingOwnersCoupled`.

## Radicle/src/forms/static_collection.cpp:add_static_collection_part (#602 WP-9 C-37)

Appends ONAM and its DATA at the end of the record. One part is ONAM plus one non-empty DATA: corpus 22713 of 22713 ONAM are followed by exactly one non-empty DATA, so an empty placements span is refused with `StaticCollectionError`. Part append order is kept: xEdit sorts parts by ONAM, but the corpus is not sorted (see the fields.json:SCOL note), so append matches the vanilla files; sorted-array behavior stays with D-25. The ONAM is encoded through `encode_plugin_form_id` with the plugin's form ID context, so a static owned by a plugin that is neither the SCOL's plugin nor one of its masters is refused with `StaticCollectionError` (the encode error is rethrown). Target signature checks run only when the static is owned by the SCOL's plugin (`validate_part_target`, the same shape as `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:validate_entry_target`): it must resolve there and be one of the 13 xEdit targets. A null encoding is refused. A missing record returns false; a record that is not SCOL throws `StaticCollectionError`.

## Radicle/src/forms/static_collection.cpp:remove_static_collection_part (#602 WP-9 C-37)

`part_index` counts every ONAM in file order, including a null-link ONAM. `decode_static_collection_parts` omits null-link parts, so the decoded vector and the edit index differ only for a file that holds a null ONAM; no vanilla record has one. Removes the ONAM and the DATA after it. Refuses to remove the last part because xEdit `Parts` is required, and refuses an index past the last part.

## Radicle/src/forms/static_collection.cpp:set_static_collection_part_placements (#602 WP-9 C-37)

Replaces the DATA after the part's ONAM and inserts one when the part has none. Empty placements are refused, because one part is ONAM plus one non-empty DATA (corpus 22713 of 22713); the caller removes the whole part with `remove_static_collection_part` instead. Placements keep caller order: xEdit's `wbArrayS` has no sort key and the corpus is unsorted (fields.json:SCOL note). The placements array is 28 bytes per element, written as seven little-endian f32 values.

## Record-level root condition lists (#602 WP-7)

`Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:root_insert_anchor` looks up `k_root_list_anchors`, a table of record signature, successor set and `end_when_absent`. The insert anchor is the first successor subrecord present, searched from `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:root_window_begin`. With no successor present, an `end_when_absent` row appends the list at the record end; PACK and QUST keep `nullopt` (no list can be created). The root list is the top-level `wbConditions` member of each record (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas @93cc0bc5`). Scoped lists (effects, aliases, branches, targets, tabs, phases, actions, start scenes) are outside this table. PACK, INFO, PERK and QUST keep their prior successor sets. QUST's top-level lists sit inside `wbRStruct` members (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10737-10739 @93cc0bc5`), so they are still read through `root_window_limit`.

Per record: xEdit line of the top-level `wbConditions`; successor subrecords in xEdit order; corpus on the seven official masters (records, records with a root list, subrecord before and after the list).

- ACTI (`:5668`, CITC `:5667`; NVNM, then end): 2196 records, 91 lists; before CITC 91 (count agrees 91/91); after NVNM 3, end 88.
- CAMS (`:7883`; DATA, MNAM): 772, 78; before MODT 78; after DATA 78; no CITC.
- CLFM (`:9590`; end): 166, 10; before FNAM 10; after end 10.
- COBJ (`:10272`; CNAM, BNAM, NAM1, NAM2, NAM3, ANAM, FNAM, INTV): 4152, 2215; before DESC 2132, FVPA 83; after CNAM 2214, INTV 1.
- CPTH (`:7932`; ANAM, DATA, SNAM): 447, 327; before EDID 327; after ANAM 327.
- FACT (`:6845`, CITC `:6844`; end): 851, 1; before CITC 1 (agrees); after end 1.
- FURN (`:6881`, CITC `:6880`; COCT, CNTO, MNAM, WBDT, NAM1, ENAM, FNPR, XMRK, SNAM, APPR, OBTE, NVNM): 783, 1; before CITC 1 (agrees); after COCT 1.
- HDPT (`:7054`; end): 420, 40; before RNAM 40; after end 40.
- IDLE (`:9648`; DNAM, ENAM, ANAM, DATA, GNAM): 3705, 2105; before EDID 2105; after DNAM 2104, ANAM 1.
- LSCR (`:9953`; NNAM, TNAM, ONAM, ZNAM, MOD2): 448, 278; before DESC 278; after NNAM 278.
- MGEF (`:10209`; end): 832, 132; before DNAM 132; after end 132.
- MUST (`:8815`, CITC `:8814`; SNAM): 624, 103; before CITC 103 (agrees); after SNAM 39, end 64.
- SCEN (`:9125`; SCQS, NNAM, TNAM, XNAM; window starts after the last PNAM, `root_window_begin`): 4778 records, all with PNAM; 7 with a top-level list (before VNAM 6, CNAM 1; after XNAM 6, TNAM 1; no CITC). 1150 records carry nested CTDA runs (Phases, Actors, Actions) that the window excludes. The last PNAM is the top-level Parent Quest because nothing after the Actions array is a nested PNAM.
- SMBN (`:8725`, CITCReq `:8724`; DNAM, XNAM): 136, 90; before CITC 90 (agrees); after DNAM 90; 46 list-less records keep CITC 0.
- SMEN (`:8767`, CITCReq `:8766`; DNAM, XNAM, ENAM): 18, 1; before CITC 1 (agrees); after DNAM 1; 17 list-less records keep CITC 0.
- SMQN (`:8740`, CITCReq `:8739`; DNAM, XNAM, MNAM, HNAM, QNAM, NNAM): 346, 294; before CITC 294 (agrees); after DNAM 294; 52 list-less records keep CITC 0.
- SNDR (`:9418`; LNAM, BNAM, DNAM, ITMC, ITMS): 7427, 639; before ONAM 639; after LNAM 639.

CITC: an insert writes a CITC only for the owners in `Radicle/src/schema/ctda.cpp:k_citc_list_owners` (ACTI, FACT, FURN, MUST, SMBN, SMQN, SMEN), which are the xEdit `wbCITC` and `wbCITCReq` rows before `wbConditions`. A replace updates the existing CITC count. A clear drops the CITC with the list for ACTI, FACT, FURN and MUST (`Radicle/src/schema/ctda.cpp:drops_empty_citc`), because no corpus record of those types keeps a zero-count CITC without a list. SMBN, SMQN and SMEN keep CITC = 0 because `wbCITCReq` is required, as PACK already does.

Authoring (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json`): CITC (optional, coupled, as FACT) and CTDA were added to ACTI, FURN and MUST; CTDA alone was added to IDLE (after EDID) and MGEF (last). SCEN stays without a CTDA authoring entry: its Phases, Actors and Actions reuse CTDA before VNAM, so a flat entry makes `preflight_authoring_record` report an order error on every scene with nested conditions (`Radicle/tests/test_dialogue_subrecords.cpp:SceneOnlyRemovesTopLevelSignaturesThatNoGroupReuses`); the SCEN root list is created through `k_root_list_anchors` instead. The other new rows already had CTDA, and no record without an authoring block gained one.

A SCEN with no PNAM is refused: `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:root_window_begin` returns nullopt, so `root_condition_window` reports `alias_structure_invalid` and both the read and `set_record_conditions` return that status with the record unchanged. PNAM is required in xEdit and all 4778 corpus SCEN records carry one. The CITC drop on a cleared ACTI, FACT, FURN or MUST list stays in place, since no corpus record of those types keeps a zero-count CITC without a list.

## Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:message_button_ranges (#602 WP-7 XA-2 B-2 C-2 D-22 A-46 B-18 B-39 B-45)

Tests for the FACT, IDLE and MUST anchors (#602 A-46 B-18 B-45, previously resting on the `k_root_list_anchors` rows and the corpus scan alone): `Radicle/tests/test_root_condition_lists.cpp:RootConditionLists.FactListAppendsAtEndAndDropsItsCitcWhenCleared` (PLVD `:6843`, CITC `:6844`, conditions `:6845`), `Radicle/tests/test_root_condition_lists.cpp:RootConditionLists.IdleListLandsAfterEdidBeforeDnamWithoutCitc` (`:9648`, conditions between EDID and DNAM, no CITC row) and `Radicle/tests/test_root_condition_lists.cpp:RootConditionLists.MustListLandsBeforeSnamAndCountsIntoItsCitc` (CITC `:8814`, conditions `:8815`, SNAM `:8816`). FURN joins them for #602 B-11 B-14: `Radicle/tests/test_root_condition_lists.cpp:RootConditionLists.FurnCreatesCitcBeforeMnamAndDropsItWhenCleared` builds a FURN holding `FNAM`, `MNAM`, `ENAM` and `XMRK` and requires the list to land between `FNAM` and `MNAM` (the anchor is the first subrecord in record order that is a member of `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:k_furn_root_successors`, because `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:first_member_index` (`:509`) scans the subrecord list and not the successor set, so a record carrying `XMRK` before `MNAM` anchors at `XMRK`; the fixture puts `MNAM` first), the `CITC` count to follow the condition count to 2 and the empty `CITC` to be dropped again on clear, because `Radicle/src/schema/ctda.cpp:owns_citc_list` lists FURN with an empty `after` and `Radicle/src/schema/ctda.cpp:drops_empty_citc` lists it among the optional-`CITC` records.

MESG is the one record whose conditions sit inside a nested container outside the original five scope kinds. xEdit `wbRecord(MESG, 'Message', ...)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8179`, pin 93cc0bc5) ends with `wbRArray('Menu Buttons', wbRStruct('Menu Button', [wbLStringKC(ITXT, 'Button Text'), wbConditions]))` (`:8199-8203`), so each menu button is one ITXT followed by its own condition run. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:condition_scopes` gains `{ "record": "MESG", "container": "Menu Buttons", "member": "Conditions", "scope": "message_button" }`, rendered into `include/fo4/schema/generated_condition_scopes.inc` by `Radicle/tools/condition_scope_codegen.py`, so the path is `Menu Buttons[i].Conditions` against the record's own signature, the same shape as `Effects[i].Conditions`. The container name is xEdit's RArray name, as for Effects, Branches, Tabs, Aliases and Targets.

`Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:message_button_ranges` opens one range at every ITXT, closes it at the next ITXT or at the record end, and anchors an insert directly after the opening ITXT. The kind is a new `ConditionScopeKind::message_button` (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/condition_scopes.hpp`), added to the `scope_ranges` switch and to the kind list in `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:nested_scope_ranges`, so the button lists stay out of the record-level window and the whole read, replace, insert, C++ and `radicle_plugin_set_conditions` path is reused unchanged.

Corpus, from a read-only scan of the seven official masters: Fallout4.esm 1469 MESG records and 231 menu buttons, DLCCoast 230/31, DLCNukaWorld 170/33, DLCworkshop03 15/4, DLCRobot 45/1, DLCworkshop01 17/0, DLCworkshop02 32/0, 300 buttons in total and 63 of them with conditions. No CTDA, CIS1 or CIS2 appears before the first ITXT, no button holds a condition without a CTDA, and no button holds two condition runs, so every shipped condition falls inside exactly one range. The button layouts are 237 empty, 45 with one CTDA, and then `CTDA CIS1 CIS2` x3, `CTDA CIS2 CTDA` x12, `CTDA CTDA` x1, a four-CTDA run x1 and a seven-CTDA run x1. The CIS2 between two CTDAs belongs to the first condition, which is what `Radicle/src/schema/ctda.cpp:read_ctda_conditions_in` already assumes.

A MESG has no record-level list: `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:root_insert_anchor` has no MESG row, so `root_condition_window` reports `no_list` and a bare write returns `no_condition_list` (`Radicle/tests/test_condition_scopes_mesg.cpp:ConditionScopesMesg.BareRootWriteIsRefusedBesideButtonLists`). No count subrecord is written either: `Radicle/src/schema/ctda.cpp:k_citc_list_owners` has no MESG row and the anchor is an ITXT, and xEdit gives a menu button no CITC.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_condition_scopes_mesg.cpp` covers path resolution and its negatives, the per-button read with an out-of-range index, the insert landing after its button text with the sibling buttons byte-identical, the replace dropping a CIS1 with its condition, and the bare root refusal. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_conditions.cpp:ConditionsCApi.MesgMenuButtonScopeWritesThroughTheRadicleExport` writes and reads `Menu Buttons[1].Conditions` through `radicle_plugin_set_conditions` and `radicle_record_conditions`.

The shared plugin builder and assertions moved to `Radicle/tests/condition_scope_fixture.hpp`; `Radicle/tests/test_condition_scopes_mesg.cpp` keeps its own cases.

With it, every C-47 member has a row: BTXT and its conditions, ITXT, RNAM, ANAM, ITID, UNAM, VNAM, TNAM and its conditions, and the COCT/CNTO holotapes.

## Condition parameter strings and the authoring table (#602 WP-7 XA-2)

CIS1 and CIS2 are authorable today, on the condition row: `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/ctda.hpp:CtdaCondition` carries `parameter1_string` and `parameter2_string`, `Radicle/src/schema/ctda.cpp:serialize_ctda_run` writes them as CIS1 and CIS2 after their CTDA and `Radicle/src/schema/ctda.cpp:read_ctda_conditions_in` reads them back, and the generic C ABI exposes the same two fields on `radicle_condition` (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_conditions.h`). `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_conditions.cpp:ConditionsCApi.SetReplacesTheRootListAndRereadsIt` writes a CIS1 string through the export and reads it back from the written file; `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_conditions.cpp:ConditionsCApi.MesgMenuButtonScopeWritesThroughTheRadicleExport` writes both parameter strings on one menu-button condition and reads both back.

They are deliberately not entries in a record's `authoring` list, and cannot be: CIS1 and CIS2 repeat after each CTDA inside one condition run, so a listed CIS rule index both follows and precedes the listed CTDA index. `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` reports `subrecord_order_invalid` as soon as a listed rule index decreases, so a repeatable group member that interleaves with another listed member has to stay unlisted; the same reason keeps CTDA, CIS1 and CIS2 out of the audit of MESG, LSCR, SMQN, SMBN and TERM. Authoring a condition string therefore goes through the condition API, not through `radicle_plugin_set_record_string`.

## Radicle/src/c_api_env.cpp:radicle_env_referenced_by (#602 D-3)

`radicle_env` builds one `fo4::ConflictGraph` on the first `radicle_env_referenced_by` or `radicle_env_references_from` call, inside `std::call_once` (`reference_graph`), from `env.value.plugin(i)` in load order. `ConflictGraph::build` indexes its span by position, so a hit's `load_order` is already the env plugin index, and `copy_reference_hits` writes it to `plugin_index` without a `find_plugin` lookup. `record` goes through `to_c_key`, which borrows the owner name from the environment as the other env exports do. An unknown key is OK with NULL/0 because `referenced_by` and `references_from` return empty vectors for it. `subrecord` is the four-character signature with a NUL. The exports moved `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` from 44 to 45, and `bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` and `bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` were regenerated with `generate_interop.py include <cs out> <probe out>`. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_referenced_by.cpp:CApiReferencedBy.ReportsInboundAndOutboundLinksWithPluginIndex`.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MUSC (#602 track lists)

MUSC TNAM (`Tracks`, targets MUST, nullable) is a `formlink_lists` row with `packed_array` storage and `appendable` mutation, so the list insert and remove paths edit it by index. xEdit `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8683` (pinned 93cc0bc5, record at `:8665`) is a `wbArray` of Track form links with targets [MUST, NULL]: unsorted (`wbArray`, not `wbArrayS`) and NULL allowed. The anchor `["WNAM","PNAM","FNAM","EDID"]` is nearest-first in xEdit member order (EDID, FNAM, PNAM, WNAM, TNAM), so a created TNAM lands after WNAM. Corpus (Fallout4.esm and the six DLC masters, read-only, `reader.py`): 134 MUSC records, 134 with TNAM, no record with two, 465 entries, 0 NULL entries, 0 zero-byte payloads, none off a four-byte boundary.

MUST SNAM (`Tracks`, targets MUST, nullable) is a packed appendable `formlink_lists` row, as MUSC. xEdit `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8816` (record at `:8795`) is a `wbArray` of Track form links with targets [MUST, NULL]: unsorted, NULL allowed. The anchor is nearest-first in xEdit order: `CIS2`, `CIS1`, `CTDA`, `CITC`, `FNAM` (cue points, `:8813`), `LNAM`, `BNAM`, `ANAM`, `DNAM`, `FLTV`, `CNAM`, `EDID`. Each condition is CTDA followed by optional CIS1 and CIS2 (`wbConditions`, `:5183-5252`), so both CIS signatures come before CTDA. ## Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:packed_formlink_list_path (#602 track lists)

The field-path entry points fall back to this helper when `formlink_field_descriptor(path)` finds nothing: `radicle_plugin_set_record_formlink` in `Radicle/src/c_api_fields.cpp` and the path overload of `fo4::record_field_count` in `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp`. It returns a list only for packed_array storage, so other list kinds keep the unknown-path result. Index-out-of-range maps to NOT_FOUND on the C side, as the field path did. A bad target type or record mismatch maps to INVALID_ARGUMENT; the C++ field path threw where the list path returns a status, and both reach the same C code.

## Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:insert_record_formlink_list_null_element (#602 track lists)

A NULL insert dispatches on storage the same way the element insert does: packed_array lists go to `insert_packed_element` with a zero element, so the single array subrecord grows by four bytes; per-subrecord lists keep `insert_encoded_element`. The nullable refusal is unchanged. Before this, a NULL insert into MUSC or MUST `Tracks` went through the per-subrecord path and threw from `matching_positions` on the array's size.

## Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:empty_list_insertion_point (#602 track lists)

The first element of an absent flat list goes after the last subrecord whose signature is any listed anchor predecessor (the maximum position over the predecessors present), not after the first listed predecessor that exists. The list order is therefore not significant for predecessors. Example: MUST with `CITC CTDA CIS2 CTDA` and no SNAM places SNAM after the final CTDA; the old first-listed rule put it after CIS2, inside the condition block. With no predecessor present, the first present successor in list order anchors the insert before it; with no anchor and `append_when_empty`, the element goes at the end of the record; otherwise insertion fails closed. Tests: `MusicTrackLists.AppendAfterLastConditionSubrecordWhenTracksAbsent`, `WP9CobjRows.CategoryKeywordAnchorsAfterTheNearestPresentPredecessor` (unchanged position), `FormLinkListMutation.InsertsFirstEmptyElementAfterPrecedingSibling`.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MOVT (#602 B-43)

- xEdit: `wbSPED` at Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9147-9355 is chosen by `wbFormVersionDecider([28, 60, 104])` (Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:5590-5617). The decider compares the record's form version (`MainRecord.Version`), not the payload size. So 28, 60 and 104 are form-version thresholds: arm 0 below 28, arm 1 for 28 to 59, arm 2 for 60 to 103, arm 3 from 104. The arms are 40, 44, 68 and 112 bytes, because `wbUnused` is a zero-size `wbEmpty` (Core/wbInterface.pas:7951-7956). No arm is 28, 60 or 104 bytes.
- Added: 28 f32 scalar rows for arm 3 only. MOVT\Left, Right, Forward and Back, each with Standing, Walk, Run and Sprint, sit at SPED offsets 0 to 60 (4 bytes apart). MOVT\Pitch, Roll and Yaw sit at 64 to 108 (`wbFloatAngle` in xEdit; stored raw with identity presentation, as INAM is). Each row has `embedded`, `minimum_payload_size: 112` and `insertion: existing_only`. `scalar_field_bytes` (Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes) returns no bytes for a payload under the floor, and `patch_scalar_field` refuses the write, so arms 0 to 2 never expose these rows.
- Why arm 3 only: it is the only arm with the Standing, Walk, Run and Sprint names, and it holds 81 of 103 records. A floor cannot separate the other arms: their Walk and Run sit at offsets 0 and 4, which are Standing and Walk in arm 3, and a floor of 40, 44 or 68 would also expose them on a 112-byte payload. Arms 0 to 2 (22 corpus records) need exact `payload_size` gates, so they are skipped. Add them when needed.
- Gate choice: the payload length identifies the arm. `min_form_version: 104` would match xEdit's boundary and the corpus (112-byte payloads start at version 105, and none sit at 103 or 104), but it was not used.
- Corpus (same scan): 103 MOVT records, all with SPED. Payload size by form version: 40 bytes in 1 record (v24); 44 in 5 (v31 to 55); 68 in 16 (v60 to 102); 112 in 81 (v105 to 131). Every record's size equals the arm the xEdit decider selects for its version, so there are 0 mismatches. No record sits at version 103 or 104, so the 104 boundary has no corpus evidence.
- Gate: the rows are gated by form version >= 104 (xEdit's decider threshold, Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:5590-5612) and payload >= 112. The test fixture uses 112 bytes. The earlier statement that SPED is deferred (the WP-11 section of this file, MOVT paragraph) is superseded by this entry.
- Not touched: RACE, FURN, ARMO and ARMA rows. Test: Radicle/tests/test_ipds_movt_rows.cpp.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN container items and marker rows (#602 B-11 B-14)

Adds `FURN\ItemTotal` (COCT, u32, `existing_only`) and the `FURN\Items` subrecord group, mirroring `CONT\Items`: count COCT, one required CNTO member (payload 8, default `0000000001000000`), `FURN\ItemCount` (i32 at offset 4) and `FURN\ItemObject` (FormLink at offset 0, nullable, `sigBaseObjects`). The group descriptor is generated, and insertion anchors on the first successor through `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:first_successor_index` (called at line 537). xEdit: `wbCOCT` 3315 and `wbCNTOs` 3316 (`wbCNTO` 3300), FURN record at 6848, COCT and CNTOs at 6882-6883 (after CITC 6880 and conditions 6881), MNAM at 6884. Successors are the FURN subrecords that follow the items in record order: MNAM, WBDT, NAM1, ENAM, NAM0, FNPR, XMRK, SNAM, APPR, OBTE, OBTF, OBTS, STOP, NVNM. FULL is left out on purpose: the header FULL precedes MODL, and `first_successor_index` takes the first matching subrecord in record order, so a successor FULL would insert a new COCT before the header. COED (optional, payload 12) is part of xEdit `wbCNTO` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3300-3313`, `wbCOED` at 3290), so xEdit allows it after each FURN CNTO (6883). The group lists it as an optional member, mirroring `CONT\Items`, so removing a run takes its COED with its CNTO and an insert does not land between them. Vanilla has no COED in FURN: 0 across the seven masters (783 records, 67 with CNTO), so the member is layout-only.

COCT and FNPR are absent from `include/fo4/schema/non_formid_slots.inc`, `non_formid_slots_manual.inc` and `formid_subrecords.inc`, because they hold counts and flags with no form IDs (COCT is a u32 count, FNPR is a u16 type and a u16 flag set).

Corpus (Fallout 4 official masters, `Radicle/` survey through `wp6-survey/reader.py` with `python -I`): 783 FURN records (Fallout4.esm 598, DLCRobot 11, DLCworkshop01 29, DLCworkshop02 3, DLCworkshop03 54, DLCCoast 32, DLCNukaWorld 56). COCT is in 98 records (all 4 bytes); CNTO is 145 subrecords in 67 records (all 8 bytes). COCT equals the CNTO count in all 98 records; 31 records carry COCT 0 with no CNTO; no record has CNTO without COCT.

Marker rows, all `repeated` scalar rows (the Nth occurrence of the subrecord, `insertion` `existing_only`). `subrecord_group` needs a count subrecord (`Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group`, `count_subrecord` check at line 166), and the marker arrays have none, so they cannot be a group. Rows: `FURN\MarkerIndex` (ENAM, i32, whole payload; 36 of 36 are -1), `FURN\MarkerDisabledPoints` (NAM0, u16 flags at offset 2, `payload_size` 4; the two unknown bytes at 0-1 are not exposed; 36 pairs in 36 records, all 0 in the unknown bytes and 12 = Right and Left in every record; bits 2 and 3 only), `FURN\MarkerEntryType` (FNPR, u16 enum at offset 0, values 0-4 with names 1 Sit, 2 Lay, 4 Lean, `payload_size` 4; FNPR is 263 entries in 147 records, with value 1 in 262 entries and value 0 once; xEdit leaves value 0 blank, so it has no name here; values 2 and 4 are unobserved), and `FURN\MarkerEntryPoints` (FNPR, u16 flags at offset 2; names Front, Behind, Right, Left, Up as in `wbFurnitureEntryTypeFlags` at `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:7987`; observed 13 in 189 entries, 14 in 73, 0 once; bits 0-3 seen, bit 4 Up unobserved). ENAM occurs as 36 pairs with NAM0 in every record, the counts are equal, and the pairs alternate ENAM then NAM0 in every record. Markers: `wbRArray('Markers')` at 6902-6909, FNPR at 6910-6913.

Existing singles, no new rows: `FURN\BenchType` (WBDT, 6885; 783 records, 782 one byte and one two byte, values 0 686, 1 1, 2 2, 5 22, 7 1, 8 70, 9 1; 3, 4 and 6 are unobserved), `FURN\ActiveMarkers` (MNAM, 6884; 783 records, all 4 bytes; observed bits 0-6 and 23-27, 30, 31, all named in xEdit; bits 7-22, 28 and 29 are unobserved), `FURN\MarkerModel` (XMRK, 6914; 603 records). NAM1 (6901) is `FURN\AssociatedForm`.

Not covered:
- SNAM marker parameters (`wbSNAMMarkerParams` at 6915, defined at 5314): each SNAM is an array of elements, each holding a keyword form ID plus a version-gated 4-byte tail. Corpus SNAM sizes are 24 (565), 48 (123), 96 (12), 72 (13), 20 (67), 40 (2) and 168 (1), so no scalar row can index it. Skipped.
- APPR (6916, `wbAPPR` at 5275, keyword array): not in this batch; no rows.
- OBTE, OBTF, OBTS, STOP, FULL and NVNM inside the object template (6917, template at 5520): no rows; FULL stays localized at the record level.
- The FURN item group has no insert/remove for the marker rows (`existing_only`, no count). Item insert and remove go through the group.
- Authoring is unchanged. FURN authoring already lists COCT (coupled); CONT authoring has no COCT or CNTO entries either, so FURN does not add them.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/non_formid_slots.inc` still lists FURN ENAM (36) and NAM0 at lines 63 and 66. That list is a corpus scan that needs fo4inspect, which was not run, so it was not regenerated.
- The older FURN "not covered" lines for ENAM, NAM0, FNPR and CNTO (around lines 1986 and 1990) are superseded by this entry.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO (#602 A-13)

ARMO gains 14 scalar rows, 11 FormLink rows and the Resistance pair. The `formlink_fields` key is new on ARMO. xEdit (pinned 93cc0bc5, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas`): `wbRecord(ARMO)` at :5786-5842; `DATA` at :5828 (Value s32 at 0, Weight f32 at 4, Health u32 at 8, 12 bytes); `FNAM` at :5833 (Armor Rating u16 at 0, Base Addon Index u16 at 2, Stagger Rating u8 at 4 with `wbStaggerEnum` at :5106 = None, Small, Medium, Large, Extra Large, then 3 unused bytes, 8 bytes); `BOD2` at :3393 (one u32 first-person flags, no armor type); `DAMA` at :5839 through `wbDamageTypeArray` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8454`, a DMGT link plus a u32 amount, curve table only from form version 152); `PTRN` :5796 [TRNS]; `EITM` through `wbEnchantment` :5798 [ENCH]; `YNAM` :5813 and `ZNAM` :5814 [SNDR]; `ETYP` :5815 [EQUP, NULL]; `BIDS` :5816 [IPDS, NULL] and `BAMT` :5817 [MATT, NULL]; `RNAM` :5818 [RACE]; `INRD` :5821 [INNR]; `TNAM` :5840 [ARMO]. OBND uses `wbObjectBounds` (`wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9074`), the ACTI row shape with payload 12. Rows: OBND 6 (payload 12), DATA 3 and FNAM 3 (payloads 12 and 8), BOD2 whole-payload u32 (the RACE FirstPersonFlags shape), the Resistance pair (the WEAP DamageType and DamageAmount shape: stride 8, `max_form_version` 152, DMGT). The pair is covered by the signature-keyed `k_repeated_struct_layouts` in `src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp`, so no C++ change is needed. Insertion is existing_only throughout. The ARMO authoring block is unchanged: it lists no OBND, FNAM, BOD2 or links.

Corpus (Fallout4.esm plus the six DLC masters, read with the survey reader, read-only): 1027 ARMO records (688 in Fallout4.esm), all form version 131. OBND, DATA, FNAM, BOD2 and RNAM each have one size in every record (12, 12, 8, 4, 4). EITM 277 entries (4 bytes), ETYP 3, BAMT 1, INRD 351, YNAM 3, ZNAM 3, PTRN 695 (all 4 bytes). TNAM and BIDS have no occurrence, so those rows follow xEdit only. DAMA: 392 records, 242 with one 8-byte entry and 150 with two (542 entries, all 8 bytes at version 131); all 542 resolve to DMGT in Fallout4.esm. No link payload is zero in any link row. FNAM byte 4 is 0 in all 1027 records, so no stagger value above None occurs in the corpus; the names are xEdit's, and the 0..4 bounds match WEAP `Stagger`.

Skipped: Models (INDX and MODL, a repeated per-entry struct with 1396 pairs; no existing row shape covers it). KWDA and KSIZ are already covered, because ARMO is listed in `keyword_records`. APPR (Attach Parent Slots) has a formlink_lists row only on RACE, and that row is appendable and needs RACE authoring, so ARMO is not covered. MO2S and MO4S (material swaps inside the Male and Female world-model groups) have no row shape on any record. Strings (MOD2, MO2T, ICON, MICO, ICO2, MIC2) and the localized FULL and DESC are outside this brief. DEST, VMAD, OBTE, OBTF, OBTS and STOP are outside this brief. There is no BOD2 armor type: xEdit defines one u32 and the corpus payload is 4 bytes in every record.

The `formlink_fields` key is new on ARMA. xEdit: `wbRecord(ARMA)` at :5845-5887; `wbBOD2` at :3393; `DNAM` at :5854 (Male Priority u8 at 0, Female Priority u8 at 1, Weight slider Male u8 at 2 and Female u8 at 3, each with flags Unknown 0 (0x01) and Enabled (0x02), two unknown bytes at 4-5, Detection Sound Value u8 at 6, one unknown byte at 7, Weapon Adjust f32 at 8; 12 bytes); `RNAM` at :5853 [RACE]; `NAM0` at :5881 and `NAM1` [TXST, NULL]; `NAM2` at :5883 and `NAM3` [FLST, NULL]; `SNDD` at :5886 [FSTS, NULL]; `ONAM` at :5887 [ARTO]. The unknown bytes at 4-5 and 7 have no row.

Corpus: 1065 ARMA records (739 in Fallout4.esm), form versions 64 to 131 (1021 at 131). DNAM is 12 bytes and BOD2 is 4 bytes at every version, so no version gate is needed and `payload_size` 12 is used. RNAM 1065 (4 bytes; 70 point at a DLC master index), NAM0 26, NAM1 24, NAM2 3, SNDD 288, ONAM 107; NAM3 has no occurrence. No link payload is zero. Weight slider Male byte: 0 in 1045 records and 3 in 20 (both flag bits set). Weight slider Female byte: 0 in all 1065. Unknown bytes 4-5: 0x0000 in 160 records and 0x0200 in 905. MOD2 to MOD5 and MO2T to MO5T (strings). BSMP, BSMB and BSMS (Sculpt Data, nested groups). The DNAM unknown bytes (no row).

Corpus versus xEdit: no disagreement found. Every top-byte-0 link resolves to the xEdit target signature, the DAMA targets resolve to DMGT, and the BOD2 and DATA, FNAM and DNAM sizes match the xEdit struct widths.

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE DATA` gains 37 scalar rows (`RACE\MaleHeight` through `RACE\OrientationRoll`), all `subrecord: DATA`, embedded `offset`, `insertion: existing_only`. xEdit: `wbStruct(DATA, 'Data', ...)`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11069-11193`. Offsets are the sums of xEdit member sizes; the 200-byte layout is the form version 131 layout.
- Gates (`min_form_version`, read by `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots`): 109 for the weights (xEdit `wbFromVersion(109)`, :11072-11081, offsets 8-28), Flags (32, :11082), the rows from Acceleration Rate (36) to Shield Biped Object (60) and Injured Health Pct (56). 124 for `wbFromVersion(124)` Beard Biped Object (:11128), which moves every later member by 4: Beard 64, Body 68, Aim 72, Flight 76, Angular Acceleration 80, Angular Tolerance 84, Flags 2 88, Unknown Float1 92, Unknown Float2 96, Unknown Float3 120, Pipboy 128, XP 132 (i16), Severable Debris Scale 134, Severable Debris and Decal Count 138-139, Explodable Debris Scale 140, Explodable Debris and Decal Count 144-145, OnCripple Debris Scale 170, Count 174, Decal Count 175, Orientation Pitch 192, Orientation Roll 196.

So from 109 to 123 the 109 rows are exposed and the 124 rows are not; below 109 only the two Height rows (0 and 4) are exposed, and the weights, Flags and the rest sit at other offsets there and are not rowed.
- Pitch (`wbFromVersion(98)`, :11191) and Roll (`wbFromVersion(101)`, :11192) are trailing optional tails: `minimum_payload_size` 196 and 200, matching their end offsets.

Biped Object rows (Shield, Beard, Body, Pipboy) are `i32` enums with `wbBipedObjectEnum` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3319-3353`): value -1 None, value N is the Nth name from '30 - Hair Top' (0) to '61 - FX' (31). Flags (:11082-11115, 32 names) and Flags 2 (:11134-11158, 23 names) use the xEdit bit names, including "Unknown 3", "Unknown 4" and "Unknown 14" (precedent: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ALCH\Flags`, which names "Unknown 3" and "Unknown 4").

No other DATA size exists in the masters. Every row ends at or before 200. Flags bits set: 0-4, 6-17, 19-25, 28, 30, 31, all named; bits 5, 18, 26, 27 and 29 are named but unset in the corpus. Flags 2 bits set: 0-2, 5-20, 22, all named (3, 4, 21 unset). No bit above the 23 names is set. Size values: 0 (22), 1 (61), 2 (12), 3 (15). Biped values: Shield -1 (91), 29 (15), 30 (4); Beard -1 (105), 18 (5); Body -1 (74), 2 (12), 3 (24); Pipboy -1 (93), 0 (3), 30 (14), all inside -1..31. XP 0..100. Male height 0.825..1.55. Severable Debris Count 0 (93), 3 (5), 5 (12); Explodable Debris Count 0 (91), 3 (4), 8 (12), 20 (3); Severable Decal Count 0 (73), 1 (11), 2 (15), 3 (1), 5 (10); OnCripple Debris Count 0 (105), 71 (4), 100 (1). No non-finite value in the sampled float offsets.
- Not covered: Unknown Bytes1-8 (offsets 48, 52, 100, 104, 108, 112, 116, 124), byte runs with no row. The FormLink members (xEdit :11176-11181 and :11182-11190, Severable and Explodable Explosion, Debris and Impact DataSet at 146-166, OnCripple Explosion, Debris and Impact DataSet at 176-184, Subsegment Explosion at 188 from form version 118) get no formlink rows: they are FormLinks, not scalars, and they are already remapped by the struct handler `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp:race_data_offsets`, so adding rows needs its own double-count review. Pre-109 and 109-123 layouts of shifted members are not rowed.

Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).
- XLOC payload: `REFR\LockLevel`, `REFR\LockFlags` and `REFR\LockKey` require a 16-byte payload (`payload_size` 16, `payload_sizes: [16]`). xEdit `wbStruct(XLOC)` has `SetOptionalFrom(4)` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11672`, so xEdit accepts shorter payloads and these rows would hide them. Every corpus level (0, 1, 25, 50, 75, 100, 253, 254, 255; 1,797 records) is named. 251 and 252 do not occur in the corpus. Bounds stay 0..255.

- `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:value_membership_issues`, `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:stored_integer`, `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:unnamed_bit_list` (#602 D-16): value-level membership warnings, xEdit's `<Unknown: N>` display (`Core/wbInterface.pas:12336-21405`). `stored_integer` parses the string `decode_scalar` already produced with `std::from_chars` and requires the whole string to be consumed, so only integer storages reach the checks (a flag or enum row on `f32` or `zstring` is skipped); the brief forbids reading the payload bytes a second time. A row with no `names` is skipped outright, so `identity` and `percent_0_100` rows never warn. Enumeration: any stored value with no name in the row emits `scalar_enum_value_unnamed`. Flags: the rows carry single-bit masks (`ScalarName::value` is `1 << bit`, `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarName`), so the union of the row's masks is compared against the stored value and the remainder emits `scalar_flag_bits_unnamed` naming each bit. Both are `PreflightSeverity::warning`, matching the read-only rule at `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/preflight.hpp`: real-data tests only fail on `error`, so vanilla records with unnamed bits (for example `CLFM\Flags` bit 3+, where the generated row names bits 0-2 from xEdit `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas`) still pass. Flags rows exist only on u8, u16 and u32 storage in `schema/fallout4/fields.json`, so the `std::uint64_t` widening never sign-extends. Enumeration rows may be `i32`, which `from_chars` handles. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_preflight.cpp:ScalarPreflight.EnumerationValueWithNoGeneratedNameIsAWarning` (NOTE `DNAM` 4 unnamed, 3 named; `NOTE\Type` names 0-3, storage max 255 so no range warning competes), `Radicle/tests/test_preflight.cpp:ScalarPreflight.FlagValueWithUnnamedBitsIsAWarning` (CLFM `FNAM` 8 -> bit 3, 4 -> clean, 0x81 -> bit 7 alongside named bit 0). - `Radicle/src/localization/strings.cpp:add_string`, `Radicle/src/localization/strings.cpp:next_string_id` and `Radicle/src/plugin/localized_writes.cpp:add_record_localized_string` (#602 D-18): a localized plugin resolves text through a string table, so writing a string into one needs an allocated ID. `next_string_id` is the highest stored ID plus one, starting at 1, and returns 0 when a stored ID is already `0xFFFFFFFF` (no free ID); `add_string` copies the text without its terminator (the in-memory convention of `read_string_table`, `write_string_table` adds the NUL back), returns 0 for empty text and throws `StringTableError` on an embedded NUL or an exhausted ID space. xEdit `Core/wbLocalization.pas:434` (`TwbLocalizationFile.AddString`) only accepts an ID at or above `NextID` and sets `NextID := ID + 1`; `Core/wbLocalization.pas:718` (`TwbLocalizationHandler.AddValue`) returns 0 for an empty value and allocates the new ID as the highest `NextID` across the three files.
