Radicle allocates per table, so an ID can repeat across .STRINGS/.DLSTRINGS/.ILSTRINGS; every lookup goes through the kind-carrying table, so no read can confuse the two, and xEdit keeps one shared space for file tidiness rather than for correctness. `add_record_localized_string` refuses a non-localized plugin, an unlocalized (record, subrecord) pair, a missing record or instance, a payload that is not exactly four bytes, and empty text; it reports `unchanged` when the record already carries the allocated ID and leaves the bytes untouched. The strings of a plugin are not held by `Plugin`, so the caller owns the table and can write it with `write_string_table_file`. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_localized_value_writes.cpp` (`LocalizedValueWrites`), including the refusals and the ID space exhaustion.
- `Radicle/src/localization/strings.cpp:string_table_kind`, `Radicle/src/localization/strings.cpp:string_table_extension` and `Radicle/src/localization/strings.cpp:string_table_path` (#602 D-20): the table a localized field lives in is decided by (record, subrecord), not by the field or its size. The rules are xEdit `Core/wbLocalization.pas:558` (`TwbLocalizationHandler.LocalizedValueDecider`): DESC is a dlstring except in LSCR, QUST CNAM and BOOK CNAM are dlstrings, every INFO subrecord other than RNAM is an ilstring, and everything else is a string. `string_table_extension` returns the xEdit spellings `Core/wbLocalization.pas:103` (`.STRINGS`, `.DLSTRINGS`, `.ILSTRINGS`). `string_table_path` is xEdit `Core/wbLocalization.pas:696` (`GetLocalizationFileNameByType`): a Data-relative `Strings` folder holding `<plugin stem>_<language><extension>`, with the plugin extension dropped by `std::filesystem::path::stem` where xEdit used `ChangeFileExt` (the two differ only for a name that is nothing but a leading dot). No whole-plugin export helper was added: `string_table_path` plus the existing `write_string_table_file` is the export, and the three-table walk belongs to the localize/delocalize work. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_localization_tables.cpp` (`LocalizationTables`), which also re-derives the expected kind for every row of `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_lstring_fields.inc` instead of pinning a count.

- `Radicle/src/plugin/localization_plugin.cpp:localize_plugin`, `Radicle/src/plugin/localization_plugin.cpp:delocalize_plugin`, `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:PluginLocalizationStatus`, `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:PluginLocalizationResult` (#602 D-19): the whole-plugin localization switch. xEdit `xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:12821` (`mniNavLocalizationSwitchClick`) collects every `dtLString` element of the file, and for localize adds each value through `Core/wbLocalization.pas:718` (`TwbLocalizationHandler.AddValue`), writes the returned ID back into the element as four bytes, and finally inverts the file's localized flag; delocalize reads each stored ID back with translation off and writes the resolved text inline, then inverts the flag again. Radicle's dtLString set is `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/localized_fields.hpp:is_localized_field` over the generated lstring rows, and the table is chosen by `Radicle/src/localization/strings.cpp:string_table_kind`, so both directions visit the same fields xEdit's element walk does. `visit_records` covers nested records (INFO inside DIAL inside QUST), which the plugin test exercises through a child group. Both functions work in two passes: the first validates and collects, the second rewrites, so a refusal returns with the plugin bytes, the plugin localized flag and the caller's tables untouched. An empty inline string has no table entry: `add_string` returns 0 for it, the field stores four zero bytes, and delocalize maps ID 0 back to an empty inline string, matching `Core/wbLocalization.pas:803` (`GetValue`, which returns empty text for ID 0). `PluginLocalizationResult::empty_text` counts those fields; `converted` counts rewritten fields and stays 0 on every refusal. Statuses: `converted`, `already_localized` (localize on a plugin that already carries the flag), `not_localized` (delocalize without it), `unconvertible_field` (localize on a localized field whose payload is not one NUL-terminated string, or delocalize on a payload that is not exactly four bytes) and `unresolved_string_id` (delocalize on an ID with no entry in the matching table). The last one is a deliberate deviation: xEdit's `GetValue` leaves the out-parameter empty when `Find` misses and the caller then writes that empty text into the record, which loses the string; Radicle refuses the whole operation instead. A plugin with undecodable records is refused up front by `Radicle/src/plugin/record_edit.hpp:require_plugin_decodable`, because such a record would keep its inline text in a file that now claims to be localized. IDs are allocated one per field in visit order and never reused; xEdit reuses a duplicate only when its handler has `ReuseDup` set. The flag itself is flipped by `Radicle/src/plugin/flags.cpp:set_plugin_localized_flag`, which mirrors `set_plugin_master_flag` and keeps `Plugin::tes4`'s record flags and `PluginHeader::tes4_flags` in step. `Radicle/include/fo4/localization/strings.hpp:LocalizationTables` holds the three tables and `Radicle/src/localization/strings.cpp:table_for` selects one by kind; `Radicle/src/localization/strings.cpp:write_localization_tables` writes all three as `<data_dir>/Strings/<plugin stem>_<language><extension>`, since xEdit's `AddValue` also creates the absent files rather than only the one it stores into. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_plugin_localization.cpp` (`PluginLocalization`): `LocalizeConvertsInlineStringsAndFlipsTheFlag` (six fields across the three tables with exact IDs and stored text, one empty field as ID 0, EDID left inline), `LocalizeThenDelocalizeRestoresEveryPayload` (every record and subrecord payload equals the original map again), `LocalizeRefusesAPayloadThatIsNotOneTerminatedString`, `LocalizeRefusesAnAlreadyLocalizedPlugin`, `DelocalizeRefusesAPluginThatIsNotLocalized`, `DelocalizeRefusesAPayloadThatIsNotAStringId`, `DelocalizeRefusesAStringIdMissingFromTheTable`, `DelocalizeResolvesAStoredStringId` and `LocalizedTablesWriteTheirThreeFiles` (three files under `Strings` read back with `read_string_table_file`). Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).
## Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:compact_to_esl (#602 D-10)

- Scope: `compact_to_esl` moves every native record whose local form ID sits outside the light-plugin slot range into a free slot of that range, rekeys the plugin's own formlinks through `renumber_local_record`, and returns an `EslCompactionResult`. It is the library form of PET's `CompactToEslCore` (`PluginEditTool/FO4RecordEditor.Core/Services/WriteService.Esl.cs:14`), which reached Mutagen directly.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:esl_slot_range` answers the slot question with a copy of the caller's `PluginHeader` whose TES4 flags carry `RecordFlags::small_file`, so `local_form_id_range` takes its light branch: `0x800-0xFFF` for a plugin that already has masters and `0x001-0xFFF` otherwise (`Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:allows_hardcoded_range`). That keeps the range identical to `esl_eligibility` (`Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:esl_eligibility`), which PET's `EslSlots` matches except for its extra `HasForeignReference` test; the foreign-reference case is deliberately dropped here, it only widens the range downward and never strands a record.
- The ESL flag is set on the working copy only while renumbering, so the light branch of `local_form_id_range` bounds every new ID, and both `header.tes4_flags` and `tes4.header.flags` are restored before the copy is published. PET does the same: `CompactToEslCore` renumbers and lowers HEDR, and `SetLightFlagCore` sets the flag as a separate step. The returned `EslCompactionStatus::already_compatible` therefore means "every native ID already fits the light range", not "this plugin is now an ESL".
- Records that are not direct children of a top-level group are never renumbered: they sit inside a form-ID-labeled child group (`Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:group_label_is_form_id`) and a cell's placed references carry placement state that a bare ID move does not cover. Such records are reported as `EslCompactionBlocker::nested` with `EslCompactionStatus::blocked_nested_records` and nothing is written, which mirrors PET's refusal message ("keep cell-placed records within ... when authoring them").
- `EslCompactionStatus::capacity_exceeded` is returned before any mutation when the native record count already exceeds the slot count, and again mid-run if the slot walk runs out; `rekey_failed` covers a `renumber_local_record` refusal (target slot taken, nesting). Every failure path leaves the caller's `Plugin` untouched: the work happens on a copy that is only moved back on success. `renumber_local_record` can still throw `FormIdError` (for example the transactional rekey guard) and that exception escapes with the input plugin unchanged.
- The HEDR next form ID value is set to the first free slot after the last assignment, matching PET's `while (next <= last && inRange.Contains(next)) next++`. The caller-owned flags mean the value can legitimately exceed the light mask when the range is full, exactly as PET leaves it.
- xEdit has no single library call to compare against; the closest behavior is the light-plugin compaction in `xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:13054-13373` (row D-14), which also renumbers into `0x800-0xFFF` and leaves flag changes to a separate action.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_esl_compaction.cpp` (`EslCompaction`): an in-range record keeps its slot and the out-of-range record takes the next free one with its NAME link rekeyed and the HEDR lowered, a moved CELL relabels its child GRUP and survives a write/reload, a nested out-of-range REFR blocks without touching the bytes, an already-in-range plugin only lowers HEDR, and `esl_slot_range` reports `0x800-0xFFF` with capacity `0x800` on a plugin without masters and `0x001-0xFFF` with capacity `0xFFF` on one with a master (`allows_hardcoded_range` in `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp`).

## Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:renumber_local_record — child GRUP relabel (#602 D-13)

- Scope: renumbering a top-level record now rewrites the form-ID-labeled child group that carries the old parent ID instead of refusing the operation, which removes the "parent GRUP label rewriting is proven" guard. `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:relabel_form_id_child_groups` walks every group, resolves each label through the plugin's form ID context, and rewrites the label when it resolves to the record being moved; `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:relabel_record_child_groups` encodes the new ID in the same context. Only labels that resolve to the moved key change, so a DIAL's INFO group, a CELL's temporary group and a WRLD's cell group are all covered at any nesting depth.
- Ordering matters and is not interchangeable: the form-link rekey runs first because it matches the old key inside record payloads, and the relabel runs second because it matches the old raw label; neither touches the other's surface (`Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:rekey_form_links` never writes group headers, and the relabel never writes payloads).
- `Radicle/include/fo4/headers.hpp:set_label_as_u32` is the single label encoder, replacing the copies that lived in `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:renumber_local_record`'s guard and `Radicle/src/plugin/writer.cpp:remap_group_form_id_labels`; `Radicle/tests/test_record_lifecycle.cpp` covers it through `RenumberRelabelsDialTopicChildren` and `RenumberRelabelsWrldWorldChildren`.
- Repointing other plugins' references into the moved key is closed by `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:repoint_record_references` (see the section below; tested by `Radicle/tests/test_repoint_references.cpp` `ReferenceRepoint.RepointsEveryReferencingPluginOfTheOrder`). `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:renumber_local_record` still rewrites only the plugin it is given, so the caller runs the repoint after a renumber.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_record_lifecycle.cpp` (`RecordLifecycle.RenumberRelabelsDialTopicChildren`, `RecordLifecycle.RenumberRelabelsWrldWorldChildren`, both over `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:relabel_record_child_groups`): the moved record is findable under the new key, the old key is gone, the child group label holds the new code, the moved record's own child record keeps its separate id, and a write/reload round trip keeps the relabeled group.

## Radicle/src/forms/copy_as_wrapper.cpp:copy_record_as_wrapper (#602 D-14)

- Scope: the library form of PET's `copyAsWrapper` (`PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginCopyAsWrapper.cpp:51`), which drove the same four library calls from the PET backend. The operation copies the source record as NEW into the destination (the copy keeps the original payload, so it keeps the original entries), then copies the same record as an override of the source and replaces that override's entries with exactly one entry at level 1 and count 1 pointing at the copy. The entry replacement goes through `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:replace_leveled_list_entries`, which rewrites only LLCT and LVLO, so the override keeps its own header subrecords and the source EditorID that copy-as-override carried over. The wrapped record keeps the source FormKey and the source EditorID; the copy carries the caller's EditorID when one is given.
- xEdit: `xeMainForm.pas:3195-3227` (`CopyInto` with `AsWrapper`, invoked from `TfrmMain.CopyInto` at `:2817`): `wbCopyElementToFile(..., True, True, ...)` for the copy, `wbCopyElementToFile(..., False, False, ...)` for the override, `MainRecord.Assign(Low(Integer), nil, False)` to wipe it, one `Leveled List Entries` element set to the copy with `Count` 1 and `Level` 1, and `MainRecord.EditorID := EditorID` to keep the source EditorID. The library mirrors that order.
- Signatures: LVLI, LVLN and LVSP only. This is a documented deviation from the row text, which cites the xEdit menu also offering LVLB, LVLC, LVLP and LVSC: those four have no record definition anywhere in `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` (nor in `wbDefinitionsCommon.pas`), and the FO4 definitions carry exactly three leveled lists (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9986` LVLN, `:10009` LVLI, `:10033` LVSP). xEdit's menu predicate is game-independent (`xeMainForm.pas:15632-15638`) and lists the seven signatures for every game, so wrapping the four extra ones on Fallout 4 would author records the game does not describe. Extending the set needs a definition, not a menu entry.
- Failure handling: every step runs on a copy of the destination and the copy is published only on `WrapperCopyStatus::wrapped`, so all other statuses leave the caller's plugin byte-identical (`Radicle/src/forms/copy_as_wrapper.cpp:44`, `:76`). `source_missing` covers a key that is not in the source plugin, `nested_source` a record that needs a destination container (`RecordCopyNewStatus::parent_cell_missing`/`parent_dial_missing` from `Radicle/src/forms/copy_as_new.cpp:copy_record_as_new`, `RecordCopyStatus::source_containment_unsupported` from `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:copy_record_as_override`), `unsupported_signature` anything else copy-as-new refuses, `override_failed` any override status other than `RecordCopyStatus::inserted` (a destination that already holds the record is reported by `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:copy_record_as_override` as `already_exists`, and is refused rather than having that record's list overwritten), and `leveled_list_failed` a refused entry replacement. A malformed leveled-list payload still throws `LeveledListError` out of `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:replace_leveled_list_entries`, with the destination untouched.
- The PET layer keeps the surrounding policy, which the library deliberately does not take over: the load-order "LOSES" warning, the same-EditorID refusal, the comparison of an existing destination override against the source, and the master list of the destination.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_copy_as_wrapper.cpp` (`CopyAsWrapper`): a wrapped LVLI leaves the destination with the copy holding both entries and the wrapped record holding one entry pointing at the copy (checked byte-level through a write/reload round trip, plus the added `Source.esp` master), the no-EditorID case keeps the source EditorID on both records, a MISC source is refused as `unsupported_signature`, a missing key is refused as `source_missing`, and a second wrap of a record the destination already holds is refused as `override_failed` with the wrapped record keeping its single entry and the destination still holding exactly two LVLI records. The wrapped entry's raw LVLO bytes are asserted (level 1, count 1, chance none 0). Every refusal leaves the destination bytes and master list unchanged.

## Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_kind.hpp:ConflictCategory and Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:classify_record_conflict (#602 D-1)

- Scope: xEdit's conflict categories as a library API over the existing conflict graph. `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_kind.hpp:ConflictCategory` mirrors `TConflictAll` and `ConflictRole` mirrors `TConflictThis` at the pin `93cc0bc5` `Core/wbInterface.pas:491-499` / `:501-519`, and `ConflictPriority` mirrors the implemented half of `TwbConflictPriority` at `:577-584`. The enumerator order is the xEdit order, and the classification comparisons (`> benign`, `> override_`, `>= identical_to_master_wins`, `< conflict`) rely on it, so inserting an enumerator in the middle changes results.
- The algorithm is the top-level element compare of `xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2600-2745`: per version a node is `ignored` (partial form or an ignore-priority rule), `master` at index 0, else `identical_to_master` when it matches version 0, `wins` when it matches the previous version or is the last version, `loses` otherwise; `cpBenignIfAdded` becomes `benign` when the master does not define the element and no later version overrides it; `benign`/`override_` clamp the role; the category comes from the number of distinct values (0 or 1 `no_conflict`, 2 with differing ends `override_`, otherwise `conflict`), then the priority cases (`benign`, `override_`, `critical` after dropping the missing value), then the last node is forced to `wins`/`identical_to_master_wins` when the element priority is above benign and the overall role is above `override_`, then roles are rewritten for the `no_conflict`/`override_`/`conflict` categories, and finally any role at or above `identical_to_master_wins` raises the category to `conflict`. A record defined by a single plugin is `only_one` with role `only_one`.
- Versions come from `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_graph.hpp:ConflictGraph::versions` and are matched to the plugins in the `load_order` span by `PluginKey`; `RecordVersion::partial_form` is the xEdit partial-form node, which contributes no value and role `ignored`. `roles` is one entry per version in that same order. A record's comparable bytes are its signature, its `header.flags` and its subrecord sequence, excluding subrecords whose rule is `ignore` (`Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:record_value`).
- Subrecord rows are aligned by subrecord signature plus its ordinal among equal signatures in that version, in order of first appearance, because Radicle has no definition tree to align by; a key that a version does not define is an unassigned node, which is how xEdit models an override that drops a subrecord.
- Priorities are caller data (`ConflictPriorityRule`), not schema data: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` rows carry no conflict marks, so every element is `normal` unless the caller says otherwise. Porting the 145 ignore/benign/critical marks from `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` into the schema is the remaining half of D-1. `cpTranslate`, `cpNormalIgnoreEmpty` and `cpFormID` are not implemented: they need localized-string and form-version handling the compare does not do. The record element itself takes its priority from `ConflictQuery::record_priority`.
- Deliberate behavior notes: a subrecord mark does not propagate to the record row, so a record whose only difference is a benign or critical subrecord is still `override_` at the record level (xEdit's viewer propagates a child's `ConflictAll` up to the record node in its own node-tree pass, which this API does not replicate; callers that want the strongest child mark read `RecordConflict::subrecords`). The record bytes include the subrecord order, so an override that writes the same subrecords in a different order is a record-level difference while its rows stay `no_conflict` (Radicle's writer preserves file order, xEdit compares in definition order). The last-node `wins` rewrite also rewrites an `ignored` last node, which is what the pinned `xeMainForm.pas:2724-2731` does for a partial-form last version.
- Remaining D-1 work: field-level rows inside a subrecord (xEdit walks its definition tree one level further, which needs the `fields.json` offset/size rows per record), the sibling-compare benign downgrade (`aSiblingCompare`, `xeMainForm.pas:2704`), `ctNotDefined` for nodes no plugin defines, and the injected-record `cpCritical` promotion (`:2596`).
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_conflict_kind.cpp` (`ConflictKind`), synthetic plugins over a real `ConflictGraph`: a record in one plugin is `only_one`; an identical override is `no_conflict` with roles `master`/`identical_to_master`; one changed subrecord is `override_`; an override restored by a later plugin is `conflict` with roles `master`/`loses`/`identical_to_master_wins`; three values are `conflict` with `loses`/`wins`; an added subrecord with `benign_if_added` is a `benign` row while the record stays `override_`; a `critical` row keeps the record `conflict`; `record_priority` drives the record category for `critical` and `ignore`; an ignored subrecord removes both its row and the record difference; two repeated subrecords align by ordinal; a partial-form version contributes no value and stays `ignored`; an unknown key is `unknown` with no roles; `classify_conflicts` covers every key `ConflictGraph::all_keys` reports, single-plugin records included.

## Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_kind.hpp:compare_record_across_plugins (#602 D-2)

- Scope: the N-way value compare that `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/plugin_diff.hpp:diff_plugins` cannot answer, because that function takes exactly two plugins and reports per-record `added`/`removed`/`changed` plus the changed subrecord signatures. `compare_record_across_plugins` takes the whole load order and returns, for one key, the groups of plugins whose record content is byte-identical (`RecordComparison::record_groups`) and the same grouping per subrecord (`FieldComparison::groups`, aligned by signature and ordinal exactly as `classify_record_conflict` aligns its rows).
- xEdit has no N-way API to port: its record compare is pairwise (`Core/wbImplementation.pas` `TwbMainRecord.ContentEquals`, line 10090) and its referenced-by list (lines 12339-12361) is the D-3 half that #648 already put on the C ABI. xEdit's conflict viewer reaches the same answer by comparing every node in turn while walking the definition tree; this API answers it in one call off the same `ConflictGraph` and the same value strings as the classification, so a caller can pair a `ConflictCategory` with the plugins that actually differ.
- Groups are ordered by first appearance in load order and list `PluginKey`s, not load-order indices, so a caller does not have to reproduce the version list that `Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:resolve_versions` builds (it drops plugins outside the `load_order` span). A plugin with no version of the key, and a partial form, appear in no group. `ConflictPriority::ignore` rules remove the field row and drop those bytes from the record value, so a record whose only difference is ignored compares as one group.
- Shared internals: `Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:build_subrecord_rows` is the row builder both `append_subrecord_rows` (classification) and `compare_record_across_plugins` use, and `group_identical_versions` is the grouping. `compare_conflicts_across_plugins` covers only the shared keys that `ConflictGraph::conflicts` reports (two or more versions); it does not mirror `classify_conflicts`, which covers every key.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_conflict_compare.cpp` (`ConflictCompare`), synthetic plugins over a real `ConflictGraph`: three plugins group as two value groups with the identical override beside the master and the differing one alone, including the per-field row; three distinct values give three single-plugin groups; two repeated subrecords are compared per ordinal and only the changed ordinal splits; an `ignore` rule removes the field row and collapses the record to one group; a key no plugin carries returns no groups; `compare_conflicts_across_plugins` reports only the shared key and leaves the untouched one to a direct compare.

## Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:copy_record_deep (#602 D-12)

- Scope: the deep half of xEdit's `TwbElement.CopyInto` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:19294-19311` at `93cc0bc5`): when the copied record has a child group, xEdit copies that group instead of the record alone, so the parent and every child record move together. `copy_record_deep` copies the parent with `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:copy_record_as_override` (so masters, form ID re-encoding and form-link rekeying are that function's job) and then reproduces the source's owned child group under the destination parent via `Radicle/src/plugin/copy_hierarchy.cpp:merge_child_group`, which walks nested groups and clones each record with `clone_record` (the same helper the REFR containment path uses). `RecordDeepCopyResult::children` lists the record keys copied inside that group, nested ones included.
- The parent must be a top-level record: the child group is placed by `Radicle/src/plugin/copy_hierarchy.cpp:adjacent_child_group` at the position right after the parent, which is the adjacency `owned_child_group` (from `Radicle/src/plugin/child_groups.hpp`) reads. A nested parent (a REFR or an exterior CELL under a WRLD) is refused with `RecordCopyStatus::source_containment_unsupported`, the same status `copy_record_as_override` uses for the containment cases it cannot reproduce. A record with no owned child group behaves as a plain override copy, which is what xEdit does when `MainRecord.ChildGroup` is unassigned.
- Overwrite follows the caller's flag: the parent goes through `copy_record_as_override`'s `already_exists`/`replaced` handling, and `merge_child_group` replaces a child that already exists under the same key in place and refuses the whole operation when `overwrite` is false, so a refusal leaves the caller's plugin untouched (all edits happen on a copy that is only published at the end).
- Masters are registered before any clone: `Radicle/src/plugin/copy_hierarchy.cpp:add_required_masters` unions the owners of every copied record key with the owners of their form-link targets (`collect_form_links`) and remaps them onto the destination, so a child that points at a record from another plugin drags that plugin in as a master. The owner kind comes from the source's own master table (`owner_kind`), the same rule `copy_record_as_override` and `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp` use.
- Still open in D-12: a nested parent, that is the exterior CELL (its record sits inside a WRLD's block/subblock/cell groups) and the REFR, is refused rather than copied; `Radicle/src/plugin/copy_hierarchy.cpp:plan_nested_copy` grows the destination hierarchy a cell at a time for the single-REFR case, and generalising it to a whole nested parent is the remaining work. Cell persistent, temporary and visible-distant subgroups and WRLD block groups are handled by the recursion once the parent is top-level.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_deep_copy.cpp` (`RecordDeepCopy`), synthetic DIAL-with-INFO plugins: a deep copy into an empty patch inserts the dialog, both INFO records and the `Base.esm` master, and the topic-children group survives a write and reload with its label; a second copy without overwrite reports `already_exists` and leaves the bytes identical; an overwrite replaces the changed INFO in place, keeps the unchanged one and adds the new one with no duplicate; a record with no child group is a plain override; a nested INFO as the source and a missing key are refused and report `source_containment_unsupported` and `source_missing` with the destination untouched.

## Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:repoint_record_references (#602 D-13)

- Scope: the second half of `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:renumber_local_record`, the cross-plugin reference update the row names. xEdit reaches it from the navigation tree's Change Form ID action (`source:xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:10137-10346`), which renumbers the record, collects the referencing records through `Master.ReferencedBy` and hands them to `TfrmMain.ShowChangeReferencedBy` (`source:xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:17323-17400`); that dialog's per-record work is the exchange of the old form ID for the new one inside each selected record (`source:xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:17374`). PET's renumber path (`source:PluginEditTool/FO4RecordEditor.Core/Services/WriteService.cs:451`) remaps *in-plugin* links with `mod.RemapLinks` and then tells the user in its own message that references in other plugins are NOT updated, so the cross-plugin half is a caller-driven library call here rather than part of the renumber.
- `repoint_record_references(std::span<Plugin*>, from, to)` walks the span, counts the schema-proven links that resolve to `from` in each plugin (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/form_links.hpp:collect_form_links`, so a link that fails to resolve is not counted), and rewrites them with `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/form_links.hpp:rekey_form_links(plugin, from, to)`, which re-encodes the new key in each plugin's own form ID context.
- Both keys must be owned by the same plugin, which is exactly what `renumber_local_record` produces (`Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:renumber_local_record` builds `FormKey{next.key, new_local}`): a plugin that referenced the old key already carries that owner as a master, so no master list surgery and no owner-kind guess is needed, and `ReferenceRepointStatus::mismatched_owners` refuses the case where the owner changes, and an empty or identical pair reports `no_references` without touching anything. Refusing there is deliberate: pointing another plugin at a key owned by a third plugin means adding that plugin as a master of every referencing plugin, which needs the master kind, the load-order position and the light/full policy of each one; the pieces exist (`Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/writer.hpp:remap_plugin_masters`, `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:owner_kind`) but the decision is the caller's.
- The operation is transactional across the whole span, not per plugin: every touched plugin is copied, every copy is rekeyed, and only then are the copies moved back, so a throw from `rekey_form_links` (undecodable record, unsupported VMAD or mixed NAVM/NAVI payload) leaves all of the caller's plugins untouched.
- `ReferenceRepointResult::references` counts link hits, so a record holding two links to the same key counts twice; `plugins` lists the changed plugin keys in span order and is empty when nothing matched, which is `ReferenceRepointStatus::no_references`. A plugin whose own record was renumbered is not special-cased: its self-references were already rewritten by the renumber, and a remaining one would be repointed like any other.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_repoint_references.cpp` (`ReferenceRepoint`), synthetic plugins over a real load order: a MISC record whose NAME link points at a WEAP record is repointed after that WEAP record is renumbered 000800 to 000900, asserted on the raw link value (`0x00000900`), on the written and reloaded bytes and through `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_graph.hpp:ConflictGraph::referenced_by` for both the old and the new key; a key no plugin references reports `no_references` and leaves the bytes identical; a key owned by another plugin reports `mismatched_owners` and leaves the bytes identical; two referencing plugins are both repointed and both listed.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:CELL (#602 A-29)

- Scope: `CELL` gains 27 scalar rows, 1 counted array with 4 members plus its count row, 13 FormLink field rows and 2 FormLink list rows, all emitted by `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:load_lists`. The record previously declared `fields: []` and only the localized `FULL`. This is the write/edit half of A-29; the typed read half stays in `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:decode_cell`.
- xEdit: `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5953-6101` (`wbRecord(CELL, 'Cell')`). Helpers read from the same pin: `wbCellGrid` at `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8416`, `wbOwnership` at `:9093`, `wbByteColors` at `:6696`, `wbLandFlags` at `:7999`.
- `CELL\Flags`: xEdit declares `DATA` as `itU16` flags (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5966`). The row is `embedded` at offset 0 with `payload_size: 2` rather than whole-payload, because `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:decode_cell` accepts a 1-byte `DATA` as well; a whole-payload `u16` row would make `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` throw on those records, and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` would report `invalid_scalar_storage` for a valid plugin. An embedded row returns an absent slot instead.
- `CELL\GridX`/`GridY`/`LandFlags`: `XCLC` is 8 bytes (X, Y) or 12 (X, Y, land flags, 3 unused) per `wbCellGrid` `SetOptionalFrom(2)`. X and Y use `minimum_payload_size: 8` so both shapes address them; `LandFlags` uses `payload_size: 12`.
- `CELL\Lighting*` (rows read and written through `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes`): 21 rows over the 40-byte `XCLL` prefix only, `minimum_payload_size: 40`. `wbByteColors` is four bytes (R, G, B, unused), so each color is three byte rows, following the existing `KYWD`/`LCRT`/`AACT` `ColorRed`/`ColorGreen`/`ColorBlue` rows. The prefix is form-version independent: offsets 0-39 are Ambient, Directional, Fog Near color, Fog Near, Fog Far, Directional Rotation XY/Z, Directional Fade, Fog Clip Distance, Fog Power.
- `CELL\WaterHeight` (`XCLW`, read by `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:loaded_water_height`) is whole-payload `f32`. xEdit notes XCLW can hold `$FF7FFFFF`; that is still four bytes, so the row shape holds, and the sentinel is normalized on the read side by `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:loaded_water_height`.
- `CELL\WaterCurrentVelocityCount` plus `CELL\WaterCurrentVelocities` mirror the existing `REFR` pair exactly (count row `XWCN` whole-payload `u32`, `XWCU` counted array stride 16, members at 0, 4, 8, 12). `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py` requires the count row, so both were added.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REFR XWCN` is marked `coupled` like CELL's `XWCN`, so `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:editable` refuses a generic remove of the count alone, which would otherwise orphan the `XWCU` array; `Radicle/tests/test_counted_array.cpp:CountedArray.CountSubrecordCannotBeRemovedAloneFromItsArray` pins that, and the generated row in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints_subrecord_authoring_constraints_shard02.inc` is hand-synced to match.
- `CELL\Owner` (`XOWN`, `payload_sizes: [12]`) plus `CELL\OwnerRank` (`XRNK`, whole-payload `i32`) copy the established `PARW\Owner`/`PARW\OwnerRank` rows from the same schema file. `XOWN` is 12 bytes: link, 4 unused, No Crime byte, 3 unused (`wbOwnership`).
- FormLink nullability follows xEdit's target lists. `LTMP` is `[LGTM, NULL]` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6042`), so `CELL\LightingTemplate` keeps `nullable: true`; `XCWT` (`:6064`), `XLCN` (`:6051`), `XEZN` (`:6080`), `XCIM` (`:6082`), `XCAS` (`:6079`), `XCMO` (`:6081`), `XCCM` (`:6078`), `XGDR` (`:6083`), `XILL` (`:6069`) and `RVIS` (`:5989`) list no NULL and are now `nullable: false`. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field` refuses a zero target for them with `schema::FormLinkFieldError`; a stored zero still reads as an absent link, so a `CELL` that already carries `XCWT` `00000000` decodes as no water. `Radicle/tests/test_cell_rows.cpp:CellRows.LinkRowsNameTheirSubrecordsOffsetsPayloadsAndTargets` pins the flag on all 13 rows, and `Radicle/tests/test_cell_rows.cpp:CellRows.LinkWritesRefuseNullExceptOnTheLightingTemplate` writes `FormKey{}` to `XCWT` and expects `schema::FormLinkFieldError`, with `XCWT` unchanged, then writes it to `LTMP`, rewrites the plugin and reads back a zero. Clearing the water therefore goes through removing `XCWT` rather than writing zero; CELL's authoring rows below make that reachable (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:CELL`).
- `CELL\ExteriorLodWorldspace` (link at `XILW` offset 0, `payload_sizes: [16]`) and `CELL\ExteriorLodOffsetX/Y/Z` (`XILW` offsets 4, 8, 12, `payload_size: 16`) are the exterior LOD data. `XILW` is the only `CELL` subrecord that carries both a link and scalars, so it needs no `subrecord_group`.
- `CELL\Regions` is the FormLink list over `XCLR`, `storage: packed_array`, `mutation: appendable`, targets `REGN`, matching xEdit's `wbArrayS(XCLR, ...)`. An earlier revision of this row used the default `per_subrecord` storage and was wrong: measured over the seven official masters, every `CELL` carries at most one `XCLR` and its size is 4 to 36 bytes in four-byte steps (Fallout4.esm 4,805 cells with `XCLR`; the whole 15,413-entry corpus resolves to `REGN` with no zero or unresolved entry). `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:matching_positions` throws on a non-four-byte element and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` reports `invalid_formlink_list_storage`, so the per-subrecord shape would have failed on any real cell with two or more regions. `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:packed_formid_array_offsets` already treated `CELL XCLR` as a packed array, so the schema now agrees with the remap table.
- `CELL\PreVisReferences` is the FormLink list over `XPRI`, `storage: packed_array`, `appendable`, targets the nine placed-reference signatures xEdit checks (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6095`): `REFR`, `PGRE`, `PHZD`, `PMIS`, `PARW`, `PBAR`, `PBEA`, `PCON`, `PFLA`. Also packed: at most one `XPRI` per `CELL`, size a multiple of four and up to 2,464 bytes in Fallout4.esm. `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp:record_fixed_layout_offsets` already had `{"CELL", {"XPRI", 4, {0}, false, 0}}`, and the two claims union and dedupe in `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:visit_formlink_offsets`. Corpus: 40,750 `XPRI` entries in Fallout4.esm, none zero, none unresolved, all inside the target list (40,749 `REFR` and one `PMIS`), which is what keeps `Radicle/tests/test_check_errors.cpp:CheckErrors.VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings` free of `wrong_target_type`.
- `CELL\Lighting*` tail rows are deliberately absent. From `Fog Color Far` onwards every offset depends on the ambient block width: `wbAmbientColors` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:6635`) is a 24-byte directional block plus `Specular` (4 bytes) and `Fresnel Power` (4 bytes) from form version 30, so the block is 24 or 32 bytes. Measured `XCLL` payloads in Fallout4.esm are 92 bytes (579 records, the 7-field tail), 128 (10) and 136 (606, at form version 131), i.e. `40 + ambient + tail` with a tail of 28 or 64. A schema row cannot express a version-relative offset, so writing Fog Color Far, Fog Max, Light Fade Begin/End, Inherits, Near/Far Height Mid/Range, Fog Color High Near/Far and the five scale fields still needs the typed path or a new address vocabulary.
- `CELL\PreVisTimestamp` (`VISI`) and `CELL\PreCombinedTimestamp` (`PCMB`) are whole-payload `u16` rows: xEdit declares both as `wbByteArray(..., 2)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5978`, `:5980`), so the payload is exactly the 2-byte timestamp and no offset applies. A payload of any other width is malformed, and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` throws for it, which `Radicle/tests/test_cell_rows.cpp` (`CellRows::ShortPayloadsHideRowsInsteadOfReportingThem`) pins.
- Not rowed (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` keeps no row and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` therefore ignores them): `XCRI` (combined reference index: a meshes count, a references count, a mesh-ID array and a `Reference`/`Combined Mesh` pair array, so it changes shape with both counts and is not a flat link list), `MHDT` (max height data array), `TVDT` (unknown), and the `CELL` record header flags. All stay readable as raw subrecord payloads.
- Generators: `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py` and `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py` were re-run; both `--check` clean. `generated_scalar_fields.inc` renumbers the shared `k_scalar_names_N` tables after the insertion point, which is expected output, not a hand edit. `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` was regenerated with `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py --write`; `CELL` moves from tier L2 to L4.
- `CELL\Flags` (`Radicle/tests/test_cell_rows.cpp:CellRows.ShortPayloadsHideRowsInsteadOfReportingThem`) is an embedded row with `payload_size: 2`, so a 1-byte `DATA` is a payload that does not expose the row: `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` returns an empty span and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` returns `subrecord_missing`, because `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` leaves the slot invalid for a payload that fails `payload_size`. Only a whole-payload row of the wrong width (an `XCLW` that is not four bytes, an `ANAM`-shaped `f32`) sets `malformed` and reaches the `ScalarError` throw.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_cell_rows.cpp` covers the row descriptors, the flag names, the link targets, the packed `XCLR` and `XPRI` list shapes, byte-exact reads, a write-then-reread round trip with neighbor bytes held (`CellRows::WritesLightingBytesWithoutTouchingTheirNeighbors`), an `XPRI` element set plus append with an out-of-range set refused, and a short-payload case where `CELL\Flags`, `CELL\LandFlags` and every `XCLL` row report absent and refuse mutation.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN (#602 C-33)

- Scope: `REGN` gains 9 scalar rows and 2 FormLink field rows, all consumed through `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` and `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:formlink_field_descriptor`. `RDMP` was already declared in `localized_subrecords`. The record entry landed with the authoring block below; `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` has since added the typed read decode, and there is still no create function and no C ABI, and the object, grass and weather arrays are unrowed.
- Authoring: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN` is `top_level` with EDID, RCLR, WNAM, RPLI, RPLD, RDAT, RDMO, RDMP and RLDM, so the generated entry `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc` (REGN rule 1238, 9 rules) makes `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/subrecord_authoring.hpp:create_record` create a REGN. `RCLR` is `minimum` 1 with the four-byte default `00000000`: all 106 Fallout4.esm and all 28 DLCNukaWorld records carry exactly one four-byte `RCLR`, so a created region matches the corpus shape and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` is clean on it. `ANAM` is deliberately not a rule: xEdit gives the region area an `wbUnknown(ANAM)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9151-9164`) and the region data entry a `wbFloat` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11915`), and one rule position cannot cover both, so `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:create_with_rules` reports `SubrecordAddStatus::not_authorable` for it and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` skips it as an unruled subrecord instead of reporting `subrecord_order_invalid`. `RDOT`, `RDGS`, `RDWT`, `ICON` and `RDSA` are unruled for the same reason and stay raw.
- Order: `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` requires the rule order to be non-decreasing, so a REGN with a repeated area (`RPLI RPLD RPLI`) or `RLDM` before `RDAT` reports `subrecord_order_invalid`. The check skips unruled subrecords (`RDOT RDGS RDWT ICON RDSA ANAM`), and `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_with_rules` (reached from `add_record_subrecord`) returns `unknown_order` for any add to a record that holds an unruled subrecord.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp:RegnRows.CreatesARegionInAuthoringOrder` creates a region, checks the EDID then RCLR order, the four zero colour bytes, a clean preflight before and after a save and reload, the `not_authorable` refusal for `ANAM` and the `below_minimum` refusal when the only `RCLR` is removed.
- xEdit: `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11870-11959` (`wbRecord(REGN, 'Region')`, flags bit 6 Border Region, `SetUnordered`).
- `REGN\MapColorRed`/`Green`/`Blue` are `RCLR` offsets 0, 1 and 2, following the `KYWD\Color*` shape (`wbByteColors`, the fourth byte unused). Corpus: one `RCLR`, always 4 bytes, in all 106 Fallout4.esm and all 28 DLCNukaWorld records.
- `REGN\RegionDataType`, `RegionDataOverride` and `RegionDataPriority` are one `RDAT` entry header at offsets 0, 4 and 5, all `repeated: true` because a record holds one `RDAT` per region data entry and Fallout4.esm has records with up to 5 (69 records with one, 24 with none, 11 with two, one with four and one with five; DLCNukaWorld has up to 2). Every `RDAT` in the seven masters is exactly 8 bytes. The type values present are the xEdit enum range: 2 Objects, 3 Weather, 4 Map, 5 Land, 6 Grass, 7 Sound (Fallout4.esm 5, 30, 19, 3, 2 and 41 entries), so the row is an `enum` bounded 0 to 7 with the six named values and 0/1 unnamed. `REGN\RegionDataOverride` is an `enum` too, over xEdit's `wbBoolEnum` `False`/`True` names (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11891`, `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:7240-7247`); it was declared `identity` until this pass, which showed a raw 0 or 1 where xEdit shows the boolean. The corpus keeps every one of the 138 `RDAT` override bytes in those masters at 0 or 1 (98 zero, 40 one), so the row's bound is unchanged.
- `REGN\OcclusionAccuracyDist` (`ANAM`, whole-payload `f32`, `repeated: true`) is present once in 25 Fallout4.esm and 13 DLCNukaWorld records, always 4 bytes. `REGN\LodDisplayDistanceMultiplier` (`RLDM`, whole-payload `f32`, `repeated: true`) is xEdit-only: no record in any of the seven masters carries `RLDM`, so the row is unproven against the corpus and ships only because it is the field C-33 names. Both sit inside the region data entry, past the `RDAT` header, so they are repeated like the header rows.
- `REGN\Worldspace` (`WNAM`, offset 0, `payload_sizes: [4]`, targets `WRLD`, not nullable) matches `wbFormIDCkNoReach` at `:11875`, which admits no NULL and no reach check; `Radicle/src/graph/reachability.cpp` already treats WNAM by its own rule. Corpus: 0 or 1 `WNAM`, always 4 bytes (68 Fallout4.esm, 23 DLCNukaWorld).
- `REGN\Music` (`RDMO`, offset 0, `payload_sizes: [4]`, targets `MUSC`, not nullable, `repeated: true`) is the music link of a sound entry, so it repeats with the entries: 0 or 1 `RDMO`, always 4 bytes, in 14 Fallout4.esm and 9 DLCNukaWorld records.
- `REGN\RegionAreaEdgeFalloff` (`RPLI`, whole-payload `u32`, `repeated: true`) is the edge fall-off of a region area, one row per `RPLI`: xEdit starts each region area with `wbInteger(RPLI, 'Edge Fall-off', itU32)` inside `wbRArray('Region Areas', wbRStruct('Region Area', ...))`, so a record with several areas carries several `RPLI`. The row is whole-payload because the struct member is a bare `itU32` with no trailing members; the neighbouring area members (`RPLD` points, the area's `ANAM`) follow as separate subrecords. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` therefore reads and writes it directly, and `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` exposes one slot per `RPLI`. Corpus coverage was not measured for this row: `Radicle/tools/corpus/non_formid_slots.py` needs a `fo4inspect` binary and nothing is built on this machine, so the row rests on the xEdit pin alone. `RPLD` (points, 8-byte `f32` pairs, count implied by the payload) needs an array kind without a count subrecord, which `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_counted_array` does not have.
- Not rowed: `RDOT` (objects, 52-byte struct with a checked link at offset 0), `RDGS` (grass, 8-byte struct), `RDWT` (weather, 12-byte struct of link, chance and global) are mixed or multi-member arrays that belong to the WP-2 array vocabulary. The remap side already covers `RDOT`, `RDGS` and `RDWT` in `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp:record_fixed_layout_offsets`. `ICON` is a string and stays raw. Superseded for this record by the REGN entry-array and entry-payload section below, which rows `REGN\Icon`, `REGN\Object`, `REGN\Grass`, `REGN\Weather`, `REGN\WeatherGlobal` and `REGN\Sound`; `RPLD` deliberately keeps no row (it repeats once per region area, and a strided row cannot also be `repeated`). `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/unclaimed_link_allowlist.inc` keeps `{"REGN", "RDAT"}` because the new rows claim scalars there, not links, so `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:allowed_unclaimed_payload` still needs the entry.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp` (`RegnRows::DeclaresColorsDataEntryFieldsAndLinks`, `ReadsColorsDataEntriesAndLinks`, `CountsRepeatedDataEntries`, `WritesColorsDataEntryFieldsAndLinksThenRereads`, `MalformedPayloadsHideOrRefuseRows`) over a synthetic plugin: byte-exact reads of every new row including two `RPLI` areas, entry counts, a write-then-reread round trip that touches only the second `RPLI` and holds the first at 80, an out-of-range repeated write refused with `subrecord_missing`, and a truncated `RCLR`/`RDAT` reporting absent where a whole-payload `ANAM` or `RPLI` of the wrong width throws and leaves its bytes alone.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:OMOD (#602 B-54)

- Rows and authoring for `wbRecord(OMOD, 'Object Modification'` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12501-12545`; DATA struct `:12510-12537`). The authoring block `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:OMOD` is `top_level` with EDID, FULL, DESC, MODL (coupled) + MODT, MODC, MODS, MODF, DATA, MNAM, FNAM, LNAM, NAM1, FLTR, matching xEdit's order; the generated entry is `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc` (first rule 910, 14 rules), so `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:authoring_subrecords` returns them.
- Scalar rows (each embedded, `minimum_payload_size` 20 = the byte after Attach Point, so a shorter DATA hides them: `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` returns empty below the minimum): `OMOD\IncludeCount` u32 at 0, `OMOD\PropertyCount` u32 at 4, `OMOD\UnknownBool1` u8 at 8 and `OMOD\UnknownBool2` u8 at 9 (enum False/True), `OMOD\FormType` u32 at 10, `OMOD\MaxRank` u8 at 14, `OMOD\LevelTierScaledOffset` u8 at 15. `OMOD\IncludeCount` and `OMOD\PropertyCount` are raw u32 rows with no coupling to the arrays they count: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` writes any in-range u32, and `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:omod_data_layout_offsets` then derives the Attach Parent Slots / Items / Include / Property offsets from that value, so a count that disagrees with the actual row count desyncs the DATA walk (the payload fails closed on the total, not on the count).
- `OMOD\FormType` enum names are the four `Sig2Int` values from xEdit `:12515-12520`: ARMO 1330467393 Armor, NPC_ 1598246990 Non-player character, WEAP 1346454871 Weapon, NONE 1162760014 None. Form Type is an enum and is never remapped.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:OMOD` `OMOD\LooseMod` is LNAM +0 with `target_union: sigBaseObjects`, `payload_sizes: [4]`, nullable (`wbFormIDCk(LNAM, 'Loose Mod', sigBaseObjects)`, `:12541`: `sigBaseObjects` itself lists NULL, as its first entry, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:75`), matching the `COBJ\CreatedObject` row (`:10273`).
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:OMOD` `OMOD\AttachPoint` is a FormLink field at DATA +16, nullable over KYWD only (`wbFormIDCk('Attach Point', [KYWD, NULL])`, `:12525`).
- `OMOD\TargetOMODKeywords` (MNAM) and `OMOD\FilterKeywords` (FNAM) are packed KYWD arrays, appendable, anchored on DATA/DESC/FULL/EDID and MNAM/DATA/DESC/FULL/EDID for the first element of an absent list (`:12540-12541`). xEdit gives neither a count element, so `packed_array` in `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:FormLinkListStorage` is the storage.
- Attach Parent Slots, the legacy Items array, the Include rows and the property rows are deliberately not rows: their offsets depend on counts inside DATA, so they stay with the walker `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:omod_data_layout_offsets` (landed in #608): u32 count then 4-byte KYWD slots, u32 count then 8-byte Items, Include Count rows of 7 bytes (Mod form ID at row +0), Property Count rows of 24 bytes with the value-type decider at row +0.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:OMOD` `OMOD\Priority` (NAM1, `wbInteger(NAM1, 'Priority', itU8)`, `:12544`) and `OMOD\Filter` (FLTR, `wbFLTR := wbString(FLTR, 'Filter')`, `:5274`, used at `:12543`) are whole-subrecord rows: neither carries an offset or `minimum_payload_size`, so `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` returns the entire subrecord payload for both and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` replaces the FLTR payload wholesale while it writes NAM1 at offset 0. B-54 asks for OMOD rows generally, not only DATA rows, and neither subrecord repeats in the record, so no `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` duplicate arises. The signature-only `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_descriptor` lookup stays nullopt for NAM1 because `AVIF\Type` (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:AVIF`) is already a non-embedded NAM1 row, and it excludes non-embedded zstrings, so FLTR cannot join it either; both rows have to be looked up by record plus path, which is what `Radicle/tests/test_omod_rows.cpp:scalar_field` does.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_omod_rows.cpp` (`OmodRows`) covers descriptor offsets/storage/minimum payload, the Form Type enum names and a negative lookup, reads and writes of the seven scalars through `set_record_scalar`, a 16-byte DATA that hides every header row and refuses Attach Point, Attach Point and Loose Mod target-type refusals, packed MNAM/FNAM insert and remove, the generated authoring order, and `create_record` for OMOD. `OmodRows.PriorityAndFilterRowsOwnTheirWholeSubrecord` covers the two whole-subrecord rows: the NAM1 u8 and FLTR zstring descriptors, a read of each, the out-of-range u8 and wrong-setter refusals, an out-of-range index, an `unchanged` write, and a reread that shows NAM1 at 9, FLTR as `NewFilter` and DATA untouched; the fixture `Radicle/tests/test_omod_rows.cpp:make_plugin` gained the FLTR subrecord for it.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:PERK header (#602 C-10)

- Header rows for `wbRecord(PERK, 'Perk'` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7582-7691`; DATA struct `:7592-7602`). Authoring `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:PERK` is `top_level` with EDID, VMAD, FULL, DESC, ICON and DATA; the generated entry is `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc` (PERK rule, 6 rules), so `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:authoring_subrecords` returns them. DATA is `minimum` 1, `maximum` 65535 and `uncounted`, the same shape as DEBR DATA, because xEdit repeats it: the header struct `.SetRequired` (`:7592-7602`) and one `wbUnion(DATA, 'Effect Data', ...)` inside `wbRArrayS('Effects', ...)` (`:7606`, `:7613`) share the signature, so a PERK holds one DATA per effect section. `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:create_with_rules` still writes one required DATA for a new perk, and its payload is the xEdit header default `0000010100` (Trait 0, Level 0, Num Ranks 1, Playable 1, Hidden 0), kept on the rule because `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:default_usable` needs an explicit default.
- SNAM, NNAM and FNAM are deliberately not authoring rules. One DATA rule has one position in the generated order, while real perks place DATA both before SNAM (header) and after FNAM (effects), so any rule between those two positions makes `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` report `subrecord_order_invalid` on the effect DATA and `subrecord_cardinality_invalid` on the second DATA. Read-only scan of the seven official masters, 656 PERK records: the previous nine-rule list flags 402 records with `subrecord_order_invalid` and 583 with `subrecord_cardinality_invalid`, the six-rule list flags none; every record has at least one DATA (73 records with one, 583 with two or more, up to 35), SNAM is in 329, NNAM in 360 and FNAM in 93. A perk with no DATA at all is still refused with `required_subrecord_missing`, but the flat rule list cannot tell the header DATA from an effect DATA, so a perk whose only DATA is an effect DATA passes.
- The DATA header scalars are rows: `PERK\Trait` (u8 at 0, the `wbBoolEnum` of `wbInteger('Trait', itU8, wbBoolEnum)`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7593`), `PERK\Level` (u8 at 1, `:7594`), `PERK\NumRanks` (u8 at 2, `:7595`), `PERK\Playable` (u8 at 3, bool enum, `wbFromSize(4, ...)` `:7599`) and `PERK\Hidden` (u8 at 4, bool enum, `wbFromSize(5, ...)` `:7601`). Playable is offset 3, not 4: the members are sequential and `wbFromSize` only hides one when the DATA is shorter, so `wbRecordSizeDecider` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:5792-5816`) returns the real member for `DataSize >= 4` and `>= 5`; the vanilla 5-byte `0000010100` is Trait 0, Level 0, Num Ranks 1, Playable 1, Hidden 0. `minimum_payload_size` is 3 for the first three and 4 and 5 for the last two, the same gate as the decider, so a short header DATA simply does not expose the fields past its end, like every other embedded struct row.
- Those five rows are the reason `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidates` has a PERK branch: it returns the first DATA subrecord that precedes the first PRKE, and nothing when the first DATA follows a PRKE. Without it `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` would see one DATA per effect section, set `duplicate` and make `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots` throw `ScalarError` on every perk that has effects. The rule is the single-member binding xEdit does for the header struct; a malformed record whose second DATA precedes the effects is not ambiguous here, the first one is the header, and a record with no header DATA before its effects returns `ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` instead of writing into an effect payload.
- xEdit clamps Num Ranks from 0 to 1 on load and on set (`wbPERKNumRanksAfterLoad` and `wbPERKNumRanksAfterSet`, `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:1033-1045, 1440-1455`). That is an editor convenience, not a storage rule, so `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:PERK` does not copy it: `PERK\NumRanks` writes 0 when asked to, and the vanilla value is unchanged. Mutagen's `Perk.xml` `Data` struct (`PluginEditTool/Mutagen/Mutagen.Bethesda.Fallout4/Records/Major Records/Perk.xml`) lists the same five members in the same order with no size gate, so the field order and widths are confirmed by both oracles; Radicle follows xEdit's `wbFromSize` gates.
- `PERK\Image` is the ICON string and `PERK\SWF` the FNAM string (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:PERK`, both `insertion: existing_only`); xEdit FNAM has no form ID and is not in the link scan.
- `PERK\Sound` (SNAM) targets SNDR and is not nullable; `PERK\NextPerk` (NNAM) targets PERK and is nullable, matching `wbFormIDCk(NNAM, 'Next Perk', [PERK, NULL])` (`:7603-7604`). A row is nullable when the target list it names carries NULL, either in the call (`[PERK, NULL]`, `[KYWD, NULL]`; SNAM's `[SNDR]` has none) or in the union itself (`sigBaseObjects`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:75`); nothing adds NULL to a list. Both have `payload_sizes: [4]`, so `Radicle/tests/test_perk_rows.cpp` (`PerkRows`) writes them on a record that already holds two DATA subrecords and the single-occurrence slot still resolves.
- The effect section (PRKE, the PRKC plus condition rows, EPFT, EPFB, EPF2, EPF3, EPFD, PRKF) is still not rows: `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupDescriptor` has no per-member discriminator, so the union DATA payload (Quest+Stage / Ability / Entry Point) and the EPFD decider cannot be expressed, and offsets past the first occurrence of a repeated subrecord are not addressable. The DATA remap stays with `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:perk_formid_offsets`.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_perk_rows.cpp` (`PerkRows`) covers the ICON/FNAM strings, SNAM/NNAM writes with a target-type refusal and a reread, the generated authoring order, and `create_record` for PERK. `PerkRows.HeaderDataScalarsResolveOnTheHeaderDataOnly` writes all five header scalars and asserts the exact five header bytes with the effect DATA byte-identical, `PerkRows.HeaderDataScalarsAreMissingWithoutAHeaderData` asserts `subrecord_missing` for a perk whose only DATA follows a PRKE and for a perk with no DATA at all, and `ScalarError` for a Level above 255.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACTI, ALCH, AMMO, ARMO, BOOK, CONT, DOOR, FLOR, FURN, INGR, KEYM, LIGH, MISC, MSTT, NPC_, PROJ, TACT, WEAP (#602 XA-1 B-3 C-4 A-35)

The destructible group is a single xEdit definition, `wbDEST := wbRStruct('Destructible', [` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4275-4328`, carried by 18 records, so all 18 get the same 18 rows: `DestructionHealth` (DEST offset 0, i32), `DestructionStageCount` (DEST offset 4, u8), `DestructionFlags` (DEST offset 5, u8, flags), `DestructionResistances` (a `counted_array` on DAMC, stride 8) with the member `DestructionResistanceValue` (offset 4, u32) and the link row `DestructionDamageType` (DAMC offset 0, stride 8, target DMGT), the six DSTD scalars `DestructionStageHealthPercent` (offset 0, u8, `percent_0_100`), `DestructionStageIndex` (1, u8), `DestructionStageModelDamageStage` (2, u8), `DestructionStageFlags` (3, u8, flags) and `DestructionStageSelfDamagePerSecond` (4, i32), `DestructionStageDebrisCount` (16, i32), the DSTD link rows `DestructionStageExplosion` (offset 8, EXPL, nullable) and `DestructionStageDebris` (offset 12, DEBR, nullable), the per-stage strings `DestructionStageSequenceName` (DSTA) and `DestructionStageModel` (DMDL), `DestructionStageColorRemapping` (DMDC offset 0, f32) and the link row `DestructionStageMaterialSwap` (DMDS offset 0, MSWP). Every DSTD, DSTA, DMDL, DMDC and DMDS row is `repeated` with `payload_size` 20 or 4, so stage N is addressed through `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/field_address.hpp:FieldAddress` and `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/field_address.hpp:resolve_field_slots`.

- DEST payload: `wbStruct(DEST, 'Header', [` at `:4276` is Health, `'DEST Count'` (`itU8`, `:4278`), Flags (`:4279`) and `wbByteArray('Unknown', 2)` (`:4283`), eight bytes, so the rows use `payload_size` 8 at offsets 0, 4 and 5. The two unknown bytes stay unexposed, as xEdit does not name them. DSTD is `wbStruct(DSTD, 'Destruction Stage Data', [...], cpNormal, True)` at `:4294`, twenty bytes, so its rows use `payload_size` 20. `wbModelInfo(DMDT)` at `:4319` is cpIgnore, so DMDT carries no row, and `wbEmpty(DSTF, 'End Marker', cpNormal, True)` at `:4325` is a marker, not a field.
- DEST offset 4 is the stage count, not the resistance count. A read-only survey of the shipped masters (Fallout4.esm plus the six DLC esm, records walked group by group) found 443 records with a DEST subrecord of at least 8 bytes, and in all 443 offset 4 equals the number of DSTD subrecords in the same record; it equals the DAMC element count in only 3 of them (DLCworkshop03 has one record with 4 DAMC elements and 3 stages). The row is therefore named `DestructionStageCount`, and its label stays `Stage count`. Bounds are 0..255 with `presentation` `identity`, because xEdit leaves the field a plain `itU8` and the corpus holds 0 to 5.
- Resistances: `wbArrayS(DAMC, 'Resistances', wbStructSK([0], 'Resistance', [wbFormIDCk('Damage Type', [DMGT]), wbInteger('Value', itU32)]))` at `:4288` declares no count element, so the row is a `counted_array` with an empty `count_subrecord` and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:counted_array_subrecords` takes the element count from the payload length over the stride. Reading and writing an element, and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_counted_element` or `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:remove_record_counted_element` on the payload, are therefore correct as they stand: there is no counter subrecord to keep in step, and the guard that refuses to empty an uncounted array applies.
- Stages are `wbRArray('Stages', ...)` at `:4292`, an uncounted run of subrecords, so a stage's rows are addressed by slot position rather than by an array descriptor. No schema shape covers the run: `subrecord_group` demands a fixed `payload_size` per member and DSTA and DMDL are length-varied strings, demands a 4-byte count subrecord and this group's count lives at DEST offset 4, and refuses out-of-order members while xEdit marks the Model member `SetUnordered` (`:4317`). Adding a group would also route every destructible scalar and link read through `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots` and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots` group validation and throw on records that group shape rejects. Whole-stage add and remove are therefore hand-written in `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp`, next to the hand-written table `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_repeated_struct_layouts`.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:insert_destructible_stage` and `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:remove_destructible_stage` add or drop one stage run. A stage starts at a DSTD and ends at the next DSTD or, for the last one, at the first following subrecord that is not a stage member (`Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:stage_member`). Insert writes a 20-byte zero DSTD and an empty DSTF, so the caller fills the stage through the existing rows; the optional DSTA, DMDL, DMDT, DMDC and DMDS are not created. The carrier check is `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:destructible_carrier`, which asks the generated rows for `<record>\DestructionStageHealthPercent`, so the 18 carriers are not listed twice. `record_mismatch` is a record whose rows lack that path, `header_missing` is a carrier whose DEST is absent, duplicated or not 8 bytes, and `too_many_stages` guards the u8 count. Inserting into a record with no stages puts the run directly after the last DEST or DAMC (`Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:stage_start`).
- `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:insert_destructible_stage` takes a slot position in `0 .. stage count` inclusive, so `index == stage count` appends the run after the last stage, and `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:remove_destructible_stage` takes `0 .. stage count - 1`. Both bounds are measured against the spans of the record as it stands when the call starts, so a caller that inserts first and then probes an out-of-range index must probe against the new count.
- `repeated` indexes the nth **such subrecord**, not the nth stage. `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` collects the indices whose signature matches the row's `subrecord` and refuses only when `repeated` is false, so `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\DestructionStageSequenceName` (DSTA), `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\DestructionStageColorRemapping` (DMDC) and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\DestructionStageMaterialSwap` (DMDS) address the first/second/... DSTA, DMDC and DMDS in the record. Every stage carries a DSTD (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\DestructionStageHealthPercent`), but DSTA, DMDC and DMDS are optional per stage, so in a stage lacking a DMDS the row at index N of DMDS is a later stage's. Only DSTD is a reliable stage index; the other three are exact only when every stage carries one.
- `DestructionStageCount` (DEST offset 4) stays a raw `u8` as far as the row API is concerned: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\DestructionStageCount` is `existing_only` and `fo4::set_record_scalar` writes the byte without touching the DSTD run, and `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:insert_destructible_stage` and `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:remove_destructible_stage` write the byte without going through that row. The survey below found count and DSTD equal in all 443 shipped masters, and the stage mutators keep them equal; a caller that sets the count row by hand can still desync it.
- Coverage: the parity matrix counts move as expected. ACTI goes from 11 to 22 scalar rows and ARMO from 14 to 24, `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` is regenerated by `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py`, and the two generated tables `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc` and `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_formlink_lists.inc` are regenerated by `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py` and `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py`. No C ABI export, no hand-written C++ and no remap table changed; DAMC is already in `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_repeated_struct_layouts`.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp` (`DestructibleRows`): the group is asserted present on all 18 carriers and absent on STAT, the header reads and writes Health, Stage count and Flags (with a 300 refused as out of range) and the reread DEST is checked byte by byte, the resistances read, write, insert and remove with a record without DAMC refused, and the DSTD, DSTA, DMDL, DMDC and DMDS rows read and write per subrecord. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp:WholeStageInsertAndRemoveKeepTheHeaderCount` covers the whole-stage mutators, with an out-of-range, a wrong-record, a header-less and a missing-record refusal; `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp:StageModelRowsAreIndexedPerSubrecordNotPerStage` covers the subrecord-versus-stage mismatch; `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp:AuthoringListsCoverTheHeaderAndTheStageMembers` covers the authoring entries. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds here).
- The destructible authoring rules are one and the same group on every carrier that has an authoring block: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\DEST` (and the sixteen other carriers) list `DEST` (0..1, `coupled`), `DAMC` (0..1), then `DSTD`, `DSTA`, `DMDL`, `DMDT`, `DMDC`, `DMDS` and `DSTF` (0..255, not `coupled`), copied from `wbDEST` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4275-4328`), which is the one definition all eighteen records carry (`:5642`, `:5683`, `:5704`, `:5751`, `:5812`, `:5901`, `:6195`, `:6490`, `:6867`, `:7089`, `:7120`, `:9798`, `:9836`, `:9884`, `:10225`, `:10373`, `:12174`, `:12892`). Before this change only FLOR and PROJ listed the stage members, PROJ listed `DSTD`, `DMDL`, `DMDT` and `DSTF` as 0..1 `coupled`, and LIGH listed none, so `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp` (the `subrecord_cardinality_invalid` branch) reported a second stage on a projectile as too many `DSTD`. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LIGH` takes the group after `KWDA`, the position `wbDEST` holds in the LIGH record (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9884`).
- MISC carries `wbDEST` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10225`). Its `authoring` block in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MISC` lists the whole MISC order from xEdit (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10212-10250`, EDID through CDIX), so `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:record_authoring_constraint` returns rules for it, and the field and FormLink rows for `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MISC\DestructionHealth` and its siblings exist. MISC is now creatable, so the refused-creation examples in `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:RefusedCreationConsumesNoFormId` and `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_authoring.cpp:CreateRecordRefusalsLeaveThePluginUntouched` use REGN, which has no authoring block. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:MiscCreatesFromItsGeneratedDefaults` and `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:MiscDestructionStagesFollowTheXEditOrder`.
- The group's rules are one flattened run, `DSTD* DSTA* DMDL* DMDT* DMDC* DMDS* DSTF*`, while a real stage interleaves `DSTD ... DSTF` per stage. `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:local_layout_valid` and the order branch of `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp` therefore report `subrecord_order_invalid` for a record whose stages interleave, and `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp:MultiStageProjectilePassesAuthoringCardinality` asserts the cardinality code only for that reason. The limitation is older than this change, since FLOR already carried the same rules; per-stage ordering needs a rule shape that repeats a run, which `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` does not have.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp:TheStageGroupCarriesTheSameAuthoringRulesOnEveryCarrier` walks the eighteen carriers, requires the nine rules with their bounds and `coupled` flags and requires an authoring block on MISC as well, so it fails if a carrier loses the group or gains the old 0..1 cap. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp:MultiStageProjectilePassesAuthoringCardinality` stages a two-stage PROJ fixture (`Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp:make_proj_plugin`) and asserts no cardinality issue on `PROJ\DSTD` and `PROJ\DSTF`, that a doubled `DEST` still reports one, and that `DSTD` stays unauthorable to add while `OBND` reports `already_present`. Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:GeneratedSchemaMarksSiblingOwnersCoupled now expects `{"MODL", "DEST"}` as PROJ's only coupled rules.
- Payload sizes: the same read-only survey sized every payload: DEST 8 bytes in all 443 records, DSTD 20 bytes in all 868, DMDS 4 bytes in all 18, DSTA and DMDL length-varied strings, exactly the widths the rows declare. DMDC occurs in none of the seven masters, so `DestructionStageColorRemapping` follows `wbDMDC := wbFloat(DMDC, 'Color Remapping Index')` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4273` alone. Earlier revisions of this note claimed "Deviation from xEdit: none found"; that was wrong on the two points above (optional per-stage subrecords indexed by subrecord, and an unsynced stage count) and they are now stated instead.
- The real-data order check has to model the repeating run, because the flat rule list is the right answer for a *single* stage and the wrong answer for the second one. `Radicle/tests/authoring_order.hpp:authoring_order_violation` walks a record's subrecords against `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:authoring_subrecords` and returns the first rule index that goes backwards, except when the decrease is a run restart: a maximal contiguous span of rules whose `maximum` is above 1 is one repeating run, and the decrease is accepted only at the run's first rule and only once that first rule has been seen in the current run. For ACTI the run is `DSTD` (relative index 12) through `DSTF` (18), the first rule of the run is `DSTD` (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACTI\DSTD`, `maximum` 255, preceded by the `maximum` 1 `DAMC`), so `DSTD DSTA DMDL DMDT DMDC DMDS DSTF DSTD ...` is one stage after another and passes, while `DSTD DMDL DSTA` (a member before the run's first rule) and `... KSIZ DSTD` (a run reopened after a rule outside it) both still fail. The failing shapes before this change were `DLCRobot.esm`, `DLCworkshop01.esm` and `DLCCoast.esm` ACTI records whose second stage restarts at `DSTD` and were reported as `DSTD is out of authoring order: index 12 follows 18`. `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:local_layout_valid` and the order branch of `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp` keep the flat non-decreasing model on purpose, so a real multi-stage record is still reported as `subrecord_order_invalid` there (the limitation in the bullet above); `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:FurnTemplateBlockFollowsTheAuthoringOrderInPreflight` pins that the preflight model still refuses `OBTS` before `OBTF`, which a run restart would accept, so the two models are not interchangeable and preflight was left alone.
- The real-data scalar walk has to read a localized string row the way the SDK does. `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records_real.cpp:RowsDecodeAndAuthoringLimitsHold` used `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:decode_scalar` for every row, which requires a single NUL-terminated string, but `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:TERM\BodyText` (`BTXT`), `TERM\ItemText` (`ITXT`), `TERM\ItemResponseText` (`RNAM`) and `TERM\ItemDisplayText` (`UNAM`) are `wbLStringKC` in xEdit (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12715-12751`, `BTXT`, `ITXT`, `RNAM` and `UNAM`) and are listed in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:TERM.localized_subrecords`, so in the localized official masters they hold a four-byte string-table ID and no NUL. The walk now calls `Radicle/src/schema/localized_fields.cpp:read_localized_string` for a `zstring` row whose `localized` flag is set or whose `(record, subrecord)` pair `Radicle/src/schema/localized_fields.cpp:is_localized_field` reports, and keeps `decode_scalar` for every other row. That is the pair predicate `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` already skips a four-byte localized string row with, and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` refuses a scalar write with; the test was the only caller that decoded one. Two thousand four hundred and forty-two `TERM\BodyText` and `TERM\ItemText` failures in `DLCRobot.esm` and the other masters were this.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:MultiStageDestructibleFollowsTheAuthoringOrderPerStage` stages a two-stage ACTI fixture (`Radicle/tests/object_base_fixture.hpp:destructible_acti_plugin`) and asserts `Radicle/tests/authoring_order.hpp:authoring_order_violation` is empty on `DEST DSTD DSTA DMDL DSTF DSTD DSTA DMDL DSTF` and names `DSTA` on `DEST DSTD DMDL DSTA DSTF`, so it fails if the run restart is dropped (the real-data failure returns) or if the restart is widened to a mid-stage member. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds here).

## Destructible stage members (#602 XA-1, B-3, C-4, A-35)

- `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/destructible_stage.hpp:insert_destructible_stage_member` and `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/destructible_stage.hpp:remove_destructible_stage_member` add or drop one optional member of one stage, addressed by stage index. They exist because no other path can: the five optional members carry `0..255` authoring rules with no default bytes (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc` holds `nullptr` and size 0 for `DSTA`, so `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:default_usable` returns false and `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_record_subrecord` answers `SubrecordAddStatus::no_default`), and even with a default the flattened rule run would fail `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:local_layout_valid`, whose non-decreasing rule index a real interleaved stage run `DSTD ... DSTF DSTD ... DSTF` violates. `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:insert_destructible_stage` covers the whole stage only, and writes a zero `DSTD` plus an empty `DSTF`.
