- Member order inside a stage is xEdit's `wbDEST` order (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4275-4328`): `DSTD`, `DSTA`, `DMDL`, `DMDT`, `DMDC`, `DMDS`, `DSTF`. `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:member_rank` holds that order, `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:stage_member` keeps the stage scan of `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:stage_spans` on the same list, and `insert_destructible_stage_member` puts a new member before the first member of the stage that ranks after it, which in a well-formed stage is the `DSTF`. This fixed order is stricter than xEdit's, since the Model struct is `SetUnordered` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4323`) and only its required member DMDL (`:4318`) is fixed; so insert refuses DMDC, DMDS (and DMDT, if it were insertable) into a stage without DMDL, and remove refuses DMDL while DMDT, DMDC or DMDS remains in that stage, both with `model_required` and before any mutation (`Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:stage_has_model_follower`).
- `DSTD` and `DSTF` are refused with `not_optional_member` (they delimit the stage, so whole-stage insert and remove own them), a second copy of a member already in that stage with `member_present`, and anything that is not a stage member at all, including `DEST`, `DAMC` and unrelated subrecords, with the same `not_optional_member`. Defaults come from `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:member_default`: `DSTA` and `DMDL` get a one-byte empty zstring, `DMDC` and `DMDS` four zero bytes, matching their rows (`DMDC` is a 4-byte f32, `DMDS` a 4-byte link). `DMDT` is refused with `no_default`: it is `wbModelInfo` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8918`), a `cpIgnore` decider union whose size varies with the model's texture list, which is why it has no read or write row either (the same reason AMMO `NAM2` stays out). A `DMDS` inserted this way starts as a null link in a row xEdit marks `nullable: false`; the caller sets it straight after through `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:set_record_formlink_field` with the `DestructionStageMaterialSwap` row, and nothing validates it in between.
- Stage index and header checks are `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:locate_stage`, shared by both mutators, so both answer `record_missing`, `record_mismatch`, `header_missing` and `stage_index_out_of_range` exactly as `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:insert_destructible_stage` does. Neither mutator touches the `DEST` stage count: they only add or drop members inside an existing stage.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_stage_members.cpp` (`DestructibleStageMembers`). `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_stage_members.cpp:InsertPlacesTheMemberInsideTheAddressedStage` walks the subrecord signature order of a two-stage `PROJ` after every insert, checks the reread order, the one-byte `DSTA` payloads, the zero `DMDC`, the `DMDS` set to `000A30:Fallout4.esm` through the link row, and that the `DEST` count byte stays 2. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_stage_members.cpp:InsertRefusesMembersWithoutADefaultOrASlot` covers `DMDT`, `DSTD`, `DSTF`, `DEST`, `DAMC`, `EDID`, `DATA`, an already present `DMDL`, an out-of-range stage and the three record-level refusals, and requires the plugin to stay pristine (`Radicle/tests/plugin_bytes.hpp:original_bytes` is non-empty while nothing has been mutated). `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_stage_members.cpp:RemoveDropsOnlyTheAddressedStageMember` removes a member of stage 0 and of stage 1 in turn and requires the reread record to equal the in-memory order and the DEST count byte to stay 2. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_stage_members.cpp:InsertRefusesModelFollowersWithoutDMDL` refuses DMDC and DMDS in the DMDL-less stage 1 with `model_required` and requires the written plugin to stay byte-identical, then allows them once DMDL is in. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_stage_members.cpp:RemoveRefusesDMDLWhileAModelFollowerRemains` refuses DMDL removal while DMDC or DMDS is in stage 0, byte-identical, and allows it once both are gone. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds here).

## Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:insert_destructible_header (#602 XA-1, B-3, C-4, A-35)

- `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/destructible_stage.hpp:insert_destructible_header` and `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/destructible_stage.hpp:remove_destructible_header` create and drop the whole destructible group on a carrier. The stage and stage-member mutators in the same file need a `DEST` to address, and no other path can write one: `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_record_subrecord` reaches `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_with_rules`, whose first gate `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:editable` (`:74`, the refusal at `:88`) rejects any `coupled` rule, so the `coupled` `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\DEST` rule comes back as `SubrecordAddStatus::not_authorable` and its absent default bytes are never reached. `DAMC` is `0..1` and not `coupled`, so it clears `editable` and is refused one step later, at `:97`, with `SubrecordAddStatus::no_default`, because `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc` gives it a null default of size 0 (`{Signature::from_string("DAMC"), 0, 1, nullptr, 0, false, false}`); `DSTD`, `DSTA` and the other stage members are `0..255` and not `uncounted`, so `editable` refuses them like `DEST`, with `not_authorable`. Header creation does not close the resistance ADD gap: `DAMC` stays absent, so `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_counted_element` still needs an existing `DAMC` subrecord to extend and `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp:ResistanceArrayRefusesARecordWithoutDamc` keeps asserting `CountedArrayMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` for a record that has none. An earlier version of this call wrote an empty `DAMC`, a shape no other path produces, and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:remove_record_counted_element` refuses to leave it behind (`CountedArrayMutationStatus::would_empty`), so this call no longer writes one.
- `insert_destructible_header` writes the eight zero bytes xEdit's `wbStruct(DEST, 'Header', [...])` declares (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4276-4283` (TODO-verify: line numbers read from a local xEdit copy, not the pinned 93cc0bc5)), with the stage count byte at offset 4 set to the number of `DSTD` subrecords already in the record (`Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:header_payload`), so a record that carries stages without a header comes out consistent instead of desynced. It writes a `DEST` and nothing else: 358 of the 359 `DEST` headers in `Fallout4.esm` (333) and `DLCCoast.esm` (26) carry no `DAMC`, and xEdit declares the resistance array optional (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4288`, `wbArrayS(DAMC, 'Resistances', ...)`), so writing an empty `DAMC` would put a subrecord in the record that the shipped data almost never has. `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:header_payload` returns no payload when the record holds more than `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:k_max_stages` `DSTD` subrecords, and `insert_destructible_header` answers `DestructibleHeaderStatus::too_many_stages` without mutating the record instead of truncating the count byte with `& 0xFF`, which would write a count of 0 for 256 stages.
- Placement is the authoring rule order, not the end of the record: `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:group_position` takes the rule list from `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:record_authoring_constraint` and `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:authoring_subrecords`, refuses with `DestructibleHeaderStatus::unknown_order` when the record holds a subrecord that is not in its rules (the same refusal `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_with_rules` makes), and otherwise inserts after the last subrecord whose rule index is at or below `DEST`'s. On the eighteen carriers that puts the group after the model block and before the fields that follow it, which is where `wbDEST` sits in each record definition. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACTI` has no `NVNM` rule, so an ACTI that carries a navmesh blob is refused rather than written out of order. FURN had the same gap for the five marker subrecords its destructible carriers use; they are ruled now, see `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\ENAM, NAM0, FNPR, SNAM and NVNM` below.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:group_position` now decides the slot and its validity in one walk: the slot is the index after the last existing subrecord whose rule index is at or below the anchor's, so a record without `EDID` still gets the group after every leading subrecord the schema ranks earlier (`VMAD`, `OBND`, the model block) and before the first subrecord it ranks later; a record whose ruled subrecords are not in non-decreasing rule order has no determinate slot and returns `std::nullopt`, which `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:insert_destructible_header` turns into `DestructibleHeaderStatus::unknown_order` instead of appending the group after a subrecord the schema orders after `DEST` (a `KSIZ` before an `OBND` was the old failure shape). This is the same monotone order rule `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:local_layout_valid` applies on the generic add path, and no other caller reaches `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:group_position`. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_header.cpp:InsertOrdersTheHeaderWithoutEdidAndRefusesACrossedRecord` inserts into an `EDID`-less ACTI carrying `VMAD OBND MODL MODT KSIZ`, requires the `DEST` between `MODT` and `KSIZ`, requires the crossed `KSIZ OBND` record to answer `unknown_order` with the written plugin byte-identical to the original, and reverts the whole plugin after the header is removed. The old code appended the `DEST` after the crossed record, so the `unknown_order` expectation is what separates old from new; the no-`EDID` half is a placement pin, not a regression guard. A read-only scan of the seven official masters found 12118 carrier records without `DEST`; 9129 of those hold only ruled subrecords and all 9129 are in non-decreasing rule order, while the other 2989 carry at least one unruled subrecord and were already refused. The count of ruled-but-non-monotone carriers was therefore 0, so the new refusal takes nothing away from vanilla data.
- `remove_destructible_header` drops `DEST`, `DAMC` and every stage member in one pass (`Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:group_member`, which reuses `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:stage_member` so the seven stage signatures are listed once), leaving the rest of the record untouched. Both mutators answer `record_missing` and `record_mismatch` before any change. Insert refuses a record that already carries a `DEST` **or** a `DAMC`, through `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:carries_header` and with `DestructibleHeaderStatus::header_present`, rather than counting `DEST` subrecords: a duplicated or short `DEST` (which `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:header_index` reports as absent for the stage mutators) cannot be joined by a second one, and a record whose group is a `DAMC` without a `DEST` cannot be given a second `DAMC`, which `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:counted_array_subrecords` would throw on as a duplicate and which would make `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` drop every resistance slot. A record that carries only stage members still takes the header, and `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:header_payload` seeds the count byte from its existing `DSTD`s. Remove's `header_missing` check is `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:has_group_member`, the same predicate the erase uses, so a record whose group is only a `DAMC` or only stage members is cleaned instead of refused, and remove drops every `DEST`, `DAMC` and stage member in the record, which makes it the repair path for a malformed group. The erase is deliberately signature-wide rather than span-bounded: a `DEST`, `DAMC` or stage member that sits outside the contiguous run is dropped too, which is what makes remove the repair path for the doubled `DEST` fixture. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_header.cpp:DuplicatedHeaderIsPresentToInsertAndRemovable` covers the doubled `DEST` of the ARMO fixture, where insert is `header_present` and remove leaves `EDID DATA`.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_header.cpp` (`DestructibleHeader`), a file of its own so `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp` (711 lines) stays clear of the 750-line limit. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_header.cpp:InsertAndRemoveCreateAndDropTheWholeGroup` inserts the header on a bare ACTI, on an ACTI carrying `OBND MODL MODT KSIZ KWDA` and on a DOOR, asserts the group lands between `MODT` and `KSIZ` on the second, writes Health through the existing row, requires the resistance insert to answer `CountedArrayMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` because the header carries no `DAMC`, and adds a stage through `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:insert_destructible_stage` on the record that has neither, re-reads the written bytes (Health 800, count byte 1, no `DAMC`, an empty `DSTF`) and then removes all three headers and requires the whole plugin to be byte-identical to the original file. It also covers the two refusals with a mutated-state check, `DestructibleHeaderStatus::header_present` on a second insert, and `record_missing`, `record_mismatch` and `header_missing`. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_header.cpp:InsertRefusesARecordWithASubrecordOutsideItsRules` covers `unknown_order` with an ACTI carrying `NVNM`. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_header.cpp:InsertSeedsTheStageCountAndRemoveDropsStagesWithoutADestHeader` (an ACTI carrying two `DSTD` and no `DEST`) detects the remove path refusing a stages-only group with `header_missing` and leaving orphaned `DSTD`s behind: it requires insert to be `updated` with the `DEST` count byte at 2 and the group `EDID DEST DSTD DSTD`, then remove to leave `EDID` alone. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_header.cpp:DamcWithoutDestIsRefusedOnInsertAndCleanedByRemove` (an ACTI carrying `DAMC` and no `DEST`) detects the second `DAMC` that made `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:counted_array_subrecords` throw on the resistance array: it requires insert to be `header_present` with the record still `EDID DAMC`, then remove to drop the `DAMC`. `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_header.cpp:InsertRefusesAStageCountThatDoesNotFitTheByte` (an ACTI carrying 256 `DSTD` and no `DEST`) detects the truncated count byte: it requires `DestructibleHeaderStatus::too_many_stages` and a plugin byte-identical to the original, so an insert that writes a `DEST` with count 0 fails it. The regression these detect is a group written at the end of the record, a `DAMC` invented by header creation that no shipped header carries, a duplicated `DAMC`, a count byte wrapped by 256 stages, and a removal that leaves orphaned stage subrecords behind. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds here).

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\ENAM, NAM0, FNPR, SNAM and NVNM (#602 XA-1)

- Why they are ruled: `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:group_position` returns `nullopt` when any subrecord of the record is missing from its authoring rules, so `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/destructible_stage.hpp:insert_destructible_header` answered `DestructibleHeaderStatus::unknown_order` on every FURN record carrying marker data, which is the shape the `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\Markers` and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\MarkerEntryPointList` groups address.
- Order comes from xEdit (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10639-10709`): `wbRArray('Markers', wbRStruct('Marker', [wbInteger(ENAM, 'Marker Index', itS32), wbStruct(NAM0, 'Disabled Entry Points', ...)]))` at `:10692-10699`, `wbRArray('Marker Entry Points', wbStruct(FNPR, 'Marker', [Type u16, Entry Points u16]))` at `:10700-10703`, `wbString(XMRK, 'Marker Model')` at `:10704`, `wbSNAMMarkerParams` (`:9013`) at `:10705` and `wbNVNM` (`:7856`) at `:10708` (TODO-verify: line numbers read from a local xEdit copy, not the pinned 93cc0bc5). The five rules sit at those positions, so the tail of the FURN list reads `NAM1, ENAM, NAM0, FNPR, XMRK, SNAM, APPR, OBTE, OBTF, OBTS, STOP, NVNM`, and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` keeps accepting the vanilla marker tail. The vanilla subrecord order behind that claim is measured, not pending: the read-only scan of the seven masters recorded in the `Radicle/docs/code-notes/Radicle.md:Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN authoring` entry below walked all 783 FURN records and found 144 PRPS subrecords, every one of them after `KWDA` (144/144), and `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records_real.cpp:RowsDecodeAndAuthoringLimitsHold` on the data runner re-runs that order check.
- Bounds: ENAM, NAM0 and FNPR are one subrecord per array entry, so they are `0..65535` like the other uncounted `wbRArray` rules (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:KSSM\KNAM`). SNAM is a single packed `wbArray` payload of 24-byte structs and NVNM a single `wbStruct`, so both are `0..1`.
- Residual refusals on FURN, all three since closed: `PRPS`, `CNTO` and `COED` were the three signatures xEdit's FURN order names and the rule list omitted, so a furniture carrying properties or items answered `DestructibleHeaderStatus::unknown_order` to the header insert: `Radicle/src/plugin/destructible_stage.cpp:group_position` refuses a record as soon as one of its subrecords has no rule, and the same list gates `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_record_subrecord`. Their rows are not the blocker and are not missing: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\Properties` (the uncounted `counted_array` over PRPS, stride 8), `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\PropertyActorValue` and the `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\Items` member rows `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\ItemObject` and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\ItemCount` read and write today, and every one of them is `existing_only`, so nothing but a rule is missing. Neither signature is structurally excluded: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_` already rules `PRPS` as `0..1` and `CNTO` and `COED` as `0..65535`, the shapes FURN needs, at xEdit's positions (PRPS between `DSTF` and `NTRM`, `CNTO` and `COED` between `COCT` and `MNAM`), and FURN's list simply never got them, the same open item `Radicle/docs/code-notes/Radicle.md:Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:PRPS rows (#602 WP-9)` records for ACTI, CONT, MSTT, RACE and TERM. All three are ruled now, `CNTO` and `COED` as of `297532a2` and `PRPS` at the slot the corpus scan proves (see `Radicle/docs/code-notes/Radicle.md:Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN authoring` below), and none of them would hand generic add a new path: a repeated rule without `uncounted` is not `editable`, so `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:editable` makes `add_record_subrecord` answer `SubrecordAddStatus::not_authorable` for `CNTO` and `COED` (the marker arrays above are rules for the same reason), and a `0..1` `PRPS` rule with no `default` stops at `SubrecordAddStatus::no_default`, which leaves `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_subrecord_group` the only path that creates a FURN `CNTO` and writes the `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\ItemTotal` count. The order those rules would claim is what `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records_real.cpp:RowsDecodeAndAuthoringLimitsHold` checks on the data runner.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_header.cpp:InsertAcceptsAFurnRecordThatCarriesMarkerData`; the regression it detects is the refusal above. The vanilla order over the 783 FURN records of the seven masters is checked by `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records_real.cpp:RowsDecodeAndAuthoringLimitsHold`, which runs only on the data runner.

## Radicle/tests/object_base_fixture.hpp:read_row (#602 XA-1)

- `Radicle/tests/object_base_fixture.hpp:read_row` reports `absent` for a slot the schema does not offer, and it tested only `index >= resolved.slots.size()`. `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` pushes one slot per element even when the payload is too short and gates `valid` instead, and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_slot_bytes` slices `payload.subspan(offset, width)` regardless, so the 17-byte `OBTS` of `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:ShortObjectTemplateCombinationsHideTheirHeaderRows` produced one byte against the 18-byte `minimum_payload_size` of `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_\ObjectTemplateLevelMin` and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:decode_scalar` returned `"0"` where the test expected `absent`.
- The helper now checks `valid`, the idiom `Radicle/tests/test_furn_marker_params.cpp:read_member`, `Radicle/tests/test_race_link_rows.cpp`, `Radicle/tests/test_npc_attack_data_rows.cpp` and `Radicle/tests/test_npc_face_tint_rows.cpp` already use. The regression it detects is a short-payload row that reads as a value instead of as absent; the write side was already correct, since `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar`, reached from `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:set_record_scalar`, tests `!resolved.slots[index].valid` and answers `ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing`.

## Typed edit module C ABI (XA-6, #602)

The five typed edit modules that were C++-only now have C exports. Each module keeps the surface of its C++ header: decode returns a heap view freed by the matching `radicle_*_free`, creation returns the new key, and setters refuse a key whose record is absent with `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`.

- `Radicle/src/c_api_forms_internal.hpp:TextStore` is the shared text store for decoded views. It keeps every emitted string in a `std::deque<std::string>`, so a `const char*` handed to the caller stays valid while later fields of the same view are filled; a `std::vector` would reallocate and dangle it. Strings are converted out of the stored Windows-1252 (`fo4::text::windows1252_to_utf8`) exactly as `Radicle/src/c_api_env_internal.hpp:stored_text` does for scalars.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_forms_internal.hpp:TextStore::keep` (the three-argument overload) maps `fo4::schema::LocalizedString` onto `radicle_name_kind` plus either inline text or a string ID, matching the existing `radicle_name_kind` contract in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h`.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_forms_internal.hpp:text_representable` and `bad_text` gate every incoming string before it reaches the writer: `fo4::text::utf8_to_windows1252` failing means the round trip through the stored table cannot hold the value, so the call reports `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` instead of writing a lossy field.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_armor.cpp:radicle_armor_decode` wraps `fo4::forms::decode_armor`; `radicle_armor_addon_decode` wraps `decode_armor_addon` and widens the ARMA `std::byte` unknowns (`unknown_before_detection`, `unknown_before_weapon_adjust`) to `uint8_t`. `Radicle/src/c_api_armor.cpp:radicle_plugin_create_armor` and `radicle_plugin_create_armor_addon` take the same optional-string shape as `fo4::forms::ArmorCreation`, so a NULL model means "absent", not "empty".
- `Radicle/src/c_api_armor.cpp:radicle_plugin_set_armor_models` and `radicle_plugin_set_armor_addon_models` wrap `fo4::forms::set_armor_model_fields` / `set_armor_addon_model_fields`; both keep the ARMO/ARMA `bool` return and turn a `false` into `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` rather than inventing a new status.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_eyes.cpp:radicle_eyes_decode` reports the stored FULL length in `full_raw_size` and resolves `full_text` only when the full subrecord resolves to text; `radicle_plugin_create_eyes` forwards `fo4::forms::create_eyes`'s refusal of the master, deleted, compressed and small-file record bits as `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, so the C caller sees the same rule as `Radicle/src/forms/eyes.cpp:create_eyes`.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_faction.cpp:radicle_faction_relations_decode` and `radicle_faction_ranks_decode` expose the FACT XNAM and rank arrays. The rank view keeps its `std::vector<std::byte>` insignia in `RankHolder::insignia` and points `radicle_faction_rank::insignia` into it, because that pointer must outlive the decode call; `ranks` and `insignia` are sized before the loop so the pointers stay valid. `radicle_plugin_add_faction_relation` and its siblings build a `fo4::forms::FactionRelation`, whose `reaction` is `fo4::forms::FactionCombatReaction`; the C layer passes the raw byte through (`0` neutral, `1` enemy, `2` ally, `3` friendly) and lets `Radicle/src/forms/faction.cpp:require_relation_target` validate the target.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_components.cpp:radicle_components_decode` wraps `fo4::forms::decode_components` for the two covered signatures (MISC CVPA, COBJ FVPA) and reports `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR` for a record whose signature carries no component array, while `radicle_plugin_set_record_components` reports `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` for the same record: a read of a foreign record shape is a parse problem, a write request for one is a bad argument. `radicle_record_supports_components` is the cheap pre-check for callers.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_cell.cpp:radicle_exterior_cell_layout_for` must convert the `fo4::forms::CellError` thrown by `fo4::forms::exterior_cell_grid_layout` for coordinates outside -110..110 (`Radicle/include/fo4/forms/cell.hpp:k_exterior_cell_min_coordinate`), otherwise the exception would cross the C ABI. It maps to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_cell.cpp:find_cell` refuses the same out-of-range coordinates with `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` before it looks for the worldspace plugin, so `radicle_env_find_exterior_cell` and `radicle_exterior_cell_layout_for` agree on out-of-range input instead of one reporting a parse error and the other a bad argument. Its remaining `CellError` cases stay `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR` because those describe a malformed worldspace hierarchy.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_cell.cpp:ref_for` re-indexes the environment for a found CELL, because `fo4::forms::find_exterior_cell` returns a `const fo4::Record*` and the C API hands out `radicle_record` handles, which are `fo4::env::RecordRef` values (`Radicle/src/c_api_env_internal.hpp:to_handle`).
- Registration: the five sources are added to `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt:radicle_c` on their own `target_sources` line so parallel lanes do not collide.
- Bindings: `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py:HEADERS` lists the five new headers, and `RadicleNative.g.cs` plus `bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` were regenerated. `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is unchanged: this lane only adds exports and structs, it changes no existing signature.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_forms_modules.cpp` (`FormsModulesCApi.ComponentsDecodeReportsStoredEntries`, `ComponentsDecodeRefusesARecordWithoutComponents`, `ComponentsSupportReportsCoveredSignatures`, `SetComponentsReplacesTheStoredArray`, `EyesCreateDecodeAndSetText`, `ArmorCreateDecodeAndSetModels`, `FactionCreateRelationAndRank`, `ExteriorCellLayoutUsesFlooredGridGroups`, `InteriorCellCreationAndExteriorRefusal`). They build synthetic plugins in memory, author with the new exports, write, reload an environment and decode the result, and each test carries a refusal case (a record without a component array, an out-of-range coordinate, an orphan rank title, a master-flagged EYES creation).

## Radicle/include/fo4/patch/delta_patch.hpp:build_delta_patch (#602 D-32)

`build_delta_patch` is the minimal library core of xEdit "Create delta patch" (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:3635` `TfrmMain.mniNavCreateDeltaPatchClick`, which copies the newer module and reloads it in `fsIsDeltaPatch` mode so only records that differ from the comparison file survive). It takes two plugins already loaded in an environment, copies the newer one and drops every record whose stored form equals the older module's record at the same local form ID.

- `Radicle/src/patch/delta_patch.cpp:same_stored_record` is the comparison: signature, `RecordHeader::form_version`, header flags and every subrecord's signature and bytes, in order. It compares the stored bytes, not resolved `FormKey`s, so it assumes both modules carry the same master order, which holds for two versions of one module. A difference in any component keeps the record, so the patch is never smaller than xEdit's. Header flags are part of the comparison on purpose: a record that only gained the deleted flag differs and survives, so a delta patch carries the newer module's deletions instead of optimising them away.
- The older-side lookup in `Radicle/src/patch/delta_patch.cpp:build_delta_patch` rebuilds the key as `FormKey{older, record->form_key.local()}` rather than reusing the newer record's key, whose owner is the newer module. Two modules whose `MAST` tables differ, so that one and the same local ID resolves through different master indexes, therefore still match by local ID (`Radicle/tests/test_delta_patch.cpp:DeltaPatchCApi.SameLocalIdUnderADifferentMasterListIsStillDropped`).
- `Radicle/src/patch/delta_patch.cpp:build_delta_patch` skips a record whose `Record::undecodable` is set and keeps it in the patch, because removal goes through `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:remove_records`, which calls `require_decodable` on the keys it is given.
- Removal uses `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:remove_records` rather than `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:delete_local_record`. The delete path refuses a record that an in-plugin FormLink still targets; a delta patch must drop it, because the older module supplies that record at runtime. The consequence is that a delta patch can leave a kept record pointing at a record that only the older module has.
- `DeltaPatchCounts::removed` is `remove_records`' return value. `DeltaPatchCounts::kept` counts the patch's records after removal and excludes the TES4 header, which `Radicle/src/plugin/reader.cpp:collect_records` returns as its first element, so `kept + removed` is the newer module's record count without the header and `kept` is what the C ABI reports as surviving records. The TES4 header is never compared and never lands in the removal list: `Radicle/src/patch/delta_patch.cpp:build_delta_patch` skips it by `Radicle/include/fo4/signature.hpp:sig_tes4`, `Radicle/src/plugin/reader.cpp:find_record` refuses it as a lookup result in both overloads, and removal walks `Plugin::groups`, which the header is not part of.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_patch.cpp:radicle_env_build_delta_patch` checks both names are loaded (`RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`) before calling the library, then writes the patch with `fo4::write_plugin_file`, the same write path `Radicle/src/c_api.cpp:radicle_plugin_write_file` uses. Two names that resolve to one module are refused by `Radicle/src/patch/delta_patch.cpp:build_delta_patch` and surface as `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` through the `DeltaPatchError` catch, so the C ABI does not repeat that check.
- Not covered here, and still open on #86: list merging, the script host (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:9164` `mniNavApplyScriptClick`) and xEdit's `.esu` delta extension and `fsIsDeltaPatch` loader mode. The patch keeps the newer module's HEDR next form ID; it does not renumber and it does not rewrite the master list.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_delta_patch.cpp` (`DeltaPatchCApi.BuildDropsRecordsIdenticalToTheOlderModule`, `PatchIsWrittenOnlyByASuccessfulBuild`) build two synthetic modules, one record identical and one differing plus one only in the newer module, and assert the counts, that the identical record is gone from the written patch, that the differing and extra records are readable through an environment, and that nothing is written when a call is refused. `DeltaPatchCApi.RecordOnlyInTheOlderPluginIsNotCopiedIntoThePatch` pins the other direction, a record only in the older module, which the patch neither carries nor counts; `DeltaPatchCApi.SameLocalIdUnderADifferentMasterListIsStillDropped` pins the master-indexed local ID match; `DeltaPatchCApi.DeletedFlagDifferenceKeepsTheRecord` pins that a record whose only change is the deleted flag survives with the flag still set in the written patch.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR (#602 A-1 A-2)

- Scope: ACHR gains 5 scalar rows (`ACHR\Radius`, `ACHR\Count`, `ACHR\HealthPercent`, `ACHR\LockLevel`, `ACHR\LockFlags`) and 4 FormLink rows (`ACHR\EncounterZone`, `ACHR\LockKey`, `ACHR\Emittance`, `ACHR\MultiboundReference`), all `insertion: existing_only`. The rows are what give both READ and WRITE for lock, radius, health and emittance through the path-addressed scalar and FormLink setters; before them ACHR had no rows at all, so `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_create.cpp:create_placed_actor` created an actor whose extra data could not be addressed.
- xEdit: `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4483` (`wbRefRecord(ACHR)`) is the ACHR definition. `XEZN` :4496, `wbStruct(XLOC)` :4502-4521 with `SetOptionalFrom(4)`, `XCNT` :4549 (`itS32`), `XRDS` :4550 (`wbFloat`), `XHLT` :4551 (`itU32`), `XEMI` :4611, `XMBR` :4614.
- Lock rows share one payload, as in REFR: `ACHR\LockLevel` (u8 at offset 0) and `ACHR\LockFlags` (u8 at offset 8, bit 2 `Leveled Lock`) sit inside the 16-byte XLOC struct, and `ACHR\LockKey` is the FormLink at offset 4 (`payload_sizes: [16]`, `nullable: true` for xEdit's `[KEYM, NULL]`). The 11 level names are copied from the REFR rows (#602 C-28 C-29).
- `ACHR\MultiboundReference` deliberately differs from `REFR\MultiboundReference`: xEdit uses `sigReferences` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4614` for ACHR, so the row admits PLYR, ACHR, REFR, PGRE, PHZD, PMIS, PARW, PBAR, PBEA, PCON and PFLA, where REFR's row (`:11565`) admits REFR only. NULL is left out of the list, as every other Radicle reference row does.
- XLOC payload gate: the three XLOC rows carry `payload_size` 16 (`payload_sizes: [16]` for the key), so a shorter XLOC hides all three instead of reading a level out of a 4-byte payload. xEdit accepts 4, 8, 12 and 16 bytes (`SetOptionalFrom(4)`); `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` returns an empty span when the payload size is not the row's, which is what the test asserts for a 4-byte XLOC. No ACHR corpus survey was available in this worktree, so the 16-byte choice follows the REFR rows and all-16-byte vanilla XLOC evidence recorded above.
- Remap coverage: `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/structured_formids.inc:15` already maps XLOC's key at offset 4 for every record that carries it, and `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formid_subrecords.inc` already lists XEZN, XEMI and XMBR, so `ACHR\LockKey`, `ACHR\EncounterZone`, `ACHR\Emittance` and `ACHR\MultiboundReference` are remapped with no code change.
- Later ACHR rows closed most of what this row listed, tested by `Radicle/tests/test_achr_rows.cpp`, `Radicle/tests/test_achr_extra_rows.cpp` and `Radicle/tests/test_achr_parity_rows.cpp`: patrol `XPRD`, `INAM` and `TNAM` (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR\PatrolIdleTime`, `ACHR\PatrolIdle`, `ACHR\PatrolTopic`), ragdoll `XRGD` (`ACHR\RagdollBoneId` to `ACHR\RagdollRotationZ`, a stride-28 scalar read and written by occurrence), `XLTW`, `XPWR` (`ACHR\ReflectedBy`, `ACHR\ReflectionType`), `XLCM`, `XLKR`, `XAPR` (`ACHR\ActivateParentDelay`), `XLCN`/`XLRL`/`XLRT`, `XWCN`/`XWCU`, `XPLK`, `XHTW`, `XFVC`, `XRFG`, `XATR`, `XESP`, `XLYR` (`ACHR\Layer`, `test_achr_rows.cpp:79,151,439`), `XMSP` (`ACHR\MaterialSwap`, `test_achr_rows.cpp:80,152,440`) and `XAPD` (`ACHR\ParentActivateOnly`, `test_achr_extra_rows.cpp:213,244,272` and `test_achr_parity_rows.cpp:143,279`). Still open, with no ACHR row: `XPPA`, `PDTO`, `XRGB`, `XIS2` and `XATP`.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_achr_rows.cpp` (`AchrRows`, registered in `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt`). Row descriptors (offset, storage, payload gates, targets, lock enum and flag names), a read of all 9 rows from a built ACHR, a 4-byte XLOC that hides the lock rows and drops the `LockKey` link offset, a radius read of the wrong width that throws `ScalarError`, writes (HealthPercent, LockLevel, LockKey, EncounterZone) with a reread and byte checks, and `record_missing` negatives for both setters. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).

## Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_create.cpp:create_placed_reference — ACHR creation (#602 A-1)

- `PlacedReferenceKind::npc` makes `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_create.cpp:create_placed_reference` stage an ACHR instead of a REFR: the signature is chosen at `placed_reference_create.cpp` (`npc ? k_achr : k_refr`), and a placed actor gets the same NAME (base form ID) plus a 24-byte zero DATA as a placed object.
- A base owned by this plugin must be an NPC_ record for `kind == npc` (`placed_reference_create.cpp`, `k_npc`); any other signature throws `PlacedReferenceError("placed NPC base is not an NPC_ record")`. `PlacedReferenceKind::variant` is refused outright with `"placed reference variants cannot be created yet"`, so the eight ReferenceRecord variants can only be decoded, not authored.
- Limit, by design: only a local base is type-checked. A base owned by one of the plugin's masters is accepted on ownership alone (`detail::has_master`), so a master-owned base of the wrong signature still creates an ACHR. Resolving a master record needs the master's own file, which this function does not load; xEdit checks the base with a wb form-ID-check call (`NAME`, `[NPC_]`) at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4483` (the `wbRefRecord(ACHR, 'Placed NPC', ...)` definition).
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_placed_reference_create.cpp:PlacedReferenceCreate.CreatesPlacedActorInInteriorCellAndRoundTrips` and `PlacedReferenceCreate.RefusesVariantKindAndNonNpcBaseWithoutMutation` (added by #602 A-1). Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).

PARW now has 14 scalar rows and 9 FormLink rows, the same counts as PGRE.

C-30 is closed too: REFR has an authoring block (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REFR`, tested by `Radicle/tests/test_preflight.cpp` `AuthoringPreflight.RefrAuthoringBlockListsTheSingletonsInXEditOrder`).

Row descriptors (subrecord, offset, storage, link payload sizes and targets, and the 14/9 per-record counts), a read/write round trip of all three scalars through `scalar_field_bytes` and `patch_scalar_field`, an embedded write on `PARW\OwnerNoCrime` that leaves its siblings alone, and negatives: a 2-byte XAMC throws `ScalarError`, and the shared `XAMC`/`XFVC` subrecords have no signature-only `scalar_descriptor`, so the record path is required. ## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR shared reference rows (#602 A-1 A-2)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR` gains the shared reference rows ACHR was still missing from the `wbRefRecord`/`ReferenceRecord` family, so READ and WRITE reach them through the same record-plus-path scalar and FormLink setters the REFR and the eight variant rows use: scalars `ACHR\Scale` (XSCL f32 0..10), `ACHR\HeadTrackingWeight` (XHTW f32), `ACHR\FavorCost` (XFVC f32), `ACHR\EnableParentFlags` (XESP u8 at offset 4 of the 8-byte struct, bits 0 `Set Enable State to Opposite of Parent` and 1 `Pop In`), `ACHR\OwnerRank` (XRNK i32) and `ACHR\OwnerNoCrime` (XOWN u8 at offset 8 of the 12-byte struct, enum False/True), and FormLinks `ACHR\Base` (NAME, NPC_), `ACHR\EnableParent` (XESP at offset 0, nullable, `sigReferences` without NULL), `ACHR\Owner` (XOWN at offset 0, `[FACT, NPC_]`, payload size 12), `ACHR\ReferenceGroup` (XRFG, RFGP), `ACHR\Layer` (XLYR, LAYR), `ACHR\MaterialSwap` (XMSP, MSWP) and `ACHR\AttachRef` (XATR, the ten reference signatures of `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4577`).
- xEdit: ACHR is defined at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4483`; NAME at `:4494`, XRFG `:4572`, XLYR `:4573`, XMSP `:4574`, XATR `:4577`, XHTW `:4601`, XFVC `:4602`, XESP `:4605`, XOWN and XRNK through `wbOwnership` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9093`, the 12-byte owner struct and its `No Crime` byte at offset 8), and XSCL `:4620`. `wbXESP` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4330`) is the 8-byte enable-parent struct, and `sigReferences` is `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:67`.
- ACHR has no XAMC, so there is no `ACHR\AmmoCount` row, unlike REFR (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11583` is REFR's XAMC): the two definitions are not identical even though they share the helper. XRNK is written by `wbOwnership`, which is why ACHR gets `OwnerRank` beside `Owner`.
- Row shapes are copied from the precedent rows of the same subrecords: `REFR\Scale`, `PARW\EnableParentFlags`, `PARW\OwnerNoCrime`, `PARW\OwnerRank`, `PARW\EnableParent`, `PARW\Owner`, `REFR\Layer`, `REFR\MaterialSwap`, `REFR\ReferenceGroup`. Remap coverage needs no change: XOWN, XESP and XATR are already slots in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/structured_formids.inc` and `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formid_subrecords.inc`.
- Still open in A-1 and A-2 after the later ACHR rows (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR`): `XPPA` (no row), `PDTO` (no row), `XRGB` (no row), `XIS2`/`XIBS` (no row) and `XATP` (no row). The patrol, ragdoll, `XLCM`, `XLKR`, `XAPR`, `XWCN`/`XWCU`, `XLTW`, `XPWR`, `XPLK`, `XLCN`/`XLRL`/`XLRT`, `XAPD`, `XATR`, `XHTW`, `XFVC`, `XRFG`, `XLYR` and `XMSP` rows are closed (see the ACHR row above, `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR`). `XESP`'s DOOR form is not re-checked here. No ACHR corpus survey was available in this worktree, so the rows carry no authoring defaults and ACHR still has no authoring block.

All 100 enum names (0 Cave .. 98 `Custom 98`, 99 `Custom 99`) are copied verbatim from that `wbEnum`, including `Gov't Building / Monument`; the `TNAM` rows of the other 27 records are unrelated scalars, so this row is addressed by record plus path only.

XLCN is non-nullable with one target; XLRL carries `targets: [LCRT, LCTN]` with `nullable: true` for xEdit's trailing NULL, the second Radicle REFR link row to be nullable after `REFR\LockKey`. Both are `payload_sizes: [4]`, `offset: 0`, `insertion: existing_only`, and both subrecords are already remap slots in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formid_subrecords.inc`, so no remap code changed.
