## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:QUST (#602 C-16)

- Scope: QUST gains its general-data block. Five scalar/string rows on DNAM as one 12-byte struct (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:QUST\Flags` at offset 0 u16 flags, `QUST\Priority` offset 2 u8, `QUST\DelayTime` offset 4 f32, `QUST\Type` offset 8 u8), each carrying `payload_size: 12` so a shorter DNAM hides them instead of reading past the payload. The unused bytes at offsets 3 and 9-11 are not rows. String rows `QUST\Name` (FULL), `QUST\Filter` (FLTR), `QUST\Description` (NNAM) and `QUST\SwfFile` (SNAM). FormLink fields `QUST\Location` (LNAM to LCTN), `QUST\QuestCompletionXp` (XNAM to GLOB) and `QUST\QuestGroup` (GNAM to KYWD), all offset 0, one 4-byte payload. FormLink list `QUST\TextDisplayGlobals` (QTGL to GLOB), repeated per subrecord.
- Authoring: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:QUST` gains a `top_level` placement with 11 subrecord rules (EDID, VMAD, FULL, DNAM minimum 1 with a 12-zero-byte default, ENAM, LNAM, XNAM, QTGL 0..65535, FLTR, GNAM, SNAM). QUST previously had no authoring entry, so `create_record(QUST, ...)` returned `not_authorable`; it now creates a record holding EDID and a zeroed DNAM. No rule is `coupled`: DNAM is minimum 1 so it is present in any record this schema creates, and the general rows are all `existing_only`, so nothing is inserted into an existing record.
- CTDA and NNAM are deliberately absent from the `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:QUST` authoring rules. Both are reused by the nested stage, objective and alias sections: `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10740` (Stages) reuses `CTDA` in Log Entries and Targets, and `:10772` (Objectives) reuses `NNAM` as Display Text. `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:local_layout_valid` and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` both require the schema-known subrecords of a record to appear in non-decreasing rule index order, so a flat CTDA (index 9) or NNAM (index 10) rule reported `subrecord_order_invalid` on any real quest whose objectives carry display text, and made `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:subrecord_authoring` refuse every add to such a record. GNAM and SNAM stay: both are top-level only, so they keep their maximum-1 cardinality check. `Radicle/tests/test_qust_general_rows.cpp:AuthoringAcceptsAQuestWithNestedStageConditions` pins a quest that carries stage and objective CTDA and NNAM after FLTR and asserts no order issue.
- xEdit: `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10684` (`wbRecord(QUST)`) for the general block, DNAM struct, ENAM enum and the FLTR string. The DNAM flag names and the 15 Type names are xEdit's. QUST carries no `GNAM` in xEdit; `QuestGroup` comes from Mutagen (`PluginEditTool/Mutagen/Mutagen.Bethesda.Fallout4/Records/Major Records/Quest.xml`, `FormLink name="QuestGroup" recordType="GNAM" refName="Keyword"`), which places it after NNAM and before SNAM — that is the rule order used here.
- `CITC` is deliberately absent: QUST's two condition arrays are plain repeated `CTDA` (`wbConditions`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5183`), and no QUST subrecord in the pinned xEdit is `CITC`. Adding `CITC` to the authoring rules would let `add_record_subrecord` write a count subrecord the record never uses.
- `NAM0` is not in this row's block. In QUST it is `Next Quest` (QUST) inside a Log Entry (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10759`), a repeated structure that belongs with the stage and log-entry rows, not the general data.
- Nullability follows the repo convention used for every other lane (CMPO `ModScrapScalar` is Mutagen `IFormLinkNullable` yet `nullable: false`): the LNAM, XNAM and GNAM rows and the QTGL list are `nullable: false`. Mutagen types all four as nullable; the CORPUS does not distinguish, so the flag matches the neighboring rows rather than Mutagen.
- Anchors: `QUST\TextDisplayGlobals` carries `anchor_predecessors` (LNAM, XNAM, ENAM, DNAM, FULL, VMAD, EDID) so the first QTGL of an empty list lands after the last present predecessor and before FLTR, matching the xEdit order (QTGL array, then FLTR) and the Mutagen write order. FLTR is not a predecessor: it follows the QTGL block in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:QUST`, and `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:empty_list_insertion_point` takes the LAST present predecessor, so listing it placed the first QTGL after it. The list is `appendable`, so a record with no anchor still takes the entry at the end of the record.
- Derived files: the four codegen `--check` targets were re-run; `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc`, `.../generated_record_constraints.inc` and `.../generated_formlink_lists.inc` changed, `.../generated_lstring_fields.inc` did not. Every scalar name array after QUST's shifts index by two, which is the bulk of the scalar diff. `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` regenerates: QUST moves from L2 to L4 and the tier counts go to L0 5, L1 0, L2 4, L3 0, L4 138.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_qust_general_rows.cpp` (`QustGeneralRows`, 10 cases) covers the row descriptors (offsets, storage, 12-byte payload, presentations, name tables), a read of every general field and link from a built plugin, a write of each field plus a reparse that compares the exact DNAM and ENAM bytes and the renamed strings, a bounds refusal (Priority 256, Flags 65536) with a byte-identical plugin, a 4-byte DNAM that exposes nothing and refuses a write, a FormLink edit plus a null refusal, the QTGL list read/edit/insert/remove with the resulting subrecord order, an empty-list insert that lands before FLTR, a creation that emits exactly EDID and a 12-zero-byte DNAM, and an authoring refusal for `QOBJ` (unknown order) and a `QTGL` removal (`not_authorable`, repeatable). Negative cases are the two refusals and the short-payload case. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:TERM (#602 C-47)

- Scope: TERM gains the two repeated item blocks and the holotapes. Body text: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:TERM\BodyText` (BTXT, `repeated`). Menu items: `TERM\ItemText` (ITXT), `TERM\ItemResponseText` (RNAM), `TERM\ItemType` (ANAM, u8, 17 names), `TERM\ItemId` (ITID, u16), `TERM\ItemDisplayText` (UNAM), `TERM\ItemImage` (VNAM), all `repeated`, plus the FormLink field `TERM\ItemSubmenu` (TNAM to TERM, `repeated`, one 4-byte payload). Holotapes: the `TERM\Holotapes` subrecord group (`count_subrecord` COCT, one required non-repeatable CNTO member with `payload_size` 8 and the `0000000001000000` default), its `TERM\HolotapeCount` (i32 at offset 4) and `TERM\Holotape` (offset 0, nullable, target NOTE) rows and the `TERM\HolotapeTotal` COCT u32 row the generator requires for a group count. All rows are `insertion: existing_only`; no authoring rule changed, so nothing is inserted into an existing record and TERM creation is unchanged.
- Row addressing: a `repeated` row is indexed by *occurrence* of its own subrecord, not by menu-item or body-text index. ITXT, ANAM and ITID are the leader and the two members Mutagen marks `nullable="False"` (`PluginEditTool/Mutagen/Mutagen.Bethesda.Fallout4/Records/Major Records/Terminal.xml`), so for those three the occurrence index is the item index. RNAM, UNAM, VNAM and TNAM are optional per item, so their occurrence index can skip an item that does not carry them; a caller that needs the item index must read the optional member of the item it is editing rather than assume alignment. This is the same trade-off `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:HDPT\PartFilename` already ships.
- xEdit: `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12671` (`wbRecord(TERM)`), body text at `:12719-12727` (`wbLStringKC(BTXT)`, `wbConditions`, `SetCountPath(BSIZ)`) and menu items at `:12729-12764` (`ITXT`, `RNAM`, `ANAM` enum, `ITID`, `UNAM`, `VNAM`, `TNAM`, `wbConditions`, `SetCountPath(ISIZ)`). Holotapes at `:12699-12709` (`wbInteger(COCT)` then the `CNTO` array with a wb form-ID-check call on `Item` ([NULL, NOTE]) and a count defaulting to 1, `SetCountPath(COCT)`). The 17 ANAM names are xEdit's.
- Not covered, and why: the **per-item conditions** (the `wbConditions` repeated CTDA inside each body-text and menu-item entry). They are not a plain repeated row: each condition is a variable-length CTDA plus its optional CIS1/CIS2 parameter strings (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5183-5251`), so CTRL is needed and the term conditions now go through the `condition_scopes` rows described in `Radicle/src/schema/condition_scopes.cpp:terminal_body_text_ranges and terminal_menu_item_ranges (#602 C-47)`, which are separate from the string rows below. The body-text and menu-item **string** members also cannot go in a subrecord group: `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` requires a fixed `payload_size` for every member, and BTXT, ITXT, RNAM, UNAM and VNAM are variable-length. `TERM\ActiveMarkers` (MNAM u32) is unchanged and is not the xEdit `wbMNAMFurnitureMarker` struct; it is out of this row.
- Corpus: not scanned in this lane (no `FO4_DATA_DIR` on the authoring machine), so the row shapes come from xEdit plus Mutagen only. The one unverified assumption is that every vanilla menu item carries the required ITXT, ANAM and ITID, and that body-text entries always carry BTXT; the env-gated real-data test is the place to confirm both.
- Derived files: the four codegen `--check` targets were re-run. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc` gained the rows and now emits three `k_subrecord_groups` entries (CONT, FURN, TERM) instead of two; `.../generated_formlink_lists.inc` gained `TERM\ItemSubmenu`. `.../generated_record_constraints.inc` and `.../generated_lstring_fields.inc` did not change (BTXT, ITXT, RNAM and UNAM were already in TERM's `localized_subrecords`). `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` regenerates TERM from 9 to 13 fields, 2 to 5 lists and 7 to 10 rows.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_term_menu_rows.cpp` (`TermMenuRows`, 11 cases) covers the row descriptors (subrecord, storage, enum names, the ANAM target list, the group's count and member shape), reads by occurrence, writes of each member with exact payload comparison after a reparse, a bounds refusal (ItemType 256, ItemId 65536) with a byte-identical plugin, reads of the holotape runs, a link and count write that leaves COCT alone, an insert in the middle and a remove with the resulting subrecord order and the synced COCT, an insert into a terminal with no holotapes that lands after EDID and before MNAM, `TERM\HolotapeTotal` refused as a plain scalar, and `add`/`remove` of CNTO and COCT refused by authoring. Negative cases are the two bounds refusals, the scalar refusal and the two authoring refusals. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).

## Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:insert_scene_phase (#602 C-35)

- Scope: SCEN phases gain add, remove and a NAM0 name edit. Everything else in C-35 (actor add/remove, action add/remove, action payload writes, action NAM0, creation) is still open.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:insert_scene_phase` writes one phase as `HNAM`, `NAM0` (the name), `NEXT`, `NEXT`, `WNAM` 350, `HNAM`, matching `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8899-8922`: two empty NEXT separators per phase and an HNAM marker on each side. 350 is xEdit's `SetDefaultNativeValue(350)` for `WNAM Editor Width`. Phase `FNAM` and `SCQS` are deliberately not written, because xEdit gives neither a native default (unlike WNAM) and a zeroed `SCQS` would mean "set parent quest stage 0" rather than "no stage"; a phase added this way reports `subrecord_missing` for `SCEN\Phase\Flags` and `SCEN\Phase\QuestStageOn*` until a caller inserts those subrecords.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:phase_anchor` picks the insertion index. Before an existing phase it is that phase's opening HNAM. Past the last phase it is the last phase's closing HNAM plus one, so a new phase lands after the phases and before the actors; with no phases at all it is the first actor, then the first action, then `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:tail_anchor`. `tail_anchor` is the first `PNAM`, `INAM`, `CRIS`, `SCQS` or `TNAM`, which is the tail block that `Radicle/src/environment/scene_layout.cpp:scene_layout` reports as `SceneLayout::tail`; those five are the only SCEN subrecords after the action array (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9105-9131`).
- Removing uses the phase's own `[open, close]` span from `SceneLayout::phases`, so each phase is independent: `Radicle/src/environment/scene_layout.cpp:scene_layout` treats every HNAM as one phase's close and the next HNAM as the following phase's open, and each phase carries both markers.
- Both edits return `fo4::SubrecordGroupMutationStatus` (`Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:45`), which already carries `record_missing` and `index_out_of_range`. A record that is not SCEN, or a malformed SCEN, throws `fo4::schema::ScalarError` through `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:checked_layout`, the same way `set_scene_scalar` does.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:set_scene_phase_name` replaces the phase's NAM0 zstring in `[open + 1, close)` and reports `unchanged` when the bytes already match. `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:phase_body` is that span.
- C ABI: `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_dialogue.h:radicle_plugin_insert_scene_phase`, `:radicle_plugin_remove_scene_phase` and `:radicle_plugin_set_scene_phase_name`, implemented in `Radicle/src/c_api_dialogue.cpp`. They map `index_out_of_range` and a thrown `ScalarError` to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `record_missing` to `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`. `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is unchanged; `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` was regenerated with `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` and gained the three declarations.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_scene_phase_edit.cpp` (`ScenePhaseEdit`, 5 cases) covers insert-in-the-middle and append-at-the-end placement, removal compared byte-for-byte against the pre-edit subrecord list, the name setter's three statuses, and the refusals (`index_out_of_range`, `record_missing`, a thrown `ScalarError` on a QUST key) with an unchanged `write_plugin` byte image. `Radicle/tests/test_dialogue_writer_c_api.cpp:DialogueWriterCApi.ScenePhaseAuthoringStatusesMapAndSurviveReload` covers the three exports' status mapping, the phase count, a write/reload round trip and the decoded phase names.

## Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:insert_scene_actor (#602 C-35)

- SCEN actor groups and action groups are now addable and removable next to the phases. `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:insert_scene_actor` and `:remove_scene_actor` treat one actor as the `ALID`/`LNAM`/`DNAM` four-byte triplet that `Radicle/src/environment/scene_layout.cpp:scene_layout` records in `SceneLayout::actors`, so removal erases exactly those three subrecords and leaves the phases, the actions and the tail untouched.
- The inserted actor carries xEdit's stored defaults (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8924-8952` at 93cc0bc5): `ALID` -1 (`SetDefaultNativeValue(-1)`), `LNAM` 0 (no default) and `DNAM` 26 (`SetDefaultNativeValue(26)`). `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:new_actor_subrecords` builds them; a decoded actor then reports the -1 alias.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:actor_anchor` puts the new triplet where the caller's index falls among the existing actors, after the last actor when the index is the actor count, and otherwise before the first action, so a scene with no actors gains one between the phases and the actions. `:groups_end` is that fallback: after the last action, else after the last actor, else after the last phase, else `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:tail_anchor`.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:insert_scene_action` writes the action's own `ANAM` type, the `ALID` -1 default and the empty closing `ANAM`, and no payload: xEdit's `wbSceneActionTypeAfterSet` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:1501-1520`) removes the type-specific action element whenever the type changes, so a new action is header-only. `:new_action_subrecords` builds the three subrecords and `:action_anchor` places them among the actions, or after the last action when there is no action at that index. A type above 6 is not in the stored enum (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8956-8966`) and throws `fo4::schema::ScalarError`.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:remove_scene_action` erases the action's whole `[open, close]` span from `SceneLayout::actions`, payload included, which keeps every later action and the tail aligned.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:insert_at` is the shared insertion used by the phase, actor and action inserts: it splices the new subrecords at the anchor and marks the record modified, so all three report the same `fo4::SubrecordGroupMutationStatus`.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:set_scene_action_name` writes the action's NAM0 name. It replaces the zstring in the action header span when NAM0 is present (`unchanged` when the bytes already match) and otherwise inserts NAM0 at the action opener plus one, which is its slot in the header order (`Radicle/src/environment/scene_layout.cpp:k_action_header`, NAM0 before ALID), so a header-only action from `insert_scene_action` gains a name without breaking the header walk. An out-of-range action index reports `subrecord_missing`, the same status `:set_scene_phase_name` uses.
- C ABI: `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_dialogue.h:radicle_plugin_insert_scene_actor`, `:radicle_plugin_remove_scene_actor`, `:radicle_plugin_insert_scene_action`, `:radicle_plugin_remove_scene_action` and `:radicle_plugin_set_scene_action_name`, implemented in `Radicle/src/c_api_dialogue.cpp`. `record_missing` maps to `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, `index_out_of_range` and a thrown `ScalarError` to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is unchanged and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` was regenerated with `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py`.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_scene_actor_action_edit.cpp` (`SceneActorEdit`, `SceneActionEdit`, `SceneActorActionEdit`, 10 cases) covers insert placement (middle, append-at-the-end, into an actor-less scene), removal compared byte-for-byte against the pre-edit subrecord list for both a triplet and a full action span with payload, the header-only action's decoded defaults, the name setter's replace, insert and refusal paths, and the refusal statuses. `Radicle/tests/test_dialogue_writer_c_api.cpp:DialogueWriterCApi.SceneActorAndActionAuthoringStatusesMapAndSurviveReload` covers the four exports' status mapping, the group counts, a write/reload round trip and the decoded actor and action values.

## Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:set_scene_action_formlink, Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:action_type_matches, Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:k_scalars (#602 C-35)

- Scope: the type-specific payload of a SCEN action becomes addressable. `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:k_scalars` and `:k_links` gained rows in the new `Scope::action_payload`, whose span is `{SceneActionSpan::header_end, close}` from `Radicle/src/environment/scene_layout.cpp:scene_layout`, so a payload subrecord can never be confused with the same signature in the action header, in the scene tail or in a phase. The rows are xEdit's union at `source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9012-9103 @93cc0bc5`: `DMAX`, `DMIN`, `CRIS` (two floats), `DEMO`, `DEVA`, `SNAM` and `TNAM` for the timer, `DTGT`, and the link members `DATA`, `PNAM`, `VENC`, `ONAM`, `PTOP`, `NTOP`, `NETO`, `QTOP`, `PLVD`, `JOUT`, `DALC`, `NPOT`, `NNGT`, `NNUT`, `NQUT`, `NPOS`, `NNGS`, `NNUS`, `NQUS`, `STSC` and the radio-only `HTID` play sound.
- The action type is part of the address: `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:action_type_matches` reads the u16 from the action's opening `ANAM` and tests it against the row's bit mask in `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:action_type_bit`, built from `k_dialogue_action` through `k_radio_action`. A row whose mask excludes the stored type reports `subrecord_missing`, which is what keeps `SCEN\Action\AnimArchType` (`PNAM` as a KYWD in a dialogue action) away from the package action's `PNAM`, whose element is a PACK in a list. A type of 16 or more cannot be shifted into the mask and matches nothing.
- Member names follow xEdit's labels, and only the ones whose meaning differs per type were split: `SCEN\Action\DialogueSubtype` is the `VENC` of a dialogue or radio action while `SCEN\Action\PlayerPositiveDialogueSubtype` is the `VENC` of a player or NPC response action, and `SCEN\Action\Topic` serves both `DATA` members because xEdit labels both "Topic" over `[DIAL,NULL]`.
- Both writers edit an existing payload subrecord only; a payload the action does not carry stays `subrecord_missing`, and no member is inserted. Insertion would need an order for members that xEdit fills from the struct order, and the members that xEdit stores as lists (`PNAM` packages, `HTID`/`DTID` headtracking, `LCEP` start scenes with their own `CITC` conditions) are still opaque views. Timer `SCQS` (xEdit's `itS16` "Set Parent Quest Stage") has no row either: the corpus already caught one wrong stored width in this record, and 2 against 4 bytes cannot be settled without the game. Writing the action's `ANAM` type in place is still refused (`SCEN\Action\Type` is not a row), because xEdit drops the payload on a type change.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/scene_writer.cpp:set_scene_action_formlink` is the payload link writer. It shares `:check_link_target` and `:write_link` with `set_scene_formlink`, which keeps one copy of the NULL, owner and target-signature rules and the four-byte read-back compare. A payload path through the index-free `:set_scene_formlink` throws "requires an action index" and a header or tail path through the new writer throws "is not an action payload link", so neither export can silently write the other scope.
- C ABI: `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_dialogue.h:radicle_plugin_set_scene_action_formlink` in `Radicle/src/c_api_dialogue.cpp` maps `record_missing` to `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, `record_mismatch` and a thrown `FormLinkFieldError` or `FormIdError` to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and `subrecord_missing` to `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PluginFile.cs:SetSceneActionFormLink` wraps it and `RadicleNative.g.cs` was regenerated with `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py`; `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is unchanged.
- A payload member is only reachable when the action header walk stops before it, so an action whose stored `SNAM` or `TNAM` doubles as a header member needs its header copy first, exactly as official data stores it. `Radicle/tests/test_scene_writer.cpp:SceneWriter.ActionPayloadRowsFollowTheStoredActionType` covers that shape: two `SNAM`s in a timer action where only the second is `SCEN\Action\TimerMax`, the same `DMAX` written in a dialogue and in a radio action, the type-gated refusals, the index-free export's refusal, and the payload bytes after a write/reload round trip. `Radicle/tests/test_dialogue_writer_c_api.cpp:DialogueWriterCApi.FieldSceneAndAuthoringStatusesMapAndSurviveReload` covers the export's status mapping. Nothing in this lane was compiled or run: CI is the first build.
## Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_vmad, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_vmad_script, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_vmad_property, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:remove_vmad_script, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:remove_vmad_property, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:replace_vmad_property (#602 D-23 B-1 XA-3)

- Scope: the leading-script list and the property list of every record that carries a plain VMAD become authorable. `add_vmad` creates the payload; `add_vmad_script` and `remove_vmad_script` insert or drop a whole script entry at a script index; `add_vmad_property` and `remove_vmad_property` do the same inside one script; `replace_vmad_property` swaps one property entry, which is how a property type, name or flag set changes. Scalar value edits stay on `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_vmad_property`. No C ABI or C# export was added in this lane, so the structure API is native-only for now; the C ABI surface for nested VMAD struct marshalling is a separate piece of work.
- Offsets: `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_property` records `VmadProperty::offset` (first byte of the entry, its name length) and already had `value_offset`/`value_size` (the value bytes alone), and `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_vmad_scripts` now records `VmadScript::offset` (first byte of the name length) and `VmadScript::property_count_offset` (the u16 property count, read after the script flags). `read_property` throws nothing on a zero-length property (type 0) so `value_offset + value_size` is the entry end for every type, including the empty one.
- Splicing: an entry is removed as `[offset, value_offset + value_size)` for a property and `[offset, next script's offset or leading_end)` for a script, so the inserted bytes can never shift a recorded offset that is still needed. `VmadEdit::leading_end` is `vmad->data.size() - scripts.trailing_bytes`, which keeps every insertion inside the script list: a quest or scene fragment tail after the scripts is preserved byte-for-byte, and a script removed at the end of the list leaves the tail where it was. The count word is written after the splice from the list length (`+1` on add, `-1` on remove) rather than incremented in place, so the count cannot drift from the entries. The script count lives at data offset 4 (version and object format are the first two 16-bit words); the property count lives at `property_count_offset`, which is always before the splice point, so it stays valid after it.
- Vocabulary: `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:encode_property` re-encodes one property from its decoded form. Types 0 through 5 keep their scalar shape, 7 and 17 write their struct members, 11 through 15 write their array count and elements, 16 writes a zero element count, and any other type ends in `schema::ScalarError`. Struct members are scalars only: `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:append_typed_value` refuses a member of type 7 or 11 through 17, which is why `structs_of` also refuses a property whose members could not be decoded (`Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:decode_structs` returns `nullopt` for a non-scalar member). Both decoded shapes of an object value are handled by `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:object_value`: a property carries `optional<RawFormId>` plus `optional<int16_t> alias`, a struct member carries `optional<VmadObjectElement>`, and object format 1 puts the form ID first while format 2 puts a zero word then the alias first. The empty payload `add_vmad` writes, `06 00 02 00 00 00`, is xEdit's own default: version 6 and object format 2 from `SetDefaultNativeValue` at `source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3873-3881 @93cc0bc5`, then no scripts.
- Where a new VMAD goes: after the EDID subrecord, else at index 0. Every one of the 31 records whose `schema/fallout4/fields.json` authoring rule list names VMAD has VMAD at index 1 behind EDID (`ALCH`, `AMMO`, `BOOK`, `INGR`, `KEYM`, `FLOR`, `PARW`, `PBAR`, `PBEA`, `PCON`, `PFLA`, `PGRE`, `PHZD`, `PMIS`, `TREE`, `STAT`, `LIGH`, `NOTE`, `PACK`, `INFO`, `ACTI`, `CONT`, `DOOR`, `FURN`, `MSTT`, `TACT`, `TERM`, `SCEN`, `WEAP`, `MGEF`, `NPC_`), and xEdit opens each of those records with `wbEDID, wbVMAD`. The generic authoring path (`src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:default_usable` requires `has_default()`) cannot add a VMAD because `fields.json` gives VMAD no default, which is why `add_vmad` owns the payload.
- `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:vmad_authorable` is the record-signature allow list. It is the 31 records above plus `ACHR`, `ARMO`, `MISC`, `QUST`, `RACE`, `REFR` and `PERK`: those seven carry VMAD in xEdit (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4493` ACHR, `:5794` Armor, `:10218` Misc. Item, `:10689` Quest, `:11449` Race, `:3212` inside `ReferenceRecord`, which is REFR and the placed family, `:7587` Perk) but have no VMAD row in `schema/fallout4/fields.json`, and adding one is a schema and generator change this lane does not own. `REFR`, `PARW`, `PBAR`, `PBEA`, `PCON`, `PFLA`, `PGRE`, `PHZD` and `PMIS` are the reference family: `ReferenceRecord` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3200,3212` carries the VMAD, and the placed records at `:5944-5951` are built from it. Everything else, including records that hold a fragmented VMAD only, returns `not_authorable` (`SNDR`, checked by the test).
- Refusals: an index past the end, a record or subrecord that is absent, a record that already has a VMAD (`already_present`), a script name or property name longer than 65535 bytes, a property whose typed value is missing, a non-finite float, a struct property that holds more than one struct, a nonempty type 16, an object value whose owner or target type is not allowed (the `encode_value` rules already used by the scalar setter), and a duplicate VMAD subrecord all end in a `schema::ScalarError` or a status before the payload changes. `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:load_vmad` is the single gate: it refuses a payload whose `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:vmad_coverage` is not complete (unsupported property, malformed, truncated, unknown trailing bytes), a payload that `read_vmad_scripts` marked unsupported, and a version or object format outside 5/6 and 1/2. A truncated payload is caught by `vmad_coverage` first, so a structure edit throws `schema::ScalarError` and not the `parse_error` the reader raises internally. An undecodable record is refused by `src/plugin/record_edit.hpp:find_mutable_record` before any of this.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_structure.cpp`. `VmadStructure.AddAndRemoveScriptKeepEveryOtherByte`, `VmadStructure.AddedPropertiesReparseAndRemovingThemRestoresThePayload` (all 14 encodable property types added at the tail, then removed one by one until the payload is byte-identical to the original), `VmadStructure.ReplacingAPropertyWithItselfIsByteIdenticalForEveryType` (both object formats, `unchanged`), `VmadStructure.ReplaceWritesStructValuesAndChangesAPropertyType`, `VmadStructure.AddVmadWritesTheEmptyPayloadAfterEditorId`, `VmadStructure.AddVmadWithoutEditorIdGoesFirstAndRefusesOtherRecords`, `VmadStructure.StructureEditsRefuseBadIndicesAndUnencodableValuesAtomically` (negative cases, and the plugin bytes are unchanged afterwards), `VmadStructure.MalformedDuplicateAndUnsupportedPayloadsRefuseStructureEdits` (five malformed payloads plus a duplicate VMAD) and `VmadStructure.StructureEditsPreserveTheQuestFragmentTail` (a synthetic QUST tail survives script and property edits). The fixture gained `Radicle/tests/vmad_writer_fixture.hpp:plugin_bytes_without_vmad` for the records with no VMAD. Nothing in this lane was compiled or run: CI is the first build.

## Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:remove_quest_vmad_fragment (#602 D-24 C-3 C-12 C-18 C-36)

- Scope, and what it deliberately refuses: a QUST fragment binding that already exists can be renamed (`set_quest_vmad_fragment` rewrites its script name and its fragment name) or dropped (`remove_quest_vmad_fragment`). Creating a binding where none exists is not in this slice. That is not caution for its own sake: the fragment script entry in the extras (its name, its flags and its property list) and the fragment function name are the game's own conventions (the CK generates them when it compiles the fragment script), the `Quest Stage Index` i32 is a chronological `logentry` rather than the array position (`Radicle/docs/code-notes/Radicle.md`, section `src/forms/quest_vmad.cpp:sync_quest_vmad_stages`), and none of those can be derived from the payload. Inventing them would write a VMAD the CK rejects, so the caller supplies the two names and the script entry must already be there.
- Addressing: by quest stage, not by array index, because that is the key this writer reads and writes the list with (`wbStructSK([0, 1], 'Fragment', ...)` at `source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3993-4001 @93cc0bc5`, summary keys `Quest Stage` and `Quest Stage Index`). xEdit declares `Quest Stage` and `Quest Stage Index` as `itU32` and sorts the list on both (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3993-4001 @93cc0bc5`); the reader splits the first u32 into `stage` u16 and an `unknown` u16 (`src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras`), so the writer's pair ignores that high word. Whether it is zero in shipped quests is UNPROVEN (see the `find_quest_fragment` section below). `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:find_quest_fragment` returns `binding_missing` when no fragment carries the key and throws `schema::ScalarError` when the payload binds one stage twice, since the sort key allows duplicates but the vocabulary is one binding per stage. It later gained the optional `Quest Stage Index` beside the stage: see the `find_quest_fragment` section below.
- Offsets: `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras` now records `QuestVmadFragment::offset` (first byte of the entry), `QuestVmadFragment::end` (first byte after the two names) and `QuestVmadFragment::unknown_byte` (the `wbUnknown(1)` between the stage index and `ScriptName`), and `QuestVmadExtras::count_offset` (the u16 `FragmentCount`, `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3981`). The writer rebuilds the entry with `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:append_quest_fragment` in the same field order the reader uses (stage u16, unknown u16, stage index u32, unknown byte u8, script name, function name), so an unchanged fragment re-encodes to identical bytes and `set_quest_vmad_fragment` reports `unchanged` instead of rewriting. Everything else in the entry, the extras script name, its flags, its properties, the other bindings and the alias list are never re-encoded, and `xEdit` reads the count with `SetCountPath('FragmentCount', True)` (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4003`), which is why the count word is written from the list length rather than patched.
- Splicing: the entry range is the decoded `[offset, end)`, shifted by `QuestFragmentEdit::tail_start`, which is the extras start (`data.size() - trailing_bytes` from `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_vmad_scripts`). Removing an entry shifts everything after it down by exactly its own size: the test asserts the size drop equals the entry size, that the bytes before the first fragment are byte-identical, that everything from the removed entry's old position onward equals the original bytes from the next entry's start, and that the alias count still holds its bytes. The count word sits before the fragment list (`count_offset` is 1) so a splice never invalidates it.
- Refusals: a record that is not QUST, a record with no VMAD, a record with no extras region (`binding_missing`), a stage that is not bound, a repeated stage, an empty script or fragment name, a fragment script name longer than 65535 bytes (the name encoder raises before any splice), and any payload the loader refuses: `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:load_quest_fragments` runs the same `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:load_vmad` gate as the script and property edits (coverage complete, no unsupported property, version 5/6, object format 1/2) and then refuses extras that `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras` marks unsupported or does not fully consume. Every refusal returns a status or throws before the payload changes, which the tests check by comparing whole-plugin bytes.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_quest_fragments.cpp`. `VmadQuestFragments.NamesAreRewrittenInPlace` (a two-fragment QUST: the edited entry keeps its stage, unknown words, stage index, unknown byte and the extras script name; the prefix before the entry and the suffix after it are byte-identical; renaming with the same names reports `unchanged`), `VmadQuestFragments.RemovalDropsTheBindingAndItsCount` (removing one binding keeps the other binding byte-for-byte, rewrites the count to 1, then removing the last one leaves the extras header and the alias count with a zero count), and `VmadQuestFragments.EditsRefuseForeignRecordsAndBadPayloads` (a plain REFR VMAD is `not_authorable`, a QUST without extras is `binding_missing`, a missing record is `record_missing`, an absent stage is `binding_missing`, empty names and a truncated tail and a duplicated stage throw `schema::ScalarError`, and the plugin bytes are unchanged in every case). Wired in at `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt`. Nothing here was compiled or run: CI is the first build.

## Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment (#602 D-24 C-3 C-12 C-18 C-36)

- Scope: creating a quest fragment binding. `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment` is the `QUST` counterpart of `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:add_vmad_fragment`, and it exists because the word the earlier lane called underivable is caller data, not a derived value: the caller passes the `Quest Stage Index` beside the stage, exactly as it passes the key on the five other fragment records and the script and fragment names everywhere. The refusal was right that the word cannot be computed - the read-only survey in the section on `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment` finds the stored index is a CK-assigned slot, neither the file ordinal nor the sorted ordinal within a stage - and that is the reason it is a parameter here rather than a guess. The extras fragment script entry is still never invented: this writer requires one, as `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:add_vmad_fragment` does.
- Addressing: the key is the pair `(stage, stage_index)`, which is xEdit's own sort key for the list (`wbStructSK([0, 1], 'Fragment', ...)` at `source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3993-4001 @93cc0bc5`). The pair rather than the stage alone, because 80 of the 885 vanilla quests with fragments bind one stage more than once and a stage alone does not name one entry. `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment` therefore reports `already_present` only for a repeated pair; a repeated stage carrying a new index is a legal insert, which is what the second half of the test drives.
- Placement: `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/vmad.hpp:QuestVmadExtras::entries_begin` is new, and `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras` records it as the position right after the extras header (the version byte, the `FragmentCount` u16, the fragment script name and its optional flags and property list), which is the first byte a fragment entry can occupy. The entry is spliced at the first existing entry whose `(stage, stage_index)` is greater, else after the last one, so the list keeps xEdit's declared order. Both words compare as unsigned 32-bit, because xEdit reads `Quest Stage Index` with `wbInteger('Quest Stage Index', itU32)` (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3996 @93cc0bc5`) and sorts the array by its sort key: `TwbIntegerDef.ToSortKey` (`source:xEdit Core/wbInterface.pas:12909 @93cc0bc5`) reads `itU32` through `PCardinal` (`:12929`) and formats eight hex digits (`:12952`), which `CompareSortKeys` compares with `CompareStr` (`source:xEdit Core/wbImplementation.pas:2166 @93cc0bc5`). `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment` therefore casts both the stored `std::int32_t` stage index and the argument to `std::uint32_t` in the duplicate check and in the placement comparison, so an index at or above `0x80000000` sorts after smaller indexes at the same stage instead of before them. Deviation, from the same survey: the CK does not sort - the stored list is in ascending `(stage, index)` order in only 339 of those 885 records - so on a record that is already unsorted the new entry lands where its key belongs among the existing keys and the rest of the list keeps its stored order. xEdit sorts the whole array on save (`wbArrayS`), which is the order this writer follows.
- Bytes: the new entry is `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:append_quest_fragment` output with `unknown` zero and `unknown_byte` 1, the value `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment` sets (see its own section below). `FragmentCount` is rewritten from the new list length through `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:put` at `edit.tail_start + edit.extras.count_offset` after the splice; the count word sits before the entries, so the splice cannot invalidate it. Everything else - the extras script entry, the other entries, the alias list and the leading scripts - is never re-encoded.
- Refusals: the loader's own (`record_missing`, `not_authorable` for a non-QUST record, `subrecord_missing`, `binding_missing` for a QUST VMAD with no extras region, and `schema::ScalarError` for an unsupported, malformed, truncated or duplicate VMAD, trailing bytes, or an unsupported version or object format); an extras region whose fragment script entry has an empty name, which is `binding_missing` for the same reason `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:add_vmad_fragment` refuses it; an empty script or fragment name and a list already at 65535 entries, both `schema::ScalarError`; and a repeated `(stage, stage_index)` pair, which is `already_present`. Every refusal returns or throws before the splice, and the test compares whole-plugin bytes afterwards.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_quest_fragments.cpp`. `VmadQuestFragments.AddedBindingLandsInStageOrderAndRemovalRestoresThePayload` (a two-fragment quest gains stage 15 between the entries: the count becomes 3, the bytes before the insertion point other than the count word and from the stage-20 entry onward are byte-identical to the original, a repeated pair is `already_present`, stage 5 lands at `entries_begin` and stage 30 directly before the alias count word, then removing 5, 15 and 30 restores the payload byte-for-byte; the second half drives a quest that binds stage 10 twice - adding `(10, 9)` appends, adding `(10, 3)` lands between `(10, 0)` and `(10, 5)`, and the stage-keyed `remove_quest_vmad_fragment` still throws on that record), `VmadQuestFragments.HighStageIndexLandsAfterSmallerIndexesAtTheSameStage` (a quest that binds stage 10 at indexes 0 and 5 gains index `0x80000000`: the new entry lands after both, the count word is rewritten to 3 and the entries before the new one are byte-identical, and repeating the pair is `already_present`; this fails if the comparison treats the stored index as signed, which would sort `0x80000000` before 0) and `VmadQuestFragments.AddedBindingRefusesBoundStagesAndMissingFragmentSections` (a plain REFR VMAD, a QUST with no extras, a QUST whose fragment script name is empty, a repeated pair, a missing record, empty names and a truncated tail; whole-plugin bytes unchanged in every case). Wired in at `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt`. Nothing here was compiled or run: CI is the first build.
- Closed by the `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:find_quest_fragment` section below: `set_quest_vmad_fragment` and `remove_quest_vmad_fragment` now take the `(stage, stage_index)` pair this function already uses, so the 80 vanilla quests that bind one stage twice can have one binding renamed or removed. The stage-only form stays for single-binding callers and refuses an ambiguous stage with an explicit `schema::ScalarError`.

## Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment (RE #763, unknown byte)

- Value: a created QUST fragment binding writes `unknown_byte` 1. `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment` sets it on the new `QuestVmadFragment`, and it is the only path that creates a quest fragment entry. `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:append_quest_fragment` is shared with `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment`, which re-encodes a read entry and keeps the byte it had. xEdit names the byte `wbUnknown(1)` in the fragment struct at `source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3993-4001 @93cc0bc5`.
- Why 1: a read-only scan of the vanilla masters found the byte is 1 in all 10,686 QUST fragment entries and 0 in none. The value is a match to vanilla, not a known rule. It stays until RE #763 says what the byte means, and this section is the place to revisit it.
- Preserved: `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras` keeps whatever byte an existing entry has, and neither `set_quest_vmad_fragment` nor `remove_quest_vmad_fragment` normalises it. `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_quest_fragments.cpp:VmadQuestFragments.AddedBindingLandsInStageOrderAndRemovalRestoresThePayload` checks the created entry's raw bytes, which end in 1, and that the existing entries on either side of the insertion stay byte-identical across the add and the removals.

## Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:set_vmad_fragment, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:remove_vmad_fragment (#602 D-24 C-3 C-12 C-18 C-36)

- Scope: the non-quest fragment records. `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:is_fragment_record` covers `PACK`, `INFO`, `SCEN`, `PERK` and `TERM`. A binding that already exists can be renamed or dropped; creating one where none exists is out of scope for the same reason the quest row gives (`Radicle/docs/code-notes/Radicle.md`, section `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment`): the fragment script entry and the function name are the CK's own conventions and cannot be derived from the payload. `QUST` keeps its own writer, `set_quest_vmad_fragment` and `remove_quest_vmad_fragment` in `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp`, because its entries carry a stage and an alias list this file does not model.
- Two layouts, one key type. `PACK`, `INFO` and `SCEN` are the flagged family (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3893-3960, 4024-4066 @93cc0bc5`): the extras are `[i8 Extra bind data version][u8 Flags][ScriptEntry][Fragments]` and the entry is `[u8 unknown][ScriptName][FragmentName]`. `PERK` and `TERM` are the indexed family (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3937-3971`; `TERM` reuses `wbVMADFragmentedPERK` at `:12680`): `[i8 version][ScriptEntry][u16 count][Fragments]`, entry `[u32 Fragment Index][u8 unknown][ScriptName][FragmentName]`. `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:load_fragment_section` reports which one it saw in `FragmentSection::indexed`; the caller passes the same `key` either way, a flag index for the flagged family and a `Fragment Index` for the indexed one.
- The flagged family stores no fragment count. The list length is the population count of the `Flags` byte, so `src/schema/vmad.cpp:walk_flagged_fragments` and `wbScriptFragmentsPackCounter` agree, and the entries sit in ascending set-bit order (`wbArray('Fragments', // Do NOT sort, ordered OnBegin, OnEnd`). `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:read_flagged_bindings` reproduces that order and its `key` is the bit position, which is why removal clears one bit (`FragmentSection::flags & ~(1u << key)`) and does not renumber the others: clearing bit 0 of `0b11` leaves `0b01`, so the surviving entry is still read as the `OnEnd` slot it was. `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:fragment_flag_bits` is 3 for `PACK` (`OnBegin`, `OnEnd`, `OnChange`) and 2 for `INFO` and `SCEN`, matching the same walker.
- Byte preservation: `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:FragmentBinding::unknown` keeps the `wbUnknown(1)` byte between the key and the names, so a rename that changes only the two names re-encodes to the bytes already there and reports `unchanged`; `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:encode_binding` is the only re-encoder and it writes key, unknown byte, script name, fragment name in reader order. The splice is `[offset, end)`, so for `SCEN` the phase array after the main entries is never touched, and for the indexed family the u16 count sits before the entries so rewriting it from the list length cannot be invalidated by the splice.
- Refusals: a record outside the five signatures is `not_authorable` and is checked before any payload check; a missing record is `record_missing`; no VMAD is `subrecord_missing`; a VMAD with no extras, an empty fragment script name in the extras, or a `key` no binding carries is `binding_missing`; empty names and a name longer than 65535 bytes raise `schema::ScalarError`; and the same gate as the script and property edits (coverage complete, no unsupported property, version 5/6, object format 1/2) runs first, so a malformed or unknown-trailing-byte payload raises before anything is written. `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:Cursor` and the `skip_*` helpers walk the fragment script entry with the same type table `src/schema/vmad.cpp:walk_property` uses and fail closed on any type they cannot size, rather than guessing a width.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_fragments.cpp`. `VmadFragments.FlaggedRecordsRenameOneBindingAndKeepEveryOtherByte` (PACK, INFO and SCEN: the whole VMAD equals the expected bytes with only the two names changed, and a rename to the same names reports `unchanged`), `VmadFragments.FlaggedRemovalClearsItsFlagAndKeepsTheOtherEntryByteForByte` (`0b11` to `0b01` keeps the surviving entry's unknown byte and function, then to `0b00`, then `binding_missing`), `VmadFragments.IndexedRecordsRenameAndRemoveByFragmentIndex` (PERK and TERM: the u32 key survives a rename, and removing 100 leaves 200 byte-for-byte with a count of 1), `VmadFragments.ScenePhaseFragmentsSurviveMainFragmentEdits` (the phase entry is byte-identical after a rename and a removal upstream of it), `VmadFragments.EditsRefuseForeignRecordsAndBadKeys` and `VmadFragments.ScriptlessAndMalformedSectionsAreRefused` (every refusal above, each asserting the whole plugin bytes are unchanged). Wired in at `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt`. Nothing here was compiled or run: CI is the first build.
- Settled by the corpus, 2026-10-19: xEdit labels the `SCEN` flags `{1} 'OnBegin', {2} 'OnEnd'` (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4028-4032 @93cc0bc5`) while `PACK` and `INFO` use `{0}` and `{1}` (`:3900-3906`, `:3896-3902`). A read-only scan of the seven local masters under `D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Fallout 4/Data` (`Fallout4.esm` and the DLC masters) finds 636 `SCEN` VMADs whose flags byte is `0` (307), `1` (48), `2` (206) or `3` (73), and every one of them is fully consumed by `src/schema/vmad.cpp:walk_flagged_fragments` scanning the low two bits, so the labels are cosmetic and the walker is right. The same scan shows the phase array is always present (a u16 count, `0` for 251 of the 636) and that `SCEN` flags of `0` still carry phase fragments (307 records), so a phase list is not gated by the main flag bits.

## Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:add_vmad_fragment (#602 D-24 C-3 C-12 C-18 C-36)

- Scope: creating a fragment binding on the five non-quest fragment records. `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:add_vmad_fragment` writes into a fragment section that is already there; it never creates one. A VMAD with no extras region returns `binding_missing` (the loader's `extras_start == data.size()` branch), and so does an extras region whose fragment script entry has an empty name, which `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:skip_script_entry` reports by returning false. The fragment script entry holds the fragment script's name, flags and properties; inventing it would mean inventing a script the game then fails to bind, which is the same reason `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment` refuses to invent one.
- Placement: `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:FragmentSection::entries_begin` is the first byte a binding could occupy, recorded by the loader right after the fragment script entry for the flagged family and right after the u16 count for the indexed family. `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:add_vmad_fragment` splices at the first existing binding whose `key` is greater, else after the last one, so the list stays in ascending key order, which is the order both families are read in (`wbScriptFragmentsPackCounter` walks the flag bits upward; `PERK` and `TERM` use `wbArrayS` with the fragment index as its sort key, `source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3937-3971 @93cc0bc5`).
- The new entry's `unknown` byte is zero: it is `wbUnknown(1)` in xEdit with the default native value, and `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:encode_binding` writes it in reader order for both families. The count follows the list length, so the indexed family rewrites its u16 through `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:put_u16` at `FragmentSection::count_offset` and the flagged family sets one bit in `FragmentSection::flags` at `FragmentSection::flags_offset`; nothing else in the payload moves.
- Refusals, checked in this order: the loader's own refusals (`record_missing`, `not_authorable`, `subrecord_missing`, `binding_missing`, and `schema::ScalarError` for an unsupported, malformed, truncated or duplicate VMAD, a payload with trailing bytes, or an unsupported version/object format); an empty script or fragment name (`schema::ScalarError`); a flagged `key` at or past `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:fragment_flag_bits` for the record's signature, which is `index_out_of_range` because the flag byte cannot express it; an already bound `key`, which is `already_present`; and a fragment list already at 65535 entries, which raises `schema::ScalarError` rather than wrapping the u16 count. Every refusal happens before the splice, which the tests check by comparing whole-plugin bytes.
- The `key` is the caller's contract: a `PERK` fragment index is a perk entry point index and a `TERM` fragment index is a terminal menu index, and neither list is decoded in this file, so the caller has to name a key the record actually has. Same boundary as the fragment script entry above, and recorded in `Radicle/docs/VMAD.md`.
- `QUST` creation is not this function's job and is no longer missing: `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment` creates a quest binding with the caller supplying the `Quest Stage Index`, addressed by the `(stage, stage_index)` pair this writer keys the list by. See its own section above.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_fragments.cpp`. `VmadFragments.CreatedBindingLandsInKeyOrderAndRemovalRestoresThePayload` (PACK flags `0b101` gains key 1 between the two entries: the whole VMAD equals flags `0b111` with the new zero-unknown entry in the middle, the payload grows, a repeat is `already_present`, key 3 is `index_out_of_range`, empty names raise, and removing the new binding restores the original bytes exactly), `VmadFragments.CreatedBindingWorksOnIndexedAndTwoBitRecords` (PERK and TERM gain a `Fragment Index` between and after the existing entries with the u16 count raised to 3 and 2, and INFO, which has two flag bits, gains bit 1 and then reports `index_out_of_range` for key 2), and the `add_vmad_fragment` cases added to `VmadFragments.EditsRefuseForeignRecordsAndBadKeys` and `VmadFragments.ScriptlessAndMalformedSectionsAreRefused` (a non-fragment record, a VMAD with no extras, a fragment script with an empty name, a payload with a trailing byte). Nothing here was compiled or run: CI is the first build.

## Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_scene_vmad_extras, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:add_scene_vmad_phase_fragment, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:set_scene_vmad_phase_fragment, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:remove_scene_vmad_phase_fragment (#602)

- The gap this closes: the `SCEN` phase fragment list was the one fragment variant with no typed view and no writer. `src/schema/vmad.cpp:walk_flagged_fragments` walked it only to step over it, so `vmad_coverage` counted its entries (`VmadCoverage::fragment_count`) while nothing could read or author them; `docs/VMAD.md` never named it. Every other variant was already covered: `QUST` stage fragments and alias scripts (`src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras`, `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment`), the flagged `INFO`/`PACK`/`SCEN` main bindings and the indexed `PERK`/`TERM` bindings (`src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp`).
- xEdit: `wbVMADFragmentedSCEN` (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4024-4066 @93cc0bc5`) puts `wbArrayS('Phase Fragments', wbStructSK([1, 0], 'Phase Fragment', [Phase Flag u8, Phase Index u32, Unknown s8, ScriptName, FragmentName]), -2)` after the flagged `Fragments` array. The sort key is `(Phase Index, Phase Flag)`, the `-2` is the u16 count prefix, and the flag labels are `{1} 'OnStart', {2} 'OnCompletion'` (`:4051-4055`), which the corpus reads as masks `0x01` and `0x02` (see the survey below), the same cosmetic-label offset the main `SCEN` flags have.
- Layout, and why the entry width matters: the phase entry is `[u8 Phase Flag][u32 Phase Index][s8 Unknown][ScriptName][FragmentName]`, so its fixed part is 6 bytes, not the 1 the neighbouring flagged main entry uses (its key is the flag bit, so only the unknown byte is stored). `src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_scene_vmad_extras` and `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:load_fragment_section` both skip the leading version byte, then read the flag, then a full u32 index, then the unknown byte; a reader that took the index as u16 would misplace every following entry and the u16 count would then be read out of a name. The reader is given the extras span (the first byte after the leading script list, `data.size() - VmadScripts::trailing_bytes`) and reports a truncated entry or an unsupported property through `SceneVmadExtras::unsupported` and `unsupported_reason` instead of throwing; see the `SceneVmadExtras` entry below.
- Corpus survey, read-only over the seven local masters under `D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Fallout 4/Data` (`Fallout4.esm` and the DLC masters), 2026-10-19: 636 `SCEN` records carry a VMAD, 634 of them have a fragment section and all 634 are fully consumed by the new reader, with 738 phase entries in all; the remaining 2 have no fragment section at all and stay `binding_missing`. Phase flags are `1` (350 entries), `2` (386) and `0` (2); the phase index runs 0 to 52; the `Unknown` byte is `1` in all 738 entries; 251 scenes carry an empty phase list and 307 carry phases with a zero main flags byte; no scene binds the same `(index, flag)` twice; the entries are in `(index, flag)` order in 555 of the 634 and out of it in 79, which is why the writer inserts at the sort position rather than at the end.
- Addressing and splicing: a phase fragment is addressed by `(Phase Index, Phase Flag)`, xEdit's own sort key, so a scene that binds one phase index twice with different flags stays addressable, unlike the stage-only `QUST` address. `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:find_phase` returns `binding_missing` for a pair that is not bound; `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:encode_phase` is the only re-encoder and writes flag, index, unknown, script name, fragment name in reader order, so a rename that changes only the two names reports `unchanged` and leaves the payload alone. Removal splices `[offset, end)` and rewrites the u16 count at `FragmentSection::phase_count_offset` from the list length; creation splices at the first entry whose `(index, flag)` sorts after the new one, else after the last, and rewrites the same count. The count word sits before the entries, so a splice never invalidates it.
- Refusals: a record that is not `SCEN` is `not_authorable`, checked through `FragmentSection::scene` after the loader, so a `PACK` or `INFO` record with a valid fragment section is refused rather than misread; no VMAD is `subrecord_missing` (`src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:load_fragment_section`), and no fragment section or an empty fragment script name is `binding_missing`; an unbound `(index, flag)` is `binding_missing` on set and remove and `already_present` on create; a phase flag of `0` or one with a bit outside `0x03` is `index_out_of_range` (`src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:k_scene_phase_flags`), because such a flag names no phase event; empty names raise `schema::ScalarError`; a phase list already at 65535 entries raises rather than wrapping the count; and the loader's own gate (coverage complete, no unsupported property, version 5/6, object format 1/2) runs first. One shape the scanner accepts and the loader refuses: a `SCEN` fragment section whose bytes end right after the main bindings, with no u16 phase count, is `complete` for `src/schema/vmad.cpp:walk_flagged_fragments` (it reads the phase array only when bytes remain) and raises `schema::ScalarError` in `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:load_fragment_section`, which reads the count unconditionally. No vanilla record has that shape (all 634 `SCEN` fragment sections carry the count, zero or not), and refusing it keeps a phase list from being read out of the wrong offset.
- The new entry's `Unknown` byte is zero, following `src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:encode_binding` and xEdit's `wbUnknown` default, not the corpus value: all 738 vanilla phase entries and all 3142 vanilla flagged main entries (`INFO` 2554, `SCEN` 400, `PACK` 188) store `1`. So a created binding is byte-shaped like xEdit's new entry but unlike anything the game's own writer produced. Whether the game needs `1` is not settled here, and the same question already applied to `add_vmad_fragment`; changing it would change both writers and their tests together, so it is left as it is and recorded as an open question for a lane that can test a created binding in game.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_fragments.cpp`. `VmadFragments.ScenePhaseFragmentsDecodeAndRoundTripByPhaseIndexAndFlag` (a two-phase scene: the decoded flags, per-entry flag, index, unknown byte, names and 24-byte entry width; a `(index, flag)` pair that is not bound is `binding_missing` and leaves the payload alone; a rename keeps the other entry and the unknown byte byte-for-byte and a repeat is `unchanged`; removal drops the entry and the count to 1 with the surviving entry byte-identical; re-creating the removed entry restores the original VMAD byte-for-byte) and `VmadFragments.CreatedScenePhaseFragmentLandsInPhaseOrderAndRefusalsHold` (a scene with a zero flags byte and no main bindings gains a phase entry between two existing ones with the count at 3, the whole VMAD equalling the expected bytes; a repeat pair is `already_present`, a flag of `0`, `4` or `0x80` is `index_out_of_range`, empty names throw, a `PACK` record is `not_authorable`, a payload with no fragment section is `binding_missing`, a `SCEN` payload whose fragment section stops after the main bindings is `complete` for `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:vmad_coverage` yet throws `schema::ScalarError` in all three writers, and the plugin bytes are unchanged after every refusal). The regression they catch is a reader or writer that sizes the phase entry as 4 fixed bytes instead of 6, drops or double-counts the u16 phase count, or loses the phase list when a main binding is edited. Nothing in this lane was compiled or run: CI is the first build.
- Left open, with the evidence: creating a `QUST` fragment binding (`src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment` still requires the stage to be bound). The `Quest Stage Index` word cannot be invented; an independent 2026-10-19 scan including the DLC masters finds 10568 stage groups, of which 49 do not number their fragments `0..k-1` (examples `stage 500 -> [2]`, `stage 50 -> [1]`), and the index equals the file-order ordinal within a stage in 10760 of 10893 entries with 133 counterexamples, so no rule reproduces it. Editing the script entries inside a quest alias (`QuestVmadAliasScripts` is decoded by `src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras` but carries no offsets and no writer) is the other remaining variant-level gap; `src/forms/quest_vmad.cpp:sync_quest_vmad_aliases` splices whole aliases from the quest alias editor and does not touch the scripts inside them.

## Radicle/include/fo4/schema/vmad.hpp:SceneVmadExtras, Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_scene_vmad_extras (#602)

- `SceneVmadExtras::unsupported` and `SceneVmadExtras::unsupported_reason` mirror `QuestVmadExtras` and `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras`. Both readers catch the anonymous-namespace `UnsupportedVmadProperty` (thrown by `walk_property` for a type-6 fragment property, among others) by its own type and report a fixed reason, "a VMAD property in the scene extras is unsupported" or "a VMAD property in the quest extras is unsupported". Both catch `parse_error` and report its `what()`, such as a truncated entry or a SCEN with no u16 phase count. `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras` used to catch all `std::exception`; it now catches `parse_error` only, because every fault its body raises is a `parse_error` (`Slice` truncation, an unknown object format) or `UnsupportedVmadProperty`. Other `std::exception` types (out_of_range, bad_alloc) are not parse faults, so both readers let them propagate to the caller: `Radicle/src/quest/runtime.cpp:quest_runtime_data_record` catches them at `:84`. A malformed SCEN therefore reports `unsupported` instead of throwing. `fully_consumed` stays false on either path.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_fragments.cpp:VmadFragments.SceneUnsupportedFragmentPropertyReportsInsteadOfThrowing` (a SCEN fragment script with a type-6 property reports `unsupported` with a non-empty reason instead of escaping as an exception) and `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_fragments.cpp:VmadFragments.ScenePhaseFragmentsDecodeAndRoundTripByPhaseIndexAndFlag` (a normal SCEN decodes with `unsupported` false and an empty reason). Nothing here was compiled or run: CI is the first build.
- Regression coverage for the scene reader (`Radicle/tests/test_vmad_fragments.cpp`, anchored to `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_scene_vmad_extras`): `VmadFragments.SceneExtrasWithTruncatedOrMissingPhaseListReportUnsupported` detects a truncated phase entry, or a SCEN with no u16 phase count, escaping as an exception or being read as an empty, fully consumed list. `VmadFragments.SceneExtrasWithTrailingBytesDecodeButAreNotFullyConsumed` detects trailing bytes after the phase list being accepted as fully consumed. `VmadFragments.ScenePhaseListReadsObjectPropertiesInFormatOne` detects a format 1 object property in a SCEN fragment script being read with the format 2 layout, which reports unsupported and loses the phase list. `VmadFragments.ZeroPhaseSceneGainsItsFirstPhaseFragment` detects an add into an empty phase array splicing at the wrong offset or leaving the u16 count stale.

## Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment (#602 D-24 C-3 C-12 C-18 C-36)

- Vanilla survey, read-only over the seven local masters under `D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Fallout 4/Data`, 2026-10-18, `Fallout4.esm` only for the fragment counts: 1336 `QUST` records, 920 with exactly one VMAD, 885 with a non-zero fragment count, 7150 fragment entries in all. The high half of the stage word is 0 in 7150 of 7150 entries, so reading the stage as `u16` and the next `u16` as unused (`Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:walk_quest_extra`, `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras`) matches the data.
- `Quest Stage Index` is a CK-assigned slot number, not an ordinal: of 6880 stage groups, 6771 hold one fragment, 109 hold two and the rest three or more; 63 groups do not number their fragments `0..n-1` (examples `stage 10 -> [1]`, `stage 100 -> [2]`, `stage 90 -> [0, 2, 1]`, `stage 0 -> [0, 1, 3, 4]`). Across whole records the indices in file order are `0..n-1` in only 135 of 885, and the `(stage, index)` list is sorted in 339 of 885 and unsorted in 546. So neither the global ordinal nor the sorted ordinal within a stage reproduces the stored value, and `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_fragment_edits.cpp:add_vmad_fragment` deliberately has no `QUST` counterpart: a new quest binding would have to invent this word, and the index also decides where the entry sorts, which the game reads in file order.
- The cost of the stage-keyed address: 80 of the 885 quests with fragments bind one stage more than once, and `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:find_quest_fragment` refuses both a rename and a removal for those, because a stage alone does not name one entry. Addressing a quest entry by `(stage, stage_index)` instead would cover them, and the survey above is what such a change would have to be tested against.
- #602 B-44 MSWP substitutions: `schema/fallout4/fields.json` `MSWP` gained `MSWP\OriginalMaterial` (BNAM, zstring, repeated), `MSWP\ReplacementMaterial` (SNAM, zstring, repeated) and `MSWP\ColorRemappingIndex` (CNAM, f32, repeated). xEdit `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12437` declares `wbRArrayS('Material Substitutions', wbRStructSK([0], 'Substitution', [BNAM, SNAM, FNAM, CNAM]))`, so each substitution is four separate subrecords, not one struct payload; a flat repeated row per signature is the matching shape (same as the RACE NAME/PHTN repeated-rows precedent). Substitutions pair by ordinal, which the flat rows preserve.
- #602 B-44 MSWP authoring: `schema/fallout4/fields.json` `MSWP.authoring.subrecords` lists EDID only (minimum 0, maximum 1). The interleaved `BNAM`, `SNAM` and `CNAM` group cannot be listed: each substitution is `BNAM`, `SNAM`, `CNAM`, so a listed rule index would fall within the record and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` would report `subrecord_order_invalid` (see the interleaved-group rule in the authoring-order note). The three rows stay (`MSWP\OriginalMaterial`, `MSWP\ReplacementMaterial`, `MSWP\ColorRemappingIndex`) with row `insertion` `existing_only`, so a substitution member is readable and editable but not added or removed on its own.
- #602 B-44 MSWP FNAM deviation: `Radicle/tests/test_mswp_rows.cpp:RowsUseTheXEditSubrecordsAndStorage` asserts `schema::scalar_field_descriptor("MSWP\FNAM")` has no value, so the first FNAM ('Tree Folder') and the obsolete in-struct FNAM that xEdit moves up are both left without a row. One record has two meanings for the same signature at two nesting levels, and the schema resolves a row by record plus path only, so a single FNAM row could not tell them apart. The bytes stay preserved and untouched, which the same test checks in `subrecord_at(reread, "FNAM", 0)`.
- #602 B-44 MSWP tests: `Radicle/tests/test_mswp_rows.cpp` (`MswpRows`) covers row descriptors and storage, the ordinal count and decoded values of two substitutions plus the color index (`Radicle/tests/test_mswp_rows.cpp:MswpRows.ReadsOneColorIndexPerSubstitution`), a one-pair write that leaves its neighbors and the FNAM and EDID bytes byte-identical, the wrong-setter and out-of-range refusals, and authoring preflight (`Radicle/tests/test_mswp_rows.cpp:MswpRows.InterleavedSubstitutionsPassAuthoringPreflight`).
- #602 B-44 parity: `docs/FO4_PARITY.md` was regenerated with `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py --write`; its MSWP named-field row now shows 1 BNAM, 2 SNAM and one f32 CNAM entry where it previously showed none (`Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py`). Adding `"repeated": true` to `MSWP\ColorRemappingIndex` moved that table's Repeated column for MSWP from 2 to 3, since all three substitution rows are now repeated.
- #602 B-10 FSTS counts: `schema/fallout4/fields.json` FSTS gained five `kind: scalar` rows on XCNT, `FSTS\WalkingCount` (offset 0), `FSTS\RunningCount` (4), `FSTS\SprintingCount` (8), `FSTS\SneakingCount` (12) and `FSTS\SwimmingCount` (16), all u32, `payload_size` 20, `minimum` 0, `maximum` 4294967295, `insertion` `existing_only`. xEdit `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8692` declares `wbStruct(XCNT, 'Footstep Counts', [Walking, Running, Sprinting, Sneaking, Swimming])` with five u32 in that order, and the record previously carried `"fields": []`, so the counts had no generic row at all. `payload_size` 20 makes a short XCNT hide the rows past its end, the same gate EXPL DATA uses.
- #602 B-10 derived counts: `src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` refuses a generic write to `FSTS` XCNT with `ScalarError`, alongside the counted-array and subrecord-group count refusals. XCNT is derived from the five `DATA` category sections: `src/environment/sound.cpp:decode_footstep_set` slices `DATA` with the counts, and `src/environment/sound.cpp:decode_footstep_counts` fails a record whose counts do not sum to `DATA` size / 4. Writing one count alone would desync `DATA`, and no category-aware insert or remove exists yet, so the counts stay readable and non-writable. Mutagen derives the same five values from its `WalkFootsteps`..`SwimFootsteps` lists on write (`PluginEditTool/Mutagen/Mutagen.Bethesda.Fallout4/Records/Major Records/FootstepSet.cs` `WriteBinaryCountCustom`).
- #602 B-10 signature lookup: adding five XCNT rows makes `schema::scalar_descriptor(XCNT)` ambiguous, because `src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_descriptor` returns nothing as soon as two rows name a signature. REFR `ItemCount` also names XCNT, so the signature-only lookup changes from that row to no row; every caller reaches the row by record plus path (`schema::scalar_field_descriptor(Signature, path)`).
- #602 B-10 tests: `Radicle/tests/test_fsts_rows.cpp` (`FstsRows`) covers the five row descriptors and offsets, the ambiguity of the signature-only lookup, decoded counts from a built FSTS and its five `FSTS\Footsteps` links, the refusal of generic count writes plus a byte-identical reread, and the 20-byte payload gate on a 12-byte XCNT.
- #602 B-10 open: the five `DATA` category lists are still one flat `FSTS\Footsteps` link row. Splitting them needs a row kind whose element offset is the prefix sum of the five counts, which `schema::FormLinkFieldDescriptor` cannot express (`offset` and `address.stride` are fixed). `src/environment/sound.cpp:decode_footstep_set` already exposes `FootstepSetData::categories`, so the typed read path has the split; only the generic rows and authoring are missing.
- #602 B-43 version unions: `tools/field_address_codegen.py:form_version_windows_disjoint` lets two embedded rows claim the same bytes on one record when their form-version windows cannot both apply to a record. `min_form_version` is inclusive and `max_form_version` exclusive in `src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` (`form_version >= min_form_version` and `form_version < max_form_version`), so the windows are disjoint exactly when one row's `max_form_version` is non-zero and not above the other's `min_form_version`. `tools/field_address_codegen.py:reject_overlaps` consults it before the `when` discriminator checks; the exemption is limited to rows that are both `embedded`, so a whole-payload row still cannot be paired with anything on the same subrecord.
- #602 B-43 rule tests: `Radicle/tools/test_field_address_version_windows.py` (`FormVersionWindowTests`) runs under `python -m unittest` and directly on the file. It accepts the disjoint pairs (below 60 with 60 to 103, below 60 with 104 and up, 104 and up with below 104), rejects the overlapping pairs (a gated row with an ungated row, 60 and up with below 104, equal windows, and nested windows), and keeps a whole-payload row rejected. Registered as `radicle_field_address_version_windows` next to `radicle_field_address_codegen`.

- #602 B-43 gates: `MOVT\*Below60` carries `max_form_version: 60` and `minimum_payload_size: 40`, one row set for xEdit arms 0 and 1 because both store Walk and Run at the same offsets per direction (0 and 4) and the pitch, roll and yaw pair at 32 and 36; only the record's version separates them. `MOVT\Unknown40Below60` adds arm 1's trailing bare float at offset 40 with `minimum_payload_size: 44`. `MOVT\*From60` carries `min_form_version: 60`, `max_form_version: 104` and `minimum_payload_size: 68`, and holds the direction pairs at 0 to 28, pitch at 32 and 36, roll at 40 and 44, yaw at 48 and 52 and the three unlabelled trailing floats at 56, 60 and 64. The gates are the record's form version plus a payload floor rather than an exact size, because the decider reads the arm's bytes whatever the payload length; the existing arm 3 rows keep `min_form_version: 104` and `minimum_payload_size: 112`.
- #602 B-43 tests: `Radicle/tests/test_ipds_movt_rows.cpp` (`MOVTRows`) gained `LegacySpeedRowsCoverThe40And44ByteLayouts`, `MiddleSpeedRowsCoverThe68ByteLayout`, `EachSpeedLayoutHidesOutsideItsFormVersionWindow` (versions 131, 104, 60, 59 and an oversized payload below 60) and `WritesALegacySpeedRowAndRefusesTheOtherLayouts`. - #602 B-43 parity: Mutagen models only the arm 3 names in `PluginEditTool/Mutagen/Mutagen.Bethesda.Fallout4/Records/Major Records/MovementType.xml`, so the legacy rows put the schema ahead of Mutagen rather than behind it; `docs/FO4_PARITY.md` was regenerated and MOVT now reports 61 named fields instead of 33.

(unused)`, and marks the C byte as possibly unused; the rows keep it.
