## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json: repeated member groups still unexpressible (#602 B-10 B-25 B-23 B-47 C-17)

Round 8 of the small-record lane checked the five remaining rows against `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` and `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_counted_array` and found one shared blocker: every one of them needs a run of subrecords whose element boundaries are neither a fixed stride inside one payload nor a count subrecord. `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:COUNTED_ARRAY_KEYS` gives an array a single subrecord plus a stride, `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:SUBRECORD_GROUP_KEYS` gives a group a four-character `count_subrecord` and one fixed `payload_size` per member, and neither can express a run of subrecords whose element is a sequence of sibling subrecords. No rows were added for these; each stays at the state the earlier entries in this file record.

- FSTS (`#602 B-10`): the five XCNT count rows and the flat `FSTS\Footsteps` link row exist, and `Radicle/src/environment/sound.cpp:decode_footstep_set` already splits the categories. The five `DATA` category arrays need an element offset that is the running sum of the five XCNT values (xEdit `wbArray(...).SetCountPath('..\XCNT\Walking Count', True)` per category, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8700-8717`), which `schema::FormLinkFieldDescriptor` cannot express because `offset` and `address.stride` are fixed at generation time. Round 12 checked the three existing row kinds again and none reaches it, so the row stays at read and edit and the missing mechanism is recorded here: a packed link array whose count is one u32 of a multi-counter sibling subrecord, where the array is the concatenation of one segment per counter in a declared order (`Radicle/src/environment/sound.cpp:decode_footstep_set` walks `DATA` from `counts[4]` down to `counts[0]`, so the segments run reversed against the XCNT offsets 0, 4, 8, 12, 16), so an insert or remove must pick the counter covering the affected element and move it by one. Three concrete blockers: `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:FormLinkListDescriptor` carries one `counter` signature and `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:reconcile_counter` writes that whole subrecord as a single u32 (and erases it at count 0, which would drop the other four FSTS counters); `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:load_lists` hardcodes `"counter": ""` for every `formlink_lists` entry and validates no key set, so a `counter` key in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FSTS` would be silently ignored rather than rejected; and `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_counted_array` wants exactly one whole-payload u32 row for its `count_subrecord`, which a 20-byte five-counter XCNT is not. The typed read path already splits the categories, so the gap is generic rows and authoring only.
- IPDS pair add and remove (`#602 B-25`): `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IPDS` gains one `kind: subrecord_group` row, `IPDS\Data`, whose only member is PNAM, `required`, not `repeatable`, `payload_size` 8, with no `count_subrecord` and no `default`. This entry corrects the earlier claim that a pair insert or remove "has no descriptor to drive it": that claim rested on xEdit's element being "two PNAM subrecords in a row", but the corpus entry above records 3695 PNAM occurrences in the seven masters and every one is 8 bytes, so one pair is one PNAM subrecord and a one-member group delimits one pair per span. `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` only rejects a member signature that repeats within one run, which a single non-repeatable member does not. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` breaks a run at the second PNAM (`*member == 0`), so `fo4::subrecord_group_spans` returns one span per pair, `fo4::insert_record_subrecord_group` writes an 8-byte zero pair at the span boundary, and `fo4::remove_record_subrecord_group` erases one span. The two `formlink_fields` rows (`IPDS\Material`, `IPDS\Impact`) stay at record level, so their paths, offsets, `payload_sizes` [8] and the `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp` `k_ipds` remap branch are unchanged; the group adds no FormLink rows, and `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_formlink_lists.inc` is byte-identical after regeneration. One side effect is deliberate: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots` now runs `group_spans` for any row whose subrecord is a group member, so an IPDS PNAM that is not exactly 8 bytes fails the Material and Impact rows with `schema::FormLinkFieldError` before the older `payload_sizes` check sees it. An inserted pair starts as two null links and the caller fills it through `fo4::set_record_formlink_field`, because both rows are non-nullable. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_ipds_movt_rows.cpp` (`IPDSRows.DataGroupHoldsOneEightBytePnamPerSpan`, `IPDSRows.InsertsAPairFillsItThroughTheRowsAndRemovesIt`, `IPDSRows.ShortPnamFailsThePairRowsAndTheGroupClosed`).
- INNR naming rules (`#602 B-23`): xEdit nests `wbRArray('Naming Rules', wbRStruct('Ruleset', [VNAM count, wbRArray('Names', wbRStruct('Name', [WNAM, wbKeywords, XNAM, YNAM]))]))` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12346-12386`). Even one level in, a Name carries a length-varied WNAM and a keyword pair, so no member can carry the fixed `payload_size` the group kind requires.
- NOCM (`#602 B-47`): xEdit marks the EDID element `dfInternalEditOnly` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12454-12457`), not the record. Copy-as-new refuses NOCM through Radicle's own `Radicle/src/forms/copy_as_new.cpp:refused_top_level` (`:50-52`, checked at `:202-203`), which returns `unsupported_signature`. NAM1 now has a row (see the B-47 entry below), and only the DATA run and the per-tuple INTV, which sit between INDX occurrences, stay unexpressible.
- QUST alias replacement (`#602 C-17`): resolved. `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias` used to erase the alias range and insert a freshly encoded alias, dropping every member the creation struct does not model. It now keeps those members and splices them back at their xEdit member position through `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:merge_alias_members`, and refuses when a preserved member has no position, the preserved members are out of order, or the spliced alias does not decode. See the `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias` section below.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NOCM\Index and NOCM\Model (#602 B-47)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NOCM\Index` rows `wbInteger(INDX, 'Index', itU32)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12462`) as a `repeated` embedded u32 `existing_only` row at offset 0 with `payload_size` 4, the shape of `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\WorldModelColorRemappingIndex`. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NOCM\Model` rows `wbString(NAM1, 'Model')` (`:12466`) as a `repeated` string `existing_only` row, the shape of `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\DestructionStageModel`. Both are occurrence rows: the k-th INDX and the k-th NAM1 of the record, not the k-th entry. INDX sits on the inner tuple struct (`:12461`) and NAM1 on the outer entry struct (`:12459`) of `wbRArray('Unknown', ...)` (`:12458`). The two occurrence lists are independent: Fallout4.esm's only NOCM has INDX 197, DATA 1589, INTV 197 and NAM1 87, so they do not pair 1:1 and an occurrence number in one says nothing about the other.
- The round-8 entry above ("repeated member groups still unexpressible") said the generic path refuses NOCM with `unsupported_signature`. That is wrong: `unsupported_signature` belongs to copy-as-new (`Radicle/src/forms/copy_as_new.cpp:RecordCopyNewStatus`), not to reading, and Radicle already decodes and writes NOCM generically (`Radicle/tests/test_world_misc_records.cpp:make_plugin` writes INDX, DATA, INTV and NAM1). Only the nested arrays stay unexpressible.
- Remap is unchanged by these rows: NOCM INDX already stays unremapped (`Radicle/tests/test_generator_gap_remap.cpp:NpcTemplateAttacksAndOvisIndexRemapRecordQualified`) and NOCM NAM1 is already in the deny list (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/non_formid_slots.inc:146`). `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NOCM` authoring is untouched (EDID, INDX), so no preflight order rule changes.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_world_misc_records.cpp:WorldMiscRecordsSynthetic.NavmeshObstacleIndexAndModelRowsWriteTheirPayloads` writes the index and the model on the fixture NOCM 3012, asserts both payloads after a write and reread, and checks that the DATA and INTV payloads still equal their fixture bytes. Regressions detected: (a) an index write that does not reach INDX, or lands on another subrecord, fails the reread `INDX == 7` assert; (b) a write that corrupts the adjacent DATA or INTV bytes of the same tuple fails the `DATA == zeros(8)` or `INTV == u32(0)` assert; (c) the negative case asks for occurrence 1 of `NOCM\Index` on a one-entry record and expects `subrecord_missing`, so a writer that inserts a new INDX instead returns `updated` and fails. Not covered: the fixture has one INDX occurrence, so a write that lands on the wrong INDX occurrence of a multi-entry record is not detected by any test here, and needs a two-entry NOCM fixture. `Radicle/tests/test_world_misc_records.cpp:WorldMiscRecordsSynthetic.ArrayPayloadRecordsExposeNoRows` no longer lists NOCM, which now exposes a scalar and a string row.
- Parity: `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py:main` regenerated `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md`; NOCM moves from 0 to 1 scalar row and gains 1 string row.
- TODO: the DATA run (`wbRArray('Unknown Datas', wbUnknown(DATA))`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12460-12463`) and INTV, which is one `wbUnknown(INTV)` per tuple and not an array (`:12464`), still have no row kind. Each tuple is INDX, a DATA run and one INTV, with no count subrecord and no fixed stride to delimit a tuple, and authoring stays at EDID and INDX.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE morph sliders, tint count and neck fat rows (#602 C-27)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\MorphGroupSliders` rows `MPGS`, which xEdit defines as `wbArray(MPGS, 'Morph Group Sliders', wbInteger('Index', itU32, wbIntToHexStr, wbHexStrToInt))` inside `wbMorphGroups` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3165`, reached from the male and female morph groups at `:11277` and `:11296`). One MPGS subrecord carries a whole run of u32 slider indices, so the row is strided (`offset` 0, `stride` 4, `storage` u32, `presentation` identity) and deliberately not `repeated`: `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:parse_address` rejects `repeated` together with `stride`, and `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` walks the strides of every MPGS present, so slider N of morph group M is a distinct slot.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\TotalTintCount` rows `TINL`, xEdit's `wbInteger(TINL, 'Total Number of Tints in List', itU16, nil, nil, cpNormal, False)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11206`, with xEdit's own `Needs Count Updated` note). It is a whole-payload u16, like `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\XPValue` is a whole-payload i16, and the row only rewrites the count of an existing TINL. Nothing desyncs from the write because no tint-list rows exist: `wbTintTemplateGroups` (`:3064`) owns TETI/TETO/TNAM and stays unrowed, as the earlier RACE audit bullet already recorded.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\NeckFatAdjustmentsScaleX` and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\NeckFatAdjustmentsScaleY` row the two floats of xEdit's `wbStruct(NNAM, 'Male Neck Fat Adjustments Scale', ...)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11269`) and its female twin (`:11287`): four unknown bytes, then f32 X at offset 4 and f32 Y at offset 8, `payload_size` 12. Both head sections use the same subrecord with the same layout, so the rows are `repeated` and the occurrence is the gender: `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` lists candidate subrecords in record order, and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` writes the nth, so index 0 is the male head section and index 1 the female one, under the male-first order xEdit fixes at `:11266-11296`. The four unknown bytes are not rowed.
- Not rowed: `RACE\MovementTypeNames` (`MTNM`). xEdit is `wbRArrayS('Movement Type Names', wbString(MTNM, 'Name', 4))` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11202`), an array of fixed four-byte names with no terminator. The string kind forbids `storage`, `payload_size`, `stride`, `array_offset` and the numeric keys (`Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:STRING_FORBIDDEN`) and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:slot_string_bytes` requires a NUL inside the slot, so a four-character name such as Walk cannot be addressed until a fixed-width string storage exists -- it gained one in a later lane (the RACE movement type names section below). Not rowed either: `RACE\CollarTextureSet` (`NAM2`, three NAM2 uses in one record, as the earlier audit bullet records; rowed `repeated: true` in the RACE movement data overrides section below), the `SPCT` count of `SPLO`, and `RACE\PRPS` property lists, which stay with their own paths.
- Evidence boundary: these four rows rest on the pinned xEdit definition alone. No corpus scan of the seven masters was run for this change, so per-row carrier counts, payload sizes and slot counts on vanilla records are unmeasured here, and CI is the compiler for `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_race_weap_rows.cpp:MorphTintAndNeckFatRowsReadAndWrite`, which pins the strided, whole-payload and repeated shapes, reads and rewrites one slider index, the tint count, the male neck-fat Y and the female neck-fat X on a synthetic RACE record, and asserts `subrecord_missing` for an index past the last slider, past the last neck-fat occurrence, the second slot of a single TINL, and a four-byte-too-short NNAM payload on `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_race_weap_rows.cpp:MorphTintAndNeckFatRowsReadAndWrite`.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE movement data overrides and collar rows (#602 C-27)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE` gains 56 `SPED` rows for the movement data overrides of `wbRArrayS('Movement Data Overrides', wbRStructSK([0], 'Override', [<the `MTYP` link>, wbSPED]))` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11250-11252`). They copy the committed rows of `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MOVT` for the same `wbSPED` union, so the arm boundaries and the 40, 44, 68 and 112 byte payload sizes are the ones the `MOVT SPED` section of this file derived from the seven masters, not a fresh reading of xEdit. 28 rows carry `min_form_version: 104` and `minimum_payload_size: 112`, 17 carry `min_form_version: 60`, `max_form_version: 104` and floor 68, and 11 carry `max_form_version: 60` with floors 40 and 44 (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\MovementOverrideUnknown40Below60`).
- Every one of them is `repeated: true`, so the override index is the `SPED` occurrence, the way `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\MovementType` addresses the i-th `MTYP`; the row never touches the paired `MTYP` or the neighbouring override. `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` gives a payload under the floor no valid slot, so a 68-byte override never exposes an arm-3 row and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` answers `subrecord_missing`. Arm 0 and arm 1 share the `max_form_version: 60` window and are separated by the floor alone: a 40-byte payload exposes the ten floor-40 rows and not `MovementOverrideUnknown40Below60`, a 44-byte payload exposes all eleven. The xEdit decider is a form-version decider (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:5590-5617`), which the payload length identifies in the corpus, the same trade the `MOVT` rows make.
- `RACE\CollarTextureSet` (`NAM2`, target `TXST`, not nullable, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11245`) now has a row: `repeated: true` and with no declared payload size. RACE uses `NAM2` three times, twice as a zero-length marker (`wbEmpty(NAM2, 'Marker NAM2 #1')` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11201` and `:11226`) and once as the collar, so a non-repeated row would trip the duplicate check in `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots`, and a row with `payload_sizes: [4]` would trip the payload-size check in `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots` on every real RACE record. With no declared payload size the two markers resolve as `misfit` slots, so `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field` throws `FormLinkFieldError` on index 0 and 1 and writes index 2, the collar. The cost is that `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:record_field_count` counts the markers: it reports 3 on a real RACE and the collar is the last index. Reading or remapping the markers stays safe, because `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_schema.cpp:schema_formlink_offsets` reports offset 0 for them but `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:remap_raw` returns early on `offset + 4 > data.size()`.
- Still unrowed after this lane: `RACE\MovementTypeNames` (`MTNM`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11202`) and the `SPCT` count of `SPLO` (`:11062`). `MTNM` is `wbString(MTNM, 'Name', 4)`, an array of four-byte names with no terminator, and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:slot_string_bytes` requires a NUL inside the slot, so it needs a fixed-width string storage that the string kind does not have (`Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:STRING_FORBIDDEN` forbids the numeric keys a width would need) -- that storage landed in a later lane and `MTNM` is rowed there (the RACE movement type names section below). `SPCT` is the `SetCountPath` count of the `SPLO` array, and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` refuses a row on a counted-array count subrecord, so a row there needs list-aware insert and remove first.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_race_link_rows.cpp:RaceScalarRows` reads a synthetic RACE with two `MTYP`/`SPED` overrides, asserts the second override's `RightSprint` decodes to the fixture float at offset 28, writes `7.5` there and rereads the bytes, and gets `subrecord_missing` for a third override; `Radicle/tests/test_race_link_rows.cpp:MovementOverrideRowsHideOutsideTheirLayoutWindow` covers the 68-byte payload and a form version 40 record. `Radicle/tests/test_race_link_rows.cpp:CollarTextureSetIsTheNam2AfterTheEmptyMarkers` asserts the two markers throw `FormLinkFieldError`, the third `NAM2` writes, and the markers survive the rewrite. Not compiled here; CI is the compiler.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA and ARMO model bundle color and flag rows (#602 A-13 A-15)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA\BipedMaleColorRemappingIndex`, `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA\BipedFemaleColorRemappingIndex`, `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA\FirstPersonMaleColorRemappingIndex` and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA\FirstPersonFemaleColorRemappingIndex` row xEdit's `wbMO2C` to `wbMO5C`, each `wbFloat(Signature, 'Color Remapping Index')` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4267-4270`), reached through `wbTexturedModel` for ARMA's Biped Model and 1st Person groups (`:5872-5873`, `:5877-5878`). Every row is offset 0, `storage` f32, `payload_size` 4, `insertion: existing_only`, and each of the four subrecords appears once in a record, so none is `repeated`.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA\BipedMaleModelFlags` and its female, first-person male and first-person female twins row `wbMO2F` to `wbMO5F`, each `wbInteger(Signature, 'Flags', itU8, wbModelFlags)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4261-4264`). `wbModelFlags` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4256-4259`) names bit 0 `Has FaceBones Model` and bit 1 `Has 1stPerson Model`, so `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA\BipedMaleModelFlags` is `presentation: flags`, the same shape `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_name_value` reads for the other flag rows with those two bit names, `storage` u8 and `payload_size` 1; `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:encode_scalar` keeps the u8 bound, so a value above 255 throws `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError`.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMO\WorldModelColorRemappingIndex` rows `MODC`, again `wbFloat(MODC, 'Color Remapping Index')` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4266`), but ARMO passes `wbMODC` for both its Male and its Female world model (`:5800` and `:5806`), so the same subrecord appears twice in a record. The row is therefore `repeated` (offset 0, f32, `payload_size` 4), and `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` plus `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` make index 0 the male world model and index 1 the female one, the male-first order xEdit fixes at `:5799-5809`; a record with a single MODC leaves one slot. The earlier ARMA audit bullet's reading of `[wbMO2C, wbMO2S, wbMO2F]` (`:5872`) is what makes the ARMA rows non-repeated, because each of those signatures appears once there.
- Not rowed, and why the model bundle still has a hole: `MO2T` to `MO5T` are not `TXST` links. `wbTexturedModel` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9238-9260`) passes the second signature to `wbModelInfo`, whose FO4 branch (`:8918` onward) builds a binary blob of counters, texture and material file-hash entries and addon nodes, which is why the MO*T members sit in authoring with no default and no row, exactly as `MODT`, `MODC`, `MODS` and `MODF` do on other records. Still unrowed on ARMA: the sculpt data sequence (`wbArmorAddonBSMPSequence`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5881`) and the DNAM unknown bytes, both as the earlier ARMA audit bullet recorded.
- Outside this change: `Radicle/src/forms/armor.cpp:create_armor_addon` and `Radicle/src/forms/armor.cpp:create_armor` write EDID, the model strings and DATA and never a `BOD2` payload, so a record created through them carries no `ARMA\FirstPersonFlags` or `ARMO\FirstPersonFlags`, while xEdit's `wbBOD2` sits in both records' definitions and `wbARMAAfterLoad` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:1940`) exists only to migrate a legacy `BODT` into it. No create path in `Radicle/src/forms` writes BOD2, ARMO authoring is `EDID, DATA, DESC, DEST, ICO2, ICON, MIC2, MICO, MO2T, MOD2, MO4T, MOD4` and ARMA authoring is `EDID, DNAM, MOD2, MO2T, MOD3, MO3T, MOD4, MO4T, MOD5, MO5T`, so this is a pre-existing creation gap rather than a row gap and is reported to the lead instead of being changed here.
- Evidence boundary: this change reads the pinned xEdit definitions only, in the same way `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_descriptor` reads the generated rows, and no corpus scan of the seven masters was run, so ARMA/ARMO carrier counts for MO*C and MO*F and the number of records with two MODC are unmeasured here. CI is the compiler for `Radicle/tests/test_armo_arma_rows.cpp:ModelColorRemappingAndFlagRowsReadAndWrite`, which pins the four ARMA color rows, the four flag rows with their bit names, and the repeated ARMO row, reads them off the synthetic ARMO/ARMA records, rewrites one color index, one flag byte and the female MODC, and asserts `subrecord_missing` for a second flag occurrence and for a third MODC plus a throw for a flag value above the u8 bound.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REFR\ReflectedBy — XPWR reflection rows (#602 C-28 C-31 A-1)

- Scope: the XPWR rows land on ten records at once — `REFR`, `ACHR` and the eight `ReferenceRecord` variants (`PARW`, `PBAR`, `PBEA`, `PCON`, `PFLA`, `PGRE`, `PHZD`, `PMIS`). Each gets `<record>\ReflectedBy` (a reference at offset 0) and `<record>\ReflectionType` (`u32` at offset 4, `presentation: flags`, bits 0 `Reflection` and 1 `Refraction`), both `insertion: existing_only` and both `repeated: true`, because xEdit models XPWR as an array (`wbRArrayS` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11536`), not a single struct. The row gives READ and WRITE for reflection data through the generic path-addressed scalar and FormLink setters; no typed setter was added.
- xEdit: three copies of one definition, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3218` (the shared `wbRefRecord` helper at `:3202` that the eight variants call), `:4528` (`wbRefRecord(ACHR)` at `:4483`) and `:11537` (`wbRefRecord(REFR)` at `:11347`): `wbStructSK(XPWR, [0], 'Water', [wbFormIDCk('Reference', [ACHR, REFR]), wbInteger('Type', itU32, wbFlags(['Reflection', 'Refraction']))]).SetOptionalFrom(1)`. The record is the water surface and each element names a reference reflected or refracted by it, which is why the field is `ReflectedBy` and not `Reference`.
- `payload_sizes: [8, 4]` on the link and `payload_size: 8` on the type row are taken straight from `SetOptionalFrom(1)`: the type is the only optional element, so a 4-byte XPWR is a complete form ID with no type. A 4-byte payload therefore still reads `ReflectedBy` and hides `ReflectionType` — `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` returns an empty span for an embedded field past the end of a shorter payload — which the ACHR test asserts by resizing both XPWR payloads to 4 bytes.
- Ambiguity, as with XHLT: XPWR now carries a row on ten records, so `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:scalar_descriptor` stays empty for the bare subrecord signature and every lookup has to be record + path. `Radicle/tests/test_parw_rows.cpp:ParwRows.SharedSubrecordsNeedTheRecordPath` pins that with an explicit `scalar_descriptor(XPWR)` absence check.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_achr_rows.cpp:AchrRows.RepeatedXpwrRowsAddressEachOccurrenceAndGateShortPayloads` writes the second occurrence's type, refuses the third (`subrecord_missing`), retargets the second link, refuses a NULL target (`FormLinkFieldError`), rereads both written payloads from the re-serialized plugin and then gates the shortened payload; `Radicle/tests/test_parw_rows.cpp:ParwRows.ProjectileRecordsCarryTheSharedXpwrReflectionRows` pins the offsets, the flag/storage shape, the two payload sizes and the ACHR/REFR target list on a variant record. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR\PatrolIdleTime — patrol rows (#602 A-2 C-29)

- Scope: ACHR gains `ACHR\PatrolIdleTime` (XPRD, `f32`, single) plus the FormLink rows `ACHR\PatrolIdle` (INAM, IDLE) and `ACHR\PatrolTopic` (TNAM, DIAL); REFR gains `REFR\PatrolIdleTime` and `REFR\PatrolIdle`, both `repeated: true` with the matching xEdit shapes. That is the WRITE the row asked for on patrol idle time and on the idle/topic links; all five rows are `insertion: existing_only`, because a patrol group is authored as a whole block and Radicle has no group-row kind that could append one.
- xEdit: ACHR carries one `wbRStruct('Patrol Data', ...)` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4537-4543` (`wbFloat(XPRD, 'Idle Time')` :4538, `wbEmpty(XPPA)` :4539, `wbFormIDCk(INAM, 'Idle', [IDLE, NULL])` :4540, `wbPDTOs` :4541, `wbFormIDCk(TNAM, 'Topic', [DIAL, NULL])` :4542), REFR an array of the same struct minus TNAM at `:11699-11704`. The nesting is why ACHR's rows are single-valued and REFR's are repeated: `wbRStruct` against `wbRArray('Patrol', wbRStruct('Data', ...))`.
- `INAM` and `TNAM` are whole-payload form IDs and already listed in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formid_subrecords.inc:59` and `:141`, so the rows remap on copy and on write with no code change. NULL is in both xEdit lists, so the two link rows are `nullable: true`, the same treatment `ACHR\LockKey` gets.
- Still open in this row (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR\PatrolIdleTime`): `XPPA` is a zero-length marker with no value to expose (no row), `PDTO` is a union (`wbStruct(PDTO, ...)` at `:4339-4347`) of a u32 type plus either a DIAL form ID or a 4-byte subtype string (no row), and `XRGB` has no row. `XRGD` is closed: the 28-byte bone struct is rowed as a stride-28 scalar (`ACHR\RagdollBoneId` to `ACHR\RagdollRotationZ`), read and written by occurrence in `Radicle/tests/test_achr_rows.cpp`. Patrol exposure stops at idle time, idle and topic.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_achr_rows.cpp:AchrRows.PatrolRowsReadAndWriteIdleTimeIdleAndTopic` (descriptors, target lists in both directions, a read of all three rows from the built actor, a write with a reread, `subrecord_missing` past the single occurrence and a NULL-target refusal) and `Radicle/tests/test_refr_extra_rows.cpp:REFRExtraRows.RepeatedPatrolRowsAddressEachOccurrence` (two patrol groups, the per-occurrence counts, a write of the second group's idle time and idle link, the same two negatives and byte checks of both groups after the round trip). Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR\LevelModifier — level modifier and lit water rows (#602 A-2 C-28 C-29)

- Scope: ACHR and REFR each gain `LevelModifier` (XLCM, `i32`, `presentation: enum` with xEdit's four names Easy/Medium/Hard/Very Hard) and `LitWater` (XLTW, a reference at offset 0, `repeated: true`, targets ACHR and REFR, `nullable: false`), all `insertion: existing_only`. XLCM is the level modifier xEdit shows next to the reference's level, XLTW the lit-water list; neither had a row before, so both were preserved and remapped but unreachable through the path-addressed setters.
- xEdit: one shared definition `wbXLCM := wbInteger(XLCM, 'Level Modifier', itS32, wbEnum([...]))` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4353-4357`, used by `wbRefRecord(ACHR)` at `:4546` and `wbRefRecord(REFR)` at `:11629`; `wbRArrayS('Lit Water', wbFormIDCk(XLTW, 'Water', [REFR, ACHR]))` at `:4524-4525` for ACHR and `wbRArrayS('Lit Water', wbFormIDCk(XLTW, 'Water', [ACHR, REFR]))` at `:11533-11534` for REFR. XLCM is not part of the shared `wbRefRecord` helper at `:3202`, so only ACHR and REFR get the row; XLTW is not in it either.
- Bounds are the whole `i32` range, not 0..3: xEdit's `wbEnum` displays an unnamed value as `<Unknown: n>` instead of refusing it, and mods carry such values, so the row stays writable and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:value_membership_issues` warns with `scalar_enum_value_unnamed` — the same treatment `ACHR\LockLevel` gives its eleven named levels.
- `XLTW` is a whole-payload form ID and already listed in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formid_subrecords.inc`, so `LitWater` remaps on copy and on write with no code change.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_achr_rows.cpp:AchrRows.LevelModifierAndLitWaterRowsReadAndWrite` and `Radicle/tests/test_refr_extra_rows.cpp:REFRExtraRows.LevelModifierAndLitWaterRowsReadAndWrite` cover the enum name lookup with an unnamed-value negative, the repeated non-nullable link, a scalar write with a reread, a link write that lands as the retargeted raw index and a NULL-target refusal. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR\RagdollBoneId — strided ragdoll rows (#602 A-2 C-29)

- Scope: ACHR and REFR each gain seven `XRGD` rows — `RagdollBoneId` (u8 at offset 0), `RagdollPositionX/Y/Z` (f32 at 4, 8, 12) and `RagdollRotationX/Y/Z` (f32 at 16, 20, 24) — every one of them `"stride": 28` and `insertion: existing_only`. This is the ragdoll WRITE the row asked for, and it corrects the earlier note that said no Radicle row kind covers ragdoll: `stride` addresses an unpacked array whose element size is fixed and whose count comes from the payload length, which is exactly XRGD's shape.
- xEdit: `wbRagdoll` in `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9134-9149` is `wbRStruct('Ragdoll Data', [wbArray(XRGD, 'Bones', wbStruct('Bone', [wbInteger('Bone Id', itU8), wbUnused(3), wbVec3PosRot]))...])`, applied by `wbRefRecord(ACHR)` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4499` and `wbRefRecord(REFR)` at `:11518`. The element is 1 + 3 + 24 bytes, so the stride is 28 and each bone occupies `id, pad[3], position xyz, rotation xyz`. `XRGB` ('Biped Rotation') is wrapped in `IsTES4(nil, ...)` at `wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9146`, so it has no Fallout 4 row and the earlier four-byte `XRGB` claim in this document does not apply.
- `stride` and `repeated` are mutually exclusive in `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:parse_address`, so the rows carry `stride` alone: `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` then derives slot count from `(payload size - array_offset) / stride`, and an XRGD whose length is not a multiple of 28 yields no slots at all and sets `misaligned` — a malformed ragdoll reads as absent instead of reading a bone out of another bone's bytes. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` gates on `index >= slots.size()`, which is what makes per-bone writes and the `subrecord_missing` negative below work without the `repeated` flag.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_achr_rows.cpp:AchrRows.StridedRagdollRowsAddressEachBoneAndGateTheStride` (two bones, per-bone reads of the id, position and rotation slots, a write of the second bone's id and rotation, an index past the last bone, a reread, then a 30-byte XRGD that must produce zero fields and empty reads) and `Radicle/tests/test_refr_extra_rows.cpp:REFRExtraRows.StridedRagdollRowsAddressEachBone` (the same shape on a REFR, with the rewritten 56-byte payload checked byte by byte and an out-of-range bone id throwing `ScalarError`). Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).

## Radicle/tests/test_weapon.cpp:WeaponScalarWrites (#602 C-54)

- Scope: WEAP scalar writes now have a save-and-reparse proof. `Radicle/tests/test_weapon.cpp:scalar_weapon_plugin` builds a synthetic WEAP carrying a 132-byte DNAM and a 41-byte FNAM plus a second WEAP holding the same DNAM bytes, so one test shows both that the addressed words change and that a sibling record is untouched.
- The unknown byte runs C-54 named are `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:WEAP\UnknownAfterAnimationAttackSeconds` (DNAM offset 110, u16, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12988`), `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:WEAP\UnknownEnd` (DNAM offset 128, u32, `:12993`) and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:WEAP\BoltAnimationSeconds` (FNAM offset 20, u32, `:13001`); the rows already existed, so this row is the missing write proof rather than new rows. FNAM is 41 bytes because `Rumble - Peroid (ms)` at `:13011` ends at offset 40.
- `Radicle/tests/test_weapon.cpp` (`WeaponScalarWrites.SaveAndReparseChangesOnlyTheAddressedWords`) writes Speed (DNAM 4), the u16 unknown after Animation Attack Seconds, Stagger (DNAM 124), the u32 unknown at DNAM 128 and Bolt Animation Seconds (FNAM 20), then reparses and compares the whole DNAM and FNAM payloads against the originals with exactly those ranges patched, checks the second WEAP still carries the pristine DNAM, and re-applies the same two values to the reparsed plugin expecting `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:ScalarMutationStatus::unchanged` and an identical `Radicle/src/plugin/writer.cpp:write_plugin` byte stream.
- `Radicle/tests/test_weapon.cpp` (`WeaponScalarWrites.RefusesTheFieldsOfAShortDnamOrFnamAndKeepsTheirBytes`) drops one byte from DNAM and one from FNAM in turn: the fields inside the short subrecord report `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` while the fields of the other subrecord still write, and both payloads survive the round trip with only the permitted write applied. That is the failure mode `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_slot_bytes` guards by treating a payload of the wrong size as no slot at all.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\AttachParentSlots (#602 B-6 B-51)

- Gap: FURN's authoring block carried 34 subrecords and stopped at XMRK, so APPR, OBTE, OBTF, OBTS and STOP were schema-unknown for FURN even though xEdit has them at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6916-6917` (`wbAPPR` then `wbObjectTemplate`, expanded at `:5520`: OBTE Count, the combinations run of OBTF, FULL and OBTS, then the STOP marker). NPC_ already named the same five.
- Change: the five rules are appended to `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\AttachParentSlots`'s record in that xEdit order with NPC_'s values (APPR 0..1, OBTE 0..1 `coupled`, OBTF 0..65535, OBTS 0..65535, STOP 0..1). Appending after XMRK keeps the generated order equal to the order real records use, which is what the authoring-order check in `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` compares against.
- Preflight: `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` skips a subrecord with no rule, so FURN's unrowed SNAM, ENAM, NAM0 and FNPR runs neither break the order check nor count against a maximum. `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp` reports `subrecord_order_invalid` once per record.
- Not insertion: `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:editable` refuses a `coupled` rule and any rule with a maximum above one that is not `uncounted`, so OBTE, OBTF and OBTS are still not addable through `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_with_rules`, and a record that also holds SNAM or FNPR would report `unknown_order` anyway. Adding a FURN object template needs a hand-written block like the one `Radicle/src/forms/armor.cpp:template_boundary` uses for ARMO; that is still open for NPC_ too.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:FurnObjectTemplateRulesMatchNpcAndFollowXmrk` checks the five rules exist, sit after XMRK in that order and match NPC_'s minimum, maximum and coupled flag. `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:FurnTemplateBlockFollowsTheAuthoringOrderInPreflight` reads a synthetic FURN record whose template block is in xEdit order and asserts no `subrecord_order_invalid`, then swaps OBTS before OBTF and asserts the code appears.
- Untested here: no master file is available in this worktree, so the counts real FURN records carry for OBTE, OBTF, OBTS, STOP and APPR are unchecked. `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records_real.cpp` covers them on the data runner, where a count above these maxima or an out-of-order block would fail.

The counted-array rows themselves are in `k_counted_arrays` (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc`), not in `k_scalar_fields`; their member rows are in `k_scalar_fields` and are counted here, which is why the seven `MODT` member rows moved `WEAP` from 63 to 70.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MSWP\Substitutions, Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans (#602 B-44)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MSWP\Substitutions` models xEdit's `wbRArrayS('Material Substitutions', wbRStructSK([0], 'Substitution', [BNAM, SNAM, FNAM, CNAM]))` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12442-12452`) as a count-less `subrecord_group`: leader `BNAM`, then `SNAM`, `FNAM`, `CNAM`. Until this row the four signatures were addressable only as flat repeated rows, so a whole substitution could not be added or removed.
- Member sizes are 0 (variable) on purpose. `CNAM` is an f32 in xEdit, but `Radicle/tests/test_environment_material_swap.cpp` carries a 2-byte `CNAM` inside a run (`MSWP` 0x802) taken from the corpus, and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` refuses a member whose payload differs from its declared size. The row path already refuses a non-4-byte `CNAM` (`Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` throws for a whole-payload f32 of the wrong width), so the group stays permissive and the width check stays where it already was.
- `BNAM` is the only required member, matching `wbRStructSK([0])`: the struct exists only when its first element is present, and the corpus has runs with `BNAM` alone and runs with `BNAM,CNAM` and no `SNAM` (`Radicle/tests/test_environment_material_swap.cpp` MSWP 0x800 third run and 0x802). Marking `SNAM` or `CNAM` required would make `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` refuse those records on every row write.
- New member key `skippable` (`Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:GROUP_MEMBER_KEYS`, `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupMemberDescriptor`). A skippable member that appears before the first leader belongs to no run and is passed over instead of refused. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` threw `SubrecordGroupError` there before, which the corpus shape of `MSWP` requires: the record-level `FNAM` 'Tree Folder' precedes the first `BNAM`, and `MSWP` 0x801 carries a bare `SNAM` with no substitution at all. The refusal is kept for non-skippable members, which is what `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_group.cpp:SubrecordGroup.MismatchedCountAndOrphanMembersFailClosed` asserts for `CONT`'s `COED`.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_subrecord_group` now creates an optional member when it declares a default (`if (!member.required && member.default_payload.empty()) continue;`). `MSWP` needs it: `SNAM` and `CNAM` cannot be required, so without this rule an inserted substitution would be a bare `BNAM` and the caller could not reach the new `SNAM` through `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MSWP\ReplacementMaterial`, whose index would be out of range. `default` already means "the bytes insert writes" for the required members of `INFO\Response`, so the rule generalizes an existing meaning rather than adding one. No existing group declares a default on an optional member, so no other group changes.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots` and `formlink_slots` consult `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:subrecord_group_for_member` for every row whose signature is a member, so the three `MSWP` rows now also require the group to parse. Every signature that can appear outside a run is skippable, so no `MSWP` record that the rows accepted before is refused now, except one whose run is out of order or repeats a member, which xEdit's ordered struct cannot read either.
- Not covered: the record-level `FNAM` 'Tree Folder' still has no row (`Radicle/tests/test_mswp_rows.cpp:MswpRows.RowsUseTheXEditSubrecordsAndStorage` asserts the signature-only lookup stays absent), and no `successors` are declared, so `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:first_successor_index` appends a new run at the end of the record, which is the position xEdit gives the substitutions.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_mswp_rows.cpp:MswpRows.SubstitutionGroupIsALeaderRunOfSkippableMembers` asserts the descriptor (leader required, three skippable members, defaults, and that `subrecord_group_for_member` finds the group from `CNAM`). `MswpRows.SpansSkipTheTreeFolderAndFollowEachLeader` asserts the two runs of the fixture are subrecord 2..5 and 5..7, so the leading `FNAM` is outside both. `MswpRows.InsertsASubstitutionWithItsDefaultMaterialsAndColor` inserts between the two runs, checks an out-of-range index, and asserts the reparsed bytes: the new `BNAM` and `SNAM` are one NUL, the new `CNAM` is 0.0f, and the two original runs keep their bytes. `MswpRows.RemovesOneSubstitutionAndKeepsItsNeighbors` removes the first run and asserts the second run survives with no `CNAM` left. `MswpRows.ASkippableMemberBeforeTheFirstLeaderBelongsToNoRun` is the negative case for the new key: a bare `SNAM` yields no runs and an insert after it leaves the `SNAM` byte-identical. `MswpRows.OutOfOrderSubstitutionFailsClosedWithoutMutation` is the negative case for the group: `BNAM,CNAM,SNAM` throws `SubrecordGroupError` on insert and remove and `ScalarError` on a row write, with the plugin bytes unchanged.
- Parity: `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py --check` still passes; the group adds no rows, so `MSWP` stays at 3 scalar rows in `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md`.
- Generator test: the two `k_subrecord_group_members_0` render expectations in `Radicle/tools/test_subrecord_group_codegen.py:SubrecordGroupCodegenTests.test_subrecord_group_expands_member_rows_and_renders_the_table` gained the new trailing descriptor field. `Radicle/tools/test_field_address_codegen.py` is at the 750-line source cap, so the new key is asserted from `Radicle/tests/test_mswp_rows.cpp:MswpRows.SubstitutionGroupIsALeaderRunOfSkippableMembers` against the generated table instead of from a new Python test method.
- No corpus scan was run for this change; the member shapes come from the fixtures cited above and from xEdit, not from a measured master run. TODO-verify: measure `MSWP` run shapes across the official masters on the data runner, in particular whether any run repeats a member or orders `CNAM` before `SNAM`, because those are the only shapes the new group refuses.
## Radicle/include/fo4/environment/world.hpp:CellData and Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:decode_cell_extras (#602 A-29)
- The typed CELL decode now covers the subrecords the row listed as undecoded: `VISI` and `PCMB` timestamps, the `XCLR` region list, the `XPRI` PreVis reference list, `XCAS` acoustic space, `XCMO` music type, `XCCM` sky/weather region, `XGDR` god rays, `XILL` lock list, `XOWN` owner with `XRNK` rank, `XILW` exterior LOD, `XWCN`/`XWCU` water currents and the `XWEM` water environment map. `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:decode_cell_extras` holds them so `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:decode_cell` stays inside the 750-line source limit.
- xEdit: `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5953-6101`. `XCLR` is `wbArrayS` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6046`: a single packed subrecord of N*4 bytes, not one 4-byte subrecord per region. `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:link_list` takes it with `Reader::unique`, throws `WorldDecodeError` when the size is not a multiple of 4, and pushes one link per 4 bytes; the same shape covers `XPRI` at `:6074`. The corpus has at most one `XCLR` and one `XPRI` per CELL (see the `CELL\Regions` and `CELL\PreVisReferences` bullets above). `XWCU` is a single `wbArray` whose element count xEdit takes from `XWCN` (`:6050-6058`), so `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/world.hpp:WaterCurrent` is decoded with a 16-byte stride and a payload that is not a multiple of 16 throws. `XWCN` and `XWCU` are decoded independently and never cross-checked, matching the read-only schema row `CELL\WaterCurrentVelocityCount`.
- `XOWN` is the FO4 `wbStruct` form (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9093-9101`): the owner link at offset 0, four unused bytes, a No Crime byte and three more unused bytes, 12 bytes total; the No Crime byte is not decoded because no row claims it. The faction rank is the separate `XRNK` subrecord, so `CellData::owner_rank` is an `i32` read from its own 4-byte payload.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/world.hpp:ExteriorLod` follows `wbStruct(XILW, 'Exterior LOD', [link, three floats])` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6064-6069`: the WRLD link at offset 0 and the three offsets at 4, 8 and 12. The schema rows `CELL\ExteriorLodWorldspace` and `CELL\ExteriorLodOffset*` already read the same four slots.
- The eleven `XCLL` members past `Inherits` (Near Height Mid, Near Height Range, Fog Color High Near, Fog Color High Far, High Density Scale, Fog Near Scale, Fog Far Scale, Fog High Near Scale, Fog High Far Scale, Far Height Mid, Far Height Range, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6024-6034`) are gated one by one on the payload length, the way `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:decode_lighting` already gated `Fog Color Far` through `Inherits`: a 135-byte payload keeps Far Height Mid and drops Far Height Range. `Inherits` itself stays gated on `has_inherits`. An LGTM `DATA` has `unused(4)` at that offset (88 at form version 30) followed by the same 11 members, and `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:decode_lighting_template` calls `decode_lighting(..., false)`, so those members are filled for LGTM too. A 136-byte payload reads the whole tail, a 92-byte payload stops at Light Fade End because it is short, and a 128-byte payload stops before Far Height Mid. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_environment_base_records.cpp:lgtm_data` is a 136-byte fixture, and `Radicle/tests/test_environment_base_records.cpp:BaseRecordsTest.DecodesSkyRecords` asserts Near Height Mid through Far Height Range on it.
- `XWEM` is `wbString`, decoded through `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/environment.hpp:zstring_view`, so a payload that is not exactly one NUL-terminated string throws.
- Still missing on this row: the `XCRI` Combined Reference Index struct (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6075-6089`) has two counts inside one payload plus a mesh array and a reference/mesh pair array, which no `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py` kind expresses; the localized `FULL` name is served by `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/strings.hpp:StringTables::resolve_name`; and the new `CellData` members are not surfaced through `radicle_cell_info` in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h`, which is a by-value struct and cannot carry the two link lists.
- Write coverage for the rest of the row: `Radicle/tests/test_cell_rows.cpp:CellRows.WritesScalarsAndLinksThenRereads` writes `CELL\Owner` over the 12-byte `XOWN` payload and the reread keeps the No Crime byte, so the row's "no WRITE for flags, lighting, water, regions, owner, lock list and LOD data" is stale; the same test writes the `XILL` lock list and the `XCLR` region list.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_environment_world.cpp:WorldEnvironmentTest.DecodesCellLightingTailAndExtraSubrecords` reads every new member byte-exactly from a synthetic plugin and checks the negative cases (a 135-byte `XCLL`, a 2-byte `XCLR`, a 6-byte `XPRI` and a 20-byte `XWCU` all throw `fo4::env::WorldDecodeError`, and the `XCLR` and `XPRI` in the good record are each one 8-byte subrecord with two links); `Radicle/tests/xcll_fixture.hpp:xcll_bytes` now writes the full 136-byte tail so `DecodesCellFields` and `RejectsMalformedAndWrongRecords` keep their truncated-payload coverage.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\Sprites, Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans (#602 B-31)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\Sprites` rows the sprite array of xEdit's `wbRecord(LENS)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12405-12426`): `wbRArrayS('Lens Flare Sprites', wbRStructSK([0], 'Flare', [wbString(DNAM, 'Lens Flare Sprite ID'), wbString(FNAM, 'Texture'), wbStruct(LFSD, 'Lens Flare Data', [...])])).SetCountPath(LFSP)`. It is a `subrecord_group` with `count_subrecord` `LFSP` and three required, non-repeatable members: `DNAM` (payload 0, default `00`), `FNAM` (payload 0, default `00`) and `LFSD` (payload 36). The sprite DNAM and FNAM are zero-terminated strings, so a member carries no fixed `payload_size` and the defaults are a single NUL, the same shape as `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MSWP\Substitutions`.
- Corpus evidence, read-only scan of the seven masters (re-run 2026-10-19): 35 LENS records and 299 sprites in `Fallout4.esm`, 440 sprites across all seven; every `LFSP` value equals the number of `DNAM`,`FNAM`,`LFSD` triples that follow it (0 mismatches), every `LFSD` is 36 bytes, and `DNAM`/`FNAM` are `HexShape01Close`/`Effects\LensFlares\LensHexShape01_d.DDS` style zstrings whose payload is exactly the text plus one NUL (440 of 440, no trailing bytes and no missing terminator).
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\SpriteTotal` rows `LFSP` as a whole-payload u32, which `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:load_schema` requires for a group's count subrecord. `LFSP` stays out of the LENS authoring list, as the earlier LENS entry records: the sprite DNAM follows it in vanilla and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` would reject that order.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\SpriteTintRed`, `LENS\SpriteTintGreen`, `LENS\SpriteTintBlue`, `LENS\SpriteWidth`, `LENS\SpriteHeight`, `LENS\SpritePosition`, `LENS\SpriteAngularFade`, `LENS\SpriteOpacity` and `LENS\SpriteFlags` row the nine `LFSD` fields at offsets 0 to 32: xEdit's `wbFloatColors('Tint')` is three floats (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:6810-6834`), then `Width`, `Height`, `Position`, `Angular Fade` and `Opacity` as floats and the u32 flags (bit 0 `Rotates`, bit 1 `Shrinks When Occluded`). They are member `fields` of `LFSD`, so `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` emits them as `repeated` rows addressed by sprite occurrence, the shape of `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\NeckFatAdjustmentsScaleX` and `CONT\ItemCount`.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` now starts a counted group's scan after its count subrecord, because the LENS record-level DNAM (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\FadeDistanceRadiusScale`, scoped by `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidates`) shares its signature with the sprite leader DNAM and would otherwise open a run of its own. The invariant holds in the masters: `COCT` precedes `CNTO` in all 452 vanilla CONT, FURN and TERM records that carry both. Deviation: a counted group whose counter follows its runs now fails the count check instead of scanning, and no vanilla record does that. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots` already validates the group before a scalar write, so writing `LENS\FadeDistanceRadiusScale` on a record whose sprite array is malformed now throws `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` instead of reporting a missing subrecord.
- Tests in `Radicle/tests/test_material_impact_records.cpp`: `LensSpriteGroupRowsFollowTheCountSubrecord` pins the descriptor (LFSP count, three required members, the 36-byte LFSD) and the spans of the fixture LENS 000806 as [4,7) and [7,10), so the record-level DNAM at index 2 belongs to no run, and of 00080D (no record DNAM) as [2,5); `LensSpriteRowsAddressOneSpriteAtATime` writes `LENS\SpriteOpacity` occurrence 1 and `LENS\SpriteFlags` occurrence 0 and asserts only their own 36-byte `LFSD` changed, that occurrence 2 is `subrecord_missing`, and that bit 1 reads `Shrinks When Occluded`; `LensSpriteInsertAndRemoveKeepTheSpriteTotal` removes sprite 0 (LFSP drops to 1, SpriteB survives) and inserts at index 1 (LFSP rises to 3, the new sprite has an empty DNAM and FNAM and 36 zero bytes, its neighbours keep their payloads); `LensSpriteCountMismatchFailsClosed` is the negative case, an `LFSP` of 2 with one sprite refuses insert and remove with `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupError` and leaves the plugin bytes unchanged.
- Not rowed: the sprite DNAM and FNAM strings themselves. `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` only accepts scalar and FormLink rows on a member, so a sprite's text stays readable through `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` only.
- `#602 B-23` INNR naming rules stay unrowed, and the reason is sharper than the round 8 entry recorded. Corpus scan of `Fallout4.esm` (7 INNR records, e.g. form `0x23c063` with 1158 subrecords): each ruleset is `VNAM` (u32 count) followed by that many names, and one name is the tuple `WNAM` (zstring), `KSIZ` (u32), `KWDA` (one packed array of form IDs) and `YNAM` (u16), with `XNAM` absent everywhere. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` requires member indices to be non-decreasing across a run and repeats only of the immediately preceding repeatable member, so no group descriptor can hold a run of repeated tuples; the missing mechanism is a counted sub-run inside a run (a nested element count), which `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` and `group_spans` would both need.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\SpriteId` and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\SpriteTexture` now row the sprite's two strings: the sprite ID on member `DNAM` and the texture on member `FNAM`, both `kind: string` with `offset` 0, no `storage`, no `payload_size` and no `minimum_payload_size`, `insertion: existing_only` and neither localized, because xEdit declares plain `wbString(DNAM, 'Lens Flare Sprite ID')` and `wbString(FNAM, 'Texture')` rather than `wbLString` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12412-12413`). The expanded rows are `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:ScalarDescriptor` rows with `storage` `zstring`, `embedded` true at offset 0, `address.repeated` true and `payload_size` 0, so the slot of a sprite string is whatever NUL-terminated prefix the member subrecord already carries.
- `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` accepts a member field row with `kind: string`: `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:GROUP_ROW_FORBIDDEN` no longer bars `kind` itself, the row must carry a non-negative `offset`, and `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:STRING_FORBIDDEN` rejects `storage`, `presentation`, `minimum`, `maximum` and `names` on it, so `storage: zstring` on a member row stays an error and `payload_size`, `stride` and `array_offset` stay barred by the member key list. Every expanded member row (scalar and string) is now marked `group_member`, and `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:reject_overlaps` skips the pair when exactly one row of the same signature is a group member row and the two layouts differ: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\FadeDistanceRadiusScale` is a whole-payload, non-repeated `DNAM` row while `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\SpriteId` is an embedded, repeated one, and the member row addresses its own run instance rather than the record-level subrecord. A repeated whole-payload row on the same signature is still rejected (`Radicle/tools/test_subrecord_group_string_rows.py:SubrecordGroupStringRowTests.test_member_string_row_still_conflicts_with_a_repeated_whole_payload_row`).
- Addressing is the group's span ordinal. `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidates` takes a `repeated` flag from `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots`, which passes `address.repeated`; for a LENS `DNAM` row that is true, the branch returns the `DNAM` subrecords after the first `LFSP` (`Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:after_marker`), which are exactly the sprite run leaders because `DNAM` is the group's required, non-repeatable leader. Slot k is therefore sprite k, the same ordinal the `LFSD` member rows use, and the record-level `DNAM` stays with `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LENS\FadeDistanceRadiusScale` through `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:before_marker`. The sprite texture needs no scope: `FNAM` is only ever a sprite texture in a LENS record, and the corpus check above confirms one `FNAM` per sprite in all 49 records. Deviation: a `DNAM` that follows `LFSP` but belongs to no run (a malformed array) still counts as a slot for the read path; `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots` validates the run shape through `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` first, so a write to a record whose run shape is malformed throws `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError`. The counter value is not part of that check: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_counter` is what compares it with the run count, and only `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_subrecord_group` and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:remove_record_subrecord_group` call it, so a record with `LFSP` 2 and three complete runs still offers three slots to a scalar write.
- The read is `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:slot_string_bytes`: the slot is the payload from the row offset up to and including the first NUL, and a payload without a NUL throws instead of returning a truncated string. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:decode_scalar` keeps its whole-payload rule unchanged, so a NUL-terminated whole-payload row still refuses a missing NUL, and `Radicle/tests/test_stat_lod_rows.cpp:StatLodRows.ASlotWithoutATerminatorFailsClosed` keeps its behaviour.
- The write is `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar`: a group member string row whose slot is the whole payload is replaced by the encoded value, so its subrecord grows and shrinks to exactly the text plus its NUL — the shape `TwbStringDef.FromStringNative` stores for a variable-size def (`Core/wbInterface.pas:15690-15726` requests `Length(b) + 1` bytes when `sdSize = 0`) and the shape the sprite string payloads of the seven masters carry, per the corpus bullet above. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:group_member` supplies the member descriptor; a member string row that does not own its whole payload — a fixed-size member, or a string sharing its payload with a field that follows it — still refuses a value whose encoded length exceeds the slot, because `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` refuses a size change on a fixed-size member, and a shorter value there keeps the subrecord's size and zero-fills the tail, so a shortened string never reads back with the bytes of the longer one. The existing slot is a `std::span` into the member payload and `data = encoded` reallocates it, so `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` copies the slot length out and lets the span fall out of scope before the resize. Growth is what makes a sprite inserted by `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_subrecord_group` writable at all: the schema default of both sprite members is a single NUL, so the earlier refusal left every new sprite's ID and texture permanently empty. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` still refuses every other embedded string row, so `Radicle/tests/test_stat_lod_rows.cpp:StatLodRows.RefusesGenericWritesAndKeepsTheBytes` is unaffected.
- Tests in `Radicle/tests/test_material_impact_records.cpp`, on the new three-sprite fixture record 00080F (a record-level `DNAM` float, `LFSP` 3, then three sprites): `LensSpriteStringsAddressOneSpriteAtATime` reads all three IDs and all three textures by ordinal, writes the middle sprite's ID and texture, asserts occurrence 3 of either row is `subrecord_missing`, and then asserts the reread record byte for byte: the record-level `DNAM` is still the 3.0f float, sprite 2's two subrecords hold the new text, the other four strings and all three 36-byte `LFSD` payloads are unchanged. It detects a write that lands on the wrong sprite, one that leaks into the record-level `DNAM`, and an off-by-one in the span ordinal. `LensSpriteStringWritesResizeTheirMemberPayload` writes `SpriteBB` (9 bytes into an 8-byte slot) and `flare_c_long.dds` (17 into 12) and asserts the reread record carries both longer values, then writes a shorter value into the now 9-byte slot and asserts the payload shrank to `S` plus its NUL, shrinks the 17-byte texture to `f.dds` the same way, and reports `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:ScalarMutationStatus::unchanged` when the same value is rewritten. It detects a write that cannot resize a sprite string, and one that leaves a padded payload behind a shortened value. `SpriteStringRowsSkipTheRecordLevelDnam` pins fixture LENS 000806, whose record-level `DNAM` is the corpus shape 0.7f (`33 33 33 3F`, no NUL byte in its four bytes) rather than the NUL-leading `1.0f` it carried before: it asserts `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidates` returns subrecord indices 4 and 7 for the repeated `DNAM` row and index 2 for the record-level one, and that both sprite string rows count 2 and read `SpriteA`, `SpriteB`, `flare_a.dds` and `flare_b.dds`. It detects a `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` call that loses the `repeated` flag and scopes the sprite row to the record-level `DNAM`. `InsertedSpriteAcceptsAnIdAndTexture` inserts a sprite at index 1 of LENS 000806 and then writes its ID and its texture, which the one-byte schema default made impossible before the growth rule: it asserts `LFSP` 3, the new `DNAM` and `FNAM` carrying the written text, both neighbours byte-identical, the new `LFSD` 36 zero bytes, and it reads the two new strings back through the row ordinals. `LensSpriteStringWithoutATerminatorFailsClosed` is the negative case: a sprite `DNAM` of `xy` with no NUL reads and writes as `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` while its neighbour's texture still reads, and the plugin bytes are unchanged. It detects a read that truncates an unterminated string to the payload.
- `Radicle/tests/test_material_impact_records.cpp:MaterialImpactSynthetic.EveryScalarRowDecodesOnTheFixture` now resolves every row through `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_slot_bytes` instead of taking the first subrecord of a row's signature. The old shape decoded the record-level `DNAM` of 000806 through `LENS\SpriteId` — a 4-byte float read as a string — and it called `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` outside its `EXPECT_NO_THROW`, so a fixture change there would have aborted the run instead of reporting it. That float was `1.0f`, whose leading NUL byte let the mis-scoped read pass; 000806 now carries the corpus' 0.7f instead. The row's real path is the string tests above.
- The real-data check `Radicle/tests/test_material_impact_records_real.cpp:MaterialImpactRecordsReal.EveryBatchRecordMatchesItsAuthoringAndDecodesEveryRow` now passes each row's own `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/field_address.hpp:FieldAddress` `repeated` flag to `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidates`. The two-argument call it used before took the `false` default, so `LENS\SpriteId` was scoped to the record-level `DNAM` before `LFSP` and ran a 4-byte float through `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:slot_string_bytes`, which throws when the slot holds no NUL. That is not hypothetical: `Fallout4.esm` LENS 001F5496 carries `FadeDistanceRadiusScale` 0.7f = `33 33 33 3F`, and a read-only scan of the seven masters finds it as the only pre-`LFSP` LENS `DNAM` without a NUL byte across all 49 LENS records, so the old call failed the data runner on that one record. `Radicle/tests/test_material_impact_records.cpp:SpriteStringRowsSkipTheRecordLevelDnam` gives the synthetic fixture the same shape, so the regression now fails in the unit suite as well.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/behavior_layout.hpp:behavior_field_candidates` no longer defaults `repeated` to `false`, so every caller states the row's own flag and a wiring mistake of this kind cannot pass silently again. `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_formid_offsets` and `Radicle/tests/test_behavior_writer_real.cpp` pass `false` because their branch is `PACK`-only and ignores the flag.
- `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py:main` regenerated `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md`: LENS moves from 0 to 2 string rows and from 9 to 11 member rows.
- Python coverage for the new parser rules is `Radicle/tools/test_subrecord_group_string_rows.py`: the expanded row shape, the rejected keys, the `kind` value, the missing offset and the overlap exemption. It detects a `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` or `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:reject_overlaps` change that stops accepting a string member row (the LENS schema would fail to load) or starts accepting a string row with a storage key.
- `#602 B-23` INNR naming rules stay unrowed, and the reason is sharper than the round 8 entry recorded. Corpus scan of `Fallout4.esm` (7 INNR records, e.g. form `0x23c063` with 1158 subrecords): each ruleset is `VNAM` (u32 count) followed by that many names, and one name is the tuple `WNAM` (zstring), `KSIZ` (u32), `KWDA` (one packed array of form IDs) and `YNAM` (u16), with `XNAM` absent everywhere. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` requires member indices to be non-decreasing across a run and repeats only of the immediately preceding repeatable member, so no group descriptor can hold a run of repeated tuples; the missing mechanism is a counted sub-run inside a run (a nested element count), which `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` and `group_spans` would both need.
## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_cell.h:radicle_cell_info and Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:radicle_cell_get_info (#602 A-29)
- `Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:radicle_cell_get_info` now copies every `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/world.hpp:CellData` member into `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_cell.h:radicle_cell_info`: the previs and precombined timestamps, the acoustic space, music type, sky/weather region, god rays, lock list and owner keys, the owner rank, the exterior LOD, the water current count and the water environment map. The new members are appended after `water`, so every existing member keeps its offset and only `sizeof(radicle_cell_info)` grows. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is not changed by this lane.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_cell.h:radicle_cell_lighting_tail` carries the eleven `XCLL` members past `Inherits` that `Radicle/src/environment/world.cpp:decode_lighting` already decoded. It is a separate struct instead of more members of `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h:radicle_cell_lighting` because that struct is embedded in the middle of `radicle_cell_info` and of `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_records.h:radicle_lighting_template_info`, where growing it would move `god_rays`.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_env_internal.hpp:to_c_lighting_tail` groups the tail the way its payload-length gates do: `has_near_height` covers Near Height Mid and Range, `has_high_fog_colors` covers Fog Color High Near and Far, `has_fog_scales` covers the four scale floats, `has_far_height` covers Far Height Mid and Range, and `has_high_density_scale` stands alone. A 135-byte payload therefore reports `has_near_height` 1 with `has_far_height` 0.
- The two link lists cannot live in a by-value struct, so they get their own exports: `Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:radicle_cell_get_regions` for `XCLR` and `Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:radicle_cell_get_previs_references` for `XPRI`, both through `Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:cell_link_list` and `Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:copy_form_keys`, released with `Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:radicle_free_form_keys`. `Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:radicle_cell_get_water_currents` does the same for `XWCU` with `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_cell.h:radicle_water_current` and `Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:radicle_free_water_currents`. All three null the out pointer and zero the count before decoding, so a malformed record leaves an empty list behind its parse error.
- Managed: `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleEnvironment.cs:CellInfo` gains the same members, `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleEnvironment.cs:Lighting` gains the tail groups, and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleEnvironment.cs:CellRegions`, `CellPrevisReferences` and `CellWaterCurrents` wrap the three list exports through the existing `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/Core.cs:Call.Copy` helper. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` are regenerated by `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py`.
- `radicle_cell_info`, `radicle_cell_lighting_tail`, `radicle_water_current`, `radicle_cell_child` and the CELL query exports moved from `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h` to `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_cell.h` in the same change, because the additions pushed the env header past the 750-line source limit. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h` includes `fo4/c_api_cell.h` at its foot the way it already includes `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_records.h`, so every existing includer keeps the declarations; `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h:radicle_byte_color` and `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h:radicle_cell_lighting` stay in the env header because `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_records.h:radicle_lighting_template_info` uses them. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` already lists `fo4/c_api_cell.h` in its `HEADERS`, so no generator change was needed.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_cell_abi_extras.cpp:CellAbiTest.ExposesCellMembersLightingTailAndPackedLists` reads every new member through the C ABI from a synthetic `Extras.esp`, and `Radicle/tests/test_cell_abi_extras.cpp:CellAbiTest.ReportsShortTailsMalformedSubrecordsAndNonCells` covers the negative cases (a 135-byte `XCLL`, a 2-byte `XCLR`, a WRLD record and null arguments). Still missing: no managed test reads the new members, because the world fixture in `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/EnvironmentTests.cs` has no CELL carrying the extras; and `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/world.hpp:CellData` still has no `XCRI` Combined Reference Index.

## Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:is_derived_scalar_row and Radicle/tests/test_sound_writer_real.cpp:EveryScalarStringAndLinkPathEditsFirstAndLastSlotsWithoutTouchingOtherBytes (#602 real-data)

- The real-data job failed this sweep two ways, both in the test, and both are the sweep disagreeing with a writer refusal that xEdit backs. `Radicle/tests/test_sound_writer_real.cpp:EveryScalarStringAndLinkPathEditsFirstAndLastSlotsWithoutTouchingOtherBytes` resolved `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` against `original` while writing into `sample`, so every slot it picked was one resolution behind the record it was editing; it now resolves against `fo4::find_record(sample, record.form_key)`, the same record `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` writes, and takes the `existing` bytes for the value flip from that same record.
- That staleness is the whole of the 424 `ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` results: the sweep writes `SNDR\DescriptorType` (`CNAM`) into every SNDR record that carries one, and `SNDR\DbVariance`, `SNDR\FrequencyShift`, `SNDR\FrequencyVariance`, `SNDR\Priority` and `SNDR\StaticAttenuation` are all `BNAM` rows guarded by `FieldDiscriminator{CNAM, ..., {519001098, 1415912003}}`. xEdit `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9430-9439` makes `BNAM` a union whose arm is chosen by `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:1556:wbSNDRDataDecider`: `CNAM` `$ED157AE3` `AutoWeapon` gives the Base Descriptor FormID, and anything else (`$1EEF540A` `Standard`, `$54651A43` `Compound`, or an absent `CNAM`, matching `match_absent`) gives the five-value struct. Writing `1` into `CNAM` therefore really does turn those four `BNAM` rows into a FormID, and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` returning `subrecord_missing` for them is correct. `DbVariance` sorts before `DescriptorType`, so it is written before the guard breaks and succeeds; the other four sort after and account for the count: four rows per SNDR record that carries a listed `CNAM`, which is the shape of the 424. TODO-verify: the per-record multiplier is inferred from the 424 total and was not measured, because no master was read on this machine; the data runner can count the SNDR records with a listed `CNAM` to confirm four times that number.
- The exception is the derived count. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:is_derived_scalar_row` is the new single answer to "does another mechanism own this value": it reports the counted-array counts, the subrecord group counts and `FSTS` `XCNT`. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` keeps its three messages but now takes the `FSTS` `XCNT` condition from the predicate instead of naming the signatures inline, and the sweep skips any row the predicate reports, counting them in the `derived_rows` record property so the skip stays visible evidence. xEdit `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8694-8714` is the reason `XCNT` is derived: the five `XCNT` words are the `SetCountPath('..\XCNT\...', True)` of the five `DATA` footstep arrays, so a direct write would desync the record.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_fsts_rows.cpp:FstsRows.RefusesGenericEditsOfTheDerivedCounts` now also pins the predicate itself (`FSTS`+`XCNT` true, `FSTS`+`DATA` false, `SNDR`+`XCNT` false), which is the contract the sweep relies on; the regression it detects is the predicate and the writer drifting apart, which is what let the sweep call the scalar setter on a derived row in the first place. The sweep needs the real masters, so its own coverage stays on the data runner.

## Radicle/tests/test_vegetation_real.cpp:EveryNewScalarPathEditsOfficialRecordsWithoutLosingData (#602 real-data)

- The real-data job failed this sweep with `FLOR\DestructionStageModel is a string field; use the string setter` on Fallout4.esm and `FLOR\Model is a string field; use the string setter` on three DLC masters. The sweep fed every row of `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:scalar_fields` to `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` through the scalar setter, and a string-kind row is still a `scalar_fields` row: `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarFieldDescriptor` carries `ScalarStorage::zstring` for the string rows, the older precedents being `FSTP\Tag`, `SNDR\Notes` and `SNDR\Sounds`. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FLOR\Model` is a `kind: string` row added with the WP-9 bounds/model rows, and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FLOR\DestructionStageModel` and `FLOR\DestructionStageSequenceName` are the per-stage strings added with the destructible group rows, so the sweep reached a row it must not send to the scalar setter. The fix is the kind filter the sweep lacked: `zstring` rows are skipped and counted in the `string_rows` record property, which is why Fallout4.esm stopped at `DestructionStageModel` (it sorts before `Model`) and the DLC masters at `Model`. The string writes for the same row shapes stay covered by `Radicle/tests/test_destructible_rows.cpp:StageModelRowsAreIndexedPerSubrecordNotPerStage` (ACTI `DMDL` and `DSTA`) and `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_bounds_model_rows.cpp` (an ANIO `MODL` write); what this sweep no longer exercises is the real-data addressing of the three FLOR string rows.
- The same sweep had a second, latent mismatch that the exception hid. It wrote slot 0 of every row with the index-less `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_scalar` overload, then verified by patching `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:patch_scalar_field` into every subrecord carrying that signature. Every destructible row is `repeated` (DSTD, DSTA, DMDL, DMDC, DMDS; see the destructible group entry above) and a real stage run interleaves them, so stage 2 and later were compared against stage 1's value. The sweep now resolves `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` for the row, writes index 0 explicitly, records the written subrecord index in `applied_subrecord`, and the verification patches only that subrecord. The regression this detects is a record whose stage runs disagree: with the old verification the byte compare failed on the stages the sweep never wrote.
- The write side also stopped hand-rolling its own subrecord lookup. It now takes the first `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` slot and skips the row when that slot is not valid, which is the same resolution `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` uses, so a row whose payload size, guard or duplicate count makes it unwritable is skipped instead of throwing. The old lookup read the first subrecord with the row's signature and would have thrown `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` on a record with two `DAMC` subrecords, which `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` reports as `duplicate` for the counted-array member row `FLOR\DestructionResistanceValue` (`repeated` false, stride 8). Multi-element resistance and property arrays stay with the counted-array rows and their own tests.
- Not verified: no C++ build or real-data run happens on this machine, so the sweep's own coverage still rests on the data runner. TODO-verify: confirm on the data runner that the `fields` and `string_rows` record properties are non-zero for Fallout4.esm and the DLC masters, which is what shows the kind filter and the slot resolution are doing their work rather than skipping everything.
## Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionData and Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region (#602 C-33)
- Scope: `REGN` gains a typed read-only decode in a new `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp` and `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp`, registered as `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt` `src/environment/region.cpp`. `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` throws `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/world.hpp:WorldDecodeError` on a wrong signature or a malformed present subrecord, the same error every other environment decode uses. It is the last piece the `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN` note called out as missing ("no typed REGN decode or create function"); there is still no REGN create function.
