- xEdit proof: `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` at the pinned commit, `wbRecord(REGN, 'Region')` at `:11870` through `:11959`. `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` covers `RCLR` (`:11875`), `WNAM` (`:11876`), `wbRegionAreas` (`:11877`), the region data entry struct (`:11878` through `:11957`) and the `RDMO` music link (`:11900`).
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionData.map_color` is the whole 4-byte `RCLR` payload: `wbByteColors` is `{u8 Red, u8 Green, u8 Blue, wbUnused(1)}` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:6680-6692`), so `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` reads it with `reader.sized(RCLR, 4)` and `Reader::color`, and any other length is malformed. Corpus: one 4-byte `RCLR` in all 106 Fallout4.esm and all 28 DLCNukaWorld records.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionData.worldspace` is the `WNAM` link, resolved through `Reader::link` (`wbFormIDCkNoReach`, no NULL and no reach check).
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionArea`: `wbRegionAreas` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9151-9166`) is a plain `wbRStruct`, not a `wbStructSK`, so its members are in definition order and an `RPLI` always opens an area. `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` therefore starts a new area on every 4-byte `RPLI` and attaches each following `RPLD` to the area it last opened; an `RPLD` before any `RPLI`, or an `RPLI` that is not four bytes, is malformed. An `RPLD` after an `RDAT` with no new `RPLI` still attaches to the last area, where xEdit flags and skips it by the same top-level lookup (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:10531-10539`); no shipped `REGN` has one (0 of 153 in the seven official masters). A record with two areas and no points (the shape the existing `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp:RegnRows.CountsRepeatedDataEntries` fixture uses) decodes as two empty areas.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionArea.points` is one packed `RPLD` subrecord of 8-byte `{f32 X, f32 Y}` pairs, not one subrecord per point: xEdit declares it `wbArray(RPLD, 'Points', wbStruct('Point', [wbFloat('X'), wbFloat('Y')]))` (`:9157-9161`), which is `wbArray` and not `wbRArray`, and its `wbRPLDAfterLoad` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:1105`) walks the loaded element list to flip the point winding, which only exists for a packed payload. `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:read_points` rejects a length that is not a multiple of 8.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionDataEntry`: each 8-byte `RDAT` header `{u32 Type, u8 Override, u8 Priority, 2 unused}` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11880-11894`) opens one entry. `wbRStructSK([0], 'Region Data Entry', ...)` keys the entry on that header and the header is `SetRequired`, so an entry payload belongs to the `RDAT` that precedes it with no `RPLI` in between (an `RPLI` closes the entry) and `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` reports a payload that appears before the first header as malformed, and likewise an `RLDM` or entry payload that appears after an `RPLI` following the last header with no new `RDAT` (refused as "appears outside an open RDAT data entry"). Corpus: all 146 entry payloads in the 153 `REGN` records of the seven official masters (REGN records per master: Fallout4.esm 106, DLCNukaWorld.esm 28, DLCCoast.esm 19, the other four none) follow the `RDAT` that opens their entry, and none precedes it; all 124 `RPLD` payloads follow an `RPLI`.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionObject` is the packed 52-byte `RDOT` element (`wbArray(RDOT, 'Objects', ...)`, `:11909-11942`), read by `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:read_objects` at offsets 0 object form ID, 4 parent index, 6 two unused bytes, 8 density, 12 clustering, 13 min slope, 14 max slope, 15 flags, 16 radius with parent, 18 radius, 20 min height, 24 max height, 28 sink, 32 sink variance, 36 size variance, 40/42/44 angle variance, 46 two unused bytes and 48 four unused bytes. That stride and its offset-0 link are the ones `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp:record_fixed_layout_offsets` already remaps (`{"REGN", {"RDOT", 52, {0}, false, 0}}`), so the typed decode and the form ID remap agree on the element shape.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionDataEntry.grasses` is the packed 8-byte `RDGS` element `{Grass form ID, 4 unused}` (`wbArrayS(RDGS, ...)`, `:11944-11948`); the element carries no other named member, so the list holds plain form IDs like `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/world.hpp:CellData.regions` does over the packed `XCLR`, and the four unused bytes are dropped. `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionWeather` is the packed 12-byte `RDWT` element `{Weather form ID, Chance u32, Global form ID}` (`wbArrayS(RDWT, ...)`, `:11950-11955`). The global is `wbFormIDCk('Global', [GLOB, NULL])`, so a raw zero becomes `std::nullopt` in `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:read_weathers` rather than a link to a null key.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionSound` is the packed 12-byte `RDSA` element `{Sound form ID, Flags u32, Chance f32}`. Fallout 4's sound subrecord is `RDSA`: `wbRegionSounds` is `wbArrayS(IfThen(wbIsOblivion or wbIsFallout3, RDSD, RDSA), 'Sounds', ...)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9168-9187`), so `RDSD` is the Oblivion and Fallout 3 spelling and is deliberately not decoded. The row text also named `RDMD`: that signature is declared (`Core/wbDefinitionsSignatures.pas:1248`) and is the Oblivion and Fallout 3 `'Music Type'` u32 under `wbMusicEnum` (`Core/wbDefinitionsTES4.pas:3309`; hidden in Fallout 3 and New Vegas by `SetDontShow(wbNeverShow)`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO3.pas:7182`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFNV.pas:7861`). It is absent from `wbRecord(REGN, 'Region')` in Fallout 4 (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11870-11959`), where `RDMO` carries the music link instead, and no `REGN` record in the seven official masters carries one, so nothing decodes it. The 12-byte stride and its offset-0 link are again the ones `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp:record_fixed_layout_offsets` already uses for `RDSA`.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionDataEntry.map_name` is `RDMP`, a `wbLString` (`:11904`). `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:stored_name` mirrors `Radicle/src/environment/dialogue.cpp:localized`: a localized plugin stores a 4-byte string ID and anything else is malformed, while a non-localized plugin stores inline NUL-terminated text. The result is the shared `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/environment.hpp:RecordName`, so a caller reads it exactly as it reads a dialogue response.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionDataEntry.lod_display_distance_multiplier` is `RLDM`, the `wbFloat(RLDM, 'LOD Display Distance Multiplier')` that closes every region data entry (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11956`). `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` reads it as a four-byte float on the open entry and refuses it outside an open `RDAT` entry. Corpus: no `REGN` record in the seven official masters carries one, so the member rests on the xEdit pin alone.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionDataEntry.occlusion_accuracy_dist` is the four-byte `ANAM` float of the entry position, and `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionArea.unknown_anam` stores the area-position `ANAM` float as unknown, the name xEdit gives it (`wbUnknown`), because xEdit places `ANAM` twice: `wbRegionAreas` ends its `'Region Area'` struct with `wbUnknown(ANAM)` for Fallout 4 (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9162-9164`) while the region data entry ends with `wbFloat(ANAM, 'Occlusion Accuracy Dist')` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11957`). `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` follows xEdit's positional reading: an `ANAM` that arrives while an entry is open belongs to that entry, and one that follows an `RPLI` before any later `RDAT` sets `unknown_anam` on the area that `RPLI` opened (a new `RPLI` closes the open entry). Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_regn_region_decode.cpp:RegnRows.DecodesAnamInBothXEditPositionsAndEntryLodMultiplier` record 000F25 (RPLI, RPLD, RDAT, RDWT, RPLI, ANAM). Corpus: 41 `ANAM` subrecords in those masters, 25 in the entry position and 16 in the area position, and every one is four bytes holding 2048.0 or 4096.0, which is why `unknown_anam` is typed as the same float even though xEdit names it `wbUnknown` there; the decode requires four bytes in both positions, a size xEdit does not state for the untyped area member. An `RLDM` or entry payload after a reopened `RPLI` with no new `RDAT` is refused by `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` (records 000F26 and 000F27 of the same test). xEdit does not refuse these subrecords: REGN is `SetUnordered` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11959`), and its record loop flags a subrecord that no top-level `REGN` member declares (`Core/wbInterface.pas:10109-10120` looks the signature up in `recSignatures`, which `Core/wbInterface.pas:10012-10049` fills from the top-level members) as unexpected or out of order and skips it (the region data entry struct is not unordered, so it exposes only `RDAT`, `Core/wbInterface.pas:11719-11725`) (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:10531-10539`). Radicle refuses such records instead of guessing. Corpus: a one-off scan of the seven official masters (2026-10-20) found 153 `REGN` records, none with an `RPLI` after an `RDAT`, so the refusal never triggers on shipped data.
- `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:payload_matches_type` is the region data type gate: `RDOT` belongs to type 2, `RDWT` to 3, `RDMP` to 4, `RDGS` to 6 and `RDMO` and `RDSA` to 7, and no payload belongs to any other type. xEdit states the same pairing through `wbGetREGNType`, which reads `RDAT\Type` of the enclosing `'Region Data Entry'` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:2392-2407`), and the `SetDontShow` predicates that hide each family when it does not match (`wbREGNObjectsDontShow` type 2, `wbREGNWeatherDontShow` 3, `wbREGNMapDontShow` 4, `wbREGNGrassDontShow` 6, `wbREGNSoundDontShow` 7, `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:2142-2175`). `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` refuses a mismatched payload instead of attaching it to the entry. Those predicates are display predicates, not load rules: `SetDontShow` hides a family whose type does not match, but the member stays part of the `'Region Data Entry'` struct and Fallout 4's record is `SetUnordered` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11959`), so xEdit still reads a mismatched payload into the hidden member, while `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` fails the whole record through `Radicle/src/environment/record_reader.hpp:Reader::fail`. The refusal is deliberately stricter than xEdit, is unreachable for shipped data and only a hand-built or exotic plugin can reach it; if a caller ever has to read such a record, the refusal is what should be revisited, not the pairing. Two of the seven predicates have no Fallout 4 user: `wbREGNLandDontShow` (type 5) and `wbREGNImposterDontShow` (8) (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:2147-2155`) are referenced only by the Skyrim definition's `wbICON` (`Core/wbDefinitionsTES5.pas:9909`) and by New Vegas (`Core/wbDefinitionsFNV.pas:7879`), and `wbRecord(REGN, 'Region')` in Fallout 4 (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11870-11959`) declares no land and no imposter member, so types 0, 1, 5 and 8 have no payload to pair with and `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:payload_matches_type` refuses every payload under them. Corpus: all 146 payloads in the 153 records of those masters match their entry type (type 2 `RDOT` 5, type 3 `RDWT` 47, type 4 `RDMP` 19, type 6 `RDGS` 2, type 7 `RDMO` 28 and `RDSA` 45), so the gate is a no-op on shipped data and only rejects hand-built records.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN\RegionDataOverride` is an `enum` row over the `RDAT` offset 4 with the `False`/`True` names of xEdit's `wbBoolEnum` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11891`; `wbBoolEnum` itself at `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:7240-7247`), not the raw 0 and 1 it was declared as before. The scalar row still reads and writes the same byte; only the presentation changed, and the row shares the generated name table with every other `False`/`True` enum.
- Deliberately not modeled: `ICON`, which Fallout 4 declares as `wbString(ICON, 'Inventory Image')` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5256`) and which the `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN` note already leaves raw. No `REGN` record in the seven official masters carries one. The record flags bit 6 "Border Region" (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11871-11874`) are likewise not copied into `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionData`; the record header already carries them, and `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/container.hpp:RecordHeader` is reachable from the same `RecordRef`.
- No C ABI: `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionData` holds variable-length areas, points, entries and per-type payloads, so it does not fit the by-value shape of `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_cell.h:radicle_cell_info`. Nothing exports the decode, so `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is untouched, `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` are unchanged, and no C# binding was added. If a caller needs it later, the honest shape is an entry-count export plus per-entry array exports released by a free function, like `Radicle/src/c_api_world.cpp:radicle_cell_get_water_currents`.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_environment_region.cpp:RegionEnvironmentTest.DecodesTypedRegionAreasEntriesAndPayloads` builds a synthetic `Regions.esp` with two areas (two packed points then one), one data entry for each of the xEdit types 2 to 7 carrying its own payload, a `RDWT` pair whose second global is null, an `RDMO` music link and an inline `RDMP`, and asserts every decoded byte and link; the regression it detects is a decode that reads the wrong offsets inside the 52-byte object, loses the area or entry grouping, or resolves a null `RDWT` global to a key. `Radicle/tests/test_environment_region.cpp:RegionEnvironmentTest.RejectsMalformedTypedRegionPayloads` covers twelve negatives in one plugin: a `RPLD` before any `RPLI`, a `RPLD` that is not a multiple of 8, a 2-byte `RPLI`, a 4-byte `RDAT`, a 51-byte `RDOT`, a 13-byte `RDWT`, a 7-byte `RDGS`, an 11-byte `RDSA`, a payload before the first `RDAT`, a 2-byte `RDMP`, a 2-byte `WNAM` and a `CELL` record. Both tests load the plugin through `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/environment.hpp:Environment::load`, which is the only path that can resolve links.
- Not built: nothing on this machine compiles or runs the suite, so the offsets, the `std::array` assignment in `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:read_objects` and the new CMake source line were reviewed by reading, not by a compiler.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FSTS\WalkingFootsteps, Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:packed_segment (#602 B-10)

- `#602 B-10` closes the five `DATA` category arrays of `FSTS`. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FSTS` gains five `formlink_lists` rows (`FSTS\SwimmingFootsteps` segment 0 through `FSTS\WalkingFootsteps` segment 4) on `DATA`, each with `counter` `XCNT`, `counter_payload_size` 20, `segment_counters` `[16, 12, 8, 4, 0]` and its own `segment_index`. The flat `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FSTS\Footsteps` link row stays: `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/SoundAuthoringTests.cs` and `Radicle/tests/test_sound_authoring.cpp:SoundAuthoring` address it by path.
- xEdit (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:8694-8717`) declares `wbStruct(XCNT, 'Footstep Counts', [Walking, Running, Sprinting, Sneaking, Swimming])` and then one `wbArray` per category inside a single `wbStruct(DATA, 'Footsteps', ...)`, in the order Swimming, Sneaking, Sprinting, Running, Walking, each with `SetCountPath('..\XCNT\<category> Count', True)`. So one packed `DATA` subrecord holds the concatenation of the five segments, and a segment's element offset is the running sum of the counts of the segments stored before it. `Radicle/src/environment/sound.cpp:decode_footstep_set` already walked `DATA` in exactly that order, which is why the counter table is `[16, 12, 8, 4, 0]` and not `[0, 4, 8, 12, 16]`.
- The new descriptor fields are `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:FormLinkListDescriptor::segment_index`, `first_segment`, `segment_count` and `counter_payload_size`, indexing `k_generated_packed_segment_counters` (emitted by `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:render`). `segment_count` 0 keeps the old single-counter packed list, so the thirty-six existing packed and keyword lists are untouched.
- `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:packed_segment` is the one place that turns a descriptor into `{base, count}`: it reads every counter of the body, refuses a counter payload whose size is not `counter_payload_size` ("counter subrecord has the wrong size"), refuses a body whose element count is not the counter sum ("counters do not match the link array") and refuses links without a counter at all. Every read, edit, insert, remove, move and clear path of the packed storage goes through it, so a record whose `XCNT` and `DATA` disagree is refused atomically before any byte moves; `Radicle/tests/test_fsts_rows.cpp:FstsRows.CategoryListsRefuseACounterThatDoesNotMatchTheBody` is the negative case for a 4-element body against 5 counted elements and for a 12-byte `XCNT`.
- `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:reconcile_counter` replaces the file-local counter writer it was extracted from. The single-counter branch is byte-for-byte the old behaviour (resize to four bytes, erase at zero); the segmented branch writes only this list's u32 and never erases the shared counter, because `XCNT` is a required subrecord of `FSTS` and its other four counters belong to sibling lists. `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:remove_packed_element` and `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:clear_packed` erase just the segment's byte range and erase `DATA` only when it becomes empty.
- `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_list_read.cpp:record_formlink_list_values` slices the resolved slots from `base` instead of taking all of them; without that it compared the whole `DATA` slot count against one segment's count and threw "has invalid list storage" for every category but the last.
- The generator enforces the layout: `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:parse_list_segment` requires the three segment keys together, `packed_array` storage, a counter signature, a counter payload that is a positive multiple of four and covers every declared offset, unique offsets and an in-range `segment_index`, and every list sharing a `(record, counter)` pair must declare the same `segment_counters`. `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:load_lists` allows sibling segmented rows to share one `(record, subrecord)` pair (they are a partition of it) while still rejecting a duplicate for unsegmented rows, and skips segmented rows in the `reject_overlaps` table because their element addresses are runtime values, not static slot ranges.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_fsts_rows.cpp:FstsRows.CategoryListsSliceThePackedFootstepArray` (per-category sizes and values from one `DATA` payload), `CategoryInsertRewritesItsCountAndShiftsOnlyItsBytes` (insert at walking index 0 writes `XCNT` `{2,2,0,1,1}`, `DATA` `{815,814,812,813,815,811}` and survives a write/read round trip), `CategoryRemoveAndClearRewriteOnlyTheirOwnCount` (remove, out-of-range after removal, clear of an empty segment stays `unchanged`, clear of the only non-empty segment zeroes all five counters and drops `DATA`), and the mismatch test above. `Radicle/tools/test_formlink_list_storage.py:FormLinkListSegmentTests` covers the generator keys, the shared-body rule and the rendered table.
- Not covered: the counts stay non-writable through the generic scalar rows (`Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` still refuses `FSTS` `XCNT`), so a category can only be resized through its list row; and `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_list_read.cpp:record_formlink_list_values` for a segmented list resolves the whole `DATA` payload, which is what `resolve_field_slots` already did for the flat row.

## Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans (#602 B-23, skipped)

- `#602 B-23` INNR naming rules stay unrowed. xEdit (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12346-12386`) nests `wbRArray('Naming Rules', wbRStruct('Ruleset', [VNAM count, wbRArray('Names', wbRStruct('Name', [WNAM, wbKeywords, XNAM, YNAM]))]))`, so the real layout is `[VNAM N][N × (WNAM KSIZ KWDA [XNAM] YNAM)]` repeated per ruleset. Corpus scan of `Fallout4.esm` agrees (`XNAM` absent everywhere).
- The missing piece is a counted sub-run inside a run. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` walks one flat run and rejects any member whose index is lower than the previous one ("out of order or repeated"), so the second `WNAM` of a ruleset is refused; `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupDescriptor` has no way to say that `VNAM` bounds a nested repetition, and `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:SubrecordGroupSpan` is a flat `{first, end}` pair with no level, so the per-tuple boundaries an insert or remove would need do not exist.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:records[INNR] naming rules (#602 B-23)

- `#602 B-23` INNR naming rules. xEdit (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12346-12386`) nests `wbRArray('Naming Rules', wbRStruct('Ruleset', [VNAM count, wbRArray('Names', wbRStruct('Name', [WNAM, wbKeywords, XNAM, YNAM]))]))`, so the real layout is `[VNAM N][N × (WNAM KSIZ KWDA [XNAM] YNAM)]` repeated per ruleset. Corpus scan of `Fallout4.esm` agrees (`XNAM` absent everywhere).
- The missing piece is a counted sub-run inside a run. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` walks one flat run and rejects any member whose index is lower than the previous one ("out of order or repeated"), so the second `WNAM` of a ruleset is refused; `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupDescriptor` has no way to say that `VNAM` bounds a nested repetition, and `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:SubrecordGroupSpan` is a flat `{first, end}` pair with no level, so the per-tuple boundaries an insert or remove would need do not exist.
- A count held in a separate subrecord is now expressible (the `FSTS` segment lists above), and the name members themselves would resolve as ordinary repeated rows because each `WNAM`, `KSIZ`, `KWDA`, `XNAM` and `YNAM` occurrence is one tuple slot in order. What still blocks the row is the group half: nested run spans plus a `VNAM` rewrite on add and remove. That is a redesign of `group_spans` and of `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group`, not an extension of the segment mechanism.
- Closed as far as the row half goes: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:INNR\RulesetCount`, `INNR\NameText`, `INNR\KeywordCount`, `INNR\PropertyValue`, `INNR\PropertyTarget`, `INNR\PropertyOperator` and `INNR\NameIndex` are `repeated` rows over `VNAM`, `WNAM`, `KSIZ`, `XNAM` and `YNAM`, so every naming-rule member except the keyword list and the two counts reads through `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar`, and the counts are refused there. The index of a row is the occurrence index of its own subrecord in the record, not the name index, so a caller pairs a `KSIZ` with its name by position, not by value.
- `KWDA` has no row and cannot get one of either shape: a per-subrecord FormLink row (`Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:load_lists` emits `address.repeated` from the storage kind) demands a 4-byte payload while one `KWDA` holds that name's whole packed keyword array, and a `packed_array` list row is emitted with `repeated` false so `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` reports `duplicate` on the second `KWDA`. Its counter `KSIZ` repeats once per name, and `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:subrecord_index` takes the first occurrence, so a list descriptor would measure name 1's count against every keyword in the record. `Radicle/tests/test_kwda_formlink_lists.cpp:KwdaFormLinkList.InnrIsNotAFlatKeywordRecord` keeps guarding that.
- Closed later (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:INNR\NamingRules`): the group descriptor and the add and remove of a name or a ruleset, tested by `Radicle/tests/test_nested_group_runs.cpp` `InsertingAndRemovingANameKeepsItsRulesetCount` and `InsertingAndRemovingARulesetRoundTripsTheBytes`. Still open: the per-name keyword list (no KWDA row under INNR; `INNR\KeywordCount` reads only the KSIZ count).
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:INNR\NameText` is a `kind: string` row because `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:INNR.localized_subrecords` already lists `WNAM`. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` refuses it in a plugin whose TES4 localized flag is set, and `Radicle/src/schema/localized_fields.cpp:read_localized_string` reads the string-id form. The real-data walk in `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records_real.cpp:RowsDecodeAndAuthoringLimitsHold` sent every `zstring` row through `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:decode_scalar`, which requires an inline NUL-terminated string, so it now routes a localized pair through `read_localized_string` first; that is the same branch `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records_real.cpp` already carries. Without it the row would report a false failure on the localized masters.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:INNR\RulesetCount` (`VNAM`) and `INNR\KeywordCount` (`KSIZ`) are xEdit-maintained counts (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:16622` declares `VNAM` `wbCounterAfterSet` and `wbKSIZ` counts the `wbKWDAs` array), so a write through the generic row would desync a record from its own payload. The schema refuses counters two ways and INNR has neither descriptor: `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_counted_array` and `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` emit the `count_subrecord` tables that `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:is_derived_scalar_row` consults, while a counter with no array or group row is listed there as a record/subrecord pair: `FSTS` `XCNT` is that precedent and `INNR` `VNAM`/`KSIZ` join it. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` throws `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` for them before it resolves a slot, so no index ever reaches the payload.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:ItemModRecordsSynthetic.InnrNamingRuleRowsAddressEachName` builds a two-name INNR and asserts the row count per subrecord, the decoded property float, target, operator, index and keyword count of the second name, that a write to `INNR\NameText` and `INNR\NameIndex` at index 1 lands on the second name while the first name, both `KWDA` payloads and `VNAM` stay byte-identical, and that an index past the last name reports `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` with the whole plugin byte-identical, and that writing either count is refused with `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError`. The shared fixture in `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:make_plugin` now carries the two names with one `XNAM` property each, which is what `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:ItemModRecordsSynthetic.EveryScalarRowDecodesOnTheFixture` needs to decode the new rows.
- TODO-verify: nothing on this machine compiles, so the row addressing, the enum name tables, the `read_localized_string` branch, the two counter refusals and the reworked `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:ItemModRecordsSynthetic.InnrNamingRuleRowsAddressEachName` expectations are unverified by a compiler; CI is the first build.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:OTFT\Items, COLL\CollidesWith, COLL\DebugColor*, SCSN\Category, SCSN\Multiplier (#602 flat runs)

- Selection: every unrowed xEdit member of `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` (pin read at `~/ds-proxy/xedit-src/Core`) was listed per record against `fields.json` rows, then filtered to plain shapes that an existing row kind already expresses. TERM body text and menu items (`BTXT`, `ITXT`, `RNAM`, `ANAM`, `ITID`, `UNAM`, `VNAM`, `TNAM`) are already rows (`Radicle/tests/test_term_menu_rows.cpp`); TERM `BSIZ` and `ISIZ` are embedded counts. LVLI, LVLN and LVSP are owned by `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp` and SNDR by `Radicle/src/environment/sound.cpp` (the SNDR `ITMC`, `ITMS`, `ITME` members are item markers, not a flat run). The older notes that call OTFT INAM and COLL CNAM "no row for the packed array" predate `storage: packed_array` (EQUP PNAM, MUSC TNAM, MUST SNAM, CELL XCLR); those two rows are the same shape.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:OTFT\Items` is a packed, appendable, non-nullable list on `INAM` with targets `[ARMO, LVLI]` (`wbArrayS(INAM, 'Items', wbFormIDCk('Item', [ARMO, LVLI]))`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9359`). `anchor_predecessors` is `["EDID"]` because OTFT has no sibling list, as `EQUP\SlotParents`. The array is sorted in xEdit (`wbArrayS`), as CELL XCLR and COBJ FNAM, and Radicle does not reorder it: an insert lands at the requested index. Corpus (Fallout4.esm and the six official DLC masters, read-only): 477 OTFT records, each with exactly one INAM of 4 to 36 bytes (all multiples of 4), 902 entries resolving to 607 ARMO and 295 LVLI, no NULL entry.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:COLL\CollidesWith` is a packed, appendable, non-nullable list on `CNAM` targeting `[COLL]` (`wbArrayS(CNAM, 'Collides With', wbFormIDCk('Forms', [COLL]))`, `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9559`). Anchors are nearest-first in xEdit order (`INTV`, `MNAM`, `GNAM`, `FNAM`, `BNAM`, `DESC`, `EDID`, `:9549-9558`), so a created CNAM lands after INTV. Corpus: 57 COLL records, 56 with one CNAM of 4 to 60 bytes (multiples of 4), 1143 entries all resolving to COLL, no NULL.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:COLL\DebugColorRed`, `COLL\DebugColorGreen` and `COLL\DebugColorBlue` row `wbByteColors(FNAM, 'Debug Color')` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9551`; `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:6680` declares Red, Green, Blue as u8 and `wbUnused(1)`), at offsets 0 to 2 with `payload_size` 4, the shape of `FLOR\MarkerColorRed`. The unused fourth byte is not a row and is preserved. Corpus: 57 of 57 FNAM payloads are 4 bytes, the fourth byte is always 0, channels span 0 to 255. COLL FNAM was already in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/non_formid_slots.inc`, so no remap or unclaimed-link entry changed.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:SCSN\Category` (`CNAM` offset 0, targets `[SNCT]`, not nullable) and `SCSN\Multiplier` (`CNAM` offset 4, f32) are `repeated` rows with `payload_size` 8 over `wbRArray('Category Multipliers', wbStruct(CNAM, 'Category Multiplier', [wbFormIDCk('Category', [SNCT]), wbFloat('Multiplier')]))` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12653-12656`), the IPDS PNAM shape. The remap side already had `SCSN CNAM` in `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_record_stride_layouts`. Corpus: 11 SCSN records, 53 CNAM, all 8 bytes, every link an SNCT, multiplier from 0.0 to 0.5. SCSN authoring is unchanged (it does not list CNAM, and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` skips subrecords with no rule), so these rows only edit existing CNAM subrecords.
- Not rowed here: TERM `PNAM` marker color (4 bytes in 1074 of 1074 corpus records, same shape as COLL FNAM, one more row group), TERM `SNAM` (xEdit declares both a 4-byte looping sound link and the 24-byte `wbSNAMMarkerParams` struct on the same signature, and the corpus holds only the 24-byte form), KSSM `RNAM` (reverb enum plus SNDR link, needs the `wbReverbClassEnum` names), EQUP `ANAM` (corpus values include a CONT and `0xFFFFFFFF`, which an AVIF target rejects), MUST `FNAM` cue points (an uncounted float array) and STAG `TNAM` (a link followed by a zstring).
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_list_rows.cpp:WP9ListRows.OutfitItemsAndCollidesWithAreAppendablePackedListsInXEditOrder` (regression: OTFT or COLL list rows missing, nullable, wrongly typed, or a created CNAM placed before MNAM or INTV), `WP9ListRows.CollisionDebugColorEditsRgbAndKeepsTheUnusedByte` (regression: a write to a color channel clobbering the fourth byte or accepting 256) and `WP9ListRows.SnapshotCategoryMultipliersEditPerSubrecordAndRefuseWrongTargets` (regression: the two SCSN rows addressing the same subrecord index differently, or accepting a non-SNCT target). `Radicle/tests/test_audio_records.cpp:AudioRecordsSynthetic.EveryDeclaredRowDecodesFromTheFixture` needed a CNAM on its SCSN fixture because it requires every declared row to decode.

## include/fo4/papyrus/interpreter.hpp:Interpreter

The first working slice of a Papyrus interpreter over an already parsed `fo4::pex::PexFile`, C++ only, with no engine and no natives. `include/fo4/papyrus/value.hpp:Value` is the runtime model (None, String, Integer, Float, Bool, Object, Array); `include/fo4/papyrus/value.hpp:Array` is a `std::shared_ptr` payload, so two variables holding the same array see each other's writes, which is what Papyrus reference semantics require. `src/papyrus/value.cpp:castScalar` is the whole conversion table (Int/Float/Bool/String), `src/papyrus/value.cpp:equalValues` compares Strings case-insensitively and Floats with the VM's `9.999995e-05` epsilon, and `src/papyrus/value.cpp:orderValues` orders Strings, numbers and Bools only.

`include/fo4/papyrus/interpreter.hpp:Interpreter` keeps a `std::deque<Frame>` and drives every frame from one loop in `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::run`, so a Papyrus call is a `pushFrame` and never C++ recursion; the deque is what keeps `Frame&` valid across a push. `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute` is defined in `src/papyrus/execute.cpp` and dispatches on the mnemonic, validating `instruction.opCode` against `pex::PexFile::kOpCodes` first and taking the required argument count from the same table, so an out-of-range opcode is `Status::UnknownOpcode` and a short argument list is `Status::StackUnderflow` before any operand is read. Operand order follows the compiler: `src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute` reads the destination from `args[0]` for arithmetic, comparisons, `strcat`, `assign`, `cast`, `array_create`, `array_length` and `array_getelement`, from `args[2]` for `propget`, `args[1]` for `array_findelement`, `array_rfindelement` and `callparent`, and `propget`/`propset` take the property name first, the receiver second and then the destination or the new value. `jmp`, `jmpt` and `jmpf` treat their offset operand as relative to the current instruction and `src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute` rejects a target below zero or above the instruction count as `Status::BadJumpTarget`, and a target equal to the count is the implicit return.

Method resolution is `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::findFunction`: named state first, then the empty state, then the same two on each parent class, capped at 64 hops so a cyclic parent chain cannot spin. `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::invoke` tries the loaded script objects first and only then `include/fo4/papyrus/host.hpp:Host::callNative`, so a function flagged `isNative` or a script the host has not loaded both fall through to the registry; a name that resolves nowhere is `Status::FunctionNotFound`. The state used for a `callmethod` is `ObjectRef::state` of the receiver, which is how a named state shadows the empty state for the same function name.

Object state lives in the host, not in the pex. `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::resolveIdentifier` asks `Host::getVariable` before falling back to the pex default in `pex::PexVariable::defaultValue`, and `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::writeOperand` always goes to `Host::setVariable` for a script variable, so a host that keeps instance state sees reads and writes consistently. `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:objectOf` is the only place a `fo4::papyrus::Value` becomes a `fo4::papyrus::ObjectRef`: `Host::getVariable`/`Host::setVariable` are asked only when the frame's `self` is an object, and a frame whose `self` is None (a global call) answers `Status::NullObject` instead, the same status `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::runFunction` gives a `self` that is not an object. The identifier `self` resolves to the frame's receiver and `::NoneVar` to None. `propget`/`propset` in `src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute` resolve the property through the receiver's own script and its parents: an auto property (`pex::PexProperty::isAutoVar`) reads or writes its backing variable through the host, a property with a read or write handler invokes that handler as a normal function with the receiver as `self`, and anything else goes to `Host::getProperty`/`Host::setProperty`.

Errors are typed. `src/papyrus/status.cpp:statusName` names every `Status` and `src/papyrus/status.cpp:isFatal` separates the structural errors (unknown opcode, bad jump, stack underflow, depth or budget exceeded, host and internal errors) from the language-level ones (division by zero, index out of range, type mismatch, null array or object, function not found, argument count, string too long). This slice stops the whole `Run` on any error and returns `Status` with `Result::value` as None, which is the dividing function returning None; real Papyrus logs the error and hands None back to the caller, and resuming would need the engine's error state, so the deviation is deliberate. `Limits::maxInstructions` is counted per Run and `Limits::maxCallDepth` per frame stack, so a self-jump loop and unbounded recursion both end with a status instead of hanging. Host state is mutated as the callbacks are made and is not rolled back on error, so a Run is atomic only as far as the host itself is.

Covered now, and no longer refused: the five struct opcodes `struct_create`, `struct_get`, `struct_set`, `array_findstruct` and `array_rfindstruct` (#821 step 3, see the struct section below) and `GoToState` (see `Radicle/src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::gotoState`). Not covered, deliberately: latent functions, `Wait`, events and the registration table, every Fallout 4 native (the registry is empty in tree; only tests add entries), garbage collection and object lifetime, and save and restore of VM state. `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::coerce` validates and copies a value verbatim, converting only when the runtime scalar type differs from the declared one, because the compiler inserts `cast` where a conversion is needed. `Result` carries no message text, only the status.

Tests are in `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_vm.cpp`, one file, with a `TestHost` that stores scripts, natives, properties and variables in maps: `PapyrusVm.IntegerArithmeticWrapsAndDivisionTruncatesTowardZero` (a wrap and a negative division), `PapyrusVm.DivisionByZeroIsReportedAndTheFunctionYieldsNone`, `PapyrusVm.StringConcatFormatsNumbersAndEqualityIgnoresCase`, `PapyrusVm.ScalarCastsFollowThePapyrusTable`, `PapyrusVm.CastingAnArrayToAScalarIsRejected`, `PapyrusVm.LoopJumpsAreRelativeToTheCurrentInstruction`, `PapyrusVm.BadJumpTargetIsRejectedInsteadOfReadingPastTheFunction`, `PapyrusVm.RecursionReturnsThroughTheCallerDestinationSlot`, `PapyrusVm.RecursionStopsAtTheCallDepthLimit`, `PapyrusVm.InstructionBudgetStopsAnEndlessLoop`, `PapyrusVm.ArrayInstructionsMutateTheSharedArrayInPlace`, `PapyrusVm.ArrayOverrunAndOverlongArraysAreReported`, `PapyrusVm.MethodsResolveThroughTheParentChainAndCallParentRestartsThere`, `PapyrusVm.NamedStatesShadowTheEmptyStateForTheSameFunctionName`, `PapyrusVm.NativeFunctionsResolveThroughTheHostRegistry`, `PapyrusVm.PropertiesUseTheHostAndAutoVariablesUseTheBackingVariable`, `PapyrusVm.UnknownIdentifierAndArgumentCountAreRejected`, `PapyrusVm.StructCreateRefusesAnUntypedDestinationAndUnknownOpcodesAreRejected`, `PapyrusVm.AFunctionMissingFromTheScriptIsReported` and `PapyrusVm.CodeSurvivesThePexWriterAndReaderRoundTrip` stay in `tests/test_papyrus_vm.cpp`; the struct opcodes now run and are covered in `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_structs.cpp` (below), and `GoToState` in the same file. A C ABI over this VM is `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus.h:radicle_papyrus_run` (#821 step 3): a handle type owning an `Interpreter` plus a `Host` implementation built from C function pointers, value constructors/accessors, a native callback, and a status-to-int mapping. `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` moved to 57 with it.

Review fixes in `src/papyrus/execute.cpp`, `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp`, `src/papyrus/value.cpp`, `src/papyrus/array_ops.cpp` and `src/papyrus/status.cpp`, with regression tests in `tests/test_papyrus_vm.cpp` (gtest suite `PapyrusVm`). Each behavioral fix names its test below. Two existing tests were wrong and are corrected in the test file only.

- `src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute` (dispatch): an instruction whose non-empty `mnemonic` differs from the `pex::PexFile::kOpCodes` entry for its `opCode` is `Status::UnknownOpcode`, so the operation and its argument count come from the same entry (`PapyrusVm.StructCreateRefusesAnUntypedDestinationAndUnknownOpcodesAreRejected`, the `Mismatch` case).
- `src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute` (`jumpTo`): a target equal to the instruction count is legal and is the implicit `return` None that `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::run` takes when a frame's `ip` reaches the end; a target above the count or below zero is `Status::BadJumpTarget` (`PapyrusVm.BadJumpTargetIsRejectedInsteadOfReadingPastTheFunction`, the `ToEnd` case).
- Test-only correction in `tests/test_papyrus_vm.cpp` (`PapyrusVm.InstructionBudgetStopsAnEndlessLoop`): the loop spins on `jmp 0`. The old `jmp -1` gives `Status::BadJumpTarget` for a negative target, so the old test expected the wrong status. The budget path passes on the old code too.
- Test-only correction in `tests/test_papyrus_vm.cpp` (`PapyrusVm.RecursionReturnsThroughTheCallerDestinationSlot` and `PapyrusVm.RecursionStopsAtTheCallDepthLimit`): the `jmpf` at index 1 of `Factorial` uses offset `+3`, which lands on the `isub` at index 4. The old `+4` jumped past the `isub` and gave 5 instead of 120.
- `src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute` (`propget`/`propset`): a property with a non-native read or write handler runs that handler as a frame with the receiver as `self`. The old code looked the handler up by name, and `src/pex/pex.cpp:readFunction` never sets a handler name, so the lookup always failed (`PapyrusVm.PropertyHandlersRunEvenWhenTheirFunctionNamesAreEmpty`).
- `src/papyrus/value.cpp:orderValues`: two Integers compare as integers, so values above 2^24 order exactly (`PapyrusVm.IntegerOrderingIsExactBeyondFloatPrecision`).
- `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::castTo` and `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::toBool`: a Bool target is decided before the None shortcut. None, a null object and a null array give false; a non-null object or array gives true. `src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute` (`not`) uses the same `toBool`. `src/papyrus/value.cpp:castScalar` returns false for String to Bool, so `toBool` gives `Status::TypeMismatch`; that choice has not been checked against Papyrus. `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::readBoolOperand` decides a `jmpt`/`jmpf` condition with that same `toBool`, so a branch and `not` agree on every operand kind and there is one truthiness rule in the VM; while branches were Bool-only, a Bool local holding None (an implicit None return stored through `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::coerce`) stopped the Run with `Status::TypeMismatch` where `not` on the same value succeeded (`PapyrusVm.ScalarCastsFollowThePapyrusTable`: the `CastRef` cases branch on an explicit `cast` to Bool, and the `NotNone` case branches on `::NoneVar` directly).
- `src/papyrus/array_ops.cpp:arrayFindElement`: a negative start in `array_rfindelement` counts from the end, so `-1` is the last element (`PapyrusVm.ArrayInstructionsMutateTheSharedArrayInPlace`, the `LastIndex` case).
- `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::run`: the loop stops once `firstError_` is set, so a failed write of a return value into the caller, which `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::popFrame` records, ends the Run (`PapyrusVm.AFailedReturnWriteStopsTheRunInsteadOfContinuingTheCaller`).
- `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::runFunction` and `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::runObjectFunction`: the body runs inside `try`, and an exception escaping it becomes `Status::HostError` through `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:hostFailure`, so a fault in a `include/fo4/papyrus/host.hpp:Host` callback is no longer reported as an interpreter bug (`PapyrusVm.NativeFunctionsResolveThroughTheHostRegistry`, the `Blast` case, whose native throws). `Status::InternalError` is left to the interpreter's own invariant returns, `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::readOperand` (an operand kind outside `pex::PexValueType`) and `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::writeOperand` (a destination that is not an identifier). The interpreter reports its own failures as `Status` values and never throws deliberately, so anything reaching those handlers came through the host; an allocation failure inside the interpreter would be reported as `HostError` as well, which is accepted because `src/papyrus/status.cpp:isFatal` classes both as fatal.
- `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::run` (native entry): a native entry reached with no owning `pex::PexObject` is `Status::FunctionNotFound` instead of dereferencing a null object, and a result the host produced is passed through `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::coerce` to the function's declared `returnType`, the same step the `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::invoke` path takes through `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::storeResult`. A host that answers a `Int`-declared native with a Float value now reaches the caller as an Int, and a result the declared type cannot hold is `Status::TypeMismatch` rather than being handed on as it came (`PapyrusVm.NativeFunctionsResolveThroughTheHostRegistry`, the `Boost` native, which returns a Float for its `Int` return type).
- `src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute` (`strcat`): a joined length above `include/fo4/papyrus/interpreter.hpp:Limits::maxStringLength` (1 MiB by default) is `Status::StringTooLong`, which `src/papyrus/status.cpp:isFatal` classes as non-fatal, like `ArrayTooLong` (`PapyrusVm.StringConcatFormatsNumbersAndEqualityIgnoresCase`, the 8 and 9 cases). The test uses one concatenation over the cap, not a doubling loop, because on the old code a doubling loop would grow until memory ran out instead of failing the assertion. It asserts the enumerator and `src/papyrus/status.cpp:isFatal` false, not the `statusName` text, so it cannot pass on a name table that drifted from the enumerator.
- `src/papyrus/array_ops.cpp:coerceElement`: a non-null Array is never stored as an element, so arrays cannot nest, and `src/papyrus/value.cpp:equalValues` and `src/papyrus/value.cpp:valueToString` recurse at most one level (`PapyrusVm.ArrayOverrunAndOverlongArraysAreReported`, the `Nest` case). No recursion guard was added to either function, because a nested array can no longer be built.
- `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::writeOperand`: writes to `::NoneVar` are discarded, so a later read still gives None (`PapyrusVm.WritesToNoneVarAreDiscardedAndReadBackAsNone`).
- `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::findFunction` (owner out-parameter) and `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::runFunction`: an entry function found on a parent class runs with that parent as its owner, so reads of the parent's variables resolve (`PapyrusVm.MethodsResolveThroughTheParentChainAndCallParentRestartsThere`, the `Level` case). `src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::run` calls `include/fo4/papyrus/host.hpp:Host::callNative` for a native entry instead of running zero instructions (`PapyrusVm.NativeFunctionsResolveThroughTheHostRegistry`, the direct `Boost` call).

## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/value.hpp:Struct (#821 step 3)

`ValueType::Struct` and `Value::structure` add the Fallout 4 struct value. `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/value.hpp:Struct` holds the declared `typeName` and a member map keyed by the folded (lower case) member name, so member access ignores case like every other Papyrus identifier. The payload is a `std::shared_ptr`, so a struct is a reference value: `assign` copies the handle and two variables see each other's writes (`Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_structs.cpp:PapyrusStructs.StructsAreReferenceValuesSharedThroughAssignment`). `Radicle/src/papyrus/value.cpp:valueToString` renders `[Struct]`, `Radicle/src/papyrus/value.cpp:equalValues` compares two engaged structs by `typeName` and then member by member, recursively, through `equalValuesWithin` with a depth cap of 32 and one budget of 4096 struct visits shared by the whole comparison (`kMaxEqualStructVisits`, decremented per struct compared). The budget bounds acyclic shared-child graphs: when `X` and `Y` point at the same child and the two sides are equal, each level doubles the visits (a 16-level chain costs about 2^16 visits), so the budget stops the comparison and it returns false (`PapyrusStructs.StructEqualityOfSharedChainsStopsAtTheVisitBudget`). A cyclic struct is bounded by the depth cap instead, because the first recursion that exceeds depth 32 returns false and the member loop stops there (`PapyrusStructs.StructEqualityOfACyclicStructStopsAtTheDepthCap`); a string member compares case-insensitively and an int against a float compares numerically. This is the `cmp_eq` rule from RE #762 (struct `==` compares members, not payload identity), and `orderValues` still refuses structs. `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/value.hpp:declaredValueType` still maps an unknown type name to `Object`; the interpreter decides that a declared name is a struct by looking it up in the PEX struct table (`Radicle/src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::findStruct`), which is why `value.cpp` does not need that table.

## Radicle/src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute (struct opcodes) (#821 step 3)

Operand shapes are the compiler's, read off `PluginEditTool/native/src/papyrus/Decompiler.cpp`: `struct_create <dest>`, `struct_get <dest> <struct> <member>`, `struct_set <struct> <member> <value>`, `array_findstruct <array> <dest> <member> <value> <start>` and `array_rfindstruct` the same reversed. `struct_create` takes the destination's declared type through `declaredOperandType` and builds the value with `Radicle/src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::makeStruct`: every member starts at its type default (`include/fo4/papyrus/value.hpp:defaultValueFor`, which gives `None` for a struct-typed member) and takes its `PexStructMember::defaultValue` literal when it has one, coerced to the member type. A `None` literal keeps the type default, so an `Int` member with a `None` default is `0`. Struct-typed members are not expanded, so a self-nesting type creates one struct and no depth limit is needed. `array_create` likewise leaves struct elements `None` (`src/papyrus/array_ops.cpp:arrayCreate`), so a struct comes into being only through `struct_create`. A destination whose declared type is not in the object's struct table is `Status::UnknownIdentifier`, which is also why a `struct_create` into an untyped temp is refused rather than guessed. `struct_set` coerces the value to the declared member type (`Status::TypeMismatch` otherwise), `struct_get` and `struct_set` fold the member name, and an unknown member is `Status::UnknownIdentifier`. `array_findstruct`/`array_rfindstruct` follow RE #762 (`src/papyrus/struct_ops.cpp:Interpreter::findStructInArray`): a null or empty array stores `-1` with no error; an array whose element type name is not a struct in the object's struct table is `Status::TypeMismatch`; a reverse start of `-1` means the last element; a start outside `[0, size)` after that rule stores `-1` (no clamping); a `None` element matches only a `None` search value; a struct element without the member, or a member name no struct of that type declares, is `Status::UnknownIdentifier`; a search value whose type differs from the member's declared type (a struct-typed member counts as `Struct`) is `Status::TypeMismatch`. The start defaults (0 forward, -1 reverse) are the compiler's, in-repo only; #762 does not state them. `Radicle/src/papyrus/array_ops.cpp:coerceElement` accepts a struct into an array whose element type name matches its `typeName`. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_structs.cpp:PapyrusStructs.CreateFillsEveryMemberDefaultAndSetWritesIt`, `StructGetReadsACaseInsensitiveMemberName`, `StructSetEnforcesTheDeclaredMemberType`, `StructGetRejectsAnUnknownMember`, `StructCreateRejectsATypeThatIsNotAStruct`, `NestedStructMembersAreAssignedAndReadable`, `StructArrayFindStructReturnsForwardAndReverseIndexes`, `StructReturnValueCoercesAgainstTheDeclaredReturnType`, `StructEqualityComparesMembersNotIdentity`, `StructEqualityOfACyclicStructStopsAtTheDepthCap`, `StructEqualityOfSharedChainsStopsAtTheVisitBudget`, `StructTypedMemberStartsAsNoneUntilAssigned`, `SelfNestingStructCreatesOneStructWithANoneMember`, `NoneMemberDefaultKeepsTheScalarZero`, `StructSearchReturnsMinusOneForANullArray`, `StructSearchTreatsOutOfRangeStartsAsMinusOne`, `StructSearchMatchesANoneElementOnlyForANoneValue`, `StructSearchRejectsAnUnknownMemberAndAMemberTypeMismatch` and `StructSearchRejectsAnArrayThatIsNotOfStructs`.

## Radicle/src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::gotoState (#821 step 3)

`GoToState` is the state machine's own native, so `Radicle/src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::invoke` intercepts it after a non-native function declared in the PEX and before `Host::callNative`; a script that declares its own `GotoState` still wins because `findFunction` runs first. It requires exactly one `String` argument and an object receiver, sets `ObjectRef::state` in place (the `shared_ptr` is what the caller and every frame share, so the change is visible after the call), and stores `None` into the call's destination. The next `callmethod` on the same `ObjectRef` dispatches the named state, which `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_structs.cpp:PapyrusStructs.GotoStateChangesTheReceiverStateForTheNextCall` pins. `Host::gate("vm.states.gotostate")` is consulted first and a refusal is `Status::GateRefused` (`PapyrusStructs.GotoStateHonoursTheHostGate`). This is not a full state machine: state entry/exit events, `OnBeginState`/`OnEndState` and state-scoped auto-properties are not run.

## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/host.hpp:Host::gate (#821 step 3)

`Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/host.hpp:Host::gate` is a default-allow policy hook; `Radicle/src/papyrus/host.cpp:Host::gate` returns true, so a standalone runtime runs without an engine policy. GardenEngine's evidence registry implements it to refuse a semantic family by key, and the interpreter treats a refusal as `Status::GateRefused` (`Radicle/src/papyrus/status.cpp:isFatal` classes it fatal). The key names are the caller's; the interpreter uses `vm.states.gotostate` for the one decision it owns today.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus.h:radicle_papyrus_run (#821 step 3)

The C ABI skeleton over the interpreter. A `radicle_papyrus` handle owns the added `radicle_pex` handles (borrowed, they must outlive it) and a `Radicle/src/c_api_papyrus.cpp:CallbackHost` that answers `findObject` from those files and forwards variables, properties, natives and the gate to `radicle_papyrus_callbacks`. A callback returns 1 when it handled the request and 0 to fall back; a missing callback is not handled, so a runtime with no callbacks still runs pure PEX code. Values cross as `radicle_papyrus_value` handles with constructors and accessors for every kind (none, string, int, float, bool, object, array, struct); a handle is owned by its creator and released with `radicle_papyrus_value_destroy`, and a value a callback returns is copied and freed by the runtime. `radicle_papyrus_run` clears every out-parameter before its checks, copies the argument values, runs `Interpreter::runFunction` and reports the interpreter `Status` through `radicle_papyrus_status` (one value per `fo4::papyrus::Status`, named by `radicle_papyrus_status_name`); a non-OK run leaves `out_result` NULL. The C ABI version moved 56 to 57 for this header. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` gained function-pointer support (a callback field becomes an `IntPtr` in the generated struct) and the header, so `RadicleNative.g.cs` and `abi_layout_probe.cpp` carry the new surface. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_papyrus.cpp:CApiPapyrusTest.RunsAStructFunctionAndReturnsItsMember`, `NativeCallbackAndVariableCallbackServeTheRun`, `GateRefusalAndUnknownFunctionAreReported`, `ValueConstructorsRoundTrip` and `RejectsBadArgumentsAndClearsOutParameters`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/owner.hpp:OwnerId and OwnerRegistry (#821 step 5)

`Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/owner.hpp:OwnerId` is the canonical identity of whatever a script runs on: kind (`Form`, `PlacedReference`, `DynamicReference`, `QuestAlias`, `RuntimeInstance`), base form key and discriminator, with `key()` as the stable text form for identity maps and save data. Equality and ordering are over all three fields, so two placed references, two aliases of one quest and two runtime instances of one base form never collapse into one owner. `OwnerRegistry::allocateRuntimeInstance` hands out a distinct discriminator per base form and `countFor` reports how many it has allocated.

## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/registration.hpp:RegistrationRegistry (#821 step 5)

`RegistrationRegistry` is the typed timer and custom-event registry: a `ScriptRegistration` keeps its whole payload (`CustomEvent` name, or timer interval, repeat flag and `ClockSource`), `matchCustomEvent` folds the name and returns the matching entries in registration order, and `advance` is session-only: a foreign owner is refused and counted, a game-time timer is counted as unbound while the game clock is unavailable instead of firing on the wrong clock, a repeating timer keeps its remainder, and a non-repeating one unregisters after it fires. Timer fire counts use the same boundary tolerance as the C# registry (`nextafter` bump before the floor) so a 2.5 s advance over a 2 s interval fires once, not zero times.

## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/runtime.hpp:Runtime (#821 steps 4-5)

The runtime owns the script set, the instance table, the scheduler, the native and override registries, the registration registry and the owner registry. `attach` creates an instance for an `OwnerId`, `initialize` runs `OnInit` once behind the `vm.lifecycle.oninit_barrier` gate (properties are supplied at attach time, a failed `OnInit` leaves the instance `Failed` and closed, and queued events are refused when it fails), `sendEvent` applies the lifecycle rules (`Failed`/`NotInitialized` refuse and count, `Initializing` refuses or queues as the counted approximation under `vm.lifecycle.event_during_oninit` and the `OnInitArrivalPolicy`), and a `Ready` event is checked against the script's declared functions and the override registry before it enters the scheduler. Instance variables live in the runtime keyed by the `ObjectRef` handle, which is the instance id; `setState` keeps the instance state and the `ObjectRef` in step for `GoToState`. The native registry resolves a native through the script's parent chain and enforces the target contract: only `Static` registrations are callable through the interpreter's `Host::callNative` path today, an instance- or engine-target registration is refused and counted rather than guessed. Overrides are consulted only at a bytecode entry point of an attached instance, require the declared parameter count to match, and count handled, declined and refused outcomes. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_runtime.cpp:RuntimeTest.AttachInitializesOnceAndRunsAnEvent`, `AFailedOnInitLeavesTheInstanceClosed`, `AnEventDuringOnInitIsRefusedOrQueuedByPolicy`, `ASliceParksAndThenDropsARunawayScript`, `ALatentNativeSuspendsAndResumesExactlyOnce`, `NativeRegistryRefusesAnUnknownNativeAndEnforcesRequiredScript`, `OverridesHandleDeclineAndRefuseBeforeBytecode`, `GotoStateChangesTheStateTheNextEventDispatchesIn`, `OwnerRegistryKeepsInstancesOfOneFormDistinct` and `RuntimeRegistryTest.CustomEventsMatchWithoutCaseAndTimersAdvance`.

## Radicle/src/papyrus/scheduler.cpp:Runtime::runStep (#821 step 4)

`Runtime::runStep` is the bounded fair scheduler, gated on `vm.scheduler.instruction_budget`. Waiting latent entries whose completion arrived are moved back to the ready queue with their token and value; then ready events run in arrival order, each under `max(1, remaining budget / remaining events)`, so the step never exceeds its budget and one runaway script cannot starve the rest. A slice that exhausts its share is `Status::Paused` and is parked and re-queued up to `maxParksPerEvent` times (8 by default), after which it is dropped and counted; `Status::Latent` records the token once (a reused token is refused), `Status::Ok` counts a completed event, and any other status is refused and counted. `completeLatent` accepts exactly one completion per token and refuses a second or unknown one. The interpreter side is `Radicle/src/papyrus/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::startFunction`, `resumeSlice` and `completeLatent`, with `Status::Paused` and `Status::Latent` non-fatal, `Host::callLatent` parking the frame with the call's destination, and `Host::setState` keeping the receiver in step.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus_runtime.h:radicle_papyrus_runtime_attach (#821 step 5)

The runtime C ABI over `fo4::papyrus::Runtime`: create/destroy, `add_pex` (borrowed handles, each object registered with the runtime), `attach` with the owner kind and key parts, `initialize`, `send_event`, `step` (the `radicle_papyrus_step_result` counters), `complete_latent`, `register_native` (with the latent flag and the `begin_latent` callback), `register_override`, instance variable get/set, custom-event and timer registration, unregister and `advance_clock`. Values cross as the `radicle_papyrus_value` handles from `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus.h`; `Radicle/src/c_api_papyrus_internal.hpp` now holds that handle and the value/status converters both translation units share. The callbacks carry `gate`, `call_native`, `override_function` and `begin_latent`, and a missing callback is "not handled". `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` moved 57 to 58 for this header, and `RadicleNative.g.cs` plus the layout probe are regenerated. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_papyrus_runtime.cpp:CApiPapyrusRuntimeTest.AttachesInitializesRunsAnEventAndReadsAVariable`, `LatentNativeSuspendsAndResumes` and `OverridesRegistrationsAndRefusals`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/save_state.hpp:SaveState (#821 step 6)

The versioned save state: `SaveState` holds `SavedThread` (owner key, script, fingerprint, function, program counter, locals and the optional latent wait token and native), `SavedRegistration` (owner, kind, event, interval, repeats, clock), `SavedTimer` (owner, event, elapsed, fires) and `SavedObjective` (owner, index, state). `captureSaveState` sorts every list by owner key (objectives also by index) so the JSON text and `digest()` are stable; `serialize()` writes the same field names the C# form uses and `deserialize()` parses that exact schema back, rejecting an unknown version with the C# wording. `Radicle/src/papyrus/save_state.cpp:restoreSaveState` decides per thread: a latent wait is `RejectedLatentWait` because the external answer cannot be restored, an absent script is `RejectedUnknownScript`, a changed fingerprint is `RejectedChangedScript`, and only a matching fingerprint is `Resumed` at its recorded function and program counter; the report keeps the registrations, timers and objectives and its text and digest follow the C# report shape. `Radicle/src/papyrus/save_state.cpp:scriptFingerprint` hashes a canonical text of the object (name, parent, auto state, variables, properties, structs, states, functions, parameters, locals and every instruction operand) with the SHA-256 in `Radicle/src/papyrus/sha256.cpp`, so any script change changes the fingerprint. Real frame serialization stays new design: `Runtime::captureThreads()` captures the suspended latent and parked executions through `Radicle/src/papyrus/execution.cpp:Interpreter::snapshot` (function, pc, local value strings, latent token and native), and the restore decision never invents a frame. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_save_state.cpp:PapyrusSaveState.SerializeRoundTripsAndDigestIsStable`, `RestoreDecidesPerThreadAndRejectsLatentWaits`, `RestoreRejectsAnUnsupportedVersion`, `FingerprintChangesWhenTheScriptChanges` and `RuntimeCapturesASuspendedLatentThread`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/quest_rules.hpp:identifyStartupStages (#821 step 7)

`identifyStartupStages` reads the caller-supplied startup flag on each decoded `QuestStageInput` (Radicle does not guess which QUST stage flag marks the startup stage, as #821 records): exactly one marked stage identifies the startup stage, none is `Unidentified` and more than one is `Ambiguous`, both unresolved and never guessed, and a tie is never broken by index. The `quest.startup.stage_identification` gate can refuse the whole identification, and an identified stage whose `quest.runtime.fragment_dispatch_timing` gate is refused stays `BlockedByFragments` with the stage and fragment count recorded. Quests are processed in name order and the report text and digest follow the C# form. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_quest_rules.cpp:PapyrusQuestRules.IdentifiesTheSingleMarkedStartupStage`, `RefusesToGuessNoneOrSeveralMarkedStages` and `FragmentTimingAndIdentificationGatesBlock`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/quest_rules.hpp:bindVmadValues (#821 step 7)

`bindVmadValues` binds decoded `VmadValueShape` rows to owner-local values: Int/Float/Bool require their value or are unsupported, String defaults to the empty string, an object with `hasAlias` is `AliasBound` because the alias fill order is unproven, an object without a reference is unsupported, and Array/Struct/Variable/Unknown are each their own unsupported kind with a reason. There is no path that returns a value for an unsupported shape and `silentlyDefaulted` stays 0, so a caller can count exactly what is missing instead of reading a PEX default as compatibility. Shapes are bound in name order and the report text and digest follow the C# form. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_quest_rules.cpp:PapyrusQuestRules.BindsEveryScalarShapeAndRefusesTheRest`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/quest_rules.hpp:fillQuestAliases (#821 step 7)

`fillQuestAliases` fills the alias kinds that do not need the actor runtime: `ForcedReference` binds the declared reference, `CreateReference` allocates a fresh runtime-instance owner through `OwnerRegistry` so two creations of one base stay distinct, and `Location` records the location key; `FindMatching` and `UniqueActor` stay open for the actor runtime and are never filled here. Each kind has its own `quest.alias.fill.*` evidence key (the actor kinds share `quest.alias.fill.actors`), an unproven kind leaves the alias empty, counts it and records the kind once in `openKinds`, and a proven fill with a missing value throws. Aliases are processed by quest then alias id. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_quest_rules.cpp:PapyrusQuestRules.FillsTheProvenAliasKindsAndLeavesTheActorsOpen`, `AGateRefusalLeavesTheAliasOpenAndCountsTheKind` and `AProvenFillStillNeedsItsValue`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus_save.h and Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus_quest.h (#821 steps 6-7)

The C ABI for the save state and the quest rules. `radicle_papyrus_save.h` exposes `radicle_papyrus_script_fingerprint` (a script fingerprint from a `radicle_pex`), `radicle_papyrus_save_capture` (the serialized state and its digest from a runtime) and `radicle_papyrus_save_restore` (a report, resumed and rejected counts from the JSON and the current script fingerprints), with `radicle_papyrus_string_free` releasing every returned string. `radicle_papyrus_quest.h` exposes `radicle_papyrus_identify_startup_stages` with its report and outcome arrays, `radicle_papyrus_bind_vmad_values` with a bound-property row per shape (a `radicle_papyrus_value` handle for every bound value) and `radicle_papyrus_fill_quest_aliases` with its outcomes; every report has a destroy function and carries its text and digest. `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` moved 58 to 59, `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` lists both headers, and `RadicleNative.g.cs` plus the layout probe are regenerated. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_papyrus_save_quest.cpp:CApiPapyrusSaveQuestTest.FingerprintsAndCapturesASuspendedThread` and `IdentifiesStagesBindsValuesAndFillsAliases`.
## Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfFile and Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:read_swf (#602 SWF container)

- `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:read_swf` is the container reader for the Fallout 4 menu and HUD movies (`.swf` and Scaleform `.gfx`), which Radicle had no support for. It accepts `FWS` (uncompressed), `CWS` (zlib) and the Scaleform `GFX`/`CFX` variants and parses the 8-byte header (signature, version, file length), the bit-packed `FrameSize` RECT, `FrameRate` (8.8 fixed, see `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfHeader::frame_rate_fps`) and `FrameCount`. The RECT is read MSB-first by `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:BitReader::read_signed`, and the 5-bit `Nbits` field is kept in `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfRect::nbits` so a write re-encodes the same field width; the bits between the rectangle and the next byte boundary are kept as `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfRect::padding` and written back by `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:append_rect`, and an all-zero rectangle (`nbits` 0) stays one byte.
- zlib is already a dependency (`Radicle/CMakeLists.txt` links `ZLIB::ZLIB` into `fo4` and `fo4_tests`), so `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:inflate_body` streams the compressed body through `inflate` instead of `uncompress`, because the declared file length is not always the real uncompressed size; a wrong length is reported through `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfReadResult::declared_length_matches` and does not fail the read. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:kMaxBodyBytes` (256 MiB) caps the output so a zlib bomb cannot allocate without bound. `ZWS` (LZMA) is not decoded: no LZMA library is linked, so `read_swf` returns `SwfStatus::unsupported_compression` with the version and length from the 8-byte header, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:write_swf` throws for `SwfCompression::lzma` instead of adding a dependency.
- Tag stream: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_stream` walks short and long tag headers and records `code`, `length`, `offset` (payload offset in the decompressed body) and `long_header`, keeping every payload as raw bytes; the payload heads that are decoded on top of that container are listed in `## Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_stream and Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTag (#602 SWF tag payloads)` below. `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:tag_code_name` is a display table only; codes outside the SWF 19 list and the GFx extensions that are not named there render as `Unknown`.
- Tag budget: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:kMaxTags` (1 << 18 tags) bounds the `SwfTag` objects of one read, top-level tags and every sprite child together. 1 << 18 rather than 1 << 20 because an estimated ~1 KB per `SwfTag` (not measured) would put a 1 << 20 tag flood near 1 GB; the largest movie in vanilla `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` has 12,875 tags counted recursively (315 movies scanned), well under the cap. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_stream` takes one slot per tag header before the payload is decoded, so a `DefineSprite` takes its own slot before its children; at zero it returns `SwfStatus::too_many_tags` without pushing the over-limit tag. `stop` is the over-limit header at the level where the budget ran out; when that is inside a sprite, the enclosing stream sets `stop` to the sprite's header and does not push the sprite, so `trailing_bytes` start at the outermost unfinished tag. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload` passes the count into the sprite recursion. `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:read_swf` takes the limit as an overload (`read_swf(bytes, max_tags)`) so tests can use small counts. `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:replace_tag_payload` uses a fresh budget per call, so a replace can take the file total past the limit. `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:read_swf` turns `std::bad_alloc` from inflate or tag decoding into `SwfStatus::out_of_memory`, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:inflate_body` calls `inflateEnd` on an exception so the zlib state is not leaked.
- Decoded tags are `FileAttributes` (UseNetwork bit 0, ActionScript3 bit 3, HasMetadata bit 4, UseGPU bit 5, UseDirectBlit bit 6, per the SWF spec, with the raw word kept in `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfFileAttributes::raw`), `SetBackgroundColor` (first three bytes as 0xRRGGBB), `Metadata` (up to the first NUL), `ScriptLimits`, `DefineSprite` (id, frame count and the nested stream in `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTag::children`), `SymbolClass` and `ExportAssets` (id/name pairs), `ImportAssets` 57 and `ImportAssets2` 71 (the source movie, the version and the imported id/name pairs in `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfImportAssets`, decoded by `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload`; the two bytes ImportAssets2 reserves after the URL are read but not required to be 1/0, because writers differ and the pair carries no meaning Radicle uses), `DoABC` 72 (the whole payload is ABC, empty name) and `DoABC2` 82 (flags, name, ABC span), `DoAction` and `DoInitAction` (AVM1 payload span, so an AS2 movie is still readable), `DefineBinaryData` and `End`. A nested tag's `offset` is relative to its parent payload, not to the body. `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:summarize` sets `action_script3` when the FileAttributes bit is set or any ABC block is present.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfAbc` stores the ABC span as `payload_offset`/`payload_size` into the tag payload instead of copying it; `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:abc_payload` and `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:abc_blocks` hand those spans to the ABC decoder lane, which owns `Radicle/include/fo4/abc`. `abc_blocks` walks top-level tags only, because the ABC tags are legal in frame 1 only.
- Truncation is typed. A stream that ends inside a tag header or payload returns `SwfStatus::truncated_tag` with every tag read so far; the partial payload is kept and `length` keeps the declared value, so a truncated movie does not round trip. A tag whose payload is complete but does not decode (a `DoABC2` name with no NUL, a `SymbolClass` entry that runs past the payload, a `FileAttributes` shorter than four bytes) returns `SwfStatus::malformed_tag`, keeps the raw bytes and keeps parsing the following tags. A movie with no `End` tag whose body ends exactly on a tag boundary is `ok`, because nothing was truncated.
- Writer: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:write_swf` serialises the header and then each tag from `payload` verbatim, so `children` and every decoded field are derived views that a write ignores. A byte-exact round trip needs four things the reader therefore preserves: the tag header form (`long_header` is kept even for a short payload), the RECT field width and padding bits, the bytes after the declared length (`SwfFile::trailing_bytes`, which `SwfFile::source_body` also holds so an unchanged body is detected), and, for a compressed source, the original compressed bytes in `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfFile::source_compressed_body`, which are emitted again when the rebuilt body still equals `source_body`; otherwise the body is recompressed with `compress2` at `Z_BEST_COMPRESSION`. The declared file length is preserved when the body is unchanged and recomputed from the serialised size otherwise.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:replace_tag_payload` replaces one tag payload by index, refreshes `length`, clears the decoded fields and re-decodes them, so a caller that swaps a `DoABC` payload gets fresh `abc` offsets. An out-of-range index and a payload above the 32-bit tag length field return false.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:apply_tag_plan` replaces payloads and inserts whole tags in one all-or-nothing pass, which is the shape a batch edit needs: `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:replace_tag_payload` handles one tag at a time and has no insert, so an editor that both rewrites and adds a tag had to write the movie, read it back and lose the tag indices it started with. Every index in `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTagReplacement` and `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTagInsertion` is an index into `SwfFile::tags` as the file was read, not into the partially edited stream, because the plan is validated completely before any tag moves. The plan is rejected, with the file untouched, on an out-of-range replacement index, a replacement of the terminal `End`, a duplicate replacement index, an insertion position past the `End` (so `End` stays last), a duplicate insertion position (two insertions at one index would have no defined order), an insertion of an `End` tag, a replacement or insertion payload above the 32-bit tag length field, a movie that would exceed `Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:kMaxTags`, and an inserted tag code above 0x3FF, which the short header cannot carry and whose long form the writer would only produce by accident. A plan whose replacements all match the current bytes does nothing at all, so an untouched movie still writes back byte for byte, and `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTagPlanResult::inserted_tag_indices` is empty then; otherwise it lists the final positions of the inserted tags in ascending order. Each replacement refreshes `length` and re-decodes its payload head exactly as `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:replace_tag_payload` does, and each insertion drops whatever the caller's `SwfTag` carried in `offset`, `long_header`, `children` and the decoded views before re-decoding the payload it is given, so a caller cannot smuggle a stale header form or child list into the stream. Insertions are applied from the highest position down, which is what keeps the original indices valid without an offset map, and the function does not renumber depths, splice frame boundaries or scan a display list: those are the caller's semantics, and the whole point of keeping the engine this small is that the depth, keyframe and transform edits can share it without the engine guessing at their invariants.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_plan.cpp` is a new suite file rather than an addition to `Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp`, which is already at the suite size the repository keeps to.
