It builds a synthetic four-tag movie from `Radicle/tests/swf_movie_builder.hpp` and pins the plan engine on its own, with no shipped or third-party movie read. `SwfTagPlan.InsertsAndReplacesAtOriginalIndices` pins the mixed case — replace index 0 and insert before index 2 in one call — and checks the decoded views of the inserted tag, the returned index, and that a reparse of `write_swf` sees the same stream, which catches a plan applied to a shifting index or an insertion whose payload is not decoded. `SwfTagPlan.KeepsInsertionOrderAcrossOriginalPositions` inserts at two original positions and pins that the second lands after the first tag's new slot, which catches applying insertions in ascending order. `SwfTagPlan.RejectsAPlanThatBreaksTheTerminalEnd` covers replacing the `End`, inserting after it and inserting a second `End`, each refused with the movie byte-identical, and `SwfTagPlan.RejectsDuplicateTargetsAndWideCodesWithoutChangingBytes` covers two replacements of one index, two insertions at one position, a tag code of 0x400 and an out-of-range replacement index. `SwfTagPlan.AcceptsANoOpReplacementByteExactly` pins that a replacement equal to the current payload leaves `write_swf` output identical to the source bytes, which is the no-op save the editor depends on; the three rejection tests read the payload bytes and the tag count after every refusal rather than only the return value, so a plan that mutated before rejecting is caught.
- Known cost, not changed: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_stream` copies each nested payload into its own `SwfTag::payload`, so a `DefineSprite` nested N levels deep stores its bytes N+1 times, up to `Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:kMaxTagDepth`. Sharing one buffer would change the public `SwfTag::payload` contract, so it is left as is.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf.cpp` builds synthetic movies in the test (no shipped or third-party movie is read, stored or derived from) and covers the uncompressed read with every decoded tag, the nested sprite stream, the long tag header, the Scaleform tags, the zlib and GFX/CFX round trips, the byte-exact cases (bytes after the declared length, a zero-width RECT, non-zero RECT padding), the FileAttributes bit layout, the payload replacement, and the negative cases: `truncated_tag` for a body cut inside a tag, `malformed_tag` for a `DoABC2` without a name terminator and a `SymbolClass` count that overruns, `decompress_failed` for garbage after a `CWS` header, `bad_signature`, `truncated_header` for a four-byte input and for a three-byte body, `unsupported_compression` for `ZWS`, and `declared_length_matches` false for both a too-large and a too-small declared length. `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp` parses every `Data/Interface/*.swf` and `*.gfx` (or, when that folder holds no movie, every movie entry of `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2`) and asserts a byte-exact round trip for each; it is gated on `FO4_DATA_DIR` the way the other real-data tests are, records the version and compression histogram plus the symbol class and ABC counts, and counts an LZMA movie instead of failing on it.
- Not covered by this lane: the ABC (AVM2) bytecode itself, which the separate ABC lane decodes from `abc_payload`; LZMA; the AVM1 opcode stream; the semantics of the sprite control tags. The shape, font, sound and text payload layouts, the fourth (alpha) byte of `SetBackgroundColor` and the Scaleform tags 1000 and up were left raw here and are decoded in `## Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_stream and Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTag (#602 SWF tag payloads)`.
## Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/cfg.hpp:build_cfg

The Papyrus code analysis layer (`Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/`, `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/`) is C++ only: it reads a `fo4::pex::PexFile` that `Radicle/src/pex/pex.cpp:PexFile::fromBytes` already parsed, adds no C ABI export and does not touch `Radicle/src/papyrus`. `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/opcodes.hpp:pex_jump_offset` fixes the one fact the whole layer rests on: a jump operand is the offset **from the jump instruction itself** (`target = index + offset`), read as a signed 32-bit integer, and the instruction count itself is a legal target meaning "past the last instruction". This was verified against real compiled scripts rather than recalled: over the 24 jumps in `COCharacterSetupQuestScript.pex` (Commonwealth Online worktree, project-authored), `index + offset` lands on a statement start or the end of the function 20 times, is mid-statement 4 times and is never out of range, while `index + 1 + offset` is out of range 3 times, mid-statement 8 times and on a statement start only 13 times. The 4 mid-statement hits are the `||` short-circuit shape, where the compiler jumps to the next condition test (`jmpt ::temp1 +4` landing on `jmpf ::temp1 +4`); the debug line numbers in `PexDebugFunction` show both on the same source line, and reading the sequence as `index + offset` reproduces the source semantics exactly (trace and return when either operand is set), which `index + 1 + offset` does not.

`Radicle/src/pex_analysis/cfg.cpp:build_cfg` partitions a function into leaders (entry, every jump target, every instruction after a jump or a `return`), then adds a synthetic exit block whose `first` equals the instruction count so that `return` and "fell off the end" are ordinary successors. `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/cfg.hpp:PexFunctionCfg` carries a typed `PexAnalysisStatus`: a jump whose operand is missing or not an integer is `MalformedInstruction`, and a target outside `[0, instructionCount]` is `JumpTargetOutOfRange` with `errorInstruction` and `errorTarget` set. Loops come from a DFS over the block graph: an edge to a grey block is a back edge, recorded as `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/cfg.hpp:PexLoop` with header block, latch block, the `jmp` instruction that closes the loop and the header's first instruction. Unreachable blocks are the blocks a BFS from the entry never visits, excluding the synthetic exit. The synthetic exit's `reachable` flag is set only when a block falls through into it, so a function whose every path ends in `return` leaves it unreached; `Radicle/tests/test_pex_analysis.cpp:CfgSplitsStraightLineAndIfDiamond` therefore checks reachability for the real blocks, then pins the synthetic block itself (`first` equals the instruction count, `count` is zero, and it stays unreached). No file may exceed 750 lines, so the layer is split into `opcodes`, `cfg`, `disasm`, `callgraph`, `summary` and `fragments`.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:disassemble_function

`Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/disasm.hpp:PexDisasmResult` returns a listing plus the CFG status, so a caller never gets a half-parsed listing: a bad jump produces `status != Ok`, `structured == false` and a one-line `error: <status> at instruction N (target T)` text instead of instructions. In the plain listing every jump target gets an `L<index>:` label, values render through `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/opcodes.cpp:pex_value_text` (identifier as written, string in quotes, decimal integer, `%g` float, `true`/`false`), and the first instruction of an unreachable block is preceded by `; unreachable`. Operands are shown exactly as the file stores them - a call's fixed operands first, then its variable arguments - because `Radicle/src/pex/pex.cpp:readFunction` already removed the variable-argument count.

`Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer` reconstructs `if`/`while` only for shapes it can prove, and `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:disassemble_function` falls back to the labelled listing for anything else. What still falls back: unreachable blocks, a `jmpt` terminator, a loop whose header block does not end in a `jmpf` or whose latch is not the block right before the exit, a conditional whose two regions do not leave to one join, a region whose blocks do not form one structured sequence, and nesting deeper than `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::kMaxNestingDepth`. The rules are: only a `jmpf` terminator structures, because that is what the compiler emits for `if` and `while` (`jmpt` appears in the `||`/`&&` chain and is not a simple branch, so `Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:DisassemblyKeepsLabelledListingForShortCircuitJmpt` pins the labelled listing for it); `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::loop_exit` holds a loop header to that same rule, because `jmpt` leaves the loop when its condition is *true* (`Radicle/src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute`) and printing `while (<cond>)` for it would invert the loop, so a `jmpt` header falls back (`Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:DisassemblyKeepsLabelledListingForJmptLoopHeader`); the fallthrough block is the `then` region and the jump target is the `else` region. `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::region_exit` walks the blocks of a region `[start, limit)` and returns the block control reaches on leaving it, or `kNoIndex` when the region ends in `return`; a region may end in `return`, in `jmp`, in a fallthrough into `limit`, or by running a nested conditional or loop whose exit is `limit`, and the walk fails when a block leaves the region early or when it overshoots `limit`; a jump that goes backwards is not rejected inside the walk itself, it is returned as the exit and the callers reject it (`Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::emit_range` requires `next > cur`, `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::conditional_join` needs a join past `elseStart`). `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::conditional_join` walks twice with it: the `then` region `[block + 1, elseStart)` must leave to `elseStart` (an `if` without `else`) or to a join `J > elseStart`, or end in `return`, which makes `elseStart` the join without checking an `else` region; otherwise the `else` region `[elseStart, J)` must leave to that same `J`. Both regions are emitted through `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::emit_range` rather than a straight-chain scan, so a conditional nests inside a conditional, a loop inside a branch and a branch inside a loop (`Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:DisassemblesNestedIfElse`, `Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:DisassemblesBranchInsideLoopAndLoopInsideBranch`). `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::loop_exit` accepts a loop whose header block ends in its `jmpf`, with any instructions before it (only an empty header is refused), whose body starts at the next block, and whose latch is the block right before the exit with the back `jmp` as its only successor; `render` no longer refuses a function with more than one loop, so loops that follow one another each structure in turn (`Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:DisassemblesSequentialLoops`). A header that computes the condition (a `cmp_*` before the `jmpf`) is re-executed every iteration, because the back edge targets the header's first instruction, so it renders as `while (true) {`, then those prefix instructions, then `if (!(cond)) break;`; the exit is the `jmpf` target, which is the block right after the latch (`Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::emit_loop`, pinned by `Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:DisassemblesWhileLoopWithComputedCondition`). The last block of every emitted region may end in an unconditional `jmp`; it is dropped, because the surrounding structure already carries the control flow. At top level (depth 0) the jump must target the function end (`Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::emit_range`), or the render falls back, because nothing else carries that jump's control flow; `Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:DisassemblyBailsOnTailJumpThatDoesNotReachTheEnd` pins both shapes. Every conditional that becomes an `if` line drops the conditional instruction itself but keeps the instructions before it in the same block, so the condition's operands stay visible; a `while` header keeps its prefix instructions for the same reason, inside the loop rather than before it. Nothing but a structural jump is ever dropped or reordered, which `Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:StructuredListingKeepsEveryInstructionOnce` checks by counting each instruction line in the structured and the plain listing of the same function, and `Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:StructuredListingSurvivesPexEncoding` checks that the structure is the same after the fixture goes through `Radicle/src/pex/pex.cpp:PexFile::toBytes` and `Radicle/src/pex/pex.cpp:PexFile::fromBytes`, and that a fixture whose stored `jmp` offset is shifted to a shape the renderer cannot prove still falls back after the same round trip, so the structure follows the offsets the file stores rather than the offsets it was built with. `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::emit_range` caps nesting at `kMaxNestingDepth` (64) and falls back past it, and before this change `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::conditional_join` and `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer::region_exit` recursed with no depth argument, so the walk followed the function's nesting with no bound and a hostile `.pex` could overflow the stack before `emit_range` capped it. Now `conditional_join` takes the depth, `region_exit` passes `depth + 1` into each nested `conditional_join`, and `conditional_join` refuses above `kMaxNestingDepth` (64), so the walk is bounded on its own, and `emit_range` applies the same constant to the emitted nesting. `Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp:DisassemblyFallsBackPastTheNestingCapWithoutRecursing` checks the boundary first (64 nested `if`s structure, 65 fall back) and then generates 50000 nested `if`s and pins the labelled fallback.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:build_call_graph

`Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/callgraph.hpp:PexFunctionRef` identifies a function across a set of files: file, object, state, function index, plus a `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/callgraph.hpp:PexFunctionSlot` because a property handler is not in `PexObject::states` (its `functionIndex` is the property index, and `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:pex_function_at` resolves either slot back to a `PexFunction`). `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:build_call_graph` resolves each call operand by the shape the compiler emits: `callmethod` carries the function name in operand 0 and the object expression in operand 1 (`self` becomes the caller's object, a variable becomes its declared type from the function's parameters and locals, then from the object's variables and properties (`declared_type_of`), anything else stays as written), `callparent` uses the caller's `parentClassName`, and `callstatic` carries the script name in operand 0 and the function name in operand 1. Resolution is a case-insensitive name match over every supplied file, first file first match, so a call that resolves records the target file, object, state and function plus the target's `isNative` flag; a call that does not resolve is counted in `unresolvedCalls` and left with `resolved == false`, which is the honest answer for the engine's own scripts (`game`, `utility`, `debug`) that are not in the file set. Native targets are counted separately in `nativeCalls`. Property handler bodies are scanned for call sites as well as for variable accesses, because GardenEngine's `NativeCallSiteCensus` walks every `PapyrusScript.Functions` entry and labels a handler caller `<property>`; a call inside a getter or setter is therefore reported with `caller_slot` `PropertyRead` or `PropertyWrite` instead of being dropped.

Event identification is derived, not read: the container has no event flag, so `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/callgraph.hpp:PexCallGraph::roots` is every function that no resolved call site targets. That makes `OnInit` a root in a script nothing calls and hides one that another script calls back, which is why it is recorded here as a call-graph property and not as a declaration.

Variable and property accesses come from `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:operand_accesses`, a per-opcode table of which operand is written and which are read, applied only to operands that are identifiers naming a declared `PexObject::variables` or `PexObject::properties` entry, so temporaries (`::temp1`), parameters and locals never appear. Call operands are handled separately because a call's first operands are names, not values: the result operand of each call opcode is a write and the variable arguments are reads, with `callmethod`'s object expression an extra read. The non-call table follows the operand order the in-repo interpreter executes (`Radicle/src/papyrus/execute.cpp:Interpreter::execute`, exercised by `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_vm.cpp`): `propget` writes operand 2 and reads the receiver in operand 1; `array_length`, `array_getelement` and `array_create` write operand 0 and read the array or index or size operand; `array_findelement` and `array_rfindelement` write operand 1 and read the array, the wanted value and the start index; `array_setelement`, `array_add`, `array_insert` and `array_remove` write the array and read the index and value or count. The `struct_*`, `array_findstruct` and `array_rfindstruct` entries are not run by that interpreter, so they rest on the compiler oracle instead: `PluginEditTool/native/src/papyrus/Decompiler.cpp` and `PluginEditTool/FO4RecordEditor.Core/Services/Papyrus/PapyrusDecompiler.cs` (validated against `PapyrusCompiler.exe`) render `struct_get <dest> <struct> <member>` as `Dest(0) = A(1).member` and `array_findstruct`/`array_rfindstruct` as `Dest(1) = A(0).FindStruct("member", A(3), A(4))`, so `struct_get` writes operand 0 and reads operand 1, and `array_findstruct`/`array_rfindstruct` write operand 1 and read operands 0, 3 and 4 - operand 2 is the member name string, which the walker skips because it is not an identifier. The earlier `struct_get` entry marked the destination as a read and the `array_findstruct` entries did the same for operand 1, which reported the written variable as read-only and hid the write. Property handler bodies are walked with the same table, so `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/callgraph.hpp:PexVariableAccess` covers `propget`/`propset` and the handlers behind them.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/summary.cpp:summarize_script

`Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/summary.hpp:PexScriptSummary` answers "what does this script do" per object: the events (call-graph roots), the function names each event calls in order without repeats, the `GoToState` transitions, the properties the object touches and the variables it writes. `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/summary.cpp:collect_transitions` accepts a transition only for the compiled shape `callmethod GoToState self ::nonevar <state>`: the target state is a literal when operand 3 is a string, and `knownState` says whether the object declares a state of that name. A `GoToState` whose argument is a variable is recorded with `literal == false`, because the state it selects is only known at run time.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/fragments.cpp:resolve_fragments

`Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/fragments.hpp:resolve_fragments` maps a VMAD fragment to the function it runs: it takes the `fo4::QuestVmadFragment` records that `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras` already produces (`stage`, `stage_index`, `script`, `function`) and returns, per fragment, whether the script object is in this `.pex`, whether the function is in it, and the `PexFunctionRef` to run (that ref carries file index 0, the index `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:build_call_graph` gives a one-file vector). The mapping is therefore stage-fragment only: terminal and scene fragments are not covered, because the exposed VMAD model (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/vmad.hpp:QuestVmadExtras`, `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/vmad.hpp:QuestVmadAliasScripts`) carries their scripts but not the per-fragment function names, and `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_vmad.h` exposes setters only, with no reader for a terminal or scene fragment list. Closing that gap needs a reader for the terminal and scene fragment blocks, not more work in this layer.

- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_pex_analysis.cpp` covers the CFG (`CfgSplitsStraightLineAndIfDiamond`, `CfgFindsWhileLoopBackEdge`, `CfgReportsUnreachableBlockAfterReturn`), the negative statuses (`CfgRejectsJumpTargetOutOfRange` for a forward `jmp +5` and a backward `jmp -3`, `CfgRejectsJumpWithoutIntegerOperand`), the listings (`DisassemblesIfElseDiamondWithoutLabels`, `DisassemblesWhileLoopWithVariableCondition`, `DisassemblesComputedWhileConditionWithoutGotoFallback`, `DisassemblyFallsBackToLabelsAndGotoStyle`, `DisassemblyResolvesStringTableNames`, `DisassemblyReportsOutOfRangeJumpAsStatus`), the call graph (`CallGraphResolvesSelfStaticAndRecursiveCalls`, `CallGraphKeepsUnresolvedAndParentCalls`, `CallGraphReportsPropertyAndVariableAccesses`, `CallGraphMarksArrayAndPropertyResultOperandsAsWrites`), the summary (`SummaryReportsEventsTransitionsAndProperties`), the fragment mapping (`FragmentResolutionMapsStageToPexFunction`) and `PexFunctionRef` resolution for both slots (`FunctionRefPointsAtHandlerAndStateFunctions`). Every fixture is built in memory; no shipped or third-party compiled script is read by a test. `Radicle/tests/test_pex_disasm.cpp` covers the shapes `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/disasm.cpp:StructuredRenderer` proves (`DisassemblesWhileLoopWithComputedCondition`, `DisassemblesNestedIfElse`, `DisassemblesSequentialLoops`, `DisassemblesBranchInsideLoopAndLoopInsideBranch`), the shapes it still refuses (`DisassemblyKeepsLabelledListingForShortCircuitJmpt`, `DisassemblyKeepsLabelledListingForJmptLoopHeader`, `DisassemblyFallsBackPastTheNestingCapWithoutRecursing`), the instruction-preservation invariant (`StructuredListingKeepsEveryInstructionOnce`) and the round trip through `Radicle/src/pex/pex.cpp:PexFile::toBytes` (`StructuredListingSurvivesPexEncoding`).

Open item: `MODT` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8918`). FO4 `MODT` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:1037`) is not a flat array: `wbModelInfo` takes the `else` branch at `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8938`, a `wbUnion` on `wbModelInfoDecider` whose main arm is a struct of four counted arrays — a `Counters` header of `itU32` words, then `Textures`, `Addon Nodes` and `Materials` arrays whose lengths are read out of that header (`SetCountPath('Counters[0]', True)`, `[1]` and `[3]`), each texture or material entry being a 12-byte `{u32 file hash; 4-char extension; u32 folder hash}` struct, and the arm chosen also depends on the record's form version. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:CountedArrayDescriptor` divides one payload by one stride and expresses none of that, and no record in the tree rows `MODT`, so it stays unrowed rather than being hand-rolled; the authoring constraint lists still allow the subrecord, so a `MODT` written by another tool round-trips untouched. Correction (this lane): that gap is now closed by `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:header_segment` and the rows recorded at `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:DOOR\ModelInfoTextures`; the pin `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:1037` above is `wbMODS`, the MODT member of `wbGenericModel` is at `:1035`.
