The vendor chest and the static it stands on carry the same `wbGenericModel` block as `DOOR`, so the second pass added `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:CONT\ColorRemapping`/`CONT\ModelFlags` (`MODC`/`MODF`) and `STAT\ColorRemapping`/`STAT\ModelFlags`; `CONT` and `STAT` carry the same `MODT` block and were rowed with it by the `MODT` pass (`Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:header_segment`, `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:CONT\ModelInfoTextures`, `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:STAT\ModelInfoTextures`). `STAT` has no keyword list in xEdit at the pinned commit, so there is nothing to row there. `STAT`'s remaining unrowed subrecord is `NVNM` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4360`), the navmesh geometry: a nested `Version`/`Pathing Cell`/grid struct whose shape depends on the form version, so it stays unrowed and is left alone; a vendor chest's static is a floor piece and carries none. The vendor script properties live in `VMAD` and are out of scope for this audit.

Not changed by this audit, and deliberately so: no new mechanism was hand-rolled. The eight new rows use the existing `formlink_fields` and string-row kinds, so `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py` and `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py` regenerate every descriptor unchanged in shape. The six model-struct rows of the second pass are whole-payload scalar rows, the shape `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ALCH\ColorRemapping` (`MODC`) and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:WEAP\ModelFlags` (`MODF`) already use: `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` throws `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` for a whole-payload field whose subrecord is not exactly four (f32) or one (u8) byte wide, and xEdit declares both subrecords at that width for every record (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4260` and `:4266`, `wbFloat` being `fkSingle` at `Core/wbInterface.pas:8142`). The tolerance question is the same one `Radicle/docs/code-notes/radicle-vegetation-writer.md` records for `TREE\CNAM`: an embedded row with `payload_size` would report a mismatched `MODC` as absent instead of refusing it, at the cost of the whole-record read that `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginReadApi.cpp` performs; the whole-payload shape was kept because it matches the nine existing `MODC` rows. `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:ObjectBaseRecordsSynthetic.ModelRowsDecodeTheirValueAndFlags` reads `DOOR\ColorRemapping` (2.5), `DOOR\ModelFlags` (bit 0 named `Has FaceBones Model`, bit 2 unnamed), `CONT\ModelFlags` (bit 1 named `Has 1stPerson Model`) and a `STAT` `MODC` (1.5) from the fixtures, and `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:ObjectBaseRecordsSynthetic.WrongSizedModelPayloadsAreRefused` is the negative case, a one-byte `MODC` and a two-byte `MODF` that `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` refuses. The fixtures in `Radicle/tests/object_base_fixture.hpp:make_plugin` gained the same two subrecords for `CONT` and `DOOR`, so `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:ObjectBaseRecordsSynthetic.EveryScalarRowDecodesOnTheFixture` decodes them on every run. `Radicle/tests/object_base_fixture.hpp:template_record_plugin` and `Radicle/tests/object_base_fixture.hpp:only_record` are the FURN fixture and lookup generalized to any signature, because a fixture whose `TES4` carries no `MAST` cannot resolve a form key (`Radicle/src/plugin/reader.cpp:assign_record_form_keys` swallows the `Radicle/src/formid.cpp:FormIdError`). `Radicle/tests/test_npc_link_rows.cpp:NpcLinkRows.SingleLinkRowsCarryTheirOwnTargetType` pins the four single-link descriptors and their target types, `Radicle/tests/test_npc_link_rows.cpp:NpcLinkRows.SingleLinkRowsReadRetargetAndRefuseForeignTargets` reads, retargets and rereads them through `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field` and refuses a foreign target type for each of the four, and `Radicle/tests/test_npc_link_rows.cpp:NpcLinkRows.ShortSingleLinkPayloadIsRefused` is the negative case, a 2-byte `PTRN` that `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots` rejects as an unexpected payload size without touching the record. The attack rows get the same treatment in `Radicle/tests/test_npc_attack_data_rows.cpp:NpcAttackDataRows.SlotAndTextRowsSitBesideTheAttackStruct`, `NpcAttackDataRows.SlotAndTextRowsReadWriteAndRefuseForeignTargets` and `NpcAttackDataRows.ShortSlotPayloadIsRefused`.

Not verified without a compiler: whether any official master carries an `NPC_` `PTRN`, `STCP`, `NTRM`, `FTYP`, `ATKW` or `ATKS` whose payload is not four bytes. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots` throws `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:FormLinkFieldError` for such a payload, the way `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:DOOR\PreviewTransform` already behaves, so a measurement on the data runner is the only remaining check. No corpus scan was run for this change.
## Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/lexer.hpp:lex and Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp:Lexer::next (#602)

- New module: Radicle could read compiled Papyrus (`.pex`) but not Papyrus source (`.psc`). `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp` turns source text into tokens, `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser.cpp` builds the `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/ast.hpp:Script` tree, and `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/summary.cpp` derives the logic. C++ only, no C ABI, no generated file: the three source groups are registered in `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt` with one `target_sources` line and the two test files with one line each in the `fo4_tests` list. `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/lexer.hpp:lex` and `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/parser.hpp:parse` are the two entry points; both return a result struct that carries the error instead of throwing, so no exception escapes `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser.cpp:parse`.
- `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp:Lexer::next` is the only place that reads characters. It calls `Lexer::skip_trivia` first, then emits one `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/token.hpp:TokenKind` token with its `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/token.hpp:SourcePosition` (line, column, byte offset) attached by `Lexer::make`. Keywords are matched case-insensitively through `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp:keyword_kind` against the sorted `kKeywords` table, so `function`/`Function`/`FUNCTION` are one token kind; identifiers keep their original spelling in `Token::text`.
- `Lexer::skip_trivia` covers all three comment forms and line continuation. `;` to end of line is `Lexer::skip_line_comment`; `;/` opens a block comment that `Lexer::skip_block_comment` closes at `/;` and reports as `LexErrorKind::UnterminatedBlockComment` at the opening position if the file ends first; `{` opens a doc comment that `Lexer::skip_doc_comment` closes at `}` and surfaces as `TokenKind::DocComment` with the inner text. A backslash followed only by horizontal space and then a line break is a continuation and produces no token, so a statement may be split across lines. Deviation from the token list in the issue: `/;` outside a block comment is `LexErrorKind::InvalidCharacter` rather than a token, because no Papyrus construct uses it as an operator.
- `Lexer::advance` treats CRLF as one line break, so a Windows-authored `.psc` and its LF copy produce identical line and column numbers. A UTF-8 BOM is skipped by the `Lexer::Lexer` constructor before the first token, because the CK and the Creation Kit export both write one.
- `Lexer::next` keeps a `parenDepth_` counter that `Lexer::lex_punctuation` increments on `(` and `[` and decrements on `)` and `]`. A line break inside parentheses or brackets emits no `TokenKind::NewLine`, so a call or a `New T[...]` may be wrapped over several lines; outside them the break is a statement separator. This is the reason `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser_stmt.cpp:Parser::end_statement` can treat a newline as the end of a statement.
- `Lexer::lex_number` produces `TokenKind::Integer` for decimal and `0x` hexadecimal and `TokenKind::Float` for a form with a fractional part or an exponent (`1.5`, `.5`, `1e10`, `2.5E-3`). `Lexer::wrap_integer` folds the decimal digits into 32 bits the way the game stores an int, and `Lexer::parse_double` is a hand-rolled reader rather than `strtod` on purpose: `strtod` is locale-dependent and would mis-parse `1.5` under a comma-decimal locale. A bare `0x` with no digits is `LexErrorKind::InvalidNumber`.
- `Lexer::lex_string` reads a double-quoted literal and decodes `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\\`, `\"` and `\'` into `Token::stringValue`, keeping the raw text in `Token::text`. A backslash immediately before a line break is a continuation inside the string and contributes no character, which is how long Papyrus message strings are written in the wild. A line break that is not preceded by a backslash, or end of file, is `LexErrorKind::UnterminatedString` reported at the opening quote.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/token.hpp:LexError` carries the kind, a human-readable message and the position, and `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/token.hpp:LexResult` returns the tokens lexed so far alongside it; `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp:token_kind_name` gives every token kind the wording used in parser messages, so an error reads `expected '=' but found 'EndIf'`.
- Parser shape: `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser.cpp:Parser::parse_script` reads the header through `Parser::parse_script_header` (`ScriptName`, `Extends`, and the `Native`/`Hidden`/`Conditional`/`BetaOnly`/`DebugOnly` flags) and then loops `Parser::parse_declaration`, which dispatches on the keyword and hands the destination vectors over through `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/parser_internal.hpp:DeclarationTarget`. `Parser::take_doc` attaches a pending `TokenKind::DocComment` to the declaration that follows it. A keyword that cannot open a declaration is `ParseErrorKind::UnknownDeclaration`, and a missing `EndIf`, `EndWhile`, `EndState`, `EndFunction`, `EndProperty`, `EndStruct` or `EndGroup` fails with the matching `ParseErrorKind::Unbalanced*` kind instead of running to the end of file silently.
- `Parser::expect_name`, `Parser::expect_qualified_name`, `Parser::expect_member_name` and `Parser::expect_type` are the name readers: a plain identifier, a `Struct:Member` qualified name built by `Parser::expect_qualified_name`, a possibly dotted name read by `Parser::expect_member_name` for function, event and custom event names, and a type optionally followed by `[]` which sets `isArray`. Every one of them requires a `TokenKind::Identifier`, so a name that collides with a Papyrus keyword is rejected here, which matches the compiler: `Hidden`, `Native` and `Const` are reserved and cannot name a member.
- `Parser::parse_property_rest` handles all three property forms in one place: `Auto`, `AutoReadOnly`, `Const`, and a full property with `Get`/`Set` accessor bodies, each accessor parsed as a `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/ast.hpp:FunctionDeclaration` with `FunctionKind::Function` in `PropertyDeclaration::accessors`. `Parser::parse_function_rest` covers `Function` and `Event` with parameters and defaults, `Native`, `Global`, `DebugOnly`, `BetaOnly` and a return type that defaults to `None`. `Parser::parse_state` covers `Auto State`, nested states, and the variables, functions, custom events and structs a state may declare. `Parser::parse_group` records the group name and its trailing identifier flags and then collects the names of the properties and variables declared before `EndGroup` into `GroupDeclaration::propertyNames`, so a group reports what it contains without duplicating the declarations; `Parser::parse_struct` and `Parser::parse_custom_event` cover the remaining two declarations. `Parser::parse_script_header` also consumes a stray `Const` after the script flags, because the compiler accepts it there, and takes the doc comment that follows the header as `Script::doc`.
- Expression precedence is one function per level, in `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser_expr.cpp`: `Parser::parse_or` (`||`) calls `Parser::parse_and` (`&&`) calls `Parser::parse_comparison` (`==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) calls `Parser::parse_additive` (`+`, `-`) calls `Parser::parse_multiplicative` (`*`, `/`, `%`) calls `Parser::parse_unary` (`-`, `+`, `!`) calls `Parser::parse_cast` (`As`, `Is`) calls `Parser::parse_postfix` calls `Parser::parse_primary`. `Parser::parse_postfix` loops over array indexing, member access and calls, and `Parser::parse_arguments` records a named argument (`Name = value`) in `Expression::argumentNames` so a call site keeps both the name and the position. `Parser::parse_new` reads `New T` and `New T[size]` and marks the array form in `Expression::arrayNew`. `Parser::parse_unary` holds the recursion guard, `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/parser_internal.hpp:DepthGuard` against `kMaxNestingDepth` (96), so a pathological file fails with `ParseErrorKind::DepthLimit` rather than overflowing the stack. Deviation: `As` and `Is` bind tighter than unary minus here, so `-a As T` parses as `-(a As T)`; no vanilla script depends on the other reading.
- Statements, in `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser_stmt.cpp`: `Parser::parse_block` stops at the block-ending keyword, `Parser::parse_if` builds an `ElseIf`/`Else` chain into `Statement::branches`, `Parser::parse_while` and `Parser::parse_return` cover the loop and the return, and `Parser::parse_assignment_or_declaration` covers a variable declaration, a plain assignment and the compound forms through `Parser::take_assignment_operator` (`+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`). `Parser::looks_like_declaration` decides between a declaration and an expression statement by scanning for `name`, an optional `Struct:Member` qualification, an optional `[]` and then a second name, so `Health = 5` stays an assignment while `int Health = 5` is a declaration. An assignment whose target is not assignable (a literal, a call result) is `ParseErrorKind::InvalidAssignmentTarget` through `is_assignable`.
- `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/summary.cpp:summarize` walks the AST and fills `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/summary.hpp:ScriptSummary`: the script name, base script, auto state, imports, declared and auto properties, states, and one `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/summary.hpp:FunctionSummary` per function, event and custom event, each carrying the state it belongs to. `summarize` then folds every function's lists into the script-level lists with `append_unique`, so a caller gets both the per-function detail and the whole-script roll-up.
- `walk_expression` takes a `written` flag: a property on the left of an assignment goes to `propertiesWritten`, anywhere else to `propertiesRead`, and `build_path` rebuilds a member chain into one string so a read and a write of the same member compare equal. `build_path` joins member access with a dot, writes an index as `[]` and a call as `()`, so `Self.Container.Items[0].Count` becomes `Self.Container.Items[].Count` and the index expression itself is never part of the key. `walk_call` records a called function by its full path and treats `GoToState` specially: `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/summary.cpp:is_goto_state` matches the last dotted segment case-insensitively, so `GoToState("Busy")` and `Self.GoToState("Busy")` are both a transition and neither is a called function. `record_transition` takes the state from the first argument, which may be a string literal or a constant identifier, and appends it to `stateTransitions`. `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/summary.cpp:find_function` looks a function up by name.
- State membership is a dotted path, not a name prefix: `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/summary.cpp:join_state` builds it, `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/summary.cpp:collect_state` puts it in `FunctionSummary::state` for every function and custom event of the state and recurses into nested states, and the same path goes into `ScriptSummary::states`. A function declared at script level carries an empty `state`, and `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/summary.cpp:summarize_function` and `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/summary.cpp:summarize_custom_event` are the two builders. A custom event is summarized as an event with an empty body, because its declaration has no body.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_source.cpp` holds nineteen cases over inline `.psc` strings, each naming the regression it detects: `LexesCommentsContinuationsAndDocComments`, `ParsesLiteralsOfEveryKind`, `ParsesScriptHeaderImportsAndFlags`, `ParsesAutoAndFullPropertiesWithDefaults`, `ParsesGroupsStructsAndCustomEvents`, `ParsesStatesWithFunctionsAndNestedStates`, `ParsesFunctionSignaturesWithDefaultsAndModifiers`, `ParsesIfChainsLoopsAndCompoundAssignment`, `AppliesExpressionPrecedenceToCastsCallsAndArrays`, `SummarizesCallsPropertiesWritesAndStateTransitions`, plus the negative cases `RejectsUnterminatedStringAndBlockComment`, `RejectsUnknownTokenWithPosition`, `RejectsUnbalancedBlockKeywords`, `RejectsAssignmentToALiteral`, `RejectsNestingPastTheDepthLimit`, `LexesSameLengthIdentifiersAsIdentifiers`, `LexesHugeFloatExponentWithoutOverflow`, `SummarizesPropertyAccessorBodies` and `RejectsLongChainsPastTheDepthLimitWithoutRecursing`. `AppliesExpressionPrecedenceToCastsCallsAndArrays` pins the tree shape, not just the accepted text, so a precedence regression fails it.
- Real data: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_source_real.cpp:ParsesEveryCorpusScript` walks every `.psc` under the roots named by the `FO4_PSC_CORPUS` environment variable (`;`-separated), or under `FO4_TESTDATA_DIR/papyrus` when it is unset, parses each file and requires a non-empty script name and at least one function across the corpus. It calls `GTEST_SKIP` when no `.psc` file is found, the same gate the other `*_real.cpp` suites use, so CI without a script corpus stays green.
- Not covered: the parser does no symbol resolution, no type checking and no constant folding, so a call to an undefined function or a wrong argument count parses fine, and the summary cannot tell a local variable from a property: `propertiesRead` and `propertiesWritten` hold every name read or written, locals included, and a caller that wants only properties must intersect them with `declaredProperties`. There is no writer: this module reads `.psc` and never emits one. `Is` and `As` are recorded as an `ExpressionKind::Is` and an `ExpressionKind::Cast` with the target type in `Expression::text`, and nothing checks that the type exists. `Struct` is accepted inside a `State` because the AST has the slot and the grammar is ambiguous there; no vanilla script is known to do it. Binary literals (`0b`) and character literals are not lexed, and the summary records the callee path as written, so a call through a variable or a cast receiver is recorded under that path rather than resolved to a function.
## Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile and Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code (ABC lane)

Fallout 4 UI scripting is ActionScript 3 compiled to ABC inside SWF `DoABC` (tag 72, the ABC bytes are the whole payload) and `DoABC2` (tag 82, a u32 flags word and a NUL-terminated name precede the ABC bytes) tags. This lane adds a read-only decoder over a raw ABC byte span (no SWF container; the SWF lane owns `Radicle/include/fo4/swf`). `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:AbcFile::parse` walks the file, `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:detail::parse_constant_pool` the seven constant pools, `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:opcode_info` and `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code` the instruction stream, `Radicle/src/abc/disassembly.cpp:disassemble` the listing and `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:summarize` the logic summary. Headers are `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp`, `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/opcodes.hpp` and `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/summary.hpp`; `Radicle/src/abc/abc_internal.hpp` holds the two functions shared between translation units, and the `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:ByteReader` definitions live in `Radicle/src/abc/byte_reader.cpp`, split out of `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp` so that file stays under the repository's 750-line ceiling. No C ABI export, no `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` change, no generator or binding touched.

- Errors are typed, not thrown: `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcStatus` has fourteen values (`Ok` plus thirteen failure codes) and every entry point returns one. `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:ByteReader` keeps a sticky status, so the first failure wins and every later read returns a zero value instead of reading out of range; `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:status_name` gives tools a printable phrase.

- Layout facts were checked against two independent implementations instead of recall: the AVM2 reference implementation (avmplus `core/AbcParser.cpp` `parseCpool`) and RABCDAsm `abcfile.d`. All seven pools — ints, uints, doubles, strings, namespaces, namespace sets, multinames — reserve index 0 and read `count - 1` entries. Namespace sets are the trap: `AbcParser.cpp` reads `for (i = 1; i < ns_set_count; ++i)`, so they have the reserved slot too, and reading `count` entries there would shift every later byte. Int and uint pool entries are full-width 32-bit varints: `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:parse_int_pool` reads them with `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:ByteReader::s32` and `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:parse_uint_pool` with `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:ByteReader::u32`, unmasked. Doubles are 8 raw little-endian bytes read by `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:ByteReader::d64`. The int and uint width is not re-checked against the two references in this note.

- Counts are bounded before allocation. `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:read_count` and `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:count_fits` reject a count the remaining bytes cannot hold at that structure's minimum encoded entry size (`AbcStatus::CountOutOfRange`), the guard avmplus applies to namespace sets. The bound is per entry, not per byte: a method needs 4 bytes (`param_count`, `return_type`, `name`, `flags`), an instance plus its class 6, a body 8, an exception 5, a trait 2, a metadata entry 2, a namespace 2 and a double 8, so a count can never exceed `remaining / entry_size + 1` (the `+ 1` is the reserved pool slot 0). That caps a crafted file at the element count its own size can encode. The residual amplification is the pools whose minimum entry is one byte while the in-memory element is far larger, `multinames` (about 56 B), `strings` (32 B) and `ns_sets` (24 B), so a 5 MB crafted ABC can still ask for a few hundred MB of vectors; every read is bounds-checked, so that is memory pressure and not a memory-safety hole.

- `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:ByteReader::u32` reads at most five bytes; a fifth byte that still carries the continuation bit is `AbcStatus::VarintTooLong` rather than a silent truncation. `Radicle/src/abc/byte_reader.cpp:ByteReader::u30` is the masked wrapper (`u32() & 0x3FFFFFFF`), the same 30-bit mask RABCDAsm's `readU30` applies, and it is what the count and index fields use. `AbcStatus::Truncated` covers every read past the end, including a null span.

- `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:parse_instances` reads each instance as name, super index and a flags byte. `protected_ns` (`Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcInstanceInfo::protected_ns`) is read only when `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcInstanceInfo::has_protected_ns` (flags & 0x08) is set, and stays 0 otherwise. The interface count is always read and checked against the bytes remaining (`AbcStatus::CountOutOfRange`), then the interfaces, then the instance initializer index.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcValueKind` has fifteen values, `Undefined` (0x00) included. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:is_value_kind` accepts exactly those fifteen codes and anything else is `AbcStatus::BadValueKind`. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:AbcFile::optional_value_at` renders each kind, `undefined` for 0x00. The check covers trait value kinds and method optional values.

- `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:parse_multiname_pool` case 0x1D (TypeName) requires the name and every parameter to be earlier pool entries, otherwise `AbcStatus::IndexOutOfRange`, and the parameter count is checked against the bytes remaining. The expanded node count (the name and parameters, recursively) is capped at `kMaxTypeNameExpansion` = 64, and going over it is `AbcStatus::TypeNameTooLarge`. The cap is a local choice, not from the spec. The earlier-entry rule is a local choice as well: RABCDAsm's `readMultiname` (case `ASType.TypeName`) reads `name` and `params` without validating them, and avmplus validates them by a different rule — `AbcParser::parseCpool` requires `0 < basetype < mn_count` and says in a comment that a forward reference there is legal, requires the parameter count to be exactly 1, requires the parameter index to be below `mn_count` with 0 legal for `Vector<*>`, and rejects cycles in a separate pass over `cpool_mn_offsets` — so a forward or self reference is a hard `AbcStatus::IndexOutOfRange` here where both references would keep parsing. It is kept because it is what makes the recursion in `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::multiname_at` terminate on a cyclic pool, and no compiler emits one. Both rules are now exercised against real bytecode: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:AbcCorpusReal` parses every shipped Interface `DoABC2` block, and neither the earlier-entry rule nor the 64-node cap fires on any of the 675 blocks, so a TypeName in the shipped UI bytecode always names an earlier entry and never expands past 64 nodes.

- `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::parse_traits` follows the per-kind layout of `trait_info`: Slot/Const carry slot id, type name, value index and an optional value kind; Class/Function carry slot id plus a class index; Method/Getter/Setter carry a dispatch id plus a method index. Slot id comes before type name, the order the AVM2 overview gives for `trait_info`. Traits are flat: a Class/Function trait names its class by index and does not nest, so the parser cannot recurse and the old `kMaxTraitDepth`/`AbcStatus::NestingTooDeep` guard is gone.

- Trait metadata is an index, not a copy. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::parse_metadata` reads the `metadata_info` pool once, between the methods and the classes; each entry is its name, its item count, all keys, then all values (the order RABCDAsm `abcfile.d:readMetadata` and JPEXS `ABC.java` read, not interleaved; avmplus `AbcParser.cpp:parseMetadataInfos` skips the items without telling the two apart), and `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcTrait::metadata` holds indices into `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::metadata`. The array is read for every trait kind whose metadata attribute bit is set, Slot and Const included. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::check_pool_indices` then re-checks every metadata index in instances, classes, scripts and bodies against the pool size, together with the other structural indices, and returns `AbcStatus::IndexOutOfRange`, so a bad index is a typed error instead of a lookup miss.

- `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:AbcFile::parse` consumes the span exactly and returns `AbcStatus::TrailingBytes` for anything left over. That is deliberate: a `DoABC` payload has no padding, so a leftover byte means the walk drifted. The unit tests use it as the end-to-end proof that the pool, class and body layouts are byte-exact.

- Opcode numbers and operand counts come from the reference implementation's generated table (`avmplus core/opcodes.tbl`, whose `ABC_OP(<operands>, ...)` field is the u30 operand count) and operand kinds from RABCDAsm `abcfile.d` `opcodeInfo` (multiname, string, namespace, class, method, u8, s8, s24, switch), which `disassembler.d` only imports. Cross-checking was worth it: 0x1B is `lookupswitch`, 0x1C/0x1D are `pushwith`/`popscope`, `callpropvoid` is 0x4F, `getslot` is 0x6C, `convert_s` is 0x70 and `deletepropertylate` is 0x6B — a from-memory table gets each of those wrong.

- `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:kMnemonics` is the 256-entry name table written four entries per line, one hex row per line (244 explicit names; the tail 0xF4-0xFF stays value-initialised), and `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:operand_specs` groups opcodes by operand signature. A `nullptr` entry means no file-facing AVM2 defines the opcode, and `decode_code` returns `AbcStatus::BadOpcode` for it rather than guessing an instruction length. The null set is 0x00, 0x0A-0x0B, 0x22, 0x33-0x34, 0x3F, 0x4B, 0x4D, 0x54, 0x5B-0x5C, 0x79-0x7F, 0x8A-0x8F, 0x98-0x9F, 0xB5-0xBF, 0xC8-0xCF, 0xD8-0xEE and 0xF4-0xFF, and every one of them is accounted for by a reference: avmplus's `ABC_UNUSED_OP` rows, the rows whose operand count is -1 because the opcode is VM-internal (0x33-0x34 lix8/lix16, 0x4B callsuperid, 0x4D callinterface, 0x5B-0x5C findpropglobalstrict/findpropglobal, 0xF4-0xF5 restargc/restarg, which the verifier only generates after analysis), the `VMCFG_FLOAT`-gated rows (0x0A lf32x4, 0x0B sf32x4, 0x22 pushfloat, 0x54 pushfloat4, 0x79 convert_f, 0x7A unplus, 0x7B convert_f4) and the Tamarin-only opcodes RABCDAsm names while avmplus leaves them unused (0x00 db, 0x22 pushuninitialized, 0x33 pushdecimal, 0x34 pushdnan, 0x5B deldescendants). RABCDAsm names all 256 opcodes, placeholders included, so its table is not a definition list on its own; 0x5B and 0x5C are the one place the two references disagree on a name, and no real file has been seen to use either. Two source disagreements are resolved toward the spec: `setpropertylate` (0x69) and `deletepropertylate` (0x6B) stay as no-operand opcodes (RABCDAsm round-trips them, avmplus dropped them), and `coerce_b/i/d/u/o`, `sxi1/8/16` and `li8`..`sf64` stay as no-operand because `opcodes.tbl` gives them operand count 0 even though RABCDAsm marks their kind unknown.

- Branch targets are resolved in a second pass, once every instruction length is known, and the two kinds of branch use different bases (`Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code`). An ordinary branch is relative to the byte after the instruction: `target = instruction.offset + instruction.length + s24`. A `lookupswitch` default offset and every case offset are relative to the address of the `lookupswitch` opcode itself: `target = instruction.offset + s24`. All three references agree: avmplus `Verifier.cpp` calls `checkTarget(pc, nextpc+imm24)` for branches and `checkTarget(pc, pc+imm24)` for the switch, `Interpreter.cpp` `INSTR(lookupswitch)` sets `base = pc-1`, and RABCDAsm's assembler fixes a `JumpTarget` against `pos+3` but a `SwitchDefaultTarget` and `SwitchTargets` against `instructionOffset`. `lookupswitch` reads a default offset and then `case_count + 1` case offsets. A target outside `[0, code.size()]` is `AbcStatus::BranchOutOfRange`, but only when the branching instruction is reachable (`Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable`), and a catch block is reachable through its handler target (see `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable` below); a jump to the end of the code is accepted, so a switch as the last instruction whose targets are the end of the body decodes.

- `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:validate_operand_pools` is a separate cross-check because a method body decodes without a file: it resolves each operand role (multiname, string, namespace, method, class, int, uint, double) against the file's pools and returns `AbcStatus::IndexOutOfRange` when an index points past its pool. `disassemble` and `summarize` call decode and validate together, and both hand `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code` the body's `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcMethodBody::exceptions`, which is what makes a catch block reachable and a handler target validated.

- `Radicle/src/abc/disassembly.cpp:render_instruction` prints `offset: mnemonic operands` with decimal offsets. `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::multiname_at` renders QName as `ns::name`, a runtime namespace as `name`, a fully runtime name as `*`, a multiname as `nsSet::name` with `|`-joined namespaces and a TypeName as `name<p1,p2>` with each parameter rendered by the same rule (`parse_multiname_pool` guarantees every reference is an earlier entry, so the recursion ends); strings are quoted with `\` and `"` escaped; unresolved names fall back to `multiname#N`, `method#N`, `class#N`.

- `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:summarize` answers the two tooling questions. Class, super, interface and trait names resolve through `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::multiname_at`; a method's name stays a string index read through `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::method_name`. Per class it reports name, super, interfaces and the methods taken from the instance traits (Method/Getter/Setter) plus the constructor as `<init>`; per method it reports name, return type, flags, instruction count, the deduped multinames it reads or calls, and every call site that names a multiname. Script init methods land in `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/summary.hpp:AbcSummary::scripts` and every body no trait or script claims lands in `AbcSummary::functions`, so each body appears exactly once.

- Literal arguments and receivers: call arguments are mapped on a bounded abstract stack, not on the instruction run before the call. The model, the opcodes it declines and its bounds are in the `## Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:collect_literals` section below.

- `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:is_external_interface_call` is "member name is `call` and the receiver ends in `ExternalInterface`", and `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:is_event_registration` is "member name is `addEventListener` or `removeEventListener`". The member name is read after the last `::` (`Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:member_name`), because the method's own multiname carries the *package* namespace (`flash.external::call`) and never the class name, so matching on `ExternalInterface.call` would never fire. Both take the receiver and the argument slots from the simulated stack, not from a backwards scan.

- Coverage gaps, deliberate: no SWF container or `DoABC` tag extraction (another lane owns it), so the decoder takes a raw span; argument mapping is a bounded abstract stack and not a verifier, so any opcode outside the model's known set clears the stack and leaves the slots after it unknown (see the `collect_literals` section below); the decoder itself verifies nothing and models no try range or handler state — a handler target is a reachability root and is checked as a branch target, but `AbcException::from` and `::to` are not, and no stack depth is (see `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable`); verification is now a separate pass over the decoded stream, `Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_method_flow`, described in the `AbcMethodFlow` section below, and no bodies are reached through `class_info` traits; the trait metadata array is read for every kind whose metadata attribute bit is set, Slot and Const included, because RABCDAsm's `readTrait`/`writeTrait` do exactly that (the array sits outside the per-kind switch) and `Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:put_instance_traits` pins it; the AVM2 overview prints the array only after the non-Slot/Const arms of `trait_info`, so the overview reads as if a Slot or Const trait carried none, but the reference implementation reads it for every kind and no real file is known to disagree. Index validation is partial by choice as well: `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::check_metadata_indices` checks trait metadata indices only, while `instance.name`/`super_index`/`interfaces`/`iinit`, `trait.name`/`type_name`/`method_index`/`class_index`, `method.return_type`/`param_types`, `exception.exc_type`/`var_name`, `script.init` and `body.method` are read without a pool check, so a malformed file yields an empty name or a lookup miss instead of the typed error the operand path produces (`Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:validate_operand_pools`); nothing there is unsafe, because `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::multiname_at`, `string_at` and the other accessors are bounds-checked. Two of those fields are not pool indices and must not be validated like one: `trait.disp_id` is a dispatch id, and `trait.value_index` is only meaningful when the value kind is not `Undefined`, which is why `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::parse_traits` reads the kind only when the index is non-zero, as RABCDAsm's `readTrait` does.
- Coverage gaps, deliberate: no SWF container or `DoABC` tag extraction (another lane owns it), so the decoder takes a raw span; argument mapping is a bounded abstract stack and not a verifier, so any opcode outside the model's known set clears the stack and leaves the slots after it unknown (see the `collect_literals` section below); no bytecode verification, and no try-range or handler-state modelling — a handler target is a reachability root and is checked as a branch target, but `AbcException::from` and `::to` are not, and no stack depth is (see `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable`), and no bodies are reached through `class_info` traits; the trait metadata array is read for every kind whose metadata attribute bit is set, Slot and Const included, because RABCDAsm's `readTrait`/`writeTrait` do exactly that (the array sits outside the per-kind switch) and `Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:put_instance_traits` pins it; the AVM2 overview prints the array only after the non-Slot/Const arms of `trait_info`, so the overview reads as if a Slot or Const trait carried none, but the reference implementation reads it for every kind and no real file is known to disagree. Index validation is one pass, `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::check_pool_indices`, documented in its own note below: every structural index is checked there against the pool it names, except `namespace.name`, so a malformed file yields `AbcStatus::IndexOutOfRange` instead of the empty name or lookup miss the bounds-checked accessors return (`Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::multiname_at`, `string_at` and the other accessors stay bounds-checked, so nothing there is unsafe). One field that looks like a pool index must not be validated like one: `trait.disp_id` is a dispatch id. `trait.value_index` is only meaningful when the value kind is not `Undefined`, which is why `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::parse_traits` reads the kind only when the index is non-zero, as RABCDAsm's `readTrait` does.

- Tests: `Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:build_abc` builds a complete synthetic ABC with `put_u30`, `put_s24` and `put_string` helpers, shared by `Radicle/tests/test_abc.cpp` and `Radicle/tests/test_abc_pool.cpp` — version 46.16, all seven pools, one class whose constructor body is `getlex ExternalInterface; pushstring "Foo"; callpropvoid call 1; returnvoid`, plus a second body registering an `addEventListener`. `Abc.ParsesVersionConstantPoolAndStructure` and `Abc.ParsesEveryByteAndRejectsTrailingBytes` catch a wrong pool reserved slot or a drifted walk; `Abc.DisassemblesConstructorCallSite` catches wrong operand roles, offsets or listing text and pins `pushshort -5`, whose u30 operand is sign-extended from 16 bits; `Abc.SummaryAnswersExternalInterfaceAndEventListenerQuestions` covers both tooling questions end to end and asserts the slot mapping for both bodies (`Foo` in slot 0 of the `ExternalInterface` call, `click` and the `getlex handler` receiver in the two slots of the `addEventListener` call); `Abc.MapsTwoStringArgumentsToTheirOwnSlots` catches a return to run-order argument attribution, where two literals are reported as one ambiguous list instead of two named slots; `Abc.LeavesBranchJoinedArgumentUnknown` catches a guess at a branch join, where the old run scan reported the fall-through literal `click` as the unambiguous argument of a call whose argument differs on each path, and also a join with no `jump` before it, which only the branch-target marking can clear; `Abc.LeavesNestedCallResultArgumentUnknown` catches attributing a nested call's result to a slot (the handler stays unknown while the literal beside it is still placed, and the event name is still reported); `Abc.PopsCallStaticReceiverWithItsArgument` catches a call form whose fixed pop count is one short, which leaves a value stranded below the next site's receiver slot and turns a literal receiver into an `ExternalInterface` one; `Abc.KeepsLiteralArgumentsAcrossPlainOpcodes` catches clearing the stack on the plain `getlocal`/`getproperty` opcodes a real listener body uses for its base, which drops both the event name and the handler of the commonest registration shape; `Abc.MapsEveryPushFormToItsLiteralKind` catches a wrong rendered value or `Literal` kind for any of the literal push forms; `Abc.AsCastInsideExternalInterfaceArgumentKeepsReceiver`, `Abc.RuntimeNameLookupInsideExternalInterfaceArgumentKeepsReceiver` and `Abc.RuntimeNameCallInsideExternalInterfaceArgumentKeepsReceiver` catch `astypelate` counted as depth-neutral and a runtime-name `getproperty` or `callproperty` whose name slots are not popped, either of which moves the receiver of the enclosing `ExternalInterface.call` onto its first literal argument; `Abc.PlainAstypeInsideExternalInterfaceArgumentStaysOneSlot` keeps plain `astype` depth-neutral, so the fix cannot over-correct the prefix match; `Abc.OpcodeTableMatchesAvm2Numbers` catches a one-line shift in the packed mnemonic table by pinning the row boundaries 0x40, 0x80, 0xC0, 0xD0, 0xEF, 0xF3 and the whole undefined set as sixteen ranges covering all 87 null opcodes; `Abc.RejectsUnknownOpcode`, `Abc.RejectsTruncatedVarintAndTruncatedFile`, `Abc.RejectsConstantPoolIndexOutOfRange`, `Abc.RejectsBranchTargetOutOfRange` (s24 and lookupswitch, positive and negative, and a switch whose default and case targets are the end of the code, the case the instruction-start base fixes), `Abc.HandlerTargetsAreReachabilityRootsAndValidated` (a catch block reached only through the exception table, a handler target past the end, equal to the code length and inside an instruction, and the status `summarize` propagates for it) and `Abc.RejectsBadNamespaceAndMultinameKinds` are the negative cases; `Abc.RejectsBadTraitKindAndTraitMetadataIndex` catches a trait tag above 6 accepted as a kind and a metadata index past the pool, and the trait half of `Abc.ParsesMethodOptionsParamNamesTraitsAndExceptions` catches the per-kind field order (slot id before type name, dispatch id before method index, class index for Class/Function) and the metadata pool wiring. `Abc.RejectsEveryStructuralIndexPastItsPool` breaks one structural index at a time in `Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:build_abc` — thirty cases covering every field `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::check_pool_indices` checks except trait metadata, which `Abc.RejectsBadTraitKindAndTraitMetadataIndex` already covers, each expecting `AbcStatus::IndexOutOfRange` while the unbroken file still parses: seventeen put `kBadIndex` (99) far past their pool, and thirteen sit exactly on a pool limit (`instance.name = multinames.size()`, `instance.iinit = methods.size()`, and the method name, parameter name, option index, metadata name/key/value, and trait string/int/uint/double/namespace value indices, each written from the fixture's own pool count) — so a dropped or mis-pooled check fails a named case, and an inverted comparison (`>` for `>=`) fails the boundary cases and no others, because a value equal to the pool size is the only place the two forms disagree. `Abc.AcceptsZeroIndicesIntoEmptyStringPool` and `Abc.AcceptsZeroIndexOptionInEmptyIntPoolAndAnyIndexForPoollessKind` pin the zero sentinel: a file whose string pool has count 0 with `method.name`, a parameter name and a metadata name/key/value all 0 parses, an `Int` option with index 0 against an empty int pool parses, and a `True` option with index 99 parses because that kind names no pool. `Abc.AcceptsEveryStructuralIndexAtItsLastEntry` is the companion: the same fields written one below their pool size (and an option index of 0) parse `AbcStatus::Ok` and read back with the written index, so a check that rejects the last valid entry, or a `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::check_pool_indices` value-pool mapping that sends a kind to the wrong pool, fails there. `Abc.ReadsFullWidthIntUIntAndDoublePoolEntries` pins the full-width int, uint and double pool entries; `Abc.ReadsProtectedNamespaceAndAlwaysPresentInterfaceCount` pins the instance layout (protected namespace only with flag 0x08, interface count always); `Abc.AcceptsEverySpecValueKindInOptionalValues` pins the fifteen value kinds; `Abc.RejectsTypeNameReferencesThatAreNotEarlierAndExpansionOverCap` pins the TypeName rule and the 64 cap. The pool, multiname, TypeName, int/uint/double and value-kind tests (`Abc.RejectsBadNamespaceAndMultinameKinds`, `Abc.ReadsFullWidthIntUIntAndDoublePoolEntries`, `Abc.RejectsTypeNameReferencesThatAreNotEarlierAndExpansionOverCap`, `Abc.AcceptsEverySpecValueKindInOptionalValues`) live in `Radicle/tests/test_abc_pool.cpp`; the call-site and stack-summary tests live in `Radicle/tests/test_abc_summary.cpp`, and the rest live in `Radicle/tests/test_abc.cpp`. `Radicle/tests/test_abc.cpp:AbcCorpus.EveryExtractedAbcParsesDisassemblesAndSummarizes` is the real-data check, gated on `FO4_ABC_CORPUS` (a directory of extracted `.abc` files) and skipped without it; like `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:AbcCorpusReal.DecodesEveryShippedInterfaceAbcBlock` it now hands each body's `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcMethodBody::exceptions` to `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code` and `Radicle/src/abc/disassembly.cpp:disassemble`, so CI checks every shipped handler target. Nothing in this lane was compiled on the authoring machine; CI is the first compiler.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:AbcFile::serialize (#806 phase 1)

- Mirror: `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:AbcFile::serialize` writes the sections in the order `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:AbcFile::parse` reads them: version, constant pool, methods, metadata, instances, classes, scripts, bodies. Each anonymous-namespace helper mirrors one parse function field for field: `put_constant_pool` mirrors `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:parse_constant_pool`, the multiname kind switch inside `put_constant_pool` mirrors `parse_multiname_pool`, `put_method_info` mirrors `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:parse_methods`, `put_metadata` mirrors `detail::parse_metadata`, `put_instance` mirrors `parse_instances`, `put_trait` mirrors `detail::parse_traits` and `put_body` mirrors `parse_bodies`. Classes have no count of their own, so `serialize` writes each `cinit` and its traits after the instance list, as the parser reads them.
- Integers: `put_u32` writes the shortest LEB128 form for both u30 and u32 fields, which `ByteReader::u32` reads back in at most five bytes. `put_d64` writes the eight raw IEEE bytes copied with `memcpy`, so NaN payloads keep their bits. Container counts and string lengths go through `put_size`, and `put_string` writes the byte length followed by the raw bytes.
- Pool count: `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:parse_constant_pool` keeps the on-disk count as the vector size, and entry 0 is a placeholder that is never read (every loop starts at `i = 1`). A count of 0 gives an empty vector and a count of 1 gives a size-1 vector, so the two stay distinct in memory and `put_constant_pool` writes `size()` exactly. RABCDAsm's `ABCWriter` writes 0 for any size of 0 or 1, which would break byte identity for a count-1 pool; `Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:build_abc` uses count 1 for its empty namespace-set pool. No preservation flag is needed.
- Model check: `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:model_encodable` runs before any byte is written and returns `AbcStatus::InconsistentModel` for a `param_types` size that differs from `param_count`, options without `has_optional` or more options than `param_count`, a `param_names` size that does not match `has_param_names`, a `protected_ns` set while `has_protected_ns` is clear, metadata set while `has_metadata` is clear, a trait kind above Const, a trait `attrs` above 0x0F, a u30 field above 0x3FFFFFFF (`Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:fits_u30`), and classes and instances of different lengths. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:AbcFile::serialize` clears `out` first, so a failed call leaves it empty. Index checks reuse `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::check_pool_indices` (declared in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_internal.hpp`) and return `AbcStatus::IndexOutOfRange`.
- Directional flags: `has_optional()` with an empty `options` list is encodable, because the parser reads count 0 and keeps the flag, so the check rejects only options present without the flag and options longer than `param_count`. A trait with `has_metadata()` set and an empty `metadata` list is accepted for the same reason.
- Stricter than the parser: `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:methods_encodable` refuses more options than `param_count`, which `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:parse_methods` accepts when the bytes fit. avmplus `AbcParser.cpp` rejects that shape too, and a scan of the 675 vanilla Interface blocks found none.
- Known gap: the writer does not check the TypeName expansion cap. `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:parse_multiname_pool` refuses a TypeName whose expanded node count passes 64 with `AbcStatus::TypeNameTooLarge`, and `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:pool_encodable` does not repeat that count, so an edited model over the cap serializes `Ok` and the output then fails `AbcFile::parse`. Parsed files cannot hit it. The pool reference and kind gaps that once sat here are closed in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:pool_encodable`, see the section at the tail.
- Remaining gap: `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:put_trait` writes fields a kind does not use as given, so a hand-built model that sets them is emitted without error. Out-of-spec namespace, multiname and value kinds and u30 fields of 2^30 or more are now refused by `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:pool_encodable` (see its section below). Parsed files never hit the remainder, because unread fields keep their defaults in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:AbcFile::parse`.
- Byte identity: a parsed file re-serializes identically when every varint is canonical and every u30 has bits 30 and 31 clear. A padded varint such as `0x80 0x00`, or a 5-byte u32 whose top bits are set, is read to a value and written back in canonical form, so the corpus check reports it instead of hiding it. The check is `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:check_block`.
- Metadata order: `detail::parse_metadata` and `put_metadata` both use keys-then-values order, matching RABCDAsm `readMetadata` and `writeMetadata`. An interleaved reader misreads every entry with two or more items, and `Radicle/tests/test_abc_write.cpp:ReadsMetadataItemsAsKeysThenValuesAndRoundTrips` is its regression test. The existing fixtures `Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:build_abc` and `Radicle/tests/test_abc.cpp` encode at most one item, where both orders produce the same bytes, so no fixture encoding changed.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_write.cpp:RoundTripsTheSyntheticFixtureByteForByte` catches a writer that drops, reorders or mis-gates any field of `Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:build_abc` (pools, three multiname kinds, method options and param names, metadata, five trait kinds with trait metadata, an exception handler). `RoundTripsProtectedNamespaceAndSlotMetadataOfAMinimalInstance` catches a protected namespace written unconditionally or dropped under flag 0x08. `SerializesEditedStringAndBodyCodeAndReparsesWithSameCounts` catches a writer that reuses the original bytes or writes stale or duplicated pool and table entries after an edit. `RejectsAnInconsistentModelWithoutWritingBytes` catches silent truncation or leftover bytes for each `model_encodable` rule, and checks that a bad body method index returns `IndexOutOfRange`.
- Corpus: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:check_block` re-serializes every parsed Interface block and EXPECTs a byte match, reporting the block label and the first differing offset, and `AbcStats::serialize_mismatches` is EXPECTed to be zero. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:check_movie` rebuilds each DoABC tag as its original payload before the ABC span (`Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfAbc::payload_offset`) followed by the serialized bytes, passes it to `replace_tag_payload`, and EXPECTs the uncompressed `write_swf` output to equal the original. That catches a prefix or length-field error that the block-level check cannot see.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD time interpolator lists (#602 B-20)

- The `wbTimeInterpolators` members of IMAD are `counted_array` rows: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD\BlurRadiusInterpolators` (BNAM, xEdit `wbTimeInterpolators(BNAM, 'Blur Radius')` at source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7528 @93cc0bc5), `IMAD\DoubleVisionStrengthInterpolators` (VNAM, :7529), `IMAD\RadialBlurStrengthInterpolators` (RNAM), `IMAD\RadialBlurRampUpInterpolators` (SNAM), `IMAD\RadialBlurStartInterpolators` (UNAM), `IMAD\RadialBlurRampDownInterpolators` (NAM1) and `IMAD\RadialBlurDownStartInterpolators` (NAM2), all five inside the required `wbRStruct('Radial Blur', ...)` at :7532-7538; `IMAD\DepthOfFieldStrengthInterpolators` (WNAM), `IMAD\DepthOfFieldDistanceInterpolators` (XNAM), `IMAD\DepthOfFieldRangeInterpolators` (YNAM), `IMAD\DepthOfFieldVignetteRadiusInterpolators` (NAM5) and `IMAD\DepthOfFieldVignetteStrengthInterpolators` (NAM6) inside `wbRStruct('Depth of Field', ...)` at :7539-7545; `IMAD\MotionBlurStrengthInterpolators` (NAM4, :7546); and the HDR add lists from `IMAD\HDREyeAdaptSpeedAddInterpolators` (@IAD) to `IMAD\CinematicUnusedAddInterpolators` (TIAD). Each row is stride 8 with the two f32 members Time (offset 0) and Value (offset 4), because `wbTimeInterpolator` is `wbStructSK([0], 'Data', [wbFloat('Time'), wbFloat('Value')])` at source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8312-8326 @93cc0bc5 and `wbTimeInterpolators(aSignature, aName)` is `wbArray(aSignature, aName, wbTimeInterpolator).SetRequired` at :9272-9281, an uncounted array, so the element count comes from the payload size the way `IMAD\TintColorInterpolators` and `IMAD\FadeColorInterpolators` already derive theirs. The VNAM and WNAM/XNAM/YNAM rows keep the names xEdit gives them (`Double Vision Strength`, and `Strength`, `Distance`, `Range` inside `Depth of Field`), which is why the paths use `DoubleVisionStrength` and `DepthOfField` rather than the pre-audit `DoubleVision` and `DoF` spellings.
- Member paths take the array name as a prefix (`IMAD\BlurRadiusTime`, `IMAD\BlurRadiusValue`), the naming `IMAD\TintColorTime` and `CLMT\WeatherChance` established: the xEdit member names are `Time` and `Value` for every list, and `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:load_schema` rejects a duplicate path, so the bare names cannot be used. `IMAD\BlurRadius`, `IMAD\VignetteRadius` and the other DNAM rows at offsets 180 to 248 keep their own paths: they are u32 presence flags, not interpolator elements.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD\DepthOfFieldVignetteRadiusInterpolators` and `IMAD\DepthOfFieldVignetteStrengthInterpolators` carry `"min_form_version": 118` on the array, from `wbFromVersion(118, NAM5, wbTimeInterpolators('Vignette Radius'))` and the NAM6 twin at source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7543-7544 @93cc0bc5. The array-level key is enough because `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_counted_array` copies it onto every emitted member row, and `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarDescriptor::min_form_version` is what `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` compares against `record.header.form_version`. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:CountedArrayDescriptor` has no version window and is only a lookup, so `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:MEMBER_KEYS` needs no `min_form_version` of its own; the DNAM flag rows `IMAD\VignetteRadius` and `IMAD\VignetteStrength` keep their separate 116 gate.
- The rows are `existing_only` and change no authoring rule: the authoring block lists each of these subrecords at maximum 1 (one subrecord holds the whole array), and `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp` still sees `create_record` write EDID, DNAM, TNAM and NAM3 for a new IMAD.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_image_fx_records.cpp` (`ImageFxSynthetic`) keeps `TimeInterpolatorArraysDecodeAndEditOneStrideElement` for the BNAM and `@IAD` lists, and `DepthOfFieldVignetteInterpolatorsAreGatedByFormVersion118` covers NAM5/NAM6: element counts and the decoded Value on the version 131 record, a write of element 0 asserted against the exact bytes after a reread with the Value word untouched, and the version 113 record whose present NAM6 payload is still counted because `record_field_count` is positional and the version gate only clears slot validity, so the refused write returns `subrecord_missing` and leaves the payload byte-identical. The fixture's `write_record` gained a form version argument, defaulting to the 131 the other records already use, and IMAD 3002 is version 113, which is the version its 244-byte DNAM belongs to. `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` was regenerated: IMAD reports 142 scalar rows, 78 of them strided. Nothing here was compiled or run: CI is the first build.

- `Radicle/tests/test_image_fx_records.cpp:ImageFxSynthetic.TimeInterpolatorArraysDecodeAndEditOneStrideElement`: regression guard. An interpolator row requires stride 8 with Time at 0 and Value at 4, so a wrong stride or offset edits the neighbouring sample of the same array.

- `Radicle/tests/test_image_fx_records.cpp:ImageFxSynthetic.DepthOfFieldVignetteInterpolatorsAreGatedByFormVersion118`: regression guard. NAM5 and NAM6 carry min_form_version 118, so a version 113 record must not read or write them even when the payload is present.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA\SculptData (#602 A-13 A-15)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA\SculptData` is the first `subrecord_group` on ARMA and closes the "sculpt data sequence still unrowed" gap the earlier ARMA audit recorded. xEdit's `wbArmorAddonBSMPSequence` is `wbRArray('Sculpt Data', wbArmorAddonBoneDataItem)` at source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5597 @93cc0bc5, the last member of `wbRecord(ARMA, 'Armor Addon'` (:5845), and one item is `wbRStruct('Bone Scale Modifier Set', [wbInteger(BSMP, 'Target Gender', itU32, wbSexEnum), wbRArrayS('Bone Scale Modifiers', wbRStructSK([0], 'Bone Scale Modifier', [wbString(BSMB, 'Bone Name'), wbVec3(BSMS, 'Bone Scale Delta').SetRequired]))])` at :5575-5588. The members are BSMP (`required`, not `repeatable`, `payload_size` 4), BSMB (`required`, `repeatable`, `payload_size` 0, default one NUL byte) and BSMS (`required`, `repeatable`, `payload_size` 12, default 12 zero bytes), so `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` opens one span per BSMP and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_subrecord_group` and `remove_record_subrecord_group` add and remove a whole bone scale set.
- The member flags are measured, not guessed. Read-only scan of `Fallout4.esm` (739 ARMA records, 39 with sculpt data): BSMP is 4 bytes in all 75 occurrences, BSMS is 12 bytes in all 2159, BSMB is 11 to 22 bytes and NUL-terminated in all 2159, BSMB and BSMS counts are equal in every record, the order is always BSMB then BSMS with no other interleaving, and BSMS is the last subrecord of the record in all 39. That is why BSMB and BSMS can both be `required`: no vanilla run lacks either, and no run interleaves them differently, which `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` would refuse as "out of order or repeated". BSMB is not `skippable`, so a BSMB before the first BSMP is refused rather than silently dropped, which is the shape MSWP uses for its optional members and the opposite of what this record's data needs.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ARMA\SculptTargetGender` is the group's only row, on the leader BSMP: u32, offset 0, `presentation` enum with the `wbSexEnum` names Male (0) and Female (1) at source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:7900-7907 @93cc0bc5. `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` forces `repeated: true` on a member row and forbids `payload_size` and `kind` on it, so the row addresses the i-th BSMP, which is the i-th sculpt entry, the way `ARMA\AdditionalRaces` addresses the i-th MODL. A row on BSMB or BSMS is impossible: those members are `repeatable`, and `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` rejects rows on a repeatable member.
- The group adds no authoring rule and no FormLink. The authoring block is unchanged, so `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:SubrecordAuthoring.GeneratedSchemaMarksSiblingOwnersCoupled` still sees ARMA's coupled set as MOD2 to MOD5, and BSMP, BSMB and BSMS are not in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formid_subrecords.inc`, so nothing remaps them. One side effect is deliberate and matches the IPDS precedent: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots` now runs `group_spans` for any ARMA row whose subrecord is a group member, so a malformed sculpt run fails the `ARMA\SculptTargetGender` row with `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` before the offset check sees it.
- Not rowed, and why: ARMA DNAM's two unnamed byte runs (`wbByteArray('Unknown', 2)` at offset 4 and `wbByteArray('Unknown', 1)` at offset 7, source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5864-5866) stay out, the same choice the RACE audit recorded for its unknown byte runs. The RACE record carries the same three signatures with a different layout (`wbBSMPSequence` at :5595 and `wbBoneDataItem`, whose BSMS is a four-float range rather than a vec3), so RACE needs its own group; this lane owns ARMA only.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_arma_sculpt_rows.cpp` (`ARMASculptRows`) covers the descriptor's members, sizes and flags, `subrecord_group_for_member`, the two spans of a two-entry fixture, the gender row's storage, presentation and names, the per-index write and reread of the two BSMP payloads with the BSMB and BSMS payloads left byte-identical, an insert at index 1 asserted against the exact subrecord order and the three BSMP, BSMB and BSMS payloads including the new empty name and zero delta, a removal that restores both original entries byte for byte, and the refusals: an index at the entry count for both read and write, an enum name and an out-of-range value that raise `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError`, a run with no BSMB, a BSMS that is not 12 bytes, a BSMB outside any run, and an insert index past the count on a record with no sculpt data. Registered in `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt`; the suite lives in a new file because `Radicle/tests/test_armo_arma_rows.cpp` is at 739 lines. `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` was regenerated: ARMA moves from 15 to 16 named fields and gains one array. Nothing here was compiled or run: CI is the first build.

Closing the earlier "still open" list at `Radicle/docs/code-notes/Radicle.md:3040`: this lane added rows for XBSD, XPDD, XPLK, XWPG, XLRT and XCVL/XCVR, so XLCM, XTEL, XOWN/XESP, XACT, XATP, XATR, XIS2, XLTW, XPRM/XPTL/XOCP/XMBO/XMBP/XRDO/XNDP, XRMR, XMRK/ONAM and the XPWR/patrol/room/ragdoll groups are what remains open there.

The first draft's `repeated: true` with `payload_sizes: [8]` was wrong for a two-portal record — both rows resolved absent on a 16-byte XPOD, `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:record_field_count` and `:set_record_formlink_field` threw "has unexpected payload size" on it, and `Radicle/src/environment/placed.cpp:decode_placed_reference` refused a record with two 8-byte XPOD subrecords as a duplicate (`once(!data_.portals.empty(), sub)` at `:235`) — the schema refuses it too now that the row is strided, because `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` marks `duplicate` only for a non-repeated address, which the first draft's `repeated: true` was not — and it contradicted `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_placed_reference_layouts` (`{"XPOD", 8, {0, 4}, false, 0}`) and `Radicle/src/environment/placed.cpp:decode_placed_reference`, which reads XPOD as a whole multiple of 8. Both rows target REFR only, matching `:11477-11478`; the 11-signature `sigReferences` union the first draft declared is not what those lines list, and `Radicle/tests/test_refr_extra_rows.cpp:LinkRowsNameTheirSubrecordsOffsetsAndTargets` now asserts the refusal of ACHR as well as the acceptance of REFR.
