A read-only walk of all seven official masters (Fallout4.esm, DLCCoast.esm, DLCNukaWorld.esm, DLCRobot.esm, DLCworkshop01.esm, DLCworkshop02.esm, DLCworkshop03.esm; every GRUP, compressed payloads inflated) found 6 REFR records with `XWPG` holding 7 groups: Fallout4.esm has 4 records (5 groups), DLCRobot.esm 1 and DLCworkshop03.esm 1, and all 7 groups are exact (each `XWPG` equals the number of `XWPN` subrecords before the next `XWPG`, with 0 `XWPN` outside a group). Record-level equality holds for 5 of 6 records and fails on Fallout4.esm `00066EB6`, which has two groups (`XWPG` 103 with 103 `XWPN`, then `XWPG` 18 with 18 `XWPN`): 121 `XWPN` against the first count of 103. The first draft's derived-row model therefore rejected the master shape twice: `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:is_derived_scalar_row` no longer reports `REFR` `XWPG`, and the non-repeated row would have raised "duplicate scalar subrecords" in `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots`, so the row now carries `repeated: true` and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` edits the selected group's count in place.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REFR\SplineSlack`, `REFR\SplineThickness`, `REFR\SplineHalfExtentX`, `REFR\SplineHalfExtentY`, `REFR\SplineHalfExtentZ` and `REFR\SplineWindDetachedEnd` carry `minimum_payload_size` because xEdit marks XBSD's tail optional: `.SetOptionalFrom(3)` at `:11600` makes members 0, 1 and 2 (Slack, Thickness, Half Extents) mandatory and only member 3 (Wind-Detached-End) optional, and `Core/wbImplementation.pas:22588` (`if Assigned(aBasePtr) and (i >= OptionalFromElement)`) is what turns that index into the truncation rule, so the shortest XBSD xEdit reads cleanly is 20 bytes. Every row of the mandatory prefix therefore carries `minimum_payload_size: 20` (Wind-Detached-End keeps 21), which is also what `Radicle/src/environment/placed.cpp:decode_placed_reference` requires; the first draft's 4 on `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REFR\SplineSlack` reported Slack out of a payload too short to be an XBSD. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REFR\DecalWidthScale` and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REFR\DecalHeightScale` carry `payload_size: 8` instead, because XPDD has no `SetOptionalFrom` at all, so a payload of any other size is not that struct and the rows report absent rather than reading a float out of it — the same gate the ten `ATKD` rows use, e.g. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_\AttackChance`, all `payload_size: 44`. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc:k_scalar_fields` is the generated form of both.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_refr_extra_rows.cpp:LinkRowsNameTheirSubrecordsOffsetsAndTargets` asserts each row's `address.repeated`, `address.stride` and `payload_sizes[0]` from its `LinkRow` table, so the storage choice is pinned per row rather than implied; the table's `payload_size` column mirrors the descriptor's `payload_sizes[0]`, which is 0 on the two strided XPOD rows because a strided address declares no payload size at all (the element size lives in `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_placed_reference_layouts`, stride 8), and re-adding `payload_sizes` to those schema rows would fail that assertion and make `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots` reject the 16-byte packed XPOD; `Radicle/tests/test_refr_extra_rows.cpp:PackedPortalPairsAddressEachElement` builds a 16-byte XPOD and shows both portal pairs resolving and the second pair writing in place, which a `repeated` row cannot do; `Radicle/tests/test_refr_extra_rows.cpp:ShortSplineConnectionPayloadReadsAndWrites` covers the 4-byte XPLK; and `Radicle/tests/test_refr_extra_rows.cpp:WritesTheNewRowsInPlaceAndRefusesALinkedReferenceBesideAShortXlkr` writes the second of the fixture's two `XWPG` groups, so a return to a derived or non-repeated row shows up as a refused write or a duplicate-slot error.
- No `XLRT` double count. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REFR\LocationRefTypes` is a `packed_array` FormLink list read through `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:packed_segment` (`data.size() / 4` elements), while `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_placed_reference_layouts` supplies the same per-element offsets to remap and link collection; they are separate readers, not two counts added together. The only enumeration in `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:collect_form_links_detailed` is `visit_link_offsets`, which reaches the mixed table and returns; `schema_formlink_offsets` builds `XLRT` offsets only from `formlink_fields`, where REFR has no `XLRT` row, and `visit_formlink_offsets` sorts and uniques the schema and mixed offsets before emitting them (`Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:529-536`). `k_counted_arrays` has no `XLRT` entry, so each `XLRT` subrecord element is emitted once.

## Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_placed_reference_layouts — XPWR and XPLK reference-only payloads

- `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:k_placed_reference_layouts` accepts both the 8-byte and the 4-byte `XPWR` and `XPLK` payloads: `{"XPWR", 8, {0}, true, 4}` and `{"XPLK", 8, {0}, true, 4}` name 4 as the short size, so only offset 0 is remapped and written. The 4-byte form is a lone reference, because xEdit makes the trailing member optional: `XPWR` is `wbStructSK(XPWR, ...).SetOptionalFrom(1)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3218-3226`, REFR `:11537`) and `XPLK` is a form ID followed by `wbUnknown` (`:4597-4600`, REFR `:11836-11839`). The real-data check `Radicle/tests/test_writeback_real.cpp:WritebackRealData.CopiedDlcReferencesKeepEveryLinkWhenMastersMove` found 244 vanilla 4-byte `XPLK` subrecords, and `Radicle/tests/test_environment_writeback.cpp:AcceptsReferenceOnlySplineAndReflectionLinks` pins that a 4-byte payload takes the short layout.

## Radicle/src/plugin/navmesh_writer.cpp:set_navmesh_vertex and Radicle/docs/NAVM_NAVI.md:Editing (#602 B-56)

- B-56 stays a deliberate refusal, not a missing row. `Radicle/docs/NAVM_NAVI.md` (Editing table) records it: ADD/REMOVE/CREATE is refused for counted or coupled geometry and info structures, and NAVM creation needs a parent placement the generic creator cannot supply. The three writers that exist are single-element stores, `Radicle/src/plugin/navmesh_writer.cpp:set_navmesh_vertex`, `:set_navmesh_triangle` and `:set_navmesh_door`, each of which refuses an out-of-range index with `ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` (`:58`) and never changes a count.
- Why no add or remove: the NVNM payload is one subrecord holding four count-prefixed blocks in a fixed order (`Radicle/src/environment/navmesh.cpp:decode_navmesh`, vertex count, triangle count, edge count, door count, then the opaque tail). Inserting or removing one element means rewriting the owning count and every index that refers to a later element (triangle vertex indices and edge indices, edge links, door triangle indices), and `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:navmesh_mixed_formid_offsets` validates the whole payload before any of it is touched. That is a rebuild, not a stored-data edit, and the module's contract is stored-data edits only.
- Why no creation: NAVM carries a parent (world, or cell plus grid) and a body in one record, so a creator would have to be handed a valid parent; no creator reaches NAVM (`Radicle/src/forms/` has none) and the typed decoder fails closed on a legacy form version (`:50`) and on a geometry version other than 15 (`:55`).
- The counts themselves are already exposed, not refused: `Radicle/src/c_api_navmesh.cpp:radicle_navmesh_decode` fills `vertex_count`, `triangle_count`, `edge_count` and `door_count` from the decoded vectors. What B-56 records as refused is changing them.
- Adjacent gap found while checking the row, not fixed here: NAVM `ONAM` (base objects, a count-less packed array of 4-byte links) and `MNAM` (PreCut Map Entries) have no typed reader in `Radicle/src/environment/navmesh.cpp:decode_navmesh`, but both are remapped through the form-link layer: ONAM by `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:record_specific_formid_array` (every 4-byte slot), MNAM by `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_mixed.cpp:mnam_formid_offsets` via `navmesh_mixed_formid_offsets`. `PNAM` and `NNAM` (u16 connector vertex indices) have no typed reader, and the remap skips them (`Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:navm_vertex_index_signature`), so they are never scanned as FormIDs. xEdit declares them at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7221-7238` (NAVM at `:7212`). They are out of the row's named scope, which is the refusal above.
- Verification: the issue marks B-56 unverified. The xEdit lines above were re-read at pin 93cc0bc5 (NAVM `:7212-7238`, NAVI `:7240-7260`); no master file was scanned for this entry and nothing was compiled.

## Radicle/include/fo4/abc/flow.hpp:AbcMethodFlow and Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_method_flow (#806 piece 3, AVM2 flow lane)

Method bodies now have a model, a control-flow graph and a verifier, all C++ and all separate from the decoder. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_flow.cpp:build_control_flow` blocks a decoded stream, `Radicle/src/abc/abc_flow.cpp:detail::build_exception_graph` adds the handler entry points and validates the exception table, `Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_method_flow` runs the stack and scope passes plus the method-level checks, and `Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_all_method_flows` walks a whole file. `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:encode_code` is the inverse of `decode_code`, so a body can be decoded and re-emitted; it recomputes every branch delta from the absolute `AbcDecodedOperand::target`, so an edited target is what gets written and an unchanged stream re-encodes to its own bytes. No C ABI, no `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` change, no binding or generator touched. Spec: SWF-TOOLS `crates/swftools-avm2/src/{cfg,verify,method_verify,body,multiname}.rs` (MIT OR Apache-2.0, read and translated, no Rust copied).

- Blocks and edges follow `cfg.rs:build_cfg_with_entries`. A leader is offset 0, any branch or switch target that lands on an instruction, any target supplied as an extra entry, and the byte after a block-ending instruction. A block ends on a branch (0x0C-0x1A), a `lookupswitch` (0x1B) or a terminal (`throw` 0x03, `returnvoid` 0x47, `returnvalue` 0x48); the successors are the branch target plus a fall-through for every branch but `jump` (0x10), every switch target, and a plain fall-through otherwise. `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/flow.hpp:AbcEdgeKind` keeps the three kinds because the verifier and any later editor need to tell a switch arm from a conditional one. Reachability starts at block 0 and at the extra entries, which is why a handler is reachable even when nothing falls into it. Successors are appended without a duplicate scan and deduplicated once per block with a sort and a unique, so a `lookupswitch` with many arms stays linear instead of quadratic in the edge list.
- Divergence from `cfg.rs`, deliberate: the reference rejects a bad target anywhere in the body, while `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code` deliberately validates branch targets only for reachable instructions (`Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable`), because shipped bodies carry dead code with stale offsets. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_flow.cpp:build_control_flow` therefore only promotes a valid target to a leader and reports `TargetInsideInstruction` or `TargetOutsideCode` from the reachable blocks afterwards, so a body the decoder accepts is not refused for a jump in dead code. A jump to the byte just past the last instruction is accepted by the decoder and refused here, which is the `AbcVerify.RejectsAJumpOutOfTheMethod` regression.
- Exception regions are validated only where they can fire, the `body.rs:active_exception_targets` rule: a region is checked (`from <= to <= code_len`, `target < code_len`, `target >= to`) when a reachable instruction whose opcode can throw falls inside `[from, to)`, and a handler target becomes a CFG entry at that point. The entry set is a fixpoint because splitting a block at a handler can make another throwing instruction reachable, so `Radicle/src/abc/abc_flow.cpp:detail::build_exception_graph` rebuilds until the entry list stops growing and reports `FlowIterationLimit` if it does not; the bound is one pass per instruction plus two. Each reachable instruction is scanned once across the whole fixpoint, because the entry set only grows, and the new targets are merged with `std::set_union`, so a body with many regions is not re-walked region by region on every pass. The two exception-table refusal cases put a `throw` at offset 0 in the body, because a range that covers no reachable throwing instruction is not checked at all. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_flow.cpp:opcode_can_throw` is the reference's non-throwing opcode list, not an invented one.
- The stack pass is `cfg.rs:verify_stack_impl` with the multiname resolver replaced by a pool lookup: `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/flow.hpp:multiname_runtime_pops` reads the kind of the pool entry (`RTQName*` 1, `RTQNameL*` 2, `MultinameL*` 1, everything else 0) where the reference takes a callback, because Radicle has the parsed pool. Seeds are depth 0 at block 0 and depth 1 at every handler entry, the AVM2 rule that a handler starts with the exception object; a merge with a different depth is `StackDepthMismatch`, which is what catches a handler whose entry depth disagrees with the fall-through path. The declared `max_stack` is enforced at the instruction that crosses it rather than after the walk, so the report names that byte offset. `timestamp` (0xF3) is modelled as 0 pops and 0 pushes; it was the one AVM2 opcode the table left out, so the stack pass refused every real body that carried it as an unmodelled effect.
- The scope pass is `verify.rs:verify_scope_depth_with_entries`: `pushscope`/`pushwith` raise the depth, `popscope` lowers it and may not go below `init_scope_depth`, `getscopeobject` may only name one of the local (non-initial) scope entries, and the declared `max_scope_depth` is a hard ceiling. Seeds are `init_scope_depth` at both block 0 and every handler entry, so a handler does not inherit the protected range's local scopes.
- Method-level checks, all from `method_verify.rs`: the body needs code; `local_count` must hold `this` plus every declared parameter plus one more when the method is variadic (`NEED_ARGUMENTS` or `NEED_REST`); `newactivation` needs `NEED_ACTIVATION` and `dxns`/`dxnslate` need `SET_DXNS`; catch types must be non-runtime multinames, catch variables must be non-runtime, non-attribute and not the wildcard local name (`TypeName` derivation is followed with a cycle guard, `Radicle/src/abc/abc_flow.cpp:multiname_local_name_is_wildcard`); indexed locals and the short `getlocal`/`setlocal` forms must be inside `local_count`, and `hasnext2` may not use one register for both purposes; `newfunction`/`callstatic`/`newclass` must name a real method or class; `pushstring`/`pushint`/`pushuint`/`pushdouble`/`pushnamespace`/`dxns`/`debugfile`/`debug` must name a pool entry in `1..size-1`, the 1-based rule the reserved slot requires (the older `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:validate_operand_pools` stays 0-based and is deliberately not tightened here); `callmethod` is refused outright, `newcatch` must name a declared exception, `finddef`/`getlex`/`coerce`/`astype`/`istype` need a non-runtime multiname, and the slot opcodes refuse slot 0. Every check runs over reachable blocks only, so an invalid local in dead code is not a refusal.
- Errors are `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/flow.hpp:AbcFlowIssue`: a status, the body index, the method index, the byte offset where the fault is tied to one, and a message. `offset` is `kNoFlowIndex` for method-wide facts (local layout, scope limits, exception metadata) and for a decode failure, because `decode_code` reports the status without a position; a caller that needs the byte for a truncated body has to re-decode a prefix. `AbcFlowIssue::decode` keeps the `AbcStatus` when the instruction stream itself failed, so a caller can tell a malformed stream from a present-but-invalid one. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_internal.hpp:hex_offset` prints the digits in hexadecimal; it used to print decimal after the `0x`. `AbcInstruction::offset` is a `std::size_t`, and every site that narrows it into the `std::uint32_t` issue offset or a block field casts explicitly, because CI builds at `/W4 /WX` and C4267 is fatal there.
- Hostile input: every loop is bounded. `decode_code` bounds each read and refuses a `lookupswitch` case count the remaining bytes cannot hold, the block walk is linear in the instruction count, the reachability walks visit each block once, and the exception fixpoint has an explicit iteration cap. A self-jump is one block with an edge to itself and terminates; a truncated opcode is `DecodeFailed` with `AbcStatus::Truncated`.
- Tests, written before the implementation: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_flow.cpp` (`AbcFlow`, twelve cases) covers the three-block split of a conditional branch, dead code after a return, the self-loop, a branch into the middle of an instruction, a jump past the last instruction, switch offsets measured from the opcode, handler entries, a non-contiguous layout, one fixture per operand kind through decode and re-encode (`AbcFlow.DecodesAndReencodesOneFixturePerOperandKind`), and a branch re-encoded from its absolute target (`AbcFlow.EncodesABranchFromItsAbsoluteTarget`) so an echoed immediate fails. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_verify.cpp` (`AbcVerify`, fifteen cases) covers a balanced body and its reported depths, the branch, jump, underflow and `max_stack` refusals with their offsets, a range past the code, a handler target inside its own protected range, a handler entered at depth 1, scope underflow and the scope ceiling, a truncated body and a hostile switch count, the self-jump, the fixture file's three bodies, and the failing-body index with parallel flows. `AbcVerify.SweepsHostileBodyMutationsWithoutCrashing` mutates each of four seeded bodies 64 times (one to three bytes each) and then triples `from`/`to`/`target` over the helper body's exception range, requiring that a refusal leaves the flow unverified with a message and an acceptance is verified with no issue, so a hostile byte can neither crash nor hang the passes. The fixture itself needed two repairs the verifier found: the listener body declares `local_count` 2 because its method takes a parameter, and the helper body keeps its single `returnvoid` (its exception range is still never checked, because no reachable throwing instruction covers it and the lazy rule leaves it alone), while the catch variable names `kMultinameHelper` rather than the runtime multiname that the old string index 14 happened to resolve to, which is why `Abc.ParsesMethodOptionsParamNamesTraitsAndExceptions` now reads it through `multiname_at`. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:AbcCorpusReal.DecodesEveryShippedInterfaceAbcBlock` gained the corpus half: every body in every ABC block of `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` must decode, re-encode to its own bytes and verify, with `reencode_mismatches`, `verified_flows`, `basic_blocks`, `unreachable_blocks`, `observed_max_stack` and a `flow_refusal_histogram` recorded as properties.
- Unverified: nothing was compiled or run. The corpus claims are unobserved, including whether the verifier accepts every shipped body — the refusal rules are the reference's, but Scaleform's compiler was never run through them here. The `max_stack` ceiling is checked at the crossing instruction where the reference compares the observed maximum after the walk; the accepted set is the same, the reported offset is more precise. Two shorthands are deliberate: the scope pass treats `pushwith` as a scope push like the reference does, and a `lookupswitch` with a case count of zero (a single default target) is modelled as one case arm, as the encoder writes it. The changed fixture, the two throwing-opcode exception cases and the mutation sweep are unbuilt like the rest; CI is the first compiler.

## Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:collect_literals (#602 ABC lane)

Call arguments are mapped on a bounded abstract stack, not on the instruction run that preceded the call. `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:simulate_arguments` walks a method body once and pushes one value per instruction it can name: a literal for `pushstring`, `pushint`, `pushuint`, `pushdouble`, `pushbyte`, `pushshort`, `pushtrue`, `pushfalse`, `pushnull`, `pushundefined` and `pushnan` (the pooled ones are rendered by `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:AbcFile::optional_value_at`, so `pushint`/`pushuint`/`pushdouble` read their pool entry and `pushbyte`/`pushshort` their sign-extended immediate, as the disassembly already prints it), and a named value for `getlex` and `findpropstrict` (the multiname name, kind `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/summary.hpp:AbcArgumentKind::Named`; the name is the value the opcode looked up, and it lands in whichever slot the stack puts it in, so it is not always the call's receiver). `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:apply_call` then pops the argument count plus the fixed operands `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:operand_specs` describes — one receiver for every call form, two fixed values for `call` — plus one slot per runtime name part (`Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:runtime_parts`: one for a runtime namespace, one for a runtime name, two for `RTQNameL`/`RTQNameLA`, the counts avmplus `Verifier.cpp:checkStackMulti` takes) — and reads the argument slots off the top of the stack, slot 0 deepest, which is the AVM2 order: avmplus `core/opcodes.tbl` records a stack movement that is pushes minus fixed pops, so `call`'s -1 is two fixed pops and one result and `callmethod`/`callstatic`/`callproperty`'s 0 is one fixed pop and one result. Reading that 0 as "no fixed pop" is what made an earlier revision of `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:fixed_pops` pop `callstatic` one value short and strand its receiver below the next call's receiver slot. Each slot is recorded as `AbcArgumentKind::Literal`, `AbcArgumentKind::Named` or `AbcArgumentKind::Unknown`, and `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:collect_literals` now filters the literal slots out of that mapping, which is what keeps `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/summary.hpp:AbcCallSite::literals` and `literal_unambiguous` meaningful for the consumers that already read them. A runtime name is never a named value: `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:simulate_arguments` clears the stack on any opcode that names one, except `getproperty` and `findproperty`, which first drop their name slots.

The stack is dropped, and every later slot in that body is left `Unknown`, at a branch target, at `kill`, `pushscope`, `popscope` and `pushwith`, and after any instruction whose effect the model does not know. The known-effect set is the literal pushes, `getlex`/`findpropstrict`, the call forms, `pop`, `dup`, `swap`, and the depth-only opcodes `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:stack_delta` classifies: `getlocal*`/`getglobalscope`/`getscopeobject`/`findproperty` push one `Unknown`, `setlocal*` pops one, and `getslot`/`coerce*`/`convert_*`/`astype`/`negate`/`increment`/`not`/`typeof` are depth-neutral, replacing the value on top with `Unknown` rather than keeping it. `getproperty` is depth-neutral for a constant name; with a runtime name it first drops one slot per name part (`Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:runtime_parts`). `astypelate` is not depth-neutral: it pops two and pushes one `Unknown` (`Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:simulate_arguments`). Those are worth modelling rather than clearing because they carry no value the model could name, so they can only push or replace a value with `Unknown` and can never fabricate an attribution — they only restore the depth a real body's base expression (`getlocal0`, `this.field`) contributes, which the old run scan walked past. Everything else clears the stack — `setproperty`/`getsuper`/`setsuper`, any other opcode that names a runtime multiname, the arithmetic, bitwise and comparison opcodes, `newobject`/`newarray`/`applytype`/`newclass`, `returnvalue`, `throw`, `debug`, `label` (it is outside the known set, and a `label` is not necessarily a branch target, so clearing on it is the conservative reading), `lookupswitch` and every opcode the model was never taught. A call that pops more than the stack holds clears the stack as well and leaves its own slots unknown rather than guessing a value. `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:attributes_receiver` declines `call` deliberately: avmplus `Interpreter.cpp` reads the function at `sp[-i1-1]`, which would put the receiver at the deepest popped slot like every other form, but its own comment on that line states the opposite order, and no call site is built for a `call` anyway (the opcode takes no multiname operand), so its receiver stays empty while its argument slots are still attributed.

Bounds: the simulated stack holds at most `kSimulatedStackLimit` 16 values and a body is simulated for at most `kInstructionBudget` 4096 instructions, both in `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp`; past either, the stack is cleared and the remaining calls keep unknown slots instead of allocating. Every call form has a fixed pop of at least one (`Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:fixed_pops`), so `apply_call` can only replace a value with its result and the stack cannot grow past the limit through the call path. A malformed `arg_count` (a u30 up to 2^30) cannot drive an allocation either: `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:argument_slots` clamps the slot list to the same 16, and `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/summary.hpp:AbcCallSite::arg_count` still reports the decoded count. This replaces the old 16-instruction run window (`kArgumentRunLimit`) and the backwards scans in the deleted `collect_receiver`/`ends_argument_run`.

`Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:fill_event_slots` reports the event name and the handler of an `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener` call from slots 0 and 1 into `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/summary.hpp:AbcCallSite::event_name` and `handler`, empty when the slot is unknown. `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:is_event_registration` and `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:is_external_interface_call` keep identifying a site by its target member name — that identification is sound on its own — and now take the receiver from the slot mapping instead of a run scan, which is why the listener body's receiver is `addEventListener` (the value the call pops; the fixture's base object happens to carry that same name, so the assertion is about slot order and not about the opcode's own name) and no longer `handler` (its second argument). The old run scan reported the *nearest preceding* receiver source, so an argument that happened to be a `getlex` shadowed the real receiver.

Regressions: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_summary.cpp:Abc.MapsTwoStringArgumentsToTheirOwnSlots` (two literals reach their own slots, where the run heuristic could only say "two literals, ambiguous"), `Abc.LeavesBranchJoinedArgumentUnknown` (the argument is joined from a branch, so slot 0 stays unknown where the old scan reported one of the two path literals, `Foo`, as the unambiguous argument of a call whose argument differs per path), `Abc.LeavesNestedCallResultArgumentUnknown` (a nested `ExternalInterface.call` result is unknown while the literal beside it is still placed), `Abc.PopsCallStaticReceiverWithItsArgument` (a `callstatic` that pops one value too few strands its receiver below the next call's receiver slot, so the site reads a literal as its receiver and `is_external_interface_call` returns true for a site whose real receiver is not `ExternalInterface`), `Abc.KeepsLiteralArgumentsAcrossPlainOpcodes` (the common `this.addEventListener(...)` shape, whose base is a `getlocal0`/`getproperty` chain: clearing the stack on those opcodes leaves both argument slots unknown, `literals` empty and the event name lost, where the old run scan walked past `getlocal0` and still reported `click` as the unambiguous event name), `Abc.AsTypeLateOfLiteralInsideExternalInterfaceArgumentLeavesItUnknown` (an `astypelate` over a literal value replaces that value with `Unknown`, so an operator that keeps the value or clears the stack fails), `Abc.MapsEveryPushFormToItsLiteralKind` (every literal push form's rendered value and `Literal` kind, so a wrong pool entry, a wrong `AbcValueKind` or a mis-sign-extended immediate fails) and `Abc.SummaryAnswersExternalInterfaceAndEventListenerQuestions` (the two existing tooling cases re-asserted through the slot mapping).

## Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:simulate_arguments

`Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:simulate_arguments` marks branch targets in a `std::vector<bool>` indexed with byte offsets, the same units as `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/opcodes.hpp:AbcInstruction::offset` and `AbcDecodedOperand::target`, but the vector was sized `code.size() + 1`, and `code.size()` is the number of instructions, not the byte length of the body. For any body whose byte offsets reach the instruction count — every body with multi-byte instructions, so every real one — `mark_offset` silently dropped branch targets past that limit and `targets[instruction.offset]` read past the end of the vector, undefined behaviour; the "branch target clears the stack" rule described above therefore never ran, and a call after a join could attribute the fall-through value as its receiver. The vector is now sized from the decoded byte extent, `code.back().offset + code.back().length + 1`, which covers every instruction offset and the one-past-the-end target `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code` accepts; `mark_offset` keeps its bounds check and the read is bounds-checked as well. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_summary.cpp:Abc.LeavesBranchJoinedArgumentUnknown` also covers a join with no `jump` before it (`getlex X; ifeq L; getlex Y; L: pushstring "a"; callpropvoid foo 1`), where removing the target-clearing block makes the receiver `Y` again while the first scenario's `jump` would still have cleared the stack and hidden the defect.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:check_pool_indices

`Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::check_pool_indices` is the one structural pass `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:AbcFile::parse` runs after the walk, where a narrower pass used to re-check trait metadata only. Every structural reference it covers is resolved against the pool it indexes, index 0 is the "none" sentinel and is accepted even when its pool has count 0 (see below), and every other index at or past that pool's size is `AbcStatus::IndexOutOfRange` — the typed error `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:validate_operand_pools` gives an operand — instead of the empty name or lookup miss the bounds-checked accessors return; the only pool reference it leaves alone is `namespace.name`, so a stale one is still a lookup miss rather than a typed error. Nothing about the file layout changed: the accessors stay bounds-checked, the decoder stays read-only and no C ABI moved.

- Which pool each field indexes: `instance.name`, `instance.super_index`, `instance.interfaces`, `trait.name`, `trait.type_name` (Slot and Const), `method.return_type`, `method.param_types` and `exception.exc_type` index the multinames pool; `instance.iinit`, `class.cinit`, `script.init`, `body.method` and `trait.method_index` (Method, Getter, Setter) index `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::methods`; `instance.protected_ns` indexes the namespaces pool; `exception.var_name` indexes the strings pool or the multinames pool, see below; trait metadata indexes `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::metadata`; `method.name`, `method.param_names` and metadata `name` with each item's key and value index the strings pool; `trait.value_index` and `method.options[].index` index the pool their value kind selects — strings for `Utf8`, ints for `Int`, uints for `UInt`, doubles for `Double`, namespaces for the seven namespace kinds, and no pool at all for `Undefined`, `True`, `False` and `Null` — the same mapping `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:AbcFile::optional_value_at` applies. avmplus checks the same set in `core/AbcParser.cpp` and `core/Verifier.cpp`: `resolveBindingName` for a class name, `resolveTypeName` for the super and the interfaces, `resolveMethodInfo` for `iinit`, `cinit`, a script init and a Method/Getter/Setter trait, `parseNsRef` for the protected namespace, `class_index >= classCount` for a Class trait, and `pool->getString` for metadata names, keys and values.
- A Class trait's second field is a class index but a Function trait's is a method index, so `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcTrait::class_index` is checked against `AbcFile::instances` for `AbcTraitKind::Class` and against `AbcFile::methods` for `AbcTraitKind::Function`. RABCDAsm `abcfile.d` splits them the same way, reading `r.Class.classi` and `r.Function.functioni`, and `Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:put_instance_traits` pins the difference: its Class trait carries 0, valid against one class, while its Function trait carries 2, valid against three methods and out of range against one class. avmplus is no help on that arm — `parseTraits` throws `kUnsupportedTraitsKindError` for a Function trait — so RABCDAsm is the only reference for the field.
- Index 0 is the "none" sentinel for every structural pool reference and stays valid even when its pool has count 0: `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp` builds each pool with `assign(count, ...)`, so an empty pool's `size()` is 0 and a strict `>=` check would reject index 0. The zero-sentinel fields are `instance.protected_ns` (0 is `AnyNamespace`; avmplus `parseNsRef` returns null for it), `exception.exc_type` (0 is a catch-all; avmplus calls `checkTypeName` only when the index is non-zero), `exception.var_name` (0 is no name; avmplus reads it only when non-zero), `method.name`, every `method.param_names` entry, metadata `name` with each item's key and value, `trait.value_index` (`Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:detail::parse_traits` reads its kind byte only when the index is non-zero) and `method.options[].index` for every value kind. An option's kind byte is always present and pool index 0 is not guaranteed to exist, so `method.options[].index` accepts 0 regardless of kind rather than assuming a reserved entry; avmplus `core/AbcParser.cpp` skips the index and kind bytes without range-checking either. Every non-zero index is still resolved with `>=` against the pool its kind names, and a kind that names no pool (`Undefined`, `True`, `False`, `Null`) accepts any index.
- `exception.var_name` is checked against either the strings pool or the multinames pool, because the documentation and the reference disagree about which one it is. The ABC documentation calls it a string index; avmplus `Verifier.cpp` parses the field with `parseMultiname` and says so in a comment — "abc docs specify that the name is a string but asc generates QNames" — and validates it against `pool->cpool_mn_offsets.length()` (`AbcParser.cpp`). The corpus measured here agrees with avmplus: in the 670 ABC files extracted from the shipped `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2`, all 245 non-zero `var_name` values are `0x07` QName multiname indices that resolve to `::e`, while reading the same numbers as string indices yields unrelated identifiers such as `htmlText` and `PlayReverseCallback`. Neither pool is reliably the larger one — the strings pool is larger in 669 of the 670 files, and `Interface_Pipboy_MapPage.swf.0.abc` holds 1497 multinames against 1471 strings — so a check on either pool alone is wrong in one direction: strings-only rejects the multiname indices 1471-1496 of that file, and multinames-only accepts a `var_name` past the end of the multiname pool. The check therefore rejects a non-zero `var_name` only when it is past the end of both pools. The synthetic fixture keeps writing the field as a string index (`Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:kStringHelper`), which an accept-either check keeps valid, and `Radicle/tests/test_abc.cpp` still reads it back through `string_at`.
- One field that looks like a pool index must not be checked like one. `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcTrait::disp_id` is a dispatch id: avmplus reads it as `earlyDispId` and never resolves it, and nothing in the format ties it to a pool.
- Left unchecked on purpose: `namespace.name`, a string index read by `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:parse_namespace_pool`. A stale one is a lookup miss through the bounds-checked accessors rather than a typed error; it sits in the constant-pool walk rather than in the file-level pass.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN entry arrays and region points (#602 C-33)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN` gains the four rows the record still lacked after the entry and authoring block, all `insertion: existing_only`: `REGN\Icon` (`ICON`, a plain `zstring`, xEdit `wbICON` used at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11897`), `REGN\SoundFlags` (`RDSA`, `u32` flags at `offset` 4 with `stride` 12, the four `wbFlags` names of `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9176-9181`), `REGN\SoundChance` (`RDSA`, `f32` at 8, stride 12) and `REGN\WeatherChance` (`RDWT`, `u32` at 4, stride 12; xEdit's `wbInteger('Chance', itU32)` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11952`).
- `RPLD` deliberately keeps no row: it repeats once per region area and a strided row cannot also be `repeated`. `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:parse_address` rejects `repeated` together with `stride` (line 90) because the two describe different shapes, one subrecord of N elements against N subrecords, and `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` starts a new area on every `RPLI` and appends that area's points from the `RPLD` that follows, so a multi-area `REGN` carries several `RPLD` subrecords. A strided row without `repeated` would make each of them a duplicate: `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` (lines 71-82) sets `duplicate` whenever one candidate scope holds the subrecord more than once, and a record with no scope handler has a single scope over all of its occurrences, `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots` (called from `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar`, line 176) then throws `schema::ScalarError` and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` reports an error `duplicate_scalar_subrecord` on a record that is valid. Region points stay with `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:read_points`, which walks the same 8-byte stride per `RPLD` occurrence.
- Shape: `RDSA` and `RDWT` are one subrecord holding N fixed-size structs, not N subrecords, so the rows use `offset` plus `stride` and no `repeated` flag (`RPLD` has the same shape and no row, above). `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:parse_address` rejects `repeated` together with `stride`, and `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` walks `(size - array_offset) / stride` elements and gives each element one slot at `element * stride + shape.offset`. A payload whose size is not a multiple of the stride is `misaligned` and yields no slot at all, so `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` returns `ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` and nothing is written. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_slot_bytes` hands `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:decode_scalar` only the addressed member, which is why three rows can share one `RDWT` and three more one `RDSA`. Precedent: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\MorphGroupSliders` (`stride` 4) and the LVLI `LLKC` element rows.
- FormLink rows: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN\Object` (`RDOT`, stride 52, `TREE FLOR STAT LTEX MSTT SCOL`), `REGN\Grass` (`RDGS`, stride 8, `GRAS`), `REGN\Weather` (`RDWT`, stride 12, `WTHR`), `REGN\WeatherGlobal` (`RDWT`, `offset` 8, stride 12, `GLOB`, `nullable: true` because xEdit lists NULL) and `REGN\Sound` (`RDSA`, stride 12, `SNDR SOUN`, `nullable: true`). None carries `payload_sizes`: the element count varies, and a declared size would be read as "the whole subrecord is exactly this long" by `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records_real.cpp:RowsDecodeAndAuthoringLimitsHold`. `Radicle/tests/test_form_link_schema_remap.cpp:row_subrecords` rounds its synthetic payload up to a whole stride, so each new row is exercised on one element.
- xEdit layout: `wbRegionAreas` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9151-9166`) is `RPLI` then an array of `{wbFloat X, wbFloat Y}` points; `wbRegionSounds` (`:9168-9185`) is an array of `{Sound, Flags u32, Chance f32}`; the object, grass and weather arrays are at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11909`, `:11944` and `:11950`. The strides 8, 12 and 52 match the byte counts of those structs and the strides `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp:66-69` already declares for the same subrecords.
- No double counting: `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_schema.cpp:struct_or_mixed_handler_owns` makes the `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp` struct handler win for `RDOT`, `RDGS`, `RDWT` and `RDSA`, so `schema_formlink_offsets` still reports nothing for them and `remap_record_form_links` is unchanged. The rows add the two things the struct handler cannot: a typed slot per element for `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field`, and the target lists `Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:slot_targets` answers for those offsets. `RDOT`, `RDGS`, `RDWT` and `RDSA` are in no listed-signature table, so `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:collect_form_links` never saw them and `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/unclaimed_link_allowlist.inc` needs no new entry.
- `RDOT`'s 52-byte struct is xEdit's `wbStruct('Object', ...)` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11909-11941`: the object form ID at 0, parent index u16 at 4, two unknown bytes, density f32 at 8, clustering and the two slopes, flags, two radii, five floats, the angle-variance `wbVec3` of three u16 and six trailing unknown bytes.
- Authoring is unchanged: `REGN` stays `top_level` with EDID, RCLR, WNAM, RPLI, RPLD, RDAT, RDMO, RDMP and RLDM, and none of the new rows is a rule. `RPLD` and `RPLI` repeat inside a region area, so one rule index cannot cover them, and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` skips unruled subrecords rather than reporting `subrecord_order_invalid`.
- Corpus: no official master was read for this change (the seven masters are not reachable from this worktree), so the payload widths come from xEdit and from the strides `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_records.cpp` already used.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN\WeatherChance` is `u32`, matching xEdit's `wbInteger('Chance', itU32)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11952`) and the reader that was already in place: `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:read_weathers` reads the four bytes as `u32` and `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/region.hpp:RegionWeather::chance` is `std::uint32_t`. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:validate_range` accepts values up to 4294967295 and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:parse_integer` rejects a negative with `schema::ScalarError`, so `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp:RegnRows.EntryArraysAndEntryPayloadsEditInPlace` round-trips 4000000000 and shows `-1` refused without changing the payload.
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:REGN\Object`'s six-target list is confirmed against the pinned xEdit definition: `wbFormIDCk('Object', [TREE, FLOR, STAT, LTEX, MSTT, SCOL])` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11910`, so the row's list is complete for the pinned source. Mutagen's `IRegionTarget` interface is narrower (Flora, LandscapeTexture, MovableStatic and Tree) and is not the authority here.
- Resolved risk, same class: `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidate_scopes` now returns the entry-payload subrecords `REGN\Object` (`RDOT`), `REGN\Grass` (`RDGS`), `REGN\Weather`/`REGN\WeatherGlobal` (`RDWT`) and `REGN\Sound` (`RDSA`) in one scope per `RDAT` entry, the split `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:is_entry_payload` and `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` give the typed decode: every payload subrecord belongs to the `RDAT` header that precedes it with no `RPLI` in between, and a payload subrecord that precedes the first `RDAT` belongs to no entry at all, so it stays out of every scope and gets no slot -- `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` fails such a record outright with `appears outside an open RDAT data entry`, so the rows leave a payload before the first `RDAT` unaddressable instead of folding it into a leading scope and offering a cell for it. A `REGN` that carries payload subrecords and no `RDAT` at all is the other half of that rule: `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:entry_payload_scopes` keeps every occurrence in one scope when it saw no `RDAT`, so the raw-scan behaviour holds there -- one payload still yields its single cell, and two or more still yield the `duplicate` flag from `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` plus the `duplicate_scalar_subrecord` error from `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record`, which is what `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` does to the record as well. `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidate_scopes` tests the signature with `Radicle/include/fo4/signature.hpp:Signature::view` rather than `Signature::to_string`, which allocated a `std::string` on every `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` call. `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` raises `duplicate` only when one scope holds more than one candidate (its `several_in_one_scope` flag) instead of whenever the record holds more than one `RDOT`/`RDGS`/`RDWT`/`RDSA`, so a `REGN` with two `RDAT` entries of one type and a payload subrecord each exposes one slot per entry and per element -- `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_scalar` and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field` address them by slot index, and `Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:slot_targets` keeps its target list -- while two payload subrecords inside one entry still fail closed through the same `duplicate` flag (`Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots`, `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots`, `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record`). `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidates` is unchanged for its existing callers: it flattens the scopes and every other record still yields exactly one scope, so `LENS` `DNAM`, `SCCO` `XNAM`, `PERK` `DATA` and `PACK` `CNAM`/`QNAM`/`INAM` keep their duplicate behaviour. The four signatures are the ones the strided non-`repeated` rows address; `RDMO` and `RDMP` are deliberately out of the scope list because their rows are `repeated` (or a localized string) and never reach the duplicate branch. Whether any real record has the two-entry shape is still unchecked here (no official master was read for this change). Divergence: for `RDAT`, `RPLI`, payload, `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:entry_payload_scopes` resets its scope only on `RDAT`, so it still addresses that payload under the earlier entry, while `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` refuses the whole record ("appears outside an open RDAT data entry"); the "every payload belongs to the `RDAT` that precedes it" rule above therefore no longer holds for this shape. `behavior_layout.cpp` is deliberately unchanged. Corpus: 0 of the 153 shipped `REGN` records in the seven official masters (2026-10-20) has an `RPLI` after an `RDAT`, so the divergence is unreachable on shipped data.
- `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidate_scopes` and `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidates` take the row's `repeated` flag from `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` and hand it to `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:flat_field_candidates`, so the `LENS` `DNAM` `before_marker`/`after_marker` split, the `SCCO` `XNAM` boundary, the `QUST` `NNAM` `outside_objective_array` scan, the `RACE` `MPGS` `first_occurrence` pick and the `PERK`/`PACK` branches keep the behaviour they had before the entry scopes were added; the `REGN` entry path ignores the flag because every payload row is per entry and non-repeated.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp:RegnRows.EntryArraysAndEntryPayloadsEditInPlace` builds one `REGN` with two `RDAT` entries of the Objects type (the first entry's `RDWT` holds two 12-byte elements, the second entry one), asserts the row descriptors and the 1/1/2/3/3/3 counts for `REGN\Grass`, `REGN\SoundChance`, `REGN\Object`, `REGN\WeatherChance`, `REGN\Weather` and `REGN\WeatherGlobal` through `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots`, and sees no `duplicate_scalar_subrecord` from `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_plugin`. It writes `REGN\WeatherChance` slot 0 to `4000000000` (above 2147483647, which pins the `u32` storage), refuses `-1` with `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError`, writes slots 1 and 2 to 250, gets `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` for slot 3, and compares both `RDWT` payloads, `RDSA`, `RPLD` and the first entry's `RDOT` byte for byte after a save and reload. Before the entry-scope fix the same record threw `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` out of `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:scalar_slots`, so the counts and the preflight loop are the regression.
- `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp:RegnRows.RefusesTwoPayloadsInsideOneEntry` pins the fail-closed half: one `RDAT` entry holding two `RDWT` subrecords still reports exactly one `duplicate_scalar_subrecord` on `REGN\WeatherChance` (the only scalar row over `RDWT`; `REGN\Weather` and `REGN\WeatherGlobal` are FormLink rows and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` walks scalar rows only), while `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_scalar` throws `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field` throws `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:FormLinkFieldError`.
- `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp:RegnRows.PayloadBeforeTheFirstDataHeaderGetsNoSlot` is the leading-payload case: a `REGN` whose only `RDAT` sits between two `RDWT` subrecords exposes one `REGN\WeatherChance` and one `REGN\Weather` slot through `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:entry_payload_scopes`, slot 0 writes the entry payload while the stray `RDWT` bytes stay untouched, and slot 1 returns `subrecord_missing`. The typed half of that parity is pinned by `Radicle/tests/test_environment_region.cpp:RegionEnvironmentTest.RejectsMalformedTypedRegionPayloads` on record `000E09` (a `REGN` whose `RDGS` has no `RDAT` before it), which `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` fails with `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/world.hpp:WorldDecodeError`.
- `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp:RegnRows.PayloadsWithoutAnyDataHeaderStillFailClosed` is the no-header case: a `REGN` holding two `RDWT` subrecords and no `RDAT` still reports exactly one `duplicate_scalar_subrecord` on `REGN\WeatherChance` and still throws out of `fo4::record_field_count`, `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_scalar` and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field`, because `Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:entry_payload_scopes` keeps every occurrence in one raw-scan scope when it saw no `RDAT`; before that fallback the record produced no scope at all and was silent, with no slot, no preflight issue and a zero count.
- `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp:RegnRows.RefusesEntryArrayRowsOnAMisalignedPayload` is the malformed-payload case: a 13-byte `RDWT` and an 11-byte `RDSA` inside one `RDAT` entry expose no slot, `record_field_count` is 0, the scalar and FormLink writes return `subrecord_missing` and the `RDWT` bytes are untouched.
- Split: the two typed `Radicle/src/environment/region.cpp:decode_region` tests moved out of `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp` into `Radicle/tests/test_environment_region.cpp` as `RegionEnvironmentTest.DecodesTypedRegionAreasEntriesAndPayloads` and `RegionEnvironmentTest.RejectsMalformedTypedRegionPayloads`, each file carrying its own copies of the byte builders, so the row suite stays inside the 750-line guard; `Radicle/tests/test_regn_rows.cpp` keeps the `RegnRows` schema-row tests and `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt` lists the new file next to the other `Radicle/tests/test_environment_*.cpp` sources.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE skeletal model rows (#602 C-26 C-27)

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE` gains `RACE\SkeletalModelPath` (`ANAM`, `kind: string`, `repeated: true`), one of the members of the `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11195-11202` span that had no row. xEdit writes the male and female skeletal model as two `wbString(ANAM, ...)` calls at `:11196` and `:11199` under the empty `wbEmpty(MNAM, 'Male Marker')` and `wbEmpty(FNAM, 'Female Marker')` markers. The third argument of `wbString` is `TwbStringDef`'s display size (`Core/wbInterface.pas:7644-7651`), not a fixed payload width, so both ANAM subrecords hold ordinary NUL-terminated strings.
- Shape: one row per occurrence in record order, the same shape `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE` already uses for `RACE\WrinkleMapPath` (`WMAP`, two occurrences) and `RACE\MorphGroupNames` (`MPGN`). `ANAM` is already a deliberate non-form-ID slot for `RACE` in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/non_formid_slots.inc`, and `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` allows a `repeated` row to have several occurrences of its subrecord, so the two `ANAM` subrecords become slots 0 and 1 rather than a `duplicate`.
- The empty `MNAM` and `FNAM` markers stay unrowed: they are `wbEmpty` calls with no bytes to address. `MODT` stays unrowed as well, because `wbModelInfo(MODT)` is a struct shared by both genders whose members Radicle does not address yet.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_race_link_rows.cpp:RaceScalarRows.SkeletalModelPathsEditInPlace` builds a synthetic `RACE` with two `ANAM` strings, checks the row is `zstring` and `repeated`, counts two slots, reads both back, rewrites the female skeletal model, and shows a third `ANAM` write returns `ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` with the string list unchanged. Not compiled in this lane (no C++ builds).

## Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py:render — Radicle-only rows (#602)

- `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py:render` prints one row per signature from `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` and never reads an xEdit member list. The generated table has no `radicle_only` column, and the tool's own opaque note says so: "Row counts are not compared with xEdit members. The script does not enumerate xEdit members, so unlisted members, enums, flags and structs are not attributed" (`Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py`, `OPAQUE_NOTES`, printed at the end of the block in `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md`). No macro table exists in the tool or in any branch of this repository: the string appears nowhere in the tree except this note, and the one pickaxe hit for it is the commit that added this sentence (`998605a0`), so there was no tool-reported Radicle-only row and no unexpanded-macro false positive to correct. The pinned definitions are not vendored either: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/xedit_signatures.txt` carries only each signature and its registration line, so a per-record member comparison cannot be reproduced from the repository alone.
- Audit (2026-10-19) against the pinned TES5Edit tree (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas`, `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas`, `Core/wbDefinitionsSignatures.pas` @93cc0bc5): every subrecord named by a `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` row, `authoring` entry or `localized_subrecords` entry was compared with its record's xEdit block, expanding the helpers the block calls (functions, procedures and `var X :=` aliases) and keeping each call's arguments. Counting rule: the subrecord signatures named by each record's `fields` rows (each row's own `subrecord` key), `authoring.subrecords`, `localized_subrecords`, `formlink_fields`, `formlink_lists` and `nested_formlink_lists` entries, which is 446 distinct signatures over 1942 (record, subrecord) pairs across the 145 records; a struct row's nested `members` are offsets inside the subrecord it names and are not counted separately (`LENS\Sprites`'s `LFSD` is the only member that names a subrecord of its own; counting it gives 447). All 446 exist in the pinned sources, and 17 records have an item their own block does not name. Each of the 17 is the mechanism xEdit uses instead of a literal member:

  | Record(s) | Items | xEdit mechanism | Status |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | PARW, PBAR, PBEA, PCON, PFLA, PGRE, PHZD, PMIS | DATA, EDID, NAME, VMAD, XAMC, XASP, XEMI, XESP, XEZN, XFVC, XHLT, XHTW, XLYR, XMSP, XOWN, XPWR, XRFG, XRNK, XSCL | `ReferenceRecord(PGRE, 'Placed Projectile');` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5944-5955`) calls `procedure ReferenceRecord` at `:3200`, which emits `wbRefRecord(...)` with the full member list | legitimate |
  | WTHR | the 17 cloud-texture signatures `00TX` to `@0TX` | byte-valued signatures (`_30_0TX : TwbSignature = #$30'0TX'`, `Core/wbDefinitionsSignatures.pas:1829`) built by `wbWeatherCloudTextures` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9379`) | legitimate |
  | IMAD | `@IAD`, `AIAD` to `TIAD` (21) | byte-valued signatures `#$00'IAD'` to `#$54'IAD'` (`Core/wbDefinitionsSignatures.pas:1808-1866`) | legitimate |
  | LVLI, LVLN | LLKC | `var wbFilterKeywordChances := wbArrayS(LLKC, 'Filter Keyword Chances', ...)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:9979-9984`) | legitimate |
  | SCOL | DATA, ONAM | `var wbStaticPart := ... wbStaticPartPlacements` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12621-12624`), used by `wbRArrayS('Parts', wbStaticPart, cpNormal, True)` at `:12647` | legitimate |
  | RACE | QNAM, ZNAM | `var wbEquipSlot := wbRStruct('Equip Slot', [wbFormIDCk(QNAM, 'Equip Slot', [EQUP]), wbString(ZNAM, 'Node')])` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11032-11034`) | legitimate |
  | FACT | FNAM, INAM, MNAM, RNAM | faction rank members `wbInteger(RNAM, 'Rank#', itU32)`, `wbLString(MNAM, 'Male Title', 0, cpTranslate)` and `wbString(INAM, 'Insignia (unused)')` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6771-6776`) | legitimate |
  | BOOK | DESC | `wbDESCReq := wbLStringKC(DESC, 'Description', 0, cpTranslate, True)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3695`), used by the BOOK block at `:5900` | legitimate |
  | LVSP | FULL | xEdit's LVSP block lists EDID, OBND, LVLD, LVLM, LVLF, LLCT and the entry array and no FULL (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10033-10051`) | kept: unresolved, xEdit LVSP lists no FULL but no corpus evidence either way, removal would change write behaviour; decide with real-data proof |

- The single item with no xEdit counterpart is the `FULL` entry in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:LVSP`'s `localized_subrecords`. No LVSP field row, authoring entry, test or code note uses it, and the leveled-list name subrecord is ONAM, which LVLI keeps in its own `localized_subrecords`. History suggests it is an accident: `cec5524d` added the entry when localized string decoding was wired for `RACE`, `998605a0` dropped it and `fc65e256` restored it. It is kept: `Radicle/tools/lstring_schema_codegen.py:collect` still emits the pair into `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_lstring_fields.inc`, and the LVSP localized count in the generated table in `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` stays 1 (`Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py:render`).
- LVSP has no record in the shipped masters (`Radicle/tests/test_typed_families_real.cpp:167-169`), so there is no corpus evidence either way: dropping the entry would make a mod LVSP that carries FULL be written as inline text instead of a string ID, a write-behaviour change the xEdit block alone does not justify. The entry stays and the decision waits for real-data evidence.
- Not reproducible in CI: the comparison needs the pinned Pascal sources, which are not in this repository, so nothing was added to `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py` and the matrix keeps its opaque note. The remaining 16 records stay in the table above as legitimate rather than being removed from `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json`. The expansion is deliberately over-approximate, because a helper call keeps its argument list, so a subrecord that the record only names as a target signature counts as listed; the comparison can therefore miss a Radicle-only item and never invents one. Everything it did flag is resolved above except LVSP FULL, which is kept pending real-data proof.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN authoring, Radicle/tests/test_furn_rows.cpp:FurnRows.PropertyAndItemRunsReadWriteAndRepeatOnOneFurn (#602 FURN PRPS CNTO)

- Scope: the two row sets this lane was asked for already existed at the branch base `37041a12`, so no row was added for them; the rows this lane does add are the FURN `PRPS` authoring rule and the `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\AttachParentSlots` anchors below. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\Properties` (uncounted `counted_array` on PRPS, stride 8, member `FURN\PropertyValue` f32 at offset 4, plus the stride-8 AVIF formlink `FURN\PropertyActorValue`) and the other ten records' PRPS rows came from `65c3a04d` ("PRPS property rows (#602 WP-9)"); `FURN\ItemTotal` (COCT u32) and the `FURN\Items` subrecord group (count COCT, required CNTO member of payload 8, optional COED member of payload 12) came from `bd1017e7` ("FURN container items and marker rows (#602 B-11 B-14)"). Both are ancestors of the base, and `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py`, `record_schema_codegen.py`, `lstring_schema_codegen.py`, `formlink_schema_codegen.py`, `condition_scope_codegen.py` and `parity_matrix.py` all pass `--check` there, so those rows are generated rather than hand-written. Re-adding them would have been a duplicate row, which `65c3a04d` already had to undo once for `FURN\PropertyActorValue` (`5a90d823`).
- The gap that was left is the FURN authoring block (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN`, the `authoring.subrecords` array): it carried `COCT` with `coupled: true` and no partner, and no `CNTO`, `COED` or `PRPS`. `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_with_rules` refuses `unknown_order` when the record holds any subrecord outside the rules, and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` skips unlisted subrecords (`if (!rule_index.has_value()) continue;`), so the item run and the property list were invisible to the FURN order and cardinality check.
- Added: `CNTO` (minimum 0, maximum 65535) and `COED` (0, 65535) between `COCT` and `MNAM`, the shape `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_` already gives its `COCT`/`CNTO`/`COED` triple. Four in-repo sources agree on that position: the xEdit line numbers recorded in the FURN container items entry of this file (COCT 6882, CNTOs 6883, MNAM 6884, after CITC 6880 and the condition run at 6881); `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\Items`, whose `count_subrecord` is COCT and whose `successors` start at MNAM; the WP-7 CTDA survey in this file (`FURN (:6881, CITC :6880; COCT, CNTO, MNAM, ...)`); and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:keyword_records`, whose FURN row lists the item run between COCT and MNAM. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FURN\AttachParentSlots`' `anchor_predecessors` is only consistent with that gap and does not prove what fills it: it is a membership set whose order `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:empty_list_insertion_point` never reads, and this lane adds COED and CNTO to it so the first APPR element no longer lands inside the item run. `COCT` keeps `coupled: true`, so a bare count is still not addable on its own.
- Added too: `PRPS` (0..1, not `coupled`, no `default`) between `KWDA` and `NTRM`. The slot is measured, not guessed. A read-only scan of the seven official masters on this machine (`D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Fallout 4/Data`, the corpus the FURN container items entry counts) walked every GRUP and every FURN record: 783 FURN records and 144 PRPS subrecords (Fallout4.esm 598 records/80 PRPS, DLCRobot 11/1, DLCworkshop01 29/26, DLCCoast 32/1, DLCworkshop02 3/1, DLCworkshop03 54/28, DLCNukaWorld 56/7), no record with two PRPS, and in all 144 the subrecord immediately before PRPS is `KWDA` (with `KSIZ` before that) while the one immediately after is `PNAM` in 137, `NTRM` in 5 and `FTYP` in 2. Exactly one slot in the rule list satisfies all 144; every other placement breaks records, before `KWDA` or after `PNAM` and `NVNM` 144, between `NTRM` and `FTYP` 5, between `FTYP` and `PNAM` 7, against 0 for the chosen one under `Radicle/tests/authoring_order.hpp:authoring_order_violation`, the checker `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records_real.cpp:RowsDecodeAndAuthoringLimitsHold` runs. `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` reports 28 FURN records at the chosen slot and the same 28 at the branch base, all of them on `FURN\DSTD`, so the slot adds no new finding under either checker; those 28 are the flat-model limitation `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:local_layout_valid` and the order branch of `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp` keep on purpose, which the destructible entry above records. ## D-12 / D-13 generic override copy on the C ABI

- `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h:radicle_plugin_copy_record_override` exposes the library's `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:copy_record_as_override` to PET, which until now reached the generic override copy only from C++. It takes the destination and source `radicle_plugin` handles plus the source's `radicle_form_key`, so the copy is addressed exactly as `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:copy_record_as_override` addresses it (the key must be owned by the source plugin), and it reports `RADICLE_RECORD_COPY_INSERTED`, `RADICLE_RECORD_COPY_REPLACED` or `RADICLE_RECORD_COPY_ALREADY_EXISTS` through `out_status`.
- The export writes `destination->value` only on the three mutating outcomes: `source_missing` maps to `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` and `source_containment_unsupported` to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, so a refused copy leaves the destination handle byte-identical. The caller-visible key does not change, because `copy_record_as_override` keeps the source key rather than allocating a local one, which is what distinguishes this export from `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h:radicle_plugin_copy_record_as_new`.
- Containment beyond a cell or dialogue group is not synthesized here; `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:plan_nested_copy` decides what is reproducible and the export surfaces its refusal instead of guessing, which is the same contract the C++ callers get.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_authoring.cpp:CApiAuthoring.CopiesARecordAsAnOverrideThroughTheExport` authors an ARMO in a `Source.esp` handle, copies it into a `Target.esp` handle and pins the copied record's subrecord order in the destination's written bytes. It detects the realistic regression of a copy that lands in the wrong plugin or drops the destination write; the same test is the negative case for `already_exists` without `overwrite`, `replaced` with it, `not found` for an unowned local ID, and the three NULL-argument refusals. Not built on the authoring machine; CI is the first compiler.

## D-26 MGEF counter effects and the in-subrecord counter

- `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:FormLinkListDescriptor::counter_offset` is the second counter shape Radicle knows: a nonzero offset means the count is a u16 at that offset inside `counter`, the counter subrecord itself. xEdit declares MGEF's list as `wbRArrayS('Counter Effects', wbFormIDCk(ESCE, 'Effect', [MGEF]), cpNormal, False, nil, wbCounterEffectsAfterSet)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10204`), whose `wbCounterEffectsAfterSet` calls `wbCounterByPathAfterSet('Magic Effect Data\DATA - Data\Counter effect count', aElement)`, and the count is maintained on the container by `wbMGEFAfterSet` -> `wbCounterContainerByPathAfterSet('Magic Effect Data\DATA - Data\Counter effect count', 'Counter Effects', aElement)`; `Counter Effect Count` is member 5 of the MGEF DATA struct, a `wbInteger(..., itU16)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10110`). The DATA layout Radicle already pins confirms the offset: `Resist Value` is the form link at 16 and `Casting Light` the one at 24, so the u16 sits at 20 with the two unused bytes xEdit shows between them. (TODO-verify: citation read from a local xEdit copy, not the pinned 93cc0bc5; line numbers may differ.)
- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` MGEF now carries `MGEF\CounterEffects` (ESCE, targets MGEF, `anchor_predecessors: ["DATA"]`). The explicit anchor is what lets the first element of an empty list land directly after DATA; the derived anchors of a record with one list would otherwise be empty and `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:empty_list_insertion_point` would fail closed.
- `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:reconcile_counter` writes the u16 in place for that shape and never erases the counter subrecord, because DATA is a required member that also holds the record's form links. A count above 0xFFFF, a missing counter subrecord or one shorter than `counter_offset + 2` throws `FormLinkListError` instead of truncating or resizing, so a fail-closed edit leaves the caller's plugin untouched.
- The upkeep was missing on the per-subrecord list paths: `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:insert_encoded_element`, `remove_record_formlink_list_element`, `remove_record_formlink_list_elements_matching` and `clear_record_formlink_list` now reconcile the counter the way the packed-array paths already did. MGEF is the only per-subrecord list that declares a counter, so the added calls are inert for every other list in the table and the change cannot move existing bytes.
- Generator: `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:parse_list_counter_offset` accepts the new `counter_offset` row key, rejects it without a counter or alongside the packed-array segment keys, and emits it as the last descriptor field; `Radicle/tools/test_formlink_list_storage.py` pins both the refusal messages and the rendered row. The counter is a u16 because that is what the only such field in the schema is; a u32 in-subrecord counter would need the size as a second key.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_formlink_lists.cpp:FormLinkListMutation.MaintainsTheCounterStoredInsideAnotherSubrecord` detects the regression this row names — an insert, a removal and a clear that leave the game's count stale — by reading the u16 back out of DATA offset 20 after each edit and checking that clearing leaves DATA in place. `FormLinkListMutation.RefusesACounterSubrecordTooShortForTheCount` is the negative case and pins that the refused insert leaves the plugin's bytes unchanged. Not built on the authoring machine; CI is the first compiler.

## D-14 / D-10 deviation: the leveled lists xEdit's wrapper menu also names are not FO4 signatures

- `Radicle/src/forms/copy_as_wrapper.cpp:k_wrapper_signatures` covers LVLI, LVLN and LVSP, and `Radicle/src/plugin/maintenance.cpp:compact_to_esl` is the ESL compaction as a library call. The row asked for LVLB, LVLC, LVLP and LVSC as well, on the strength of `xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:15867`, where the CopyAsWrapper menu is visible for `LVLC`, `LVLI`, `LVSP` and `LVLN`.
