The only three FO4 leveled lists are the ones `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:is_leveled_list` accepts, so the wrapper's signature set is already complete for this game and adding the other four would create rows no FO4 record can satisfy.

## Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_kind.hpp:FieldConflict and Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:append_field_rows (#602 D-1)

- Field-level rows, the last missing level of the D-1 classification: `Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:append_field_rows` runs the same `Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:classify_nodes` the subrecord rows use, once per `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarFieldDescriptor` row of the record signature, and appends a `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_kind.hpp:FieldConflict` per row that at least one version defines. `RecordConflict::fields` is that list, beside `RecordConflict::subrecords`.
- `Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:field_value` reads a version's bytes for one row through `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/field_address.hpp:resolve_field_slots` plus `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:scalar_slot_bytes`, so a row obeys the schema's offsets, form-version gates and repeated-array stride; a row whose subrecord is absent in a version contributes no value (an unassigned node), and a duplicate, malformed or misaligned subrecord, or a `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError`, makes the whole row unassigned rather than guessed at. A repeated row (for example `MISC\DestructionStageHealthPercent` over several DSTD subrecords) compares the concatenation of all its slots in order, one row for the array rather than one per element, which is the one place this level is coarser than xEdit's element tree.
- Rows are limited to `schema::scalar_fields`, which also carries the members of counted arrays and subrecord groups (`Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py` expands them into the scalar list), so a member row such as `MISC\DestructionResistanceValue` appears only when its DAMC subrecord is present. String, formlink, nested-list and localized elements have no row here: they are the subrecord row's business.
- The row's priority is its subrecord's `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_kind.hpp:ConflictPriorityRule`, since the rule list is keyed by (record, subrecord) and the schema carries no per-element marks yet; `ConflictPriority::ignore` on the subrecord drops its field rows too, matching the subrecord row and `record_value`.

## Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:record_is_injected (#602 D-1 D-8)

- `Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:record_is_injected` is the xEdit injected-record predicate of `Core/wbImplementation.pas:11985` (`TwbMainRecord.GetIsInjected`) in the terms the conflict graph already has: the plugin the key's form ID names is loaded, that plugin holds no record with the key, and at least one version's stored bytes claim that owner. The last condition is what separates an injected record from a normal override, exactly as `Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:check_injected_records` does it for the D-7 finding; a key whose owner is not loaded stays alone (a missing master, not a proven injection).
- `Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:element_priority` applies xEdit's promotion `if aInjected and (Priority >= cpNormal) then Priority := cpCritical` (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2596`) to the record row, every subrecord row and every field row, and `Radicle/src/graph/conflict_kind.cpp:classify_record_conflict` suppresses it for GMST and DFOB, which the two call sites in the pinned `xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2419` and `:17263` exclude by name. A caller priority below `ConflictPriority::normal` is left alone, matching `>= cpNormal`.
- A record with a single version stays `only_one`: xEdit's `lNodeCount = 1` branch (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:2534-2544`) returns `caOnlyOne` without consulting the priority, so the promotion cannot turn a lone injected record into `critical` on its own. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_conflict_kind.cpp:ConflictKind.AnInjectedRecordIsPromotedToCritical` (two plugins carry `000900:Master.esm` while Master.esm has no `000900`: `critical` with roles master, wins) and `Radicle/tests/test_conflict_kind.cpp:ConflictKind.ARecordItsOwnerDefinesIsNotInjected` (the same shape with the owner defining `000900`: `override_`, so the promotion, not the difference, is what raises the category).

## Radicle/src/c_api_conflict.cpp:radicle_env_classify_conflicts (#602 D-1)

- The C ABI export for the D-1 classification: one tab-separated row per element, `record, level, path, category, roles`, where level is `record`, `subrecord` or `field`, the path is the subrecord signature or the schema field path (empty at record level) and roles are comma-separated, one per plugin in load order. `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_kind.hpp:conflict_category_name` and `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_kind.hpp:conflict_role_name` are the canonical spellings, so the library and the ABI cannot drift.
- The export classifies the whole load order of the `radicle_env` with no caller priorities (`Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_kind.hpp:ConflictPriorityRule` is caller data and has no ABI surface yet), builds its own `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/conflict_graph.hpp:ConflictGraph` because the environment's cached graph lives behind `Radicle/src/c_api_env.cpp:reference_graph`, and frees through `radicle_free_string_array` like `radicle_env_check_errors`.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_conflict.cpp:CApiConflict.ClassifiesRecordSubrecordAndFieldRows` (a base and one override with a changed DEST health: the record row, the DEST and EDID subrecord rows and the `MISC\DestructionHealth` and `MISC\DestructionStageCount` field rows are asserted literally, the DAMC member row is asserted absent, and the three null-argument refusals) and `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_conflict.cpp:CApiConflict.ARecordOnePluginDefinesIsOnlyOne` (six rows, record and field at `only_one`).

## Radicle/include/fo4/patch/list_merge.hpp:build_list_merge_patch (#602 D-32)

- List merging, the second half of D-32 beside `Radicle/include/fo4/patch/delta_patch.hpp:build_delta_patch`: the library form of xEdit's "Create Merged Patch" (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:3858` `mniNavCreateMergedPatchClick`, the per-group worker at `:3929` and its FO4 call sites at `:4140-4148`). One call covers one signature and returns the patch plugin plus `Radicle/include/fo4/patch/list_merge.hpp:ListMergeCounts`; the caller writes it with `fo4::write_plugin_file`.
- Signatures: LVLI, LVLN and LVSP through `Radicle/include/fo4/forms/leveled_list.hpp:decode_leveled_list` and `:replace_leveled_list_entries`, and FLST through the `FLST\Items` row of `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:formlink_list_descriptor` with `:record_formlink_list_values`, `:clear_record_formlink_list` and `:insert_record_formlink_list_element`. Any other signature is refused with `Radicle/include/fo4/patch/list_merge.hpp:ListMergeError`, which is where xEdit's remaining groups (CONT, FACT, RACE, CREA, NPC_, ALCH, ARMO at `xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:4144-4160`) would land.
- A record is merged only when at least two plugins hold it (`Master.OverrideCount < 2` skips it in xEdit), and the patch receives the winning record copied by `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:copy_record_as_override` with its list replaced. `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:build_list_merge_patch` writes nothing for a record whose winner already holds the merged list, which is what `ListMergeCounts::unchanged` counts.
- `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:master_file_holder` is the xEdit `MainRecord.MasterRecordsFromMasterFilesAndSelf` step: the list an override is compared against is the one in the nearest earlier plugin that the override's own plugin lists as a master, not the previous override in load order. That difference is the whole point of a merged patch -- a later plugin that drops an entry relative to its master does not remove an entry an unrelated earlier plugin added -- and a version with no master-file holder contributes nothing, as xEdit's `Continue` does.
- `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:merge_leveled_entries` is `UpdateTargetList` (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:3871-3910`) reworked per item. xEdit keys its lists on `DisplaySortKey[True]` (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:3954`), the extended key of `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8791` (`wbStructExSK(LVLO, [0, 2], [3], ...)`), so its identity is (Level, referenced form, Count): a changed Count reads as a drop plus an add, and a second override that changes the same item's Count leaves a second row beside the first. Radicle keys on (Level, referenced form) through `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:same_leveled_item`. `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:entries_of_item` collects an item's copies from the holder and from the override; where the two multisets differ, the target's rows for that item are replaced by the override's, at the first replaced position (appended when the target has none). An override that keeps one of seven copies therefore removes six, which a set walk cannot express, and a later override's Count replaces an earlier one, a deliberate deviation from xEdit's two rows. An item the override holds exactly as its holder did keeps the target's rows, so a later override identical to its master does not undo an earlier override's change. The pass visits each item once per entry of both lists and rescans them, O(n^2) in list length, which is acceptable for LVLO sizes; a grouped map is the upgrade if a list outgrows it.
- `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:merge_form_list` is the same shape for the FLST set (`aAsSet` at `xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:4147`) and keeps the load order rather than sorting: keys the override drops are erased from the target, keys it adds are appended unless the target already holds them, so the written list is the first version's order followed by the appended keys (`000801:Master.esm`, then `000803:First.esp`). A sort on `FormKey`'s `operator<` (owner filename, then local id) would put First.esp first. The entries are written back through `clear_record_formlink_list` plus one insert each, because FLST's LNAM is one subrecord per element.
- `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:add_entry_masters` is the master-table upkeep a merged list needs and the winner's own copy cannot supply: `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:copy_record_as_override` adds masters only for the links of the record it copies, so an entry contributed by an unrelated earlier plugin -- or any entry the winner's own links do not name -- would reach `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:encode_form_key` (or the FLST path's `encode_plugin_form_id`) with no prefix to encode it and throw `FormIdError`. `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:entry_owners` therefore collects the owner of every merged entry's item and the owner `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:encode_coed` re-encodes out of `LeveledListEntry::extra` (`LeveledListExtraData::owner`), because a COED owner can be the only reference a merged entry makes to its plugin. The owners are appended to the patch's table, which is then sorted into environment load order by `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/writer.hpp:sort_plugin_masters` over the load order `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:master_load_order` extends with every master the environment does not carry (`sort_plugin_masters` throws `FormIdError` for a master missing from the load order, so the raw environment order cannot be passed). Appending and sorting replaces the earlier position scan, which inserted before the first existing master with a greater environment index and was therefore only correct when the table it inserted into was already in load order; `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:copy_record_as_override` builds that table from a `std::set<PluginKey>` iterated in folded-filename order, which is not load order, so a winner linking `First.esp` and `Master.esm` reached `remap_plugin_masters` with `[First.esp, Master.esm]`. The kind is `Radicle/include/fo4/environment/environment.hpp:PluginInfo::kind` for a loaded owner; an owner that is not loaded takes the kind the first merged version that lists it as a master records -- `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:add_entry_masters` passes the whole version span, not just the winner, because a merged entry can come from any of them -- and `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:owner_kind` throws `Radicle/include/fo4/patch/list_merge.hpp:ListMergeError` only when no merged version carries it, instead of guessing from `PluginKey::looks_light` -- which only recognises the `.esl` extension, so a small-file-flagged `.esp` owner was recorded as full and the form-ID encoder masked its local ids with `0x00FFFFFF` rather than `0x0FFF`. The patch is re-encoded through `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/writer.hpp:remap_plugin_masters` before the list is written, and both remaps receive `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:environment_type_lookup` as their `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/form_links.hpp:FormLinkTypeLookup`, so a COED owner that lives in a master of the load order -- never in the patch -- can still be typed. The order matters: `replace_leveled_list_entries` and `write_form_list` encode against the table as it stands, so the remap has to happen first, and it also re-encodes the records already in the patch, which is why LVLO's item slot and FLST's LNAM are covered by `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:remap_form_links` (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/structured_formids.inc` carries LVLO at offset 4, and LNAM is a listed link subrecord). Each added master re-encodes the whole patch and the sort is a second such pass whenever the table moved, so a load order that merges many records pays one copy per record -- the same shape `copy_record_as_override` already has per copied record, and not worth a deferred remap until a merged patch of that size is measured.
- TODO-verify: `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:encode_coed` writes a COED union dword back verbatim, while `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:visit_coed_formids` treats it as a FormID when the owner is `NPC_`. A merged entry therefore carries the union in the encoding of the plugin it was decoded from, which equals the patch's encoding exactly when the union's target plugin sits at the same master index in both; the load-order sort makes that the common case but does not guarantee it, and nothing here tracks the contributing plugin per entry to remap it. Whether a shipped COED union ever points outside its own plugin's index space is unmeasured (the decode note above marks the union's meaning TODO-verify), so the merge passes it through rather than guessing.
- `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:same_leveled_multiset` compares the merged LVL entries with the winner's as a multiset of whole entries, COED included, and the `std::is_permutation` over the FLST keys in `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:build_list_merge_patch` does the same for FLST, so a winner that already holds the merged rows in any stored order writes no record. The COED comparison is new: an earlier override's COED on an item the winner left as its master had is now written, where the (level, item, count) comparison dropped it. The FLST comparison stays order-insensitive, so a winner that only reorders a FormList is not written even though the merged list keeps load order; an ordered comparison is an open choice.
- The FLST write path encodes through `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp`'s own `encode_plugin_form_id` call, so it reports `Radicle/include/fo4/formid.hpp:FormIdError` and not `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:FormLinkListError`; `Radicle/src/c_api_patch.cpp:radicle_env_build_list_merge_patch` catches it as `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` beside the other two, so a refused merge is an argument error at the ABI rather than the generic failure the outer `guarded` reports.
- Deviation: xEdit compares the lists as text of `DisplaySortKey[True]` and keeps the target list in that string order, while Radicle compares decoded entries and FormKeys and lets `Radicle/src/forms/leveled_list.cpp:sorted_entries` re-sort the written LVLO run; the written list is therefore the same set in the game's sort order rather than xEdit's string order.
- Not covered, and still open on #86: the `.esu` delta extension and `fsIsDeltaPatch` loader mode, the script host (`xEdit/xeMainForm.pas:9164`), the count-subrecord update for the other groups (LLCT is maintained by `replace_leveled_list_entries`) and the ordered-list (`OrderedList` EditorID) case, which needs the winning plugin's EditorID convention.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_list_merge.cpp` (`ListMerge`): three plugins over one LVLI where the winner drops an entry relative to the master but an unrelated earlier plugin added it -- the patch keeps both surviving entries with exact level, local form id, count and owner, the master table is asserted to be Master.esm followed by First.esp (the owner of the kept entry, not a master of the winner), and the patch bytes are written and read back; a load order whose winner already holds the merged list writes no record at all; `ListMerge.AMultisetRemovalDropsOnlyTheCopiesTheOverrideDrops` (a master with three copies of one item, a First.esp override that keeps one, and a Second.esp winner identical to the master) asserts the rows (1, 000800), (2, 000801), (3, 000803), which the set-based walk fails with five rows; `ListMerge.ALaterOverrideWinsAConflictingCountOfOneItem` (First.esp, Second.esp and Third.esp give one item the counts 2, 3 and 1 over Master.esm) asserts one row with count 3, which the set-based walk fails with two rows; `TheMergedPatchMasterTableIsInLoadOrder` adds a fourth plugin whose winner links First.esp and Master.esm, so `copy_record_as_override` alone leaves the table `[First.esp, Master.esm, Second.esp]`, and asserts `[Master.esm, First.esp, Second.esp]`, which fails if the load-order sort is dropped; `AMergedEntryKeepsItsCoedOwnerAsAMaster` merges an entry whose COED names `000805:First.esp` while every item it carries belongs to Master.esm, so First.esp reaches the table only through `entry_owners` and `encode_coed` throws without it; `ACoedOwnerIsTypedFromTheLoadOrder` gives the winner a COED whose owner is an `NPC_` record in a loaded master and a nonzero union, so `copy_record_as_override` and `remap_plugin_masters` both have to type that owner from the environment -- with a plugin-scoped type source the whole merge is refused instead of writing; `ASecondMergedRecordKeepsTheOwnerTypesOfTheFirst` merges two LVLI records over four plugins so that the second copy -- the winner `Third.esp` links `000802:First.esp`, an owner the patch does not carry yet -- adds `First.esp` to a patch that already holds the first record's COED, which is refused unless `Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:copy_record_as_override` hands its lookup to the master remap as well as the record remap; `AnOwnerOutsideTheLoadOrderIsTypedFromTheVersionThatCarriesIt` merges an entry owned by `Missing.esm`, which no loaded plugin carries but `First.esp` lists as a master, so `Radicle/src/patch/list_merge.cpp:owner_kind` has to search every merged version instead of the winner alone; an FLST merge asserts the load-order union (`000801:Master.esm`, then `000803:First.esp`, which a sort would reverse), the same two masters and the write/reload round trip; MISC is refused as `ListMergeError`. `Radicle/src/c_api_patch.cpp:radicle_env_build_list_merge_patch` exposes the same call with the signature and patch name as strings, and `Radicle/tests/test_delta_patch.cpp` (`DeltaPatchCApi`) covers it beside the delta patch export: `ListMergeWritesAPatchAndCountsTheMergedLists` merges an LVLI over three plugins -- the winner keeps an entry owned by itself and drops one its master holds, while the middle plugin contributes an entry of its own -- and asserts `merged`/`unchanged` plus the record in the written patch, which detects a merge that loses the entry owner's master and throws instead of writing; two plugins cannot carry that assertion, because a winner whose master-file holder is the version directly before it always reproduces its own list, so `merged` stays 0 and nothing is written; `ListMergeRefusesBadArgumentsAndZeroesTheCounts` is the negative case for the five NULL arguments, a signature that is not four characters, the unsupported signature, the counts zeroed by a refused call and the absent output file. `Radicle/tests/test_leveled_list_real.cpp:LeveledListMergeReal.Lvli210B67MergesToTheThreeRowsOfItsNukaWorldWinner` (skipped without `FO4_DATA_DIR`) merges `Fallout4.esm` with `DLCNukaWorld.esm`, the only two official masters that define `0x210B67` (a read-only scan found Fallout4 with eight rows, seven of them `0x1DF283`, and NukaWorld with three), and asserts that the winner has three rows and that no patch record is written for it; ## Radicle/src/plugin/mutation.cpp:copy_record_as_override

- The caller's `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/form_links.hpp:FormLinkTypeLookup` reaches both remaps, not only the record one. The master-table remap re-encodes the records already in the destination, so it re-walks their `COED` subrecords through `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:visit_coed_formids`; with an empty lookup `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/writer.hpp:remap_plugin_masters` falls back to the patch-scoped `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/form_links.hpp:plugin_type_lookup`, which cannot type a COED owner that lives in a master and never in the patch. A later copy that adds a master therefore threw `FormIdError` ("cannot safely remap COED union: owner type unknown"), which `Radicle/src/c_api_patch.cpp:radicle_env_build_list_merge_patch` reported as `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` for the whole merge. An empty lookup still falls back to the patch, so the `PluginEditTool/native` copy paths keep their old behaviour. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_list_merge.cpp` `ListMerge.ASecondMergedRecordKeepsTheOwnerTypesOfTheFirst`. `Radicle/src/forms/placed_reference_copy.cpp:copy_record_for_destination` and `Radicle/src/plugin/copy_hierarchy.cpp:clone_record` still call `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:remap_record_form_links` with no lookup, so a `COED` with a non-null owner and a nonzero union still throws on those paths; that is pre-existing, and those callers hold no environment to type an owner from, so there is no better lookup to pass.

## Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:find_quest_fragment, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_fragment, Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:remove_quest_fragment (#602 D-24 C-3 C-12 C-18 C-36)

- Scope: the last open piece of the quest fragment row. `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment` and `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:remove_quest_vmad_fragment` addressed a binding by stage alone, so the 80 of 885 vanilla quests that bind one stage twice (survey in the `set_quest_vmad_fragment` section above) could have no binding renamed or removed. Both now also take the `(stage, stage_index)` pair, which is the key `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment` already writes and this writer orders the list by. xEdit's key is the whole `Quest Stage` u32 and `Quest Stage Index` u32 (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3993-4001 @93cc0bc5`), while `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_quest_vmad_extras` reads the first u32 as `stage` u16 plus an `unknown` u16. The writer's pair ignores that word, so two entries that differ only in it are refused as a duplicate (fail-closed) though xEdit may keep them distinct; whether the word is zero in shipped quests is UNPROVEN.

- Addressing: `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:find_quest_fragment` takes `std::optional<std::int32_t> stage_index` beside the stage. With no index it is the old stage-only search; with an index it skips every entry whose `QuestVmadFragment::stage_index` differs, so a stage bound twice names one entry. The repeated-key guard is kept for both forms, because a payload that binds the same pair twice cannot be addressed either: the stage-only form throws `schema::ScalarError("the quest VMAD binds one stage twice; address the fragment by its stage index")` and the pair form throws `"the quest VMAD binds one stage index twice"`. That refusal is what the brief called failing closed: the writer never picks the first of two entries, and it was already a throw before this change, so the stage-only form's behavior on an ambiguous stage is unchanged in kind and only the message now names the remedy.

- Overloads, not a widened signature: `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment` and `:remove_quest_vmad_fragment` each keep their stage-only form and gain a pair form whose `stage_index` sits where `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment` puts it, so the address reads `(stage, stage_index)` at every quest fragment entry point. Both forms delegate to `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_fragment` and `:remove_quest_fragment` in the file's anonymous namespace, which hold the one body per operation and pass `std::nullopt` for the stage-only caller. A defaulted parameter was not used because the index belongs before the script and fragment names, and C++ forbids a defaulted parameter ahead of a non-defaulted one.

- Byte preservation: the single-binding path is bit-identical to before. The finder's index filter is a no-op when no index is passed, and the splice, the re-encode through `src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:append_quest_fragment`, the `unchanged` early return, the count rewrite and the `detail::mark_record_modified` call are the same code moved into the two helpers, so nothing about the bytes written changed. The pair form writes the same entry range with the same encoder, so it inherits the guarantees the stage-only form had: the fragment script entry, the alias list, the other bindings and every byte outside the entry keep their bytes.

- Refusals: unchanged from the stage-only row (`record_missing`, `not_authorable`, `subrecord_missing`, `binding_missing` for a QUST VMAD with no extras or a key no entry carries, empty names and every payload the loader refuses, all before any splice) plus the pair form's own `binding_missing` for a stage index that no entry of that stage carries. A wrong index leaves the payload untouched, which the test checks by comparing whole-plugin bytes.

- C ABI: the pair form is exported, and only the pair form. The follow-up this row recorded is done: `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:radicle_plugin_set_quest_vmad_fragment` and `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:radicle_plugin_remove_quest_vmad_fragment` take the stage and the stage index as two parameters, so no sentinel for stage only is needed. The stage-only forms have no export. The section below holds the details. The other structure writers, including `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:add_quest_vmad_fragment`, remain native only.

- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_quest_fragments.cpp:VmadQuestFragments.StageBoundTwiceIsAddressedByStageIndex` drives the fixture that binds stage 10 twice (indices 0 and 5). It checks that the stage-only set and remove both throw with the ambiguity message and leave the whole plugin byte-identical; that the pair form reports `unchanged` for the entry whose names already match and `updated` for the other one, with the first entry's `[offset, end)` and every byte outside the second entry identical to the original; that the write/reload round trip still passes `vmad_coverage` and decodes both entries with the edited names; that a stage index no entry carries is `binding_missing` and does not touch the bytes; that removing index 5 drops exactly that entry's bytes and rewrites the count to 1; and that once one binding is left the stage-only form works again (`unchanged`, then a rename, then a removal), after which the empty list reports `binding_missing` for both forms. `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_quest_fragments.cpp:VmadQuestFragments.DuplicateStageIndexIsRefused` drives the same-pair tail (two entries that both carry stage 10 and index 0) and checks that both pair-form calls throw the `stage index twice` refusal and leave the whole plugin byte-identical. Wired in at `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt` already. Nothing here was compiled or run: CI is the first build.

## Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:radicle_plugin_set_quest_vmad_fragment, Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:radicle_plugin_remove_quest_vmad_fragment

- Scope: the C export of the pair form of quest fragment set and remove. `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:radicle_plugin_set_quest_vmad_fragment` calls `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:set_quest_vmad_fragment` with the `(stage, stage_index)` overload, and `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:radicle_plugin_remove_quest_vmad_fragment` calls `remove_quest_vmad_fragment` with the matching overload. No export of the stage-only forms exists, and no C caller of this section's functions was present before, so the C side defines its own shape from `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:edit`, the existing leading-script setter helper. Creating a binding stays native only.
- Status mapping: `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:fragment_status` returns `RADICLE_STATUS_OK` for `updated` and `unchanged`, which the C ABI does not tell apart, the same as the `radicle_plugin_set_vmad_*` exports. `record_missing`, `subrecord_missing` and `binding_missing` return `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, and `PluginFile.SetQuestVmadFragment` reports that as `false` through `Call.Found`. `not_authorable` returns `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Any other value returns `RADICLE_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`.
- Ambiguity: a repeated pair throws `schema::ScalarError` from `Radicle/src/plugin/vmad_writer.cpp:find_quest_fragment`. `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:fragment_edit` maps it to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` through `fail_exception`, as the leading-script exports do, so the refusal is told apart by its text (`stage index twice`) that `radicle_last_error` returns, not by its status.
- Null checks: `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:radicle_plugin_set_quest_vmad_fragment` refuses a null script or function name, and names that are not valid UTF-8, before the writer runs. `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad.cpp:fragment_edit` refuses a null plugin or an invalid record key. Every refusal returns before any splice, so the plugin bytes are unchanged.
- C# wrapper: `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PluginFile.cs:PluginFile.SetQuestVmadFragment` and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PluginFile.cs:PluginFile.RemoveQuestVmadFragment` sit beside the leading-script setters. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PluginFile.cs:PluginFile.SetQuestVmadFragment` refuses a null name with an `ArgumentNullException` and an embedded NUL in either name with an `ArgumentException`, both before the native call. The generated imports are in `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs`, regenerated with `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py`, and the ABI probe was unchanged.
- ABI: these exports took 53 of `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h`, after the NIF and DDS exports took 52 in #706.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_quest_fragments.cpp:VmadQuestFragments.CApiPairFormEditsOneOfTwoBindingsAndRefusesBadInput` checks the null plugin, the null name, an invalid name, an absent index and an absent record, each with its status, then edits the bound index, removes the other one and reads the saved file back. `VmadQuestFragments.CApiPairFormRefusesDuplicatePairAndLeavesBytesUnchanged` checks that a repeated pair reports the `stage index twice` text through `radicle_last_error` and that the saved subrecord equals the original. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/VmadAuthoringTests.cs:VmadAuthoringTests.QuestFragmentEditsRefuseOtherRecordsAndMissingKeysWithoutTouchingBytes` checks that a non-quest record throws `RadicleException`, that an absent record returns `false`, that an embedded NUL throws `ArgumentException`, and that the bytes are unchanged. The C# test has no positive round trip on a quest, so the native success path is covered only by the C-level gtest.

## Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp:ascii_lower

`ascii_lower` returned `bool`, so every nonzero character compared equal and `equals_ignore_case` matched on length only. `keyword_kind` then returned the first keyword of the same length: `Int` and `Foo` lexed as `new`, `Ab` as `as`. Returning `char` restores the case-insensitive comparison. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_source.cpp:LexesSameLengthIdentifiersAsIdentifiers`.

## Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp:parse_double

The exponent accumulator is clamped with `std::min` to a cap of 10000, so a long exponent cannot overflow `int` (undefined behaviour) or drive the scaling loop toward INT_MAX iterations. The clamp replaces a `exponent < kExponentCap` test taken before the multiply, which let the accumulator reach 99999 and made the constant read tighter than it was. A capped exponent still saturates the value to inf or 0. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_source.cpp:LexesHugeFloatExponentWithoutOverflow`.

## Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser_expr.cpp:Parser::chain_within

The postfix, cast and binary loops (`parse_postfix`, `parse_cast`, `parse_or`, `parse_and`, `parse_comparison`, `parse_additive`, `parse_multiplicative`) build a left-leaning tree, one node per link (a `.name(...)` link is two nodes, the member and the call), so a long chain makes `~Expression` and the summary walkers recurse once per link. `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser_internal.hpp:Parser::links_` is a single counter for the whole statement or declaration, reset by `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser_stmt.cpp:Parser::parse_statement` and `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser.cpp:Parser::parse_declaration`; each loop increments it through `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser_expr.cpp:Parser::chain_within` and fails with `ParseErrorKind::DepthLimit` past `kMaxChainLength` (512, in `parser_internal.hpp`). The counter is shared rather than one local per loop because the loops nest: a parenthesised group re-enters through `parse_primary`, so seven separate budgets multiply across nesting levels (96 levels x 512 links is ~49k nodes of left spine, enough to overflow the stack while every level stays inside both bounds). With one counter per statement the link total is the tree-depth bound. The chain bound is looser than the 96-level nesting bound because real scripts chain more operators than they nest parentheses. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_source.cpp:RejectsLongChainsPastTheDepthLimitWithoutRecursing` (200 and 512 links accepted, 513 and 5000 rejected, and 32 nested groups of 21 links rejected although every group is inside the per-level bound).

## Radicle/src/papyrus_source/summary.cpp:summarize

Property `Get` and `Set` bodies are summarized as functions named `<Property>.<Accessor>` (for example `Scaled.Get`) with an empty state. Their calls, property reads and property writes then reach `ScriptSummary::calledFunctions`, `propertiesRead` and `propertiesWritten` through the existing aggregation. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_source.cpp:SummarizesPropertyAccessorBodies`.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_\ActorSounds

- Source: xEdit `wbRStruct('Actor Sounds', [CS2H count, wbActorSounds, CS2E, CS2F])` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10432-10436`), where `wbActorSounds` is a `wbRArrayS('Sounds', wbRStructSK([0], 'Sound', [wbFormIDCk(CS2K, 'Keyword', [KYWD]), wbFormIDCk(CS2D, 'Sound', [SNDR]).SetRequired]))` with `SetCountPath(CS2H)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8399-8414`). CS2K is not required and CS2D is, so a sound is an optional keyword followed by its sound, and CS2H counts sounds.
- Corpus, read-only over the sixteen local masters and cc plugins (Fallout4.esm, the DLC masters and the `cc*.esl` files, excluding the duplicate `ccOTMFO4001-Remnants - Copy.esl`; 4477 NPC_ records): 53 NPC_ records carry actor sounds (Fallout4.esm 30, DLCNukaWorld 13, DLCCoast 8, DLCRobot 2). Every one has exactly one CS2H of 4 bytes, one CS2E of 0 bytes and one CS2F of 1 byte, so CS2E and CS2F are once per record, not once per sound. CS2D is 56 entries of 4 bytes and CS2K is 3 entries of 4 bytes. CS2H equals the CS2D count in 53 of 53. The subrecord shape of the CS2 region is CS2H, CS2D, CS2E, CS2F in 52 records and CS2H, then three CS2K+CS2D pairs, then CS2E, CS2F in one, always contiguous, with the keyword directly before its sound and NAM8 before CS2H.
- Why the group needed a new member flag: a keyword leads its sound and is absent from 52 of 53 records, so it cannot be the required leader, and a sound-leader group would attach each keyword to the previous sound (or leave the first one outside every run) and make remove orphan it. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupMemberDescriptor.leading` marks such an optional member. `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` accepts `leading` only on optional, non-repeatable, non-skippable members that precede every other member, and takes the first non-leading member as the leader, which it still requires to be required and non-repeatable.
- Run splitting: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` starts a run at a leading member or the leader and ends it at the next leading member or leader once the run holds its leader. A run with a keyword and no sound, or two keywords in a row, throws `SubrecordGroupError`. For groups without leading members the result is unchanged.
- Rows: `NPC_\ActorSoundTotal` is the whole-payload CS2H u32 (a plain write is refused as for `CONT\ItemTotal`). `NPC_\ActorSoundKeyword` and `NPC_\ActorSoundSound` stay FormLink rows outside the group because the codegen takes group links only from required members; both address the nth CS2K or CS2D, so with a keyword present on only some sounds the keyword index is not the sound index.
- Insert and remove: insert writes one zero CS2D (a null sound) before the next run or after the last run. In a record with no CS2H it is refused with `SubrecordGroupMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` and the plugin is unchanged: the group sets `requires_existing_count` (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupDescriptor.requires_existing_count`, parsed in `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group`, enforced in `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_subrecord_group`) because a first sound would need CS2E and CS2F as well, which xEdit requires and all 53 corpus records carry, and an insert that wrote only CS2H and CS2D would leave an incomplete struct. CONT, FURN and TERM groups do not set the flag and still create their count on a first insert. Remove erases the run including its keyword and decrements CS2H.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_npc_furn_attach_slots.cpp` (`NpcFurnAttachSlots`) asserts the descriptor (optional leading CS2K, required CS2D, count CS2H), that a keyword that follows a sound starts the next run and not the previous one (a model that takes it as the previous sound's trailer would fail the span check), that remove takes the keyword with its sound and keeps CS2H in step, that insert lands before the next keyword and before CS2E, that adding the first sound to an NPC_ with no CS2H is refused with the plugin bytes unchanged, and that a keyword with no sound fails closed on insert, remove and a FormLink write without changing the plugin. `Radicle/tools/test_subrecord_group_codegen.py` covers the `leading` rules and rendering. `Radicle/tests/test_npc_real.cpp:NpcReal.ActorSoundRunsMatchTheStoredCountAndKeepEachKeywordWithItsSound` checks every official-master NPC_: runs equal the stored CS2H, equal the CS2D count, and each run is an optional keyword plus a sound.
- Not verified here: nothing was compiled on this machine, so the C++ tests have not run; the corpus figures above come from a read-only Python walk of the masters, not from the C++ reader.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:INNR\NamingRules and Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_group_members — counted sub-runs inside a group run (#602 B-23)

The earlier INNR entries in this file (the `#602 B-23` bullet in the LENS section and the round 8 bullet) both stopped at "no group descriptor can hold this"; this entry closes it by extending the group kind rather than by adding a new kind. xEdit's record is `wbRecord(INNR, 'Instance Naming Rules', [wbEDID, wbInteger(UNAM, 'Target', itU32, ...), wbRArray('Naming Rules', wbRStruct('Ruleset', [wbInteger(VNAM, 'Count', itU32, nil, cpBenign).IncludeFlag(dfSkipImplicitEdit), wbRArray('Names', wbRStruct('Name', [wbLStringKC(WNAM, 'Text', 0, cpTranslate), wbKeywords, wbStruct(XNAM, 'Property', [...]), wbInteger(YNAM, 'Index', itU16)])).SetCountPath(VNAM)]))])` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12337-12380`. The shape is a count subrecord (`VNAM`) followed by that many runs, each run made of several subrecords (`WNAM`, the `KSIZ`/`KWDA` pair `wbKeywords` builds at `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8655-8676`, the optional `XNAM`, `YNAM`), and the counted sub-run is itself nested one level inside the outer `wbRArray` run (a `Ruleset` is exactly `VNAM` plus its names, so `VNAM` repeats once per ruleset).

- Mechanism: `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:GROUP_RUN_KEYS` adds a `run` key to a `subrecord_group` row, naming a `count_member` (one of the group's own members, four-byte, non-repeatable) and a nested `members` list parsed by the extracted `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_group_members`, the same function the group's own members use. A run member may not be a group member, the group's `count_subrecord`, a successor or another run member, and a run leader must be required and non-repeatable. One nested run per group is enough for the shape xEdit has (one counted sub-run inside a run), so the descriptor carries a single `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupRunDescriptor` rather than a list, and the group entry in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc` gained a trailing `SubrecordGroupRunDescriptor{}` (or the generator's `k_subrecord_group_run_members_<group>` table) and nothing else moved.
- Split: the new functions pushed `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp` past the 750-line guard, so the counted-array and subrecord-group code moved to `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp` and the two symbols the value side still needs (`Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_internal.hpp:group_spans` and `:read_counter`) are declared there. `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp` keeps the scalar, string and FormLink write paths and the field counts; the moved anchors in this file were repointed.
- Runtime: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` consumes the nested runs immediately after the count member, reading the count from that member's whole four-byte payload and requiring exactly that many tuples each starting with the run leader, with the same non-decreasing order, required-member and payload-size checks the outer run uses. A run member that appears after those tuples (the under-counted direction) throws the same `count does not match its nested runs` error, so no orphan tuple survives an insert or remove. `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:SubrecordGroupSpan` gained `runs`, the tuple spans of that outer run, so a caller can address a name inside a ruleset.
- Mutation: `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:insert_record_subrecord_group_run` and `remove_record_subrecord_group_run` take an outer run index plus a nested index, insert or erase one tuple and move only that ruleset's `VNAM`; `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_run_counter` finds the count member inside the addressed span, so the male/female-style repetition of a count subrecord is what the scoping fixes. Inserting or removing a whole ruleset stays on `insert_record_subrecord_group` / `remove_record_subrecord_group`, which already wrote only the required members, so a new ruleset starts as `VNAM` 0. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:is_subrecord_group_count_subrecord` now also answers true for a run's `count_member`, and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:subrecord_group_for_member` searches run members too, so a row on `WNAM` or `YNAM` validates the whole naming-rules structure before it writes.
- Rows: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:INNR\NameText` (`WNAM`, string, `localized`, `repeated`) and `INNR\NameIndex` (`YNAM`, u16, `repeated`). `YNAM` is also `required: true` in the run: all 1425 corpus tuples carry it and xEdit's `wbInteger(YNAM, 'Index', itU16)` is non-optional, so an inserted name gets `WNAM` plus a two-byte zero `YNAM` and both rows address the same element count. `XNAM` stays optional (0 occurrences). `KSIZ`, `KWDA` and `XNAM` stay unrowed: `KSIZ` is the count of the packed `KWDA` payload and a generic write would desync them, and `KWDA` is a packed FormLink array that needs the keyword-list machinery, not a run member row.
- Corpus, read-only scan of the seven official masters (Fallout4.esm 7 INNR, DLCRobot 2, DLCCoast 5, DLCNukaWorld 6, the other three none): 20 records, 200 `VNAM` rulesets, 1425 names, and every `VNAM` equals the number of tuples that follow it (0 mismatches). Tuple shapes are `WNAM KSIZ KWDA YNAM` 1417 times and `WNAM YNAM` 8 times, so `KSIZ` and `KWDA` must be optional; payloads are `WNAM` 4 (the masters set the TES4 localized flag, so `WNAM` is a string id), `KSIZ` 4, `KWDA` 4 to 24 and `YNAM` 2; `XNAM` never occurs. Every subrecord of every INNR record is in the eight-signature vocabulary, and a `VNAM` is preceded only by `UNAM` (20), `YNAM` (61) or another `VNAM` (119, so empty rulesets are normal and an inserted `VNAM` 0 matches vanilla).
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_nested_group_runs.cpp` pins the descriptor and the spans of a two-ruleset fixture (`SpansScopeEachNestedRunToItsOwnCountSubrecord`), refuses a count too high, one too low, a tuple without its leader and a tuple member of the wrong size (`CountMismatchAndMissingLeaderFailClosed`), keeps the ruleset count in step across a name insert and remove, asserts the inserted `WNAM` and `YNAM` row counts stay equal, and proves the rewrite is byte-identical (`InsertingAndRemovingANameKeepsItsRulesetCount`), round-trips a whole ruleset the same way (`InsertingAndRemovingARulesetRoundTripsTheBytes`), writes one name's text and index at a time (`NameRowsAddressOneNameAtATime`), refuses a name row on a record whose `VNAM` is wrong (`NameRowsRefuseARecordWhoseRulesetCountIsWrong`), refuses a name insert into a localized plugin (`InsertingANameIntoALocalizedNameRefuses`) and reports the missing record and out-of-range indexes (`NestedMutationsReportMissingRecordsAndRanges`). The generator side is `Radicle/tools/test_subrecord_group_codegen.py:SubrecordGroupCodegenTests.test_subrecord_group_run_expands_nested_rows_and_renders_the_table`, `...test_subrecord_group_without_a_run_renders_an_empty_descriptor`, `...test_subrecord_group_run_member_rows_are_expanded` and `...test_subrecord_group_run_declaration_is_checked`. `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp`'s INNR fixture gained a one-name ruleset so its every-row decode test still covers the two new rows, and `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records_real.cpp` now skips a localized row in a localized plugin, the same skip `Radicle/tests/test_config_records_real.cpp` makes for `GMST\StringValue`.
- Still open on the same shape: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\MorphPresets` is the other FO4 nesting of this kind — `wbMorphGroups` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3130-3167` puts `wbInteger(MPPC, 'Count', itU32)` before `wbRArray('Morph Presets', wbRStruct('Morph Preset', [MPPI, MPPN, MPPM, MPPT, MPPF])).SetCountPath(MPPC)` inside a `wbRStruct('Morph Group', [MPGN, ..., MPPK, MPGS])`, and `MPPC` repeats once per morph group (male and female). The kind now expresses it; the record has no row because RACE's morph rows are `repeated` scalars today and converting them is a separate change. `NPC_` actor sounds (`CS2H` with `CS2K`/`CS2D` pairs at `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8399-8414`) needs no nested count, only the two-member counted group the earlier audit note asked for, and it is still unrowed.
- Merge note: the merged tree also carries the `#716` INNR row half — `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:INNR\RulesetCount` (`VNAM`), `INNR\KeywordCount` (`KSIZ`), `INNR\PropertyValue`, `INNR\PropertyTarget` and `INNR\PropertyOperator` (`XNAM`), and `INNR\NameIndex` (`YNAM`) — so `KSIZ` and `XNAM` are readable rows here too, while `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:is_derived_scalar_row` still refuses generic writes to `INNR` `VNAM` and `KSIZ`, and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_subrecord_group_run` keeps each ruleset's `VNAM` in step with its names. `INNR\NameText` keeps the `localized` flag from this side.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:IMAD

`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` rows the 32 IMAD time-interpolator arrays xEdit decodes and Radicle left opaque: the eleven named ones (BNAM 7528, VNAM 7529, RNAM 7533, SNAM 7534, UNAM 7535, NAM1 7536, NAM2 7537, WNAM 7540, XNAM 7541, YNAM 7542, NAM4 7546) and the 21 Add halves of the HDR and Cinematic MultAdd pairs (7548-7564, 7567-7570). Each is a `counted_array` with stride 8 over `wbTimeInterpolators` = `wbArray(sig, name, wbTimeInterpolator)` (`wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9272`; the value-level overload at 8326 serves nested arrays), whose element is the `wbTimeInterpolator` struct `{Time f32, Value f32}` (`wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8312`), so every row is Time at offset 0 and Value at offset 4, with the count taken from the payload length the way the TNAM/NAM3 color arrays already in this record take it from stride 20. Corpus check over the seven official masters: the 32 new rows decode 18,300 elements across 269 IMAD records, no payload that is not a whole number of 8-byte elements, no value outside the f32 row bounds. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_image_fx_records.cpp:ImageFxSynthetic.TimeInterpolatorArraysDecodeAndEditOneStrideElement` (stride-8 addressing, one element edited, and the neighbouring sample left intact), with `Radicle/tests/test_image_fx_records_real.cpp:ImageFxRecordsReal.EveryBatchRecordMatchesItsAuthoringAndDecodesEveryRow` decoding the same rows across every shipped record.

NAM5 (7543) and NAM6 (7544) are `wbFromVersion(118, ...)` and are rowed as counted arrays with an array-level `min_form_version` 118 (`IMAD\DepthOfFieldVignetteRadiusInterpolators`, `IMAD\DepthOfFieldVignetteStrengthInterpolators`). The 21 Mult halves (`\u0000IAD`..`\u0014IAD`) are rowed the same way as the Add halves: each is a stride-8 counted array over the `{Time, Value}` members. `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:valid_signature` accepts any four characters up to 0xFF, so the bytes below 0x20 in those signatures pass. Their counts stay visible through the DNAM count rows (`IMAD\HDREyeAdaptSpeedMult`, labelled "mult count"), and each interpolator's element count is read from its rows (`record_field_count` on `IMAD\HDREyeAdaptSpeedMultTime` reads 2 on record 3001 and 0 on record 3002). Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_image_fx_records.cpp:HdrMultInterpolatorRowsDecodeAndEditOneStrideElement`.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:MUST

`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` rows `MUST\CuePoints` as a `counted_array` over FNAM (8813), stride 4, one `MUST\CuePoint` f32 at offset 0, so the element count is the payload length divided by four, as with the DAMC and PRPS arrays. `wbArray(FNAM, 'Cue Points', wbFloat('Point'))` stores one raw array in a single subrecord, not one subrecord per cue point, which is why the row is a counted array and not a repeated field. Corpus check: 20 of the 624 official MUST records carry FNAM, every payload is 68..152 bytes and a whole number of four-byte elements, and the widest observed cue point is 199.37. FNAM is also an authoring subrecord between LNAM and CITC, at most one per record, so `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record` enforces its position and cardinality. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_music_track_lists.cpp:MusicTrackLists.CuePointRowsDecodeAndWriteOneArrayElement` and `MusicTrackLists.TruncatedCuePointPayloadRefusesElementWrites`, the second pinning that a payload which is not a whole number of elements yields no rows and refuses the write instead of overwriting the trailing bytes.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:SMQN

`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` rows `SMQN\Quests` as a `per_subrecord` FormLink list over NNAM (8756) with target QUST and `mutation: existing_only`, matching `wbRArray('Quests', wbRStructSK([0], 'Quest', [wbFormIDCk(NNAM, 'Quest', [QUST]), wbFloat(RNAM, 'Hours until reset', ...)]))` (8754-8759). The row declares `counter: QNAM`, so `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:remove_record_formlink_list_element`, `remove_record_formlink_list_elements_matching` and `clear_record_formlink_list` rewrite the count through `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:reconcile_counter`; a per-subrecord counter is overwritten in place rather than erased, so an emptied run keeps QNAM=0, while the packed-array counters (KSIZ, XCNT) are still dropped when their list empties. The row also declares `element_tail: RNAM` (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:FormLinkListDescriptor::element_tail`, parsed in `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py`), because xEdit's element is the pair `wbRStructSK([0], [NNAM, optional RNAM])` (8754-8759): `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:erase_list_element` drops the RNAM subrecords directly after a removed NNAM, and `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:move_list_element` moves the NNAM+RNAM block as one unit while any subrecords between blocks keep their slot. Insertion stays refused by `mutation: existing_only`, which is why `insert_encoded_element` never reconciles a per-subrecord counter. NNAM is also an authoring subrecord after QNAM with a maximum of 65535, so preflight checks where each NNAM sits while RNAM, which has no row, is ignored. Corpus check: 346 SMQN records, 1,468 NNAM subrecords, all 4 bytes, and QNAM equals the NNAM count in every one of them; two carry QNAM=0. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_story_manager_records.cpp:StoryManagerRecordsSynthetic.QuestListRowsReadAndRetargetEveryQuestNodeEntry` and `StoryManagerRecordsSynthetic.QuestListRemovalAndClearKeepTheDeclaredCount` (remove to one, remove to zero, remove by target and clear, each asserting the re-read QNAM), with `Radicle/tests/test_story_manager_records_real.cpp:StoryManagerRecordsReal.EveryBatchRecordMatchesItsAuthoringAndDecodesEveryRow` asserting the same list-length-equals-QNAM invariant across the official masters.

RNAM keeps no scalar row; it follows its NNAM through `element_tail`. It is optional per quest (382 occurrences against 1,468 NNAM, never more), so a repeated scalar row would address the Nth quest that happens to carry hours rather than the Nth quest, and the group model cannot carry it either: `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` rejects member rows unless the member is `required` and non-repeatable, so an optional member cannot hold fields. Closing it needs optional-member rows in a subrecord group, not a new row here.
## Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:AbcCorpusReal

The ABC decoder had never run on game bytecode: `Radicle/tests/test_abc.cpp:AbcCorpus.EveryExtractedAbcParsesDisassemblesAndSummarizes` is gated on `FO4_ABC_CORPUS` and nothing in the tree extracts `.abc` files, so it skipped everywhere. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:AbcCorpusReal.DecodesEveryShippedInterfaceAbcBlock` takes the corpus the way `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp:SwfRealData` already does, with no new extractor: it gates on `FO4_DATA_DIR`, reads `Data/Interface/*.swf` and `*.gfx` when that directory exists (`Radicle/tests/real_data_movies.hpp:is_movie` and `:read_file` are shared with `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp`), and falls back to every movie entry of `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` through `Radicle/include/fo4/archive/ba2.hpp:read_ba2_general_file` and `extract_ba2_general_entry`, parses each movie with `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:read_swf`, and takes the ABC spans from `fo4::swf::abc_blocks`, whose `SwfAbcBlock::payload` is what `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:abc_payload` sliced out of the `DoABC2` tag. The archive pass is selected by the result of the loose-file pass, not by the directory's existence: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp` enters it when `stats.blocks == 0`, so a `Data/Interface` directory that yields movies but no bytecode scans the archive as well. Each span goes through `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::parse`, `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code`, `validate_operand_pools`, `Radicle/src/abc/disassembly.cpp:disassemble` per body and `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:summarize`. `decode_code` and `disassemble` are handed each body's `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcMethodBody::exceptions`, so the 149 shipped bodies that carry a handler table have their handler targets checked on every CI run (see `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable`).

- The accounting is total, so nothing is skipped silently: `stats.blocks == stats.parsed + stats.unsupported_total()` and `stats.total_movies == stats.movies + stats.lzma + stats.unreadable`. A block whose parse is not `AbcStatus::Ok` is counted in `stats.unsupported` under its own `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:status_name`, and the per-status counts are recorded as `unsupported_status_histogram`. An LZMA movie is counted in `lzma` and not failed on, exactly as `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp:check_movie` does. `AbcStatus::TrailingBytes` is counted separately and asserted to be zero, because a `DoABC` payload has no padding, so a leftover byte means the pool, class or body walk drifted. The zero counts the measurement says must hold on the shipped archive are asserted: `EXPECT_EQ(stats.unsupported_total(), 0u)`, with `unsupported_status_histogram` in the failure message, on every build, and `EXPECT_EQ(stats.lzma, 0u)` only when `exact_counts_known(build)` holds (AE 1.11.240.0), because that zero is a fact about the pinned archive and not about the format. Without the first, a regression that made 674 of the 675 blocks return e.g. `AbcStatus::IndexOutOfRange` would still satisfy `blocks == parsed + unsupported_total()` and `parsed > 0` and CI would stay green on a test whose purpose is exactly that drift. The movie identity `total_movies == movies + lzma + unreadable` does not catch a misclassified movie, because the movie only moves from one term to another; the pinned `lzma == 0` is what catches a compression signature that stopped being recognised, so a movie that should be read is counted as LZMA instead. `EXPECT_GT(stats.parsed, 0u)` keeps a corpus that yields no bytecode from passing as green.
- Every instruction of every body must decode and every operand index must resolve: `decode_code` and `validate_operand_pools` are asserted per body, and `summarize` is asserted per block, so a wrong operand width, a wrong opcode table row, an index role that points past its pool or a summary that loses a body fails on real bytecode and not only on the synthetic file.
- The summary's shape is recorded as `RecordProperty` histograms (`class_histogram`, `method_histogram`, `script_histogram`, bucketed 0 / 1-4 / 5-16 / 17-64 / 65-256 / 257+) plus exact totals (`total_classes`, `total_methods`, `total_scripts`, `bodies`, `instructions`), so a regression that halves the decoded class or method count is visible in the CI test output without a stored baseline file. `summary.classes.size() == file.instances.size()` is asserted per block as well.
- Measured on the authoring machine against the shipped AE 1.11.240.0 `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` (BA2 version 8, 1101 entries, 315 movies): 675 `DoABC2` blocks, all 675 parse `Ok`, 30985 bodies, 815701 instructions, 2958 classes, 31097 methods, 2936 scripts, 0 unsupported, 0 LZMA and 0 `TrailingBytes`. The `Data/Interface` loose-file branch is not covered by that run, because the install used for it has no extracted `Interface` directory, and the archive branch is the one the CI data runner takes as well (its `FO4_DATA_DIR` holds root `*.esm`/`*.ba2` files).
- The one real-data surprise the run produced was in `decode_code`, not in this test: see `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable`.

## Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable

`decode_code` rejected a whole method body when any branch target fell outside `[0, code.size()]`, and shipped bytecode does contain such a target. Two of the 30985 bodies in the AE `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` corpus have one, both immediately after a `returnvalue`, so both are unreachable: `Interface\BarterMenu.swf` method body at index 572 holds `10 4a 00 00` at offset 44 of a 116-byte body, a `jump +74` whose target 122 is 6 bytes past the end, and `Interface\ContainerMenu.swf` body 568 holds `10 53 00 00` at offset 76 of a 157-byte body, targeting 163. Every other target in the corpus lands on an instruction start, which is what shows the decode is aligned and the two jumps are real. `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable` therefore walks the instructions from offset 0 over fallthrough and over branch and `lookupswitch` targets, and `decode_code` range-checks a target only when the branching instruction is reachable.

- Which reference this matches: avmplus's `Verifier::checkTarget` (`Verifier.cpp:3339`) rejects `target < code_pos || target >= code_pos + code_length`, one byte tighter than this decoder — `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:in_code_range` accepts `target == code.size()`, the local choice that lets a `lookupswitch` ending the body target its end — but it is called only from the verifier's reachable-instruction worklist, so a target in dead code is never checked. RABCDAsm resolves a `JumpTarget` against `pos+3` in `abcfile.d:1429` (the switch default against `instructionOffset` at `abcfile.d:1437` and each case at `abcfile.d:1446`) and does not reject an out-of-range target either: `abcfile.d:1506 translateLabel` clamps it to the last instruction index (`abcfile.d:1514`) or to 0 (`abcfile.d:1520`), and `disassembler.d:1586` only consumes the resolved `index`. Reachability is the middle rule: the shipped files decode, and a reachable branch to nowhere is still `AbcStatus::BranchOutOfRange`.
- Handler targets are reachability roots. `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/opcodes.hpp:decode_code` takes the body's exception table as a defaulted `std::span<const AbcException>`, so a raw-span caller is unchanged, and `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable` is seeded with every `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcException::target` alongside offset 0. That is the edge avmplus draws from each reachable throwing instruction inside a handler's try range: `Verifier.cpp:980-994` (the range test at `:982`) gives the handler a frame state holding one value, the exception object (`state->stackDepth = 0; state->scopeDepth = 0` and `state->push(handler->traits)` at `:986-993`), and calls `checkTarget(pc, code_pos + handler->target, /*isExceptionEdge*/true)` at `:994`, so the catch block is verified like any other block and its own branch targets are checked at `Verifier.cpp:1042-1078`. This decoder has no stack simulation (the gap above), so it takes the target as a root without modelling that state and checks no stack depth; `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcMethodBody::max_stack` is still read and never checked.
- A handler target is validated as a branch target, not as a record: it must be inside the body and on an instruction start, otherwise `AbcStatus::BranchOutOfRange`, which is avmplus's own error for it — `Verifier.cpp:3339-3341` (`checkTarget`) rejects `target < code_pos || target >= code_pos+code_length` and a backward target that is not an `OP_label` or a known frame state, and `Verifier.cpp:994` is what reaches it from the exception edge. So `target == code.size()` is invalid for a handler even though a `lookupswitch` ending the body may target the end (`Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:in_code_range`). `AbcException::from` and `::to` are still read raw: avmplus also requires `from <= to <= target < code_length` (`Verifier.cpp:3696-3702`, `kIllegalExceptionHandlerError`), and this decoder does not check it.
- Measured on the shipped AE 1.11.240.0 `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` with the abc-real lane's Python mirror (`~/ds-proxy/scratch/abc-real-probe/probe.py`, extended to keep the tables): of the 30985 bodies, 149 carry an exception table (250 handler records: 49 bodies with one, 99 with two, one with three), 0 records break avmplus's `from <= to <= target < code_length`, 0 handler targets are off an instruction start, and none of the 250 is reachable by fallthrough — every catch block was dead code to this decoder before, and in each of the 149 bodies the reachable set grows by 22 to 28 handler-only instructions, while the decoded instruction list of every shipped body is unchanged, since the only change to decoding is that a target is range-checked when its branch is reachable. No shipped body changes status, so `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:AbcCorpusReal.DecodesEveryShippedInterfaceAbcBlock` stays green, and the two bodies with a dead out-of-range jump are unaffected because both have `exception_count` 0.
- Regressions: `Radicle/tests/test_abc.cpp:Abc.HandlerTargetsAreReachabilityRootsAndValidated` pins both directions — a `jump +1000` in a catch block nothing falls through is `AbcStatus::BranchOutOfRange` with the table and `AbcStatus::Ok` without it (target 1005), a well-formed catch block stays `Ok` and disassembles to `1: jump 5`, a handler target past the end, one equal to the code length and one inside a two-byte instruction are all `AbcStatus::BranchOutOfRange`, and `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:build_method_summary` propagates the status through `summarize`.
- `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:ends_control_flow` lists the opcodes with no fallthrough — `throw` 0x03, `jump` 0x10, `lookupswitch` 0x1B, `returnvoid` 0x47, `returnvalue` 0x48 — so the walk does not treat the bytes after a `returnvalue` as reachable, which is exactly the case the corpus contains. An out-of-range target is not followed, because there is no instruction to follow it to.
- An unreachable instruction still decodes and still gets its resolved `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/opcodes.hpp:AbcDecodedOperand::target`, which may be past the end of the code; only the range check is skipped, so `Radicle/src/abc/disassembly.cpp:render_instruction` formats that out-of-range target as a number and `Radicle/src/abc/summary.cpp:build_method_summary` counts the body. For the two shipped bodies that reversal is the point of the change, not a no-op: there was no instruction list before, `decode_code` returned `AbcStatus::BranchOutOfRange` for the whole body and `summarize` propagated that status.
- Regressions: `Radicle/tests/test_abc.cpp:Abc.RejectsBranchTargetOutOfRange` pins both sides — a reachable `jump +1000` and a reachable `lookupswitch` case target 900 stay `AbcStatus::BranchOutOfRange`, while a `jump +1000` behind a `returnvoid` now decodes with target 1005 — and `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:AbcCorpusReal` fails if the rule is tightened back, because the two shipped bodies stop decoding.
## Radicle/src/environment/environment.cpp:Environment::from_plugins

`Environment::load` now only reads the files and hands them to `Environment::from_plugins`, which owns the rest of the build: the duplicate and unnamed key check, `apply_master_kinds`, `plugins_`, the per-plugin form-id contexts, the containers and the version vectors. The factory exists for callers that already hold their load order in memory and cannot re-read it from disk. `PluginEditTool/native/src/plugin/RadiclePluginMaintenance.cpp:invokeLegacyBackend` builds one per `CleanPlugin` call that has deleted references, from the backend's own loaded plugins, because that backend holds staged edits that are not saved yet and a master read back from disk would not be the version the session is working on. The order and the validation are the ones `load` documents, lowest priority first, and the plugins are moved into the environment, so the caller's own plugins are untouched. `Environment::load` behaviour is unchanged; the duplicate check now runs after every file is read and names the plugin through its own `Plugin::path`, the same file name the read loop used.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACHR\ParentActivateOnly, ACHR\ActivateParentDelay, ACHR\ActivateParent, ACHR\LinkedReferenceKeyword, ACHR\LinkedReference, ACHR\LocationRefTypes, ACHR\Comments and QUST\NextAliasID (#602 parity gaps)

Ranking method, so the next round can repeat it: a record's score is its record count in the seven official masters (`Fallout4.esm`, `DLCRobot.esm`, `DLCworkshop01.esm`, `DLCCoast.esm`, `DLCworkshop02.esm`, `DLCworkshop03.esm`, `DLCNukaWorld.esm`; 2,192,230 records over 137 signatures, counted by walking the top level, skipping `GRUP` by its own size and records by header plus `data_size`) times the number of subrecords xEdit decodes for it that no Radicle row, `formlink_lists` entry, `localized_subrecords` entry or `authoring` declaration names. The xEdit side comes from `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` with comments stripped and every `wbRecord`/`wbRefRecord`/`ReferenceRecord` argument list expanded, including the shared helpers (`wbEDID`, `wbConditions`, `wbPDTOs`, `wbSNAMMarkerParams`, ...) resolved through their `NAME := <expr>` bodies, so a subrecord that only appears inside a helper still counts. `VMAD` is dropped because another lane owns it, and `EDID` because it is the record editor ID: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` declares it through `authoring` on 142 of 145 records and never as a field row, so counting it would rank records by count alone. Excluded records: `NPC_`, `REGN`, `LENS`, `AECH`. The resulting order was REFR 13 gaps, SCEN 49, INFO 2, ACHR 16, CELL 2, QUST 50, PACK 15; this lane took ranks 4-6. `CELL` was skipped although it sits in that band: its two gaps are `TVDT`, a `wbByteArray` (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6040`), and `XCRI`, a variable-length `wbStruct` of counts and counted arrays (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6088-6098`), and neither is expressible with the existing `scalar`, `string`, `counted_array` or `subrecord_group` kinds.

`ACHR` was missing five subrecords that xEdit decodes at the top level of the record, and each now has a row. `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4623` is `wbString(MNAM, 'Comments')` -> the `string` row `ACHR\Comments`. `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4561` is `wbInteger(XAPD, 'Parent Activate Only', itU8, wbBoolEnum)` -> the `enum` row `ACHR\ParentActivateOnly` with the `wbBoolEnum` names `False`/`True` (`wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:7240-7247`). `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4584-4590` is the water-current pair, skipped on purpose: no `ACHR` in any master carries `XWCN`/`XWCU`, so there is no corpus evidence for the rows `REFR` already has. `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4553-4557` is `wbRArrayS('Linked References', wbStructSK(XLKR, [0], ...))` -> `ACHR\LinkedReferenceKeyword` at offset 0 and `ACHR\LinkedReference` at offset 4, both `repeated`; `ACHR\LinkedReferenceKeyword` carries `payload_sizes: [4, 8]` and `ACHR\LinkedReference` `[8]`, because `SetOptionalFrom(1)` makes the reference field optional and a legal four-byte `XLKR` carries only the keyword slot at offset 0 (the seven masters have no four-byte `XLKR`, but a mod may write one). Those two `XLKR` rows are additive to the heuristic remap: `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:visit_formlink_offsets` unions the schema offsets with `visit_link_offsets`, which already scans `XLKR` through `Radicle/src/schema/form_links.cpp:is_formid_array_signature`, so both slots were remapped before these rows and the sort/unique union leaves the result unchanged. `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4560-4568` is the activate-parent group, `wbInteger(XAPD, ...)` plus `wbRArrayS('Activate Parent Refs', wbStructSK(XAPR, [0], ...))` -> `ACHR\ActivateParent` at offset 0 and the `f32` row `ACHR\ActivateParentDelay` at offset 4. `wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4581` is `wbArray(XLRT, 'Location Ref Type', wbFormIDCk('Ref', [LCRT, NULL]))`: one subrecord holding N four-byte refs, so it becomes the `packed_array` list `ACHR\LocationRefTypes` rather than a repeated field row. `wbRArrayS` writes one subrecord per element and `wbArray` writes one subrecord for the whole array, which is why `XLKR`/`XAPR` are `repeated` field rows and `XLRT` is a list.

`QUST` was missing `wbInteger(ANAM, 'Next Alias ID', itU32).SetRequired` (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10805`) -> the `u32` row `QUST\NextAliasID`. The row is safe next to the generic form-ID remapper, source: `Radicle/src/schema/form_link_schema.cpp:qust_non_formid_signature` already lists `ANAM` as a deliberate non-form-ID subrecord of `QUST`.

Invariant: a generic scalar write to `QUST\NextAliasID` is refused with `ScalarMutationStatus::next_alias_id_too_low` when the value is at or below the highest non-collection alias ID (`Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar`, helper `highest_alias_id`). Vanilla keeps the counter above every alias ID, and `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:grow_next_alias_id` keeps it that way for alias inserts, so a value at or below the highest ID would hand out a duplicate on the next add. The C API maps the refusal to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` in `Radicle/src/c_api_fields.cpp:map_scalar_status`. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_quest_structure.cpp:QuestStructure.NextAliasIdRowReadsAndWritesTheStoredCounter`, whose fixture has alias IDs 1 and 2 and counter 5: writing 1 and 2 is refused and leaves the counter at 5, writing 3 is accepted and rereads as 3.

Corpus evidence, read-only over the seven masters: `ACHR` `XAPD` 1356 records, every payload 1 byte, values 0 (1354) and 1 (2), so the enum has exactly the two `wbBoolEnum` names; `ACHR` `XAPR` 1445 subrecords, all 8 bytes, first form ID resolving to `REFR` (1095) plus foreign-master refs; `ACHR` `XLKR` 16676 subrecords, all 8 bytes, first slot resolving to `KYWD` (12071) and `NULL` (4605), second slot to `REFR` (16095) and `ACHR` (581), each slot summing to 16676; `ACHR` `XLRT` 2429 subrecords of 4/8/12/16/20 bytes, first form ID resolving to `LCRT` (1971); `ACHR` `MNAM` 1 record of 47 bytes; `QUST` `ANAM` 1909 records, all 4 bytes, values 0-94 with 2 the most common. Remaining in the ranking after this change: `ACHR` 11 gaps (`DATA`, owned by the placed-reference typed module, the zero-length markers `ONAM`/`XATP`/`XIBS`/`XIS2`/`XLKT`/`XPPA`, the structs `PDTO`/`XPLK`, and the unevidenced `XWCN`/`XWCU`) and `QUST` 49, all quest alias and objective/stage members owned by `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp`, `quest_aliases_decode.cpp`, `quest_objectives.cpp` and `quest_stages.cpp`.

Tests. `Radicle/tests/test_achr_parity_rows.cpp:AchrParityRows.ParentActivateOnlyAndCommentsDecodeFromTheirOwnSubrecords` catches the `XAPD`/`MNAM` rows going missing or drifting off `XAPD`/`MNAM` and the enum losing its `False`/`True` names, which would leave the parent-activate flag and the comment unreadable. `Radicle/tests/test_achr_parity_rows.cpp:AchrParityRows.ActivateParentLinkAndDelayShareEachEightByteEntry` catches a wrong `XAPR` delay offset, which would read the reference form ID as a float and write it back over the form ID, and pins the absent-not-malformed rule for a four-byte `XAPR`. `Radicle/tests/test_achr_parity_rows.cpp:AchrParityRows.LinkedReferenceKeywordAndReferenceShareEachEightByteEntry` catches the same off-by-one between the two `XLKR` fields and a lost `KYWD` target; `AchrParityRows.FourByteLinkedReferenceKeepsTheKeywordSlot` catches the keyword row narrowing to `[8]`, which would make `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:formlink_slots` throw on a legal four-byte `XLKR` and hide the keyword from the writer. `Radicle/tests/test_achr_parity_rows.cpp:AchrParityRows.LocationRefTypesAreAPackedArrayOfFourByteRefs` catches `XLRT` being modelled as one four-byte link, which would hide every ref after the first, and pins the write-back through `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:set_record_formlink_list_element`. `Radicle/tests/test_achr_parity_rows.cpp:AchrParityRows.WritesTheParentFlagAndDelayThenRereads` catches a row that reads but cannot write, a `u8` write past its storage that should throw `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` instead of truncating, and an `XAPR` link that would accept a disallowed target type. `Radicle/tests/test_quest_structure.cpp:QuestStructure.NextAliasIdRowReadsAndWritesTheStoredCounter` catches the `QUST` counter row disappearing, being read from the wrong width, the alias decoding breaking when the counter is written, or a write at or below an existing alias ID being accepted. Both ACHR and QUST gaps were checked against the real masters, but nothing in this lane was compiled locally; CI is the first compiler.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_\Packages and Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NPC_\HeadParts

`NPC_\Package` and `NPC_\HeadPart` were `formlink_fields` rows (`repeated: true`, `payload_sizes: [4]`, `insertion: existing_only`), so PKID and PNAM could be read and rewritten by index but not added or removed. xEdit gives neither a count subrecord: `wbRArray('Packages', wbFormIDCk(PKID, 'Package', [PACK]))` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10400-10402` and `wbRArrayS('Head Parts', wbFormIDCk(PNAM, 'Head Part', [HDPT]))` at `:10417` repeat the subrecord itself, so no counter has to be kept in sync. The missing capability is therefore the `per_subrecord` `formlink_lists` shape that `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\MalePresets` and `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:KSSM\Keywords` already use, not a counter row.

The two list rows cannot sit beside the field rows. `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:reject_overlaps` compares the list row's synthetic address with the field row's and refuses a non-segmented pair with `ValueError: overlapping FormLink fields in NPC_.PKID: 'NPC_\Package' and 'NPC_\Packages': whole-payload field covers the subrecord`. Only a segmented list is skipped (`Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:load_lists`, the `if row.get("segment") is not None: continue` branch, which is why `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:FSTS\Footsteps` can share DATA with its five category lists). The field rows were therefore replaced rather than kept: `NPC_\Package` and `NPC_\HeadPart` no longer resolve through `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:formlink_field_descriptor`, and `NPC_\Packages` and `NPC_\HeadParts` are the only paths for PKID and PNAM. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_formlink_lists.inc` was regenerated from the schema, which shifts the index of every descriptor after NPC_ in the flat generated arrays; that is the whole reason the generated diff is large.

`mutation: existing_neighbors` and `nullable: false` follow the xEdit members: neither target list carries NULL, and a null element is refused by `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:validate_record_and_target` with `FormLinkListError`. `existing_neighbors` rather than `appendable` because the `append_when_empty` fallback appends at the end of the record, which for NPC_ would place a package or head part after ATTX and fail the authoring-order check; the same choice `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE\MalePresets` makes. Element storage is checked by `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:matching_positions`, which throws for any element that is not exactly four bytes, the guard the field rows applied through `payload_sizes`.

Anchors: NPC_ declares only list rows, so the sibling-derived anchors `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:load_lists` would otherwise generate are empty, and the rows carry an explicit `anchor_predecessors` list in reverse xEdit order.
