The lists are the full predecessor set for the list's own subrecord, not a curated subset, because `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:empty_list_insertion_point` takes the LAST present predecessor: omitting a subrecord that can be the last one before the list's slot (DSTF of the destructible run, for example) would anchor the element too early. The set is the `NPC_` authoring block order up to that subrecord plus the four `wbAttackData` members the authoring block does not list (`ATKE`, `ATKW`, `ATKS`, `ATKT`; `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4073-4123`), so `NPC_\Packages` carries 48 predecessors, `NPC_\HeadParts` 61 and `NPC_\AttachParentSlots` 51; `MODF` is deliberately absent because no `NPC_` member order contains it (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10286-10489`), whatever the `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:keyword_records` row for the record says. `RNAM` is required on every NPC_ and is a predecessor of both lists, so the fail-closed `insertion_boundary_unavailable` path is unreachable on real data and is only reachable on a record that carries none of the predecessors.

Corpus (Fallout4.esm, read-only scan of both top-level `NPC_` groups, compressed records inflated): 3015 NPC_ records; PKID in 1120 of them, 1 to 10 subrecords each, 1872 subrecords; PNAM in 1602, 1 to 72 each, 17271 subrecords; every PKID, PNAM and SPLO payload exactly four bytes, so no shipped record reaches the four-byte guard. No record carries `ATKD`, `ATKE`, `ATKW`, `ATKS`, `ATKT` or `MODF`, and AIDT is present in every record and sits immediately before the PKID slot, so the attack-run members change no shipped insertion point.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_npc_link_rows.cpp:NpcLinkRows.PackageAndHeadPartArePerSubrecordListsNotFields` pins both descriptors (storage, targets, `can_insert`) and that the field paths are gone; `NpcLinkRows.PackageAndHeadPartListsSetInsertAndRemoveByIndex` sets, inserts and removes by index and asserts the sibling PKID/PNAM/SPLO runs are untouched, so a wrong index mapping or a stray subrecord shows up as a byte difference; `NpcLinkRows.RepeatedWritesReachOnlyTheirOwnSubrecord` keeps the SPLO field row's indexed write and its neighbours, the coverage the replaced rows used to share; `NpcLinkRows.OutOfRangeIndexNullAndWrongTargetTypeAreRefused` covers the index, null and target-type refusals; `NpcLinkRows.EmptyPackageListAnchorsAfterItsLastXEditOrderPredecessor` inserts the first package of an absent PKID run into a record carrying ACBS, RNAM and AIDT and asserts it lands directly after AIDT; `NpcLinkRows.EmptyPackageListRefusesAnInsertWithNoAnchor` covers the fail-closed path on a record whose only subrecord is PNAM; `NpcLinkRows.EmptyListsAnchorAfterTheWholeAttackRun` inserts the first element of each of the three rows into a fresh copy of a record carrying ACBS, RNAM, the destructible run, the whole attack run and a trailing HCLF, and asserts each lands directly after ATKT, so a list anchored on ATKD alone shows up as an element placed before ATKE; `NpcLinkRows.EmptyAttachParentSlotsAnchorsAfterTheDestructibleRun` does the same for APPR against a record ending in DSTF then HCLF, so a curated APPR anchor set shows up as a slot placed after DEST and an append-at-end shows up after HCLF; `NpcLinkRows.PackageAndHeadPartListsSetInsertAndRemoveByIndex` also asserts `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:record_field_count(plugin, key, path)` returns 3 and 2 for `NPC_\Packages` and `NPC_\HeadParts` and throws `ScalarError` for the removed `NPC_\Package`, the path-count coverage the replaced field rows used to carry; `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_fields.cpp:CApiFields.FieldCountReportsOccurrencesAndMapsStatuses` pins the exported status for a `per_subrecord` list (`RACE\MalePresets`, count 1, `RADICLE_STATUS_OK`), which was `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` while the path overload resolved `packed_array` lists only; `NpcLinkRows.OddSizedPackagePayloadIsRefused` keeps the eight-byte PKID case and asserts `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:record_formlink_list_size` throws `FormLinkListError`.

- `Radicle/tests/test_npc_link_rows.cpp:NpcLinkRows.PackageAndHeadPartArePerSubrecordListsNotFields`: PKID and PNAM must each carry one list row. A second field-shaped row on the same subrecord is refused by the codegen overlap guard, and a read-only field row leaves add and remove unoffered.

- `Radicle/tests/test_npc_link_rows.cpp:NpcLinkRows.EmptyPackageListAnchorsAfterItsLastXEditOrderPredecessor`: the first package must land after the last present xEdit-order predecessor, AIDT here (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` FO4:10399, 10400), not at the end of the record. The fixture carries a PNAM after AIDT (Head Parts follow Packages, FO4:10417), and the test asserts PKID lands between them, so an end-of-record append fails; without that PNAM the two placements produce the same bytes.

- `Radicle/tests/test_npc_link_rows.cpp:NpcLinkRows.EmptyListsAnchorAfterTheWholeAttackRun`: xEdit's `wbAttackData` repeats ATKE, ATKW, ATKS and ATKT after ATKD (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` FO4:4073-4123), so the first element of each list must land after ATKT, not after ATKD. The trailing HCLF is in none of the three anchor sets (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_formlink_lists.inc` rows `NPC_\Packages`, `NPC_\HeadParts`, `NPC_\AttachParentSlots`), so the element must sit between ATKT and HCLF; an append-at-end placement would put it after HCLF and fail the same assertion.

- `Radicle/tests/test_npc_link_rows.cpp:NpcLinkRows.EmptyAttachParentSlotsAnchorsAfterTheDestructibleRun`: the APPR anchor set carries the whole destructible run, so a first attach parent slot must land after DSTF rather than after DEST (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas` FO4:10404).

- `Radicle/tests/test_npc_link_rows.cpp:NpcLinkRows.EmptyPackageListRefusesAnInsertWithNoAnchor`: PNAM is not a PKID predecessor, so a record with no anchor must fail closed rather than append a package out of order.

Open: `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_lists.cpp:packed_formlink_list_path` accepts only `packed_array` lists, so `Radicle/src/c_api_fields.cpp:radicle_plugin_set_record_formlink` no longer resolves `NPC_\Package`; PKID and PNAM are reached through `radicle_plugin_formlink_list_set`, `radicle_plugin_formlink_list_insert`, `radicle_plugin_formlink_list_remove` and `radicle_plugin_formlink_list_clear` (`Radicle/src/c_api_fields.cpp:list_descriptor`), the same entry point `RACE\MalePresets` uses. Widening that fallback to every storage would change the behaviour of the per-subrecord lists that already exist and is not done here. The count overload is not affected: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:record_field_count(plugin, FormKey, std::string_view)` resolves a path through `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/formlink_lists.hpp:formlink_list_descriptor(Signature, std::string_view)` rather than the packed-only helper, because a count is storage-agnostic and the per-subrecord lists were otherwise unreachable by path. The object template `OBTS` keyword and include arrays stay unrowed for NPC_, as for ARMO, WEAP and FURN. Nothing in this change was compiled on the authoring machine; CI is the first compiler, and no `*_real.cpp` test names `NPC_\Packages` or `NPC_\HeadParts` yet.
## Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:fixed_string_bytes

- `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:RACE` gains `RACE\MovementTypeNames` (`MTNM`), the last RACE gap that needed a storage kind: xEdit declares `wbRArrayS('Movement Type Names', wbString(MTNM, 'Name', 4))` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11202`, a run of four-byte names with no terminator, and until now `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:STRING_FORBIDDEN` forbade the numeric keys a width would need while `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:slot_string_bytes` required a NUL inside the slot, so `Walk` could not be addressed.
- The row is `repeated: true`, not strided: `wbRArrayS` builds a `TwbSubRecordArrayDef` (`Core/wbInterface.pas:8476`, class at `:5957`), which is a subrecord array -- one `MTNM` subrecord per name -- and not `wbArrayS`'s packed `TwbArrayDef`, the shape `RACE\MorphGroupSliders` (`MPGS`) uses. Every official master confirms it: 110 RACE records across `Fallout4.esm` (45), `DLCCoast.esm` (15), `DLCNukaWorld.esm` (16), `DLCRobot.esm` (8), `DLCworkshop01.esm` (23), `DLCworkshop02.esm` (2) and `DLCworkshop03.esm` (1) carry exactly five `MTNM` subrecords, all 550 of them four bytes, in the order `WALK`, `RUN1`, `SNEK`, `BLDO`, `SWIM`. So index N is the Nth `MTNM` subrecord, the same one-row-per-occurrence shape as the `SPLO` array of `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:3285`, which is also a `wbRArrayS` and is already rowed `repeated: true`. A `stride: 4` row would address the same five names on this data but would report a three- or five-byte payload as `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots`'s `misaligned` (no slot at all, `ScalarMutationStatus::subrecord_missing` on a write) instead of the width error the storage owes, and it would need `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_slot_bytes` to cut the element out of the payload.
- The storage kind is `ScalarStorage::fixed_string` (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp`), chosen by the generator whenever a `kind: string` row carries `payload_size`, which leaves `STRING_FORBIDDEN` and becomes the width; the row must be whole-payload (`Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py` rejects an `offset` with `fixed-width string payload_size must cover the whole payload`), so `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarDescriptor::payload_size` is both the slot width and the exact payload size `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` already checks for a whole-payload row. A zstring row is unchanged: no `payload_size`, same `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:slot_string_bytes` NUL rule, same `data = encoded` write.
- `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:fixed_string_bytes` is the single width gate, called from both `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes` and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_slot_bytes`, and raises the existing `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` (`has unexpected binary width`) for a payload that is not exactly the width -- shorter and longer alike. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_shape` takes `shape.width` from `payload_size` for this storage (`Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_storage_size` stays 0, as for zstring), so a wrong-width `MTNM` is `malformed` in `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` before any slot exists and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` reports `invalid_scalar_storage` rather than decoding it. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:decode_scalar` returns the width bytes verbatim, and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:encode_scalar` accepts only a value of exactly that many characters -- xEdit itself pads a short value with NULs and truncates a long one (`Core/wbInterface.pas:15697-15713`), but Radicle refuses both, because padding invents bytes the author did not write and truncating drops them, and every stored name in the official masters is exactly four characters. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_descriptor` also excludes the new storage from signature-only resolution, like zstring, since a string row is addressed by path.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` treats `fixed_string` as a string, so `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:set_record_string` is the setter (whole-payload replacement, `data = encoded`, which is size-preserving here) and `set_record_scalar` refuses it as "not a string field"; the existing `sits in a fixed-size slot and cannot be written generically` guard keeps covering the embedded case the generator now rejects outright.
- Generated files were regenerated, never edited: `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc` gains the row through `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py`, and `Radicle/tools/parity_matrix.py:main` regenerated `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` (RACE string rows 12 to 13, repeated count 80 to 81; the storage column lists scalar rows only, so `fixed_string` does not appear there). The generator's own suites changed with it: `Radicle/tools/test_field_address_codegen.py:SchemaCodegenTests.test_string_fields` no longer rejects `payload_size` on a string row, and `Radicle/tools/test_localized_row_codegen.py:LocalizedRowTests.test_a_payload_size_makes_a_whole_payload_fixed_width_name` covers the new form, the zstring default without a width, the non-positive widths and the offset rejection. The new case lives in the second file because it is the string-row suite of `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py` and `Radicle/tools/test_field_address_codegen.py` is at the 750-line limit, so it may only shrink.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_race_weap_rows.cpp:WP9RaceWeapRows.MovementTypeNamesAreFourByteNames` pins the row (subrecord `MTNM`, `fixed_string`, `payload_size` 4, offset 0, whole-payload, repeated), reads a synthetic RACE carrying three four-byte names back as `WALK`, `RUN1` and `SWIM`, writes the middle one to `FLY1` through `Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/mutation.hpp:set_record_string` and rereads the three `MTNM` payloads, so an off-by-one slot or a write that spilled into a neighbour fails. `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_race_weap_rows.cpp:WP9RaceWeapRows.MovementTypeNamesRefuseAnotherWidth` is the negative half: a three-byte and a five-byte `MTNM` raise `ScalarError` from `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:record_field_count` and from a write, a five-character and a three-character value raise it from `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:encode_scalar` with the payload unchanged, the same value writes back as `ScalarMutationStatus::unchanged`. `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_race_weap_rows.cpp:WP9RaceWeapRows.ZstringRowsKeepTheTerminatorRule` (renamed from `FixedWidthStringsKeepTheZstringTerminatorRule`, which promised `fixed_string` coverage the case does not have -- it only touches the zstring `STAT\DistantLodLevel0` row) pins the rule the new storage must not loosen: a 260-byte `STAT\MNAM` with no NUL still raises `ScalarError` from `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:slot_string_bytes` through `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes`.
- Corpus: the seven official masters listed above were read from the local Fallout 4 install to settle the subrecord shape and the four-byte width; `CheckErrors.VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings` and the parity matrix are what CI re-checks. Nothing in this lane was compiled on the authoring machine; CI is the first compiler.
## Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:header_segment

FO4 `MODT` model information is a payload whose own leading words count its arrays, and `header_segment` resolves one of those arrays. xEdit builds the subrecord in `wbModelInfo` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8918`): for `wbGameMode >= gmTES5`, which FO4 is, the `else` branch at `:8938` returns `wbUnion(aSignature, aName, wbModelInfoDecider, ...)` (`:9014`) whose main arm `NewModelInfo` (`:8962`) is a struct of `wbArray('Counters', wbInteger('Counter', itU32, nil, nil, cpIgnore), -1, ['Textures', 'Addon Nodes', 'SRGB', 'Materials'], cpIgnore)` (`:8970`), then `wbArray('Textures', TextureFile)` (`:8976`) with `.SetCountPath('Counters\[0]', True)` (`:8977`), `wbArray('Addon Nodes', wbInteger('Addon Node', itU32))` (`:8981`) with `Counters\[1]` (`:9000`) and `wbArray('Materials', MaterialFile)` (`:9006`) with `Counters\[3]` (`:9007`); `SRGB` (counter 2) has no array of its own. An element count of `-1` is xEdit's length-prefixed variable-size array — `ArrayDef.PrefixSize` is read at `Core/wbImplementation.pas:21939` and written at `:22171` — so `Counters[0]` is the first counter *after* the prefix and the leading word is how many counter words follow rather than a counter itself. The layout the rows implement is therefore: `u32` counter count k, then k counter words at byte offsets 4, 8, …, then Textures at `4 * (1 + k)` with 12-byte entries, then Addon Nodes with 4-byte entries, then Materials with 12-byte entries. An entry is `{u32 File Hash; 4-char Extension; u32 Folder Hash}` (`:8946-8952`). A counter whose index is not below k is absent, which is how a k=3 payload carries Textures and Addon Nodes and no Materials at all.

The arm also depends on the record's form version: `wbModelInfoDecider` (`:5646`) answers arm 3 for `Version >= 40` unless the first word exceeds 8 ("arbitary limit of 8 supported headers for now"), answers a flat texture array for 38-39 and opaque bytes below 38. The rows therefore carry `min_form_version` 40, and `header_segment` refuses `k == 0` and `k > Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:k_max_header_counters` (8), which is exactly the arm-1 boundary. Every refusal returns `std::nullopt`, so a payload that is not the modelled arm exposes no slots at all instead of being mis-read, see `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots`.

The walk itself: for the record and subrecord, `header_segment` collects the arrays with a nonzero `segment_count` from `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:CountedArrayDescriptor`, in `segment_index` order, and accumulates `count * stride` from the end of the header, reading each present segment's count from `counter[count_word]`. It requires the segments to be a complete, distinct `0..n-1` set, the total to land exactly on the end of the payload, and each count to be no larger than the bytes still left in the payload divided by that segment's stride, which bounds the accumulate as well: `base` can never pass the end of the payload, so the final equality check stays exact and the multiply cannot wrap. This is the same shape `Radicle/src/schema/formlink_segments.cpp:packed_segment` gives the FSTS `DATA` segments, where the counters live in a separate `XCNT` subrecord and the segments are all four bytes wide; here the counters are the payload's own header words and the strides differ per segment.

Corpus evidence (read-only scan of `Fallout4.esm` and the six official DLC masters, 44,092 MODT payloads): every payload tiles exactly under k=2 (320 payloads), k=3 (1,840) or k=4 (41,932); k is never 1, 5, 6, 7 or above 8; every record version is 40 to 131, so no corpus record exercises the arm gate; no record carries two MODT subrecords. Texture extensions are `dds` NUL-padded to four bytes (314,814 entries, plus one all-zero entry), material extensions are `bgsm` (92,527) and `bgem` (1,411) with no terminator at all, texture counts reach 210, addon node counts reach 30 and the SRGB counter takes values 0 to 92, so it is not a boolean flag.

Insert and remove are refused for a segment by `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:counted_array_subrecords`: the count lives in the payload header, so the whole-payload counter write `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_counted_element` performs would rewrite the wrong bytes, and moving one element would have to shift every later segment. Reads and member writes go through the ordinary scalar slot path, which is why the header words are not rows of their own: they are counts, like a count subrecord, and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:is_counted_array_count_subrecord` already refuses plain writes to those.

## Radicle/include/fo4/schema/field_address.hpp:SegmentAddress

The per-row addressing for a header-counted segment is `SegmentAddress{count_word, index, count}`, carried by `FieldAddress::segment`, where `count` is how many segments share the payload and `count == 0` means the row is not a segment. Because the new member is last and defaulted, every generated row that predates this change renders byte for byte as before (`FieldAddress{false, 0, 0, FieldDiscriminator{}}`), and only segment rows append `SegmentAddress{...}` — see `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:render_address`. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/field_address.hpp:SegmentSpan` is what the resolver returns: the byte base and element count of one segment.

`Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` keeps the existing element loop and only chooses where it starts: a segment row takes `first` and `count` from `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:header_segment` and `step` from the row's stride, and a payload that is not the modelled arm `continue`s with no slot and without setting `misaligned` or `malformed`. That is deliberate: absent is not malformed, so `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` stays clean on a record whose MODT is an older format, `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` answers `subrecord_missing` (its `scalar_slots` guard), and the C API reports the field as absent rather than refusing the record.

## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:DOOR\ModelInfoTextures

Rows for the model information arm, one texture array, one addon node array and one material array per record, each with its members: `ModelInfoTextureFileHash`/`Extension`/`FolderHash` at offsets 0, 4 and 8 of a 12-byte element, `ModelInfoAddonNode` at offset 0 of a 4-byte element, and the three material members mirroring the texture ones. Every row carries `min_form_version` 40. 39 records get them: the ones whose authoring lists already allow the subrecord, which are also the records whose xEdit definition reaches `wbGenericModel` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:1030`, its `wbModelInfo(MODT)` at `:1035`) or, for MATT alone, calls `wbModelInfo(MODT)` directly (`:7975`): ACTI, ADDN, ALCH, AMMO, ANIO, ARTO, BOOK, CAMS, CLMT, CONT, DOOR, EFSH, EXPL, FLOR, FURN, GRAS, HAZD, HDPT, IDLM, INGR, IPCT, KEYM, LIGH, LVLN, MATO, MATT, MISC, MSTT, NOTE, OMOD, PROJ, SCOL, STAT, TACT, TERM, TREE, WEAP, WTHR, WRLD. Corpus carriers (of all records of that signature in the seven masters): STAT 23,563 of 23,579, MISC 3,246 of 3,258, SCOL 3,512 of 3,513, OMOD 2,147 of 3,990, ACTI 1,744 of 2,196, MSTT 1,106 of 1,106, TERM 1,031 of 1,074, FURN 783 of 783, CAMS 751 of 772, CONT 635 of 635, IPCT 616 of 865, BOOK 470 of 470, DOOR 433 of 444, HDPT 419 of 420, EXPL 336 of 342, ALCH 325 of 354, WEAP 262 of 484, ARTO 258 of 258, NOTE 252 of 252, KEYM 246 of 246, PROJ 234 of 239, ADDN 230 of 369, ANIO 168 of 168, GRAS 107 of 107, AMMO 100 of 106, LIGH 100 of 1,065, HAZD 78 of 78, TACT 74 of 74, FLOR 64 of 64, EFSH 47 of 70, LVLN 12 of 375, CLMT 10 of 11, WTHR 8 of 107, IDLM 2 of 51, INGR 1 of 1, MATT 1 of 156, TREE 1 of 1; MATO and WRLD have no MODT carrier at all in the corpus, so those two rows rest on the xEdit definition alone.

The extension is rowed as a `u32`, the four stored bytes little-endian, because a material extension such as `bgsm` fills all four bytes and has no terminator, while the string kind needs one: `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:slot_string_bytes` throws without a NUL in the slot, `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:STRING_FORBIDDEN` forbids the `stride` and numeric keys a fixed-width string member would need, and the same gap is recorded for `RACE\MovementTypeNames`. A fixed-width string storage would render these three rows as text; until it exists the raw value is lossless and `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_model_info.cpp:ModelInfoRowsDecodeEveryTextureAndMaterialEntry` pins the stored bytes.

Deliberately left out: `SRGB` (counter 2) has no array to row, the counter words are counts and not fields, `BPTD` has the same `wbGenericModel` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7695`) but no authoring list in this schema so it gets no rows, `RACE` carries MODT inside its head data and behavior graph structs (`:11197`, `:11200`, `:11230`, `:11236`) rather than at the top level, `DEBR` nests it inside `wbDebrisModel` (`:7390`), and `ARMA` reaches it through `wbTexturedModel`'s second signature. `Radicle/src/forms/proj_expl_hazd.cpp:empty_model_texture_data` already writes the empty MODT that HAZD creation defaults to — 20 bytes, k=4 and four zero counters — which is this layout with no entries; its comment calls the leading word a version, and the counter count is what it actually is. Mutagen is not an oracle here: its Fallout 4 model block keeps the subrecord opaque (`Mutagen.Bethesda.Fallout4/Records/Common Subrecords/Model.xml`, `<ByteArray name="Data" recordType="MODT" />`), so the rows rest on the xEdit definitions and the corpus scan alone.

## Radicle/tests/test_object_base_model_info.cpp:ModelInfoRowsDecodeEveryTextureAndMaterialEntry

Three tests carry this lane. `ModelInfoRowsDecodeEveryTextureAndMaterialEntry` catches a wrong header size, a wrong segment order, a wrong stride or a wrong member offset: the DOOR and CONT fixtures in `make_plugin` carry a two-texture MODT (DOOR also one addon node, CONT one material) and the test reads every file hash, extension and folder hash of every entry through `resolve_field_slots` and `decode_scalar`, pins the slot counts with `record_field_count`, pins the material extension's raw four bytes as `bgsm`, and requires no error-severity preflight issue and no issue naming a ModelInfo row on either record, plus no authoring-order issue on DOOR. `ModelInfoTextureWriteRoundTripsByteExact` catches a write that lands outside its element or a save that loses the header: it writes the second texture's file hash, asserts counted-array insert and remove throw `CountedArrayError`, and compares the reloaded MODT payload byte for byte with the expected payload. `ModelInfoPayloadsOutsideTheModelledArmAreAbsent` catches a mis-read instead of an absence: it feeds a Counters header that promises four counters and holds one, a texture counter of two over a payload holding one entry, a header of nine counters (the arm-1 boundary, which tiles but is not the modelled arm), and a valid payload on a form version 39 record, and requires each to expose no decodable slot, count zero on the addon node row, refuse the write with `subrecord_missing` and raise no preflight error. The count is taken on the addon node member rather than on a texture member because the form version 39 payload still tiles: `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` builds its two texture slots and only marks them invalid, and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:record_field_count` counts slots rather than valid slots, so the texture row answers 2 there while the addon node segment, empty in all four payloads, answers 0. The generator half is pinned by `Radicle/tools/test_counted_array_segments.py:CountedArraySegmentTests.test_segment_declaration_is_checked` and its five sibling tests, which catch a segment without its partner key, a count word or segment index outside the header bound, a segment that also declares a count subrecord, a form-version gate that does not reach the member rows, incomplete segment indexes, two segments reading the same counter, an unsegmented array sharing a segment's payload, and the rendering of `SegmentAddress{...}`; that file is new because `Radicle/tools/test_field_address_codegen.py` sits at the 750-line guard, and it is registered in `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt`. Nothing in this lane was compiled on the authoring machine; CI is the first compiler.
## Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:ItemModRecordsSynthetic.EveryScalarRowDecodesOnTheFixture and Radicle/tests/test_scalar.cpp:ScalarSchema.WeaponDnamFieldsUseTheirPayloadAndEnumBounds (#602 CI)

Review of the `MODT` commit found three failing test expectations that a Python-only verification pass cannot see, none of them in the mechanism. `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:ObjectBaseRecordsSynthetic.ModelInfoRowsDecodeEveryTextureAndMaterialEntry` and `Radicle/tests/test_object_base_records.cpp:ObjectBaseRecordsSynthetic.ModelInfoPayloadsOutsideTheModelledArmAreAbsent` counted through the plural array paths (`DOOR\ModelInfoTextures` and friends), which are `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:CountedArrayDescriptor` rows: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:record_field_count` resolves scalar rows, FormLink rows and packed FormLink lists only and throws `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` for an unknown path, so both tests failed on the first compile. They now count through a member row, the shape `Radicle/tests/test_counted_array.cpp:CountedArray.ReadsEveryMemberOfEachElement` already uses for `REFR\WaterCurrentVelocityX`.

`Radicle/tests/test_scalar.cpp:ScalarSchema.WeaponDnamFieldsUseTheirPayloadAndEnumBounds` pinned `scalar_fields(WEAP)` at 63; the `MODT` member rows are in `k_scalar_fields` (only the array rows are in `k_counted_arrays`), so the count is 70. `Radicle/tests/test_achr_rows.cpp` (ACHR), `Radicle/tests/test_parw_rows.cpp` (PARW) and `Radicle/tests/test_story_manager_records.cpp` (SCCO) pin records outside the 39 and are unchanged, and no test pins a PET column list.

`Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:ItemModRecordsSynthetic.EveryScalarRowDecodesOnTheFixture` sweeps every scalar row of every fixture record with `ASSERT_NE(sub, nullptr)`; `NOTE` is one of the 39 records and its fixture carried no `MODT`, so the first `MODT` row aborted the test. The fixture now carries one, built by `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:note_modt` (one texture, one addon node, no SRGB, one material), so the rows are exercised rather than skipped. That payload tiles exactly (a 20-byte header for k=4 plus 12 + 4 + 12 bytes of entries) and sits between `MODL` and `ICON`, which is where the generated `NOTE` authoring order puts `MODT`, so `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:ItemModRecordsSynthetic.FixtureRecordsPassAuthoringPreflight` and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` stay clean on it.

## Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_field_bytes and Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:patch_scalar_field

Both helpers take only a payload and a `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarDescriptor`, so a header-counted segment row used to read and write at `ScalarDescriptor::offset` as if it were a payload offset. That is the same offset a non-segment repeated row uses (its array starts at `array_offset`, which every generated row leaves at 0), but a segment row's bytes start at its segment base, so a `MODT` member at offset 0, 4 or 8 landed on the payload's own counter words: `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:ItemModRecordsSynthetic.EveryScalarRowDecodesOnTheFixture` decoded the counter count where the addon node should have been, and it could not see the difference because it only asserts a non-empty, decodable span. Both helpers now add the segment base before the offset, so the field-bytes path and the slot path (`Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` plus `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:scalar_slot_bytes`, which every src reader and writer uses) agree on the same bytes.

The base comes from `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:descriptor_segment`, which cannot consult the record, because neither helper carries one. `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:shared_segment_layouts` therefore rebuilds the layout from the `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:CountedArrayDescriptor` rows that name the descriptor's subrecord, requires every record that declares segments for that subrecord to agree index for index, and refuses otherwise; `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:segment_span` then walks the counters exactly as `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:header_segment` does, and additionally refuses when the descriptor's own `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/field_address.hpp:SegmentAddress` (count_word, index, stride) disagrees with the layout it found. `header_segment` now shares `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:record_segment_layouts` and `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:segment_span` with the two helpers, so the record-scoped path and the descriptor-only path cannot drift apart. Today only `MODT` declares segments and all 39 records that carry it use the same layout (Textures 12 at counter 0, Addon Nodes 4 at counter 1, Materials 12 at counter 3), so the shared lookup is unambiguous; a schema that gave one payload subrecord two layouts would make the descriptor-only path answer absent rather than guess.

`patch_scalar_field` is not only a test helper in the same sense: `Radicle/tests/test_vegetation_real.cpp:EveryNewScalarPathEditsOfficialRecordsWithoutLosingData` edits every scalar row of every `GRAS`, `TREE` and `FLOR` record in the official masters through the slot path and then replays each edited row into the original payload with `patch_scalar_field` to rebuild the expected bytes. Those three records are among the 39 that carry `MODT`, so before this change the rebuilt payload put the new value at the payload's counter word while the record carried it in its element, and the byte comparison failed on the first `MODT` member row of each record.

Semantics of the two helpers on a segment row: the bytes are the first element of the segment, the same element every other repeated row reads. A payload that is not the modelled arm, and a segment whose counter is 0, return an empty span from `scalar_field_bytes` and raise `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:ScalarError` from `patch_scalar_field`, so a missing element is absent and never a counter word read as a value.

Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:ItemModRecordsSynthetic.ModelInfoSegmentRowsReadAndWriteAtTheirSegmentBase`, on the `NOTE` fixture whose `MODT` carries one texture, one addon node and one material. It reads the addon node (segment 1) and the material file hash (segment 2) through `scalar_field_bytes` and requires 42 and 0x71727374, writes the addon node through `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` and requires the reloaded payload to be byte for byte the fixture with 7 in that slot, and requires the addon node row of a payload whose addon counter is 0 to read nothing. Without the change all three read the payload's leading counter count (4) instead. The `Radicle/tests/test_item_mod_records.cpp:note_modt` fixture helper gained an addon node list so the empty segment case reuses it rather than rebuilding the payload. Nothing in this lane was compiled on the authoring machine; CI is the first compiler.
## Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias, Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:merge_alias_members, Radicle/include/fo4/forms/quest.hpp:replace_quest_alias (#602 C-17)

Replacement used to be an erase-and-reinsert of the whole alias range from `fo4::forms::encode_quest_alias`, so an alias carrying a member `QuestAliasCreation` cannot express lost it. The members that survive are the ones the caller's creation does not write: an `ALFI` on an alias whose creation leaves `force_into_alias` unset, an `ALID` on a location alias whose creation leaves `name` unset, a `CTDA`/`CIS1` run when `conditions` is empty, the reference alias extras, `ALCC`.

`replace_quest_alias` now walks the existing range with the same `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:inspect_alias_section` span the other mutations use, collects every member the caller's creation did not write, and hands that list to `merge_alias_members` together with the encoded alias. A member is written when the encoded alias carries its signature, or when it belongs to a run the encoded alias writes: the Fill Type union of the alias kind, the `CTDA`/`CIS1`/`CIS2` condition run and the `COCT`/`CNTO`/`COED` item run (`Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:member_run`, `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:run_written`). Runs are written as a unit because a leftover member rebinds to the new run rather than staying where it was: an `ALEA` kept beside a written `ALFE`/`ALFD` makes `Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_decode.cpp:decode_location_fill` see two Fill Type variants, a kept `CIS1` rebinds its string to whichever `CTDA` now precedes it, and a kept `COED` rebinds its owner, rank and item condition to whichever `CNTO` now precedes it. Everything else is kept, so an `ALFI` on an alias whose creation leaves `force_into_alias` unset, an `ALID` on a location alias whose creation leaves `name` unset, a condition run the creation does not write, the reference alias extras and `ALCC` all survive. The Fill Type test is keyed on the creation's kind as well as the existing kind, so a kind change that writes a fill also drops a preserved member that is a fill member of the new kind alone: a location alias's `ALCC` kept beside a written reference fill would make `Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_decode.cpp:decode_reference_fill` refuse the record: a Find Matching Reference fill built from `ALNA`/`ALNT` or `ALFE`/`ALFD` reports mixed Match Type selectors, and any other fill reports multiple Fill Type variants. A same-kind location replacement still keeps `ALCC`, because it is not a location Fill Type member.

Order comes from the xEdit FO4 definition at the pin the repo already uses (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10808-10889 @93cc0bc5` for the reference alias, `:10898-10924` for the location alias, `:10933-10936` for the collection alias), which is also the order `Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_encode.cpp` already emits in: `ALST`/`ALLS`, `ALID`, `FNAM`, `ALFI`, the Fill Type union (`ALFR`; `ALUA`; `ALFA`+`ALRT`; `ALEQ`+`ALEA`; `ALCO`+`ALCA`+`ALCL`; `ALNA`+`ALNT`/`ALFE`+`ALFD`/`ALCC`; `ALFL`; `ALFA`+`KNAM`; `ALEQ`+`ALEA`; `ALFE`+`ALFD`), `CTDA`/`CIS1`/`CIS2`, the extras (`KSIZ`, `KWDA`, `COCT`, `CNTO`, `COED`, `SPOR`, `OCOR`, `GWOR`, `ECOR`, `ALLA`, `ALDN`, `ALFV`, `ALDI`, `ALSP`, `ALFC`, `ALPC`, `VTCK`), `ALCC`, `ALED`. The two alias kinds disagree on `ALCC`: the reference alias nests it in Find Matching Reference, before the conditions (`:10861-10863`), while the location alias puts it after them (`:10923`), so `alias_member_rank` keys the order table on the kind. A collection alias has no order table at all, since `ALCS`/`ALMI` is the whole alias.

`merge_alias_members` is a two-way merge: it walks the encoded members in order and flushes each preserved member whose rank is lower, which places `ALFI` ahead of a written `ALNA`/`ALNT` fill and a preserved `CTDA` run ahead of a preserved `ALCC` on a location alias. It throws `QuestError` in two cases, both before any mutation, so the clone is discarded and the plugin is untouched: a preserved member with no rank in the new kind's table (an `ALFL` inside a reference alias, or any member carried across a change to a collection alias), and a preserved run whose ranks decrease (an `ALCC` sitting before the condition run it must follow).

A replacement that changes the alias kind rewrites the alias frame instead of merging it: `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias` drops `ALST`/`ALLS`/`ALCS`/`ALMI`/`ALID`/`FNAM`/`ALFI`/`ALED` from the preserved list when `creation.kind` differs from the kind the range starts with, because the frame belongs to the alias rather than to the caller's field set. Everything else is still preserved and placed by the new kind's order, so a reference-to-location replacement that writes a location fill drops the reference fill with the fill run, while one that writes no fill refuses the `ALFR` it has nowhere to put. The opposite direction, a location alias carrying `ALCC` replaced by a reference creation that writes a fill, drops the `ALCC` for the same reason and keeps the condition run. The kind is read from the range's first subrecord through `Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_internal.hpp:alias_kind`; `find_range` never returns a collection, so the existing alias is always a reference or location alias.

`Radicle/docs/QUEST_ALIASES.md` drops its "callers must not use replacement as a generic round-trip" caveat and gains a Replacement section with the same order, the two refusals, the kind-change rule and the both-kinds Fill Type test. It no longer claims a collection `ALCS`/`ALMI` run stays one run under replacement, which `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:find_range` makes unreachable, and the kind-change frame is described as the new kind's frame.

`Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias` re-runs `Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_decode.cpp:decode_quest_aliases` on the clone after the splice and before `mark_modified`, so a splice the decoder rejects throws `QuestError` with the clone discarded and the plugin untouched, rather than writing an alias no later decode can read.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.KeepsMembersTheCreationDoesNotWrite` builds a quest whose reference alias carries `ALFI` and whose location alias carries `ALID`, `ALFI`, an `ALEA` fill, a `CTDA`/`CIS1` run and `ALCC`, replaces both with creations that write a fill the aliases did not have (Find Matching Reference for the first, Find Matching Location for the second), and asserts the resulting member sequences (`ALST`, `ALID`, `FNAM`, `ALFI`, `ALNA`, `ALNT`, `ALED` and `ALLS`, `ALID`, `FNAM`, `ALFI`, `ALFE`, `ALFD`, `CTDA`, `CIS1`, `ALCC`, `ALED`), that each preserved payload is byte-identical to the one captured before the replacement, that the location alias now decodes as a `QuestFindMatchingLocationFill` rather than as two Fill Type variants, that both Alias IDs are unchanged, that the record still decodes, and that `fo4::write_plugin` after a read/write round trip is byte-identical. `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.ReplacesAWrittenConditionRunAsAUnit` reuses the same quest, replaces the location alias with a creation carrying one condition with no strings, and asserts the old `CTDA` and its `CIS1` are gone, the `ALEA` fill the creation does not write and `ALCC` stay byte-for-byte, and the written `CTDA` equals `fo4::serialize_ctda_condition` of that condition, so the test pins the rewritten payload instead of relying on `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/ctda.hpp:CtdaCondition::unknown3` defaulting to -1. That test covers the run rule through the condition run; the item run shares the same `member_run`/`run_written` path and is pinned by `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.KeepsAnItemRunWithCoedInOrderOnARename`. `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.DropsLocationClosestToWhenAReferenceFillIsWritten` replaces that quest's location alias with a reference creation writing a Find Matching Reference fill and asserts the member sequence `ALST`, `ALID`, `FNAM`, `ALNA`, `ALNT`, `CTDA`, `CIS1`, `ALED` (the `ALCC` is gone, the condition run is byte-identical to the one captured before), that the alias decodes as a `QuestFindMatchingReferenceFill` rather than throwing, and that the write/read round trip is byte-identical. `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.RefusesPreservedMembersThatCannotBeOrdered` pins both refusals (a reference alias carrying `ALFL`, and a location alias whose `ALCC` precedes its `CTDA`) and asserts the plugin bytes are unchanged. The three replacement tests and their fixtures moved from `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp` to `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp`, the replacement/mutation suite. Nothing here was compiled or run locally: CI is the first build.

## Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias, Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:merge_alias_members, Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:alias_member_rank (#602 C-17b)

A gate review of the previous commit found three gaps, all closed here. `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias` refused a preserved member only when the new kind's order table had no rank for it, so a kind change that wrote no fill still carried over the Fill Type members the two kinds share: `ALFA`, `ALEQ`, `ALEA`, `ALFE`, `ALFD` and `ALCC`. A location alias's `ALCC` is a location Closest To Alias field but a reference Find Matching Closest fill, and a reference `ALEA` (External Alias Reference) or `ALFE`/`ALFD` (Find Matching From Event) is a location External Alias or Find Matching Location fill, so the spliced alias decoded as a Fill Type the caller never asked for: `Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_decode.cpp:decode_reference_fill` reads `ALCC` as `QuestFindMatchingReferenceFill` and `Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_decode.cpp:decode_location_fill` reads `ALFE`/`ALFD` as `QuestFindMatchingLocationFill`, and both succeed, so the reinterpretation was silent rather than a decode failure. The preserve loop in `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias` now throws `QuestError` when the kind changed, the creation wrote no fill and the member is a Fill Type member of either kind (`Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:member_run`), before the clone is committed, so the plugin stays untouched. The `ALFR` and `ALFL` cases were already refused, through the missing rank in the other kind's order, and keep that behaviour.

`Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:merge_alias_members` compared the preserved members' ranks one signature at a time, but `CIS1`/`CIS2` and `COED` sit after their run head in the order tables, so a canonical `CTDA`,`CIS1`,`CTDA` run (reference-order ranks 18, 19, 18) or a `COCT`,`CNTO`,`COED`,`CNTO`,`COED` item list (reference-order ranks 23, 24, 25, 24, 25) threw "not in member order" although `Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_decode.cpp:decode_quest_aliases` accepts both. `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:alias_member_rank` now maps a run continuation onto its run head's rank (`CIS1`/`CIS2` to `CTDA`, `COED` to `CNTO`) before the table lookup. Both the monotonic check and the two-way merge insertion use that rank, so a preserved continuation ranks with the head of its run rather than after it.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.RefusesKindChangesOverSharedFillMembers` builds a location alias carrying only `ALCC` and a reference alias carrying only `ALEA` through the new `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:alias_with_members` fixture, replaces each with a no-fill creation of the other kind, and asserts both throw with the plugin bytes unchanged (both used to succeed and decode as a Fill Type the caller did not request). `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.RefusesOrDropsASpecificReferenceOnAKindChange` covers both `ALFR` branches of a reference-to-location change: no fill refuses with unchanged bytes, and a written Find Matching Location fill drops the `ALFR` and leaves `ALLS`, `FNAM`, `ALFE`, `ALFD`, `ALED`. `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.KeepsAConditionRunWithACis1InOrderOnARename` replaces a location alias carrying `CTDA`,`CIS1`,`CTDA` with a rename that writes neither conditions nor items and asserts the member order and that the CIS1 payload is byte-identical; the two CTDA payloads are not compared, only their presence and order. It threw before the rank change. `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:QuestAliasMutation.RefusesMutationsThatWouldJoinCollectionRuns` and `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:QuestAliasMutation.RejectsAliasMarkersAfterTailBoundary` moved to `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp` as `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp:QuestAliasCollectionGrouping.RefusesMutationsThatWouldJoinCollectionRuns` and `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp:QuestAliasBoundary.RejectsAddingAnAliasWhenTheTailAlreadyHoldsMarkers`, because the mutation file was close to the 750-line ceiling; both keep their assertions, use that suite's `collection_entries` and `quest_bytes` helpers, and the `quest_with_tail` fixture lost its now-unused `alias_after_tail` parameter. `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp:QuestAliasCollectionGrouping.RefusesMutationsThatWouldJoinCollectionRuns` sets the replacement creation's `id` to the replaced Alias ID, so its `replace_quest_alias` case reaches the adjacency refusal instead of the earlier Alias ID mismatch check. `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.KeepsAnItemRunWithCoedInOrderOnARename` replaces a reference alias carrying `COCT`,`CNTO`,`COED`,`CNTO`,`COED` with a rename that writes no items, and asserts the run survives in that order, that both items decode with their counts and their `COED` extras, and that the alias survives a `fo4::write_plugin` read/write round trip. `Radicle/docs/QUEST_ALIASES.md` gains the no-fill kind-change refusal and the rank-by-run rule in its Replacement section. Nothing was compiled or run locally: CI is the first build.

## Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias — residual: a no-fill location-to-reference change keeps reference-only members (#602 C-17b)

The no-fill kind-change refusal in `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias` covers Fill Type members only. A location-to-reference change that writes no fill still preserves members that mean nothing in the location kind and are read as reference alias extras by the new kind: `KWDA`, `CNTO`/`COED`, `SPOR`, `OCOR`/`GWOR`/`ECOR`, `VTCK` and `ALPC` (`Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_extras.cpp:decode_alias_extras`). A location alias carrying reference-only members decodes, because the location path never calls `Radicle/src/forms/quest_aliases_extras.cpp:decode_alias_extras` (only the reference path does). `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:member_run` returns `none` for them under both kinds. A same-kind replacement of such an alias is refused: `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:alias_member_rank` has no location rank for them, so `merge_alias_members` throws before the clone is committed. A location-to-reference replacement that writes no fill keeps them, because they have reference ranks (`KWDA` 22, `CNTO` 24, `SPOR` 26, `VTCK` 37). A lone `KWDA` is then refused by the post-splice decode (`QUST alias keywords require both KSIZ and KWDA`, `decode_alias_extras`), but a `KSIZ`/`KWDA` pair decodes as a keyword list, and a `SPOR` decodes as a spectator override: those are silent reinterpretations. Low risk, because xEdit never writes those members into a location alias (`source:xEdit Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10898-10924 @93cc0bc5`), so reaching it needs a hand-crafted plugin. Known residual, not fixed here.
## Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias — same-kind replace keeps every member the creation leaves unset (decision needed)

Not changed by this note: behaviour is as the code stands. `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias` drops an existing member only when `replaced` marks it: the encoded alias carries its signature, or it belongs to a run the creation writes (the fill union when `fill` is not monostate, `CTDA`/`CIS1`/`CIS2` when `conditions` is non-empty, `COCT`/`CNTO`/`COED` when `items` is non-empty). Everything else is preserved and merged back in. So a same-kind replace cannot clear a modelled field the creation leaves unset or empty: `keywords` (`KSIZ`/`KWDA`), `spectator_override` (`SPOR`), `observe_dead_body_override` (`OCOR`), `guard_warn_override` (`GWOR`), `combat_override` (`ECOR`), `linked_aliases` (`ALLA`), `display_name` (`ALDN`), `forced_voice` (`ALFV`), `death_item` (`ALDI`), `spells` (`ALSP`), `factions` (`ALFC`), `packages` (`ALPC`), `voice_types` (`VTCK`), `conditions`, `items`, `force_into_alias` (`ALFI`), a location `closest_to_alias` (`ALCC`), a location `name` (`ALID`) and the fill itself. A non-empty list replaces every member of its signature, so the only way to change a list is to write it again. `replace_quest_alias` has no path that removes a member because a field is unset.

Decision needed (Nomad): (A) treat the creation as the full modelled state, so a same-kind replace removes each modelled member it does not write and keeps only the unmodelled ones, refusing those it cannot place; or (B) keep the merge and add an explicit clear path for the lists and the fill. Default until decided: (B), the current behaviour. It blocks any editor flow that must clear keywords, spells, factions, packages, conditions or a fill on an existing alias.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.KeepsReferenceExtrasInOrderOnARename

A same-kind rename of a reference alias carrying `KSIZ`/`KWDA`, `SPOR`, `OCOR`, `GWOR`, `ECOR`, `ALLA`, `ALPC` and `VTCK` (fixture `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp:reference_extras_quest`) must keep each of them byte-identical, keep the reference member order (`ALST`, `ALID`, `FNAM`, the extras, `ALED`) and keep the decoded keywords, spectator and combat overrides, packages and voice types. Regression it detects: a replace that drops the extras because the creation does not write them, or that splices one of them ahead of the frame.
