## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_collection.cpp:QuestAliasReplacementPreservation.RefusesAKindChangeToACollectionWithResidualMembers

Replacing that same reference alias with a collection creation must throw `QuestError` and leave the plugin bytes unchanged. The frame members are dropped on a kind change, but the residual `KSIZ` reaches `Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:merge_alias_members` with no position in the collection kind (`Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:alias_member_rank` returns none for a collection), so the splice is refused. Regression it detects: a collection replacement that splices reference members into an ALCS/ALMI run or drops them without an error.

## Radicle/src/schema/condition_functions.cpp:condition_run_on

The FO4 Run On table is now schema rows: `Radicle/schema/fallout4/condition_functions.json` `run_on[]` holds one row per Run On value with its name, the parameter type of Parameter #3 for that value, and whether the Reference slot carries a form ID. `Radicle/tools/condition_function_codegen.py:load_run_on` validates the rows (unique ascending values, names, a parameter type that exists, a boolean reference flag) and `render` emits `k_generated_condition_run_on` into `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_condition_functions.inc`; `Radicle/src/schema/condition_functions.cpp:condition_run_on` is a binary search over it returning `nullptr` for an unknown value, exposed through `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/condition_functions.hpp:ConditionRunOn`.

xEdit sources: the 11 names are the Run On enum at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5197-5210`; Parameter #3 is typed by the Run On value because `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:5484-5494` (`wbConditionParam3Decider`) returns the Run On value as the union index into `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5215-5248`, where entry 5 (`:5221`) is the Quest Alias encoding, entry 7 (`:5223-5244`) the Event Data member codes and the other nine are plain `itS32`; `Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:5495-5512` (`wbConditionReferenceDecider`) selects the form ID variant of Reference only when Run On = 2, matching the edit-time clear in `wbConditionRunOnAfterSet` (`Core/wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:1310-1323`). Entry 7 is not a `TConditionParameterType` member, so `event_data_code` is a Radicle-side 51st parameter type (kind `other`, no targets); types 0..49 still mirror xEdit's enum in order. Parameter #3 is not validated or rendered anywhere yet, so the column records the rule rather than feeding a consumer.

Consumers: `Radicle/src/schema/form_links_ctda.cpp:ctda_formid_offsets` now gates the Reference offset on the row's `reference_form_id` instead of the literal `2`, and `Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:check_conditions` rejects a Run On value the table does not hold instead of comparing against `10`. Its message takes the range from `Radicle/src/schema/condition_functions.cpp:condition_run_ons` (the first and last row of the ascending table, `(0-10)` today), so a regenerated table changes the message with no hand edit; `Radicle/tests/test_check_errors_conditions.cpp:RunOnAboveMyKillerIsInvalid` pins the full message.

Corpus evidence, all nine official masters at `D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Fallout 4/Data` (130,611 CTDA payloads, every one 32 bytes): Run On values 0 to 10 all occur and none is above 10; every function index is in the table; 8,008 conditions carry a non-zero Reference at Run On 2 and none carries one at any other Run On.

Regressions: `Radicle/tests/test_condition_functions.cpp:RunOnTableMatchesXEditEnum` (names, values, unknown values return null) and `:RunOnParameter3AndReferenceFollowXEditRules` (parameter 3 and the Reference flag follow the Run On value); `Radicle/tests/test_ctda_alias_formids.cpp:CtdaReferenceRunOn` (the Reference form ID is remapped at Run On 2 and left untouched otherwise, through the real remap path); `Radicle/tools/test_condition_function_codegen.py` (row validation, plus the committed schema loading 51 types, 479 functions and Run On 0..10), registered with ctest as `radicle_condition_function_codegen`.

Still open: the switchable-parameter mask `k_ctda_reference_params` in `Radicle/src/schema/form_links_ctda.cpp` stays hand-kept, although it equals the reference/actor/package set of the generated table for all 63 rows and could be derived from `condition_function`; the Voice Type and Worldspace FLST-member signature sets (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:5178` and `:5180`) remain unmodelled; Run On 5 does not yet expose the alias index in parameter 3 to any consumer.
## Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:default_payload and Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:local_layout_valid (GMST string default and HDPT parts pairing, #602 WP-9 B-15 B-17 open items)

- `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:default_payload` and `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:inline_string_default`: the authoring default for GMST DATA is `00000000` (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:GMST`), which is the four-byte localized string ID. xEdit's union member for the `'s'` EDID prefix is `wbLString('Name', 0, cpTranslate)` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6938`), and `Core/wbInterface.pas:20972` `TwbLStringDef.GetDefaultSize` returns 4 only when the file is localized; otherwise it falls through to `Core/wbInterface.pas:15827` `TwbStringDef.GetDefaultSize`, which for `sdSize` 0 is `1 + Ord(ndTerminator)`, and `wbLString` passes `aTerminator` false (`Core/wbInterface.pas:7764`), so 1 byte, the empty inline zstring. `default_payload` therefore returns a single NUL byte when the plugin is not localized and the record's own bytes select a guard-matched localized string row for that subrecord, and the rule's declared default otherwise. Only a row with a discriminator guard can select the inline default: a condition-less localized row keeps the rule's declared default bytes, so a future unflagged row cannot silently lose them. The row consulted is `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:GMST\StringValue`, the `localized` zstring row whose `when` guard is EDID byte 0 equal to 115, so the discriminator stays in one place: `inline_string_default` asks `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:scalar_fields` for the record's rows and evaluates each row's guard with `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:record_discriminator_matches`, which is now declared in `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/field_address.hpp` (it was file-local). Regression: before this, `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:create_record` for `GMST` with an `'s'` editor ID in a non-localized plugin wrote four zero bytes, `Radicle/src/schema/scalar.cpp:decode_scalar` rejects that as not a single NUL-terminated string, `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` reported `invalid_scalar_storage`, `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:layout_valid` failed and the call returned `RecordCreateStatus::preflight_failed` with no record created at all. The `'i'`, `'f'`, `'b'` and fallback branches keep the four-byte default, and a localized plugin keeps `00000000`, because `inline_string_default` returns false for a localized plugin. No corpus evidence exists for the fixed case: all seven official masters are localized, and their 2,051 GMST records hold 1,216 `'s'` EDIDs with a four-byte DATA each (read-only scan, 2026-10-19), so the non-localized form rests on the xEdit pin alone. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:GameSettingStringDefaultIsInlineTextOutsideALocalizedPlugin` creates an `'s'` GMST (one byte of DATA, authoring-clean), an `'i'` GMST (four bytes) and an `'s'` GMST in a localized plugin (four bytes); `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:RefusesDefaultFieldsInLocalizedPlugins` keeps the rule's declared default for a FULL row in a non-localized plugin.
- `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:local_layout_valid` and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_authoring_record`: HDPT NAM0 and NAM1 must occur the same number of times. xEdit's `Parts` array is `wbRArray('Parts', wbRStruct('Part', [wbInteger(NAM0, 'Part Type', itU32, ...), wbString(NAM1, 'Filename').SetRequired]))` (`Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:7041-7050`); `wbRStruct` builds a `TwbSubRecordStructDef` (`Core/wbInterface.pas:8670`), whose ordered `CanHandle` starts the struct only on its first member, NAM0 (`Core/wbInterface.pas:11555-11563`), and whose load loop assigns the members in order and stops at `MemberCount` (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:21524`), so a Part is one NAM0 followed by one NAM1 and `AddRequiredElements` creates exactly those two for a new Part (`Core/wbImplementation.pas:21269`). The pairing is declared once, as `paired_with` on the NAM0 rule in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:HDPT`, which `Radicle/tools/record_schema_codegen.py:load_constraints` validates as another subrecord of the same record and `Radicle/tools/record_schema_codegen.py:render` emits as `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc:k_generated_subrecord_pairs`. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:mismatched_subrecord_pair` reports unequal counts for `preflight_authoring_record` as `subrecord_count_mismatch`, which is what `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:authoring_clean` reads. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp:worsened_subrecord_pair` returns the first generated pair whose count distance grows from the before span to the after span; both spans must be indexed like the rule table, and that return-value explanation lives here rather than in the header. `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:add_with_rules` and `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:remove_with_rules` call it only after `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:editable` has accepted the target: the check refuses a single edit of a paired subrecord that would introduce or widen an imbalance with `unknown_order`, while a pre-existing imbalance never blocks an unrelated add or remove, an edit that leaves the distance unchanged is allowed, and an edit that reduces it is allowed. With the generated rules that path is unreachable for HDPT: both NAM0 and NAM1 are `maximum` 65535 with `uncounted` false in `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:HDPT` (see `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc`), so `editable` is false and `add_with_rules` and `remove_with_rules` answer `not_authorable` before the balance check runs. The single-subrecord refusals therefore come from `editable`, not from `worsened_subrecord_pair`; head parts cannot be authored one subrecord at a time through the generated rules, and the pair check is reachable only through a caller-supplied rule table that marks both paired subrecords editable. Corpus (read-only scan of Fallout4.esm and the six official DLC masters, 2026-10-19): 420 HDPT records, 294 NAM0 and 294 NAM1, counts (0,0) in 230 records, (1,1) in 86 and (2,2) in 104, and no record with unequal counts. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_authoring.cpp:HeadPartPartsRefuseGeneratedAddAndRemoveAsNotAuthorable` (the generated rules make a single NAM0 add or remove `not_authorable`, a record with two NAM0 and one NAM1 stays not authoring-clean, and an unrelated `DATA` add is accepted); `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_small_records.cpp:HeadPartPairEditsFollowTheExplicitEditableRules` passes an explicit rule table that marks NAM0 and NAM1 editable and drives both authoring paths through all five directions: an add that worsens the imbalance is refused as `unknown_order`, an add that pairs the extra entry is allowed, a remove from the larger side is allowed, a remove from the smaller side is refused as `unknown_order`, and a remove of the unpaired TNAM leaves the pair distance unchanged and is allowed; `Radicle/tests/test_preflight.cpp:PairCountsWorsenOnlyWhenAnEditMovesThemApart` checks that adding to a balanced pair and widening an existing imbalance are reported, while pairing the extra entry or editing an unrelated subrecord is not; and `Radicle/tests/test_actor_support_records_real.cpp:EveryBatchRecordMatchesItsAuthoringAndDecodesEveryRow`, which now also asserts the generated pairs on every shipped HDPT record of all seven masters.
- `Radicle/tools/record_schema_codegen.py:render`: the generated `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc:k_generated_subrecord_pairs` table is emitted as `inline constexpr std::array<SubrecordPairConstraint, 0> k_generated_subrecord_pairs{};` when the schema declares no `paired_with` rows, instead of a zero-length C array initialised with `= {}`, which is ill-formed C++. `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/record_constraints.hpp` includes `<array>` for that form and both range-for consumers accept either. Regression: a schema whose only authoring record has no paired subrecord used to produce a file the compiler rejects; `Radicle/tools/test_localized_row_codegen.py:RecordPairCodegenTests` covers the empty and non-empty renderings.
- `Radicle/tools/record_schema_codegen.py:render` now shards the rule table, and the record table if it ever crosses the limit. `k_generated_subrecord_authoring_constraints` holds 1,650 entries and one file was over the 750-line limit, so `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc` stays the include point at 443 lines and `#include`s `..._subrecord_authoring_constraints_shard00..02.inc` inside the array, the shape `Radicle/tools/formlink_schema_codegen.py:render` already uses: shards are included in order so every index stays an offset, a shard never splits a record's rules, and each stays under 750 lines (600 entries plus the header comment; the current shards are 590, 592 and 468 entries). `Radicle/tools/record_schema_codegen.py` also writes `newline="
"`, so regenerating on Windows no longer produces CRLF, and its `--check` reads the parent and every shard and reports an orphan shard left by a rename. Tests: `Radicle/tools/test_localized_row_codegen.py:RecordShardCodegenTests` (700 records split into two ordered shards that both stay under the limit and declare the entries in order, a short table staying inline); with the split limit lifted the first assertion fails `0 != 2`. `Radicle/tools/test_localized_row_codegen.py:RecordShardCheckTests` drives `main` over the same 700-record schema: a drifted rule shard and a drifted parent each report their own path and exit 1, an orphan `..._subrecord_authoring_constraints_shard02.inc` reports as an orphan, and the writer repairs the drift and deletes the orphan so the next `--check` is clean.

## Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:record_discriminator_matches (#602 AECH)

`Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:record_discriminator_matches` now takes a slot ordinal and matches the *n*-th occurrence of `FieldDiscriminator::subrecord`, instead of returning false for every record in which that subrecord occurs more than once. `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` counts the occurrences up front: exactly one keeps the previous record-level guard (ordinal 0), more than one switches to per-ordinal, so the *n*-th candidate subrecord of the guarded signature is compared with the *n*-th occurrence of the `when` subrecord and the row addresses that same ordinal. When the two counts disagree the guard fails for every slot, so the row stays unsized and hidden rather than reading a neighbouring element's bytes. The ordinal comes from `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:ordinal_of` and the counts from `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:count_occurrences`; both scan `Record::subrecords` and allocate nothing, and both are reached only for an external guard whose `when` subrecord repeats. Why a single `when` occurrence stays record-level: the NAVI rows are repeated on NVMI (up to 7799 occurrences in one record) and guarded on one NVER, so a strict per-ordinal rule would hide `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NAVI\LocationX`, `NAVI\LocationY`, `NAVI\LocationZ` and `NAVI\Preferred` on every navmesh record. Corpus scan of the seven official masters (read-only, session scratchpad): every NAVI record holds exactly one NVER, every SNDR record exactly one CNAM (673) and every GMST record exactly one EDID (2051), so those rows keep the behaviour they had. Residual gap, deliberate: a record with one `when` occurrence and several candidates still lets every candidate read that single discriminator; that combination does not occur for AECH, and the per-arm payload size below rejects a payload of another arm.

- AECH effect data rows (GARDEN-TOOLS #602 AECH, xEdit `wbRecord(AECH` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12206-12243`, union arms from `wbAECHDataDecider` at `:1464-1489`): ten `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:AECH` scalar rows on DNAM, all `repeated` and `existing_only`, each `when`-guarded on KNAM equalling its own type word. Overdrive (`AECH\OverdriveInputGain`, `AECH\OverdriveOutputGain`, `AECH\OverdriveUpperThreshold`, `AECH\OverdriveLowerThreshold`) reads f32 at offsets 4, 8, 12 and 16 of a 20-byte DNAM; State Variable Filter (`AECH\FilterCenterFreq`, `AECH\FilterQValue`, `AECH\FilterMode`) reads f32, f32 and a u32 enum at 4, 8 and 12 of a 16-byte DNAM, the enum carrying the four `wbEnum` names High Pass, Low Pass, Band Pass and Notch; Delay Effect (`AECH\DelayFeedback`, `AECH\DelayWetMix`, `AECH\DelayMs`) reads f32, f32 and u32 at 4, 8 and 12 of a 16-byte DNAM. The type words are the decimals of `Int64($864804BE)`, `Int64($EF575F7F)` and `Int64($18837B4F)` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12211-12213`: 2252866750, 4015480703 and 411269967, the same three values the existing `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:AECH\EffectType` enum already carried. Corpus (seven masters, read-only scan): 31 AECH records and 92 effects, with the KNAM count equal to the DNAM count in every record; KNAM words 2252866750 (23), 4015480703 (59) and 411269967 (10); DNAM 20 bytes in all 23 Overdrive effects and 16 bytes in the other 69, matching the counts recorded in the `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:ACTI and FLOR rows` bullet above, whose DNAM-union clause this entry supersedes. Enabled is 1 in all 92 effects, Filter Mode is 0 or 1, Delay MS is 30 or 100, so no row is written with a value the enum bounds reject. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_audio_records.cpp:EffectDataArmsFollowTheirEffectOrdinal` uses a three-effect fixture with one arm of each type, reads every member of every arm at its own ordinal, writes `AECH\FilterQValue` on the second effect and checks that the first and third DNAM payloads come back byte-identical and that an Overdrive row on the Filter effect and a Filter row on the Overdrive effect both report absent and refuse the write with `subrecord_missing`; `Radicle/tests/test_audio_records.cpp:EffectDataArmsHideWhenTheTypeCountDisagrees` uses two KNAM against three DNAM (two Overdrive payloads under one Overdrive type word, so pairing by value rather than by ordinal would show a row) and checks that every union row is hidden on every ordinal while `AECH\EffectEnabled` still decodes all three payloads. `Radicle/tests/test_audio_records.cpp:any_row_text` replaces the first-subrecord reader in the row-coverage test so a guarded row passes when any ordinal decodes. `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json` was the only source edited; `Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_scalar_fields.inc` and `Radicle/docs/FO4_PARITY.md` were regenerated by their scripts. Nothing in this lane was compiled on the authoring machine; CI is the first compiler.
## Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_stream and Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTag (#602 SWF tag payloads)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload` now decodes the payload head of the shape, bitmap, font, text, sound and Scaleform tags into derived views on `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTag` (`shape`, `bitmap`, `font`, `text`, `sound`, `exporter_info`, `external_image`, `font_texture`), and `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:SwfTag::clear_decoded` resets them. `SwfTag::payload` is untouched and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:write_swf` still serialises it verbatim, so nothing here can reach a written movie; `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:replace_tag_payload` re-decodes the new fields like the old ones.

Every layout comes from a source that was read for this lane, not from a corpus sample:

- AVM1 tags, from the **SWF File Format Specification version 19** (Adobe, 2012), read as the `swf-spec-19.pdf` copy mirrored at `open-flash.github.io/mirrors/swf-spec-19.pdf`. `DefineShape` 2 / `DefineShape2` 22 / `DefineShape3` 32 are ShapeId UI16 + ShapeBounds RECT; `DefineShape4` 83 adds EdgeBounds RECT and a flags byte of UB[5] reserved plus UsesFillWindingRule, UsesNonScalingStrokes, UsesScalingStrokes, which is why `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfShape` carries `has_edge_bounds`/`edge_bounds`/`flags`. `DefineBitsLossless` 20 and `DefineBitsLossless2` 36 are CharacterID UI16, BitmapFormat UI8, BitmapWidth UI16, BitmapHeight UI16, and BitmapColorTableSize UI8 only when BitmapFormat = 3, which is why `SwfBitmap::color_table_size` is optional. `DefineFont` 10 has **no** NumGlyphs field: FontID UI16 is followed by the OffsetTable, and the spec says the glyph count is the first offset divided by two, because each offset is the byte distance from the start of the offset table to that glyph's shape, so `SwfFont::glyph_count` is derived that way and an odd first offset is malformed. `DefineFont2` 48 is FontID UI16, FontFlags UB[8], LanguageCode UI8, FontNameLen UI8 + FontName, NumGlyphs UI16, OffsetTable of UI16 or UI32 by FontFlagsWideOffsets, CodeTableOffset, and `DefineFont3` 75 is the same layout with FontFlagsWideCodes required to be 1, so `SwfFont` keeps `flags`, `language`, `name`, `wide_offsets` and `wide_codes`. `DefineText` 11 and `DefineText2` 33 are CharacterID UI16, TextBounds RECT, TextMatrix MATRIX, GlyphBits UI8, AdvanceBits UI8 and TEXTRECORDs terminated by an all-zero flags byte, with an RGBA record colour in a DefineText2 and RGB in a DefineText. `DefineSound` 14 is SoundId UI16, one byte of SoundFormat UB[4] / SoundRate UB[2] / SoundSize UB[1] / SoundType UB[1], SoundSampleCount UI32 and SoundData. RECT (UB[5] Nbits, four SB[Nbits], padded to a byte) and MATRIX (HasScale and HasRotate flag bytes with their own bit widths, then NTranslateBits and two SB values) are read bitwise by `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:read_rect` and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:read_matrix_at`, the same MSB-first order `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:BitReader` already used for the frame rectangle.
- Scaleform extension tags 1000 and up, which the SWF spec does not define, from the **Scaleform GFx SDK sources**: `ExporterInfo` 1000 from `ExporterInfoImpl::ReadExporterInfoTag` in Scaleform GFx 4.2 `Src/GFx/GFx_LoaderImpl.cpp` (mirror `github.com/RetiredSDK/scaleform_sdk`, branch `scaleform_4_2`), which reads Version UI16, Flags UI32 **only when Version >= 0x10A** (Bit0 glyph textures present, Bit1 glyphs stripped from DefineFont tags, Bit2 gradient images exported), BitmapsFormat UI16, PrefixLen UI8 + Prefix, SwfNameLen UI8 + SwfName, and NumCodeOffsets UI16 + UI32[NumCodeOffsets] **only when Version >= 0x401**. `FontTextureInfo` 1002 from `GFx_FontTextureInfoLoader` in the same file and in GFx 2.1.57 `Src/GFxPlayer/GFxTagLoaders.cpp` (mirror `github.com/sigmaco/scaleform-gfx-v2.1.57`); the two SDK generations agree, and the layout is TextureID UI32, TextureFormat UI16, FileNameLen UI8 + FileName, TextureWidth UI16, TextureHeight UI16, PadPixels UI8, NominalGlyphSz UI16, NumTexGlyphs UI16 followed by NumTexGlyphs TEXGLYPH records of six floats, then NumFonts UI16 and NumFonts FONTINFO records of FontId UI16, NumGlyphs UI16 and GLYPHIDX[NumGlyphs] of two UI16 each. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload` reads NumFonts and then walks exactly that many FONTINFO records, so a truncated texture-glyph array or font list is malformed rather than silently accepted.
- `DefineExternalImage` is the one tag whose number moved between SDK generations, and Fallout 4 is on the later one. GFx 2.x declares it as **tag 1001** with CharacterID UI16 (`GFx_DefineExternalImageLoader`, GFx 2.1.57); GFx 4.x moved it to **tag 1009** and widened CharacterID to UI32 (`Tag_DefineExternalImage = 1009` in GFx 4.2 `Src/GFx/GFx_Tags.h`, loader in `Src/GFx/GFx_TagLoaders.cpp`), leaving 1001 unassigned. `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:kDefineExternalImageV4` (1009) is decoded with the UI32 form because that is the tag the shipped movies write, 1001 keeps the GFx 2.x UI16 form, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:tag_code_name` prints both as `DefineExternalImage`. Both forms read the same tail: BitmapsFormat UI16, TargetWidth UI16, TargetHeight UI16, then two length-prefixed strings. The SDK comment block documents only one string while both loaders read two (export name first, file name second); the code follows the loaders, not the comment.
- Length-prefixed strings are read by `Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:SwfReader::read_sized_string` (U8 length, then that many bytes, no NUL, length zero clears). Scaleform's `Stream::ReadStringWithLength` calls `Align()` first, but that only drops packed-bit state (`Align() { UnusedBits = 0; }`), so the strings are byte-contiguous — which is why the real 1009 payloads decode with no padding between fields.
- `SetBackgroundColor` 9 keeps the old three-byte result `0x00RRGGBB` and now puts a fourth byte in the top byte as `0xAARRGGBB`. The SWF spec defines BackgroundColor as RGB, three bytes, and no Scaleform source reads a fourth one (`SetBackgroundColorTag::Read` in GFx 4.2 `Src/GFx/GFx_SpriteDef.cpp` and `GFxSetBackgroundColorTag::Read` in GFx 3.x both call `ReadRgb`), so the alpha byte is a non-standard extension; every SetBackgroundColor payload in the shipped movies is three bytes (315 of 315, below), so the field is unchanged on real data.

Truncation and malformed payloads keep the typed behaviour `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_stream` already had: the decoder returns `SwfStatus::malformed_tag`, the raw bytes stay in `SwfTag::payload`, the following tags are still parsed, and the movie still round trips byte-identically. Nothing throws. A payload fails only when a field the decoder claims to read, a length-prefixed string, or a declared count does not fit; `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_text_records` also fails when the TEXTRECORD stream has no all-zero terminator or a record's glyph entries run past the payload, and a record whose type bit is not set is malformed. A tag whose head decodes is `ok` no matter what the body it does not parse contains — the SHAPEWITHSTYLE shape body, the glyph shape tables, the ZLIB bitmap and the sound data, and the glyph index values of a TEXTRECORD (counted, never listed), so the parsed fields and counts are the only source of rejection in this lane. On the 315 shipped movies checked on the authoring machine, no payload the reader accepted before is rejected; that is a corpus result, not a guarantee for other movies.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:summarize` gains `shape_tags`, `bitmap_tags`, `font_tags`, `text_tags`, `sound_tags`, `exporter_info_tags`, `external_image_tags` and `font_texture_tags`, incremented in `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:collect_tags` so a nested sprite tag counts like `tag_count` does.

Evidence, from a read-only local scan of `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` (315 movies, 2026-10-19, nothing stored in the repo): DefineShape 8520 tags in 280 movies, DefineShape2 777/87, DefineShape3 930/83, DefineShape4 592/52, DefineBitsLossless 46/5, DefineBitsLossless2 10/7, DefineFont3 35/9, DefineText 1/1 (`Programs/fonts_programs.swf`), DefineSound 3/3, SetBackgroundColor 315/315 all three bytes, ExporterInfo 4/4 (the four `Interface/Exported/*.gfx`, Version 0x401, Flags 0, BitmapsFormat 14), DefineExternalImage 1009 116/1 (`Interface/Exported/TutorialMenu.gfx`, CharacterID UI32, format 14, 26x26, export `Z.png`, file `Z.png.dds`). DefineFont 10, DefineFont2 48, DefineText2 33, tag 1001 and tag 1002 appear in none of them. Every one of those tags decodes with the layouts above, and the version-gated ExporterInfo split reproduces the exact payload length of all four files (TextEntry 21 bytes and 0 code offsets, SafeZone 24 and 1, TutorialMenu 256 and 58, RaceSex_menu 380 and 89), so no movie that parsed before this change reports `malformed_tag` now.

Deliberately left raw, with no cited layout in this lane: the shape body after ShapeBounds (SHAPEWITHSTYLE and its STYLECHANGERECORDs), the glyph shape tables of DefineFont/2/3, the compressed ZLIB bitmap data of DefineBitsLossless/2, the sound data of DefineSound, the glyph index values inside a TEXTRECORD, and the other GFx extension tags 1003 `DefineExternalGradient`, 1004 `DefineGradientMap`, 1005 `DefineCompactedFont`, 1006 `DefineExternalSound`, 1007 `DefineExternalStreamSound` and 1008 `DefineSubImage`, whose loaders were not read for this change.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp` (registered in `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt`) builds synthetic movies only — no shipped or third-party movie is read, stored or derived from. It pins one tag of each decoded kind (shape bounds and the DefineShape4 edge bounds and flags byte, the palette-size byte present for BitmapFormat 3 and absent for 4, the glyph counts of DefineFont 10/48/75 with their wide-offset and wide-code flags, the record and glyph-entry counts of DefineText/DefineText2, the DefineSound header, ExporterInfo, both DefineExternalImage forms and FontTextureInfo; the DefineText payload it builds uses 6-bit glyph indices and 7-bit advances, so each record's entry array ends off a byte boundary), the `summarize` counts, the fourth background-colour byte with the three-byte value unchanged, and a byte-exact round trip of one movie carrying all seventeen tags. One negative per code (sixteen: payloads cut mid-struct and counts that overrun the payload) asserts `malformed_tag`, the raw payload kept, the following tags still parsed and the byte-exact round trip. Two boundary cases the negatives cannot show stand on their own: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp:SwfTagDecode.ExporterInfoVersionGateSkipsFlagsBelow0x10A` (one ExporterInfo at Version 0x0109 and one at 0x010A) and `Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp:SwfTagDecode.DefineFontTenBoundAcceptsTheMinimumTail`. `Radicle/tests/swf_movie_builder.hpp` now holds the `SwfBuilder` and `wrap_body` fixtures shared with `Radicle/tests/test_swf.cpp`, which also had its placeholder 1000/1001/1002 payloads replaced by well-formed ones because those tags decode now. `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp` turns the new counts into per-movie `RecordProperty` numbers (`shape_movies`, `bitmap_movies`, `font_movies`, `text_movies`, `sound_movies`, `exporter_info_movies`, `external_image_movies`, `font_texture_movies`). The payloads those fixtures build are complete bodies, not headers: the four DefineShape fixtures end with a style block and an EndShapeRecord (`Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp:shape_tail`) and the two lossless fixtures carry a zlib stream, with the palette inside it for BitmapFormat 3, because `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:decode_shape_tag` and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap.cpp:decode_bitmap_tag` now parse a whole body; a fixture that stopped at the header made every test reading the all-kinds movie fail with `malformed_tag`.

Regressions the new tests detect: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp:SwfTagDecode.DecodesShapeBoundsForEveryDefineShapeVariant` catches a wrong ShapeBounds offset (reading the bounds where the flags byte is, or forgetting DefineShape4's EdgeBounds), `SwfTagDecode.DecodesLosslessBitmapHeaderAndPaletteSize` catches reading BitmapColorTableSize for a direct-colour bitmap and a swapped width/height, `SwfTagDecode.DecodesFontGlyphCountsForEveryDefineFontVariant` catches treating DefineFont 10 as if it had a NumGlyphs field, and a wrong offset-table entry width, which only its DefineFont3 case can show: an 8-byte tail sits inside the UI16 bound `2n+2` and outside the UI32 `4n+4`, while the DefineFont2 payload's 12-byte tail satisfies both, so a length bound alone can never discriminate a wrong width there. `SwfTagDecode.DefineFontTenBoundAcceptsTheMinimumTail` pins the DefineFont 10 bound from both sides, a two-byte glyph-shape tail after the offset table accepted and a one-byte tail malformed, which is the two extra bytes the old bound demanded on top of the spec minimum. `SwfTagDecode.CountsTextRecordsAndGlyphEntries` catches a drifted TEXTRECORD walk: because its payload's 6-bit glyph indices and 7-bit advances end each record off a byte boundary, the next record's flags byte is only read at the right offset if the walk rounds the bit position up to the next byte (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:BitReader::byte_position`); a floor there reads that flags byte out of the middle of a glyph entry and runs the record's glyph entries past the payload, which is the bug the real `Programs/fonts_programs.swf` tag exposed, `SwfTagDecode.DecodesSoundHeaderAndSampleCount` catches reading the packed sound byte as four bytes, `SwfTagDecode.DecodesScaleformExporterImageAndFontTextureTags` catches the 1009 UI32 character id and the ExporterInfo and FontTextureInfo field split at Version 0x0401, and `SwfTagDecode.ExporterInfoVersionGateSkipsFlagsBelow0x10A` catches the `Version >= 0x10A` Flags gate from both sides: the below-threshold payload read with Flags is malformed, and the at-threshold payload read without them reports BitmapsFormat 3 and two empty strings instead of `Menu`/`HUDMenu`, `SwfTagDecode.BackgroundColorKeepsTheFourthAlphaByte` catches dropping the fourth byte and catches a change to the three-byte result, `SwfTagDecode.SummarizesAndRoundTripsAMovieWithEveryNewTagKind` catches the new decoding reaching the writer at all, and `SwfTagDecode.TruncatedPayloadsKeepRawBytesAndParsingContinues` catches a decoder that throws, drops the payload, or stops the tag walk instead of reporting `malformed_tag` and carrying on.
## Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_source.cpp:LexesCommentsContinuationsAndDocComments

`Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp:Lexer::next` emits one `TokenKind::NewLine` for every line break outside parentheses or brackets, and a block comment is trivia: `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp:Lexer::skip_block_comment` consumes the delimiters and the body and stops at `/;`, leaving the line break that ends that line for the next call. The test asserted `lexed.tokens.front().position.line == 3u` even though its `;/ ... /;` block comment closes on line 2, so the first token is the `TokenKind::NewLine` at line 2, not `Scriptname` at line 3. Papyrus treats comment text as whitespace, so that line break is still a statement separator, and the doc-comment half of the same test already expects a `TokenKind::NewLine` after `{doc text}`. The test now skips `TokenKind::NewLine` tokens and requires the first code token to be on line 3, which still fails if the block comment's interior lines are not counted or its text is lexed. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_source.cpp:LexesCommentsContinuationsAndDocComments`.

## Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:check_links

Vanilla `Fallout4.esm` carries dangling links in slots the generated schema now proves: REFR `XRFG` (001A325C, 000939E3 and 000939E4 -> 000939E1; 0004BEF5 -> 000DB86D), REFR `XMSP` (002308BF -> 0022CE41), ACHR `XLCN` (0017610D -> 0002768B) and SCCO `SNAM` (000E9890 -> 000E9891). Because the slot is proven, `check_links` raised each as an error-severity `unresolved_link`, which turned `CheckErrors.VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings` red. `k_game_master_link_exemptions` in `Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:check_links` lists the (record signature, subrecord) pairs whose missing target is tolerated when the target is owned by the game master; it also absorbs the earlier RFGP `RNAM` and REGN `WNAM` game-master exemptions, which had the same condition. The DLBR `SNAM` exemption stays separate because it has no game-master condition. The exemption is deliberately narrow: a missing link in the same slot from a non-game-master owner, or in a different slot of the same record (for example REFR `XLCN`), still reports an error. Regression: `CheckErrors.DanglingGameMasterLinksAreExemptOnlyForKnownPairs` in `Radicle/tests/test_check_errors.cpp`.

The exemption also requires the referencing record itself to be owned by the game master (`hit.record.owner() == game_master` in `Radicle/src/graph/check_errors.cpp:check_links`): it exists because vanilla `Fallout4.esm` ships those dangling links, so a mod's own new record that links to an undefined `Fallout4.esm` form ID must still report `unresolved_link`, while a mod's override of a vanilla record (its FormKey owner is the game master) keeps the exemption. The same test covers both: a new REFR 01000840 in `Mod.esp` yields one error-severity `unresolved_link` for 000850:Fallout4.esm, and an override REFR 000840:Fallout4.esm yields none. Both fail if the exemption is keyed on the (record signature, subrecord) pair alone again.

## Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidates (QUST NNAM)

The scalar row `QUST\Description` (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json`) addresses NNAM as a non-repeated row. In a QUST, NNAM is also the display text of each objective: `Radicle/src/forms/quest_objectives.cpp:decode_quest_objectives_record` reads it after its QOBJ, and `objective_array_bounds` in the same file defines the objective array as first QOBJ up to ANAM. `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` counted every NNAM, so any quest with objectives set `duplicate`, and `Radicle/src/schema/preflight.cpp:preflight_record` raised `duplicate_scalar_subrecord` at error severity. In `Fallout4.esm` that was 176 QUST records with two or more NNAMs, and `CheckErrors.VanillaMasterHasNoErrorFindings` failed on them. `outside_objective_array` removes the NNAMs inside [first QOBJ, first ANAM) from the candidates, so the resolver, the preflight check and the writer in `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:write_scalar` all see the same set.

Vanilla evidence (read-only scan of `Fallout4.esm`, 1,336 QUST records): 1,079 have no NNAM. The other 257 have NNAMs only inside the objective array, with none before the first QOBJ and none after ANAM, and the xEdit definition of the quest Description sits after the alias block. So `QUST\Description` now reads as absent for every vanilla quest that has objectives, instead of reading an objective's display text. Quests without QOBJ keep every NNAM as a candidate, so their reads and writes are unchanged. Regression: `QustGeneralRows.ObjectiveDisplayTextIsNotTheQuestDescription` in `Radicle/tests/test_qust_general_rows.cpp`, which fails when an objective NNAM counts as a duplicate and also requires a second NNAM before the first QOBJ to still be flagged.

## Radicle/src/schema/behavior_layout.cpp:behavior_field_candidates (RACE MPGS)

The scalar row `RACE\MorphGroupSliders` (`Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json`) addresses MPGS as one non-repeated stride-4 array. In vanilla `Fallout4.esm`, a RACE carries one MPGS per morph group, each after its MPGN (nine records have more than one). Without scoping, `resolve_field_slots` set `duplicate` on those nine records, and `preflight_record` reported `duplicate_scalar_subrecord` at error severity. `first_occurrence` limits the candidates to the first MPGS, so the row addresses the first morph group. Records with no MPGS or one MPGS keep the same candidates as before. Regression: `WP9RaceWeapRows.OnlyTheFirstMorphGroupSlidersRowIsAddressed` in `Radicle/tests/test_wp9_race_weap_rows.cpp`, which fails when a second MPGS is counted as a duplicate and when the row reads a later group. Low: writes to a later group's MPGS are out of scope, so the row cannot edit them.
## Radicle/tests/test_sound_writer_real.cpp:EveryScalarStringAndLinkPathEditsFirstAndLastSlotsWithoutTouchingOtherBytes (formlink sweep)

The formlink half of `Radicle/tests/test_sound_writer_real.cpp:EveryScalarStringAndLinkPathEditsFirstAndLastSlotsWithoutTouchingOtherBytes` resolved `Radicle/src/schema/field_address.cpp:resolve_field_slots` against the pre-edit `original` record while writing into the already scalar-edited `sample`. The scalar sweep sets `SNDR\DescriptorType` (CNAM) to 1 on AutoWeapon records (CNAM 0xED157AE3), so `SNDR\BaseDescriptor` (BNAM) failed its discriminator guard on `sample` and `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer.cpp:set_record_formlink_field` returned `subrecord_missing` where the test expected `updated`. The loop now resolves against `fo4::find_record(sample, record.form_key)`, the same record the writer resolves, so an invalid live slot takes the existing `subrecord_missing` expectation and leaves the expected bytes untouched. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_sound_writer_real.cpp:EveryScalarStringAndLinkPathEditsFirstAndLastSlotsWithoutTouchingOtherBytes` on the masters holding AutoWeapon SNDR (Fallout4, DLCRobot, DLCCoast, DLCNukaWorld).

Member order pin: xEdit alias member ordering at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:10808-10889` and `:10898-10924` at 93cc0bc5.

## Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:AliasMemberRun

A run must be written as a unit: a leftover member rebinds to the new run.

## Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:alias_member_rank

A run member must rank with its run head: CIS1/CIS2 with CTDA, COED with CNTO.

## Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:merge_alias_members

Preserved members must already be in member order; otherwise this throws.

## Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias

A written fill run must also take a preserved fill member of the new kind. A kind change must rewrite the alias frame; a same-kind one must not.

Kind change and the frame (#602 r6): on a kind change the preserved list drops `ALST`/`ALLS`/`ALCS`/`ALMI`/`ALED` and also `ALID`/`ALFI` unless the creation writes them. The `ALID`/`ALFI` drop when the creation leaves `name` or `force_into_alias` unset is the chosen behaviour, not a bug: `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:RefusesOrDropsASpecificReferenceOnAKindChange` pins it (the location alias comes back as `ALLS`, `FNAM`, `ALFE`, `ALFD`, `ALED`). Keeping them would need a collection-target exception, because a collection alias has no `ALID`/`ALFI` order and `merge_alias_members` would throw on them. Documented in `Radicle/docs/QUEST_ALIASES.md` Replacement.

Kind change refusal (#602 r6): a preserved member the new kind's order does not allow is refused, not dropped. A reference alias carrying `VTCK` replaced by a location creation reaches `merge_alias_members` with `VTCK` preserved, which has no location rank and throws `QuestError` before the clone is committed. There is no drop opt-in yet; the caller rebuilds the alias with delete plus create. Empty creation fields keep the existing member (no in-place clear), which is the same rule the fill-run and condition-run checks already use.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:RefusesAKindChangeThatWouldCarryVoiceTypes` detects a kind change that silently drops a reference-only member (the old erase behaviour) or carries it into a location alias; it throws `QuestError` and leaves the plugin bytes unchanged.

## Radicle/include/fo4/forms/quest.hpp:replace_quest_alias

A kind change must rewrite the frame; an unset name or force_into_alias then drops ALID/ALFI.

## Radicle/src/forms/quest_alias_edit.cpp:replace_quest_alias (ordering invariant)

The spliced alias must decode before the clone is committed; the constraint is kept as a single line in source at the decode call.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:ctda_payload

Every form ID offset in this CTDA payload must stay null.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:alias_with_members

One alias of the given kind; extra members must already be in the kind's member order.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:unmodelled_alias_member_quest

A replacement must keep the ALFI, ALID, ALEA, CTDA/CIS1 and ALCC here.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:reference_alias_with_location_member

ALFL must not be placeable in the reference alias ordering.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:location_alias_out_of_member_order

Preserved members must be in member order: ALCC before CTDA is not.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:KeepsMembersTheCreationDoesNotWrite

ALFI must stay ahead of the written fill in the reference alias ordering. ALID, ALFI, CTDA/CIS1 and ALCC must survive; the ALEA fill must not, because a Fill Type union is one run.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:ReplacesAWrittenConditionRunAsAUnit

A written condition run must replace CTDA and CIS1; ALEA and ALCC must stay.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:DropsLocationClosestToWhenAReferenceFillIsWritten

ALCC must not survive a written reference fill: it is a reference Fill Type member.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:RefusesKindChangesOverSharedFillMembers

A location ALCC and a reference ALEA must not survive a no-fill kind change. ALCC is a reference Find Matching Closest fill member only (a location ALCC is Closest To Alias, outside the location Fill Type union), so the location-to-reference case is refused through the creation's kind. ALEA is a fill member of both kinds, so the reference-to-location case is refused through the existing kind.

## Radicle/tests/test_quest_alias_mutation.cpp:KeepsAConditionRunWithACis1InOrderOnARename

CIS1 must rank with the CTDA head of its run, so a rename that writes no conditions must keep the whole run.

## Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/parent_chain.hpp:validate_parent_chains

The parent-chain walk GardenEngine's `LoadOrderAcceptance` owned (issue #821): for every object in every file, follow `PexObject::parentClassName` through the loaded set and report the objects whose chain does not end. A name that is not in the set is `MissingParent`, a name already walked is `Cycle`, and a chain that reaches `depthLimit` parents without ending is `TooDeep` (default `k_max_parent_depth` 64, the C# limit). A parent name in `seedTypes` ends its chain, because those are the classes the caller knows outside the set; Radicle has no native-class list of its own, so the engine passes `PapyrusEventContract`'s seed types, which is why the seed list stays in the engine. Lookup is case-insensitive and the first object with a name wins across the files in argument order. That is not the rule `build_call_graph` resolves with: `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:build_call_graph` keeps scanning later files when the first same-named object lacks the function, while `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/parent_chain.cpp:validate_parent_chains` stops at the first object with the name. Calls on an inherited method (`self.InheritedFn()`) therefore stay unresolved, because the parent chain is never followed from a call site, so `unresolved_count` is inflated for normal inheritance. `chain` holds the parent names walked, the seed's parent first, including the name that closed the cycle or was missing, so a report can print the path it took. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_pex_analysis_c_api.cpp:CApiPexAnalysis.WalksParentChainsWithSeedsAndADepthLimit` (a clean chain ending at a seed type stays unreported, a missing parent reports its one name, both sides of a loop report a cycle of three names, and a limit of one reports `TooDeep` at depth one) and `CApiPexAnalysis.RejectsBadArguments`.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:build_call_graph (receiver and parent behaviour)

Read before exporting it, as #821 asked. A `callmethod`'s receiver is `args[1]`: `self` names the calling object (`selfTarget`), otherwise the declared type of the variable (parameter, local, variable, then property) names the object, and when no declaration matches the identifier itself is used as the object name (`MethodCallContract`'s rule). A `callparent`'s object is the caller's `parentClassName` and its function name is `args[0]`; `callstatic` takes `args[0]` as the object and `args[1]` as the function. Resolution scans the files in argument order for the first object with that name and the first state function with an equal name, and it never follows the parent chain: a `callparent` whose target function is declared on the grandparent stays unresolved. No walk means no cycle there, which is why the cycle and depth checks live in `validate_parent_chains` instead. `unresolvedCalls` counts every site resolution missed, `nativeCalls` counts resolved sites whose target function is native, and `roots` is every function no resolved site targets (the event derivation `Radicle/docs/code-notes/Radicle.md:Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/callgraph.hpp:PexCallGraph::roots` already documents).

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex_analysis.h:radicle_pex_callgraph_build

Exports the call graph and the parent-chain walk as ABI 56 so a non-C++ tool can read the census data `NativeCallSiteCensus` produced: `radicle_pex_callgraph_build` takes `radicle_pex` handles (a null entry means no file), and the handle answers totals, every call site, and the unresolved subset. A site reports its caller (file, object, state, function, slot) and caller names, the instruction index, the call kind, the target object and function names as written, `self_target`, `resolved`, `native_target`, and the target's indexes (all `SIZE_MAX` when unresolved). Sites keep the order `build_call_graph` produced: file, object, function, instruction, with state functions before the property handlers of the same object. `caller_slot` is `STATE` or the property handler slot, so a call inside a getter or setter is visible with the property as its caller name. Strings stay valid until destroy, and the handle copies them, so the `radicle_pex` handles may be destroyed first. The same header carries `radicle_pex_validate_parent_chains`, whose report exposes the finding rows, the flattened chain names and the checked-object count; `depth_limit` 0 means the default. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_pex_analysis_c_api.cpp:CApiPexAnalysis.BuildsEveryCallSiteWithKindTargetAndTotals` (self, parent and static sites, one unresolved and one native target, and the totals), `CApiPexAnalysis.MatchesNamesWithoutCaseAndResolvesAcrossFiles`, `ResolvesReceiversThroughDeclarations`, `StopsChainsAtTheDepthLimit`, `StopsChainsAtSeedTypesAndReportsSelfParents`, `CountsCallsInsidePropertyHandlers` and `TreatsNullFilesAndIgnoresGrandparentFunctions`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_vmad.h:radicle_record_vmad_scripts

The general VMAD reader `c_api_vmad.h` lacked: `ScriptAttachments` and `VmadValueBinder` decoded through `schema/vmad.hpp` but nothing else could. `radicle_record_vmad_scripts` takes an environment and one of its record handles, finds the record's single `VMAD` subrecord and decodes the leading script list with `fo4::read_vmad_scripts`; a record without one is `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, truncated or unknown data is `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR`, and a record from another environment is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The rows are a flat snapshot: scripts carry their flags, property count, the trailing byte count and the decoded `unsupported` flag; properties carry type, flags, the scalar value as `value_kind` plus that value's field, the leading `declared_element_count`, the array kind and the element range. Elements are flattened per property, one row per array element, and one row per struct member with `member_name` and `struct_index` set, so a struct array keeps both the member name and which struct element it belongs to (the C# binder refused structs as "not decoded"; `VmadStruct`/`VmadStructMember` already decoded them). A struct member that is not an object, string, int, float or bool, such as an array member, makes the whole property undecodable, so the reader reports it through the script's `unsupported` flag and reports the property with no rows: returning the scalar members alone would hide the dropped ones from the caller. A record the environment marked `undecodable` is refused with `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR` through `fo4::require_decodable` before the subrecord is looked up, because `NOT_FOUND` would claim its payload carries no VMAD. Names are converted to UTF-8 with `fo4::text::windows1252_to_utf8`, the same conversion `Radicle/src/c_api_placed.cpp:build_view` applies; string values are not converted, because the VMAD wire format stores them as UTF-8. `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad_read.cpp:fill_handle` raises that flag for both the struct and the struct-array forms when the property carries no `struct_elements`. `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:decode_structs` returns no value only when a member is not an object, string, int, float or bool, and an engaged vector otherwise, empty when the struct has no members or the array has a zero count, so an empty struct stays decodable and only an undecodable one raises the flag. `unsupported` and `trailing_bytes` are flags of the whole read and not of one script: `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad_read.cpp:radicle_vmad_scripts_script` copies both from the handle, so every script reports them, and a property the decoder cannot read ends the read there, which drops the scripts after it, leaves `radicle_vmad_script_count` below the count the file declares and leaves `trailing_bytes` at 0, while the scripts decoded before it also report `unsupported`. `index_in_property` is the row's position inside its property. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_vmad_read.cpp:CApiVmadReadTest.ReadsScriptsPropertiesAndObjectElements` (a synthetic plugin with a text property and a two-element object array, read through the environment), `CApiVmadReadTest.RefusesRecordsWithoutVmadAndBadIndexes`, `ReadsEveryScalarKindAndItsArray`, `ReadsPlainStructsAndStructArrays`, `ConvertsNamesFromWindows1252AndKeepsUtf8Values`, `ReportsTruncatedVmadAsParseError`, `ReportsUnsupportedPropertiesAndTrailingBytes`, `RejectsRecordsFromAnotherEnvironment` and `ReportsUndecodableRecordsAsParseErrors`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_script_set.h:radicle_script_set_resolve

Exports the resolver as ABI 55: `radicle_script_set_resolve` (with the optional per-root load indexes), `radicle_script_set_count`, `radicle_script_set_get`, `radicle_script_set_read` and `radicle_script_set_destroy`. It is built on `fo4::pex_analysis::script_set.hpp`, the resolver #817 landed, rather than a second `fo4::papyrus` copy: the load index list and the safe-name rule #822 needed were added there, so #817's implementation, its `Radicle/tests/test_script_set.cpp` and `Radicle/tests/test_script_set_real.cpp` stay the only ones. `radicle_script_set_resolve` resets `*out_set` immediately after the null check and before the index-count checks, and `radicle_script_set_get` zeroes `*out_winner` before the index check, so a rejected call cannot leave a caller's previous handle or winner in place. `root_load_index_count` must equal `radicle_assets_root_count`, which reports the roots `radicle_assets_open_roots` kept after dropping empty and duplicate entries; a caller cannot derive that count from the list it passed. The two structs are `radicle_script_set_candidate` and `radicle_script_set_winner` because `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex.h:radicle_script_resolve` already owns `radicle_script_candidate` and `radicle_script_winner` with different layouts, and the generator reads both headers, so the shorter names redeclared the types in C and in `RadicleNative.g.cs`. A candidate's `container` is the loose payload path, or the archive file path for an archived payload. `radicle_script_set_read` reads the named winner's `radicle_asset_location` through `AssetResolver::read` rather than `radicle_assets_read`, because that call resolves a path again with `locate` and would return a different payload whenever an explicit load index contradicts the root order. The set borrows the `radicle_assets` handle, so the handle must outlive it, and the strings it returns stay valid until destroy. `struct radicle_assets` moved to `Radicle/src/c_api_env_internal.hpp` so the new translation unit can reach the resolver; `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` lists the header, and the committed `RadicleNative.g.cs` and `abi_layout_probe.cpp` are regenerated. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_script_set.cpp:CApiScriptSetTest.ResolvesReadsAndCountsReplacedPayloads`, `CApiScriptSetTest.ExplicitLoadIndexMovesTheWinner` and `CApiScriptSetTest.RejectsBadArguments`, which pre-fills every out-parameter with a sentinel so a missed reset fails the call.
## Radicle/src/environment/placed.cpp:decode_placed_reference (#816)

The REFR XEMI subrecord (emittance) is one 4-byte FormKey id, read with `single_link` exactly like XEZN, so it resolves through the plugin's master list and a second XEMI is refused by `once`. It is stored in `PlacedReferenceData::emittance` (`Radicle/include/fo4/environment/placed.hpp:PlacedReferenceData`). The target is not type-checked here: xEdit allows only LIGH or REGN (`C:/Users/Ricky/ds-proxy/xedit-src/Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:11523`, `wbFormIDCk(XEMI, 'Emittance', [LIGH, REGN])`), and the caller looks up the target itself. The branch runs for every placed signature this decoder accepts (ACHR and the projectile, trap and hazard records too), since the same XEMI row exists on them (`wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:4611`, `:3256`).

## Radicle/src/c_api_placed.cpp:build_view (#816)

`radicle_placed_ref.has_emittance` is set from whether the decoded optional is present, and `emittance` is filled through the same `key` helper as `encounter_zone`, which yields the null key when absent. Both new fields come after `internal` at the end of `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h:radicle_placed_ref`, so no existing offset moved. The C# `PlacedRef.HasEmittance` and `PlacedRef.Emittance` lines and their probe offsets come from `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py`, which regenerated `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp`. `AbiLayoutTests.EveryStructMatchesTheCLayout` checks those offsets against the probe output.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PlacedReferences.cs:PlacedReference (#816)

`PlacedReference` takes `FormKey? Emittance = null` as its last parameter. `RadicleEnvironment.Convert` sets it from `HasEmittance`, not from the key's zero value, which is the same rule the other optional links follow. The default keeps existing callers compiling.

Fixture REFR 0x800 carries XEMI resolving to 0x917, and fixture REFR 0x809 carries none. `DecodesObjectReferenceFields` checks the resolved key, `EmittanceStaysEmptyForAReferenceWithoutXemi` checks that an absent XEMI yields no value (a regression where a stale or zero key was reported), and `CApiDecodesPlacedReferences` checks `has_emittance` and the resolved `emittance` through the C ABI.
