A REFR with XEMI reports the resolved FormKey through the managed `PlacedReference.Emittance`, and a REFR without XEMI reports null. It catches the wrapper dropping the field or ignoring `HasEmittance`.

## Radicle/tests/test_placed_variants_real.cpp:XemiReferencesMatchCensusInDlcRobotAndWorkshop03 (#816)

Counts the REFR records of a single-plugin load of DLCRobot.esm (expects 482) and DLCworkshop03.esm (expects 207) whose decoded `PlacedReferenceData::emittance` is set. The expectations were confirmed by a read-only raw scan of the two ESMs (37,693 and 8,184 REFR records, of which 482 and 207 carry XEMI; 35 and 9 are deleted, and the scan counts them as the test does). The regression it catches is an XEMI decode that drops or misplaces entries on real REFR layouts, which fixture bytes cannot show.
## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:outranks

Garden rule, not engine-proven. The order is copied from GE `opencw/OpenCw.Papyrus/ScriptCachePrecedence.cs:Compare` on origin/main: kind (archive before loose), then the higher load index, then the ordinal container path. The engine's real precedence for loose versus archive scripts and for CC archives is an open RE question (see the #812 RE request).

## Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/script_set.hpp:ScriptCandidate

`name`, `kind`, `container`, `load_index` and `size` are what precedence compares; `kind` must match `location.origin`, and `path` and `location` are carried so the C ABI can report and read the payload the winner names without re-resolving the path through `locate`. `container` is the loose payload path or the archive file path, so the tie-break compares the strings a caller can print. The struct is aggregate-initialised by its tests, so a new field goes at the end with a default. A caller-built candidate, the `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex.h:radicle_script_resolve` entry point, has no payload location: `Radicle/src/c_api_pex.cpp:radicle_script_resolve` fills the other fields one by one and leaves `path` and `location` empty, because precedence never reads them and there is no resolver to name a payload.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:loose_root_index

Garden rule, not engine-proven. `loose_root_index` returns the position of the first resolver root that lexically contains the loose file, which is the root `Radicle/src/archive/assets.cpp:AssetResolver::locate` would read it from (`Radicle/tests/test_script_set.cpp:ScriptSet.FirstLooseRootWinsLikeAssetResolverLocate`). It does not compute a load index: `enumerate_script_candidates` turns the position into one, using `roots.size() - 1 - i` because `AssetResolver::roots()` is ordered high to low priority, and the higher index then wins.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:enumerate_script_candidates

Sources candidates from `archive::AssetResolver::list("Scripts", ".pex", true)` and treats the resolver's own listing order as no more than a starting point: every candidate carries the `load_index` that `resolve_script_set` compares. Archive load index is the archive's position in `AssetResolver::archives()`: `archive_load_order` in `Radicle/src/archive/assets.cpp` already orders that list as INI archives first and then each plugin's archives, so the resolver order is the load order and no `AssembledLoadOrder` input is needed. A loose candidate's index is its root's entry in the caller's `root_load_index`; an empty span means the roots are ordered high to low priority, the order `AssetResolver::open_roots` documents (#693), so root `i` gets `roots().size() - 1 - i` and root order alone already expresses "a higher load index wins". A span of any other length throws `std::invalid_argument`, which `radicle_script_set_resolve` refuses itself as `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A loose path is attributed to the first root that lexically contains it (`Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:loose_root_index`), which is the root `AssetResolver::locate` would read it from, including a root list that repeats one path (`open_roots` keeps the first). Every listing is named by `script_name_from_entry`, so an entry outside `Scripts/`, without `.pex`, or with a name `SafeName` would refuse stays out. The function lists every shadowed entry (`include_shadowed=true`), because resolution, not `AssetResolver::list`, decides the winner. `size` is the listing's size, `path` keeps `.pex`, and `location` keeps the `AssetLocation` that `radicle_script_set_read` reads from, so a consumer can report and read the entry it chose. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_script_set.cpp:ScriptSet.FirstLooseRootWinsLikeAssetResolverLocate` (root order alone picks the winner), `ScriptSet.ExplicitLoadIndexOverridesTheRootOrder` (an index that contradicts the root order moves the winner and its bytes), `ScriptSet.RejectsALoadIndexCountThatMissesARoot`, `ScriptSet.NonScriptAssetsAreLeftOut` and `ScriptSet.NormalizedNamesIgnoreCaseSeparatorsScriptsPrefixAndPexSuffix`.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:normalize_script_name

One of the two name rules, and not the one enumeration uses: `enumerate_script_candidates` names every entry through `script_name_from_entry` and never calls this function. `normalize_script_name` normalizes through `normalize_asset_path`, which drops a leading `data/` component and throws `AssetPathError` for a drive or a `.`/`..` component, then strips the `scripts/` prefix and the `.pex` suffix, matching GE `NormalizeName` and `ArchiveScriptSource.ScriptName` in `opencw/OpenCw.Papyrus/ScriptSourceCandidate.cs`. `script_name_from_entry` does neither of those two: it does not drop a leading `data/`, so `data/scripts/foo.pex` is refused, and it returns nullopt instead of throwing.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:script_name_from_entry

The one name rule `enumerate_script_candidates` applies, shared by loose and archive entries so the two cannot drift the way the C# `Cache/ArchiveScriptSource.cs` and `ScriptSourceCandidate.cs` `ScriptName` copies did (one dropped the `Scripts/` prefix, one did not). An entry outside `Scripts/`, without `.pex`, or with a name `SafeName` would refuse yields nothing and stays out of the set: lower case, under `Scripts/`, `.pex` dropped, and rejected when it holds `:`, NUL, `<`, `>`, `"`, `|`, `?`, `*`, an empty, `.` or `..` part, or a part ending in `.` or a space (C# `ScriptCacheLayout.SafeName`). The rule runs on the name after `.pex` is dropped, so `Scripts/.pex` (an empty name) and `Scripts/dir/.pex` (`dir/`, a trailing slash) are refused; applying it to the path before the extension let both through as an unusable cache path. Unlike `normalize_script_name` it never throws: a resolver listing is data, so an unsafe entry is skipped instead of aborting the set. The C# loose enumeration applied no such check, but writing its cache path ran `SafeName`, so skipping those names here matches what the cache could store. Two ordering details differ from the C# and cannot matter for ASCII paths: C# `StringComparer.Ordinal` and `string.CompareOrdinal` compare UTF-16 code units, while this port compares UTF-8 bytes, so names and container paths order differently only for non-BMP characters. The rule is ASCII on purpose: `is_safe_script_name` refuses `:` and the Windows-path characters but not control bytes `0x01`-`0x1F`, and the lowercasing uses `std::tolower` on `unsigned char`, so a name differing only in a non-ASCII letter is not folded. That is current behaviour, recorded rather than changed. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_script_set.cpp:ScriptName.ReadsOnlySafeScriptsEntries`.

## Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:resolve_script_set

Groups by normalized name and returns the groups in ordinal name order, as GE `Resolve` does. The winner is the first candidate that no later candidate outranks, so an exact tie keeps the earlier input; `ScriptSet.EqualKeysKeepTheFirstSeenCandidate` pins that comparison as strict, because an inclusive one would return the last equal payload. `replaced` is the group size minus one, the count `ScriptCacheBuilder` added to `ReplacedCount`, so three copies of one script report one winner with `replaced == 2`. `ScriptWinner::index` is an addition beyond GE: it maps the winner back to the caller's span, which matters when two entries share a container and a name. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_script_set.cpp:ScriptSet.LooseScriptBeatsArchiveScriptWhateverTheLoadIndex`, `ScriptSet.HigherArchiveLoadIndexWinsWhateverTheInputOrder`, `ScriptSet.EqualKindAndLoadIndexTieBreaksByOrdinalContainerPath`, `ScriptSet.DuplicateNameInOneContainerKeepsTheFirstAndCountsTheRest` and `ScriptSet.ReplacedCountsEachLoserAndWinnersStayInNameOrder`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex.h:radicle_script_resolve

The C ABI takes caller-supplied candidates, so C# keeps its own enumeration and calls this for the winners. Kind 0 is archive and 1 is loose; any other kind is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Winners are returned in name order with `candidate_index` into the input array. Winner arrays are released with `radicle_script_free_winners`. The input struct carries no payload path or location, so `Radicle/src/c_api_pex.cpp:radicle_script_resolve` builds each `ScriptCandidate` field by field with `path` and `location` empty; only the name, kind, container and load index take part in the comparison, and a caller that needs the winning payload uses `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_script_set.h:radicle_script_set_read` instead. Building the candidate field by field rather than with an aggregate initializer is also what keeps `-Wmissing-field-initializers` quiet on GCC, which treats the aggregate form as a missing-field warning when the struct gains a field.

## Radicle/src/c_api_pex.cpp:radicle_script_normalize_name

Maps `AssetPathError` to `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` so no exception crosses the C boundary; the test `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_pex.cpp:ScriptNormalizeNameReportsInvalidArgumentForParentComponent` pins that.

## Radicle/tests/test_script_set_real.cpp:VanillaAndDlcArchivesResolveToAWinnerSet

The test enumerates `Scripts/**.pex` a second time through `Radicle/src/archive/assets.cpp:AssetResolver::list` with `include_shadowed` true and `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:script_name_from_entry`, so its expected names come from the listing rather than from `enumerate_script_candidates`, and then asserts three relations: the winners equal that name set, `sum(replaced) + winners == candidates`, and every winner's bytes open with `DE C0 57 FA`. The relations are asserted instead of the counts because the Creation Club set varies per machine. A scan on 2026-10-24 of the same `D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Fallout 4/Data` (`installed_master_and_cc_plugins`: 7 official masters plus 9 CC plugins listed in `Fallout4.ccc`; `archive_load_order` order) printed 10331 candidates, 10331 distinct names, 10331 winners, 0 replaced, 0 winners off the magic, and 0 names carrying more than one listed spelling, so nothing in that set needs the case or separator rule to pick a winner. That is one machine's history, not a pin; the regression the test catches is a resolver that loses or invents a name, reports a `replaced` count that does not match the candidates, or hands back a payload that is not a PEX. A Release run of this test alone takes 2.1 s and samples a 198 MB peak working set.

`Radicle/tests/test_script_set_real.cpp:ModArchiveShadowingAnOfficialScriptFollowsTheLoadIndex` covers the precedence path the retail set cannot reach, because vanilla and the Creation Club archives shadow nothing and the first test measures `replaced` 0. It takes the alphabetically first official winner from the real archives, writes a two-entry BA2 next to it with `Radicle/src/archive/ba2.cpp:write_ba2_general_file`: `Scripts\<name>.pex` for that official name, and `Scripts\<new>.pex` for a name the retail set does not define (a fixed probe name, suffixed until it is absent), each a four-byte PEX magic plus a marker. It resolves the same retail archives twice. Appended last, the mod archive has the higher load index: the shadowed name goes to the mod with `replaced` 1, the new name is added with `replaced` 0, the winner count is the official count plus one, the candidate count plus two, and the sum of `replaced` over the set is 1, so an added name is not counted as a loser. Inserted first it has the lowest load index: the official archive wins the shadowed name with `replaced` 1, while the new name still resolves to the mod with `replaced` 0 because nothing competes for it. Each case reads the winning location through `Radicle/src/archive/assets.cpp:AssetResolver::read`, so the assertion is about the payload the resolver hands back and not only about the container name. The regression it catches is a resolver that ignores the archive load index, that reports `replaced` 0 when an archive loses to another archive, or that reads bytes from the archive it resolved to rather than the one it chose. The generated archive is a real BA2 written by the production writer, and the official side of every comparison is the retail data; the payload is a marker rather than a compiled script because the resolver never parses what it resolves. `Radicle/tests/test_script_set_real.cpp:LooseScriptBeatsAnOfficialArchiveWhateverTheLoadIndex` covers the other half of the precedence rule against the same retail archives: it picks the first official winner whose archive position is above zero, writes the same `Scripts\<name>.pex` into a temporary loose root, and resolves one root against the retail archive list with an explicit root load index of 0, which is below that archive's position, so only the kind rule can hand back the loose copy. It asserts the loose copy wins with `replaced` 1, that reading the winning location returns the loose marker, and that the archived copy is still listed as a candidate for the same name, so the loose copy shadows an entry rather than replacing it. `Radicle/tests/test_script_set_real.cpp:CApiResolvesTheShadowingModArchiveLikeTheCppResolver` repeats the archive shadowing through the C ABI over the same retail archives plus the generated two-entry BA2, opened with `Radicle/src/c_api_archive.cpp:radicle_assets_open_roots` and resolved with `Radicle/src/c_api_script_set.cpp:radicle_script_set_resolve`: the set holds one more winner than the retail resolve, the shadowed name comes back with the mod archive as its container, `RADICLE_ASSET_ARCHIVE` as its origin, `scripts/<name>.pex` as its path and `replaced` 1, `radicle_script_set_read` returns the marker payload from that location, and the added name carries `replaced` 0 with its own payload. The regression it catches is a C wrapper that reports the name set of the C++ resolver but not the winner it chose, that loses `replaced` on the way across the ABI, or that reads bytes from a different archive than the winner names. A third entry names a second official winner with only its case and separators spelled differently: it reuses the spelling that archive's string table stores, uppercases every letter and swaps the separator style. The set still holds one more winner than the retail resolve, so the respelled name is folded rather than added, and that winner comes back with `scripts/<name>.pex` as its path rather than the stored spelling, the mod archive as its container, `RADICLE_ASSET_ARCHIVE` as its origin and `replaced` 1, `radicle_script_set_read` returns its own marker, and `sum(replaced)` over the ABI set is 2. What this adds over the same-spelling case is an ABI enumeration with a name rule of its own, which would turn the respelled entry into a second name, and a winner whose `path` echoes the archive's spelling, which would make a consumer cache under a path the set never resolved. `Radicle/tests/test_script_set_real.cpp:ModArchiveEntrySpellingFoldsToTheOfficialScriptName` exercises the case and separator rule against the retail set instead of assuming it. It takes the first official winner whose name has a directory component, reads that entry's spelling out of the archive string table through `Radicle/include/fo4/archive/ba2_reader.hpp:Ba2Reader::entries` (the path as stored, not the resolver's listing, which `Radicle/src/archive/assets.cpp:normalize_asset_path` has already folded lower case with `/` separators), and writes one mod entry that names the same script with every letter uppercased and the separator style swapped. Two assertions state the folding contract before the resolve runs: `Radicle/src/archive/assets.cpp:normalize_asset_path` maps the respelled path to `scripts/<name>.pex`, and `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:script_name_from_entry` returns the same name for both spellings. Appended last, the respelled entry adds one candidate and no name: the winner count stays at the official count, the shadowed name resolves to the mod archive with `replaced` 1 and `scripts/<name>.pex` as its reported path even though the archive stores the other spelling, `AssetResolver::read` returns the marker, and `sum(replaced)` stays 1. The regression it catches is a lookup layer that stops folding case or separators, which would turn a respelled mod entry into a second name instead of a shadowing one, and a winner whose reported `path` echoes the archive's spelling instead of the canonical name. On 2026-10-24 with `D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/Fallout 4/Data` the test takes 2.6 s and the five `ScriptSetReal` tests together 14.9 s; making `script_name_from_entry` stop lowercasing makes this test and no other fail, and renaming the mod entry by four characters makes it fail on `replaced` 0 and on the retail payload instead of the mod marker, so both the folding assertions and the shadowing assertions are live. `Radicle/tests/test_script_set_real.cpp:CApiScriptResolveFoldsACallerBuiltNameThatIsSpelledDifferently` covers the other script ABI, `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex.h:radicle_script_resolve`, which takes caller-built candidates instead of an assets handle and groups them by the `name` bytes the caller supplies, so folding is the caller's job through `Radicle/src/c_api_pex.cpp:radicle_script_normalize_name`. It builds the retail candidate list from `enumerate_script_candidates` (10331 rows on the scan above), takes an official winner whose name has a directory component, respells that entry the same way as the previous test, folds the respelled path through `radicle_script_normalize_name`, asserts the folded bytes equal the retail name, then appends one caller-built candidate named with those bytes, with the mod archive path as its container and a load index above every retail archive. `radicle_script_resolve` returns the retail winner count, so the respelled candidate took the existing name instead of adding one, the winner for that row is the caller's index with `replaced` 1, and `sum(replaced)` over the set is 1. The regression it catches is a normalizer that stops folding case or separators, which would hand `radicle_script_resolve` a second name, and a resolver that stops letting the higher load index win or stops counting the loser. Making `radicle_script_normalize_name` return its input unchanged fails this test on the folded-name assertion plus the two synthetic `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_pex.cpp` normalize tests, and no other `ScriptSetReal` test; a Release run takes 1.3 s and the six `ScriptSetReal` tests together 16.0 s. The same rows are then resolved a second time with the caller row named by the unfolded spelling, which returns one more winner than the retail resolve and lets that row win its own name with `replaced` 0, so the test states the split: `radicle_script_resolve` groups the name bytes verbatim and never folds them itself. Checked on 2026-10-24 in the engine tree at `E:/GardenEngine/GardenEngine` (worktree `docs-cleanup-376`): nothing there calls `radicle_script_resolve` yet, the cache still resolves in managed code through `opencw/OpenCw.Papyrus/ScriptCachePrecedence.cs:NormalizeName`, which does fold separators, a leading `/`, the `.pex` extension and case but leaves a leading `Scripts/` on the name, and the older `opencw/OpenCw.Papyrus/Cache/ArchiveScriptSource.cs:ScriptName` keeps only the file stem, so a loose `quests/foo` cannot shadow the archived `Scripts\Quests\Foo.pex` on that path. Both are places where a cross-over to this ABI would hand `radicle_script_resolve` a name Radicle never resolves.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex.h:radicle_script_resolve (generator)

`c_api_pex.h` is already in `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` HEADERS, so the generated `RadicleNative.g.cs` and `abi_layout_probe.cpp` carry the script exports after regeneration. No hand-written C# wrapper exists for the pex exports, and none was added.
## Radicle/include/fo4/loadorder/mo2_profile.hpp:Mo2PathTranslator — optional translator parameter

`read_mo2_instance` takes an optional `Mo2PathTranslator`, applied to ini path values before any derived folder is built. Without it, values are read as UTF-8 paths (`fo4::io::from_utf8`). fo4ide passes its Wine drive mapping (`PluginEditTool/native/src/mo2/Mo2Profile.cpp:nativePath`) so `gamepath` and `base_directory` are mapped before `%BASE_DIR%` and `data_dir` are derived.

## Radicle/src/loadorder/mo2_profile.cpp:read_mo2_instance — instance folders

`selected_profile` defaults to `Default`. `base_directory` defaults to the instance folder, and `%BASE_DIR%` in the later keys expands to it. `data_dir` is `gamepath/Data` when `gamepath` is set, and `Stock Folder/Data` replaces it when that is a directory (portable installs). With no `gamepath` and no `Stock Folder/Data`, `data_dir` is empty and the data root is left out of the asset roots. The read never throws; a missing ini gives the defaults. The `mod_directory` and `profiles_directory` keys are not verified against a real MO2 ini.

## Radicle/src/loadorder/mo2_profile.cpp:read_mo2_profile — modlist and plugins

`modlist.txt` lines starting with `+` are enabled and `-` disabled. `*` is treated as disabled, because no sample of it was checked. Other lines and empty names are skipped. A missing `modlist.txt` gives no mods. A separator is a name ending in `_separator`, matched case-insensitively. `plugins.txt` is read with `read_plugin_list`, so a missing file throws an IO error and an empty profile is never returned. `local_saves` and `local_settings` are not read; their keys were not verified.

## Radicle/src/loadorder/mo2_profile.cpp:mo2_asset_roots_low_to_high — root order

Roots are `data_dir` (skipped when empty), the enabled non-separator mod folders low to high, then `overwrite_dir` last, so the overwrite folder wins in `mo2_resolve_plugin_paths`. `radicle_mo2_asset_roots` in `Radicle/src/c_api_loadorder.cpp` returns the same order.

## Radicle/src/loadorder/mo2_profile.cpp:mo2_resolve_plugin_paths — winners and folded keys

Each root is indexed in order, and a later root overwrites an earlier entry. Keys are `fo4::text::fold(file name)`, so a case-only Unicode difference (`Ä.esp` against `ä.esp`) resolves to one plugin (#702). Lookups must use the folded key, because `fo4::PluginKey::filename()` returns the unfolded name. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_mo2_profile.cpp:NonAsciiModAndPluginNamesMatchAcrossUtf8ModlistAndWindows1252PluginsTxt`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/io/path_text.hpp:from_utf8 — UTF-8 to path without the ANSI code page

MSVC's `std::filesystem::path(std::string)` and `path::string()` use the ANSI code page. `from_utf8` builds the path from a `std::u8string`, so non-ASCII profile and mod folder names reach the file system unchanged. `read_mo2_profile` and `mo2_asset_roots_low_to_high` use it for the profile and mod folder names.

## PluginEditTool/native/src/mo2/Mo2Profile.cpp:nativePath
- On Windows `nativePath` passes the UTF-8 instance text to `std::filesystem::path(std::string)`, which reads it in the process ANSI code page. That is correct because `PluginEditTool/native/cmake/utf8.manifest` sets `activeCodePage` to UTF-8 and `fo4ide_use_utf8_code_page()` (`PluginEditTool/native/cmake/Utf8CodePage.cmake`) attaches it to every executable in the directories that call it: `PluginEditTool/native/tests/CMakeLists.txt` (which holds `fo4ide_test_mo2`), `apps/fo4ide/CMakeLists.txt` (`fo4ide`) and `tests/integration/CMakeLists.txt`. No other native CMake file adds an executable, so no conversion is added in `nativePath`. The UTF-8 code page setting needs Windows 10 1903 or later.
- `Radicle/src/loadorder/mo2_profile.cpp:expand_dir` calls the translator it is given, so the same reasoning applies. A new executable that links `fo4ide_mo2` must be created before the attaching call in its directory, or it misses the manifest.

## Radicle/src/c_api_loadorder.cpp:radicle_mo2_profile_read — output cleanup on failure

Outputs are cleared before the read, and before the empty-`profile` check. When copying the plugin rows fails after the mod rows were copied, the mod rows are freed and `out_mod_rows` and `out_mod_count` are cleared. A NULL `profile` selects the instance's `selected_profile`.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/LoadOrder.cs:LoadOrderFiles.ReadMo2PluginPaths — row split

Rows are split on the first tab. The keys are folded file names, which cannot contain a tab on Windows, so the first tab is always the separator. `mo2_resolve_plugin_paths` returns one entry per key, so `ToDictionary` does not see duplicates.
## Radicle/include/fo4/environment/terrain.hpp:decode_land_heights
- Returns the 33x33 height grid of one LAND record. `base` is the raw VHGT offset; `heights` are final values, already scaled by 8.
- Returns nullopt when VHGT is absent or the delta span is not 1089 bytes.
- Ported from GardenEngine `opencw/Services/Terrain/LandHeights.cs` (Decode), checked against xEdit `wbDefinitionsCommon.pas` VHGT (lines 8698-8714).

## Radicle/include/fo4/environment/terrain.hpp:decode_layer_alpha
- One entry per non-base ATXT layer that has VTXT data, with the 17x17 opacity grid and the quadrant and layer number.
- The texture is nullopt when the link resolves to null.
- Ported from GardenEngine `opencw/Services/Terrain/LandLayers.cs` (DecodeAlpha). Reference: `wbDefinitionsCommon.pas` ATXT/BTXT/VTXT lines 8716-8763, `wbVTXTPosition` line 4350.

## Radicle/include/fo4/environment/terrain.hpp:blend_cell_weights
- Returns, per quadrant, the base texture (first base layer of that quadrant) and the 33x33 summed weights per non-null texture.
- Ported from GardenEngine `LandLayers.cs` (CellWeights, no-neighbour overload). The per-quadrant top-8 slot selection (`Quadrant`) and the neighbour overload are not ported; the API has no slot output.

## Radicle/src/environment/terrain.cpp:decode_land_heights
- Row-start carry: each row starts from the x=0 value of the previous row, not from the base. Deltas are signed bytes multiplied by 8.
- Test: `Radicle/tests/test_environment_terrain.cpp` TerrainLand.IntegratesDeltasWithRowStartCarry. Regression: a non-carry integration starts row 1 at 40 instead of 32.

## Radicle/src/environment/terrain.cpp:layered_quadrant
- Non-base alpha layers are summed in layer order. The first base texture of the quadrant takes max(1 - total, 0). When total exceeds 1 every entry is divided by total.
- Tests: TerrainLand.BlendGivesGroundTheRemainderAndNormalisesOverfullVertices, TerrainLand.BaseTextureIsTheFirstBaseLayerOfEachQuadrant.

## Radicle/src/environment/terrain.cpp:blend_cell_weights
- Each quadrant's 17x17 is added into the 33x33 grid at offset ((quadrant & 1) * 16, (quadrant >> 1) * 16). Each vertex is divided by the number of quadrants that cover it: 1 interior, 2 on a shared edge, 4 at the centre.
- The null texture (empty owner) is kept internally and is not emitted; this changes no other texture's weight.
- Tests: TerrainLand.BlendMergesQuadrantEdgesIntoSharedVertices.

## Radicle/src/environment/terrain.cpp:decode_alpha_grid
- A VTXT position maps to row = position / 17 and col = position % 17. Rows of 17 or more are skipped. Opacity is clamped to [0, 1].
- Tests: TerrainLand.MapsAlphaPositionsOntoTheSeventeenGrid, TerrainLand.SkipsAlphaPositionsOutsideTheGrid.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_terrain.h:radicle_landscape_heights
- Fills `radicle_land_heights` (has_heights, base, 1089 heights). Fails with INVALID_ARGUMENT on null arguments or a record from another environment.
- Lives in its own header because `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h` would pass 750 lines. The C# wrapper is `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleEnvironment.cs` LandscapeHeights.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_terrain.h:radicle_landscape_blend

## Radicle/tests/test_environment_terrain_real.cpp:CommonwealthCellsDecodeWithinInvariants
- Loads only Fallout4.esm from FO4_DATA_DIR (skips without it). Decodes three Commonwealth LAND records (0x00F540, 0x00F53F, 0x00F53E).
- Invariants: heights finite, alpha finite in [0, 1], weights finite and non-negative, per-vertex weight total at most 1 + 1e-5, layers non-empty, at least one record decoded.

No hash is asserted: they are bit-exact over float math, so a pin would be fragile across compilers. The printed values are the measured reference for a later pin.

## src/environment/base_records.cpp:set_climate_weathers
Rewrites only the CLMT WLST subrecord (12-byte entries: WTHR form, int32 chance, GLOB form). Links are encoded before any mutation, so an unlisted master fails closed with FormIdError (mapped to WorldDecodeError) and leaves the plugin unchanged. No master is inserted. Field layout cites wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6115-6125.

## src/environment/base_records.cpp:set_weather_colors
Writes only the R, G and B bytes of one NAM0 colour slot at (group * time_slots + time) * 4. The fourth byte is left as stored. Group count and time-slot count come from weather_color_groups and weather_time_slots in fo4/forms/weather.hpp. NAM0 layout cites wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9433 and wbWeatherTimeOfDay at wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:8335.

## src/environment/base_records.cpp:set_weather_fog
Replaces FNAM floats only when the distance count times 4 equals weather_fnam_size for the record's form version (32, 56 or 72 bytes). Field layout cites wbDefinitionsCommon.pas:9521-9555.

## src/environment/base_records.cpp:set_weather_transition
Writes one byte at k_weather_transition_offset (3) inside the DATA subrecord, which must be weather_data_size bytes. The delta is a raw uint8; converting it to hours needs min and max values the setter does not know, so that conversion stays in radicle_weather_transition_hours. Byte position cites wbDefinitionsFO4.pas WTHR DATA "Trans Delta" near lines 13034-13140.

## src/environment/base_records.cpp:mark_edited
Clears original_range, decompressed_payload, header.data_size and uncompressed_size on the edited record so the writer re-encodes it. Setters that find identical bytes return true without calling it.

Maps a null plugin with local_id 0 to the null FormKey (encodes to 0). Any other value goes through to_form_key. Used for the optional CLMT WLST global and the weather links.

- Every split array member gets its index suffix, because field_cs emits one C# field per element when the array is not a fixed scalar array. The probe names (for example LandBlend.Base0 to Base3) must match those C# field names, or AbiLayoutTests.EveryStructMatchesTheCLayout throws. ### Radicle/src/environment/base_records.cpp:set_climate_weathers
- When the CLMT has no WLST and the list is non-empty, a WLST subrecord is inserted before the first subrecord that is not EDID. The xEdit CLMT definition orders EDID, then WLST, then FNAM, GNAM, the generic model and TNAM (C:/Users/Ricky/ds-proxy/xedit-src/Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:6115-6126, WLST at line 6117). An empty list with no WLST leaves the record unchanged.
- An existing WLST whose size is not a multiple of 12 throws WorldDecodeError before any byte is written.

### Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:loose_root_index
- The first resolver root that lexically contains the loose file wins, and the function returns that root's position i; enumerate_script_candidates maps it to roots.size() - 1 - i, so root 0 has the highest load index. Nested roots therefore misassign: a file under a nested root takes the outer root's index. AssetResolver::list (Radicle/src/archive/assets.cpp:AssetResolver::list) returns AssetListing values with a path and an AssetLocation only, so the walked root is not kept. The fix is to require non-overlapping roots (see Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/script_set.hpp:enumerate_script_candidates).

### Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/script_set.hpp:enumerate_script_candidates
- Callers must pass resolver roots that do not overlap. Overlapping roots break the loose root position in Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:loose_root_index.

### Radicle/tests/test_script_set.cpp:ScriptSet.FirstLooseRootWinsLikeAssetResolverLocate
- On Windows `Radicle/src/archive/assets.cpp:child` returns the requested lowercase spelling when the case-insensitive exact probe hits, so `AssetResolver::locate` gives `scripts/quest/foo.pex`. `Radicle/src/archive/assets.cpp:walk_loose` (used by `AssetResolver::list`) keeps the on-disk `Scripts/Quest/Foo.pex`. Both name one file, but `std::filesystem::path` equality is case-sensitive on MSVC, so the test checks identity with `std::filesystem::equivalent`. Linux returns the on-disk spelling from both, which is why it passed there. The Windows spelling difference in `locate` is left as is; it is harmless for reads.

- *out_heights is zeroed after the argument and environment checks, before decoding, so a failed decode leaves no stale heights. Neighbour radicle_landscape_blend zeroes *out_blend the same way.
