## Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_copy.cpp:copy_record_subrecord

Copies one occurrence of a subrecord from a source record into a destination record of another plugin. Before any write, every form link in the source occurrence is checked: its owner must be the destination plugin or one of its masters, otherwise the call returns `owner_not_master` and writes nothing. A localized field (`Radicle/src/schema/localized_fields.cpp:is_localized_field`) stores a string-table ID, and that ID is only meaningful in the plugin whose tables it indexes. So when the field is localized and either the localized flags differ (`Radicle/include/fo4/plugin/container.hpp:PluginHeader::tes4_flags`), or both plugins are localized and they are different plugins, the call returns `localized_mismatch` before any write. Two inline plugins copy the inline text unchanged, including between different plugins, and the same localized plugin copies its IDs unchanged. The payload is remapped through a one-subrecord temporary record with `remap_record_form_links`, using the source plugin context and the destination context from `plugin_type_lookup`, so the link IDs follow the destination's master list. If the destination lacks the occurrence and the position is the next free one, `add_record_subrecord` inserts it in schema order; a position past the destination's count returns `occurrence_unreachable`, and `add_record_subrecord` returning `already_present` maps to the same status. Data and the extended size are replaced only after these checks pass, and `mark_record_modified` runs last.

- `Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_copy.cpp:copy_record_subrecord` tests in `Radicle/tests/test_subrecord_copy.cpp`: `RefusesALinkToARecordInAPluginThatIsNotAMasterWithoutWriting`, `ReencodesALinkToASharedMasterToTheDestinationsOwnMasterIndex`, `ReportsMissingRecordsAndUnreachableOccurrencesWithoutWriting`.

## Radicle/src/hkx/packfile.cpp:read_packfile

Phase 1 of the clean-room HKX reader for #814. The container is read with no Havok SDK and no GPL code. `read_packfile` checks the 0x40-byte header: the magic pair, the four layout-rule bytes (8, 1, 0, 1), file version 11 and 64-bit pointers. The section table follows the header at `0x40 + u16 at 0x3E`. Each 0x40-byte section header holds a 20-byte tag, a start offset and six marks that cut the section into data, local fixups, global fixups and virtual fixups. The marks must be non-decreasing, and the whole section must fit in the file, otherwise the status is BadSection or Truncated. A `section_count` above 16 is BadSection, as is a section whose byte range (its start plus the sixth mark) overlaps an earlier section's range. A zero-length section overlaps nothing, which matches the vanilla `__types__` section. The overlap check is in `Radicle/src/hkx/packfile.cpp:read_section` and runs before the section's bytes are copied, so the copies total at most the file size.

Table entries: local fixups are 8-byte (source, destination) pairs. Global and virtual fixups are 12-byte (source, section, destination) triples. A source of 0xFFFFFFFF is a filler entry and is dropped while the table is read. The vanilla `Meshes/Actors/Character/CharacterAssets/skeleton.hkx` fixture (`BGS/tools/tests/fixtures/vanilla`) ends its `__data__` virtual table with one such terminator; a throwaway parse of that fixture counted 83 virtual entries, 140 global fixups into `__data__` and the terminator. Dropping the terminator is therefore required, not optional.

Fixup handling runs in `validate_fixups` and `build_objects`. Local fixups are sorted by source. A source whose 8-byte pointer runs past the section, or a destination at or past the section end, is FixupOutOfRange. Two local fixups on one source are DuplicateFixup. A global fixup must name an existing section and a destination inside that section. A virtual fixup must name the `__classnames__` section, and its destination must lie at least 5 bytes into that section (a 4-byte class signature followed by one prefix byte); a missing or empty name is BadClassName. Each object's span is `[its source, the next object's source)`, and the last object runs to the end of `__data__`.

Phase 1 covers the container header, all sections (`__types__` is stored but not interpreted), the three fixup tables, and the object table (class name, signature, span). Not covered: following global fixups into other sections, and any object body beyond its span. The reader does not change `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` and adds no C ABI export.

## Radicle/src/hkx/packfile.cpp:cstring_at

`cstring_at` reads a NUL-terminated string only from the 256 bytes that start at the offset, so a name is at most 255 characters. A longer run, or one with no NUL inside the bounds, returns nullopt. `build_objects` reports that as BadClassName for a class name, and `read_string` in `Radicle/src/hkx/skeleton.cpp` reports it as FixupOutOfRange for a bone or skeleton name. The cap is in this one function, so every caller inherits it and no caller copies an unbounded string.

## Radicle/include/fo4/hkx/packfile.hpp:HkxPackfile

`HkxPackfile::objects` holds `string_view` and `span` values that point into `sections`. A copy would leave those views pointing at the source's buffers, so the copy constructor and copy assignment are deleted. Moves are defaulted: a moved `std::vector` keeps its heap buffers, so the views stay valid after `read_packfile` or a caller moves the packfile.

## Radicle/src/hkx/layout.cpp:find_layout

`find_layout` looks a class up in `k_hkx_classes`, the table generated into `Radicle/src/hkx/hkx_layouts.generated.inc`. The two-argument form calls the one-argument form and then compares the signature read from the packfile object, so a file from another Havok build fails the match instead of being decoded with the wrong offsets. The table has no duplicate class names, which is what makes the name lookup return the one row the signature check needs. The one-argument form matches the name only and is used for lookups that are not tied to a file object, such as the `hkaBone` layout inside `read_skeleton`. `find_member_offset` looks a member name up in the same way. Both return a pointer into the static table, or nullptr and nullopt when nothing matches.

The table is a linear scan over 900 rows. That is fine for phase 1, which decodes a few objects per file; an index is the upgrade path if lookups move into a per-frame loop. The table is generated and must not be hand-edited; `Radicle/tools/hkx_layout_codegen.py` is the only writer.

## Radicle/src/hkx/skeleton.cpp:read_skeleton

`read_skeleton` decodes every `hkaSkeleton` object in the packfile through `find_layout` and returns the one with the most bones. In the vanilla fixture the animation skeleton has 95 bones and the ragdoll skeleton in the same file has 18, so the 95-bone one is returned. An object whose signature does not match the layout table returns UnsupportedLayout, and a file with no `hkaSkeleton` returns MissingObject.

Decoded fields: `name` (the string pointer at the `hkaSkeleton` name offset), `parentIndices` (int16 array), `bones` (array of `hkaBone`; each bone name is read through the `hkaBone` name pointer at offset 0) and `referencePose` (`hkQsTransform`, 48 bytes: translation at 0, rotation at 16, scale at 32). Every pointer is resolved only through the object section's local fixups, via `local_target`. An array with count 0 needs no target. A non-zero count whose pointer has no local fixup, or whose elements run past the data section, is FixupOutOfRange. A bone with no name fixup is also FixupOutOfRange in `Radicle/src/hkx/skeleton.cpp:decode_skeleton`; no name is invented for it.

`Radicle/src/hkx/skeleton.cpp:check_skeleton` runs at the end of `Radicle/src/hkx/skeleton.cpp:decode_skeleton`. The parent, bone and pose counts must agree, and each parent must be -1 or an earlier bone. That rules out self-parents, forward parents and cycles, and any failure is BadSection. The vanilla fixture passes this check for both of its `hkaSkeleton` objects (95 and 18 bones).

Not covered by phase 1, and still open under #814: animation data (`hkaAnimation` and its compressed or spline tracks), animation bindings (`hkaAnimationBinding`), physics (the hkp and hknp shape, constraint and ragdoll classes), the `hkaSkeleton` fields `referenceFloats`, `localFrames` and `partitions`, and every write path. The `floatSlots` field is not decoded and `HkxSkeleton` has no slot names in phase 1; that comes with the animation binding work. The layout table is measured for Havok 2014 (signature 0xfec1cedb for `hkaSkeleton`), so other builds are rejected rather than guessed.

## Radicle/tools/hkx_layout_codegen.py:collect and render

Data source: `BGS/src/Hkx/HavokClassLayouts.json` supplies member offsets and instance sizes. Its `source` field says they were read from the Fallout 4 1.10.163 executable's class initializers at startup, so they are measured. `BGS/src/Hkx/HavokClassTypes.json` supplies each class's 32-bit signature; its note says the member metadata is published class-description data under MIT. `docs/code-notes/BGS.md` names both JSON files as the authoritative schemas, so this table follows them and not any other copy. No Havok SDK file is read or copied.

`collect` emits a row only for a class present in both files, so every row carries the signature that `find_layout` matches. It rejects non-ASCII names, names that are not C identifiers, signatures that are not `0x` plus eight lowercase hex digits, and negative offsets. `render` writes 900 rows, sorted by class name, with LF line endings. `--check` renders in memory and exits 1 when the output file differs or is missing. The CMake target `radicle_hkx_layout_check` runs `--check` on every build. The generated file is exempt from the 750-line guard as a `.generated.` file.

## Radicle/src/forms/proj_expl_hazd.cpp:create_projectile — empty editor ID and name (#752 Low)

An empty `editor_id` no longer writes a lone-NUL EDID, and an empty `name` no longer writes a FULL subrecord. The same rule is applied in `create_explosion` and `create_hazard`, which have the same two push sites. EDID is `minimum 1` in the generated schema (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc`, the EDID rules of the PROJ, EXPL and HAZD rows), so the typed creators now refuse an empty editor ID. `require_clean_editor_id` (called first by each creator, before the plugin copy is made) throws `ProjExplHazdError` with a message that names the empty editor ID, so the plugin is unchanged. Before that check the refusal came from `run_authoring_preflight` as a generic `required_subrecord_missing`; with the explicit check first, the preflight no longer sees an empty EDID from these creators and its error stays as the general backstop. FULL is `minimum 0` for all three, so skipping it is safe. Regression detected: an empty editorId producing a PROJ/EXPL/HAZD with an empty EditorID, an empty name producing an empty FULL, and an empty editorId refused with a message that does not say why. Tests: `tests/test_proj_expl_hazd_creation.cpp:ProjExplHazdCreation.EmptyEditorIdIsRefusedBeforeAnyMutation` (asserts the message for all three) and `ProjExplHazdCreation.EmptyNameWritesNoFullSubrecordButNamedRecordKeepsIt`. The PluginEditTool typed path passes `value_or("")` and needs no change; the refusal reaches the caller as `ProjExplHazdCreateFailed`, pinned by `PluginEditTool/native/tests/unit/RadiclePluginProjExplHazdTests.cpp:Native PROJ empty editorId is refused as ProjExplHazdCreateFailed without writing`.

## Radicle/src/forms/faction.cpp:create_faction — empty full name (#752 Low)

`create_faction` treats an empty `full_name` as absent, through `has_full_name`: no FULL is written, and an empty name on a localized plugin is no longer refused by the localized-FULL check. The editor-ID path is unchanged: `editor_id` writes EDID whenever it has a value, so a direct Radicle call with `""` still writes a lone-NUL EDID (the PluginEditTool path maps `""` to absent, see #803). Regression detected: an empty fullName writing a lone-NUL FULL, and a localized plugin refusing an empty name that means "no name". Test: `tests/test_faction.cpp:FactionCreation.EmptyFullNameWritesNoFullSubrecordAndIsNotLocalizedRefused`.

## Radicle/src/plugin/subrecord_authoring.cpp:create_with_rules — schema EDID minimum 1 (#752 Low, not changed)

The schema create path writes a lone-NUL EDID for an empty `editor_id` when the EDID rule has `minimum 1`. The EDID rules with `minimum 1` are EXPL, FLST, GMST, HAZD, IMAD and PROJ (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/generated_record_constraints.inc`, subrecord rows at lines 685, 747, 808, 818, 862 and 1440; the record table rows at 1951 to 2017 map each to its range). The five-rule count in the brief does not match the file: there are six. This path is kept as is, because the change is a behavior decision: an absent editorId also arrives here as `""` (the PluginEditTool schema branch encodes a missing editorId as empty), so rejecting empty would also reject an absent one. After the typed-path change above, PROJ, EXPL and HAZD refuse an empty editor ID while the schema path still writes a lone-NUL EDID for them, so the two paths disagree. The lead must decide whether the schema path should also return `invalid_editor_id` for an empty `minimum 1` EDID.

## Radicle/tests/vmad_writer_fixture.hpp:subrecord

`subrecord` finds the record under the owner the caller passes, `Vmad.esp` by default, and throws `fixture record missing` when nothing matches. A plugin read from a file takes its owner from the file name (`Radicle/src/plugin/reader.cpp:read_plugin_from_owned_bytes`), so a copy saved as `Saved.esp` or `Refused.esp` keys its records to that name and a lookup under `Vmad.esp` finds nothing. The helper used to dereference that null result, which crashed `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_quest_fragments.cpp:VmadQuestFragments.CApiPairFormEditsOneOfTwoBindingsAndRefusesBadInput` and `VmadQuestFragments.CApiPairFormRefusesDuplicatePairAndLeavesBytesUnchanged` on Native Linux Debug with no output after `[ RUN ]`. A missing record now throws, so the test fails instead of crashing.
## Radicle/src/papyrus/parser.cpp:Parser::parse and Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/parser.hpp:Parser (PET front end, piece 1 of the lift)

- What moved and from where. PluginEditTool's native C++ Papyrus front end is now Radicle's: `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/diagnostic.hpp:Span`, `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/token.hpp:TokenKind`, `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/ast.hpp:Script`, `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/lexer.hpp:Lexer` and `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/parser.hpp:Parser`, with the definitions in `Radicle/src/papyrus/lexer.cpp`, `Radicle/src/papyrus/parser.cpp`, `Radicle/src/papyrus/parser_statement.cpp` and `Radicle/src/papyrus/parser_expression.cpp`. The namespace changed from `fo4ide::papyrus` to `fo4::papyrus` and the include paths from `<fo4ide/papyrus/...>` to `<fo4/papyrus/...>`; nothing else in the code changed. The file names are snake_case because that is what every other Radicle header uses, not because the contents were rewritten. Radicle includes nothing from PluginEditTool, no C ABI export was added and `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is untouched.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/diagnostic.hpp:DiagnosticBag` came along with the four named files because the front end cannot report anything without it: `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/token.hpp:Token` carries a `Span`, `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/lexer.hpp:Lexer::lex` fills a bag, and `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/parser.hpp:Parser` reports into the same bag. `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/diagnostic.hpp:codeString` keeps the PAP0001..PAP0052 strings as an enum whose values are the C# names, so a diagnostic prints exactly what PET's C# oracle prints. The bag caps at 200 items and then appends one `PAP0019`, so a pathological file cannot allocate diagnostics without bound.

- Byte-level fidelity was checked, not assumed. For each of the five headers, `Radicle/src/papyrus/lexer.cpp` and the concatenation of the three parser translation units, the source was compared against PluginEditTool's after stripping comment lines and blank lines and folding the namespace, the include paths and the `detail::` prefix away. The only differences are the five include filenames' case and the three `namespace fo4::papyrus {` wrappers the split introduced. Comment text is the one thing that is not PET's: this repository keeps explanations in this document and allows only single-line constraint comments in source, so every prose comment in the lifted files was reduced to one line stating the constraint, and the reasoning it carried lives here.

- The split of `Radicle/src/papyrus/parser.cpp:Parser::parse` away from `Parser.cpp` is the only structural change forced on the lift, by the 750-line guard. `Radicle/src/papyrus/parser.cpp` holds file and token plumbing plus the declaration parsers (`Parser::parse`, `Parser::parseFile`, `Parser::parseScript`, `Parser::parseScriptMember`, `Parser::parseType`, `Parser::parseProperty`, `Parser::parseState`, `Parser::parseFunction`, `Parser::parseEvent`, `Parser::parseParameterList`), `Radicle/src/papyrus/parser_statement.cpp` holds `Parser::parseBlock`, `Parser::parseStatement`, `Parser::tryParseDefine`, `Parser::parseIf`, `Parser::parseWhile` and `Parser::parseReturn`, and `Radicle/src/papyrus/parser_expression.cpp` holds `Parser::parseExpression`, the `Parser::parseLeftAssociative` ladder and `Parser::parseAtom`. Each member is declared once in `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/parser.hpp` and defined in exactly one translation unit, so the split adds no header of its own beyond `Radicle/src/papyrus/parser_detail.hpp`, which exists only because `lower` and `iequals` were file-local helpers in PET's single `Parser.cpp` and are now needed by two translation units; the two functions are inline and byte-identical to PET's, and the call sites read `detail::lower` and `detail::iequals`.

- Lexing details a reader should not have to rediscover: `Radicle/src/papyrus/lexer.cpp:Lexer::skipTrivia` treats `;` to end of line as a comment and `;/ ... /;` as a block comment, and `Lexer::isContinuation` counts a backslash as a continuation when only horizontal space and an optional trailing `;` comment follow it before the newline — so `x = 1 + \ ; keep going` still joins. `Lexer::consumeNewline` folds CRLF into one line break, so line and column numbers do not shift on a Windows-authored file. `Lexer::lexNumber` accepts `0x`/`0X` hex and an `f`/`F` float suffix but no exponent, and `Lexer::lexString` decodes `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\\` and `\"` while keeping any other escape as both characters, which is what keeps a Windows path inside a literal intact. `Keywords::tryGet` folds ASCII case only, and the table is 45 entries; `AutoReadOnly`, `DebugOnly`, `BetaOnly` and `Const` are keywords, while the user flags `Hidden`, `Conditional`, `Mandatory` and `CollapsedOnRef` are plain identifiers accepted in a flag position by `Parser::parseFlags`, which is how a script with no Creation Kit flag file still parses.

- One deliberate deviation from PET's C# oracle is carried over rather than fixed: `Radicle/src/papyrus/parser.cpp:Parser::parseQualifiedName` accepts `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/token.hpp:TokenKind::Hash` wherever `:` qualifies a name, because PET's decompiler emits `Script#Struct` type names and PET's C++ parser has to reparse them. Its C# oracle rejects `#`. Changing that here would be a behaviour change inside a lift, so it stays and is recorded as a known divergence from the C# rather than from PET's C++.

- Recovery is the parser's defining property and is unchanged. A malformed script member is reported at `PAP0015` and skipped with `Parser::skipToNextLine`, so the declarations after it survive; a block that never closes is reported once at `PAP0016` against the span that opened it instead of running to end of file; `Parser::parseProperty` opens a block only for a full, named property, so one broken property header cannot swallow the rest of the script; and `Parser::tryParseDefine` rolls both the token cursor and the diagnostic bag back through `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/diagnostic.hpp:DiagnosticBag::truncateTo` when a statement turns out to be an assignment. Every node records the span it starts at and the span that closes it, so a later editor can highlight a whole declaration.

- Tests. `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_lexer.cpp` and `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_parser.cpp` are ports of PET's `PapyrusLexerTests` and `PapyrusParserTests` into this repository's gtest suites rather than Catch2, case for case and assertion for assertion; each test name states the behaviour that must not regress, and the parser file keeps PET's two recovery fixtures (`ABrokenLineDoesNotCostTheDeclarationsAfterIt`, `ABrokenStatementDoesNotCostTheRestOfTheFunction`) because those are the cases a "simplifying" rewrite of the recovery loop breaks first. `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_parse_real.cpp:PapyrusParseReal.ParsesEveryCorpusScriptWithoutCrashing` is the corpus sweep PET's `PapyrusCorpusTests` describes, gated on `FO4_PSC_CORPUS` (falling back to PET's `FO4RE_PSC_CORPUS`) and skipped without it. It requires only PET's clean rate above 0.995; the unexplained-file and exact-count checks run only when `FO4RE_PSC_STRICT` is set, because the documented counts are unmeasured. Roots are `;`-separated here, not `:` as in PET's C++ sweep, because `:` is the Windows drive separator and this is the variable Radicle's other `*_real.cpp` suites already read. The sweep requires zero exceptions, under `FO4RE_PSC_STRICT` requires every erroring file to be one of the two documented malformed shapes (headerless under a `modified` directory, or two `ScriptName` lines), and pins PET's figures — 18,802 files, 18,782 clean, 19 + 1 malformed — when the corpus is that size.

- Why the malformed set is a rule and not a list of paths. PluginEditTool's `docs/internal/KNOWLEDGE.md` and `docs/internal/PAPYRUS.md` record the count, the 19 + 1 split and the reason (F4SE's `scripts/modified/` fragments are pasted into base scripts and carry no `ScriptName`; one mod script declares it twice), but neither records the twenty file names, and no file in either repository does. The test therefore encodes the documented shape and prints the offending paths in its failure message, which is what a literal list could not do anyway for a corpus on another machine.

- How this front end and `fo4::psc` differ, read from both sources and not measured. `fo4::psc` (`Radicle/src/papyrus_source/parser.cpp:parse`) is a second, independently written source front end that already ships; the lifted one is not a replacement for it in this piece and `fo4::psc` was not touched. Reading the two, a file can be accepted by one and rejected by the other in these places: a UTF-8 BOM is skipped by `Radicle/src/papyrus_source/lexer.cpp:Lexer::Lexer` and reported three times as `PAP0004` by the lifted lexer, which has no BOM branch; a float exponent (`1e10`) or a leading-dot literal (`.5`) is lexed as a float by `fo4::psc` and rejected by the lifted `Lexer::lexNumber`, which knows only digits, one fractional part and the `f` suffix; `#` inside a qualified name is accepted by the lifted `Parser::parseQualifiedName` and is an unexpected character for `fo4::psc`; a stray `/;` outside a block comment is `LexErrorKind::InvalidCharacter` for `fo4::psc` and is harmless here, where `/` lexes as an operator and `;` starts a comment; a declaration whose name is one of the flag keywords (`int Hidden`) parses here and is refused by `fo4::psc`, whose keyword table contains `hidden`, `conditional` and `mandatory` and whose name readers accept only identifiers; a call broken across lines inside parentheses parses for `fo4::psc`, which suppresses a newline while `parenDepth_` is positive, and reports `PAP0014` here, where every line break is a token and the continuation backslash is the only way to join lines; an assignment to a non-assignable target (`5 = x`) is `ParseErrorKind::InvalidAssignmentTarget` for `fo4::psc` and is accepted here, where `Parser::parseStatement` builds an `AssignStatement` without checking the target; and pathological nesting (past 96 levels) or a chain past 512 links is refused by `fo4::psc` with `ParseErrorKind::DepthLimit` while the lifted parser has no depth or length guard and would build the tree. On the other side, `fo4::psc` stops at the first error and returns one `ParseError`, while the lifted parser recovers and reports up to 200 diagnostics per file, which is the property its own recovery tests pin.

- Not verified, and how to verify it. Nothing in this piece was compiled, configured, built or run: no CMake configure, no `ctest`, no gtest binary, no corpus sweep. The claim that the port compiles rests on the byte-level comparison above and on PluginEditTool's own build history, not on a compiler here. The corpus sweep has never executed, so the 18,802/18,782/20 figures are PET's recorded results restated as expectations, not measurements of this front end; `FO4RE_PSC_CORPUS` is unset on the authoring machine. To run it: configure with `-DRADICLE_BUILD_TESTS=ON`, then `FO4RE_PSC_CORPUS='/path/to/Scripts/Source;/path/to/f4se/scripts' ./fo4_tests --gtest_filter='Papyrus*'` on a machine that has the corpus; the `PapyrusParseReal` case skips without the variable and prints every erroring path when the shape does not match. The `fo4::psc` comparison above is a reading of both sources, not a differential run over the corpus; no per-file accept/reject table exists yet. Whether the lifted front end's missing recursion guard can be driven to a stack overflow by a hostile `.psc` is untested here and is worth a bounded-depth test before any caller feeds it untrusted input.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf

The SWF read surface is one opaque handle over `fo4::swf::read_swf` plus `fo4::abc::AbcFile::parse` for every DoABC block. Opening parses the tree and every ABC once, so every getter is a pure function of the bytes. The two method-pool getters, `radicle_swf_abc_method_at` and `radicle_swf_abc_method_disassemble`, still return `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR` for a DoABC block that did not parse. All `const char*` the handle returns point into the handle and stay valid until `radicle_swf_destroy`; only `radicle_swf_tag_payload` and `radicle_swf_abc_method_disassemble` allocate, and both release with the existing `radicle_free_bytes` rather than a new free function. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:copy_text` NUL-terminates the listing one byte past `*out_size`, which still counts only the text, so a C reader that stops at the NUL and the C# binding that reads `*out_size` bytes get the same listing. Outputs are zeroed before any argument check, the rule `Radicle/src/c_api_dds.cpp:radicle_dds_info` and `Radicle/src/c_api_nif.cpp` follow (#706).

Three open paths: loose bytes, a loose file, and a `radicle_ba2` entry. The archive path calls `radicle_ba2_find` and `radicle_ba2_extract` and copies the entry, so no second BA2 reader exists and the archive handle only has to outlive the call, not the movie; this is what lets GardenEngine delete its `Ba2Archive.cs` wrapper by passing the archive it already holds.

`radicle_swf_open_ba2` reports `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR` with a message naming LZMA for a `ZWS` movie, because compression lives in `fo4::swf` (phase 7 needs a linked LZMA library) and the C ABI does not rename that refusal. An empty or missing file is `RADICLE_STATUS_IO_ERROR`; a truncated body, a bad signature and an over-long tag are `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR`. `radicle_swf_open_ba2` frees the extracted buffer with `std::free` rather than `radicle_free_bytes`, because `radicle_free_bytes` clears the last error, so a refused movie keeps its message for `radicle_last_error`.

## Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:flatten_tags

The C ABI exposes the tag tree flat: every tag, sprite children included, in pre-order, each row carrying `parent` (the enclosing `DefineSprite` tag index, `RADICLE_SWF_NO_INDEX` at the root frame) and the sprite id plus an `inside_sprite` flag for the tags that sit in one. `SwfTag` is a tree of `children`, so a caller cannot index it directly; flattening at open time keeps the C surface index-based like `c_api_pex.h` and keeps `parent` the only invariant a caller has to trust. `sprite_id` comes from the enclosing `DefineSprite`; the sprite tag itself reports its own id so a caller can match children to their sprite without walking up.

`tag_code_name` supplies the `name` field and never returns null, so a caller can print an unknown code without a null check. Symbols and exports are gathered from `SwfTag::symbols`/`exports` in file order (one record per `SymbolClass` and `ExportAssets` entry), and frame labels are the `FrameLabel` tags whose payload is a null-terminated string: `SwfTag` decodes no field for them, so the reader copies the payload up to the first NUL and keeps the tag index, the sprite id and the inside-sprite flag for the caller to rebind to a frame.

## Radicle/src/c_api_swf_history.cpp:top_level_position

The edit-text verbs and the plan verbs take the flat index that `radicle_swf_tag_at` reports, but `SwfFile::tags` holds only the top-level tags. `radicle_swf_detail::top_level_position` (declared in `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_internal.hpp`) walks the top-level tags, counting each `DefineSprite` with its children, and returns the top-level position for a flat index that starts a top-level tag. It returns false for a tag inside a sprite and for an index past the end. `translate` in `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_history.cpp`, `radicle_swf_edit_text_read` and `radicle_swf_edit_text_apply` in `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_verbs.cpp` all go through it, so each refuses a tag inside a sprite with a message rather than reading or writing the tag at the same top-level number. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_history.cpp:subtree_size` is the one flat-span count, declared in `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_internal.hpp:radicle_swf_detail`; it counts each tag plus its recursive children, so a DefineSprite contributes its own tag and every child including its End tag. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_verbs.cpp:timeline_tags` and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_verbs.cpp:placement_json` use the same count.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_history.cpp:EditTextAddressesTheFlatIndexPastADefineSprite` reads, writes and refuses across a DefineSprite with children. Known limit: `placement_json` in `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_verbs.cpp` reports the top-level vector index as `tag_index`, which disagrees with the flat index once a sprite precedes the placement.

## Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:radicle_swf_abc_call_at

The ABC summary and the disassembler are two views of the same parsed block and the C ABI keeps them separate on purpose. The summary view (`radicle_swf_abc_class_*`, `_script_*`, `_function_*`, then `radicle_swf_abc_call_at` and `_multiname_at`) answers the census question and is read from `fo4::abc::summarize`; `AbcMethodSummary` carries no ABC method index, so the call and multiname getters take the `owner` (`RADICLE_SWF_OWNER_CLASS`/`_SCRIPT`/`_FUNCTION`), the owner index and the method index the getter just reported. A pair of indexes that names no method is `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, an index inside a method that is out of range is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`; the two are different mistakes and a caller can tell them apart.

The pool reports the name the ABC stores, so a constructor shows the class name where the summary derives `<init>`; the two views must not be mixed for names. The method-pool view (`radicle_swf_abc_method_at`, `_disassemble`) reads `AbcFile::methods`/`bodies` directly, because that is the only view that has a body to decode: `radicle_swf_abc_method_disassemble` rejects a method without a body as `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` and a block that did not parse as `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR`. Method and return-type names are copied into the handle when the block parses (`method_name`, `multiname_at` return by value, so a `c_str()` of a temporary would dangle). A block that fails to parse is still reported by `radicle_swf_abc_info_at` with `parsed == 0`, so a census can count broken blocks instead of losing the movie. Two details come from the container: `fo4::swf::abc_blocks` indexes the root tags while the C ABI reports the flat index `radicle_swf_tag_at` takes, so the view maps one to the other, and the payload is the ABC bytes alone for both tags: a `DoABC` (72) block has no flags or name, so `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:build_abc_views` hands `AbcFile::parse` the whole payload from byte 0 and `radicle_swf_abc_info` reports flags 0 and an empty name. A `DoABC2` (82) tag already decoded its flags, name and payload offset in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload`.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp:decode_placement_tag (#806 phase 3 placement)

`decode_placement_tag` decodes PlaceObject (4), PlaceObject2 (26), PlaceObject3 (70), RemoveObject (5) and RemoveObject2 (28) into `SwfTag::placement` and `SwfTag::removal`. The layouts come from the SWF File Format Specification version 19 (`swf-spec-19.txt`, PlaceObject, PlaceObject3 and FILTER sections): the first flags byte of PlaceObject2/3 is HasClipActions 0x80, HasClipDepth 0x40, HasName 0x20, HasRatio 0x10, HasColorTransform 0x08, HasMatrix 0x04, HasCharacter 0x02, Move 0x01, and the PlaceObject3 second flags byte is Reserved 0x80, OpaqueBackground 0x40, HasVisible 0x20, HasImage 0x10, HasClassName 0x08, HasCacheAsBitmap 0x04, HasBlendMode 0x02, HasFilterList 0x01.

- Class-name erratum: the spec's field table says ClassName is read when PlaceFlagHasClassName is set **or** when PlaceFlagHasImage and PlaceFlagHasCharacter are both set, but real data disagrees. `Interface\StreamingInstallMenu.swf` in `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` has a PlaceObject3 with flags `0x06`, flags3 `0x10` and no class name, so `decode_place_object2` reads ClassName when HasClassName is set or when HasImage is set without HasCharacter. A Python port of that rule parsed all 31750 PlaceObject2, 790 PlaceObject3 and 2201 RemoveObject2 tags in that archive with no leftover bytes. The HasImage-without-character branch is not exercised by any shipped movie and is unverified.
- Filter list: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp:decode_filter_list` decodes every FILTERLIST entry into `SwfPlacement::filters` (`Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfFilter`), so the blend, cache and visible fields behind it are read at their offsets. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp:read_filter` sizes each body from the spec's DROPSHADOWFILTER, BLURFILTER, GLOWFILTER, BEVELFILTER, GRADIENTGLOWFILTER/GRADIENTBEVELFILTER, CONVOLUTIONFILTER and COLORMATRIXFILTER tables. Field widths: blur, angle and distance are FIXED (16.16, stored as doubles), strength is FIXED8 (8.8); colours are RGBA bytes stored as `0xAARRGGBB`; convolution and colour-matrix values are single-precision FLOAT, read with `std::bit_cast`. Flags: InnerShadow or InnerGlow 0x80, Knockout 0x40, CompositeSource 0x20; on the drop shadow and glow, Passes is the low 5 bits, while the bevel and both gradient types add OnTop 0x10 and take Passes from the low 4 bits. Blur Passes is the top 5 bits of its byte. Convolution Clamp is bit 1 and PreserveAlpha is bit 0. `SwfFilter` keeps every field for all eight ids and leaves the ones an id does not carry at their defaults. An unknown FilterID is malformed, as before.
- `SwfPlacement::filter_count` was removed: the count is `SwfPlacement::filters.size()`, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_keyframe.cpp:merge_placement` copies it into `SwfAuthoredFrameObject::filter_count` (the C ABI `filter_count` slot) only when the list is non-empty, as before. `read_rgba` in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp` also reads BackgroundColor, so the RGBA packing lives in one place. Blend mode was already in `SwfPlacement::blend_mode`; BitmapCache stays in `SwfPlacement::bitmap_cache` only, because `SwfAuthoredFrameObject` has no slot for it and the C ABI is not changed.
- Tests for the filter list: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_place_filters.cpp` (a new suite file, because `Radicle/tests/test_swf_place.cpp` is at 734 lines and any more tests would pass the 750-line cap). Regressions each one detects: `SwfPlaceFilters.DropShadowReadsRgbaColourFixedPointFieldsAndFlags` catches a colour read as ARGB, a 16.16 field read at 8.8 width, and a flags mask that lets Passes absorb InnerShadow; `SwfPlaceFilters.BlurAndGlowReadPassesFromTheirOwnBitsAndStrengthAtEightEight` catches blur Passes taken from the reserved low bits and a glow strength read as 16.16; `SwfPlaceFilters.BevelReadsShadowThenHighlightSignedAngleAndOnTopBeforeBlend` catches swapped bevel colours, an unsigned negative angle, OnTop folded into Passes, and a body-size drift that misplaces the blend byte; `SwfPlaceFilters.GradientGlowAndBevelReadEveryStopColourThenEveryRatio` catches stop colours interleaved with ratios and a gradient bevel (7) sized unlike a gradient glow (4); `SwfPlaceFilters.ConvolutionReadsDivisorBiasMatrixAndClampBeforeBlend` catches Clamp and PreserveAlpha swapped, a matrix read at the wrong count, and a blend byte read as matrix data; `SwfPlaceFilters.ColorMatrixKeepsAllTwentyEntriesBeforeTheBlendMode` catches a colour matrix read as 16 or 24 entries; `SwfPlaceFilters.AnUnknownFilterIdOrAShortGradientBodyMakesThePlacementMalformed` catches an unknown FilterID or a truncated stop list accepted as a placement.
- ClipActions (flag 0x80, PlaceObject2/3) are not parsed: they are the last field, so only `SwfPlacement::has_clip_actions` is recorded.
- `read_matrix` in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:read_matrix` keeps the spec defaults for a missing scale or rotate term (scale 1.0, rotate 0) and calls `BitReader::align`, because a MATRIX is padded to a byte boundary before the next field. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:BitReader::align` is the only way to set the bit cursor to a byte boundary.
- `read_color_transform` in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp:read_color_transform` reads CXFORMWITHALPHA (PlaceObject2/3) or CXFORM with three channels (PlaceObject, which has no alpha term and keeps alpha at its 256/0 defaults). Add terms follow multiply terms, as in the spec.
- PlaceObject (4) has no flags: a CXFORM follows the matrix only when bytes remain, and `decode_place_object` checks for that with `BitReader::byte_position`.
- The PlaceObject3 BackgroundColor is read as RGBA (R, G, B, A bytes) and stored as `0xAARRGGBB`, the same convention as `SetBackgroundColor` in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload`.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_place.cpp` (a new suite file, because `Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp` would pass the 750-line cap). `SwfPlacement.PlaceObject2DecodesDepthCharacterMatrixRatioAndName` catches a swapped Ratio and Name order and a wrong scale bit width, `SwfPlacement.PlaceObject2DecodesMoveClipDepthAndAlphaColorTransform` catches a dropped alpha term and a clip depth read before the colour transform, `SwfPlacement.PlaceObject1DecodesMatrixAndRgbColorTransformWithoutAlpha` catches reading an alpha channel for PlaceObject, `SwfPlacement.PlaceObject3ImageWithCharacterHasNoClassName` reproduces the flags and field order of the StreamingInstallMenu tag with a one-byte matrix and catches reading a class name when HasImage and HasCharacter are both set (the movie turns malformed), `SwfPlacement.PlaceObject3ImageWithoutCharacterReadsClassName` and `SwfPlacement.PlaceObject3HasClassNameReadsNameBeforeCharacter` catch a dropped class name, `SwfPlacement.PlaceObject3SkipsEveryFilterKindByItsSpecSize` pins the body size of filter ids 2 to 7, `SwfPlacement.PlaceObject3VisibleFlagAloneDoesNotConsumeABackgroundColor` catches the visible byte pulling in an RGBA background without the OpaqueBackground bit, `SwfPlacement.PlaceObject3SkipsFilterListAndReadsBlendCacheVisibleAndBackground` catches a filter size drift that misplaces blend, cache, visible and background, `SwfPlacement.RemoveObjectAndRemoveObject2DecodeDepthWithAndWithoutCharacter` catches RemoveObject2 reading a character id, `SwfPlacement.MatrixWithoutScaleOrRotateEndsOnAByteBoundaryBeforeRatio` catches a MATRIX that ends mid-byte before the ratio, while a missing `BitReader::align` is caught by the PlaceObject1 test, where the colour transform follows the matrix on the same cursor, and `SwfPlacement.TruncatedPlacementKeepsRawPayloadAndTheNextTagStillParses` catches a decoder that over-reads or drops the tag.
- Fixture change: `Radicle/tests/test_swf.cpp:sprite_payload` now carries a valid PlaceObject2 (5 bytes) instead of a 2-byte placeholder, because a sprite child of tag 26 is decoded now.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:decode_shape_tag (#806 phase 4 shapes and morph)

`decode_shape_tag` decodes the SHAPEWITHSTYLE body of DefineShape 2, DefineShape2 22, DefineShape3 32 and DefineShape4 83 into `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfShape`: the fill style array, the line style array, the edge and style-change record counts, and for tag 83 the edge bounds RECT and the flags byte. `decode_morph_tag` in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:decode_morph_tag` does the same for DefineMorphShape 46 and DefineMorphShape2 84 into `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfMorphShape`; its fill and line styles are stored as start/end pairs in `SwfMorphFillStyle` and `SwfMorphLineStyle`, because a renderer must be able to draw the tween and not just count it. A pair holds everything the tag carries: a solid colour pair, or two gradient matrices with the shared spread and interpolation, one `SwfMorphGradientStop` per stop (start ratio and colour, end ratio and colour), two focal points for 0x13, two bitmap matrices, and for a line the two widths, the LineStyle2 flags, two miter limits and an optional fill. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:read_morph_fill_style` and `:read_morph_line_style` write those fields instead of skipping them, and `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfMorph.KeepsTheStartAndEndStylePairs` pins the colour, stop, width and gradient values of the DefineMorphShape fixture while `SwfMorph.KeepsAMorphLineStyleFill` pins the DefineMorphShape2 line fill. The arms shipped data never reaches are pinned by one tag built in `Radicle/tests/swf_art_fixtures.hpp:morph_every_kind_payload`: a DefineMorphShape2 whose own header arrays hold a solid fill, a linear gradient (0x10, spread 1 and interpolation 1, one stop), a radial gradient (0x12, spread 2 and interpolation 2, two stops), a focal gradient (0x13, one stop and its focal pair), one fill of each bitmap kind 0x40..0x43, a version 2 line with JoinStyle 2 and its miter pair, and a line whose HasFillFlag carries a gradient fill. Every matrix in it is identity scale with its own translate pair, so a reader that drops a matrix or gives the end pair the start one's values is visible. `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfMorph.KeepsEveryFillAndLineKindTheTagCarries` reads it through the model and `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_morph.cpp:CApiSwfTest.ReadsEveryMorphFillKindThroughTheGetters` through the C getters, so no arm has a single witness: storing the start ratio in the end field and swapping a bitmap fill's matrix pair fails both tests.

The layouts come from the **SWF File Format Specification version 19** (`swf-spec-19.txt`, DefineShape, DefineMorphShape and the SHAPEWITHSTYLE sections) and were re-derived field by field from the Rust reader in `%TEMP%\swfref\ruffle-read.rs:read_define_shape`, `:read_shape_styles`, `:read_fill_style`, `:read_line_style`, `:read_gradient`, `:read_shape_record`, `:read_define_morph_shape`, `:read_morph_fill_style` and `:read_morph_line_style`.

- LineStyle2's flags field is **not** a little-endian word, and that is the one place the spec text and the data disagree. The field is StartCapStyle UB[2], JoinStyle UB[2], HasFillFlag UB[1], NoHScaleFlag UB[1], NoVScaleFlag UB[1], PixelHintingFlag UB[1], Reserved UB[5], NoClose UB[1], EndCapStyle UB[2] — the first eight bits fill the first byte and the last eight the second. Reading it as a `UI16` (as `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:read_matrix` does for a MATRIX's translate width, and as the C# port in `GardenEngine` `tools/SwfTools/ShapeParser.cs:LineFlags` does) gives a JoinStyle of 0 where the data has 2, so the decoder skips the MiterLimitFactor UI16 that follows and every later field is three bytes early. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:read_line_style` therefore reads the two bytes high first. Real data settled it: before the fix 238 of the 592 shipped DefineShape4 tags failed (a `0x0300` miter factor read as a colour byte produced fill style kinds like `0xc3` and `0xfd` and left `NumFillBits`/`NumLineBits` at `0xf`), and after it all 592 decode. The same read is used for MorphLineStyle2 in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:read_morph_line_style`.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:read_shape_styles` treats a style count of `0xFF` as the extended `UI16` form only when the shape version is 2 or later, so a DefineShape 1 with 255 fill styles keeps 255; the line style array follows the same rule, which the spec does not state but the reader in `ruffle-read.rs:read_shape_styles` applies. A declared count is also bounded by the bytes that could still encode it (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:style_count_fits`, one byte per fill style and the two UI16 widths per line style), so a count of 0xFFFF in a payload of a few bytes is `malformed_tag` instead of a walk that has to run out of data; `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:read_morph_styles` applies the same bound to both of its arrays.
- A style-change record with StateNewStyles set replaces the fill style array, the line style array **and** NumFillBits/NumLineBits: SWF 19's StyleChangeRecord (page 127) lists "Replace the current fill and line style arrays with a new set of styles" as one of the record's actions, and the style indices that follow are one-based into the arrays in force at their own record. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:read_shape_records` therefore parses the new block into the `SwfShapeStyles` it was handed, installs its bit widths and restarts the bit reader at the byte the new arrays end on. The arrays it replaced are not dropped: `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfShape` holds one pair of arrays and every generation is appended to it, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:read_records` rebases the indices of the records a block installs onto that generation's offset (`fill_base`/`line_base`), so every index the model exposes stays inside the arrays it stores. Shipped data needs that: the four archives hold 4,780 StateNewStyles records, and 4,981 of the 8,920,910 shape records name a style their tag's last generation no longer holds, so a model keeping only the final pair would hand a renderer indices past the end of the array it stores. The generations a merge adds are visible in the sweep: 29,028 fill styles and 1,999 line styles against the 22,802 and 1,093 of the last-generation-only model, with 784 gradient stops. A NewStyles block inside a morph stream is laid out as start/end style pairs (MORPHFILLSTYLEARRAY and MORPHLINESTYLEARRAY, SWF 19 pages 148 and 150), so `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:read_morph_records` walks that block through `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:read_morph_styles`, the same reader `decode_morph_tag` uses for the tag's own style arrays, instead of reading a shape's FILLSTYLEARRAY; the shared record loop is `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:read_records`, templated over `SwfShapeStyles` and `SwfMorphStyles`, so there is no mode flag to get wrong. `decode_morph_tag` stores the tag's own pairs followed by every generation its two streams install, appended and rebased by the same `read_records`, and the end stream starts from the arrays the start stream left in force because a block in either stream replaces the arrays that stream indexes: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfMorph.NewStylesBlockKeepsBothGenerationsOnTheTag` builds a block in both streams, so the tag carries eight fill pairs and three line pairs, and pins the records' rebased fill indices, 3 for the start stream's block and 6 for the end's; `SwfMorph.NewStylesRecordParsesMorphStylePairs` builds one in both edge streams, and `SwfMorph.NewStylesRecordParsesMorphGradientAndBitmapFills` builds a second whose block carries a solid fill, a focal gradient (0x13, two stops and the focal pair) and a bitmap fill (0x42, two matrices) plus a version-1 line style, so the 0x13 and 0x42 arms of `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:read_morph_fill_style` are walked inside the nested block and not only in the tag's own header arrays; dropping either arm's tail desyncs the record after the block and only that test fails. The edge record forms are the spec's: a straight edge has GeneralLineFlag, then two deltas, or VertLineFlag and one delta; a curved edge has control and anchor deltas, all at `NumBits + 2` bits wide.
- A shape record may not name a style the tag does not hold: StyleChangeRecord's FillStyle0, FillStyle1 and LineStyle are indices, zero meaning "no style" and every other value one-based into the fill and line style arrays, so an index past the end is an index a renderer would use to index past the end. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:read_records` therefore reads the three indices into locals instead of discarding them and checks each against `Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:StyleBounds`, the sizes of the arrays in force: a record that also installs new styles is checked against whichever of the old and the installed set is larger (readers disagree on which generation its own indices name), and once the block is installed `StyleBounds` moves to the new arrays so the records after it are held to those. An index outside is `malformed_tag`. The bounds are seeded by the caller because the record loop is shared: `decode_shape_tag` passes the sizes of the `SwfShapeStyles` it just read, and `decode_morph_tag` passes the tag's `SwfMorphStyles` for the start stream and carries the same `StyleBounds` into the end stream. That seeding fixed a gap the check exposed: `decode_morph_tag` used to hand `read_morph_records` a `SwfMorphStyles` with only `fill_bits`/`line_bits` set, so a morph stream's records were checked against arrays the reader believed empty, and the 62 shipped DefineMorphShape tags answer exactly that shape — every one draws fill 1 and line 1 of a tag that holds one pair of each. Handing the streams empty bounds again fails all 62 shipped morph tags, and tightening the comparison from `>` to `>=` fails 339 of the 356 shipped movies, so the bound is live over real data rather than only over fixtures; with it in place the sweep is unchanged at 11,859 shape tags, 62 morph tags and `art_failures == 0`, and 0 shipped record names a style out of range.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:decode_shape_tag` requires the record stream's EndShapeRecord to land on the last byte of the payload, so a body whose walk drifted is `malformed_tag` instead of silently short; `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:decode_morph_tag` applies the same rule to the end edge stream and prefers the declared Offset to locate it when the two disagree.
- DefineMorphShape2's header order is the spec's (SWF 19, DefineMorphShape2, page 146): CharacterId, StartBounds, EndBounds, StartEdgeBounds, EndEdgeBounds, then Reserved UB[6] with UsesNonScalingStrokes and UsesScalingStrokes as its last two bits, one byte, and only then Offset. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:decode_morph_tag` read that byte from the first byte of EndEdgeBounds and then put the cursor back after the RECT, so Offset, the style arrays and both edge streams came one byte early: a trace of the fixture showed `morph.flags` reading `0x60` where the byte is `0x02`, the Offset reading `0x2F02` where it is `0x2F`, and `malformed_tag` from the end-edges guard. The flags byte is now read after EndEdgeBounds, which `SwfMorph.DefineMorphShape2DecodesBothEdgeStreams` covers; no shipped movie carries tag 84, so the fixture is the only witness for the whole version 2 path.
- Morph edge streams: the start records are followed by a byte holding NumFillBits/NumLineBits for the end stream (the writers emit 0) and then the end records, whose Offset field counts from the byte after the Offset itself. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:decode_morph_tag` parses the start records to find their end, uses the Offset when it differs, and reads the end stream with its own bit widths rather than the start stream's.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:interpolate_morph_commands` draws a frame between the two: it takes the morph and a ratio, 0 for the start frame and 1 for the end, and returns the commands a renderer draws. SWF 19 (DefineMorphShape, page 145) keeps the style changes for both shapes only in StartEdges and one edge per edge in EndEdges, so the helper copies every style change of the start stream in place and pairs each move and edge of that stream with the next drawable command of the end stream, skipping a style change a writer left in the end stream so it cannot shift the geometry. Pairing by raw index instead would spend the end stream's first edge on the start's style change and morph every later edge toward the wrong one; the shipped corpus shows the shape of the data that punishes it, since all 62 tags carry streams of different lengths (the end stream has no style changes) and 75 of their 3,364 edge pairs change type. A pair whose edges differ in type is drawn as a curve, with the straight side promoted by the spec's rule on the same page (control point at half its delta, anchor at the endpoint, which in this model's control-relative anchor is the same half delta), so ratio 0 still draws the start shape and ratio 1 the end one exactly. Deltas blend in double, because two int32 twips can leave int32, and round to the nearest twip with halves away from zero, so a symmetric pair such as 1 and -1 lands on 1 at ratio 0.25; a ratio outside 0..1 is clamped, and a start command with no end counterpart ends the result rather than pairing it with nothing. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_morph_tween.cpp` (a file of its own, because `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp` is at the 750-line cap) holds three: `SwfMorph.InterpolatesTheEdgeStreamsAtARatio` pins the rounding and both clamped ends, `SwfMorph.InterpolationPairsGeometryAcrossTheStartStyles` pins that a start style change is copied without consuming the end stream and that an unpaired edge ends the result, and `SwfMorph.InterpolationPromotesAnEdgeThatChangesType` pins the promotion at half way and that each ratio lands on its own stream; the real-data check runs the helper on every shipped tag and records `morph_unequal_streams` (62), `morph_kind_mismatches` (75) and `morph_end_style_changes` (0, which is the spec's "contains no style information" for EndEdges holding over the corpus) beside the pair counts, so a corpus that shifts any of them is visible.

Evidence, from a read-only local scan of `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` (315 movies, 2026-10-24, nothing stored in the repo): 10,819 shape tags — DefineShape 8520, DefineShape2 777, DefineShape3 930, DefineShape4 592 — carrying 7,450,083 edge records (3,226,394 of them curved), 459,556 style-change records and 23,275 fill plus line styles; 62 DefineMorphShape tags with 3,670 draw commands across both streams, 3,364 of them edges and 306 moves or style changes; 56 lossless bitmaps (46 DefineBitsLossless, 10 DefineBitsLossless2), all BitmapFormat 5. Every one of those bodies parsed to its last byte with no leftover bytes and no `malformed_tag`, and none of them sits inside a DefineSprite, although the tree has 3,336 sprite tags. The shape styles the decoder stores take the same sweep: over the four archives it counts 29,028 fill styles (784 gradient stops between them) and 1,999 line styles, 42 of which carry a fill, and every one matches the field set its kind or flags promise — a solid fill with no matrix, stop or focal point, a gradient with its matrix and at most fifteen stops, a 0x13 with its focal point, a bitmap with its matrix and no stops, a DefineShape1..3 line with no flags, miter limit or fill, and a DefineShape4 line with a miter limit exactly when JoinStyle is two and a fill exactly when HasFillFlag is set (which is the only way a shape reaches `radicle_swf_shape_line_fill_at`). Dropping the `fill.matrix = matrix` assignment in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:read_gradient` turns 367 shipped styles into failures, so the check is live over real data and not just over the fixtures. The style pairs the decoder now stores take the same sweep: the counts each morph tag reports match the arrays it stores, and every pair matches the field set its kind has — a solid pair carries no matrix, stop or focal point, a gradient pair both matrices and at most fifteen stops (the width of NumGradients), a 0x13 pair both focal points, a bitmap pair both matrices and no stops, and a version 2 line carries a miter pair exactly when JoinStyle is two and a fill exactly when HasFillFlag is set (and then no colour pair). All 62 shipped tags are the simplest case, one solid colour pair and one colour line pair each, with 0 gradient stops and 0 line fills, so the gradient, focal, bitmap and line-fill arms of `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:read_morph_fill_style` and `:read_morph_line_style` are never witnessed by shipped data and rest on `Radicle/tests/swf_art_fixtures.hpp:morph_every_kind_payload`, read once through the model and once through the C getters; the sweep records `morph_fill_pairs`, `morph_line_pairs`, `morph_gradient_stops` and `morph_line_fills` so a patch or DLC that ships one of them moves a number. The two command streams are checked the same way: `check_morph_records` walks each stream, holds its straight plus curved edges to the tag's `start_edge_count` and `end_edge_count`, and runs every command's style indices through `record_is_consistent` against the arrays the tag stores, which is what would catch a stream parsed with the other stream's deltas or bit widths; the run counts 3,670 commands over the 62 tags and records `morph_records` beside the pair counts. Tags 6, 8, 21, 35, 90 and 84 appear in no Fallout 4 archive: a second read-only sweep, same day, of all 79 `.ba2` files in the game's Data folder parsed the 42 GNRL archives (the other 37 are DX10 texture archives, a format that holds no SWF) and found movies in four of them — `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` 315, `DLCCoast - Main.ba2` 16, `DLCNukaWorld - Main.ba2` 17, `DLCRobot - Main.ba2` 8, 356 in total — and each of the six codes counts 0 in every one of the four, so `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:decode_morph_tag`'s version 2 path (edge bounds, flags, MorphLineStyle2) and the whole of `Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap.cpp:decode_jpeg_tag` are fixture-only. The real-data test keeps that gap checkable instead of only stated: it records `morph2_tags` apart from `morph_tags` and `jpeg_tags` beside them, and the shipped corpus answers 62, 0 and 0. A patch or DLC whose movies carry DefineMorphShape2 or a JPEG tag moves one of those numbers on its own, and the same run then decodes those bodies through `check_art` and the byte-exact round trip, so the surface stops being fixture-only without a test change. The three DLC archives carry 1,040 shape tags (DLCCoast 284, DLCNukaWorld 421, DLCRobot 335) and one DefineBitsLossless2 of their own, which `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp:SwfRealData.ParsesEveryShippedMovieAndRoundTripsByteIdentically` now reads as well: over all four archives that is 356 movies, 11,859 shape tags, 8,920,910 shape record commands, 62 morph shapes carrying 3,670 morph record commands and 57 lossless bitmaps, 0 art failures, 0 unreadable movies, 0 LZMA movies and a byte-identical `write_swf` round trip for every movie.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp` is a suite of its own because `Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp` would pass the 750-line cap; its payload builders live in `Radicle/tests/swf_art_fixtures.hpp` (namespace `swf_art_test`, next to `Radicle/tests/swf_movie_builder.hpp`) because the suite itself then reached the cap, so the two files are now about 650 and 570 lines. `SwfShape.DefineShape3DecodesStylesAndEdgeRecords` catches a fill style read at the wrong colour depth and a record parser that loses the vertical and horizontal straight-edge forms, ## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_to_svg (composited frame SVG, slice a)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_to_svg` draws one root frame of a `SwfDisplayList` in row order, which is the paint order: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:build_display_list` keeps depth ascending at each level and places a sprite's expanded children straight after the sprite row, so the renderer does not recurse and does not sort. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body` looks each row's character up in the file's shape tags, then in its morph tags (see the morph rows section at the tail), and draws only decoded shapes, at `SwfFrameInstance::world_transform`. That transform's translate is already in pixels (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:transform_from_matrix` divides by 20), so `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:transform_text` prints it without a second division. The viewBox is the stage rect `file.header.frame_size` through `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:svg_open`. Bitmap fills keep the flat placeholder from `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_paths_to_svg`.

Skipped, each on purpose: text and button rows are drawn by later sections at the tail; video and bitmap rows are not shapes and draw nothing; a sprite row with a clip depth is a mask, see the hidden and sprite mask section at the tail. A morph row with a non-solid style is not drawn, as `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:character_shape` (formerly row_shape) gets nullptr from `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:interpolate_morph_shape`; see the morph rows section at the tail.

Former gaps, now closed in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body`: a hidden row that carries a clip depth opens its mask and paints nothing (Flash applying a hidden mask is recalled, unverified against Flash), and a sprite row with a clip depth masks its descendant shape rows (see the tail section).

Clip scope: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body` opens a mask at a shape row with a clip depth, visible or hidden, and emits `<clipPath id="r<index>clip" transform="matrix(...)">` with that shape's fill paths only (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_fill_paths_to_svg`), so a stroke on a mask shape is not part of the mask. A mask shape with only a stroke therefore clips everything out; that is unverified against the Flash player. The mask covers later rows at the same level whose depth is above the mask depth and at most its clip depth; a row below a masked row at the same level is masked too, because the list is depth-first. The scope ends at the first row of a lower level or at a same-level row past the clip depth. The `transform` attribute that `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body` puts on `clipPath` may be ignored by some consumers, and one that does will place the mask at the origin.

Colour: `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_display.hpp:SwfFrameInstance::world_color_transform` is added by this slice, not in the C ABI. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:compose_color` composes the sprite chain the way the engine does (`SwfTools/ArtworkStyles.cs:ColorTransform.Compose`): multiply is parent times child over 256 and add is parent multiply times child add over 256 plus parent add. The arithmetic runs in `std::int64_t` and each result is clamped to plus or minus 65536 by `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:clamp_color`, so a large parsed value cannot overflow a signed int; the bound is a chosen limit, not a value from the spec. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:color_matrix_text` writes a `feColorMatrix` with `color-interpolation-filters="sRGB"`, dividing multiply by 256 and add by 255 per channel. The filter uses `filterUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` over the stage rect (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:stage_region_text`), so strokes and zero-width shapes inside the stage are not clipped by a bounding-box region. Its user space is the root one because the filter's `<g>` carries no transform. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp` copies rows field by field, so the C ABI is unchanged and does not yet carry the colour.

Shared SVG helpers: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_defs_to_svg` and `shape_paths_to_svg` take an id prefix so several shapes can share one document; `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_fill_paths_to_svg` is the fill-only export that the mask branch uses. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_to_svg` passes `fill` and is meant to print the same bytes as before; the existing `SwfSvg` cases are the check, and they were not run here. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:svg_number` is the one number formatter.

Test regressions, all in `Radicle/tests/test_swf_display.cpp`, built from synthetic movies by `movie_of`, `place_full`, `matrix_full`, `square_shape` and `color_multiply_add`. `color_multiply_add` writes the four-channel cxform that `Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp` reads for PlaceObject2 (multiply and add each carry R, G, B and A).
- `SwfFrameSvg.PaintsShapesInDepthOrderWithTwipsScaledMatrices` catches a frame drawn in tag order rather than ascending depth (the depth-2 shape is placed first), a translate not divided from twips to pixels (400 twips must print 20), and a matrix whose b and c are swapped (0.25 and -0.25 print reversed).
- `SwfFrameSvg.PlacesASpriteChildAtItsParentsOffset` catches a sprite row drawn as a shape of its own and a child world transform that ignores the sprite placement (40 px instead of 60 px).
- `SwfFrameSvg.AppliesAPlacementColourTransformAsAColorMatrix` catches a placement colour transform dropped from the row, a multiplier divided by 255 (128 would print 0.501961), and an add term printed as a 0 to 255 value instead of a fraction (51 would print instead of 0.2).
- `SwfFrameSvg.InheritsTheSpriteColourTransformIntoItsChildren` catches a child of a tinted sprite drawn untinted because the colour is read only from the child's own placement.
- `SwfFrameSvg.ClipsOnlyTheRowsInsideTheMaskDepthRange` catches an off-by-one at the clip depth (the row at exactly the clip depth must be masked, the next depth must not), a mask shape painted as visible content, and a clipPath without its own transform.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_display.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.ClipMaskUsesOnlyFillGeometry` catches a mask shape with a stroke whose stroke path is copied into the `clipPath` (the expected clip holds the red fill path only), so a stroke widens the mask.
- `SwfFrameSvg.FrameOutsideTheRootTimelineDrawsAnEmptyStage` catches a frame index past the root timeline reading out of range or drawing a stale frame, where the expected result is an empty, well-formed stage.

Nothing here was built or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap.cpp:decode_jpeg_tag (#806 phase 4 bitmaps and JPEG)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap.cpp:decode_bitmap_tag` decodes DefineBitsLossless 20 and DefineBitsLossless2 36 and then **inflates** the image: the declared width and height give `((width * bytes_per_pixel) + 3) & ~3` bytes per row, and a zlib stream that does not produce exactly `palette + row * height` bytes is `malformed_tag` (`palette` is 0 unless the format is 3); the 64 MiB cap is applied to the row count by division before the product is formed, and the product is formed again with `palette` added. For BitmapFormat 3 the palette is **inside** the stream, not before it: SWF 19's DefineBitsLossless (pages 139 to 140) gives `ZlibBitmapData` as `COLORMAPDATA`, whose layout is `ColorTableRGB` followed by `ColormapPixelData` (page 140), and DefineBitsLossless2 the same with `ALPHACOLORMAPDATA` (page 142). The spec compresses the palette and the pixels as one block: "The COLORMAPDATA and BITMAPDATA structures contain image data. These structures are each compressed as a single block of data." `%TEMP%\swfref\sdk42_GFx_TagLoaders.cpp:GFx_DefineBitsLossless2Loader` reads only the `BitmapColorTableSize` byte, then hands zlib every remaining byte of the tag as one buffer and reads the palette out of the inflated bytes, so the palette entry count affects the expected length and not the stream offset: `(BitmapColorTableSize + 1)` entries of RGBA (4 bytes) for tag 36 and RGB (3 bytes) for tag 20, which is why the total depends on the tag code and not only on the format byte. Skipping the palette in the compressed bytes desynchronises zlib and every format-3 payload is refused, which is what `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfBitmap.LosslessColourMapInflatesThePaletteInsideTheStream` catches. `decode_jpeg_tag` handles DefineBits 6 and DefineBitsJPEG2 21 (character id then the image to the end), DefineBitsJPEG3 35 (character id, DataSize, image, alpha plane) and DefineBitsJPEG4 90 (the same with a deblocking UI16 between DataSize and the image), and JPEGTables 8 (the payload is the table stream). The alpha plane must inflate, and when `scan_jpeg_size` finds an SOF marker in the image it must inflate to exactly `width * height` bytes.

Evidence: the shipped corpus carries no JPEG tag at all, 0 of tags 6, 8, 21, 35 and 90 across the 356 movies in the four archives that hold movies (the sweep in the shape entry above), so `decode_jpeg_tag` is covered by `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp` fixtures only — a 17-byte SOF0 image plus a six-byte alpha plane — and its real-data half is unverified.

The order the decoder reads is the specification's: SWF File Format Specification version 19, DefineBitsJPEG3 (page 139) and DefineBitsJPEG4 (page 143) — character id, `AlphaDataOffset` as the count of bytes in `ImageData`, and under tag 90 only, the `DeblockParam` UI16 between that count and the image, then the image of that many bytes and the zlib alpha plane to the end of the payload, one byte per pixel and `width * height` bytes once inflated. `%TEMP%\swfref\sdk42_GFx_TagLoaders.cpp:GFx_DefineBitsJpeg3Loader` (Scaleform GFx 4.2) reads the same order, with the deblock under tag 90 only and before it seeks the image, and `%TEMP%\swfref\ruffle-read.rs:read_define_bits_jpeg_3` reads `data_size`, then the deblock when the version is 4, then the image, then the rest of the payload as alpha. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap.cpp:scan_jpeg_size` skips the repeated `0xFF` fill bytes ITU T.81 B.1.1.2 allows in front of a marker, so a filled marker still yields its SOF geometry and the alpha plane is checked against exactly `width * height`; before that skip the scan read the fill byte as the marker, took the following bytes as a length, gave up, and let the alpha plane inflate to any size, which `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfJpeg.DefineBitsJpeg3SeesTheSofBehindFillBytes` catches by feeding the old scan a five-pixel plane for a 2 by 3 image. The spec's own note that a pre-version-8 movie may carry an erroneous `0xFF 0xD9 0xFF 0xD8` before the SOI still lands in the unknown-size branch, where the plane is only required to inflate. `%TEMP%\abc-ref` holds only the ABC parser, the trait classes, the interpreter and the opcode table, so it says nothing about either path. The lossless path is verified on all 56 bitmaps of `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` (57 across the four archives that hold movies), every one of which inflates to its declared geometry, but every one of them is BitmapFormat 5 — 46 DefineBitsLossless and 11 DefineBitsLossless2, counted by a read-only walk of the 351 plain `FWS`/`CWS` movies (the five `CFX` movies are not in that count). No shipped bitmap uses format 3: the pre-change decoder started its inflate inside the palette, which no format-3 tag can survive, and the 356-movie run reported 0 art failures on the head before this change and again after it, so the colour-map arithmetic is fixture-only and those 57 say nothing about it.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_shape

`Radicle/src/c_api_swf_art.cpp` exposes the decoded art through `radicle_swf_shape_at`, `radicle_swf_shape_fill_at`, `radicle_swf_shape_fill_stop_at`, `radicle_swf_shape_line_at`, `radicle_swf_shape_line_fill_at`, `radicle_swf_shape_line_fill_stop_at`, `radicle_swf_morph_at`, `radicle_swf_morph_fill_at`, `radicle_swf_morph_fill_stop_at`, `radicle_swf_morph_line_at`, `radicle_swf_morph_line_fill_at`, `radicle_swf_morph_line_fill_stop_at`, `radicle_swf_bitmap_at`, `radicle_swf_jpeg_at` and `radicle_swf_jpeg_tables_at`, all keyed by the flat tag index `radicle_swf_tag_at` already reports, so a shape inside a DefineSprite resolves the same way. A tag that carries no body of the requested kind is `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`; an index outside the tag list, a NULL handle or a style index outside the array is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The two line-fill getters follow the morph ones: `radicle_swf_shape_line_fill_at` hands back the `radicle_swf_fill_style` a line style reports `has_fill` for, `radicle_swf_shape_line_fill_stop_at` hands back each stop of that fill, and both answer `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` for a line that carries a colour pair instead. Without them a DefineShape4's gradient stroke was the one fill a renderer could see the flag for and not read, since `radicle_swf_shape_at` exposes only the shape's own fill array. The record stream a renderer draws is exposed beside the styles: `radicle_swf_shape_at` reports `record_count` and `radicle_swf_shape_record_at` walks that many `radicle_swf_shape_record` commands in file order — a move, a style change, a straight edge or a curved edge, chosen by `radicle_swf_record_kind`. A command keeps what the tag stores, so a straight edge carries its delta in `x`/`y` with the other axis left zero (a vertical edge has only a y delta, a horizontal one only an x delta) and a curved edge its control delta in `control_x`/`control_y` followed by its anchor delta in `x`/`y`; a style change carries the `fill0`, `fill1` and `line` indices it names, one-based into the arrays `radicle_swf_shape_fill_at` and `radicle_swf_shape_line_at` walk with zero meaning "no style"; a style a later StateNewStyles block replaced is still stored, so the index never names an entry the shape lacks. Moves are deltas like the edges, and a style-change record that also moves becomes two commands, so `moves + style changes == style_change_count` while `straight + curved == edge_count`; the end record is not a command and the stream simply ends. A morph shape has two such streams and exposes both the same way: `radicle_swf_morph_at` reports `start_record_count` and `end_record_count`, `radicle_swf_morph_start_record_at` walks the start stream and `radicle_swf_morph_end_record_at` the end one, each filling the same `radicle_swf_shape_record` as the shape getter, and `start_edge_count`/`end_edge_count` bound the edges each stream contributes where the morph's single count could not say which stream a command came from. A morph whose end stream holds only the EndShapeRecord reports `end_record_count == 0` and its end-record getter answers `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, like any other index past the stream. A renderer playing the morph asks for the frame between the two states instead: `radicle_swf_morph_frame_count` reports how many commands the interpolation yields at a ratio and `radicle_swf_morph_frame_record_at` walks them, so the pairing, the straight-to-curve promotion and the clamping of ratios outside 0..1 live in one place rather than in every consumer. The handle keeps the frame it built last for each morph tag, keyed by the clamped ratio, so a walk of n commands costs one interpolation instead of n and a renderer that asks for the same frame twice pays for neither (measured on a 128-edge morph: 1,798 ns per frame query before, 8 ns after, and 217 us per walk of 130 commands before 1.6 us after); another ratio or another tag rebuilds the frame, since a cache keyed by every ratio the playhead passes would grow with the animation, and the cache sits on the handle, so frame calls on one handle must be serialized. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_morph.cpp:CApiSwfTest.RebuildsTheFrameWhenTheTagOrRatioChanges` covers both keys: two morph tags in one movie, one whose frame holds two commands and one whose start stream stores no records and therefore draws an empty frame, walked twice around a ratio change, so a frame of the wrong tag or ratio is visible. The fields and the two exports are why `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is 63, and the two frame getters are why it is 64; the cache is private to the handle and does not move the version.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_shape.version` is derived from the tag code rather than stored, because `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfShape` keeps only the DefineShape4 flags and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_art.cpp:shape_version` maps 2/22/32/83 to 1/2/3/4. `edge_bounds` equals `bounds` for the tags before DefineShape4, where the field does not exist.
- Colours are `0xAARRGGBB`. An RGB solid fill or gradient stop, which the tags before DefineShape3 use, reports `0xFF` for alpha, and the notes on `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload`'s `SetBackgroundColor` keep their own convention where a missing alpha byte is 0: the two agree on the channel order and disagree only on what "the tag has no alpha byte" means, because a fill without an alpha byte is opaque while a background without one has no alpha channel at all.
- The morph style getters report the pair rather than a resolved tween: `radicle_swf_morph_fill_at` fills a `radicle_swf_morph_fill_style` (kind, `start_color`/`end_color`, `has_start_matrix`/`has_end_matrix` with the six matrix values each, spread, interpolation, `stop_count`, and the two focal points behind `has_start_focal`/`has_end_focal`), `radicle_swf_morph_fill_stop_at` fills a `radicle_swf_morph_gradient_stop` with both ratios and both colours, and `radicle_swf_morph_line_at` fills a `radicle_swf_morph_line_style` with both widths, the LineStyle2 flags, both colours, `has_fill` and the two miter limits. `radicle_swf_morph_line_fill_at` reports the line's fill through the same fill struct and returns `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` when that line style carries a colour pair instead, which is the only NOT_FOUND the five of them return for a tag that is a morph shape. `radicle_swf_morph_line_fill_stop_at` is the stop getter for that fill: without it a line fill reported a `stop_count` no call could address, so a renderer could see that a stroke is a gradient and not read the stops it needs to draw it. It takes the line index and the stop index, returns the same `radicle_swf_morph_gradient_stop` as the fill stop getter, `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` when the line carries no fill (matching `radicle_swf_morph_line_fill_at`) and `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a line or stop index outside the arrays; `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_morph.cpp:CApiSwfTest.ReadsEveryMorphFillKindThroughTheGetters` pins both stops of the gradient line fill and those three refusals.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp` no longer defines `radicle_swf`, `tag_view` and `abc_view`; they moved to `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_internal.hpp` so the art getters in the second translation unit can read the same handle.
- The managed side reads the pairs once at open time: `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/SwfMorphs.cs:SwfFile.Morphs` walks the tag list for codes 46 and 84 and turns each into a `SwfMorphShapeRecord` keyed by the flat tag index, with `SwfMorphFillStyleRecord`, `SwfMorphLineStyleRecord`, `SwfMorphGradientStopRecord`, `SwfMatrixRecord` and `SwfRectRecord` for what the pairs hold.
