The native presence flags become nullable values — a fill's `StartMatrix`/`EndMatrix` are null unless the kind carries a matrix, `StartFocalPoint`/`EndFocalPoint` are null outside 0x13, and a line's miter limits are null unless its JoinStyle asks for them — so a renderer switches on `Kind` and never calls `Radicle.Interop.Native` itself. `StartCommands` and `EndCommands` hold the two record streams as the same `SwfShapeCommandRecord` a shape's `Commands` uses, read through `radicle_swf_morph_start_record_at` and `radicle_swf_morph_end_record_at` over `StartRecordCount`/`EndRecordCount`, so a renderer walks a morph exactly as it walks a shape and keeps `StartEdgeCount`/`EndEdgeCount` as the edge bound of each stream. `SwfFile.MorphCommandsAt(tagIndex, ratio)` draws a frame between the two states: it asks the two frame exports for the count and then each command, so a managed renderer gets the same pairing, promotion and clamping as the native model without reimplementing them, and the call throws `RadicleException` with `NotFound` for a tag that is not a morph. `Radicle.Interop.Tests/SwfTests.cs:InterpolatesAMorphFrameThroughTheManagedWrapper` builds a DefineMorphShape whose two streams each move and draw one straight edge in opposite directions, pins `MorphCommandsAt` at half way and at both clamped ends and checks that a tag without a morph and an index past the tags are refused, while `ReadsMorphStylePairsThroughTheManagedWrapper` reads a DefineMorphShape's solid pair and pins that both command lists stay empty when each stream holds only its end record, and `ReadsAMorphLineFillThroughTheManagedWrapper` reads a DefineMorphShape2 line fill, which is also what drives `radicle_swf_morph_line_fill_stop_at` from managed code, and pins the start stream's move and straight edge and the end stream's matching pair; both movies are built in the test, so no game data is needed.
- `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/SwfArt.cs` does the same for the other art kinds: `Shapes` (codes 2, 22, 32, 83), `Bitmaps` (20, 36), `Jpegs` (6, 21, 35, 90) and `JpegTables` (8), each keyed by the flat tag index and filled once at open time through the same getters. A shape fill maps `has_matrix` and kind 0x13 onto a nullable `Matrix` and `FocalPoint` and carries `SwfGradientStopRecord` entries, a bitmap reports `ColorTableSize` only for the palette formats and a JPEG reports `AlphaSize` only when `has_alpha` is set. `SwfLineStyleRecord` carries the fill a LineStyle2 HasFillFlag selects, read through `radicle_swf_shape_line_fill_at` and `radicle_swf_shape_line_fill_stop_at`, so a shape's gradient stroke reaches a renderer with its stops; a DefineShape1..3 line has no flags and keeps its colour. `Radicle.Interop.Tests/SwfTests.cs:ReadsShapeBitmapAndJpegTagsThroughTheManagedWrapper` builds one movie holding a DefineShape4 with a miter line and a gradient-fill line, a DefineBitsLossless2 (zlib through `System.IO.Compression.ZLibStream`), a DefineBits and a JPEGTables and pins all four lists, and the plain movie's test asserts all four stay empty.

## Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_timeline.hpp:SwfMovie and Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:build_movie

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:build_movie` is the first derived model over the tag list rather than another tag view: it turns the raw stream into one root timeline and one timeline per `DefineSprite`, each with a per-frame display list, its frame labels and its placement rows. The parity target is the GardenEngine PR #277 C# tool, `tools/SwfTools/SwfDocument.cs:SwfDocument.Timeline` and `tools/SwfTools/Inspection.cs:Inspection.Report`, because the editor has to reproduce that tool's census numbers on the same movies. The C# side normalises the MATRIX while reading (`Transform` keeps scale over 65536 and translate over 20), so `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_timeline.hpp:SwfTransform` does the same instead of carrying `SwfMatrix` fixed point into composition; `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:transform_from_matrix` is the only place the 16.16 and twips fields are converted, and `:compose_transform` reproduces the C# `Transform.Compose` term for term so a nested sprite's world position does not drift by a twips rounding.

The carry rules are the C# ones and are the reason this is a model rather than a filter. A fresh `PlaceObject` 4 / `PlaceObject2` 26 / `PlaceObject3` 70 replaces whatever sat at that depth and starts from identity, because an omitted MATRIX in a fresh placement means identity. A `Move` inherits every field the tag omits from the live object at that depth, so a move-only update keeps the matrix and name, and a later replacement inherits the moved matrix rather than the original one. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:build_timeline` rejects a move whose depth is not live, a placement that carries neither a character nor a move, and a class-only placement (a `PlaceObject3` with `HasClassName` and no `HasCharacter`), which the C# side also refuses because resolving the class needs the runtime. A `RemoveObject` 5 / `RemoveObject2` 28 erases the depth, so a later fresh placement starts from identity. `SwfTimeline::frames` holds the active objects in ascending depth after each `ShowFrame`, which is the state a renderer or an editor selection walks; `SwfTimeline::placements` holds one row per placement operation that resolves to a character, tagged with its 1-based frame and its authored tag index, which is the C# `Placement` record and the input to the inspection rows.

Frame counts are checked where the C# side checks them and only there: the root timeline must produce exactly `SwfHeader::frame_count` `ShowFrame` tags, and a mismatch makes the whole movie `SwfTimelineStatus::malformed` with `SwfMovie::message` set, because the root count is a header contract. A sprite's declared count is recorded in `SwfTimeline::declared_frames` but not enforced, because the C# `SwfDocument` does not enforce it either and shipped sprites exist whose declared count the reader has no reason to second-guess. `DefineSprite` definitions are indexed even when nothing places them, and a duplicate sprite id, a placement that did not decode, and a sprite whose children fail all return `malformed` rather than a half-built movie.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:census` counts only the top-level tags, as the C# `ArtworkMovie` definition table does: shapes 2/22/32/83, sprites 39, morphs 46/84, images 6/20/21/35/36/90, `DefineEditText` 37, buttons 7/34, videos 60, `SymbolClass` pairs and one row per `ImportAssets` 57 / `ImportAssets2` 71. The label half comes from `build_movie` and deliberately includes sprite definitions that are unnamed or never placed, which is the "N sprite labels in K of M sprite definitions (including unnamed/unplaced)" number the parity census publishes; counting only printed `states:` rows undercounts for exactly those definitions.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:inspect_swf` writes the report the C# tool writes for one movie: the stage line, the document class bound to `SymbolClass` id 0, the import rows, the root labels, the totals, the frame-label census, one row per named placement or text field, the `states:` line of a placed sprite, and the unnamed top-level summary. It keeps the C# limits rather than inventing new ones — 400 rows and four levels of sprite nesting by default, `SwfInspectionOptions` to move them — and it deduplicates rows inside one timeline by depth, name and character, so a repeated placement of the same instance does not flood the report. A row's position is the composed world transform; a shape's size and an edit field's rect are that same transform applied to the definition bounds (`:transformed_bounds`), converted from twips to pixels, and formatted with the C# `0.#` rounding.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_edit_text` is the one new tag decode this needed, `DefineEditText` 37, because the C# census counts those declarations and the inspection rows print their rect, text and flags. The field order follows the C# `SwfDocument.ReadText` and therefore the SWF 19 layout: character id, bounds RECT, the two flag bytes, the font id when bit 0 of the first is set, the font class string when bit 7 of the second is set, the height UI16 when either of those is set, an RGBA colour when bit 2 of the first is set, the maximum length when bit 1 of the first is set, nine layout bytes when bit 5 of the second is set, then the variable name and the initial text. The colour keeps the `0xAARRGGBB` convention the other decoded colours use. A payload that ends early is `SwfStatus::malformed_tag` with the raw bytes kept, like every other decoder, so nothing here can reject a movie the container reader accepted.

Not covered by this pass, deliberately: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:build_timeline` stops at the authored frame state, so the per-frame sprite advance and the wrap-at-end behaviour of the C# `ArtworkMovie.cs:ArtworkClip.Advance` (a child timeline advancing with its parent, clearing at frame 0) is not modelled yet; it needs the same walk plus a consumer, and SWF-TOOLS `display_list.rs` adds stable instance ids and world bounds on top of it. `SwfTimeline::placements` has no stable id, so an editor selection would still key on depth and name. Everything here is C++ only: nothing was added to `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h` or `c_api_swf.h`, and exposing frames, the census or the report across the C boundary would be ABI 65.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_place.cpp` (the placement suite, because the model is the placement walk) gains six cases built from the C# owned fixtures' failure modes rather than from any game data. `SwfTimeline.CarriesDepthStateAcrossAReplacement` pins that a replacement inherits the moved matrix and the name, `SwfTimeline.MoveOnlyUpdateCarriesIntoALaterReplacement` pins that a move-only update changes what a later replacement inherits, `SwfTimeline.RemovalClearsTheInheritedDepthState` pins that a removal resets the depth to identity, and `SwfTimeline.RejectsMoveAtAnUndefinedDepthAndAClassOnlyPlacement` pins both refusals with the movie still readable at the container level. `SwfTimeline.CountsDefinitionsLabelsAndInspectionRows` builds one movie with a shape, a `DefineEditText`, a labelled sprite placed by name and a `SymbolClass`, and pins the census, the `Document class`, `Root frame labels`, `Totals`, the frame-label census, the nested `Art/Child` row with its world size, the `states:` line and the text field's rect and text from `inspect_swf`. The matrix fixtures use an 11-bit translate field with a negative Y, so a decoder that sign-extends the wrong way fails the position assertions rather than passing on an even translation.

Review follow-up on the timeline model (`nomad/gt-806-engine-parity`). The inspection report is now held to the engine's exact text, not to substring checks: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_place.cpp:SwfTimeline.CountsDefinitionsLabelsAndInspectionRows` compares the whole `inspect_swf` string for a movie with one shape, one edit field, one labelled sprite and one document class, and that fixture places the sprite (character 3) rather than the shape as the named root instance, with the shape under the tag code `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp` uses for the same payload. Two engine formatting rules had to be adopted for that equality to be meaningful. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:format_number` now rounds with `std::nearbyint(value * 10.0) / 10.0`, which is half-to-even like the C# `Math.Round(value, 1)`, instead of `std::round`'s half-away-from-zero; 0.25 px therefore prints `0.2` in both. The sign of zero is still dropped (`rounded == 0.0 ? 0.0 : rounded`): every value in the report is an integer twip count over 20 or a definition count, so a negative zero cannot arise from a real coordinate, and the C# formatter only prints `-0` because .NET preserves the sign of a computed negative zero. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:quote_text` now reproduces `System.Text.Json`'s default escaping: `\"` and `\`, the short `\b \t \n \f \r` forms, `\uXXXX` for the other control characters, for `+ < > & '` and for everything at or above 0x7F, with surrogate pairs above the BMP. An edit field holding `<p>&` therefore prints `"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026"` like the engine, not as raw markup. Text-field rects also use the row's composed transform (`:text_field_detail` takes the `SwfTransform`), so a scaled and translated instance reports the transformed rect, which `Radicle/tests/test_swf_place.cpp:SwfTimeline.AppliesTheRowTransformToATextFieldRect` pins at `(12, -2, 20 x 4)`.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:build_index` now names `DefineButton` 7, `DefineButton2` 34 and `DefineVideoStream` 60 by the leading UI16 of their payload, so a placed button or video prints `button #N` / `video #N` instead of `undefined #N`, matching the engine's `Kind` table; `SwfTimeline.NamesButtonAndVideoCharactersFromTheirLeadingId` pins both. A placement with no character is no longer a refusal: the engine records the depth with a null character, emits no row and continues, so `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:build_timeline` keeps the slot with character id 0 for the depth carry and skips the placement row, and `SwfTimeline.KeepsACharacterLessPlacementWithoutARow` pins the state and the missing row. The two decode failures read the same way: an update that cannot be applied leaves the display list alone and the movie stays readable. A truncated `RemoveObject`/`RemoveObject2` never reaches that branch, because the read layer already refuses the tag; `SwfTimeline.RejectsATruncatedRemovalPayload` pins that rejection and the resulting unreadable movie, and the timeline guard stays as a defensive no-op.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:apply_tag_plan` follows the same review. Insertions at one position are allowed and keep plan order: `PendingInsert` sorts by position descending and, at equal positions, by plan index descending, so the plan's first insertion ends up first; `SwfTagPlanResult::inserted_tag_indices` is now returned in plan order rather than sorted, which is the order a caller addressing the plan expects. A payload that decodes to `malformed_tag`, for a replacement or an insertion, now rejects the whole plan with the file untouched, instead of being installed and left half-decoded; `SwfTagPlan.RejectsAPlanWhosePayloadDoesNotDecode` pins both directions against the byte-identical file. There is no revision counter in the C ABI for a tag plan — the plan is C++ only, `c_api_swf.h` exposes no plan entry point — so the "rejected plan leaves bytes and revision unchanged" check stays at the byte level here.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:SwfTag::clear_decoded` now resets `imports`, which it previously left behind, so a replaced `ImportAssets`/`ImportAssets2` payload cannot leave a stale source movie in the tag. `Radicle/tests/test_swf_plan.cpp:SwfTagPlan.ReplacingATagClearsItsDecodedImports` replaces a valid tag 71 payload with one byte, then asserts the decoded view is gone and `inspect_swf` no longer prints an `Imports:` line.

`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` stayed 64 in this pass and no header changed, so `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` are untouched generator output; a fresh run of `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` over `Radicle/include` reproduces both files byte for byte, which is the only check this pass ran on them, because `AbiLayoutTests.EveryStructMatchesTheCLayout` needs a built library. The SWF block 58 to 64 recorded above stands exactly as it is: 58 for the art getters, 59 and 60 for the morph style getters, 61 for the shape line-fill getters, 62 for the shape record stream, 63 for the two morph record streams and 64 for the morph frame getters. Folding that block into a single number is a lane decision rather than one of these review fixes, so nothing was renumbered and no export moved. Both generated files sit far past the 750-line working limit (3591 and 1577 lines), because the generator owns them and they were not hand-edited; the hand-written files this pass changed stay under it: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp` 651, `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp` 631, `Radicle/tests/test_swf_place.cpp` 734 and `Radicle/tests/test_swf_plan.cpp` 241.

Strictness of the two new decoders was checked against real data without building Radicle: a read-only Python pass over `D:/FO4-NG-1.10.984/Data/Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` (SHA256 `dff6b54def5d664f8a08aee5c7929d6394dbdaf94cacb9f8eacfcaf024287213`) parsed the GNRL table, inflated each movie and applied the same field rules `decode_edit_text` and the import decoders use. It read 307 movies, 767 `DefineEditText` tags and 63 `ImportAssets`/`ImportAssets2` tags with zero failures, so both stay `malformed_tag`-strict rather than silently ignored. The scan is evidence, not a test: the C++ decoders themselves remain unrun in this pass.

Additional tests on `Radicle/tests/test_swf_place.cpp`: `SwfTimeline.FreshPlaceOnALiveDepthResetsTheInheritedState` (a fresh placement on a live depth drops the inherited matrix and name), `SwfTimeline.TruncatesTheReportAtTheRowLimit` (401 named placements stop at the 400-row cap and print the truncation note), `SwfTimeline.StopsSpriteNestingAtTheDepthLimit` (a five-deep sprite chain prints level four and not level five) and `SwfTimeline.StopsASelfReferencingSprite` (a sprite that places itself stops after the second row). `SwfTimeline.RoundsHalfToEvenLikeTheEngineReport` builds a 5 x 15 twip stage so both edges land on a .25/.75 tie and pins `Stage 0.2 x 0.8`. The two formatting rules above have their own cases: `SwfTimeline.EscapesHtmlTextLikeTheJsonEncoder` places an HTML edit field holding `<p>&'` and a non-ASCII character and pins the quoted `\u003Cp\u003E\u0026\u0027\u00E9` detail with its `html` flag, and `SwfTimeline.PrintsNegativeZeroAsZero` places a character at -1 twip and pins `at (0, 0)`, which is the deliberate drop of the sign of zero rather than the .NET `-0` form.

A8 is closed on `nomad/gt-806-display-list`: `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_display.hpp:SwfDisplayList` is the per-frame state an editor selects from and a renderer draws, built by `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:build_display_list`. It reads the operation stream from the tags directly rather than from `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:build_timeline`, because a frame state needs the ordered operations (place, move, remove, `ShowFrame`) and the timeline model settles on recorded rows and final frame states. `swf_display.cpp:collect_operations` splits one timeline into frames at every `ShowFrame` and refuses a trailing operation after the last one, `swf_display.cpp:replay` applies them into a depth map exactly like the engine's clip walk (a move with no character updates the live instance in place; a placement that carries a character replaces it and inherits the name, transform and clip depth when it is a move), and `swf_display.cpp:build_display_list` emits one `SwfDisplayFrame` per `ShowFrame` for the root and for every `DefineSprite`, the root first and the sprites in character order.

Sprite advance follows `ArtworkClip.Advance` in the engine, with the wrap made a property of the frame instead of history: an instance born at its timeline's frame `created` has child age `age - (cycle_start + created)`, the cycle starting at `age - age % frame_count`, so a child of a five-frame sprite placed at root frame 1 sits at its own frame 1 when the root is at frame 2, and every wrap clears because each frame is replayed from an empty map, exactly what the engine's `Items.Clear()` at frame 0 does. The engine's early return for a single-frame timeline is kept by leaving `cycle_start` at zero when a timeline has one frame or fewer, so a static parent never appears to restart its children. Two placements of one sprite at different frames therefore advance independently, which `SwfDisplay.AdvancesTwoInstancesOfOneSpriteIndependently` pins, and a loop is visible in `SwfDisplay.LoopsAChildTimelineWhoseLengthDiffersFromItsParent` where a two-frame child of a three-frame root shows its second frame only at root frame 1.

Identity is per creation, not per depth: `SwfFrameInstance::instance_id` (ABI field `instance_id`) comes from `swf_display.cpp:Expander::id_for` keyed by the parent instance key, the depth and the creation serial inside that timeline, so a move without a character keeps the id while a placement that carries a character, and a remove followed by a place, both start a new instance and restart its child at frame 0. That is what the engine does by constructing a new `ArtworkInstance` and `ArtworkClip` for every placement that names a character, so the class-only rule of `SwfTimeline.build_timeline` (a refusal) is relaxed here to the engine's skip, because the clip walk is what the editor mirrors. `SwfDisplay.KeepsAnInstanceIdAcrossAMoveAndRenewsItAfterARemove` and `SwfDisplay.RestartsAChildWhenAPlacementReplacesTheCharacterAtOneDepth` pin both halves; the second one fails on any implementation that carries the previous creation frame across a replacement, because the child would show its second frame where the engine shows its first.

World geometry is computed once per instance: `swf_display.cpp:Expander::expand` composes the local transform with the parent's world transform, takes registered shape bounds from `swf_display.cpp:build_display_list` and runs them through `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:transformed_bounds`, so a shape inside a scaled sprite reports the composed rectangle in points rather than its local one, and a sprite instance itself carries `has_bounds` false because its rectangle would be the union of its children, which the engine computes in `sprite_bounds.rs` and Radicle does not model yet. `SwfDisplay.ComposesWorldBoundsThroughNestedTransforms` pins the composition at a half-scale parent and a double-scale child, where a local-only computation reports (10, 5, 200 x 100) and the transform-less one (5, 2.5, 100 x 50).

Where the display list deliberately differs from the timeline model, it is recorded here rather than left implicit: class-only placements are skipped, not refused; a timeline's declared frame count is not cross-checked against its `ShowFrame` count, because the rows in `SwfTimeline` already accept that drift and the census pass must not fail on a movie whose header disagrees; the `SwfDisplayOptions` budget (250000 instances per frame state) and depth cap (64) replace the engine's conversion work counter and nesting clamp; and a sprite that places itself stops after one expansion, by the stack check in `swf_display.cpp:Expander::expand`, which `SwfDisplay.StopsAtASelfReferencingSprite` pins. `SwfDisplay.RejectsWorkPastTheInstanceBudget` pins the budget rejection, where the whole build returns `malformed` with the partial frames discarded.

The read-only C ABI is ABI 65: `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_frames_open` builds the list from a parsed `radicle_swf` into its own handle, and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:radicle_swf_frames_instance_at` fills `radicle_swf_frames_instance`, which carries the id, the depth, the character, the owning timeline and its frame, both transforms, the world bounds, the name and the instance path. The handle copies every string it hands back, so it may outlive `radicle_swf_destroy` (pinned by `CApiSwfFrames.OutlivesTheMovieItWasBuiltFrom`), an unplaceable movie maps to `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR` with the walk's message (`CApiSwfFrames.RejectsBadArgumentsAndUnplaceableMovies`), and `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` moved 64 to 65 with `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSixtyFive`. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` were regenerated by `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` for the three new structs and six exports; a managed `SwfFrames` wrapper is not written yet, so the editor's view can consume the raw native imports or wait for that wrapper in its own branch. Nothing here renumbers 58 to 64.

Nothing on this branch was built or run. The tests are `Radicle/tests/test_swf_display.cpp` (seven cases, each named for the regression above, built from synthetic movies whose fixtures are the same twip rectangles the placement suite uses) and `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_display.cpp` (three cases over the same nested movie). The archive census that proves these numbers against `docs/ui/local-artwork-counts.md` is the next pass, and the C# oracle (`ArtworkClip.Advance` and `Inspection.Report`) was read, not executed.

The archive reconciliation that `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:build_display_list` and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:census` were meant to prove was run as a read-only probe, not through the C++ code. `git/806-plan-scan/census.py` (scratch, outside `Radicle/`) re-derives the counting rules of `ArtInventory.cs:ArtInventory.Describe` rather than inventing its own: scope is `Interface/Components/**/*.swf` plus the eleven menu roots; a definition is a top-level tag whose code is in `IsDefinition` (2, 22, 32, 83, 46, 84, 20, 36, 39, 7, 11, 33, 34, 37, 60, 6, 21, 35, 90) keyed by its leading UI16 character id, with a zero or duplicate id treated as `ArtworkMovie` would treat it; shapes are 2/22/32/83, sprites 39, morphs 46/84, bitmaps 6/20/21/35/36/90 and text fields 37; sprite children stay inside the `DefineSprite` payload and are not definitions. It also checks the preconditions the engine's clip walk requires, that each root and sprite `ShowFrame` count matches its declaration.

Run with `python -I` against `D:/FO4-NG-1.10.984/Data/Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` (SHA256 `dff6b54def5d664f8a08aee5c7929d6394dbdaf94cacb9f8eacfcaf024287213`), the probe read 911 entries with 307 movies, 225 component movies and all eleven menu roots. `docs/ui/local-artwork-counts.md` describes a different install (SHA256 `296d115c22de80c41ddeee2c33027bf40ac788cfe99f37de294509e4656dd6ab`, 1,101 entries) and yet the per-menu census it publishes matches this probe in all 55 cells: SPECIAL 8/19/0/0/10, level-up 1,722/207/2/0/21, Pip-Boy shell 20/38/0/1/20, stats 75/98/0/0/13, inventory 105/140/0/0/25, data 25/39/0/0/15, map 173/106/0/1/4, radio 5/9/0/0/2, loading 5/7/6/0/3, fader 4/4/6/0/0 and map markers 101/55/0/0/3, totalling 2,243 shapes, 722 sprites, 14 morphs, 2 embedded bitmap definitions and 116 declared text fields. No per-movie divergence exists to list. The 225 component movies add 6,339 shapes and 484 sprites and contribute no morphs, bitmaps or text fields, which is why the documented totals are menu-only numbers. Zero of the 236 sources failed the structural preconditions, so every one of those counts comes from a movie whose frame declarations hold. The 767 top-level `DefineEditText` tags an earlier pass measured across all 307 movies do not contradict the documented 116 that `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:census` would report: 116 are the scoped menu roots' definitions, the 225 component movies carry none, and the remaining 651 sit in 46 unselected `Interface/*Menu.swf` roots (447) and 25 `Programs/*.swf` movies (204), outside the inventory's 225-plus-11 scope.

Three documented numbers outside the five counted categories do differ and are left untouched: the entry count (911 here against 1,101), Interface and Textures/Interface DDS candidates (132 against 134) and the `Interface/Exported` subset (120 against 116). The cause is the archive revision, not a counting rule: the two installs ship the same 225 component movies and the same eleven roots, and every published definition count matches, while the extra 190 entries and the DDS drift sit in content these categories never touch. What this establishes is that the documented census is reproducible from the oracle's definitions on a different archive revision. It does not prove the C++ census: `census()` and `build_display_list` were never executed in this pass, and rendering-dependent figures in the document (frames, omissions, unsupported sources) are outside a declaration probe entirely.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_edit.cpp` is the first write path over the decoded placement model, and it is deliberately narrow. `:encode_matrix` writes a MATRIX with the field widths the values need, `:placement_matrix_span` finds those bytes inside a `PlaceObject` 4, `PlaceObject2` 26 or `PlaceObject3` 70 body, and `:replace_placement_transform` splices a re-encoded MATRIX between the two bounds and copies every other byte through untouched. The parity target is SWF-TOOLS `crates/swftools-document/src/placement.rs:104 replace_transform` with `:416 encode_matrix`, and the rule that carries over is the field minimality: HasScale and HasRotate are set only for a value that is not identity, each pair is written at the bits it needs, and a translate of zero writes a zero bit count. That width rule is what makes an edit that changes nothing leave the file alone, so `:apply_instance_transforms` compares the authored MATRIX with the request and skips a placement that already matches instead of normalising its encoding; `SwfEditTransform.KeepsAnUnchangedTransformByteExact` pins the byte identity, and `SwfEditTransform.EncodesTheMinimumBitWidthTheValuesNeed` pins the widths against hand-computed bytes (`{0x0C,0xA5,0x80}` for a 20/-20 twip translate) because a fixed-width encoder would pass every round trip and still churn every edited file.

Addressing an instance needed a transform provenance the display list did not carry, so `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_display.hpp:SwfInstancePlacement` adds it and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:replay` records two tag indices per instance: the placement that created the character and, separately, the placement that last authored a MATRIX. The editable one is the second, which is the SWF-TOOLS rule (`display_list.rs:117` resolves an edit to `transform_placement_index`, not to the creating placement), and a lifetime that never authored a MATRIX has no editable placement at all: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_edit.cpp:apply_instance_transforms` refuses it with `instance has no editable explicit matrix`, matching `batch.rs:122`, so a fresh `PlaceObject2` that carries no MATRIX cannot be edited into one by writing a transform the authored stream never had. Only the root traversal records placements, because a sprite's standalone display timeline describes a definition rather than a frame state; `build_display_list` hands the expander a null sink for those passes so a shadow list cannot address a placement that is not visible, and `SwfDisplayOptions::record_placements` keeps the whole list opt-in so `radicle_swf_frames_open`, which copies the display list by value, does not pay a path string per instance per frame for data only the editor reads.

A sprite child lives inside a `DefineSprite` body that the container keeps whole, so `Radicle/src/swf/swf_edit.cpp:rebuild_sprite_payload` re-emits the sprite id, the frame count and the child stream from `SwfTag::children`, replacing only the edited child's payload and keeping each child's header form. Before it substitutes anything it rebuilds the body with no replacements and requires that to equal the original payload, so a body the child list does not fully explain, such as bytes after the terminal `End` or a sprite whose children were cut at the depth limit, is refused rather than silently shortened. Two instance ids that resolve to one authored placement are deduplicated and refused when they disagree (`conflicting transforms target the same shared authored placement`), so a sprite child visible at two depths is one write and not last-writer-wins. The edit reaches the file only through `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:apply_tag_plan`, so a refusal leaves every tag body and the whole tag count untouched, which `SwfEditTransform.EditsTwoInstancesOfOneSharedPlacementInOnePlan` checks with its conflicting-request refusal and its written-bytes reparse; `:RewritesASpriteChildPlacementInsideItsDefineSprite` covers only the success path.

`Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:radicle_swf_detail::rebuild_views` is new on the same pass because the C handle caches `tag_view` records that hold `const SwfTag*` into `file.tags` (`:flatten_tags`), plus the summary, the symbol, export and frame-label lists, the ABC views and the morph-frame cache. Opening used to be the only builder of those views; a mutation would reallocate `file.tags` and leave every pointer `radicle_swf_tag_payload` hands out dangling. The construction now lives in one function with one caller, `open_from_bytes`, and the comment on it says a mutation has to call it before any getter runs, so the write entry point added later has a single place to refresh from instead of a second copy of the flattening. Nothing on the C boundary moved: `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` stayed 65, `c_api_swf.h` is untouched, and `swf_edit.hpp` is C++ only.

The completed stack through `nomad/gt-806-swf-frame-address` was compiled and run locally with a hand-rolled MSVC 14.44 build at `/std:c++latest /W4`, not through the project's CMake build, and that is local evidence rather than CI: this checkout has no system zlib and no fetched googletest, so the run used a cached `garden_zlib` source and googletest 1.17, compiled the thirteen `Radicle/src/swf` translation units warning-free and linked the four SWF test translation units. The suite ran 41 cases with 40 passing at that tip; the single failure was `SwfDepthReassign.RejectsASourceOrDestinationInsideAMaskRange`, not a case in this suite. The suite is `Radicle/tests/test_swf_edit.cpp` (`SwfEditTransform`, thirteen cases): the encoder's widths, a rewrite that leaves every other payload byte of the placement and every other tag identical, the byte-identical no-op, the refusal of a lifetime with no authored MATRIX, a shared placement edited once and refused when two requests disagree, a sprite child rewritten inside its `DefineSprite` with its name and clip depth intact, and a fresh matrix surviving `write_swf` and a reparse. Review added four more because the first pass left the interesting branches unexercised: a matrix re-authored by a later `Move` is edited in that `Move` and leaves the creating placement's bytes and name alone (`:transform_tag_index` is what makes that possible, and nothing tested it), a `PlaceObject` v1 body with no flag byte and a trailing CXFORM, a `PlaceObject3` body whose blend mode sits after the name, and a `DefineSprite` body with bytes after its `End` tag that must be refused instead of trimmed. The first case now also pins hand-computed bytes for a rotate plus a negative scale and refuses a 2^15 scale; `SwfEditTransform.RejectsATransformThatNeedsMoreThanTheMatrixFields` covers the validation pass encoding every request before any proof, so a value that quantizes into int32 but needs 32 signed bits is refused with `the transform does not fit the MATRIX fields` instead of failing later as a missing MATRIX; and `:SeparatesAnEmptyFrameFromAnOutOfRangeFrame` pins the two distinct refusals `apply_instance_transforms` now gives for an out-of-range root frame and a frame with no instances. The oracle on the other side was read, not run: SWF-TOOLS `placement.rs`, `batch.rs`, `document.rs` and `roundtrip.rs` state the same contracts, and Radicle now implements those rules rather than porting the Rust tests, so a passing suite here is not evidence that the Rust suite would pass there.
`Radicle/src/swf/swf_depth.cpp` is the depth write path, and it is its own translation unit because `Radicle/src/swf/swf_edit.cpp` was 434 lines when the scan landed and the 750-line gate applies to it. `:replace_placement_depth` splices the UI16 depth of a `PlaceObject` v1 (offset two), v2 (one), v3 (two), `RemoveObject` (two) or `RemoveObject2` (zero) and copies every other byte, so a rewritten tag differs from the original in exactly those two bytes. `:reassign_instance_depth` resolves the instance id through `build_instance_edit_targets`, takes the source depth and the creating placement from `SwfInstanceEditTarget::create_tag_index`, and then re-implements SWF-TOOLS `crates/swftools-document/src/depth_reorder.rs:reassign_root_instance_depth` rule for rule: `:find_lifetime`, `:validate_lifetime_state`, the mask pass, the destination control-tag pass and `:destination_occupied_during_lifetime`.

The lifetime is the interval in which the object owns its depth, not the interval in which it is visible. The scan replays placements and removals over the root tag stream and collects the creating placement, every later `Move` without a character at the source depth (a matrix, colour, ratio or name change only), and the tag that ends the lifetime: a fresh placement with a character or an effective removal (a `Move` that takes a character is refused up front). An effective removal is a `RemoveObject2`, or a `RemoveObject` whose character matches the live one. The removal is rewritten too, so an interval that ends with one keeps ending where it did; the other two terminators need a synthesized `RemoveObject2(destination)` immediately before them, because the replacement tag creates a different object at the source depth and the moved object would otherwise stay live at the destination forever. A lifetime that begins with a `Move` carrying a character, or whose creating placement silently replaces a live object at the source depth, is refused: the first would have to synthesize a removal for the object it is editing and the second for the object it is displacing.

The carry rule of the reference is not reachable in this rewrite, and the scan refuses its only entering case: a `Move` that takes a character at the source depth cannot replay after the rewrite, because the moved object no longer lives at that depth and the display replay rejects a `Move` whose depth is not live. Committing it would write a movie the read side calls malformed, so `:scan_lifetime` refuses it before any body is rewritten instead of refusing it later with a message about the destination proof. The rest of the reference's guard is kept and made independent of the terminator kind: a `PlaceObject` v1 or v3 anywhere in the lifetime, or clip actions on a lifetime tag or on the replacement, is still refused rather than rewritten, because the decoder keeps that state as opaque bytes, and `:validate_lifetime_state` checks it for every lifetime. A fresh placement with a character inherits nothing from the object it replaces, so a lifetime ending in one needs no restating; that is the accept path the synthesized-removal cases cover.

Three read-side assumptions differ from the reference, and the reference won each time. First, tag five: the reference only removes an object whose character matches, while `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:replay` erases the depth regardless, so the scan refuses a tag-five removal that names another character at the source depth while the object is live instead of ignoring the divergence. `:reassign_instance_depth` proves the result on a copy of the header and the tags before touching the movie: the moved instance must still resolve at the destination depth on the requested frame, which the preview checks by looking up the instance the creating tag produced and requiring its frame row to carry the destination depth, not merely the same tag index. When the read side and the scan disagree about whether the object is still alive, that proof fails and the edit is refused with `the reassigned object did not resolve at the destination depth after the rewrite`. Second, masks: `SwfFrameInstance` carries no `masked_by_depth`, so the frame-state test is replaced by the authored mask pass, which rejects a source or destination inside any authored clip range and any lifetime placement that carries a clip depth; that is at least as strict as the reference's two checks. Third, class-only placements: `collect_operations` skips them, so the display list never shows one, while the reference's event stream includes them as a placement; the scan keeps the reference's event so a lifetime that ends at one is not rewritten past it, and the same post-edit proof covers the case where the read side would disagree. A destination that is already live while the object is live is refused rather than swapped, matching the reference, and every refusal path runs before the plan is applied, so the tag count and every payload stay untouched.

`SwfInstanceEditTarget` and `SwfInstancePlacement` gain `create_tag_index` on this branch: piece 1 dropped it because nothing read it, and the lifetime scan needs the creating tag rather than the transform tag, which can be a later `Move`. `SwfDisplayOptions::record_placements` still gates the whole provenance list, so no read-only caller pays for the field, and it costs one `size_t` on structs the C boundary never exposes.

The completed stack was compiled and run locally with the hand-rolled MSVC 14.44 build described on the placement-transform note (`/std:c++latest /W4`, thirteen `Radicle/src/swf` translation units and the four SWF test translation units, googletest 1.17 and a cached zlib); that is local evidence, not CI, and the changes in this round are unbuilt. The suite is `Radicle/tests/test_swf_depth.cpp` (`SwfDepthReassign`, nine cases, written before the implementation), in its own translation unit with its own copies of the placement builders because `Radicle/tests/test_swf_edit.cpp` is 526 lines and the 750-line gate applies to test translation units too; `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt` registers it. Eight cases pin the rules: a lifetime renamed across its creation, its matrix-only move and its removal with the matrix intact; a synthesized removal before a fresh placement; the refused `Move` terminator that takes a character; the refused v1, v3 and clip-action lifetimes; the refused mask range on either end; the refused tag-five removal of another character at the source depth; the refused control tag; and the refused occupied destination, each with the written bytes compared against the source so a refusal is proven byte-identical. The ninth is the seeded sweep analogous to `crates/swftools-document/tests/fuzz_reassign.rs`: twenty-four seeded movies of placements, moves, removals and masks, every named root instance resolved at its first frame and moved to every depth from one to thirteen, with the oracle being that every frame of the result equals the original frame with one depth relabelled (depth, name, character and transform, sorted) and that the tag count grew by zero or one. It counts successes, refusals and synthesized removals and requires all three to be non-zero.

Branch 2 does not need a frame-targeted builder: the lifetime scan reads tags, and the frames it touches come from the existing whole-movie `build_display_list`. Branch 3 does: the neutrality comparison has to observe the edited frame before and after the rewrite, and paying for every root frame twice per edit is the cost the piece-1 review flagged. That builder belongs to branch 3, not here.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_keyframe.cpp` is the transform keyframe path, the third write operation over the placement model, and it follows SWF-TOOLS `docs/code-notes/transform-keyframe-milestone.md` and `crates/swftools-document/src/keyframe.rs:insert_root_instance_transform_keyframe_inner`. `:insert_instance_transform_keyframe` has the neutral and requested-transform overloads of the milestone's two entry points. Both insert one `PlaceObject2` immediately before the `ShowFrame` that completes the frame, with flags `0x05` (`Move|HasMatrix`), the object's depth and a MATRIX re-encoded from the current effective transform; no character, name, class, clip depth, ratio, colour transform, filter list, blend mode or clip actions. That shape is the whole contract: on a live depth, a Move without `HasCharacter` replaces only the fields it authors, so every other authored field keeps coming from the tag that authored it, and the new tag becomes the object's transform source from that frame forward. `:show_frame_index` and `:tag_frame` are the two index facts the path needs: which tag completes a frame, and which frame a tag was authored on.

The neutrality comparator is why this branch also adds the frame-targeted builder. `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_edit.hpp:SwfAuthoredFrameObject` and `:build_authored_frame` reconstruct one root frame's authored state directly from the tag stream: depth, character, instance name, class name, ratio, clip depth, the innermost live mask depth that covers the object, filter count, authored blend mode, the authored MATRIX and the two tag indices that created and last transform-authored it. The display list cannot serve as the comparator because it drops exactly the fields the milestone names: `SwfFrameInstance` has no filter count, no blend presence, no class name, no ratio and no mask membership, and it expands every sprite and every frame. `:build_authored_frame` walks only up to the frame's `ShowFrame`, merges a placement's fields only where the tag authors them, skips a class-only placement the way `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:collect_operations` does, and stamps mask membership after the frame's tags are applied. That makes the frame-targeted builder part of this branch rather than a later one: the insertion path needs it twice per edit.

The display-side single-frame builder stays out, and this is what pays for it. Resolving an instance id still costs one full `Radicle/src/swf/swf_edit.cpp:build_instance_edit_targets` call, exactly as the transform and depth branches pay it, and the keyframe path deliberately pays a second full `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:build_display_list` on the post-edit copy as its end-to-end proof. Truncating either build to one frame would make `build_instance_edit_targets` accept a movie whose later frames do not display, which would weaken the refusal contract the transform and depth edits already rely on, and the end-to-end proof re-pays that cost on every insertion anyway, so the saving would be nil. What the comparator pays instead is two `:build_authored_frame` walks of the tags up to the frame, with no sprite expansion, no bounds and no id assignment.

The guards run in the milestone's order and all of them fire before the file is touched. A version below three is refused because the inserted tag is a `PlaceObject2`; a sprite child is refused because a sprite definition is shared by every use; the instance must resolve on the frame; a frame that already owns the object's transform source is refused, which is also what makes a repeated insertion and an insertion of the value already in force leave the file byte-identical; and the requested transform must fit the MATRIX fields. The insertion then runs on a copy of the header and tags, and three things are proven on that copy before the real plan is applied. The authored frame is rebuilt and compared field by field against the pre-edit frame: for the neutral overload the effective transform must match too, and for the requested overload the inserted tag must have established an explicit MATRIX source. The whole movie is rebuilt through `build_display_list`, so an insertion the read side cannot reproduce end to end is refused rather than written, and the selected instance must still resolve on its frame with the authored transform the comparator just accepted. Only then are the same tags replaced on the real file, so every refusal leaves the tag count and every payload untouched.

One approximation is worth recording: a `PlaceObject3` that authors a filter list is merged by its filter count only when the count is non-zero, because a zero-length filter list is indistinguishable from an absent one in `SwfPlacement`. The comparator never observes the difference, because the tag this branch inserts carries no filter list at all, but a later branch that authors filters would need the presence bit to be modelled.

The completed stack was compiled and run locally with the hand-rolled MSVC 14.44 build described on the placement-transform note (`/std:c++latest /W4`, thirteen `Radicle/src/swf` translation units and the four SWF test translation units, googletest 1.17 and a cached zlib); that is local evidence, not CI, and the changes in this round are unbuilt. The suite is `Radicle/tests/test_swf_keyframe.cpp` (`SwfKeyframe`, nineteen cases, written before the implementation, with seven added in review round one) in its own translation unit with its own builders, because `Radicle/tests/test_swf_edit.cpp` and `Radicle/tests/test_swf_depth.cpp` are 581 and 594 lines and the 750-line gate applies to test translation units too; `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt` registers it. Eighteen cases pin the contract: a neutral insertion on an inherited transform with the exact tag shape, every tag outside the insertion point byte-identical, every rendered frame unchanged and the object still resolving after a write and reparse; identity materialisation for an object that authored no MATRIX; the inserted tag becoming the transform source, proven by a subsequent transform edit that changes the keyframe's frame and later frames but never the frame before it; a second insertion and an insertion on a frame that already authored the matrix both refused with the file byte-identical; a nested sprite and a pre-SWF3 movie refused; the requested-transform overload writing frame N forward while a later authored MATRIX regains ownership; a same-frame name Move surviving a neutral insertion; a ratio and a clip depth preserved on the target frame; a `PlaceObject3` filter list and blend mode preserved; mask membership preserved; the refused NaN and over-31-bit transforms; the refused out-of-range frame and unknown instance id; and an insertion that lands after a `DoAction` tag rather than before it. The nineteenth is the corpus sweep: four movies, every root instance on every frame it resolves, where a successful insertion must leave every rendered frame equal before and after and after a write and reparse, and a refused one must leave the movie byte-identical, with successes and refusals both required. The sibling suites in SWF-TOOLS (`transform_keyframe_identity.rs`, `transform_keyframe_properties.rs`, `transform_keyframe_safety.rs`) were read, not run, and the structural-identity rule they pin does not apply here: Radicle instance ids are depth and serial keys, and a matrix-only Move creates no instance and shifts no serial, so an id that resolved before the insertion still resolves after it. The post-insertion proofs are guards rather than coverage: no fixture reaches `the transform keyframe removed the selected object`, `the transform keyframe did not establish an explicit matrix source`, `the transform keyframe would change non-transform authored state`, `the transform keyframe would change the authored frame render`, `the display does not reproduce the authored transform after the insertion`, `the movie is not renderable after the keyframe insertion` or `the tag plan was refused`, because an inserted matrix-only Move cannot remove the object, always authors a MATRIX, carries no other authored field and re-encodes the very transform it compares. `SwfKeyframe.RefusesWhenTheReadSideCannotReproduceTheMovie` stops earlier, at the pre-insertion target resolution, so the post-insertion display proof is unexercised too.

The write side is ABI 66 and it is four verbs on the handle the read side already had. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_tag_plan` carries replacements and insertions; `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_apply_plan` applies one, `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_revision` reports the counter and `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_write_bytes` serializes the handle. A plan index is the flat index `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_tag_at` reports, which is what a caller already holds, but `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_edit.cpp:top_level_position` maps it to the root stream and refuses any index inside a `DefineSprite`, because `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:apply_tag_plan` inserts into `file.tags` only and a mapped child index would silently insert beside the sprite instead of inside it; a sprite body is edited by replacing its `DefineSprite` tag, which is also how `Radicle/src/swf/swf_edit.cpp:rebuild_sprite_payload` already works. The plan/result structs mirror `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTagPlan`, except that the inserted tag indices `SwfTagPlanResult` collects are not carried across the boundary: the C result is caller-owned and allocation-free, plan order fixes where each inserted tag lands, and an editor can address them through `radicle_swf_tag_at` after the call, so the list would be a second copy of a fact the caller already wrote. The semantic exports named in the ledger (`set_instance_transform`, `reassign_depth`, `insert_keyframe`) stay out, each needing its own struct and bump above 66 when the editor asks for it.

"Does not claim a change" is a fact the engine had to report rather than one the C layer could infer, so `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTagPlanResult` gains `changed`, set by `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:apply_tag_plan` from the same byte comparison it already made to skip a no-op plan, and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_edit.cpp:apply` bumps the revision only when it is true. Revision is a `uint64_t` that saturates rather than wraps, matching `document.rs:361 revision`'s `u64` and its `saturating_add(1)`, and `radicle_swf_plan_result` carries it so the caller does not have to read the handle twice. The apply path runs the plan on a copy of the file, builds the new view set from that copy, and only then moves the file and the views into the handle, so a refusal, a bad allocation during the view build, or a plan the engine rejected all leave the tag list, the cached views and the revision exactly as they were; the price is one copy of `SwfFile` per accepted plan, which `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:apply_tag_plan` already pays once for its tag vector. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:write_swf` needed no change for the byte-exact no-op save: it already re-emits the original length field, body and compressed body when the rebuilt body equals `source_body`, so `radicle_swf_write_bytes` on an unedited handle returns the bytes the movie was opened from. Two header fields are not refreshed by a plan: `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfFile::header` keeps its open-time `frame_count` and `file_length` after an insertion, so `radicle_swf_info::declared_length_matches` stays the open-time fact, a save writes the body's true length, and the written frame count is the stale declared one; a caller that inserts a `ShowFrame` has to patch the header itself, and `radicle_swf_get_info` keeps reporting the old count.

The cached views now have a build step and an install step, which is the carry-over from the piece-1 review. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_internal.hpp:build_views` fills a `swf_views` that no handle owns, `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:install_views` moves each vector into the handle and drops the morph-frame cache, and `rebuild_views` is the two calls, so opening and editing share one builder and a throw during the build can no longer leave a handle with half its views cleared and half rebuilt. That failure mode was real before the split: `rebuild_views` used to clear every cached vector first, so any exception in `flatten_tags`, `build_abc_views` or `summarize` left the getters reading empty lists over a live file. The install has to move rather than copy, because every `tag_view` holds a `const SwfTag*` into `file.tags` and a copy would point at temporaries.

The second carry-over is the frame list. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:radicle_swf_frames` now holds the movie's `revision_state` and the revision it was built at, `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:stale` compares them, and every accessor refuses with "this frame list was built before the movie was edited; reopen it" once an accepted plan has moved the handle on. The state is shared rather than read through a back-pointer because the handle may outlive the movie (`CApiSwfFrames.OutlivesTheMovieItWasBuiltFrom`), so `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:radicle_swf_destroy` only deletes the handle and the frame list's shared pointer keeps the revision state alive: a stale list keeps refusing after the movie is destroyed, which `CApiSwfEdit.RejectsAFrameListBuiltBeforeAnEdit` pins, and a list built before a no-op plan stays readable because the revision did not move.

ABI 66 is the next free number and 58 to 65 are untouched: 65 stays the read-only display list, and `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION`, `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSixtySix`, `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` all move together. Both generated files were produced scratch-first: a run of `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` over `git show HEAD:Radicle/include` reproduced the committed pair byte for byte before the header changed, the post-change run differed only by the four new structs, three exports and the version constant, and a second run over the edited header reproduced the installed pair byte for byte. The generated pair is 3,690 and 1,621 lines and stays under the generator the way the 750-line gate expects; the hand-written files on this branch are `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_edit.cpp` at 163, `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp` at 661, `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp` at 171, `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_internal.hpp` at 90 and `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_edit.cpp` at 373.

Nothing on this branch was compiled or run, so all six cases in `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_edit.cpp` (`CApiSwfEdit`, written before the implementation) are unrun, and the line counts above are file length rather than a measurement of anything. The cases follow the ledger's five plus the frame-list carry-over: `BumpsRevisionOnlyForAChangedPlan` pins that an identical replacement and an empty plan both leave the revision at 0 while two real replacements take it to 2; `AppliesAReplacementPlanAndSavesTheBytes` reopens the written bytes and finds the new frame-label name at the same tag index, which is what a stale or misplaced view rebuild would fail; `RejectsAPlanAtomicallyAndKeepsRevisionAndBytes` drives an out-of-range index, the terminal `End`, a duplicate target, a payload that does not decode and both sprite-child forms, and holds the written bytes equal to the opened bytes after every refusal; `RebuildsEveryCachedViewAfterAnInsertion` inserts a frame label, then reads the tag list, the summary count, the label list, the inserted payload and the shape decoded from index 0, which is the regression `radicle_swf_detail::rebuild_views` exists for; `SavesAnUneditedHandleByteExactly` opens a compressed movie and holds the output byte-identical before and after a no-op plan; and `RejectsAFrameListBuiltBeforeAnEdit` keeps a list readable across a no-op plan, refuses it across a real one and opens a fresh list after it. The SWF-TOOLS oracle was read, not run: `document.rs:361 revision`, `:402 apply_tag_plan` and `:532 save_noop` state the same contracts, and the C layer implements those rules rather than porting the Rust tests.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:Expander::expand (#806 frame addressing)

The display list carried the ids an editor selects but not the tags it must rewrite, so a frame row and an edit target could only be joined by re-deriving the address outside Radicle. `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_display.hpp:SwfFrameInstance` now carries `create_tag_index` and `transform_tag_index`, copied off the `LocalInstance` the replay already holds: no second walk, no path string and no id is paid for a row that used to drop them on the floor. `SwfDisplayOptions::record_placements` still gates `SwfDisplayList::placements`, which is the per-frame list with the owning sprite and the timeline frame, because that is the part that costs a string per instance per frame; the two indices cost two scalars on a struct the expansion was already building.

The index space is the placement's own, not a movie-wide one. A root row addresses a top-level tag, and a row expanded out of a `DefineSprite` addresses a child of that sprite's payload, exactly the rule `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_display.hpp:SwfInstancePlacement` already states for `create_tag_index` and `transform_tag_index`. This is the failure the fields prevent: reading a sprite row's index out of `SwfFile::tags` names an unrelated tag, and in the fixture the first sprite child and the shape definition both sit at index zero, so a caller that treats a child index as top level rewrites a shape. The nested row is also the reason the index exists on the row rather than only in the placement list, since `Radicle/src/swf/swf_edit.cpp:build_instance_edit_targets` rebuilds one root frame per call and a viewer would otherwise have to pay for it before it could address anything. The C write path does not share this index space: `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_apply_plan` takes the flat top-level tag index `radicle_swf_tag_at` reports and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_edit.cpp:top_level_position` refuses a sprite child index, so a caller must map a frame row's root-position or child-local index to the flat one before handing it to a plan verb.

`transform_tag_index` is absent rather than zero when the instance's path never authored a MATRIX, which mirrors `SwfInstancePlacement::has_authored_matrix` and `:transform_tag_index` on the list, and it is the second index that is editable: a `Move` that rewrites a transform takes ownership of it, so `create_tag_index` and `transform_tag_index` part company after any matrix-only move. Following SWF-TOOLS `display_list.rs:117`, an edit resolves to the transform source and never to the creating placement. An instance with no matrix source has no editable address at all, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_edit.cpp:apply_instance_transforms` refuses it with `instance has no editable explicit matrix`, so the empty optional and the refusal agree instead of one of them inventing tag zero.

`operator==` is now written out and deliberately excludes both fields. `Radicle/tests/test_swf_keyframe.cpp` proves render neutrality by comparing every root frame of a movie before and after an insertion, and an insertion shifts every later tag index, so an equality that included the addresses would fail a test about rendering for a reason that is not about rendering. What the operator means is "the same displayed frame", which is what every caller of it already wanted, and the comment on the operator says so.

Everything here stays inside C++. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:radicle_swf_frames_instance_at` copies field by field, so no struct grew across the boundary and `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` stayed at 66; a managed caller still needs an export before it can address a placement, which is the same rule the semantic edit exports follow.

Tests, written before the implementation, extend `Radicle/tests/test_swf_display.cpp` rather than opening a translation unit for two fields (`SwfDisplay`, nine cases now). `AddressesANestedSpriteRowWithItsOwnSpriteLocalPlacement` pins that a root row names the top-level placement that created it and a sprite row names a child of the defining `DefineSprite`, with the same slot read out of the top-level stream resolving to a different tag, which is the corruption the sprite-local rule prevents. `LeavesTheTransformIndexEmptyUntilAPlacementAuthorsAMatrix` pins the empty optional on a placement that inherits its matrix, the `Move` that then takes ownership, and `create_tag_index` staying on the creating tag while the instance id survives the move.

This branch was compiled and run, though not through the project's CMake build: this checkout has no system zlib and no fetched googletest, so configuring `fo4_tests` would mean plumbing both by hand anyway. The check is instead a hand-rolled MSVC 14.44 (Visual Studio 2022 Community, `/std:c++latest /W4`) build of the thirteen `Radicle/src/swf` translation units, zlib from a cached `garden_zlib` source, googletest 1.17, and the four SWF test translation units, linked into one binary. All thirteen sources compile warning-free at `/W4`. At the first commit the four suites showed 41 cases with 39 passing, and both failures reproduced identically on a pristine extract of the parent commit `1c76a1170` built the same way, so neither was introduced here. `SwfDisplay.AdvancesTwoInstancesOfOneSpriteIndependently` was a defect in the case itself, as the second commit records, and its fix leaves the display suite green; `SwfDepthReassign.RejectsASourceOrDestinationInsideAMaskRange` belonged to the depth branch and is fixed in review round one, so this note no longer calls either one outstanding. The combined stack has not been rebuilt since those fixes, so its 41 of 41 is not a measured result. What the run does prove is the equality decision: all twelve `SwfKeyframe` cases, including `SweepsEveryRootInstanceAndFrameForRenderNeutrality` and the two that compare `root_display_frames` across an insertion, pass with the address fields outside `operator==`, and the two new `SwfDisplay` cases pass with them populated.

## Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_census.hpp:census_movie (#807 R1 API census)

The census is the R1 deliverable: the list of names every `Programs/*.swf` movie uses but does not define, which is the builtin surface #807 R2-R7 scopes to. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_census.cpp:census_movie` walks the movie's top-level ABC blocks through `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:abc_blocks`, parses each with `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc.hpp:AbcFile::parse`, and collects four kinds of reference: an instance's super class and interfaces, every method signature's return and parameter types, every `Slot`/`Const` trait's type (and its `Utf8` value), and every multiname or string operand `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code` reports in every body. A block Radicle cannot parse is counted in `abc_blocks` but not read, which is the same split `radicle_swf_abc_info.parsed` already reports.
Two kinds of name are dropped rather than binned because they are not names: an unqualified dynamic multiname, whose rendered form is `*`, and a qualified dynamic one, `pkg::*`; neither can name a builtin surface entry, and before this rule the manifest carried one `member * 3673` row that no runtime could act on. A multiname whose namespace set carries any non-package namespace is skipped whole, a set with several public packages bins under the first in file order, and an `RTQName` renders its bare name because its namespace is only known at run time. Three reference sites are deliberately outside the walk and are worth naming because they are the likeliest disagreement point with another reader: exception catch and variable types, method default-value options, and metadata strings; a body `decode_code` refuses is skipped while its block still counts in `abc_parsed`, so a decode failure cannot silently change a parsed count.

A reference is binned from two facts, and both are load-bearing. The namespace decides the family: only a namespace of kind `0x16` (`AbcNamespaceKind::Package`) is a public name, so a private, protected, package-internal or explicit namespace is skipped outright, and `flash.*`/`scaleform.*` packages become `flash-class`, `flash-member`, `scaleform-class` or `scaleform-member`; `__AS3__.vec` is a `builtin` because `Vector.<T>` is a builtin type carried by a package namespace; any other package is a name the movie's own source declared, so it is skipped. The opcode position decides class from member: `getsuper`, `setsuper`, `callsuper`, `callproperty`, `constructprop`, `callproplex`, `callsupervoid`, `callpropvoid`, `getdescendants`, `setproperty`, `getproperty`, `initproperty` and `deleteproperty` carry a property or method name, `findpropstrict`, `findproperty` and `finddef` carry a scope lookup, and every other multiname operand (`getlex`, `coerce`, `astype`, `istype`) carries a class or type. An unqualified name (no public package) is a `builtin` in a type position, `member` in a property position and `scope` in a lookup position, after the declared-name filter described next; a `TypeName` keeps its rendered parameters but is classified by its base.

Ordering and filtering are what make the manifest reviewable and the test meaningful. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_census.cpp:declared_class_names` collects every instance name across all of a movie's blocks and `:declared_trait_names` every trait name, rendered and bare, and a reference whose base class is declared, or whose unqualified name is declared, is dropped: the movies compile their own `scaleform.clik.*` and `scaleform.gfx.*` AS3, so a `scaleform` class that a movie defines is not engine surface, while a `flash.*` class is never defined and always survives. No `scaleform` row survives in the committed manifest at all: every movie that references `scaleform.clik.*` or `scaleform.gfx.*` also carries those classes' ABC blocks, so the runtime has to execute that bundled ActionScript instead of the engine providing it, and the external surface the census pins is `flash.*` plus the top-level builtins. Rows are sorted by `census_kind_name` and then by the raw byte order of the name, so the text is stable across platforms; `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_census.hpp:census_text` writes the header, one block per movie, and the loader graph as `load` rows from string operands and `Utf8` trait values whose suffix is `.swf` or `.xml`. `CensusLoad` is the loader graph the issue asks for: the movie section is the loader and the row is the target URL exactly as the movie spells it.

The manifest is `Radicle/testdata/swf/program_census.txt` and `Radicle/tests/test_swf_census_real.cpp` is its check. On the data runner it opens `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` through `Radicle/src/archive/ba2.cpp`, censuses every entry whose path is under `Programs\` and ends `.swf`, and compares the text byte for byte with the committed manifest after rewriting only the manifest's `# game_build` line to the detected build, which is a strict comparison on both OG 1.10.163.0 and NG 1.10.984.0 because the two data folders were read here and produce identical rows; on any other build it checks the build-independent invariants (every Programs ABC block parses, all seven holotape programs are present, every movie with bytecode censuses at least one name) and records both builds instead of asserting rows it has never seen. The synthetic cases in `Radicle/tests/test_swf_census.cpp` pin the bins on `Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:build_abc` - `flash.external::ExternalInterface` as a class, `flash.external::call` as a member, `Object`/`click`/`handler`/`addEventListener`/`void` as builtins, `addEventListener` as an unqualified member - and prove that the declared names `Test`, `onClick`, `counter`, `Inner` and `helper` never reach a bin.

The committed manifest was produced from `D:/FO4-NG-1.10.984/Data/Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` (SHA256 `dff6b54def5d664f8a08aee5c7929d6394dbdaf94cacb9f8eacfcaf024287213`, 1.10.984.0) and the same census taken from the OG folder `D:/Games/FallenWorld/Stock Folder/Data/Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` (SHA256 `3119877c7fa4e2d018252102e02a959bd281f8d1b88e469a51f6a7f32c83dba7`, 1.10.163.0) differs only in that build line: 25 Programs movies, 598 ABC blocks all parsed, 2,770 distinct references and 15 loader edges; the seven programs carry 90 (AtomicCommand), 1 (GJ_Defrag), 219 (Grognak), 88 (PipFall), 96 (RedMenace), 1 (TurretHack) and 86 (ZetaInvaders) ABC blocks. This branch was not built locally, so the manifest was not produced by Radicle's own code: it came from a scratch independent python reader that mirrors `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp`, `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp` and the `AbcFile::multiname_at`/`namespace_at` rendering, validated by parsing all 598 blocks with zero trailing bytes and by re-extracting the opcode operand table from `opcodes.cpp` rather than retyping it. `SwfCensusReal` re-derives the same text through Radicle on the data runner, so a divergence between the two readers fails the real-data test instead of silently pinning a wrong manifest. Two limits are deliberate: `member` and `scope` rows are unresolved names (inherited members and globals with no static owner), which is why the issue's manifest is a census and not the final builtin list, and no shipped Programs block declares a `native` method, so the R1 surface is entirely names referenced from AS3 rather than native method declarations.

## Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/runtime.hpp:Runtime::link (#807 R2 AVM2 foundation)

R2 needs four things before an interpreter can run: a value model, the AS3 coercions, a namespace/multiname resolution model, and the class/trait/property object model the ABC blocks describe. This branch lands those and the ABC-to-runtime linker, so the interpreter's next step is opcode dispatch rather than data modelling. Nothing here runs a method yet; `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/runtime.hpp:Runtime::scripts` exposes the per-file script initializer entries the interpreter will execute and `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_runtime.cpp` pins the linked shape.

**Values and coercions.** `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/value.hpp:Value` is a `std::variant` over undefined, null, boolean, int, uint, number, string and object; kind() is derived from the active alternative so the two cannot disagree, and int32/uint32/number are one Number type for equality and relational comparison the way AVM2 treats them. `Radicle/src/avm2/coercion.cpp:to_int32`/`to_uint32` implement ToInt32/ToUint32 (NaN and infinity to zero, truncation then the 2^32 wrap), `:to_number` parses StringNumericLiteral (trim, empty to zero, signed Infinity, 0x hex, from_chars decimal, trailing characters to NaN), and `:to_string` follows ECMAScript number formatting: integral doubles below 1e21 print with no decimal point, NaN/+-Infinity print their names, and other doubles use the shortest round-trip form (`std::to_chars`). Two documented deviations from what the builtins will supply in R3: `:to_number` returns NaN for an object instead of invoking valueOf/toString, and `Radicle/src/avm2/coercion.cpp:to_primitive` derives an object's primitive from its kind (`Array` joins elements, `Error` prints "Name: message", a function prints "function name() {}"), so a script initializer that converts a user object to a number needs R3's Object.prototype methods first.

**Names.** `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/name.hpp:Namespace` keeps the ABC namespace kind and text; only Package is a public name, so a private or protected trait is reachable only through a multiname carrying that same namespace. `Multiname` carries the six shapes the ABC model can produce (QName, QNameSet, RTQName, RTQNameL/MultinameL and TypeName), `:key_matches` gives the property protocol its matching rule (local names must agree; one candidate namespace must equal the key's; a runtime namespace gives up the namespace check), and `Radicle/src/avm2/name.cpp:KeyHash` keys dynamic dictionaries by (namespace, local name) so a public and a private member of one class with the same text stay distinct.

**Objects.** `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/object.hpp:Object` is a property protocol rather than a class hierarchy of its own: own dynamic properties first, then the instance class trait chain from the most derived class, then the next prototype object, which is why a plain dynamic object reaches `Object.prototype` while a class instance resolves its traits without a prototype walk. `:Object::lookup` reports what it found (dynamic value, slot, method, accessor with its getter and setter) so the interpreter can run the accessor path itself; `:Object::read_value` and `:write_value` are the value-only fast path and refuse accessors, method writes and const slot writes, and `:Object::write_value` updates an inherited value property where it lives instead of shadowing it. Function objects bind one ABC method (`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/object.hpp:FunctionObject:body` resolves the body through `AbcFile::body_for`), array and error objects carry their kind-specific state, and a class object is the callable face the global scope exposes (statics; the class traits are linked later).

**Classes and traits.** `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/class.hpp:Trait` mirrors the ABC trait table with its resolved multiname: slot ids, declared type name, a resolved default value (Utf8/Int/UInt/Double/True/False/Null), method and dispatch indices, the function a method-like trait bound, and the class object a Class trait points at. `:Class` keeps instance and class traits, the resolved super and interface closure, `iinit`/`cinit`, `slot_count` (the highest slot id over the chain plus one, so one hierarchy agrees with every instance's slot array) and `:Class::apply_slot_defaults`, which fills a slot array base-class-first so a derived default wins. `:Class::resolve_instance_trait` walks derived to base and returns the override first, and `:Class::implements_interface` closes over the interface graph and the super chain.

**Linking ABC.** `Radicle/src/avm2/runtime.cpp:Runtime::link` is one pass over every registered `AbcFile`: `:build_class_shells` creates one Class per instance and rejects a name defined twice; `:resolve_hierarchy` resolves each super and interface by its multiname, and `:ensure_external_class` creates a placeholder class for a name the movie references but does not define (every `flash.*` superclass today), which is the R3 seam where the real builtin gets bound; `:build_prototypes` allocates each class object and prototype object and wires `prototype.__proto__` and `class.__proto__` to the superclass's; `:build_traits` resolves instance and class traits, binds method functions and Class traits to their class objects (a Function trait's ABC function index is stored in `AbcTrait::class_index`, which is why the link reads it there), and `:build_script_globals` registers package-level functions, classes and variables on `:Runtime::global_object` plus every class object by its namespace and name, and records the script initializer entries in file order. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/runtime.hpp:resolve_multiname` is the single place the ABC multiname shapes become runtime names, including TypeName parameters rendered for diagnostics. A failed link clears everything it built and marks the runtime failed so a half-linked runtime cannot be used.

**Known gaps carried into the interpreter step.** No opcode dispatch, no scope chain or activation objects, no exception regions, no function closures capturing a scope, no accessor invocation, no register/native functions, and no GC (objects are shared_ptr references; a mark-sweep collector is a later decision before the runtime holds frames across ticks). `Vector.<T>` renders but is not instantiated, and an external class has no traits until R3 binds it. The tests are `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_value.cpp` (kinds, boolean/number/string coercions, int32/uint32 wrap, strict and loose equality, the four relational operators, default object-to-string forms), `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_object.cpp` (slot reads/writes, const refusal, method and accessor lookup, dynamic properties, prototype lookup, namespace matching, slot counting) and `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_runtime.cpp` (multiname resolution, linking `abc_test_support.hpp:build_abc` with its external Object superclass and click interface, nested Class and Function traits, slot defaults, global class and script function registration, reuse refusal and failed-link cleanup). Nothing was built locally on this branch; CI is the evidence.

## R2 interpreter core: frame, scope chain, opcode dispatch (#807 R2)
