`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/interpreter.hpp:Interpreter` runs AVM2 method bodies against a linked `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/runtime.hpp:Runtime`. This is the R2 execution core, not the finished R2: opcode coverage is the census-driven set (every opcode the Programs corpus uses except `newcatch`, whose handler path needs catch-variable scoping), class static initializers are not run yet, closures capture scopes but not activation locals, and no native builtin is bound, so a script that calls one stops with `NotImplemented` naming the function. `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_interpreter.cpp` is the executable slice: straight-line arithmetic, a local/branch loop, string concatenation, object and array property reads, a `newfunction` call, a global scope write/read through `findpropstrict`/`setproperty`/`getlex`, `coerce` to int, the instruction budget, the `NotImplemented` report and a repeat run that must produce the same value.

**Frame and invocation.** `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/interpreter.hpp:Interpreter::invoke` builds one frame per call: the decoded instruction list plus its offset index (so a branch target resolves by binary search, and a target that is not an instruction boundary is refused), locals sized to the body's `local_count`, register 0 as `this`, arguments from register 1, an operand stack bounded by `InterpreterLimits::max_stack`, a scope vector and the clock-free instruction counter. Class methods get the owner class scope appended after the global scope, script functions and closures use the captured scope a `newfunction` instruction copies from its executing frame, and the interpreter refuses recursion past `max_call_depth` and execution past `max_instructions` with their own statuses rather than a generic failure. Every failure carries the opcode and code offset that was executing, which is what the corpus probe will use to report the first unimplemented instruction.

**Scopes and names.** `findpropstrict` searches the scope vector from the innermost object outward and creates a binding on the global object when nothing owns the name, `findproperty` searches without creating and pushes null on a miss, and `getlex` reads through the owning scope object. Property access goes through the object protocol from the previous branch: dynamic properties, then the class trait chain, then the prototype chain; a value property is a direct read, a method reads back as its function object, a getter is invoked with the receiver as `this`, and a missing name reads as undefined for now (the strict refusal policy and the `ReferenceError` distinction belong with R4's class semantics). `callproperty`, `callpropvoid` and `callproplex` resolve a method, a callable slot or a getter-then-call, and the `call`/`construct`/`constructsuper`/`constructprop`/`callsuper` family follows the AVM2 pop order (receiver below the function below the arguments for `call`; receiver then arguments for the property forms) with the class object, the owner superclass and the class `iinit` driving construction. `newclass` returns the class object the runtime already linked, `newfunction` creates a closure over the current scopes, and `newobject`/`newarray`/`applytype` build the dynamic object, array and a Vector stand-in the corpus initializers need.

**Values and conversions.** The arithmetic and comparison cases reuse `Radicle/src/avm2/coercion.cpp`'s coercions: `add` concatenates when either primitive is a string, keeps int+int in int and uint+uint in uint with the AVM2 wrap, and falls back to Number otherwise; `subtract`/`multiply` keep the int/uint pair and otherwise produce Number; `divide` is always Number; `modulo` keeps int/int and uint/uint; the bitwise family converts through ToInt32/ToUint32 (`urshift` returns uint); the relational and equality cases use the abstract and strict operators; `equals` is the abstract operator and `strictequals` the strict one; `convert_*` and `coerce*` map to the matching coercion, `coerce` resolves by the multiname's rendered type name (int/uint/Number/Boolean/String/Object/Vector and class types through the runtime), and `typeof` returns the AVM2 type string. `lookupswitch`, the `hasnext2`/`nextname`/`nextvalue` iteration trio (with per-object key lists in the frame, including array indices and slot traits) and the branch family are implemented; `newcatch` and the E4X and debug-only opcodes outside the census stay `NotImplemented` with their name in the message.

**What the split is and why.** The dispatch switch is large, so the case bodies are in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_a.inc` and `_b.inc`, textually included inside the switch in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp`; the per-file length gate applies to the generated-looking `.inc` files too, so the split is by line budget, not by responsibility. Value and operand helpers live in `interpreter_internal.hpp`/`interpreter_ops.cpp`, and the property, call, construction and coercion helpers live in `interpreter_property.cpp`, so each translation unit stays under the gate and the dispatch switch keeps one flat view of the opcode space. The `.inc` files carry no comments and no types of their own; a change to the dispatch that adds a case is a change to one of them and to the opcode constants in `interpreter_internal.hpp`.

**Test fixture.** `Radicle/tests/avm2_test_support.hpp` builds an ABC file in memory instead of assembling bytes: `CodeBuilder` emits opcodes with two-pass label patching for branches, and `ScriptBuilder` owns the string, multiname (one package namespace), int, uint and double pools plus methods and bodies, so a test states its code linearly and the runtime links it as a real file. The tests assert on the returned `Value` (int, string, undefined), the status and message for refusals, the global object's stored property after a scope write, and repeat-run equality; `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_interpreter.cpp` is registered in `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt`. Nothing was built locally on this branch; CI is the evidence, and the next step is the corpus probe that runs every Programs script initializer and reports the first unimplemented opcode or unbound native, then class static initializer execution and R3's builtins.

## R2 script-initializer lifecycle and corpus probe (#807 R2)

The interpreter could execute synthetic methods but not a real script initializer; this round closes the lifecycle gaps the corpus pattern showed and adds the probe that is R2's exit evidence. The pattern is `getlocal0; pushscope; ... getscopeobject 0; pushnull; newclass n; initproperty Name` for a class movie and `findpropstrict Super; getproperty Super; pushscope; ... newclass n` for an inherited class, and the first fact it establishes is that a script initializer's register 0 is the global object, not undefined: `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::run_script` now passes `borrowed_object(global)` as the receiver, which is what makes the initial `pushscope` legal.

**Builtin class resolution and class statics.** A script initializer registers its class by name and elsewhere reads a builtin class the movie never defines, so a lookup miss on a name that is a class must create the runtime's external placeholder instead of a dynamic undefined binding. `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::find_scope_binding` now resolves such a name through `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/runtime.hpp:Runtime::resolve_or_create_global_class`, which creates and registers the external class on first use (the R3 seam where the real builtin gets bound later); the heuristic for "this is a class" is a non-empty public package namespace or a capitalised bare name, and a bare lowercase package-level name still becomes the dynamic global binding a script variable needs. With class objects reachable, `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/object.hpp:Object::set_class_scope` makes a class object's trait lookup walk the class (static) traits up the super chain the same way an instance walks its instance traits, so static slots and methods resolve; `Radicle/src/avm2/runtime.cpp:Runtime::apply_class_slots` sizes each linked class object's slot array and applies the static trait defaults at link, and `Radicle/src/avm2/class.cpp:Class::compute_class_slot_count`/`:apply_class_slot_defaults` own the accounting.

**Class initialization.** The corpus pushes `newclass n` for a class whose `cinit` must run once before its statics or first instance are used. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/class.hpp:ClassInitializationState` gives each class Uninitialized/Initializing/Initialized, and `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::ensure_class_initialized` runs `cinit` once with the class object as `this` and the class scope appended, re-entry safe for a static initializer that touches its own class. `:Interpreter::initialize_class_value` is the single hook that the property read, getlex and static-call paths use when a class object reaches the stack or is called, so class initialization happens on first use; `newclass` is covered by the same hook and construction calls `ensure_class_initialized` before it allocates an instance. An external class has no `cinit` and becomes initialized immediately.

**Catch handling.** The corpus handler shape is `getlocal0; pushscope; getlocal2; pushscope; newcatch 0; dup; setlocal3; dup; pushscope; swap; setslot 1`, which only works if the exception value stays on the operand stack under the catch scope object: `newcatch` therefore leaves the thrown value in place and pushes a fresh scope object (`Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_b.inc`), and the compiler copies the exception into the catch scope's slot itself. On `throw` the handler search now also matches the exception type (`AbcException::exc_type`) through the runtime's class table and restores the frame's scope depth to the method entry depth (`Frame::entry_scope_count`) before jumping to the handler, so a handler that re-pushes its own scopes starts from the depth the compiler expects; an unmatched type falls through to the next region and finally reports UncaughtException.

**Probe and lenient limits.** `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/interpreter.hpp:InterpreterLimits::lenient_builtins` is the probe mode: an unbound native returns undefined, an unbound method call on a builtin instance returns undefined, a read or call on a nullish value returns undefined and a non-function call target returns undefined, all where the strict mode reports NotImplemented, CannotCall or NullReference. That is how `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_scripts_real.cpp` reaches the opcodes after the first native call; it walks every `Programs/*.swf` in `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2`, parses each DoABC2 block, links one runtime per movie, runs every script initializer with a 50,000-instruction budget, records link failures, unbound-native stops and other messages as properties, and fails only when a script hits an opcode the interpreter does not implement (the R2 exit criterion). Strict mode keeps the refusal semantics for ordinary use. The new unit tests are in `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_interpreter.cpp`: the initializer receiver is the global object, an unresolved `flash.display::Sprite` becomes a class object, an unbound native refuses strictly and returns undefined leniently, a thrown value is caught by a matching region and the handler returns 9, and a handler whose type does not match the thrown string leaves the exception uncaught.

**Still open for R2/R3.** `getouterscope` in a method with no captured scope (a class method) and the E4X opcodes remain NotImplemented, see `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::outer_scope_value`; `callstatic`/`callmethod` are implemented in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::call_indexed` but unused by the corpus, and the verifier still rejects `callmethod` in user bytecode (see `Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_body_opcodes`); closures capture scopes but not activation locals (the corpus compiler copies captured locals into the activation scope's slots explicitly, so this has not blocked the initializers yet); and the builtin classes are bound in R3 (see the R3 sections below). The probe's data-runner output is the evidence for the opcode criterion; nothing was built locally.

## R3 native builtin foundation: natives, boxing and core classes (#807 R3)

R2's placeholder classes are replaced by a real native dispatch path and the first builtin surface. The dispatch switch calls `FunctionObject::native_id()` when a function has no body; `Radicle/src/avm2/native_ids.hpp` is the id enumeration and `Radicle/src/avm2/native_internal.hpp` the per-family handler entry points, so adding a builtin means adding an id and a case in the owning family file (`native_object.cpp`, `native_primitive.cpp`, `native_math.cpp`, `native_top.cpp`). A family handler reports whether it handled the id, and `Interpreter::call_native_id` walks the families in order, so one translation unit never owns the whole builtin table and each stays under the length gate. Natives receive the interpreter through the public helper surface in `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/interpreter.hpp`: `call_function`, `read_property`, `write_property`, `make_instance`, `box`, `unbox`, `global_this`, `prepare_plain_object` and a deterministic `next_random` whose sequence depends only on the interpreter's seed (Math.random must stay reproducible for the deterministic tests and for corpus replay).

**Installation.** `Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp:Runtime::install_builtins` runs at the start of `link()` and creates the builtin classes through `Runtime::add_builtin_class`, which registers the same key formats the linker uses for movie classes. Object, Function, Class, Number, int, uint, Boolean, String, Math and `__AS3.vec::Vector` are created with instance methods, static constants (Number.MAX_VALUE/MIN_VALUE/NaN/Infinity, int/uint bounds, Math PI/E/LN2/LN10/LOG2E/LOG10E/SQRT1_2/SQRT2) and native constructors (`Class::native_constructor`), and the top-level functions and values (trace, isNaN, isFinite, parseInt, parseFloat, String, Number, Boolean, int, uint, Object, getTimer, NaN, Infinity, undefined) are registered on the global object. `build_traits`, `resolve_hierarchy` and the builtin install skip file-less classes so the movie linker never dereferences a null ABC file; `bind_function_class` gives every function object the Function builtin class so `.call`/`.apply`/`.toString` resolve, including functions created later by `newfunction`.

**Runtime semantics.** Constructing or calling a builtin class routes through its native constructor (`Interpreter::construct` and the `call` opcode both dispatch it), so `String(x)`/`int(x)`/`Number(x)` behave as conversions and `new Number(1)` produces a number. `box`/`unbox` wrap primitives in their builtin class instances with the primitive payload in `Object::set_primitive`, and the property/call opcodes box a primitive receiver automatically, which is how `"abc".length`, `"abc".charAt(...)` and `int.toString()` work; a boxed string also answers `length` and numeric character indices directly in `get_property`. Plain objects created by `newobject`, `newactivation` and `newcatch` get the Object builtin class through `prepare_plain_object`, so `toString`/`valueOf`/`hasOwnProperty` resolve on ordinary objects.

**Implemented natives.** Object: constructor, toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty, isPrototypeOf, propertyIsEnumerable. Function: call, apply, toString. Number: constructor, toString (radix 2-36), toFixed, valueOf. int/uint: constructor, toString (radix), valueOf. Boolean: constructor, toString, valueOf. Math: abs, min, max, floor, ceil, round, sqrt, pow, random, sin, cos, tan, atan2, log, exp. Top level: trace (no-op), isNaN, isFinite, parseInt, parseFloat, String/Number/Boolean/int/uint/Object conversions and getTimer (returns 0 until a host tick source exists). `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_builtins.cpp` exercises Math.abs, Math.PI, Math.max, String(41), int primitive toString through boxing, Boolean(0), isNaN and Object.toString through a hand-built script per case; the runtime test that treated Object as an external placeholder now expects the real builtin.

No C ABI change. Nothing was built locally on this branch; CI is the compile evidence.

## R3 continued: String, Array and Error natives (#807 R3)

The native dispatch from the previous round now carries the collection and error surface. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_string.cpp` implements String methods over the primitive payload (`native_self` unboxes a boxed receiver), `Radicle/src/avm2/native_array.cpp` implements Array/Vector methods over `ArrayObject::elements()`, and `Radicle/src/avm2/native_error.cpp` implements Error construction and `toString`. New ids are appended to `Radicle/src/avm2/native_ids.hpp`, `try_string_native`/`try_array_native`/`try_error_native` are declared in `native_internal.hpp` and tried by `Interpreter::call_native_id` after the earlier families, so the dispatcher still owns no implementation and every translation unit stays under the length gate.

**String.** charAt, charCodeAt, indexOf, lastIndexOf, substr, substring, slice, split (array result through `Interpreter::make_array`), toUpperCase, toLowerCase, replace (string pattern and function replacement, the function receiving the matched text), concat, trim, toString, valueOf and the static fromCharCode. Strings are treated as byte strings: length and charAt are byte-based and fromCharCode encodes UTF-8, which matches the ASCII-dominant Scaleform content but will read a multi-byte UTF-8 character as several units (a UTF-16 improvement belongs with R6's text work).

**Array and Vector.** The Array class is installed with the array native set: push, pop, shift, unshift, slice, splice, join, concat, indexOf, lastIndexOf, reverse, sort (default text order or a comparator function), forEach, map, filter and toString, plus the native Array constructor (single numeric argument means length, otherwise the arguments are the elements). `newarray` gives its array the Array instance class so the traits resolve, and `applytype` gives its stand-in the `__AS3__.vec::Vector` class which carries the same native set, so Vector code works without element typing yet. length and numeric element access still go through `Interpreter::array_property`, so an assign to `length` truncates and an out-of-range write grows, as before.

**Error.** `Runtime::install_builtins` now creates Error plus TypeError, ReferenceError, RangeError, SyntaxError, URIError, SecurityError, ArgumentError, EvalError, DefinitionError, VerifyError and UninitializedError, each with `error_construct` as its native constructor and `error_to_string`. The constructor derives the error name from the class object that is passed as the call's receiver (both `construct` and the class-as-function `call` path pass the class object as `self`), stores the optional message argument, and gives the `ErrorObject` its class and prototype. `get_property` answers `name` and `message` from the `ErrorObject` fields, so `new TypeError("x").name` works, and `toString` produces "Name: message" (or just the name when the message is empty).

**Tests.** `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_builtins.cpp` gained String charAt/toUpperCase/indexOf, String split-then-join, Array push length, join, pop, default sort order, Error message rendering and TypeError subclass naming. All are hand-built scripts executed through the interpreter, so they exercise the same boxing, native dispatch, prototype lookup and array element paths the corpus uses.

No C ABI change. Nothing was built locally on this branch; CI is the compile evidence.

## R3 complete: typed Vector classes and the remaining census-named builtin members (#807 R3)

The builtin surface now covers the census-named core members and the Vector families. `applytype` had been an approximation that returned an array; it now follows the AVM2 stack shape: it pops the type parameters and the base class object, resolves the element class from the first type parameter, and pushes a concrete `Vector.<T>` class object. `Runtime::resolve_vector_class` creates and caches that concrete class on first use (name rendered as `__AS3__.vec::Vector.<T>`, superclass the Vector builtin, class and prototype objects wired to the base class's), so a later `construct` on it reaches the new vector branch in `Interpreter::construct`, which builds an `ArrayObject` carrying the concrete class and its element class. `newarray` arrays still get the Array class, and the base Vector class still constructs through `array_construct`.

**Element typing.** `ArrayObject::set_element_class` carries the element class of a typed vector. `array_push`, `array_unshift` and the indexed write in `Interpreter::array_property` coerce through `Interpreter::coerce_to_class` (which routes to the existing `coerce_value` type-name rules), so a `Vector.<int>` stores 7 when pushed "7" and a wrong-class element is refused with the usual coercion TypeError; `array_construct` marks its array when the constructing class is a concrete vector. Reads keep returning the stored Value; length and out-of-range growth stay on `array_property`.

**Remaining census-named members.** Math gained acos, asin and atan (joining abs, min, max, floor, ceil, round, sqrt, pow, random, sin, cos, tan, atan2, log, exp and the constants); Number gained toExponential and toPrecision (with the existing toString/toFixed/valueOf and limits); String gained localeCompare; Array and Vector gained every, some and reduce (with forEach, map and filter already there) and their callbacks receive the element, index and the array, so a fold or predicate works through the same `call_function` path. Function objects answer `length` (declared parameter count) and a lazily created `prototype` object, class objects answer `prototype`, which is what the corpus's `call`/`prototype`/`length` member reads need.

**Tests.** `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_builtins.cpp` now has 25 cases: the previous Math/String/Array/Error set plus Math.acos, Number.MAX_VALUE, String.localeCompare, Array.every with a hand-built predicate, Array.reduce with a hand-built fold, a `Vector.<int>` that coerces "7" to 7 through applytype/construct/push, and `new Array(3)` length. Each is a hand-built ABC script executed by the interpreter, so the tests cover the native dispatch, boxing, typed element coercion and the e4x-free callback invocation paths.

**R3 status.** The builtin class set named by the census is installed and the members the manifest names are implemented; the remaining gaps are XML/XMLList with E4X opcodes, Date/RegExp, Vector's `fixed`/`sort` overloads and a few rarely used Array members. Those do not appear as method calls in the census member data (XML appears only as a type reference), so they are recorded for a later pass rather than blocking the builtin milestone. Nothing was built locally; CI is the compile evidence, and the corpus probe from R2 remains the script-initializer measurement.

## R4 start: AVM2 display list, display classes and MovieClip timeline (#807 R4)

The display runtime is a new AVM2 object family, not another native trait table. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/display.hpp` defines `DisplayObject` (transform fields x/y/scaleX/scaleY/rotation/alpha, width/height, visible, name, parent, root/stage, interaction flags), `DisplayObjectContainer` (ordered children, addChild/addChildAt/removeChild/removeChildAt/getChildAt/getChildByName/contains/setChildIndex/swapChildren), `MovieClip` (timeline, currentFrame/totalFrames/playing, goto_frame/advance_frame, frame scripts) and `TimelineDefinition` (frame count, labels, frame-script method map, script file). `ObjectKind::Display` marks the family so `Interpreter::get_property`/`set_property` route to `read_display_property`/`write_display_property`: the transform and identity properties are real fields, `parent`/`root`/`stage` return the shared object, container answers `numChildren`, MovieClip answers currentFrame/totalFrames/framesLoaded/currentLabel/currentLabels. Unknown names fall through to the normal dynamic property path, so a script can still hang custom data on a display object.

**Construction and natives.** `Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp` installs `flash.display::DisplayObject`, InteractiveObject, DisplayObjectContainer, Sprite, MovieClip, Stage, Shape, Bitmap, TextField and SimpleButton with the correct superclass chain and `display_construct` as their native constructor; `make_display_object` picks MovieClip, DisplayObjectContainer or DisplayObject from the class chain, attaches the class prototype and marks the instance class. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_display.cpp` implements the display natives: the container family, gotoAndPlay/gotoAndStop/stop/play/nextFrame/prevFrame, localToGlobal/globalToLocal (translation-only accumulation for now; rotation and scale composition belongs with the renderer), plus `geom_construct` for flash.geom Point/Rectangle/Matrix/ColorTransform and `dictionary_construct` for flash.utils.Dictionary. The flash.display/geom/utils classes join Object's global registration, so a script's `new flash.display.Sprite()` reaches the display constructor and its methods resolve through the class traits.

**Timeline.** A MovieClip with a `TimelineDefinition` advances frame by frame and wraps; `goto_frame` clamps to the frame count, maps a label string through the definition, sets the playing flag and runs the lifecycle. The lifecycle order is fixed as construct, frameScript, enterFrame, exitFrame: today the frame script (a method from the defining ABC file, invoked with the clip as `this` and the clip's class as owner) runs and its result is returned to the caller, and the enter/exit hooks are the R5 event seams. `currentLabel`/`currentLabels` read the label table and `frame_for_label` resolves a label to its frame, which is what `gotoAndPlay("label")` needs.

**Tests.** `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_display.cpp` exercises the runtime end to end: Sprite `x` write/read through setproperty/getproperty, addChild + numChildren, addChildAt + getChildAt identity, a fresh MovieClip reporting frame 1 of 1, Point construction keeping x/y, Dictionary dynamic entries, a C++-built three-frame timeline that advances and wraps and whose labels resolve, a frame-script method observed on the frame it belongs to (returned value 42), and parent/root/contains on a real container tree.

## R4 complete: SWF timeline bridge, PlaceObject playback and the host tick (#807 R4)

The display runtime from the previous commit now reads real SWF timelines. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/swf_runtime.hpp` exposes `SwfMovieData` (root and sprite timelines as per-frame PlaceObject/RemoveObject rows, frame labels, symbol-class map, document class, stage metrics), and `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp` walks the parsed `fo4::swf::SwfFile` tags: PlaceObject/PlaceObject2/PlaceObject3 become placement rows, RemoveObject/RemoveObject2 become removals, ShowFrame ends a frame, FrameLabel names it, SymbolClass fills the character→class map (id 0 is the root document class), and DefineSprite recurses into its child tags so every sprite character gets its own row timeline. No game data is copied; only the tag structure is interpreted, and the bridge reads the already-parsed optional tag fields rather than re-decoding bytes.

**Playback.** `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp` defines `SwfTimelineClip`, a `MovieClip` subclass whose overridden placement hook applies the current frame's rows: a placement resolves a character class (symbol class first, then MovieClip for a sprite character, then Shape for a leaf), reuses the object at that depth when the character matches, replaces it otherwise, updates transform/name, keeps children ordered by depth, and raises the sprite children's timelines (frame 1 when first placed, one frame per parent frame after). Removals drop the depth and its object. The frame lifecycle order from the previous commit is preserved: the subclass applies placements first, then the base MovieClip runs the frame script (now also finding a `frame<N>` method trait on the clip's class, which is how AS3 timeline scripts are linked), then the R5 enter/exit seams. `build_movie_root` picks the linked document class when it is a MovieClip subclass, otherwise the MovieClip builtin, and the stage is a real Stage instance carrying the header frame size and frame rate.

**Host contract.** `SwfRuntime::create` builds the data, stage and root clip and applies frame 1, and `SwfRuntime::advance(interpreter, dt)` is the only clock: dt accumulates against the header frame rate and each whole frame advances the root timeline, so the same dt sequence always produces the same frame sequence and snapshots (the determinism the issue requires). Two identical runs are asserted to produce the same frame/child trace in the tests.

**Tests.** `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_swf_runtime.cpp` builds synthetic `SwfFile` tag trees (root timeline with a two-frame sprite character, labels, removals; optional SymbolClass map) and checks: row/label/sprite/stage extraction, stage construction and first-frame placement, the dt accumulator advancing at frame boundaries, child sprite timelines advancing with the parent, SymbolClass choosing the placed character class, and two independent runs producing identical traces.

**Still open for R4/R5.** `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfTimelineClip::apply_frame_state` applies ratio/blend/filter/visible rows to placed objects (`Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:apply_placement_state`, described at the end of this file), but nested sprite clip-depth masks are still not in the snapshot (R8's snapshot format owns those), symbol classes whose superclass is Sprite rather than MovieClip are treated as timeline clips, and the enterFrame hooks and the Loader/LoaderInfo surface are covered by the R5 and R7 sections below. Nothing was built locally; CI is the compile evidence.

## R5: EventDispatcher, frame events, keyboard/mouse input and host-clock timers (#807 R5)

Events are now a real part of the runtime. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/events.hpp` adds `EventObject` (type, bubbles, cancelable, target, currentTarget, eventPhase, defaultPrevented, stop flags), the generic `EventListener` storage on every `Object`, the three-phase `dispatch_event` and a `HostClock` that owns the host time and the live timers. `Radicle/src/avm2/events.cpp` implements the capture, target and bubble walk: the propagation path is the display parent chain from the root to the target (a non-display dispatcher is its own path), capture listeners run root-ward before the target, the target phase runs every listener on it in priority order, and bubble listeners run target-ward afterwards; `stopPropagation` and `stopImmediatePropagation` cut the walk at the right point and the event carries the node it was last delivered to.

**Classes and methods.** `Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp` installs `flash.events::EventDispatcher` (addEventListener/removeEventListener/dispatchEvent/hasEventListener), `flash.events::Event` (preventDefault/stopPropagation/stopImmediatePropagation/isDefaultPrevented/clone/toString plus the standard string constants such as ENTER_FRAME, ADDED_TO_STAGE, MOUSE_DOWN, KEY_DOWN) and the KeyboardEvent, MouseEvent, FocusEvent, TimerEvent, ProgressEvent, IOErrorEvent, SecurityErrorEvent and ErrorEvent subclasses with their constants. DisplayObject's superclass is now EventDispatcher, so every display object has the dispatcher surface. `flash.ui::Keyboard` carries the key-code constants (letters, digits, arrows, SPACE/ENTER/ESCAPE/TAB/BACKSPACE, F1-F12, NUMBER_n/NUMPAD_n, modifier codes) and `flash.utils::Timer` carries start/stop/reset. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_events.cpp` implements the native side: event construction (including the KeyboardEvent charCode/keyCode/ctrl/alt/shift and MouseEvent localX/localY/stageX/stageY/relatedObject/buttonDelta fields as properties), clone, the dispatcher methods, and the Timer lifecycle. Event properties are answered by `read_event_property` in the interpreter's property path.

**Frame lifecycle.** `MovieClip::run_frame_lifecycle` now applies placements, runs the frame script, then dispatches `enterFrame`, then `exitFrame` on the clip, in the order the issue names. The frame events use the same dispatch path as script-dispatched events, so a listener registered from AS3 sees ENTER_FRAME without any special case.

**Host clock and input.** `HostClock` never reads the wall clock: `Interpreter::advance_host_time(dt_ms)` is the only way time moves, `getTimer` returns that accumulated time, and each running Timer accumulates dt, fires `timer` every delay and `timerComplete` when repeatCount is reached. `SwfRuntime::advance` advances the host clock by the same dt it feeds the timeline, and `SwfRuntime::key_event`/`mouse_event` turn host input into KeyboardEvent/MouseEvent dispatches on the root clip so input-driven programs work through the ordinary listener path (mouse hit-testing is still the root target; R8's snapshot/host contract owns precise picking).

**Tests.** `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_events.cpp` builds listener methods in hand-assembled ABC that append a tag to a global string and asserts: capture/target/bubble order "ctb" on a parent/child sprite tree, "ct" for a non-bubbling event, stopPropagation on the target producing "cs" and skipping the bubble, a MovieClip dispatching enterFrame then exitFrame as "ex", a Timer with delay 100/repeat 2 firing twice and completing from `advance_host_time(250)` with `getTimer` at 250, the Keyboard class constant A == 65, and host key input reaching a root-clip keyDown listener while `SwfRuntime::advance` moves the host clock.

## R5 completion: hit testing, mouse targets, focus and willTrigger (#807 R5)

The R5 gaps left by the previous round are closed. `Radicle/src/avm2/hit_test.cpp:mouse_target_at` walks the display tree from the root in reverse child order (topmost first), maps the stage point into each object's local space with `Radicle/src/avm2/hit_test.cpp:stage_to_local`, and returns the deepest visible, mouse-enabled object whose own width and height contain the point. A container with `mouseChildren` false is not descended into, so the container itself is the target. `SwfRuntime::mouse_event`, `SwfRuntime::mouse_move` and `SwfRuntime::mouse_wheel` (`Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:pointer_target`) dispatch to that target and fall back to the root when nothing is hit, which is the old behaviour. The hit transform is `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:local_matrix`, now shared with the snapshot so hit testing and the frame snapshot cannot disagree on an object's transform.

`mouse_move` tracks the object under the pointer (`SwfRuntime::roll_chain_`, see the R5 roll events section): a change dispatches mouseOut on the old target and mouseOver on the new one before mouseMove. `mouse_event` records the target on mouseDown (`SwfRuntime::mouse_down_`) and dispatches click on mouseUp only when the up target is the same object. Mouse events carry stageX/stageY and localX/localY, where the local values come from `stage_to_local` on the target.

Focus lives on the object that owns it, held weakly (`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/display.hpp:DisplayObject::focus`, `:set_focus`), so a removed focus object is not kept alive by the stage. `Radicle/src/avm2/events.cpp:set_display_focus` moves focus and dispatches focusOut on the old object then focusIn on the new one, both as FocusEvent with relatedObject, bubbling; it is reached from a script write of `focus` (`Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::set_property`), from a mouseDown on a text field or tab-enabled object, and the read path is `Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:read_display_property`. `SwfRuntime::key_event` sends keyDown and keyUp to the stage focus when one is set, otherwise to the root. `Radicle/src/avm2/events.cpp:will_trigger` answers EventDispatcher.willTrigger by walking the same display path the dispatch uses, so an ancestor listener counts.

`hitTest`, `hitTestPoint` and `hitTestObject` (`Radicle/src/avm2/native_compat.cpp:display_hit_test`) were placeholders. They now call `hit_test_point` and `hit_test_object`. `hit_test_point` requires every ancestor to be visible and the point to fall inside the object's own width and height after the inverse transform. `hit_test_object` compares the axis-aligned stage bounds of the two objects and treats an invisible or zero-size object as not hitting. The `shapeFlag` argument is ignored because the runtime keeps no shape geometry. `hitTest` now returns a Boolean where the placeholder returned null.

Limits, in order of what matters for the corpus. Hit testing reads only the width and height a script sets. The SWF bridge (`Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp`) does not yet copy a placed character's drawn bounds into those fields, so on bridge-placed content every mouse target falls back to the root, and hitTestObject on placed content is false. Closing that needs the character bounds from the A6 character model and the bounds' origin offset, not just the size. Focus Tab traversal is not implemented, so KEY_FOCUS_CHANGE and MOUSE_FOCUS_CHANGE are never dispatched. mouseOver and mouseOut carry no relatedObject. The hitTestObject rule for invisible and zero-size objects is a simplification of the AS3 behaviour and was not checked against the player.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_events.cpp` covers the topmost-child target with a disabled upper child (`MouseTargetIsTheTopmostHitChild`), point and object hits through a scaled parent with a hidden ancestor (`HitTestFollowsTheParentTransform`), focusOut then focusIn order (`FocusChangeDispatchesFocusOutThenFocusIn`), willTrigger through a display ancestor (`WillTriggerSeesDisplayAncestors`), mouseDown bubbling to the hit object then click and mouseOver/mouseOut routing through `SwfRuntime` (`SwfRuntimeRoutesMouseInputToTheHitObject`), and key routing to the stage focus (`SwfRuntimeRoutesKeysToTheStageFocus`). Nothing was built locally; CI is the compile evidence.

## R5 roll events: rollOver and rollOut boundary dispatch (#807 R5)

`Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:update_roll` is the one roll state machine. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfRuntime::mouse_move` and `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfRuntime::mouse_event` both call it with the hit target, so a press delivered without a preceding move enters the roll state first. The state is `SwfRuntime::roll_chain_`: the chain under the pointer last time, innermost first, held as weak pointers so a removed object is not kept alive. Diffing against that recorded chain, not against the old target's current parent pointers, is what keeps ancestors correct: `DisplayObjectContainer::remove_child` clears the removed child's parent, so deriving the old chain from it dropped the ancestors still under the pointer and re-sent rollOver to them. The order on a change is mouseOut on the old target (only while it is alive), rollOut on each recorded node no longer under the pointer, mouseOver on the new target, then rollOver on each node newly under the pointer, outermost first. A removed but still alive node gets rollOut on the next move, matching mouseOut; a destroyed node gets nothing.

`Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:pointer_event` makes rollOver and rollOut non-bubbling and leaves every other pointer event bubbling. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:dispatch_pointer` targets each roll event at its own node, so a rollOver listener on an ancestor fires once from that ancestor's own dispatch and never from a descendant's bubble.

Focus needed no change in this round: `Radicle/src/avm2/events.cpp:set_display_focus` moves focus and dispatches focusOut then focusIn, `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::set_property` routes a script `focus` write there, and `Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:read_display_property` answers the read.

`Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:dispatch_pointer` sets relatedObject on every roll and over/out event: the object the pointer moved to on mouseOut and rollOut, and the object it came from on mouseOver and rollOver (null when there is none). A press now rolls over its target first, so `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_events.cpp:SwfRuntimeRoutesMouseInputToTheHitObject` expects mouseOver before mouseDown.

Limits. mouseWheel does not update the roll state. The removed-node choice (rollOut to a removed but alive node, nothing for a destroyed one) and the mouseOut, rollOut, mouseOver, rollOver order were not checked against the player; the order is the commonly reported Player order. Focus is stored per owning object, so a script `focus` write on a non-stage display object moves that object's own focus rather than the stage's.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_focus_events.cpp` covers the entry, stay, leave-within-ancestor and move-to-sibling boundary with the exact log order (`RollOverAndRollOutFollowTheAncestorBoundary`), and a host press moving stage focus to a tab-enabled object while a non-tab-enabled object leaves it (`MouseDownOnATabEnabledObjectMovesStageFocus`). `RollStateSurvivesRemovingTheHoveredChild` checks that removing the hovered child does not re-send rollOver to the ancestor still under the pointer, and `RollEventsCarryTheObjectMovedFromOrTo` checks relatedObject on rollOut and rollOver. Nothing was built locally; CI is the compile evidence.

## R6: embedded font decode, TextField/TextFormat and laid-out glyph runs (#807 R6)

Text is now modelled end to end. The SWF side finally decodes DefineFont2/DefineFont3 in full:
`Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp` extends `SwfFont` with the shape offset table, the code table,
per-glyph advance widths normalised to em fractions (the tag's units per em are 1024 or 20480 for
DefineFont3), the font ascent/descent/leading and the layout flag, and
`Radicle/src/swf/swf_text.cpp` reads the offset table, the code-table offset, the code table, the
layout block, the bounds table and the kerning table with bounds checks, so a malformed font is
reported instead of half-read. The wide-offset/wide-code/layout flag bits were the wrong ones before
(0x08 is HasLayout, not wide offsets), which this fixes. `SwfReader` gained `read_s16` for the
advance and leading entries.

**Text model.** `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/fonts.hpp` adds `FontGlyph`/`FontResource`/`FontRegistry`
(a glyph keeps its code and em-fraction advance, the registry answers by character id or by name),
`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/text.hpp` adds `TextFormatData`, `GlyphPlacement`, `TextRun` and
`TextFieldObject` (a `DisplayObject` with text/htmlText/format/autoSize/wordWrap/multiline and a
measured textWidth/textHeight), and `Radicle/src/avm2/text.cpp` lays the string out: one run per line,
each character resolved to a glyph and advance from the format's font (falling back to half an em per
byte when no font is attached), with glyph positions accumulated in the run and the measured box
recomputed. The htmlText subset strips tags and decodes the five basic entities, which is the part the
census uses. TextFormat instances round-trip through `make_text_format_instance`/
`read_text_format_instance`, so AS3 can pass formats in and out.

**Classes and bridge.** `flash.text::TextField` (moved out of flash.display to its correct package,
super InteractiveObject) and `flash.text::TextFormat` are installed; a TextField instance is created
as a `TextFieldObject` wired to the runtime's font registry, its properties are answered by the
display property path (`text`, `htmlText`, `textColor`, `textWidth`, `textHeight`, `numLines`,
`wordWrap`, `multiline`, `autoSize`, `defaultTextFormat`, `length`) and `appendText`, `getLineText`,
`setTextFormat` and `getTextFormat` are natives in `native_text.cpp`. The SWF bridge collects the font
tags into `SwfMovieData::fonts` and `SwfRuntime::create` installs them into `Runtime::fonts()`, so a
movie's TextFields lay out against its own embedded fonts. `make_display_object` picks
`TextFieldObject` for a TextField-class symbol.

**Tests.** `tests/test_swf_fonts.cpp` builds synthetic DefineFont3 and DefineFont2 SWFs and asserts
glyph codes, em-fraction advances (0.5/0.25 in both unit systems), ascent/leading, offsets and the
font3 flag. `tests/test_avm2_text.cpp` covers glyph layout with a hand-built font (2 glyphs, positions
0/10, width 15, height 24), newline runs, htmlText tag stripping and entity decoding, TextFormat round
trip, script-visible text/textWidth/numLines, and appendText plus getLineText through natives.
`tests/test_swf_fonts_real.cpp` (FO4_DATA_DIR gated) decodes the fonts in `fonts_programs.swf` and
`fonts_en.swf`, asserting fonts, layout fonts and total glyph counts are non-zero and that every layout
font's advance table matches its glyph count.

## R5/R6 follow-up: placed bounds, DefineEditText instances, word wrap, UTF-16 layout (#807 R6)

The R5 limit that placed bridge objects had no size is closed. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp:read_swf_movie_data` builds the A6 character model (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_characters.cpp:build_character_model`) and copies every character that carries drawn bounds into `SwfMovieData::character_bounds` (`SwfCharacterBounds` in `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/swf_runtime.hpp`). `character_bounds_of` converts the RECT from twips: origin is the RECT's `x_min`/`y_min` and width/height are `x_max - x_min` and `y_max - y_min`, each divided by 20. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:apply_character_definition` copies that onto the new `DisplayObject::origin_x`/`origin_y` (set by `DisplayObject::set_origin`) and `width`/`height`, and runs once when the bridge creates the object, so a script's later width write is not overwritten by a frame re-application. Sprites and buttons have no drawn bounds in the model, so they still hit only through their children or not at all. `Radicle/src/avm2/hit_test.cpp:inside_bounds` and `stage_bounds` now test the local box `[origin, origin + size]`, not `[0, size]`, so a shape whose RECT starts at a negative twip still hits at its drawn edge. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_compat.cpp:display_get_bounds` adds the origin to x/y; scale and rotation are still ignored there as before.

DefineEditText characters are instantiated. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp:text_field_of` reads the decoded `SwfEditText` into `SwfMovieData::text_fields` (`SwfTextFieldData`): text, the HTML flag (flags2 0x02), WordWrap (flags1 0x40), Multiline (flags1 0x20), AutoSize (flags2 0x40 maps to left), font id, font class name, font height (twips / 20), colour (ARGB, alpha dropped to the 24-bit TextFormat colour), and the layout margins, indent and leading (twips / 20). `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:resolve_character_class` picks `flash.text::TextField` for such a character when no symbol class names one, so `make_display_object` builds a `TextFieldObject`. The bounds are applied before the text so that word wrap sees the box width. DefineText (static text) is instantiated as a Shape with its bounds, but without glyphs: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_text.cpp` keeps only the record and glyph counts, so the glyph codes are not available to the bridge. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfTimelineClip` reuses a depth's object only when both the class and the character id match, so a PlaceObject that swaps characters of one class re-applies the character definition. Radicle/src/swf is outside this round's scope.

`TextFormatData::font_id` (`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/text.hpp`) selects a font by character id. `Radicle/src/avm2/text.cpp:TextFieldObject::relayout` tries the id, then the name, then the first font with layout. `TextFieldObject::set_word_wrap` is out of line and relays out, so a script `wordWrap` write reflows the text. Display.cpp's `width` write relays out a text field for the same reason.

Word wrap is applied in `Radicle/src/avm2/text.cpp:wrap_cut`: with a positive wrap width (`width() - left_margin - right_margin`, and only when wordWrap is on), a line is cut after the last space that still fits, or before the glyph that overflows when there is no space in the line, and always keeps at least one glyph per line so the walk makes progress. Trailing spaces count toward the line's pen position, so a wrapped line's `textWidth` can include its trailing space. Flash's 2 px gutter is not modelled. `line_count` and `line_text` now come from the runs, not from the newline split, so a wrapped line counts as one line.

Layout works in UTF-16 code units. `Radicle/src/avm2/utf16.cpp:utf16_from_utf8` decodes the UTF-8 the interpreter stores (surrogate pairs for code points above U+FFFF, and an invalid byte becomes the code unit of its own value), and `Radicle/src/avm2/utf16.cpp:utf8_from_utf16` encodes back. `relayout` looks each unit up in the font, so a non-ASCII glyph resolves to its own code instead of two bytes. `TextField.length` (`Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:read_display_property`) counts the same units. The interpreter's strings are still stored as UTF-8, but the `String` natives and `length` now count UTF-16 code units (see the next section).

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_swf_runtime.cpp:PlacedCharacterBoundsDriveHitTesting` builds a DefineShape with RECT (-400, 800, -200, 400) twips placed at (100, 50) px, so origin (-20, -10), size 60 by 30, stage box x 80 to 140 and y 40 to 70; it expects hits at (80,40), (140,70) and a text hit at (15,30), and misses at (79,60), (141,60) and (120,71). `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_swf_runtime.cpp:PlacedEditTextBecomesAWrappedTextField` places a DefineEditText with a 500 by 2000 twip box (25 by 100 px), font height 400 twips (20 px), text "AA AA" with WordWrap set, and expects two runs "AA " and "AA", textWidth 25 (two A at 10 px, space at 5 px) and textHeight 48 (two lines at 24 px). `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_text.cpp:WordWrapBreaksAfterTheLastSpaceThatFits`, `WordWrapBreaksInsideAWordWhenNoSpaceFits` (AAAA in 25 px gives "AA" and "AA", and 40 px unwrapped) and `TextIsLaidOutInUtf16CodeUnits` (U+00E9 then U+1F600 as D83D DE00, widths 5 + 10 + 10 = 25) cover the layout.

Nothing was built or run locally; CI is the compile evidence.

## AVM2 strings count UTF-16 code units

Strings keep UTF-8 storage. `Radicle/src/avm2/value.cpp:Value::string` is the only constructor, and it calls `join_surrogate_halves`, which merges an adjacent high and low surrogate, each stored as a WTF-8 three-byte sequence, into the four-byte UTF-8 form. An unpaired surrogate stays a three-byte sequence (`ED A0..BF xx`). This keeps `==` correct when `charAt(0) + charAt(1)` rebuilds a non-BMP character. `Value::string` keeps the bytes it is given, apart from a joined surrogate pair, but the String natives do not keep invalid bytes. `utf16_from_utf8` turns an invalid byte into the code unit of its own value (0x80..0xFF become U+0080..U+00FF), and `utf8_from_utf16` writes that code point back as two-byte UTF-8, so `indexOf`, `substr`, `split` and the rest change an invalid byte. Only well-formed UTF-8 comes back byte for byte.

Every index and length goes through `Radicle/src/avm2/utf16.cpp:utf16_from_utf8` and back through `utf8_from_utf16`, which already accept WTF-8 surrogates. This applies to `Radicle/src/avm2/native_string.cpp:string_char_at`, `string_char_code_at`, `string_index_of`, `string_last_index_of`, `string_substr`, `string_substring`, `string_slice`, `string_split` (an empty separator splits per code unit) and `string_from_char_code` (low 16 bits of each argument, so two halves combine). `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::get_property` applies the same units to `length` and to numeric indexing of a string primitive.

Unchanged on purpose: `toUpperCase`/`toLowerCase` and `trim` stay ASCII-only, `replace` searches bytes (well-formed UTF-8 matches on character boundaries), and `localeCompare` and relational operators compare bytes. Byte order equals code point order, which differs from UTF-16 unit order only for U+E000..U+FFFF against surrogates. `indexOf` with a negative start now clamps to 0 (`native_string.cpp:string_index_of`) instead of returning 0 for every needle.

Ceiling: each index or length call decodes the whole string, so a `for (i < s.length)` loop is O(n²). Add a cached unit view on the string object if that shows up in a profile.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_string_utf16.cpp` covers the helper round trip, `Value::string` merging, `length`, `s[i]`, `charCodeAt`, `charAt`, `indexOf`, `substring`, `fromCharCode` for a pair and for a lone unit, and `==` after rebuilding a character from two halves. The indexOf, lastIndexOf, substr, slice, split and fromCharCode cases use surrogate pairs: a negative start clamps to 0 (`Radicle/src/avm2/native_string.cpp:string_index_of`), a start inside a pair matches nothing, lastIndexOf searches back from the start unit, split with a pair separator keeps the pair whole, split with an empty separator yields each half, and fromCharCode keeps the low 16 bits of each argument.

## ABC text form: whole-file dump (phase 4)

`Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc_text.hpp:render_abc_text` dumps a complete `AbcFile` as deterministic editable text. It prints the version line, then every pool by value in index order (strings quoted with \\, \", \n, \r, \t and \xNN escapes for control and non-ASCII bytes; ints and uints decimal; doubles as their exact IEEE-754 bit pattern in hex so nothing is lost; namespaces with their kind token and name string reference; ns_sets by member namespace references; multinames by kind with their components as references, including TypeName base and parameters), then metadata (name and item key/value pairs), methods (name, param count, return and parameter multinames, flags, optional values and parameter names), the instance/class/script trait tables, and the method bodies. Every reference is written as `@N`, the original pool index, so an unedited round trip can restore the exact index while an edited value can be re-interned; the pool entry lines themselves are always by value, which is what makes the dump editable.

Bodies are rendered as decoded instructions with numeric offsets kept for reference and labels (`L0`, `L1`, ...) assigned to every branch target, `lookupswitch` default/case target and exception range/boundary (`abc_text_body.cpp`). Branch operands print as `-> Lk`, switches as `switch Ldefault Lc1 Lc2 ...`, exception rows as `exception Lfrom Lto Ltarget type @N var @N`, and a labelled line is emitted for an exception range that ends at the code end. A body whose code does not decode prints a `decode failed: <status>` line and the raw bytes instead of instructions, so a dump never silently loses data. The text is stable: the same model always produces the same bytes, which the real-data test checks by hashing every vanilla block twice.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_text.cpp` renders the synthetic ABC fixture and checks every section marker, label-based branch rendering, determinism across parse → serialize → parse, and that editing a pool value changes the text. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_text_real.cpp` (FO4_DATA_DIR gated) dumps every DoABC block in every readable `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` movie, asserts no parse or decode failures, and compares block counts and a rolling FNV-1a hash between two passes so the dump is provably deterministic over the corpus. The assembler that consumes this text is phase 5; until it exists the text is a dump only.

## ABC assembler: text back to a model (phase 5)

`Radicle/include/fo4/abc/abc_asm.hpp:assemble_abc_text` reads the phase-4 text back into an `AbcFile`. The lexer (`src/abc/abc_asm_lex.cpp`) is line-based: it splits tokens while keeping quoted strings whole, unescapes the `\\"`, `\\\\`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t` and `\xNN` forms the dump emits, parses decimal integers, hexadecimal IEEE-754 doubles and `@N` references, and maps the namespace/multiname/trait/value kind tokens and opcode mnemonics back to their enums. The record parser (`src/abc/abc_asm.cpp`) walks the top-level sections, validates the declared counts against the listed entries (pools and record tables must be sequential from zero), rebuilds every pool, metadata row, method signature (including optional values and parameter names), instance, class, script and trait, and the body parser (`src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp`) turns each body block into instructions: it validates that the printed offsets are contiguous, computes each instruction length from its opcode and operand encodings, records branch, switch and exception labels, resolves every label to an absolute offset, encodes the code with `encode_code` and decodes it back to prove the round trip, then stores the code with its exceptions and traits. Errors carry the source line in `AbcTextError` so a bad edit points at the line that broke.

The done-when for phase 5 is byte-identical dump -> assemble -> serialize over every vanilla block. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm.cpp` proves the machinery on the synthetic fixture: dump/assemble/serialize equals the original bytes, the assembled model renders the identical text again, an edited pool value survives assemble + serialize, and malformed version lines and unknown opcodes are refused with a line number. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm_real.cpp` (FO4_DATA_DIR gated) runs that loop over every DoABC block in every readable `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` movie and counts parse failures, assemble failures and serialize mismatches, which must all be zero; CI on the data runner is the evidence for the corpus claim.

Still open in phase 5/6: the assembler does not yet recompute or verify `max_stack`, `local_count` and scope depths (they are preserved from the text and left to the flow verifier), it intern new-strings-by-value references only through explicit added pool lines rather than automatic interning, and the write-side C ABI is in place (see the phase 6 section below).

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:assemble_instruction_text (#806 phase 5, instruction text)

`assemble_instruction_text` turns one branch-free instruction in the body-dump form (`pushbyte -3`, `getproperty @5`, pool references as `@N`) into code bytes. It is the single-instruction counterpart of `parse_body`, and it is the form `Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:insert_instruction` takes as raw bytes. Both paths share `BodyParser::parse_operation`, so operand grammar and instruction lengths are the ones a dumped body uses. Branch and switch operands are refused (`branch operands need a method body`) because their targets are labels of a body, the same rule `edit.cpp` applies to inserted branches. The produced bytes are decoded again by `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code`, and `same_instruction` compares the decoded immediates and values with the parsed ones, so a value that does not fit its encoding is refused rather than truncated: `pushbyte 300` fails because the byte becomes 44.

Structured instructions need no new path: `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:encode_code` already encodes an `AbcInstruction` vector. What it does not do is compute `offset` and `length`, so a caller building instructions by hand must lay them out first.

Resolved: the `pushshort` operand is now written in its 16-bit form by `Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:parse_operation`; see the pushshort section below.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm.cpp:AbcAsm.AssemblesOneInstructionToItsOpcodeAndOperandBytes` pins `pushbyte -3` to `24 FD`, `getlocal 1` to `62 01` and `returnvoid` to `47`; `AbcAsm.EveryBranchFreeFixtureInstructionRoundTripsThroughTheDecoder` assembles every branch-free instruction of the synthetic fixture and requires the decoded text to equal the dumped text; `AbcAsm.RefusesInstructionTextThatIsNotOneBranchFreeInstruction` covers the empty line, an unknown mnemonic, a missing operand, trailing tokens, a branch and an out-of-range byte.

## R8 start: frame snapshots and deterministic hashing (#807 R8)

The runtime now has the host-facing frame contract. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/snapshot.hpp` defines `FrameSnapshot` as an ordered flat list of `SnapshotEntry` values plus a sound-event list. An entry carries the kind (display object, shape, bitmap or text), character id, clip depth, blend mode, visibility, alpha, `path` (materials-free identity such as `/0/1`) and `name`, the composed 2D matrix, the colour transform, and, for a text field, the laid-out `SnapshotTextRun` glyph runs (font id, size, origin, colour and per-glyph id/position/advance). `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:build_frame_snapshot` walks the display tree depth-first in child order, composes each object's local transform (translation, scale, rotation) onto its parent's, folds alpha into the colour transform, converts `TextFieldObject::runs()` into snapshot runs, and makes the root the first entry with the empty path. `snapshot_hash` is an FNV-1a over every field of every entry and every sound event, including double bit patterns, so equal snapshots hash equal and a changed tree changes the hash.

`SoundEventQueue` is the sound side of the frame contract: the host pushes play/stop/volume events while the runtime runs and exactly one `take_snapshot` drains them into the snapshot, so an event is never reported twice. `SwfRuntime` now exposes `take_snapshot()` (draining), `snapshot()` (non-draining) and `sound_events()`; display objects gained the character-id, clip-depth and blend-mode fields that the snapshot needs, and the SWF bridge fills them from each placement row (the clip depth is the one value the placement reader already decoded).

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_snapshot.cpp` builds the synthetic two-frame movie from the timeline bridge and asserts the flattened paths, names, character ids and composed transform of a shape nested in a sprite; that a placed TextField's runs produce glyph positions and advances (two glyphs at x 0 and 6 for the 12pt fallback layout); that two snapshots of the same tree are equal and hash equal; that two independent runs over the same dt sequence produce identical hash sequences; and that the sound queue drains into exactly one snapshot. That hash-sequence comparison is the deterministic record/replay shape the issue's acceptance needs, and the recorded frame hashes can become the checked-in hashes once the corpus movies run end to end.

Still open for R8: the snapshot carries no shape/bitmap reference yet (only the character id; the shape and bitmap bodies are decoded in `fo4/swf`), placed ratio, blend, visible, cache and filters reach the snapshot but not the C ABI (`Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:fill_entry`), the replay/input-recording driver and the C ABI that hands the snapshot to GardenEngine are both superseded (see `## Runtime C ABI and replay driver (#807 R8)`, which cites `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/replay.hpp` and `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_runtime.h`); only the GardenEngine-side swap is still open. Next: attach shape/bitmap ids to the bridge (`Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:make_entry` already copies colour), or start R7's Loader/URLLoader/host-call surface.
## Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfTimelineClip::apply_frame_state move placements (#807 SWF placement fidelity)

A PlaceObject2/3 with the Move flag changes only the fields it carries. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp:decode_place_object2` sets `SwfPlacement::move` from flag 0x01. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp:placement_row` copies it into `SwfPlacementRow::move`, with `has_character` (a character id is present), `has_matrix` (a matrix is present) and the matrix rotate/skew terms `rotate_skew0`/`rotate_skew1`. Before this, the row had no move or presence flag, so a move row was read as character 0. `apply_frame_state` resolved that to Shape and removed and recreated the object at its depth, which reset the transform and dropped the name and the tweened instance.

`apply_frame_state` now handles a row as follows. A row without a character reuses the object at its depth and does nothing when no object exists, so a move row never creates one. The matrix is applied when the row carries one, or when the row is not a move: a non-move row restates the whole placement, so an absent matrix still resets to identity as before. The clip depth follows the same rule, and the character id is set only when the row has one. `apply_matrix` maps the SWF matrix onto the `DisplayObject` fields it can hold. With zero rotate/skew it copies the scale exactly, signed, so a flip stays a flip. With rotate/skew it sets rotation to `atan2(rotate_skew0, scale_x)` in degrees, scale_x to `hypot(scale_x, rotate_skew0)`, and scale_y to `hypot(rotate_skew1, scale_y)` carrying the sign of the determinant. `DisplayObject` has no skew field, so a true skew is approximated by this decomposition. The snapshot reads only rotation and scale, so no snapshot or C ABI field is added.

`Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:MovieClip::goto_frame` does not replay earlier frames: it runs `apply_frame_state` for the target frame only. A move-only row whose object was never placed in this run is therefore a no-op where it used to create a Shape. Seeking therefore keeps the display list as it stands, which is a pre-existing limit; an exact seek needs a replay from frame 1.

Not in this change: ratio, blend mode, filter and visible rows are still not read into `SwfPlacementRow`, because the snapshot carries them only after the ABI lane.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_swf_runtime.cpp` adds six cases. `MoveOnlyPlacementKeepsTheTimelineObject` detects a move row recreating its object and losing the instance and transform. `MoveWithMatrixUpdatesOnlyTheMatrix` detects a move with a matrix recreating the object and losing the name and character id. `MoveWithANewCharacterReplacesTheObject` is a guard that a move row carrying a character still replaces the object; it passes before the fix too. `RotationFromMatrixSurvivesAMoveOnlyPlacement` detects rotate/skew dropped by `placement_row` or a move-only row resetting the transform to identity. `MoveOnlyPlacementKeepsTheClipDepth` detects a move without a clip depth clearing the mask. `MoveWithoutAnObjectCreatesNothing` detects a move row creating an unnamed Shape at character 0. Nothing was built or run locally; CI is the compile evidence.

## R7 start: host bridge, network loads, application domain and sound events (#807 R7)

The runtime now crosses the host boundary. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/host.hpp` defines `HostCallbacks` with the four hooks the issue's host contract names: an asset resolver for sibling SWF and XML loads, storage read/write for SharedObject, and a host-call forwarder for ExternalInterface and the Scaleform bridge. `HostBridge` wraps them so a runtime with no callbacks still reports every cross-boundary request as unavailable instead of throwing, and counts asset requests/misses, storage reads/writes and host calls/misses for the host to inspect.

**Host calls and definitions.** `flash.external::ExternalInterface` is installed with static `call`, `addCallback` and an `available` getter that reads the host-call hook's presence; `call` converts its first argument to the bridge method name, the remaining arguments to strings, forwards them through `HostCallbacks::host_call`, returns the host's string or null when the host cannot answer, and bumps the counters. `flash.system::ApplicationDomain` gains `currentDomain` (a static getter) and `getDefinition`, and the top-level `getDefinitionByName`, `getQualifiedClassName` and `getQualifiedSuperclassName` resolve through the runtime's class table, so a loaded movie can look classes up by their rendered names.

**Loading.** `flash.net::URLRequest` and `flash.net::URLLoader` are installed; `URLLoader.load` resolves the request URL through `HostBridge::resolve_asset`, stores the bytes as the loader's `data` string and dispatches `complete` (or `ioError` when the resolver misses), which is enough for the Programs' XML config loads. `flash.display::Loader` is a real display container: `load` resolves and parses a sibling SWF, builds a child `SwfRuntime` on the same runtime, attaches its root clip under the Loader entry (so the frame snapshot shows the loaded display list), registers the clip with the runtime so the host frame driver advances it, and dispatches `complete`.

**Sound.** `flash.media::Sound`, `SoundChannel` and `SoundTransform` are installed; `Sound.load` resolves and parses a SWF for its first DefineSound (or registers the raw bytes), `Sound.play` returns a channel and queues a `Play` event on the runtime's sound event queue, and `Sound.close`/`SoundChannel.stop` queue `Stop`. The SWF bridge now collects every DefineSound tag into `SwfMovieData::sounds` as `SoundResource` (format, rate, sample count, payload) and `SwfRuntime::create` registers them with the runtime, so the host plays by runtime sound id and receives the events through `take_snapshot`. `SoundEventQueue` moved into its own `sound.hpp` so the runtime owns it (the snapshot drains it) and the natives can push without depending on the display snapshot.

**Tests.** `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_host.cpp` drives a host with an in-memory asset map and a recording host-call hook: ExternalInterface.call forwards method and stringified arguments and returns the host answer (counters included), available reflects the hook, getDefinitionByName resolves a builtin class, getQualifiedClassName reports the rendered class name, URLLoader.load reads a config through the resolver and exposes it as `data`, and Sound.load + Sound.play over a resolved payload queues exactly one Play event that `SwfRuntime::take_snapshot` drains with a registered sound id.

Still open for R7 at this point. Later sections close SharedObject storage (`SharedObject and AMF3 storage`), DefineSound PCM decoding (`DefineSound PCM decode and placed colour transforms`) and the runtime C ABI with the replay driver (`Runtime C ABI and replay driver`). ApplicationDomain separation is partial in the slice below (`ApplicationDomainObject`), and a dedicated Scaleform bridge surface is still only the host-call forwarding in `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/host.hpp`.

## Incremental linking and movie script execution

A loaded movie now brings its own ABC into the runtime. `Runtime::add_file` accepts a file after
`link()` and `Runtime::link_added_file` links just that file on an already-linked runtime: it builds the
file's class shells, resolves the hierarchy (new classes may extend loaded or builtin classes), rebuilds
prototypes, builds traits only for classes that do not have them yet (`Class::traits_built`), reapplies
class slots, and registers the file's script entries once (`FileState::scripts_registered`). The full
link path now ends `build_traits` by recomputing each class's slot count after traits exist, which the
prototype pass previously computed too early.

`SwfRuntime::create` now parses every DoABC block of the movie into storage owned by the runtime
(`abc_files_`, a deque so runtime pointers stay valid), adds each to the `Runtime`, links it
incrementally, and runs each newly registered script initializer in order before frame 1. It then takes
the document class chosen by `build_movie_root` (the SymbolClass id-0 class when it is a MovieClip
subclass), applies its slot defaults, prepares the class (running its initializer once), and invokes the
instance constructor with the root clip as `this`, so a program's document class constructor runs before
the first frame. `LoaderObject` keeps the loaded child `SwfRuntime` alive, which keeps the loaded
movie's ABC storage alive for the lifetime of the class pointers the runtime holds.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_script.cpp` links a second file on an already-linked runtime, checks its
script list grows and that running the new script sees the updated global, and checks a repeated
`link_added_file` reports `AlreadyLinked`; it also builds a small SWF with a DoABC2 tag whose script
writes a global, runs `SwfRuntime::create`, and asserts the movie's script executed (one file, one
script, expected global value). The document-class constructor path shares the same code but is not yet
covered by a synthetic class test, and the real Programs corpus is still the next acceptance gate.

Still open: updated atlases/timelines. SharedObject/AMF, LZMA movie compression, the replay driver and the runtime C ABI were closed by the sections below (`SharedObject and AMF3 storage`, `Radicle/src/swf/swf_lzma.cpp:lzma_decode_swf`, `Runtime C ABI and replay driver`).

## ABC write-side C ABI (phase 6)

The C ABI can now dump a whole ABC block as text, assemble that text back to ABC bytes, and apply the assembled block to the movie so the existing byte writer persists the edit. `radicle_swf_abc_text` returns the phase-4 whole-block text for one `radicle_swf` ABC index as a NUL-terminated malloc'd buffer; `radicle_swf_abc_assemble` hands back the serialized ABC bytes for text the caller may have edited, refusing malformed text with `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR` and the assembler's error message; `radicle_swf_abc_apply_text` assembles and rewrites that DoABC/DoABC2 tag body all-or-nothing through the existing tag-plan path (`radicle_swf_apply_plan`), rebuilding the movie's cached views and bumping the revision, so `radicle_swf_write_bytes` writes the edited movie. The tag payload it builds keeps the block's original flags and name (DoABC2 stores flags, a NUL-terminated name then the ABC bytes; DoABC uses the same layout) and the code refuses any other tag. `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` moved to 67 and the C# bindings were regenerated with `tools/generate_interop.py`, so `RadicleNative.CompiledAbiVersion` and the ABI layout probe follow the header.

The C# side gains `SwfFile.AbcText(int abc)`, `SwfFile.AssembleAbc(int abc, string text)` and `SwfFile.ApplyAbcText(int abc, string text)`, plus `SwfFile.WriteBytes()`, which is the full edit loop GardenEngine needs: read the text, edit it, apply it, save the movie bytes.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_edit.cpp` builds a DoABC2 movie from the synthetic ABC fixture, checks the whole-block text has the version and a body, assembles it back byte-identically, edits the first string pool value, applies it, writes the movie, reopens the written bytes and confirms the edit is present in the new dump. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_real.cpp` runs the same loop on the first `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` movie that carries an ABC block when `FO4_DATA_DIR` is set: dump, edit a string-pool value, apply, write bytes, reopen and confirm the marker. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/SwfAbcWriteTests.cs` covers the same two loops through the bindings (a synthetic movie always, the real Interface movie when `FO4_DATA_DIR` is set), so the phase 6 done-when - dump, edit, assemble, write, re-read and confirm the edit - is checked at both the C ABI and the binding level.

Still open in phase 7: the remaining art bodies are decoded only as far as #807 needed (font outlines are closed by Phase 8 below and sound PCM by the DefineSound section). LZMA (ZWS) read/write is in-house in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_lzma.cpp`, with no linked library. AVM1 DoAction decode: the corpus evidence is in the Phase 7 corpus evidence section below.

## SharedObject and AMF3 storage (#807 R7)

`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/amf.hpp` and `src/avm2/amf.cpp` add a small AMF3 codec: undefined, null, booleans, integers (29-bit inline with double fallback), doubles, strings, dense arrays and anonymous dynamic objects. Decode refuses truncated values, unsupported markers and trailing bytes, and encode sorts object members by name so the same object always produces the same body. `shared_object_name_ok` rejects empty, over-long and path-like names before any host call, so a movie cannot address outside its storage.

`flash.net::SharedObject` is installed with a static `getLocal(name)` and `data` accessor plus `flush`, `clear` and `close`. `getLocal` reads through `HostCallbacks::read_storage` and decodes the body into the object's data (a fresh dynamic object when the slot is empty or unreadable), the `data` getter/setter expose that value to ActionScript, and `flush` encodes the data as AMF3 and writes it through `HostCallbacks::write_storage`, returning false when the host refuses. The object type lives in `net.hpp` as `SharedObjectObject` so the natives can keep the name and data between calls.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_shared.cpp` runs a two-runtime round trip against an in-memory storage map: a script calls `getLocal("save")`, writes `data.count = 5`, flushes, and the host bytes decode to an AMF3 object whose `count` is 5; a second runtime with the same storage map reads `getLocal("save").data.count` back as 5, with the storage read/write counters checked. A second test confirms `getLocal("bad/name")` returns null without touching storage.

Still open for R7 after this: a dedicated Scaleform bridge surface, which is still only the host-call forwarding in `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/host.hpp`. ApplicationDomain separation is partial in `ApplicationDomainObject` below, and DefineSound PCM decoding and the runtime C ABI with the replay driver are closed below. #806's remaining phase 7 items are in the Phase 7 notes above.

## Runtime C ABI and replay driver (#807 R8)

`include/fo4/c_api_runtime.h` and `src/c_api_runtime.cpp` give the host a complete runtime handle. `radicle_runtime_open` installs the four host callbacks (asset resolver, storage read/write, host-call forwarder) from plain C function pointers with `user` pointers and links the builtins; `radicle_runtime_open_movie` (bytes) and `radicle_runtime_open_movie_from_ba2` (archive entry) parse a movie and create its `SwfRuntime` through the same path the C++ API uses, so the movie's ABC is linked incrementally and its scripts run; `radicle_movie_advance` is the only clock; `radicle_movie_input` applies a mouse/key/char/wheel event; and `radicle_movie_snapshot` returns a flat display-list snapshot whose entries carry the composed matrix, colour transform, path/name pointers, clip depth, blend mode, visibility, alpha and text glyph runs, plus the frame's sound events. `radicle_runtime_snapshot_hash` is the deterministic frame hash, and every pointer the snapshot hands back must stay valid until `radicle_runtime_snapshot_destroy`.

`include/fo4/avm2/replay.hpp` and `src/avm2/replay.cpp` add the deterministic replay driver: `ReplayInput` is the timestamped input the host records, `apply_input` maps it onto the runtime's mouse/key/char/wheel dispatch, and `replay` applies each input whose time falls in a frame, advances the movie by a fixed dt, takes one snapshot per frame and collects `snapshot_hash` values. The C ABI `radicle_movie_replay` wraps that so a host can pass a recorded input array, a frame dt and frame count, and read back the frame-hash sequence; `swf_runtime` gained `mouse_move`, `mouse_wheel` and `char_event` so the driver has every event kind. Equal input logs and the same dt sequence must produce equal hash sequences, which is the record/replay shape the issue's acceptance needs.
