Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime.cpp` opens a runtime with host callbacks (the host-call forwarder is checked by a movie whose script calls `ExternalInterface.call` at load), opens a synthetic sprite movie, advances, checks the snapshot entry fields and that the hash changes across frames, runs the same replay log twice and requires identical hash sequences, and rejects an out-of-range input kind. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp` (`FO4_DATA_DIR` gated) opens a `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` Programs movie through the archive path with an archive-backed asset resolver, replays a recorded mouse/key log for 24 frames twice, requires the hash sequences to match, and records asset request/miss counts; if the movie needs a feature that is still missing it skips with the reason instead of failing, so CI reports the remaining gap without turning the branch red. The GardenEngine-side swap and its bindings are still open, along with the seven-program acceptance run.

## Compatibility classes for the Programs corpus (#807 R7)

The Program movies reference engine-provided classes the runtime had no shell for, and constructing one aborted a script before frame 1. `native_compat.cpp` now provides the constructor/property behaviour those classes need: `flash.display::BitmapData` (width/height/transparent/fillColor kept as properties; `rect`/`getRect` return a `flash.geom::Rectangle`; pixel/draw calls are deterministic no-ops returning 0 so time-based drawing code still runs), `flash.display::Bitmap`, `flash.display::FrameLabel`, the `flash.filters` family (`BitmapFilter`, `BlurFilter`, `GlowFilter`, `DropShadowFilter`, `ColorMatrixFilter`; constructor arguments become the AS3-named properties), `flash.ui::Mouse` (hide/show no-ops), and `flash.media::SoundMixer` (static `soundTransform` getter/setter plus `stopAll`). `flash.ui::Keyboard` gained its static constants (letters, numbers, arrows, modifiers, F-keys) and `isDown` returning false because the host owns real key state. The `flash.utils` package functions `getQualifiedClassName`, `getQualifiedSuperclassName` and `getTimer` are also registered under the package namespace, not only as globals.

`DisplayObject` now stores its `filters` array and `bitmapData` value so scripts can set them and the frame snapshot can report them: `SnapshotEntry::filter_count` is hashed with the rest of the frame (and the C ABI `radicle_runtime_entry` gained `filter_count`, ABI 69). That keeps the runtime faithful where it can be and explicitly deterministic where a feature is still a stub.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_compat.cpp` constructs `BitmapData(10,20,true,0)` and reads width/height/transparent back, constructs a `BlurFilter` and reads `blurX`, reads `Keyboard.UP` (38) and calls the package-namespaced `getQualifiedClassName` on `flash.display::Sprite`, and checks that setting filters on a display object reaches the snapshot's filter count. Movies that still need a missing API now fail later and with a clearer reason instead of aborting on class construction.

## DefineSound PCM decode and placed colour transforms (#807 R7/R8)

`include/fo4/avm2/sound_decode.hpp` and `src/avm2/sound_decode.cpp` decode a `SoundResource` into interleaved signed 16-bit samples: uncompressed native-endian 8- and 16-bit (formats 0), little-endian 16-bit (format 3) and SWF ADPCM (format 1, canonical step/index tables, 4096-sample blocks with a per-channel predictor and index header). MP3 is refused rather than guessed, and every truncated body returns false, so the host can tell a decodable sound from an unsupported codec. That closes the DefineSound half of the #807 R7 sound bullet; the runtime still queues Play/Stop events rather than mixing audio itself.

Placed colour transforms are now real. `SwfPlacementRow` carries `has_color_transform` plus multiply/add arrays, the bridge fills them from the PlaceObject colour transform (8.8 fixed converted to multipliers and additive offsets), the runtime applies them to the placed `DisplayObject`, and `build_frame_snapshot` reports them in `SnapshotEntry::color` (alpha multiplier combines with the object's alpha for the entry alpha). A synthetic placement with a colour transform therefore changes the deterministic frame hash, and GardenEngine can tint what it draws instead of ignoring the tag.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_sound_decode.cpp` decodes 16-bit big-endian and 8-bit raw bodies, decodes a hand-built ADPCM block (predictor 0/index 0 then nibbles 0x01,0x23 giving samples 0,0,7), refuses MP3/truncated/empty bodies, and checks a display object's colour transform arrives in the snapshot with the expected multipliers and offsets.

## Display API completeness for the Programs (#807 R7)

The Program census lists display members the runtime did not answer, and one undefined call aborts a script. This batch adds the construction and drawing surface: `flash.display::Graphics` (`beginFill`, `beginGradientFill`, `endFill`, `lineStyle`, `moveTo`, `lineTo`, `curveTo`, `drawRect`, `drawCircle`, `drawRoundRect`, `clear`, `copyFrom`) records each command in a `GraphicsObject` instead of rendering it, and every `DisplayObject` gets a stable `graphics` getter that lazily creates and caches the object so repeated draws target the same command list. `DisplayObject` also gains `getBounds` (a `flash.geom::Rectangle` from the object's transform and size), `hitTest`/`hitTestPoint`/`hitTestObject` (deterministic null/false placeholders until hit-testing is wired to the display list), a `transform` getter/setter that exposes and applies `colorTransform` and `matrix` views of the object's current state, and `focus`/`stageFocusRect` reads. `flash.display::LoaderInfo` is installed and `Loader.contentLoaderInfo`/`loaderInfo` return one instance carrying an `applicationDomain`; `unloadAndStop` is a no-op; `Event.formatToString` produces the AS3-shaped string. That keeps the whole construction-and-drawing prologue of a Program running instead of dying on an undefined call.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_display_api.cpp` draws into a `Shape` through its graphics object (beginFill/lineStyle/moveTo/lineTo/endFill) and calls `getBounds` on the result, reads `movieClip.transform.colorTransform.redMultiplier` as 1.0, checks `Event.formatToString` output contains the type and bubbles values, and checks `Loader.contentLoaderInfo.applicationDomain` is an `ApplicationDomain` instance.

## Phase 7 corpus evidence: AVM1 DoAction in three GFx movies, no LZMA in the Interface archive (#806)

The data-runner test `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp:SwfRealData.InterfaceCorpusDoActionCountAndNoLzmaCompression` scans every movie that `Radicle/tests/real_data_movies.hpp:is_movie` selects (`.swf` and `.gfx`) in `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` and records the counts. On Fallout 4 1.11.240.0 it sees 315 movie entries: 311 `.swf` (all CWS) and 4 `.gfx` (all CFX, zlib-compressed GFx). Zero are ZWS (LZMA). `DoAction` (tag 12) occurs 82 times, all in three `.gfx` files: `Interface\Exported\RaceSex_menu.gfx` 53 (2 top-level, 51 inside DefineSprite), `Interface\Exported\TutorialMenu.gfx` 28 (1 top-level, 27 inside sprites) and `Interface\Exported\SafeZone.gfx` 1 (top-level). `TextEntry.gfx` and every `.swf` have none. The test pins 82 and asserts zero LZMA movies, so a change in either count fails loudly.

The 82 are real tags, not a parser artefact: an independent Python walk of the zlib-inflated CFX bodies (after the 8-byte header) reaches the End tag at exactly `file_length - 8` in all four GFx files, and all 82 tag-12 payloads parse as complete AVM1 action records ending at the payload end. `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:parse_signature` maps CFX to GFx plus zlib and `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:read_swf` inflates it, so the C++ count and the Python count agree.

This reopens the AVM1 `DoAction` question. The earlier conclusion that no shipped movie justifies an AVM1 decoder was wrong, because the three GFx movies above are shipped. The earlier 1.10.984 zero count was not reproduced: no 1.10.984 install was scanned for this change. LZMA (ZWS) read and write now exist as a self-contained codec with no linked library (superseded: see `## Radicle/src/swf/swf_lzma.cpp:lzma_decode_swf and Radicle/src/swf/swf_lzma.cpp:lzma_encode_swf (#806 phase 7, ZWS)`); the Interface movies do not need it.

## Mouse/key state, FrameLabel objects and the missing RegExp class (#807 R7)

Program scripts poll Keyboard.isDown, read mouseX/mouseY and expect currentLabels to hold real
lash.display::FrameLabel instances, so the runtime now tracks that state. DisplayObject stores the
host pointer position and the SWF runtime updates it on the root clip and stage for every mouse
move/down/up; mouseX/mouseY read it instead of a hardcoded zero. Runtime keeps a pressed-key set
that SwfRuntime::key_event updates, and Keyboard.isDown answers from it (the host still owns the
real key state, this only mirrors what the input log delivered). currentLabels builds
FrameLabel instances through the class when it is installed, keeping the labels typed. A minimal
RegExp class (constructor, 	est false, exec null) keeps scripts that only construct or probe one
running, and DisplayObject.loaderInfo returns a LoaderInfo with an pplicationDomain and an empty
parameters object, complementing the Loader getters.

Tests remain the synthetic C ABI/unit suites plus the seven-Program harness; the draft PR #849 now runs
CI on every push so the compile evidence catches up with these changes.

## Duplicate class names across loaded Program movies (#807 R7)

A census of the Program groups (AtomicCommand, Grognak, PipFall, RedMenace, ZetaInvaders and their sibling asset SWFs) shows 24-29 class names repeated across movies, mostly the shared scaleform.clik constants but also common hvr/Holotapes classes. Strict duplicate rejection made a Loader child movie fail as soon as it defined one of those, which would stop every program at its first asset load. src/avm2/runtime_link.cpp:Runtime::build_shells_for_file now treats a repeated fully-qualified class name as an alias: the first definition stays authoritative and the new file's class-index references resolve to it, so the second movie links, its scripts run, and both movies share one class identity the way the Scaleform app domain behaves. A unit test links the same ABC twice and asserts the class count does not grow and the class still resolves.
## Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_characters.hpp:build_character_model (A6 character model, ABI 71)

The character model is one pass over the top-level tags. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_characters.cpp:build_character_model`
records one row per character id a placement can name: the kind (shape 2/22/32/83, morph 46/84, bitmap 6/20/21/35/36/90,
text 11/33, edit text 37, font 10/48/75/91, sprite 39, button 7/34, sound 14, video 60, imported 57/71), the defining
tag index, the drawn bounds for a shape, morph, text or edit-text definition, the pixel size a lossless bitmap carries,
and the names the two name tables attach. The bounds come from the decoder view the tag already holds, so the model
adds no second read of the payload: `SwfTag::shape`, `:morph_shape`, `:bitmap`, `:text`, `:edit_text` and `:font` are
the source, and a raw definition (`DefineButton` 7/34, `DefineFont4` 91, `DefineVideoStream` 60) is named from its
leading UI16 because that is the only field those tags carry before their format-specific body. ImportAssets pairs are
characters too: they enter as kind imported with the source movie and the symbol name, and a placement can name them
exactly like a local definition. `SymbolClass` names are attached first and `ExportAssets` only fills an unnamed id, so
a class name always wins over an export name. Rows are sorted by id, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_characters.cpp:find_character`
is the lookup the C surface uses.

Three conditions are refusals rather than guesses, and a refusal clears the model instead of returning a partial map:
two definitions of one id, a character tag whose payload is shorter than the leading UI16 the model needs, and a
`SymbolClass` or `ExportAssets` id that no definition or import carries. A placement id is not re-validated here: the
display list already treats an unknown character as an omission, and the model only answers "which character is this".
The C ABI adds `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_character_count`, `:radicle_swf_character_at` and
`:radicle_swf_character_by_id` on ABI 71; the model is built once per revision and cached on the handle (a refused
model is cached with its message, so every character getter reports the same refusal), and `radicle_swf_character`
carries the id, kind, flags, defining tag index, twip bounds, bitmap pixel size and the three name pointers. The
regenerated `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp`
carry the new struct, enum and exports; the ABI pin moved to `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSixtySeven`.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_characters.cpp` builds one hand-authored movie carrying every kind, a duplicate-id movie,
an unknown-name-table movie and a truncated-button movie, and pins the kinds, tag indices, bounds, bitmap sizes, sorted
order and every refusal. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_characters.cpp` pins the three exports, the NOT_FOUND path, the
refusal path and that a refused model leaves the other getters usable. `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp` now builds the
model for every shipped Interface movie and records `characters` and `character_model_failures`, so a shipped movie that
defines an id twice or names an unknown id fails the real-data suite. Nothing here was built or run locally; CI is the
first build, and the ABI 71 layout is uncompared against a built probe until then.

## Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_text_edit.hpp:apply_edit_text and the frame-label verbs (A4 + A5 as editing)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_edit_text` now stores the layout block instead of skipping it, so the
decoded `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfEditText` carries every declared tag-37 field: bounds, both flag
bytes, font id and class, height, colour, max length, align/left/right/indent/leading, variable and initial
text. The layout is an optional `SwfEditTextLayout` that is present exactly when the flags2 layout bit is set,
and the signed leading is kept as the 1/20-pixel value the file carries.

Editing is `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_text_edit.hpp:replace_edit_text`, which re-encodes the payload from
the decoded view and hands the bytes to the tag plan through `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_text_edit.hpp:apply_edit_text`.
The re-encode is field-ordered like the decoder and reuses the original id/RECT prefix unless the bounds are
edited, so a text edit keeps every earlier byte at its original value, a colour edit differs in exactly the four
colour bytes, and an unset edit reproduces the payload byte for byte. New text on a field that had no initial
text sets the HasText bit; a bounds edit picks the narrowest RECT that fits the four new coordinates and keeps
every later field value, refusing values that do not fit the 31-bit RECT. A refusal never reaches the plan, and
a plan refusal leaves the movie bytes untouched.

Frame labels are `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_text_edit.hpp:list_frame_labels` on the root timeline
(`timeline_id` 0) or on a `DefineSprite` timeline (its character id), reported in tag order with the 0-based
frame each label sits on. `:rename_frame_label`, `:add_frame_label` and `:remove_frame_label` go through the
tag plan: a root edit replaces, inserts before the requested frame's `ShowFrame`, or removes the label tag; a
sprite edit rebuilds the `DefineSprite` payload and replaces that one tag, because a child index is not a plan
index. Splices reuse the original tag header form and shift the length field only for the edited tag. A name
already used on the same timeline is a refusal, as is an empty name, an out-of-range label or frame, and an id
that is not a `DefineSprite`. Removal needed one addition to `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTagPlan`: a
removal list that refuses the End tag, a duplicate index, or an index that is also replaced, and the `Crt`
plan conversion simply leaves it empty.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_edit_text.cpp` pins the full field read, the byte-identical unset edit, the
text prefix, the four-byte colour diff, the bounds re-encode, and the two refusals;
`Radicle/tests/test_swf_label_edit.cpp` pins root and sprite listing, rename on both timelines, add at a frame,
remove and re-read after `write_swf`, duplicate refusal with the bytes unchanged, and the unknown-timeline and
unreached-frame refusals. `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp` counts `edit_text_tags` and `edit_text_layouts` over
every shipped Interface movie and requires at least one edit-text tag. Nothing here was built or run locally;
CI is the first compiler.

## Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_history.hpp:SwfEditHistory (edit history at ABI 71)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_history.cpp:SwfEditHistory::apply` turns every tag-plan edit into a
`Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_history.hpp:SwfEditCommand` holding the plan and the revision it produced. A
no-op plan is not a command: apply probes the plan on a copy of the current file first and returns success
without touching the history when the plan matches the bytes in force. A command is appended only after the
probe accepts it, and a refused plan leaves `commands_`, the applied prefix, the revision and the file
untouched.

Undo and redo are `Radicle/src/swf/swf_history.cpp:SwfEditHistory::replay`: it always reopens the bytes the
history was opened from and applies the first N commands again, never the edited file, so an undo of a
sequence equals the same sequence applied forward. `replay` builds the new file in a local and commits it
only on success, so a replay refusal leaves the previous state live; the revision advances once per
successful apply, undo or redo. Applying after an undo truncates the redo tail, `undo_count` and
`redo_count` report the two sides, and `write_bytes` serializes the live file.

The C surface adds an opaque `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_history` and the verbs
`:radicle_swf_history_create` (from a movie handle, starting at the bytes that handle serializes),
`:radicle_swf_history_apply`, `:radicle_swf_history_undo`, `:radicle_swf_history_redo`,
`:radicle_swf_history_revision`, `:radicle_swf_history_undo_count`, `:radicle_swf_history_redo_count`,
`:radicle_swf_history_write_bytes` and `:radicle_swf_history_destroy`. Plan indices keep the
`radicle_swf_tag_at` flat-index contract: `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_history.cpp:translate` maps a flat index to
the top-level position the native plan stores and refuses a child index, exactly like `radicle_swf_apply_plan`.
The verbs were added at ABI 70 inside this round before it was ever pushed, so there is still one bump for the
round. The PET branch numbered this surface 67, but 67 to 69 on this lineage are the ABC write side, the runtime
and the AVM2 compatibility classes, so the merge moved it to 70 on this lineage (now 71 after the Papyrus merge, `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION`).
The managed interop was regenerated (3,775 lines) and the layout probe is unchanged because the
history handle is opaque.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_history.cpp` pins command counting, the byte-identified undo/redo sequence, the
forward-vs-undo equality, a refused edit leaving revision/counts/bytes unchanged, the redo-tail truncation,
and a history that never opened. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_history.cpp` pins the same through the C
handle, the revision counter, the flat-index refusal and the missing-argument paths. Nothing here was built
or run locally; CI is the first compiler.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/SwfEditing.cs:SwfFile.ApplyPlan (PET editor read/edit surface)

The managed `SwfFile` partial grows the edit-side surface over ABI 71: `Characters()` reads the character
model (kind, id, defining tag, bounds or bitmap size, name/import), `OpenFrames()` reads timelines and the
per-frame display list with depth, character, name and transforms, `OpenHistory()` returns the replay
history with apply/undo/redo, counts, revision and write-bytes, and `ApplyPlan`/`WriteBytes` expose the
raw tag plan and the current bytes. Each wrapper owns one native handle through a `SafeHandle` and every
non-Ok status becomes a `RadicleException` carrying the Radicle message, so a refusal reaches the caller
verbatim. Tests in `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/SwfEditingTests.cs` use hand-built
movie bytes from `SwfFixtures.Movie()` and pin characters, labels, the frame-0 display list, the
plan/history undo-redo round trip, and the refusal message. Nothing was built or run locally; CI is the
first compiler.
## Radicle/include/fo4/abc/edit.hpp:insert_instruction / delete_instruction (instruction editing)

`Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:insert_instruction` and `:delete_instruction` edit one AVM2 method body
through the existing `decode_code`/`encode_code` pair rather than through a second instruction model: the
body is decoded to `AbcInstruction`s, the edit is applied to that vector, every absolute branch and switch
target is shifted by the inserted or deleted length, exception `from`/`to`/`target` offsets are shifted the
same way, instruction offsets are recomputed, and `encode_code` writes the relative operands back. A target
that names the deleted instruction, or an exception range that begins or ends inside it, is a refusal
(`AbcEditStatus::BranchTargetsDeletedInstruction` / `ExceptionRangeAffected`); an inserted instruction that
carries its own branch or switch is refused too, because its relative operands are meaningless at the new
address.

`Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:verify_and_commit` is the last step of every edit: it decodes the rewritten body,
raises `local_count` to the highest local slot any instruction names when that is above the declared count,
runs `Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_method_flow` with a temporary stack ceiling so a body that needs
more stack can still be measured, then sets `max_stack` to the larger of the declared value and the observed
depth. Any verifier refusal restores the body byte for byte, including `local_count`, `max_stack` and the
exception table, so a refused edit is invisible to the caller. A body with no edit decodes and re-encodes to
its own bytes, which `Radicle/tests/test_abc_edit.cpp` asserts together with a full parse/serialize round
trip.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_edit.cpp` pins the branch shift on insert, the byte-identical revert on
delete, the first-instruction insertion, the non-boundary and non-single-instruction refusals, the deleted
branch target refusal, the exception-range shift and restore, the `local_count` raise for an inserted
local-slot instruction, and the verifier refusal restoring the body. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp` now
inserts and deletes a `nop` at offset 0 of the first body of every shipped Interface ABC block and requires
the code, stack/local counts and exception table to come back byte-identical, recording `edit_roundtrips`
and `edit_mismatches`. Nothing here was built or run locally; CI is the first compiler.
## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex.h:radicle_pex_opcode_name

Exposes `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/opcodes.hpp:pex_op_name` over the 47-entry `Radicle/include/fo4/pex/pex.hpp:PexFile::kOpCodes` table, so GardenEngine and the PluginEditTool can label an instruction byte without carrying their own copy of the names in the same order. The range test is `PexOp::ArrayClear`, the last enumerator of `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/opcodes.hpp:PexOp`, not a literal 46, so the accepted range and the table cannot drift apart inside Radicle. A byte past it is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with `opcode <value> is outside the 0..46 name table` in `radicle_last_error`, and the out-parameters are cleared first: `pex_op_name` answers `op_XX` for those bytes, and a synthesised name is the guess a caller would then treat as a table entry. The copy-out is the `uint8_t**` and `size_t*` pair the rest of this header uses, released with `radicle_free_bytes`; the C ABI has no caller-supplied-buffer convention, so this export does not introduce one. Operand roles stay out, because this header states that the layer names none.

ABI 60 is one above dev's 59, the number the merge with `nomad/dev` took, so this export takes the next free number. The pin is now `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSeventySeven`, which holds both the compiled macro and `radicle_abi_version` at the `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` value. It was `CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSixtyOne` at 61 when `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex_analysis.h:radicle_pex_call_operand_role` raised the number; the merge of `nomad/dev`'s 61 into the SWF branch's 75 moved it to 76, and the name and the pinned value moved together.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_pex.cpp:OpcodeNameMatchesTheTableForEveryTableEntry` round-trips all 47 entries through the C call and compares each with `pex_op_name`. That catches the regression this export exists to remove: an engine-side copy of the table binds its own opcode numbers to the wrong names when Radicle's order or spelling moves. `OpcodeNameRefusesAByteOutsideTheTable` pre-fills the out-parameters with a sentinel and requires both cleared plus the exact message for 47 and 255, so a refused call cannot hand back a stale buffer. `OpcodeNameRequiresItsOutputParameters` covers the null-argument refusal, and `OpcodeNamePinsTheFirstAndLastTableEntries` pins `nop` at 0 and `array_clear` at 46, which fails on a table reordered under a name list that still has 47 entries.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus_source.h:radicle_papyrus_source_summary

Exposes `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/parser.hpp:parse` and `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus_source/summary.hpp:summarize` so an editor can refuse a `.psc` before it launches Bethesda's compiler, without a second parser. The C++ namespace is `fo4::psc`, not `fo4::papyrus_source`. The export is how GardenEngine and the PluginEditTool read the same parse the tests read: it adds no behaviour of its own.

The result is a flat tab-separated row set, the shape `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_quest.h` already uses, released with `radicle_free_string_array`; the array and every row are copies owned by the caller. One documented grammar, in row order:

```
script    <name> <parent> <auto state>
import    <module>
property  <name> <auto 0|1>
state     <path>
function  <name> <state> <native 0|1> <event 0|1>
error     <line> <column> <message>
```

An absent parent, auto state or function state is an empty field, so a function outside any state carries one empty field, its state, between its name and its two flags. A successful parse emits one `script` row first followed by its imports, declared properties, states and functions, and no `error` row. A failed parse emits exactly one `error` row and nothing else, carries the parser's own message and position, and is `RADICLE_STATUS_OK`: a bad file is the answer the caller asked for, not a tool failure, which is the distinction the editor needs. Every field has tab, carriage return, newline and NUL replaced by a space, so a row is always one line whatever the parser's message quotes.

`ScriptSummary::calledFunctions`, `propertiesRead`, `propertiesWritten` and `stateTransitions` are deliberately not rows: they are flow analysis for the runtime consumers, an editor deciding whether a file parses does not read them, and each would multiply the row count for every function. The per-function lists stay unexported for the same reason.

Refusals are separate from parse failures: a null `source`, an empty one, a size above `RADICLE_PAPYRUS_SOURCE_MAX_BYTES` (4 MiB) or a null out-parameter returns `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with `source is required`, `source must not be empty`, `source size <n> is above the 4194304-byte cap` or `out_rows and out_count are required`, and every out-parameter is cleared first. The cap is tested before the buffer is read, so a caller whose size disagrees with its buffer cannot make this layer read past it. Nothing else in the C ABI imports the Papyrus source parser, so this export also sets the first bound on what a caller may hand it.

Export 2 adds no ABI number of its own: it ships at 60, the number export 1 set on this branch (one above dev's 59).

The C ABI cases live in `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_papyrus_source.cpp` rather than the parser's own file, which is at the 750-line guard. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_papyrus_source.cpp:CApiSummaryReportsTheFieldsAnEditorNeeds` pins the exact row set for a script with an import, an auto property, an auto-read-only property, an event, a global function, a state and a state function, so a dropped field, a changed flag order or a reordered row kind fails it - the editor's row reader depends on all three. `CApiSummaryReportsAParseFailureAsARow` requires a lexer failure at line 2 column 11 to come back as one `error` row with status OK, which catches the regression this export exists to prevent: a syntax error reported as a tool error, which the caller cannot tell from a broken library. `CApiSummaryRefusesMissingEmptyAndOversizedSources` pre-fills both out-parameters, requires them cleared, and passes a short buffer with a size above the cap, so it also fails if the cap check ever moves after the read. `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_source_real.cpp:CApiSummaryMatchesTheParserOnEveryCorpusScript` runs on the `FO4_PSC_CORPUS` corpus and requires the C rows to agree with a direct parse for every file: the `script` row field for field or the `error` row's line and column, and the row count to equal one plus the imports, declared properties, states and functions, so a row kind dropped for some script the unit case never builds fails here. With `FO4_PSC_CORPUS` unset it reads `testdata/papyrus` instead, which holds four `.psc` files, so the case runs in a normal test build too.
## Radicle/tests/test_pex_analysis_real.cpp

`load_vanilla_scripts` resolves the real script set and keeps the winners whose container is an official archive, meaning a `.ba2` whose file name starts with `fallout4` or `dlc`, so the pinned totals below are official-only and do not move when Creation Club or mod archives are added or removed; that keeps 10271 of the 10331 resolved winners. The relations that must hold for any Data folder are asserted over the full set by `Radicle/tests/test_script_set_real.cpp:ScriptSetReal.VanillaAndDlcArchivesResolveToAWinnerSet` (winners equal distinct names, and `replaced` plus the winner count equals the candidate count). The three tests below share that load and each states the regression it catches.

`OfficialScriptsReportEveryCallSite` builds one `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:build_call_graph` over the loaded files and measures 30474 functions (30385 state functions and 89 property handlers), 122001 call sites, 39084 native targets, 88055 resolved, 33946 unresolved, 25680 roots, and 28 call sites whose caller slot is `PropertyRead` or `PropertyWrite`. The two handler numbers are the regression guard for #823: before it, property handler bodies were skipped and both were zero.

`OfficialScriptsResolveEveryParentChain` runs `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/parent_chain.cpp:validate_parent_chains` with no seed types and measures zero `MissingParent`, zero `Cycle` and zero `TooDeep` over 10271 objects. That is the vanilla answer, not an assumption: a reader that damaged a `parentClassName` or dropped an object would produce findings here. The engine passes `PapyrusEventContract` seeds instead, and that configuration is not measured here.

`ParentCallsDeclaredAboveTheImmediateParentStayUnresolved` measures what the resolution rule costs. Of the 33946 unresolved calls, 4 are `callparent` sites whose function is declared two or more parents up: `DLC01:WorkshopRobotScript.SetLocRefType`, two sites, three parents up on `ObjectReference`; and `DLC03:WorkshopSettlementDefendScript.Startup`, two parents up on `MinRecruitQuestScript`. The test prints three examples and asserts the count, so a change to the rule is visible in the diff of this number. `build_call_graph` is unchanged on this branch: the engine's `NativeCallSiteCensus.Collect` walks the parent chain (`current = owner.Parent`) and Radicle does not, and closing that gap is a decision for the lead.

The totals above were first estimated with a throwaway Python PEX reader outside the repo that mirrors `Radicle/src/pex/pex.cpp` and `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp`, then confirmed by a Release `fo4_tests` run with `FO4_DATA_DIR` pointing at a retail `Data` folder: every number matched the mirror exactly. The same run measured 21.3 s and a sampled 361 MB peak working set for the three tests together, which is the largest of the three real-data groups after `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_writer_real.cpp:VmadReadReal`.

## Radicle/tests/test_vmad_writer_real.cpp:VmadReadReal

`Fallout4EsmCountsAndStructArraysMatchTheCppReader` reads `Fallout4.esm` twice: once through `Radicle/src/schema/vmad.cpp:read_vmad_scripts` over a `fo4::read_plugin_file` pass, and once through `Radicle/src/c_api_vmad_read.cpp:radicle_record_vmad_scripts` over every record the loaded `radicle_env` holds. Both passes count scripts, properties, array properties (types 11 to 15 and 17), struct properties (type 7) and struct-array properties (type 17); the test asserts the two agree first, then asserts the measured totals from a Release run with `FO4_DATA_DIR` set: 13697 VMAD subrecords, 12272 scripts, 25231 properties, 1535 array properties, 10 struct properties, 319 struct-array properties, no script reported `unsupported`, and no record was refused. Those totals are the C++ reader's, not the mirror's: the throwaway Python VMAD reader these notes first quoted under-counted by 382 VMAD subrecords and 493 scripts, and the C++ reader is the truth. The refusal answer is a measured zero, not an untested path: `radicle_record_vmad_scripts` was run over every record of all seven official masters (Fallout4.esm, DLCRobot.esm, DLCworkshop01.esm, DLCCoast.esm, DLCworkshop02.esm, DLCworkshop03.esm, DLCNukaWorld.esm), 20173 records carry a VMAD and every one decoded, so no record has a shape this reader refuses on this data. The refusal and truncation paths are covered by the synthetic fixtures in `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_vmad_read.cpp`, and the counter stays so that a Data folder with a truncated payload reports a count instead of aborting the read. Struct arrays are not only counted: `Fallout4.esm:0x000920F1` (`ACTI`, `DN015SampleActivator`) carries `Samples` as six object-bearing structs, so the property's `declared_element_count` is 6 and `radicle_vmad_element_count` is 12. The reader pass runs in a scope that ends before the environment is loaded, so the 330 MB plugin is never held twice at peak.

The regression it catches is a divergence between the C read ABI and the C++ decoder on real data: an ABI that stopped early on a struct array, miscounted a declared element count, or reported a readable record as unsupported would break the equality before any total is compared. A Release run takes 8.4 s and samples a 1.75 GB peak working set, because the loaded environment holds the whole 330 MB plugin; that is this test's floor, since the parse it compares against is released before the environment loads. `Radicle/tests/test_vmad_writer_real.cpp:VmadWriterOfficial` is larger at 2.99 GB on `Fallout4.esm`, so four of those in parallel would need about 12 GB. Restructuring that test to release the source plugin before it reparses the saved bytes, and comparing untouched records against the retained original buffer instead of the plugin, did not help: it measured 3.18 GB, and 3.19 GB with an added `_heapmin()`, so the peak is inside the parse and write phase and not the coexistence of the two plugins. The change was reverted. What remains is a process-level answer: run these two tests in a serial step, or point the write-back check at a smaller official master.
## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_script_set.h:radicle_script_set_resolve — GardenEngine port for ABI 55 and 56

GardenEngine re-pins to `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` 55 (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h`), which carries the script set, and 56, which carries the VMAD read and the pex analysis; #823 stacks on #822, so one re-pin to 56 covers both, and this branch changes no header, struct or export beyond those two numbers. Exports to bind: `radicle_script_set_resolve`, `radicle_script_set_count`, `radicle_script_set_get`, `radicle_script_set_read` and `radicle_script_set_destroy` with the `radicle_script_set_candidate` and `radicle_script_set_winner` structs (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_script_set.h`); `radicle_assets_root_count` (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_env.h:545`), which supplies the root count the resolver needs; `radicle_pex_callgraph_build`, `radicle_pex_callgraph_destroy`, `radicle_pex_callgraph_totals`, `radicle_pex_callgraph_call_count`, `radicle_pex_callgraph_call`, `radicle_pex_callgraph_unresolved_count` and `radicle_pex_callgraph_unresolved` with `radicle_pex_call_site`, `radicle_pex_call_totals`, `radicle_pex_call_kind` and `radicle_pex_function_slot`; `radicle_pex_validate_parent_chains` with `radicle_pex_chain_report`, `radicle_pex_chain_problem`, `radicle_pex_chain_finding`, `radicle_pex_chain_report_checked`, `radicle_pex_chain_report_count`, `radicle_pex_chain_report_get`, `radicle_pex_chain_report_name` and `radicle_pex_chain_report_destroy` (both in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex_analysis.h`); and `radicle_record_vmad_scripts`, `radicle_vmad_script_count`, `radicle_vmad_scripts_script`, `radicle_vmad_scripts_property`, `radicle_vmad_element_count`, `radicle_vmad_scripts_element` and `radicle_vmad_scripts_destroy` with `radicle_vmad_script`, `radicle_vmad_property`, `radicle_vmad_element` and `radicle_vmad_value_kind` (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_vmad.h`). The generated bindings (`Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs:2241`) carry `CompiledAbiVersion = 56u` and the raw entry points; there is no managed wrapper for the script set, the call graph, the chain report or the VMAD read yet, so the engine calls `RadicleNative` directly or adds one.

Two resolve APIs coexist and are not interchangeable. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex.h:radicle_script_resolve` takes caller-built candidates and returns winners by candidate index through `radicle_script_candidate` and `radicle_script_winner`. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_script_set.h:radicle_script_set_resolve` takes a `radicle_assets` handle, enumerates `Scripts/**.pex` itself and returns `radicle_script_set_candidate` and `radicle_script_set_winner` (fields `path`, `container`, `load_index`, `location`); the prefix exists because both headers reach `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py`, as the note under the ABI 55 heading explains. The engine wants the assets-handle version, because that is the one that owns the enumeration and the name rules.

`ScriptCachePrecedence` (`ScriptCachePrecedence.cs:23` `NormalizeName`, `:38` `Compare`, `:62` `Resolve`) is today's owner of the precedence rule, and `ScriptCacheBuilder.Build` (`ScriptCacheBuilder.cs:37`) drives it before converting payloads. `radicle_script_set_resolve` produces the same total order and reports `replaced` per winner, which is the `ReplacedCount` the builder sums today. Three differences have to be absorbed. `NormalizeName` only trims a leading `/` and the extension, while the Radicle name is stripped of `scripts/` and `.pex` after lowercasing, so the engine's archive-side candidates must already be `Scripts/`-relative; the code that builds them is not in the copy read here and stays unknown. The safe-name refusal documented under `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/script_set.cpp:script_name_from_entry` drops a candidate the engine would keep, which the vanilla set never reaches but a mod can. And `replaced` is a `uint32_t` count, not a list, so reporting which containers lost means comparing `radicle_script_set_candidate` rows.

`NativeCallSiteCensus` (`Census/NativeCallSiteCensus.cs:111` `Collect`, `:168` `Run`) is today's owner of call-site counting, and `build_call_graph` is not a drop-in replacement for it. The census walks the parent chain to find the declaration and attributes a method site through `MethodCallContract` to the receiver type, while Radicle resolves one object and one function per site with the rule the `build_call_graph` note records, reporting each site's `PexFunctionSlot` caller (a getter or setter body is `PropertyRead` or `PropertyWrite`, which matches the census walking every `PapyrusScript.Functions` entry). On the official scripts that is 33946 unresolved of 122001 calls, 4 of them `callparent` sites whose function is declared a grandparent or higher: `DLC01:WorkshopRobotScript.SetLocRefType`, two sites, three parents up on `ObjectReference`; and `DLC03:WorkshopSettlementDefendScript.Startup`, two parents up on `MinRecruitQuestScript`. So `unresolved_count` and `root_count` from this ABI must not be read as the census's numbers until the resolution rule gains the parent walk, and `native_count` is not the census's per-native breakdown.

`validate_parent_chains` replaces the chain walk `LoadOrderAcceptance` owns in the engine, and it takes the seed types from the caller (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex_analysis.h:91`) because Radicle has no native-class list of its own; the engine passes `PapyrusEventContract`'s seeds. Lookup stops at the first object with a name, while `build_call_graph` keeps scanning later files when the first same-named object lacks the function, so the two disagree on a set that defines one script name twice. Measured over the official scripts, the report holds no finding of any kind, so seeds only matter for the engine's extension scripts.

VMAD read: names are Windows-1252 bytes converted to UTF-8, while string values are UTF-8 and are returned unchanged (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_vmad.h`); a property the decoder cannot read is not an error — its script reports `unsupported` and carries no rows for it, so a script must be read as incomplete rather than as empty. A struct array counts structs in `declared_element_count` and members in `element_total`, so a struct with no members contributes no row. Measured on `Fallout4.esm`: 13697 VMAD subrecords, 12272 scripts, 25231 properties, 1535 array properties, 10 struct properties, 319 struct-array properties.

Where the engine-side reading came from: this repository holds no GardenEngine checkout, and a search of the worktree for `ScriptCachePrecedence` and `NativeCallSiteCensus` finds only these notes. The code was read from the `OpenCw.Papyrus` copy left in the #352 scratchpad (`scratchpad/ge352/opencw/OpenCw.Papyrus`: `ScriptCachePrecedence.cs`, `ScriptCacheBuilder.cs`, `ScriptSourceCandidate.cs`, `Census/NativeCallSiteCensus.cs`), which is the copy these notes already cite. Not in that copy, and therefore unknown here: the archive-side candidate enumeration and whatever strips `Scripts/` for it, `ScriptLibrary`, `MethodCallContract`, `PapyrusEventContract` and `LoadOrderAcceptance`. Those need one read against the live checkout before the port.

## SWF plan review fixes (GT-806 cpp)

- `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:apply_tag_plan`: removals are validated against the original count (End, duplicate, replaced target all refused) and the rebuilt stream keeps inserts at their before-index; the stray closing brace that broke the TU was removed.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_history.cpp:translate`: the flat-to-top-level map is built from `history.file()` on every call, so the map can never go stale after an insert or removal; removals resolve through the same map as replacements and insertions.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_history.cpp:SwfEditHistory::apply`: the redo tail is moved into a local before truncation and copied back on a refused replay, so a refused edit keeps every redo command.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_characters.cpp:character_model`: `cache.built` is set after `build_character_model` returns, so a throw leaves the cache unbuilt.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_characters.cpp:flat_index_of_root`: `radicle_swf_character.tag_index` is the flat index that `radicle_swf_tag_at` reports; the model keeps top-level positions internally.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_characters.cpp:apply_name`: a name-table entry for id 0 or for an undefined id names nothing and does not refuse the model.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_text_edit.cpp:rename_frame_label`: bytes after the first NUL of the original FrameLabel payload (the named-anchor flag) are kept.
- `Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:required_local_count`: `hasnext2` contributes both local-register operands.

## Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:refresh_body_limits and Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:verify_and_commit (#806 phase 6, limits)

`refresh_body_limits` re-measures one body with the same routine the insert and delete edits end in, `verify_and_commit`. `local_count` is raised to the highest local slot the body names (`required_local_count`), and `max_stack` is raised to the depth `Radicle/src/abc/abc_stack.cpp:verify_stack` observes over the reachable control-flow graph. The declared value is kept when it is already larger, so a limit is only ever raised. This is the policy the insert and delete edits already had, and it means an unedited vanilla body keeps its bytes. No second stack-effect model was written: `Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_method_flow` is the stack-effect pass, and it refuses a branch merge with mismatched depths, a conflicting handler entry, an underflow and an unmodelled opcode instead of guessing. A refusal restores the body byte for byte and returns `AbcEditStatus::VerifierRefused`.

`Radicle/src/c_api_swf_abc_write.cpp:refresh_changed_bodies` runs it on the bodies of a text edit whose code bytes differ from the block the handle holds. Untouched bodies are not re-measured, so a text edit to one body does not depend on the verifier accepting another body.

## Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:replace_instruction (#806 phase 6)

`replace_instruction` swaps the instruction that starts at an offset for one branch-free instruction. A branch or exception offset equal to the replaced offset keeps naming the new instruction, and an offset at or past the end of the old instruction moves by the length change (`shift_code_targets` and `shift_exceptions`, both with boundary `offset + old_length`). Unlike `delete_instruction`, a branch that targets the replaced instruction is not a refusal, because the replacement takes over that target. A branch or switch inserted this way is refused by `decode_inserted`, and an offset that is not an instruction start is `NotAnInstructionBoundary`.

`insert_instruction`, `delete_instruction` and `replace_instruction` share `index_at`, `decode_inserted` and the two shift helpers; the insert and delete shifts do the same arithmetic as before, with the boundary and signed delta now explicit.

## Radicle/src/c_api_swf_abc_write.cpp:apply_instruction_edit (#806 phase 6, C ABI)

`radicle_swf_abc_insert_instruction` and `radicle_swf_abc_replace_instruction` assemble the text with `Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:assemble_instruction_text` (a text failure is `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR` with its message), apply the edit to a copy of the block's `AbcFile`, and hand the serialized block to `apply_file`. `apply_file` is the plan path `radicle_swf_abc_apply_text` already used, so the rewrite goes through `radicle_swf_apply_plan`, the revision moves only for a changed block, and `radicle_swf_write_bytes` persists it. An edit refusal is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with the edit's message, and the handle is unchanged. `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` moved to 72 (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h`), and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` was regenerated with `tools/generate_interop.py`. No managed wrapper was added; the two entries are raw `RadicleNative` calls.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_edit.cpp` pins the refresh cases (a declared `max_stack` of 1 raised to 2 by hand-counted pushes, a declared 4 kept, `local_count` 1 raised to 6 by `getlocal 5`, a depth-mismatched branch refused and restored) and the replace cases (a target at the replaced offset kept, a later target moved from 5 to 6 with its relative operand rewritten to 2, branch, bad-length and non-boundary refusals, and verifier refusal restoring the body). `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_edit.cpp` covers insert, replace and refusal through the C ABI on the synthetic DoABC2 block, including the unchanged revision and text after refusals.

Still open after phase 6: new strings still need explicit pool lines because automatic interning is not done; the C ABI exposes instruction edits and whole-block text edits only, not a history-wrapped instruction edit; and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:build_abc_views` takes a `DoABC` (72) payload as raw ABC, as the swf reader does, and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_abc_write.cpp:apply_file` writes it back without a header, so a DoABC-tagged block round-trips through the C ABI (see the DoABC (72) layout note). The Interface blocks the phase 5 real-data test walks are DoABC2, so this has not been observed on real data.

## Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/domain.hpp:ApplicationDomainObject (#807 R7 application domain slice)

Application domains are a parent chain plus a per-file owner. `Radicle/src/avm2/runtime.cpp:Runtime::add_file` records the domain a file is loaded into (null meaning the root domain); `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfRuntime::create` passes its `domain` argument through, and `Radicle/src/avm2/native_net.cpp:loader_load` takes it from `context_domain`, which reads `applicationDomain` off a LoaderContext, so a Loader with a context loads its movie into that domain and a Loader without one loads into the root. `Radicle/src/avm2/domain.cpp:Runtime::find_domain_definition` answers `getDefinition` and `hasDefinition`: a builtin (no file) is visible everywhere, and any other class is visible only from the domain that owns its file or from a descendant of that domain. The root is the top of every chain, so a root-owned file is visible only from a chain that ends at the root. `Radicle/src/avm2/domain.cpp:Runtime::current_domain` creates the root lazily, and `Radicle/src/avm2/native_net.cpp:app_domain_construct` defaults a new domain's parent to it.

Known gaps: `getlex` still resolves through the runtime-wide class table, so a class from a child domain is reachable from root script by name. Duplicate class names alias the first definition (see the duplicate-class note above), so a child cannot shadow a parent class. `getDefinition` returns null instead of throwing ReferenceError. The default for a Loader with no context is the root domain (the conservative choice that keeps the pre-R7 global lookup working); Flash may default to a child domain, which was not verified here. `new LoaderContext(false, domain)` goes through the generic `Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp` instance_construct and ignores its arguments, so only `ctx.applicationDomain = d` takes effect and the constructor form loads into the root. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_compat.cpp:make_loader_info` always reports the root domain on `contentLoaderInfo.applicationDomain`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/host.hpp:HostBridge::install_function (#807 R7 host function registry)

`HostBridge::call_host` tries a host-installed named function first (`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/host.hpp:HostBridge::install_function`), then falls back to the unnamed `HostCallbacks::host_call` hook. `HostBridge::available` backs `ExternalInterface.available` so a host that only installs named functions still reports available. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_net.cpp:ext_add_callback` stores the script Function in `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/runtime.hpp:Runtime::set_external_callback`; the host reads it with `Runtime::external_callback` and invokes it through `Interpreter::call_function`. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain.cpp`.
## Radicle/src/swf/swf_lzma.cpp:lzma_decode_swf and Radicle/src/swf/swf_lzma.cpp:lzma_encode_swf (#806 phase 7, ZWS)

No LZMA library is vendored or linked, so this TU is a self-contained LZMA codec. `lzma_decode_swf` takes the 5 LZMA property bytes followed by the raw stream and decodes exactly `out_size` bytes (the declared FileLength minus 8), because a ZWS stream normally has no end marker; an end marker before `out_size` is refused. The decoder implements literals, matched literals, simple matches and all four rep forms, following the LZMA specification's state machine. Input bytes past the end read as zero and are counted; more than `kMaxOverrun` (5) overruns fail the decode, which covers the encoder's 5-byte flush and no more.

`lzma_encode_swf` writes properties `0x5D` (lc=3, lp=0, pb=2), a 16 MiB dictionary, and a stream of literals, simple matches found through a 3-byte hash of the most recent occurrence, and rep0 long matches. It never emits rep1..rep3 or short reps, so those decoder paths are checked only against the spec, not by a round trip.

Container layout (`Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:read_swf`, `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:write_swf`): `ZWS`, version, UI32 FileLength, UI32 compressed length (written as the byte count of properties plus stream), then the properties and stream from byte 12. The reader ignores the compressed length field. The layout was recalled from the SWF specification, not checked against a spec copy or a real ZWS file, since neither is in this tree and the shipped Interface corpus has no ZWS movie. The compressed-length semantics are the first thing to verify on a real movie.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:write_swf` reuses `source_compressed_body` only when the requested compression equals the one the movie was read with, so an unchanged ZWS movie round-trips byte-exactly and a CWS source written as ZWS never carries zlib bytes under a ZWS signature. A GFx movie with LZMA throws, because GFX has no LZMA signature.

C ABI: `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:map_swf_status` has no `unsupported_compression` case, because nothing produces that `SwfStatus` any more (`read_swf` no longer returns it), so `radicle_swf_open_bytes` (through `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:open_from_bytes`) opens ZWS movies and `radicle_swf_info.compression` reports 2. `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` moved to 73 (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h`) and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` was regenerated with `tools/generate_interop.py`; the only changed line is `CompiledAbiVersion`.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_lzma.cpp` checks the ZWS header fields (signature, FileLength, compressed length, props byte 0x5D, dictionary bytes 00 00 00 01, leading range-coder byte 0), a byte-exact round trip of an unchanged movie, a changed body re-encoded and read back, decompress failures for a stream with no bytes after the properties, bad properties byte 0xE1 and a non-zero leading range byte, and the GFx refusal. `Radicle/tests/test_swf.cpp:SwfContainerTest.ReportsZwsWithoutAValidStreamAsDecompressFailure` replaces the old "ZWS is unsupported" assertion.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload SoundStreamHead (#806 phase 7, sound)

Tags 18 and 45 decode into `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfSoundStreamHead`: the packed playback byte keeps its reserved nibble, and the stream byte gives compression, rate, size and type. The UI16 sample count is followed by an SI16 latency seek only when compression is 2 (MP3). Any other length is `malformed_tag`, so the raw payload is kept. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:encode_sound_stream_head` rebuilds the bytes from the struct; `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:encode_define_sound` does the same for the DefineSound header, taking the sample bytes from the caller because `SwfSound` stores only their length.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_sound.cpp` covers a DefineSound payload rebuilt byte-exactly, a PCM stream head with reserved bits 0xA kept, an MP3 stream head with latency -1, and an MP3 head without its latency refused as malformed with the raw payload kept.

## Phase 7 open items (#806)

Font glyph outline editing (item 2 of the phase-7 brief) is closed by Phase 8 below: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_glyph.cpp:read_glyph_shapes` decodes each glyph SHAPE, `Radicle/src/swf/swf_glyph_edit.cpp:replace_glyph_payload` validates a replacement and rebuilds the offset table and code-table offset, and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_art.cpp:radicle_swf_font_replace_glyph` is the C verb. The LZMA codec is covered by the notes above; the AVM1 DoAction question is reopened by the Phase 7 corpus evidence note (`Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp:SwfRealData.InterfaceCorpusDoActionCountAndNoLzmaCompression`).

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_b.inc:k_callproperty returns the owning receiver (#807 CI fix)

`Interpreter::call_property` passes the method `this` as `borrowed_object`, a `shared_ptr` with a no-op deleter. A native such as `Array.sort` or `Array.reverse` returns `self`, so the pushed result was a non-owning alias of the receiver. When the receiver lived only on the operand stack (`newarray` then `callproperty sort`), the owning `receiver` local died at the end of the opcode and the next `getproperty` or `callproperty join` read a freed array, giving `undefined` or "avm2 value is not an object". The opcode now pushes the owning `receiver` whenever the result object is the same pointer. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_builtins.cpp:Avm2Builtins.ArraySortOrdersNumericElementsByText` and `ArraySortThenJoinShowsTheOrder`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfRuntime::create next_script_ (#807 CI fix)

`next_script_` started at 0, so a movie created inside a runtime that already had linked scripts re-ran them. `Loader.load` runs from inside script 0, so the loader re-entered the running initializer, recursed and overflowed the stack (segfault in `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain.cpp` LoaderContextDomainReceivesTheSecondMovieDefinitions and LoaderWithoutAContextLoadsIntoTheCurrentDomain). `create` now starts at `runtime.scripts().size()`, so only scripts linked from the movie's own ABC blocks run.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_document_class.cpp:document_class_abc (#807 CI fix)

The constructor body did run once the document class constructor was bound to its ABC file; the test ABC simply had no "yes" string, so `pushstring 4` stored the property name "documentReady". The pool now holds "yes" at index 5 and the constructor pushes it.
## Phase 8: DefineFont glyph shapes (#806)

- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_glyph.cpp:read_glyph_shapes` decodes every glyph SHAPE from the offset table. A glyph SHAPE has a NumFillBits/NumLineBits nibble header and no style table, so the decoder seeds one implicit fill (fill style 1, the text colour) to pass the shared `read_shape_records` bound check. A NewStyles block that adds fill or line entries is refused because the SHAPE has no style table. An empty NewStyles block adds nothing, so the bounds check cannot see it; it is accepted and dropped on re-encode because `read_shape_records` does not expose the flag. All glyphs of one font share one `ShapeRecordCounts` budget, and any unreadable glyph clears `font.glyphs` while the tag still decodes with its codes and layout.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_text.cpp:decode_text_tag` now stores the DefineFont (tag 10) offsets and shapes, and keeps the layout bounds and kerning pairs that it used to skip, so the font can be re-encoded.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:encode_glyph_shape` writes the canonical SHAPE: each field takes its minimal width, a MoveTo directly followed by a StyleChange is one record, a straight edge with one zero delta is written as vertical or horizontal, and an empty style change writes fill0 as zero so it does not end the shape. A source glyph that uses a non-minimal width, an explicit zero style field or a separate MoveTo record will re-encode to different bytes; the unchanged-font test uses canonical bytes only.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:encode_define_font` recomputes the offset table and the code-table offset from the glyph order, so glyph shapes must be stored in index order. Every DefineFont2/3 writes the code table (UI8 codes unless wide, DefineFont3 always wide) and its CodeTableOffset; HasLayout only gates the metrics, bounds and kerning. Kerning codes use the same UI8/UI16 width as the code table, then SI16 adjustments, matching `swf_text.cpp:decode_text_tag`.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_glyph_edit.cpp:replace_glyph_payload` builds the replacement payload and refuses a shape whose style changes name a fill style above 1 or any line style (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_glyph_edit.cpp:styles_are_in_range`). The decoder seeds exactly fill style 1 and an empty line list, so such a glyph would re-read as unreadable and clear the font's glyphs. The result is the existing bool plus message, with an empty payload on refusal, not a numeric code. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_glyph.cpp:RefusesStyleReferencesOutsideTheImplicitStyleLists`. The C verb `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_art.cpp:radicle_swf_font_replace_glyph` applies it through `radicle_swf_apply_plan`, so the revision and view rebuild stay in one path.
- The ABI moved to 74 for the three glyph getters and the replace verb; `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` regenerated `RadicleNative.g.cs` and `abi_layout_probe.cpp`.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_art.cpp:to_shape_record` rejects a negative record kind as well as one above CURVED_EDGE, because the C enum is signed on the C# side.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_glyph.cpp:kFont2Payload` is the hand-derived DefineFont2 with flags 0x84 (layout and wide codes), two empty glyphs (`00 00`), table start 7, glyph offsets 6 and 8, CodeTableOffset 10, shapes at 13..16, codes 41 00 42 00 at 17, ascent 800 (20 03), descent 200 (C8 00), leading -50 (CE FF), advances 512 and 256 (00 02 00 01), two zero RECTs (00 00), kerning count 0 (00 00): 35 bytes.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_glyph.cpp:kFont2ReplacedPayload` replaces glyph 0 with style fill1 plus edge x=8: the 26 bits `0001001 1100110001000 000000` after the header give `10 13 98 80 00`; offsets become 6, 11, CodeTableOffset 13, total 38 bytes.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_glyph.cpp:kFont3Payload` is the hand-derived DefineFont3 with flags 0x80, one glyph, offsets 4 and 6, shape `00 00`, code `41 00`, six zero metric bytes, advance 10240 (00 28), zero RECT (00), kerning count 1, and the pair 41 00 42 00 FE FF (adjustment -2): 32 bytes.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_glyph.cpp:EncodesDefineFont2WithoutLayoutAndZeroGlyphs` expects `03 00 08 00 00 00 00 04 00 00 00`: zero glyphs, CodeTableOffset 4 pointing exactly at the end of the tag, which `decode_text_tag` accepts because its check is `> data.size()`.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_glyph.cpp:UnreadableGlyphKeepsTheFontDecodedWithoutGlyphs` changes the first offset of `kFont3Payload` to 0x20, so the glyph starts at 39 in a 32-byte tag; the font still decodes with codes and layout and `replace_glyph_payload` refuses it.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_glyph.cpp:kShapeBytes` was re-derived bit by bit: header 0x10, then 67 record bits (MoveTo 4,4 with fill1; edges 8,0 horizontal; 0,8 vertical; -8,-8 diagonal; six zero end bits) padded to 9 bytes.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp:font2_payload` and `font3_payload` were rewritten to real DefineFont2 and DefineFont3 layouts (31 and 29 bytes); the old fixtures pointed past the end of their tags.
- `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_glyph.cpp:ReplacesGlyphShapeAndRebuildsTheView` covers the four C verbs against a DefineFont tag at index 0.
## Phase 9: DefineText/DefineText2 glyph records (#806)

- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_text.cpp:decode_text_records` now fills `SwfText::records` instead of only counting. Each record is a TEXTRECORD read in spec order: flags byte (bit 7 must be 1, bits 4-6 ignored, bit 3 HasFont, bit 2 HasColor, bit 1 HasYOffset, bit 0 HasXOffset), then FontID u16, colour (RGB, or RGBA for DefineText2), XOffset s16, YOffset s16, TextHeight u16, GlyphCount u8, then GlyphCount entries of GlyphBits-wide index and AdvanceBits signed advance, bit-packed and byte-aligned at the record end. A flags byte of 0 terminates the list; running out of data before it is malformed.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfTextRecord` keeps each optional field as present in the record. A DefineText RGB colour is stored as `0xFF000000 | rgb` (alpha 0xFF); DefineText2 keeps its alpha byte in bits 24-31, matching `swf_tags.cpp:decode_edit_text`.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfText` keeps `record_count` and `glyph_count`, which are set from `records` (record count and summed glyph count) only on success.
- `Radicle/src/swf/swf_text.cpp:decode_text_tag` still assigns `out_tag.text` only when the whole decode succeeds, so a malformed text tag keeps its payload and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload` leaves `.text` unset. `write_swf` re-emits the stored payload, so a malformed text tag is byte-identical on the way out.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_text_glyph.cpp:DecodesDefineTextRecordsWithOpaqueRgbColour` uses a hand-derived DefineText payload: header `07 00 00 00 04 08`, record 1 flags 0x8D (font 3, RGB 11 22 33, XOffset -10, height 240, two glyphs (1,10) and (2,-3) packed into 3 bytes), record 2 flags 0x82 (YOffset -4, zero glyphs), terminator 00.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_text_glyph.cpp:DecodesDefineTextRecordWithBothOffsetFlags` uses flags 0x83 (HasYOffset and HasXOffset with the type bit): X 6, Y -8, no font, colour, height or glyphs. `Radicle/tests/test_swf_text_glyph.cpp:WritesAnEditedDefineTextBackWithItsOffsets` replaces the payload through `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:replace_tag_payload` with X 12 and Y -2, writes the movie and reads it back, checking the new payload and offsets; the unchanged movie must also write back byte-identical.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_text_glyph.cpp:DecodesDefineText2RgbaColourAndNegativeAdvance` checks the RGBA path (alpha 0x80) and a 6-bit index with a 7-bit advance of -20 (`0001011101100` padded to `17 60`).
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_text_glyph.cpp:RejectsMalformedRecordsAndKeepsThePayload` covers a missing terminator (both tags), a clear type bit, and glyph entries cut short. It checks the status, the kept payload, the unset `.text` and the byte-identical `write_swf`.
- The DefineText colour-cut and glyph-cut cases in `Radicle/tests/test_swf_tags.cpp` (the malformed table) and the record and glyph counts in `CountsTextRecordsAndGlyphEntries` still hold with the new reader.

## R8 slice: LoaderContext domain, contentLoaderInfo domain and display snapshot hash (#807 R8)

This closes the two R7 gaps named in the `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/domain.hpp:ApplicationDomainObject` note. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_net.cpp:loader_context_construct` is the constructor of LoaderContext (native id `loader_context_construct`, appended at the end of `Radicle/src/avm2/native_ids.hpp:native::Id`). It stores argument 1 as the `applicationDomain` property, or null when the argument is not an object, so `Radicle/src/avm2/native_net.cpp:context_domain` reads the constructor form the same way it reads `ctx.applicationDomain = d`. No C ABI change.

`Radicle/src/avm2/native_net.cpp:loader_load` records the context domain on `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/net.hpp:LoaderObject::domain`. A null value means the root domain, the same meaning a null domain has in `Radicle/src/avm2/runtime.cpp:Runtime::add_file`. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_compat.cpp:make_loader_info` takes that domain and falls back to `Runtime::current_domain` when it is null. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_compat.cpp:loader_content_loader_info` passes the loader's domain, and `Radicle/src/avm2/native_compat.cpp:display_loader_info` passes null. Fixed (#807 R8 loaderInfo identity): the cache used to be a dynamic `loaderInfo` property, but `loaderInfo` is a getter trait on DisplayObject and Loader, so `Radicle/src/avm2/object.cpp:Object::write_value` refused the write (accessor kind) and every read built a new LoaderInfo. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/net.hpp:LoaderObject::content_loader_info` now holds the cached value, which `Radicle/src/avm2/native_compat.cpp:content_loader_info` fills on first read. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_compat.cpp:refresh_content_loader_info` moves the cached info to the domain of each load; `Radicle/src/avm2/native_net.cpp:loader_load` calls it right after `loader->domain` is set, so a held reference reports the latest domain. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_compat.cpp:display_loader_info` returns the parent Loader's cached info when the object is that Loader's content root. Other display objects still get a fresh LoaderInfo per read, because the runtime has no per-movie owner to cache on yet. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_display_api.cpp:ContentLoaderInfoIsTheSameObjectOnEveryRead`, `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain.cpp:LoadedContentLoaderInfoIsTheLoadersContentLoaderInfo` and `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain.cpp:HeldContentLoaderInfoTakesTheDomainOfALaterLoad`.

`Radicle/src/avm2/display_snapshot.cpp:display_snapshot_text` writes one line per node, depth-first in child order, indented two spaces per nesting level. Fields are: class name (`DisplayObject::display_class`), depth (the node's index in its parent's child list, because no placement depth is stored on a DisplayObject and `clip_depth` is not printed), character id, local bounds (origin to origin plus size, before the parent transform), the composed stage matrix from `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:compose_matrix`, visible, blend mode, ratio (or `none`), placed filter count, alpha, child count, and for a TextFieldObject the text as a byte length, a colon and the raw bytes. Reals are fixed-point with four decimals, rounded through `std::llround`, so -0.0 prints as 0 and the text does not depend on the platform's float formatting. `Radicle/src/avm2/display_snapshot.cpp:fixed` runs `llround` only on a finite value whose scaled magnitude is below 9e18 (inside the `long long` range). A NaN prints as `nan`; an infinite value, or a finite one too large for that range, prints as `inf` or `-inf`, so the conversion never sees a non-finite or out-of-range value. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_display_snapshot.cpp:NonFiniteAndOutOfRangeValuesPrintAsWords`.

`Radicle/src/avm2/display_snapshot.cpp:fnv1a64` is the standard FNV-1a 64 (offset basis 14695981039346656037, prime 1099511628211). `Radicle/src/avm2/display_snapshot.cpp:display_snapshot_hash` hashes the bytes of `display_snapshot_text`. Closed gap: `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:snapshot_hash` uses the same standard basis, since `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:Hasher` was corrected to 14695981039346656037 (see the tail section of this file).

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_display_snapshot.cpp:StageTree` builds a stage with a 30 by 40 sprite at (10, 20) with alpha 0.5, a hidden TextField "Hi there" at x 5, and a holder with scale_x 2 that contains a sprite at x 3. Hand derivation of the holder's child: the composed tx is parent.a * 3 = 2 * 3 = 6, which prints as 60000. The text expectation is in `kExpectedText`. The FNV expectations are the published vectors for the empty string and for "a" (af63dc4c8601ec8c). `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain.cpp:run_loader_script` gained a compare mode, used by `ContentLoaderInfoReportsTheContextDomain` and `ContentLoaderInfoReportsTheRootDomainWithoutAContext`. `LoaderContextConstructorStoresTheDomainArgument` covers the constructor form.

## Radicle/src/avm2/text.cpp:StaticTextObject::text (StaticText from DefineText, #806 phase 10)

This supersedes the DefineText paragraph of the R5/R6 follow-up note above: a DefineText or DefineText2 character is no longer a bare Shape. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp:static_text_records_of` copies each `SwfTextRecord` of `SwfText::records` into a `StaticTextRecord` (`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/text.hpp:StaticTextRecord`). A record without the HasFont flag keeps the font of the record before it, as the SWF rule says the font carries across records. The font is an optional, so a text whose first record has no font stays unresolved unless that record has no glyphs. Colour and offset are decoded into `SwfTextRecord` but `StaticTextRecord` keeps only the font and the glyph indexes, and `text()` returns only the string, so nothing carries them forward. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp:collect_timeline` stores the records in `SwfMovieData::static_texts` keyed by the character id, and the character still gets its bounds from `character_bounds`.

`Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:resolve_character_class` picks `flash.text::StaticText` for such a character after the symbol class, sprite and TextField checks and before the Shape fallback. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:apply_character_definition` hands the records to the object. `Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:make_display_object` builds a `StaticTextObject` for the class and any subclass of it, with the runtime's `FontRegistry` pointer, the same way `TextFieldObject` gets its registry.

`Radicle/src/avm2/text.cpp:StaticTextObject::text` builds the string from UTF-16 code units. Records with no glyphs are skipped before the font check. For each other record it finds the font by id under the movie's owner key (see the last section), then reads `FontResource::glyphs[glyph_index].code`. The glyph index is the position in the font's code table, which is the order `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp:collect_timeline` uses for DefineFont2 and DefineFont3. If a record with glyphs has no font, its font is missing for that movie, or a glyph index is past the table, the whole result is `""`; there is no partial text. A style-only record without a font therefore does not blank the text. The result is converted with `utf8_from_utf16`.

`Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:read_display_property` returns `text` for an object where `is_static_text()` holds. `DisplayObject::is_static_text` is a virtual defaulting to false, like `is_text_field`. There is no setter, so a script write to `text` is not handled by the display property path.

`Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:entry_kind` keeps the Shape kind for static text. The class name is now `flash.text::StaticText`, which does not contain "Shape", so the explicit `is_static_text` branch is what keeps the snapshot kind unchanged for consumers. `Radicle/src/avm2/display_snapshot.cpp:append_node` prints the class name and does not print the static text.

`Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp:Runtime::install_builtins` registers `flash.text::StaticText` with `flash.display::DisplayObject` as its base and the same `display_construct` native constructor as the other display classes, so `new StaticText()` goes through `make_display_object` and reads as `""`. Nothing has been checked against Flash for that constructor case. No native method ids were added because StaticText has no methods.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_static_text.cpp:DefineTextPlacesAStaticTextThatReadsTheFontCodes` builds a DefineFont2 (codes 'H', 'i') and a two-record DefineText from hand-derived bytes, places it, and expects "Hi" from both the method and `read_display_property`. `TextIsEmptyWhenNoFontIsSelected` and `TextIsEmptyWhenAGlyphIsOutsideTheFontTable` cover the empty-string cases. `SnapshotKeepsStaticTextAsAShape` checks the Shape kind. The placement row is appended as a struct to the decoded file, since the byte fixtures cover the font and text tags only.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:parse_operation pushshort canonical and wide forms (GT-806 ABC gaps)

`pushshort` is the only instruction whose operand has the `Role::Immediate` role with the U30 encoding (opcode 0x25, operand table in `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp`). Flash emits two forms. The canonical form is the 16-bit two's complement value as a u30: `pushshort -5` is `25 FB FF 03` and `pushshort 300` is `25 AC 02`. The wide form is a sign-extended 32-bit value as a five-byte u32: `pushshort -5` is `25 FB FF FF FF 0F`. The Interface archive has 1334 canonical and 74 wide pushshort in 12 movies, and every wide value lies in 0xFFFF8000 to 0xFFFFFFFF. `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:decode_code` reads an Immediate operand with `ByteReader::u32` into `AbcDecodedOperand::value` and sets `immediate` to the low 16 bits sign-extended, so a wide value keeps its five bytes. `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:encode_code` writes an Immediate operand with `put_u32`. Both used the u30 path before, which masks to 30 bits and rewrote the wide form's last byte (`0F` became `03`). `Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:parse_operation` accepts the wide text form only for 0xFFFF8000 to 0xFFFFFFFF, so `pushshort 4294967291` assembles to the five-byte form, and `pushshort 65536` is still refused with "does not fit 16 bits". `Radicle/src/abc/abc_text_body.cpp:render_operand` prints a value above 0xFFFF unsigned for the same reason. Before, the dump printed `-5` for both forms, so the wide form re-assembled as three bytes and the next instruction's offset failed with "instruction offsets are not contiguous". A value between 0x10000 and 0xFFFF7FFF has no text form and is refused on assembly, so such a block fails loudly rather than re-encoding to different bytes; no shipped block has one. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_pushshort.cpp:WideSignExtendedFormKeepsItsFiveBytes` and the byte-exact corpus checks in `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp`.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_text_body.cpp:render_body exception labels (GT-806 ABC round trip)

`render_body` numbers code labels from `collect_label_offsets`, which takes branch targets, switch targets and exception endpoints. The exception lines used a second map numbered from the endpoints alone, so an exception could name `L<k>` for an offset that the code section defined under a different `L<k>:`. The old numbering put a label at the wrong offset in 46 movies of `Fallout4 - Interface.ba2` (read-only scan). `render_body` now builds one `labels` map before the decode status check, and the code labels and the exception lines both read it. In that archive every exception endpoint (750 operands in 149 bodies) is an instruction start or the code end, so each has a label line. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm_real.cpp:EveryVanillaInterfaceBlockDumpAssemblesBackByteForByte` assembles the dump back, and `Radicle/tests/test_abc_real.cpp:DecodesEveryShippedInterfaceAbcBlock` reports the first differing byte when a re-encode mismatches.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_text_body.cpp:render_body absolute targets (GT-806 ABC round trip)

`render_body` used to give every collected target a label, but it printed an `Lk:` definition only for an offset that starts an instruction or equals `code.size()`. The two shipped dead branches documented in `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:mark_reachable` have a target past the end (`Interface\BarterMenu.swf` body 572 targets 122 of a 116-byte body, `Interface\ContainerMenu.swf` body 568 targets 163 of 157), so those dumps carried a `-> Lk` reference with no definition and `Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:parse_body` refused the whole block with `label Lk is not defined`. Labels are now built only over the labelable offsets (`code_boundaries` in the same file: every decoded `Radicle/include/fo4/abc/opcodes.hpp:AbcInstruction::offset` plus the code size), numbered densely in sorted order, so a well-formed body renders exactly as before, same `Lk` names.
