A target that is not labelable prints the absolute form instead — `-> =122`, `switch =122 =130 ...`, `exception =10 =20 =30` — which `Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:parse_body` resolves through `pending_target`: the token after `=` is parsed as a `std::int64_t`, range-checked into `std::int32_t`, and assigned straight to `operand.target` or `exception.from`/`::to`/`::target` with no label lookup. Because `encode_code` truncates an S24 value silently, `Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:parse_body` checks every branch, dead or live, against the signed 24-bit window: `target - (offset + length)` for a jump and `target - offset` for a switch default or case (the same origins `encode_code` uses), and refuses the body with "target offset is outside the signed 24-bit range" otherwise. Exception endpoints are absolute u32 values, so a negative `=N` is refused with "exception offset is negative" instead of wrapping. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:BodyParser::fail` prefixes `line N: ` only when `first_line` is nonzero, and `Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:parse_instruction_text` passes 0, so a one-instruction error from `assemble_instruction_text` (which the C API reports through `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_abc_write.cpp`) carries no fake `line 1:` prefix. The bytes still round-trip because `Radicle/src/abc/opcodes.cpp:encode_code` recomputes the relative immediate from the absolute target (`target - next` for S24, `target - instruction start` for switch default and cases), so the on-disk encoding is untouched and the two shipped dead branches now assemble. `parse_body` also takes the body block's first source line, so a failed assemble reports that body's line in `AbcTextError::line` rather than the flush point's line after it. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm.cpp:DeadBranchTargetsRenderAsAbsoluteOffsetsAndRoundTripByteForByte` builds a `returnvoid` followed by a dead `jump +1000` (target 1005 of a 5-byte body) and a dead mid-instruction target 3, checks the rendered `=offset` form for both and holds the assembled body code and the serialized file byte-identical. It now also covers a dead `lookupswitch` with absolute default 1000 and case 3, and an exception whose `from` is mid-instruction (`exception =2`); a malformed `=` token (`=`, `=abc`, `=1x`, `=2147483648`), an out-of-window branch (`=9000000`), an out-of-window switch default and a negative exception (`=-5`) each must fail assembly with a message; `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm_real.cpp:EveryVanillaInterfaceBlockDumpAssemblesBackByteForByte` assembles every vanilla block and now names the movie, block index, build, and the first differing byte of any failure.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_a.inc:k_pushscope scope depth (GT-806 ABC gaps)

`pushscope` and `pushwith` share one case. Before the push, the interpreter raises `InterpreterStatus::ScopeDepthExceeded` when `scopes.size() + body->init_scope_depth >= body->max_scope_depth + entry_scope_count`. That is the verifier's depth model (`Radicle/src/abc/abc_stack.cpp:observed_max_scope_depth` starts at `init_scope_depth`, each push adds one, and the ceiling is `max_scope_depth`) measured from the entry scopes, so the global and class scopes that `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::invoke` inserts before `entry_scope_count` are not charged to the body. The status is named after `CallDepthExceeded`, appended to `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/interpreter.hpp:InterpreterStatus` so no existing value shifts, and `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:interpreter_status_name` maps it to "scope depth exceeded". The static check in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_stack.cpp` does not run before the interpreter. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_scope_depth.cpp` runs two `pushscope` calls at `max_scope_depth` 2 (Ok) and 1 (`ScopeDepthExceeded`) through `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::run_script`.

## Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:build_abc_views DoABC (72) layout (GT-806 ABC gaps, fixed)

The SWF layout is: `DoABC2` (82) carries u32 flags, a NUL-terminated name, then the ABC bytes; `DoABC` (72) carries only the ABC bytes. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload` follows that (72 sets `payload_size` with no header), and `Radicle/tests/test_swf_doabc_round_trip.cpp:DoAbcCarriesRawAbcWithoutAFlagsOrNameHeader` pins it. The C ABI follows that now. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:build_abc_views` takes each `abc_blocks` payload as it is for both tags; the old split of a 72 payload (a flags-and-name header read back from raw ABC) is gone. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_abc_write.cpp:apply_file` writes the flags-and-name header only when the tag at `swf->tags[view->tag_index]` is DoABC2 (82), so a 72 block is rewritten as bare ABC. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf.h:radicle_swf_abc_info` reports `name` as "" for a 72 block. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf.cpp:DecodesDoAbcBlocksByTheirTagLayoutAndRefusesAnUnterminatedName` pins the 82 header, the raw 72 parse from payload offset 0, a 72 `apply_text` rewrite that returns the exact ABC bytes, and an unterminated 82 name refused at open (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_tags.cpp:decode_tag_payload` returns malformed_tag, so `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:open_from_bytes` fails with PARSE_ERROR). `Radicle/tests/test_swf_doabc_round_trip.cpp:DoAbc2KeepsItsFlagsAndNameAndRewritesByteExact` is the DoABC2 round trip through `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:replace_tag_payload` and `write_swf`.
Fixed: `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_abc_write.cpp:check_block` and `apply_file` both use the flat `swf->tags` index that `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:build_abc_views` stores, so a DefineSprite with children before the DoABC no longer misdirects an edit. The regression test is `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_abc_sprite.cpp:ApplyTextKeepsTheDoAbc2PayloadWhenASpriteComesFirst`.
Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_static_text.cpp:DefineTextPlacesAStaticTextThatReadsTheFontCodes` builds a DefineFont2 (codes 'H', 'i') and a two-record DefineText from hand-derived bytes, places it, and expects "Hi" from both the method and `read_display_property`. `TextIsEmptyWhenNoFontIsSelected` and `TextIsEmptyWhenAGlyphIsOutsideTheFontTable` cover the empty-string cases. `SnapshotKeepsStaticTextAsAShape` checks the Shape kind. The placement row is appended as a struct to the decoded file, since the byte fixtures cover the font and text tags only. `DefineText2ReadsGlyphsPastEachRgbaColour` places a DefineText2 whose record carries an RGBA colour, so a missed alpha byte would shift the glyph count and fail. `ZeroGlyphRecordWithoutFontDoesNotBlankTheText` puts a zero-glyph record without a font first and expects "Hi" from the records after it. `FontIdReusedByAnotherMovieReadsItsOwnFont` loads two movies in one runtime, each with a DefineFont2 id 1 (codes 'H', 'i' and 'X', 'Y') and a DefineText id 7, and expects each to read its own font.

## Font registry keyed by movie (#806 review lows)

`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/fonts.hpp:FontResource` carries an `owner` key. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/fonts.hpp:FontRegistry::find`, `find_by_name` and `first_with_layout` match only the fonts of the owner they are given. The runtime-wide registry used to match a bare character id, so a Loader-loaded movie that reused font id 1 read the first movie's font. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:next_font_owner` hands out keys from a process-wide atomic counter that starts at 1, so 0 stays the key for fonts and text objects that no movie has attached. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfRuntime::create` sets `SwfMovieData::font_owner` (`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/swf_runtime.hpp:SwfMovieData`) and copies each of the movie's fonts into `Runtime::fonts` under that key. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:apply_character_definition` passes the key to each text object through `set_font_owner` (`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/text.hpp:StaticTextObject::set_font_owner` and `TextFieldObject::set_font_owner`). Keys are never reused, so a released movie's fonts cannot match a later movie. The lookup is still a linear scan over every font in the runtime.

Font tags: `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp:collect_timeline` registers DefineFont2 (48) and DefineFont3 (75) only. DefineFont (10) is not registered because its tag has no code table: the codes come from DefineFontInfo (tag 13), which `Radicle/src/swf/swf_text.cpp:decode_text_tag` does not read. Registering it would map every glyph to code 0, so a DefineText would read NULs. DefineFont4 (91) is not registered either: its outlines are CFF data that `decode_text_tag` does not decode, so there is no code table to register. A DefineText that names a font id of either tag still reads "" as before.

Owner 0 is the key of script-made text (`Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:display_construct` builds it without a movie). `Radicle/src/avm2/text.cpp:FontRegistry::find_by_name` and `first_with_layout` treat owner 0 as matching any owner so those fields still reach embedded fonts; `find` stays strict because the id collision it guards against needs a movie owner. A Loader-loaded child with no embedded font falls back to device metrics rather than borrowing the parent's font.

Fonts are released when a movie is closed. `Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:radicle_movie_close` calls `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfRuntime::release_fonts`, which removes the movie's owner key from the registry with `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/fonts.hpp:FontRegistry::remove_owner`. The registry is shared: `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/runtime.hpp:Runtime::font_registry` hands the same `std::shared_ptr<FontRegistry>` to `SwfRuntime::create`, so a release never reads the `Runtime`, which the host may already have closed. The `SwfRuntime` itself is not destroyed on close, because `radicle_runtime::movies` keeps it: the runtime holds raw pointers into each movie's ABC files (`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/runtime.hpp:ScriptEntry::file` and `Runtime::FileState::file`), and destroying the movie would leave them dangling. Open: a Loader child movie releases its fonts only when the whole runtime closes, since no unload path calls `release_fonts` yet. A `SwfRuntime::create` that fails after its fonts are registered also keeps them until the runtime closes.

Owner-0 registration order: `Radicle/src/avm2/text.cpp:FontRegistry::first_with_layout` with owner 0 returns the earliest-registered font with a layout across every owner. Registration order is the order of `SwfRuntime::create` calls, so after a movie is released, script-made text reads the earliest surviving movie's layout font. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_text.cpp:OwnerZeroReadsTheEarliestRegisteredLayoutFontAcrossOwners` for the order, `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_static_text.cpp:ReleasingAMovieEvictsItsFontsAndKeepsTheOthers` for the release.

## Snapshot colour offsets and the snapshot hash (#807 follow-up)

`Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:make_entry` stores each colour offset in an `int32` (`SnapshotColorTransform`), but a script can assign any Number to `colorTransform.redOffset`. `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:color_offset` returns 0 for NaN and clamps every other value to the int32 range before the cast, so an out-of-range offset is no longer undefined behaviour. The display-tree text already prints a scaled magnitude (value times 10000) of 9e18 or more as `inf` (`Radicle/src/avm2/display_snapshot.cpp:fixed`). `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:snapshot_hash` uses the standard FNV-1a 64 basis (see the tail section of this file for the one-time value change). Test: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_snapshot.cpp:ColorOffsetsOutsideTheIntRangeClampToIt`.
## Radicle/src/avm2/native_system.cpp:Runtime::install_system_builtins (R8 L3a static classes, #807)

`Runtime::install_system_builtins` runs as the last step of `Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp:Runtime::install_builtins`, so `flash.events::EventDispatcher` already exists when its `find_class` lookup runs. It installs `flash.text::TextFieldAutoSize`, `flash.system::Capabilities`, `flash.system::Security`, `flash.system::SecurityDomain` (shell only), `flash.text::Font`, `flash.filters::BitmapFilterQuality` and the interface `flash.events::IEventDispatcher`.

The constants and fixed values are `TraitKind::Const` class traits, the same mechanism as `Math.PI`, not native getters. A script read is identical. A write to them is not rejected by this code. `Capabilities.version` ("WIN 32,0,0,0") is a guessed value. `Capabilities.languages` and `SecurityDomain.currentDomain` are not installed; the plan lists them for Grognak, and whether a movie reads them is unverified.

`Security.sandboxType` is "application" as the L3a plan says. The plan also says Grognak compares `sandboxType` with `REMOTE`, which is false under this value. Unverified against the movie.

`IEventDispatcher` sets `Class::is_interface` and is pushed into `EventDispatcher` `interfaces`, so `Class::implements_interface` holds for every EventDispatcher subclass.

`Font.enumerateFonts` is `native::Id::font_enumerate_fonts`. `try_system_native` in `Radicle/src/avm2/native_system.cpp` handles it, and `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_support.cpp` dispatches to it before `try_compat_native`. `Font.registerFont` and the Security no-ops `allowDomain`, `allowInsecureDomain` and `loadPolicyFile` reuse `native::Id::compat_undefined`.

`Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:write_display_property` maps the string constants through `auto_size_from_value`, and an integer still maps to the enum. `Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:read_display_property` returns the name from `auto_size_name`. It used to return the enum number, so any script that compared the old number now sees a string. No existing test reads `autoSize`.

Not built or run locally. CI is the check for `tests/test_avm2_system_classes.cpp`.

## utf16 helpers in their own header

`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/utf16.hpp` declares `utf16_from_utf8` and `utf8_from_utf16`, defined in `Radicle/src/avm2/utf16.cpp`. `Radicle/src/avm2/value.cpp:Value::string` includes only this header, so it no longer pulls in `text.hpp`. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/text.hpp` includes it, so existing users still compile.

## BGSCodeObj host call table (#807 R8 L1)

- `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bgs.cpp:install_bgs_code_object`: the seven Scaleform Programs reach the host through `BGSExternalInterface.call(codeObj, name, ...args)`, which does `codeObj[name] as Function` and then `f.apply(null, args)`, and every caller discards the result. So the host populates the document root's `BGSCodeObj` Object with eleven native Functions (`registerSound`, `playSound`, `playRegisteredSound`, `stopRegisteredSound`, `pauseRegisteredSound`, `getHighscore`, `setHighscore`, `getSaveData`, `setSaveData`, `closeHolotape`, `showTutorialOverlay`). Host answers reach the script only as callbacks, not as return values. The table is `kBgsFunctions`, and each Function gets its own `native::Id` (`Radicle/src/avm2/native_ids.hpp`, the `bgs_*` entries).
- `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bgs.cpp:try_bgs_native`: each call stringifies its arguments and forwards them through `HostBridge::call_host` under the method name `bgs.<name>`. The host sees that name on `host_call`, or on a named `HostBridge::install_function("bgs.<name>")` entry. It returns the host string, or null when the host gives no answer. `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_support.cpp:Interpreter::call_native_id` dispatches to it after the other families.
- Design decision: the brief asked for a separate bgs-call hook beside `host_call`. It was not added. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/host.hpp:HostBridge::call_host` already routes the `bgs.` names to the host, and a second hook would have no caller. A side effect: an ExternalInterface.call with a `bgs.` name reaches the same handler, so the namespaces are shared.
- Population: `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfRuntime::create` calls `install_bgs_code_object` after the document constructor returns, and only when `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/swf_runtime.hpp:SwfRuntimeOptions` has `bgs_host` set (default off, so existing hosts see no change). A root without `BGSCodeObj` (GJ_Defrag, TurretHack) is a no-op. A value that is not a plain Object is skipped. The lookup goes through `Object::read_value`, so a declared slot and a dynamic property both work.
- Access paths: the table is reachable by fixed-name access (`codeObj.playSound`, then `apply`, which `Radicle/src/avm2/native_object.cpp:function_apply` spreads from the Array argument). Runtime-name access (`codeObj[name]` with a computed name) needs `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_b.inc:Interpreter` `k_getproperty` to pop a runtime name, which it does not yet do; that support is lane L0, so until L0 lands the BGSExternalInterface path is not runnable. Arguments reach the host through `to_string`, the same stringification `Radicle/src/avm2/native_net.cpp:ext_call` applies to ExternalInterface.call arguments.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_bgs_bridge.cpp:BgsCodeObjApplyReachesTheHostWithItsName` (fixed-name apply reaches the host as `bgs.playSound` with `["x"]` and returns the host string), `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_bgs_bridge.cpp:AbsentBgsFunctionReadsUndefinedWithoutThrowing` (a missing fixed name reads undefined and calls nothing), `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_bgs_bridge.cpp:MovieWithoutBgsCodeObjCreatesWithNoCodeObject`, and `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_bgs_bridge.cpp:DisabledHostLeavesBgsCodeObjWithoutFunctions`. Nothing was built or run locally; CI is the oracle.
## Runtime-name multinames (#807 R8 L0)

- `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/interpreter.hpp:Interpreter::resolve_runtime_multiname` is an inline guard. A multiname with a fixed name and a fixed namespace returns at once, so QName, QNameSet and TypeName never reach a call. Only RuntimeNamespace (RTQName, RTQNameA), RuntimeName (MultinameL, MultinameLA) and Dynamic (RTQNameL, RTQNameLA) call `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::pop_runtime_operands`.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::pop_runtime_operands` pops the runtime operands of a multiname from under the handler's own operands. A runtime namespace sits below a runtime name, and `above` counts the operands the handler still pops above them: the value of a set, or the arguments of a call. The helper erases only the parts, so each handler keeps its existing pop order. A stack that holds too few operands returns `InterpreterStatus::StackUnderflow`.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::pop_runtime_operands` moves the public namespace (kind Package, empty name) to the front of a RuntimeName's ns_set copy with `std::stable_partition`. `Radicle/src/avm2/name.cpp:primary_key` takes `namespaces.front()`, and `Radicle/src/avm2/object.cpp:Object::write_value` creates a missing key under it. Without the move, `o[name] = v` stored under a private namespace listed first, and a public `o.foo` missed it. Reads match over the whole set, so only writes depend on the order. `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::find_scope_binding` also reads the front namespace, so a runtime-name lookup now sees the public namespace there.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::pop_runtime_operands` converts each runtime operand with `to_string`, so a number key reaches `is_array_index` as its decimal text, and an object key converts through its string form. Radicle registers no AS3 `Namespace` class, so a runtime namespace operand becomes a `Package` namespace named by its string. A QName object used as the name is out of scope and converts the same way.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::pop_runtime_operands` sets the kind of the copy by operand shape. `RuntimeName` (MultinameL, MultinameLA) keeps the ns_set namespaces and becomes `QNameSet`. `RuntimeNamespace` (RTQName, RTQNameA) keeps its fixed name and becomes `QName`. `Dynamic` (RTQNameL, RTQNameLA) takes both parts from the stack and becomes `QName`. The copy is stored in `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/interpreter.hpp:Interpreter::Frame` as `runtime_name`, so the handler's pointer stays valid for the instruction.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/runtime.cpp:resolve_multiname` sets `attribute` for RTQNameLA in the `Dynamic` branch, as it does for RTQNameA. The copy keeps the flag, and `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::find_scope_binding` skips package and global class resolution for an attribute name. RTQNameL leaves the flag unset.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_b.inc:op::k_getproperty` takes 0 operands above the name. `op::k_setproperty` and `op::k_initproperty` take 1 (the value). `op::k_findpropstrict` and `op::k_findproperty` take 0. `op::k_deleteproperty` takes 0. `op::k_getsuper` takes 0 and `op::k_setsuper` takes 1. `op::k_constructprop`, `op::k_callproperty`, `op::k_callproplex`, `op::k_callpropvoid`, `op::k_callsuper` and `op::k_callsupervoid` take the argument count. `op::k_getlex` is unchanged, and getdescendants has no handler.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_a.inc:op::k_instanceof` and `op::k_in` moved here from `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_b.inc`, unchanged, so dispatch_b stays under the 750-line guard after the eight handlers gained their call.
- `Radicle/tests/avm2_test_support.hpp:ScriptBuilder::finish` emits the empty ns_set, then each entry of `ns_sets_`. The member's default `{1u}` is pool ns_set 1, the public set that `ScriptBuilder::multiname_l` names by default. `ScriptBuilder::namespace_set` appends a set and returns its pool index, and `ScriptBuilder::multiname_l` takes that index. `ScriptBuilder::rtqname_l` builds RTQNameL next to `ScriptBuilder::rtqname`. The default package takes pool string 0 (the empty string) instead of calling `string_of` after the pool is copied. Before, a builder whose first multiname had no default package could point a namespace name past the pool.
- `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_runtime_names.cpp:GetpropertyReadsAPlainObjectByRuntimeName`, `SetpropertyStoresUnderTheRuntimeNameForReadBack`, `CallpropertyCallsAFunctionStoredUnderARuntimeName`, `ArrayReadsAnIntegerRuntimeNameAsAnIndex`, `RuntimeNameOperandsLeaveTheStackBalanced`, `MissingRuntimeNameLeavesTheStackBalanced`, `RtqnameTakesItsNamespaceFromTheStack`, `RtqnameLTakesItsNamespaceAndNameFromTheStack`, `InitpropertyDefinesUnderTheRuntimeName`, `NegativeRuntimeNameStoresADynamicKey`, `SetpropertyWritesUnderThePublicNamespaceFirst`, `GetpropertyWithoutOperandsIsAStackUnderflow` and `GetpropertyWithOneOperandIsAStackUnderflow` run through `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::run_script`.

## Host-to-script calls (#807 R8 L2)

- `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_runtime.h:radicle_movie_call`: the host calls a public method on a loaded movie's root clip. Each argument is a `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_runtime.h:radicle_call_arg` (a kind tag, then the field that kind names: `flag`, an int32 where nonzero is true, for a boolean; `number` for a number; or a NUL-terminated UTF-8 `text` for a string). `Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:call_argument` reads only that field. The result is UTF-8 text stringified by `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/coercion.hpp:to_string`, in memory the caller releases with `radicle_free_bytes`. An undefined or null result returns NULL with size 0. The Scaleform Programs' Main entry points (SetPlatform, InitProgram, ProcessUserEvent, Pause, ConfirmQuit, SetHighscore, SetSaveData, OnLeftStickInput) reach the script through this path.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:call_argument` turns a tag into a `Value`. An unknown kind, or a string kind with a NULL `text`, is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- `Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:call_failure_status` maps the interpreter status. An absent member (`NoSuchProperty`) is `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`. A member that is not a method (`CannotCall`) is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Any other failure, such as a thrown exception or the instruction budget, is `RADICLE_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`. The interpreter's message goes to `radicle_last_error`.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:SwfRuntime::call_root` looks the member up with `Object::lookup` on the root clip, the lookup `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::call_property` uses, and calls `Interpreter::call_function` with the root as `this`. Only `LookupKind::Method` is callable. A dynamic property that holds a Function, and an accessor, are refused as not a method. Widening that is a separate decision.
- The member name is built with `builtin_name` (fixed name, public package). The host passes a plain string, so the runtime-name path from R8 L0 is not involved.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/swf_runtime.hpp:SwfRuntime::call_root` takes the `Interpreter` as its first argument, as `SwfRuntime::advance` does, because the runtime does not own one.
- ABI: this lane moved `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` from 74 to 75 for the new export and the `radicle_call_arg` type. The merge with `nomad/dev` (ABI 61) settled on 76, and the pin is now `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSeventySeven`. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` (`RadicleNative.CompiledAbiVersion`) needs regenerating. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_runtime.h` is not in `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py:HEADERS`, so the export and the struct are not bound in C# by this change; the hand-written `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RuntimeNative.cs` also does not bind `radicle_movie_call` yet (deferred). `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.hpp:max_instructions` is a cumulative budget shared by `radicle_movie_advance` and `radicle_movie_call` (follow-up: reset per host entry).
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime.cpp:MovieCallReturnsTypedResultsFromTheRootMethods` (Ping(String) returns its string, Add(Number, Number) returns "5", a null argument returns NULL with size 0) and `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime.cpp:MovieCallFailsCleanlyForAbsentOrNonMethodMembers` (an absent name is NOT_FOUND with the name in the error, a dynamic property is INVALID_ARGUMENT, a bad kind and a NULL name are INVALID_ARGUMENT). `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime.cpp:member_root_file` builds the document class with `avm2_test::ScriptBuilder`, and sets the parameter types after `finish`, because the builder cannot declare them.
- Not built or run locally; CI is the oracle.
## ByteArray (#807 R8 L3b)

- `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bytearray.cpp:Runtime::install_bytearray_builtins`: installs `flash.utils::ByteArray` and `flash.utils::Endian`. ByteArray gets the native constructor `native::Id::bytearray_construct`, Getter/Setter pairs for `length`, `position` and `endian`, a Getter for `bytesAvailable`, and Methods `writeByte`, `readByte`, `readUnsignedByte`, `writeUTFBytes`, `readUTFBytes` and `clear`. Endian holds the Const strings `BIG_ENDIAN` and `LITTLE_ENDIAN`, the same mechanism as `Radicle/src/avm2/native_system.cpp:Runtime::install_system_builtins`.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/runtime.cpp:Runtime::link`: runs `install_bytearray_builtins` after `install_builtins` (which ends with `install_system_builtins`) and before `build_class_shells`. It is kept out of `Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp:Runtime::install_builtins`, which must stay at 717 lines.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/native_ids.hpp:native::Id`: the ByteArray ids are appended after `bgs_show_tutorial_overlay`, so no existing id shifts and `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bytearray.cpp:try_bytearray_native` tests one contiguous range.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/bytearray.hpp:ByteArrayObject`: storage is a `std::vector<std::uint8_t>` with `position_` and `little_endian_`. `byte_at` returns 0 past the end, and `set_byte_at` zero-fills and extends the vector when the index is past the end. It drops a write at or past `kMaxByteArraySize`, so the vector never exceeds that size. This follows the brief: reads past the end give 0 and writes extend.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bytearray.cpp:bytearray_member`: `readByte` returns the byte as signed `int8` and `readUnsignedByte` returns it unsigned. Both return 0 past the end and still advance `position`. `writeByte` stores at `position` and advances it. `writeUTFBytes` writes each UTF-8 byte of the string. `readUTFBytes(n)` clamps `n` to the bytes available from `position`, so it returns only bytes that exist, with no NUL padding, and `position` advances by the count returned. Flash throws EOFError for reads past the end; this lane returns 0 from `readByte` and `readUnsignedByte` there, as the brief asked. The Flash behaviour is unverified.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bytearray.cpp:length_set`: resizes with zero-fill or truncates. `clear_bytes` resizes to 0 and resets `position`.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bytearray.cpp:endian_set`: accepts only "bigEndian" or "littleEndian" and stores the flag. No reader applies it yet, because this lane has no multi-byte integer accessors, so `endian` is read back and changes nothing.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bytearray.cpp:try_bytearray_native`: answers `bytearray_construct` first, then the range `bytearray_length_get` through `bytearray_clear`. Every other id returns false. A call on a receiver that is not a ByteArray returns undefined. `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_support.cpp:Interpreter::call_native_id` calls it after `try_system_native` and before `try_compat_native`. Construction reaches it through `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::construct`, which passes the class object as `self` when `native_constructor` is set.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:byte_array_index_access`: a fixed name that `is_array_index` accepts reads or writes one byte. A write stores `to_uint32` truncated to uint8, so `ba[i] = 256` stores 0, as Flash's byte coercion does. A read past the end returns 0 and does not extend the array.
- `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::array_property`: the ByteArray branch runs before the Array branch. It always returns Ok and sets `handled` only for index names. For other names, `Interpreter::get_property` and `Interpreter::set_property` fall through to the accessor lookup, so `length`, `position` and the rest still work.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/object.hpp:ObjectKind` adds `ByteArray` after `Event`. `Radicle/src/avm2/object.cpp:object_kind_name` returns "bytearray", and `Radicle/src/avm2/coercion.cpp:object_default_to_string` prints it as "[object Object]" with Event. Those are the only switches that list every ObjectKind, and they have no default, so both cases are required.
- Limits: sizes are capped at `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/bytearray.hpp:kMaxByteArraySize`, which is 2^28 bytes (256 MiB). That value is my choice and is not checked against Flash. A `length`, `position` or `readUTFBytes` count that is above the cap, negative or not finite returns the TypeError status from `native_bytearray.cpp:length_set`, `position_set` or `read_utf_bytes`. An index write at or past the cap is dropped with no error, while `writeByte` and `writeUTFBytes` still advance `position`. An `endian` other than the two names returns the TypeError status from `native_bytearray.cpp:endian_set`.
- Skipped per the brief: `compress`, `uncompress`, `readObject`, `writeObject` and `writeBytes`. writeBytes is not trivial here because it needs a ByteArray argument and an offset/length form.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_bytearray.cpp` (suite `Avm2ByteArray`, 17 tests): `ReadsBackWhatWasWrittenFromPositionZero`, `PositionAdvancesWithEachWrite`, `LengthGrowsWithWrites`, `SettingLengthZeroFillsWhenGrowingAndTruncatesWhenShrinking`, `IndexWriteExtendsTheArrayAndIndexReadReturnsTheByte`, `IndexWriteGrowsLengthToTheWrittenIndex`, `IndexReadPastTheEndAndUnwrittenIndexesReadZero`, `ReadByteIsSignedAndReadUnsignedByteIsNot`, `WriteUtfBytesThenReadUtfBytesRoundTripsMultiByteText`, `EndianDefaultsToBigAndReadsBackWhatWasSet`, `BytesAvailableCountsFromPositionToTheEnd`, `ClearEmptiesTheArrayAndResetsThePosition`, `Base64DecoderShapedLoopWritesIndexedBytesAndReadsThemBack` (sum 360), `IndexLoopOverLengthSumsEveryByte` (sum 15), `SettingLengthAboveTheCapIsATypeError`, `ReadUtfBytesClampsToBytesAvailable` and `IndexWriteBeyondTheCapIsDropped`.
- Not compiled or run in this lane (no local builds). CI is the oracle. Unverified: MSVC /W4 /WX on the new TU and on the edited `interpreter_property.cpp`, `runtime.cpp` and `native_ids.hpp`; the relational compare on `native::Id` in `try_bytearray_native`; the receiver reaching the native as `self` for `callproperty`, which was traced through `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::invoke` and not run; and the TypeError for a bad `endian`, which is my choice and not checked against the player.

## Fake BGS host and acceptance harness (#807 R8 L4)

- `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:ReplaysTheSevenProgramsDeterministically` drives the C++ runtime, not `radicle_movie_call`. The C ABI opens movies through `Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:open_movie_bytes`, which calls `SwfRuntime::create` with default options, so `SwfRuntimeOptions.bgs_host` stays off and `BGSCodeObj` gets no functions. Without the flag nothing reaches the fake host, so the harness sets `options.bgs_host = true` on the C++ `SwfRuntime::create`. The entry points are the ones `radicle_movie_call` uses (`SwfRuntime::call_root`), and the frames come from `Radicle/src/avm2/replay.cpp:replay`, the function `radicle_movie_replay` wraps. Adding an options-taking C ABI open is the follow-up that would let C-level hosts enable the bridge.
- Because the C++ path does not set `radicle_last_error`, `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:run_program` puts its own reason in `ProgramRun::failure` (the `SwfRuntime::last_error` text for a failed create, the `ExecutionResult::message` for a failed call), and the test prints that to std::cerr as `[r8-programs]`.
- `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:drive_movie` calls `SetPlatform(0, false)` (Number, Boolean) and then `InitProgram()` when `init` is set, then replays 180 frames. It fails the run when `SwfRuntime::playing` is false afterwards (a frame script stopped the movie) or when the frame hashes hold one distinct value (state never changed). The argument types are unverified: the plan gives only the arity, so the number and boolean are guesses that the CI log will confirm or refute. `ProcessUserEvent` and `Pause` are not called, because the replay never called them before and their argument meaning is unverified (plan 1c risk e).
- `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:program_inputs` is the input log: 40 mouse moves, a click, Enter, Space and a second click. The negative control does not change it. It skips `SetPlatform` and `InitProgram` instead, through the `init` flag of `drive_movie`.
- `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:resolve_bytes` resolves through `candidate_paths` and extracts the bytes from the archive. The movie itself is one of the counted resolutions, so `asset_misses` is the only miss count reported. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:resolve_asset` (the C callback still used by `RunsAProgramMovieDeterministically`) shares `candidate_paths`. The plan's resolver fix (splitting `Programs\` and matching case-insensitively) is not in this lane.
- `Radicle/tests/fake_bgs_host.hpp:FakeBgsHost::host_call` is the callback that `HostBridge::call_host` reaches through `HostCallbacks::host_call`, so the `bgs.<name>` names that `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bgs.cpp:try_bgs_native` forwards arrive here. It records every call in order, including non-`bgs.` names from ExternalInterface, and answers only the `bgs.` names that have state: `getHighscore` returns the stored string unchanged or nothing, `setHighscore` stores its second argument unchanged as a string (no numeric parse), `getSaveData` and `setSaveData` use the save-data map, and `registerSound` adds to the sound registry. The play, stop, pause, close and overlay calls only record.
- `Radicle/tests/fake_bgs_host.hpp:FakeBgsHost::log_hash` is the host-log hash. It is FNV-1a 64 with the standard offset basis, a 0xFF byte after each method or argument, and a 0xFE byte after each call. The bytes can not occur in UTF-8 text, so the separators keep the encoding unambiguous. The frame hash in `Radicle/src/avm2/replay.cpp:replay` uses `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:snapshot_hash`, which now has the standard FNV-1a 64 offset basis (see the tail section of this file), but feeds different bytes, so the two hashes are still not interchangeable.
- `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:kPinned` holds the pins. A zero entry means unpinned, and `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:check_pins` compares only the nonzero fields. The pins are empty until a CI run supplies them. The test prints `R8_HASH <program> <snapshot_hash> <hostlog_hash> <bgs_calls>` for each program that completes, with the snapshot hash taken from the last replayed frame.
- The negative control in `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:ReplaysTheSevenProgramsDeterministically` runs AtomicCommand and PipFall with `init` and then without it, after `ASSERT_TRUE` on the base run. The `init=false` run does not require `ok()`: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:drive_movie` skips its playing and distinct-hash gates when `init` is false, so a static screen still yields a hash vector. The frame-hash sequences and the host logs must each differ. The bgs call counts are not compared, because InitProgram may make no bgs call. It compares whole sequences, not only the final hash, so a final frame that happens to match cannot fail it. This is one deviation from the plan's wording.
- `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:run_program_body` counts the `bgs.` calls the host saw into `ProgramRun::bgs_calls`. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:run_program` wraps it and turns a `std::exception` into the run's failure. The test loop requires at least one bgs call for AtomicCommand, PipFall, RedMenace, ZetaInvaders and Grognak. TurretHack and GJ_Defrag only report the count, because their init calls are unverified.
- `ran` counts a program only when both runs complete. The old `GTEST_SKIP` on `ran == 0` is gone, and `EXPECT_EQ(ran, 7u)` now fails when any program does not run. Every failure (missing entry, failed run, nondeterminism, missing bgs call) is appended to `failed` as `program: reason`, and `failed` is the message of both `EXPECT_EQ(ran, 7u)` and `EXPECT_EQ(mismatches, 0u)`.
- Not built or run locally. CI is the oracle. Unverified: whether `Interpreter` errors inside `replay` surface through `Radicle/src/avm2/replay.cpp:replay` (the frame count and `SwfRuntime::playing` are checked, not the script status), and whether the MSVC /W4 build accepts `Radicle/tests/fake_bgs_host.hpp:FakeBgsHost::sounds` as an unused accessor.
## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex_analysis.h:radicle_pex_call_operand_role

Exposes `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/opcodes.hpp:pex_call_operand_role`, implemented in `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/opcodes.cpp:pex_call_operand_role`, so a caller can name the fixed operands of a call instruction without carrying its own opcode table. `callmethod` is name, receiver, result; `callparent` is name, result; `callstatic` is owning script, name, result. Every other opcode, and every index at or past those fixed operands, is `RADICLE_PEX_OPERAND_NONE`, which is also what an opcode past the 0..46 table returns, so a caller can walk indexes until the role goes away instead of trusting a count it computed itself.

It lives in the analysis header, not `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex.h`, because that header's `radicle_pex_object_code` contract says so: "Instruction arguments are the decoded operands in file order with the variable-argument count removed: a call opcode's fixed operands come first and its variable arguments follow. What any operand means is the caller's business; this layer names no operand roles." Adding a role lookup there would have contradicted the header's own sentence and forced a reword. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex_analysis.h:radicle_pex_call_site` already names call kinds and resolved targets, so this table sits in the layer that already interprets calls and leaves the PEX layer's contract true as written.

The shape is deliberately the smallest that answers the question: one enum, one function that returns it, no handle, no status and no allocation, because the lookup reads a fixed table and has no failure mode to report. A caller sums the roles by walking indexes until `RADICLE_PEX_OPERAND_NONE`, and the test below pins that walk to the number of fixed operands the encoder writes.

Provenance: the table was carried in GardenEngine as `opencw/Services/Papyrus/RadiclePexLowering.cs:RadiclePexLowering.Roles`, `:RadiclePexLowering.OperandOf` and `CallOperandRole` (PR #544), next to a second copy of the mnemonic table that `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_pex.h:radicle_pex_opcode_name` already owns. The engine copy is what this export replaces once the pin moves; nothing in the engine was changed by this branch.

ABI 61 is one above the 60 the exports above ship at. The current pin is `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSeventySeven`, which pins `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` after the merges described in the note above.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_pex_analysis_c_api.cpp:NamesTheFixedOperandRolesOfEveryCallShape` pins all eight fixed slots of the three call opcodes through the C call, which catches the swap that matters - a receiver and function name exchanged makes the interpreter dispatch on a literal and makes an analysis attribute the call to the wrong script, and exchanging `callstatic`'s owning script with its name resolves a native against the wrong script. `GivesNoRoleToVariadicOrMissingOperands` requires index 3 of `callmethod`, index 2 of `callparent` and a far index to be NONE, which catches a table that pads every call shape to three roles, where a caller would read a variadic argument as the receiver. `NamesNoRoleOutsideTheThreeCallOpcodes` sweeps 0..46 and then 47 and 255, which catches roles leaking onto `propset` or `assign` and catches an unguarded index past the table. `AgreesWithTheFixedOperandCountOfEveryCallOpcode` requires the number of named roles to equal `Radicle/include/fo4/pex/pex.hpp:PexFile::kOpCodes[opcode].args` for each of the three, which catches the role table and the argument-count table drifting apart, the state where a consumer reads a fixed operand the encoder never writes.

The callgraph now reads those positions from the table instead of spelling them twice. `Radicle/include/fo4/pex_analysis/opcodes.hpp:pex_call_operand_index` and `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/opcodes.cpp:pex_call_operand_index` return the index a role sits at, or `kNoIndex` when the opcode's table gives no such role; it walks indexes until `pex_call_operand_role` answers `None`, so the numbers 0/1/2 still appear only in `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/opcodes.cpp:pex_call_operand_role`. `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:build_call_graph` asks it for `FunctionName`, `Receiver` and `OwningScript`, and `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:collect_accesses` asks it for `Result` and `Receiver`, which let `Radicle/src/pex_analysis/callgraph.cpp:call_result_operand` be deleted: that switch held a third copy of the result positions (2 for a method and a static call, 1 for a parent).

The derivation is unchanged by construction rather than by inspection, which is the only reason this went in without a test run. The table answers `callmethod` name 0, receiver 1, result 2; `callparent` name 0, result 1; `callstatic` owning script 0, name 1, result 2 - the same six numbers the inline code wrote. `kNoIndex` is `SIZE_MAX`, so the guards keep the shape they had - `args.size() > index`, which is the old `args.size() > 1` and `args.size() > nameOperand` written once, and the static branch's `!args.empty()` is that same test at index 0 - so each is false exactly where the old hand-written bound was false; the parent branch still takes `object.parentClassName` and never reads a receiver, because the table gives `callparent` no `Receiver`; and the `opCode == PexOp::CallMethod` test that guarded the receiver read in `collect_accesses` is subsumed, since only a method call has a `Receiver` at all. No call site gained a condition, and the variadic loop still starts at the result operand and marks it `Write`.

Not built and not run: `Radicle/tests/test_pex_analysis.cpp` (the synthetic callgraph cases) and the real-data callgraph assertions are untouched and remain the contract, but nothing compiled this branch, so the claim above rests on the two derivations being the same six numbers and the same guard shape, not on a green run. The role table's own tests in `Radicle/tests/test_pex_analysis_c_api.cpp` still pin it, including the case that requires each call opcode's role count to equal the encoder's argument count.
## Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NOCM\Obstacle and Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:GROUP_RUN_KEYS — uncounted sub-runs in a group run (#602 B-23, NOCM)

The INNR entry above modelled a nested run that a member of the outer run counts. NOCM has the same two-level shape with no count subrecord anywhere, so this closes it by letting `run.count_member` be empty rather than by adding a second kind: the group's own count stays optional (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupDescriptor.count_subrecord`) and now the run's count does too (`Radicle/include/fo4/schema/scalar.hpp:SubrecordGroupRunDescriptor.count_member`).

- Source: xEdit `wbRecord(NOCM, 'Navmesh Obstacle Manager', [wbEDID, wbRArray('Unknown', wbRStruct('Unknown', [wbRArray('Unknown', wbRStruct('Unknown', [wbInteger(INDX, 'Index', itU32), wbRArray('Unknown Datas', wbUnknown(DATA)), wbUnknown(INTV)])), wbString(NAM1, 'Model')]))])` at `Core/wbDefinitionsFO4.pas:12453-12469`. Neither `wbRArray` sets a count path, so nothing in the record states how many runs belong to a model: the outer run is `INDX`-started tuples followed by one `NAM1`, and the inner tuple is `INDX`, any number of `DATA`, then a required `INTV`. Every NOCM subrecord is one of those four signatures.
- Mechanism: `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group` accepts `"count_member": ""` and skips the four-byte non-repeatable member check that a named count has to pass; `Radicle/tools/subrecord_group_render.py:render_subrecord_groups` then writes `SubrecordGroupRunDescriptor{Signature{}, ...}`. A run member still may not be one of the group's own members, its count subrecord, a successor or another run member, and the run leader must still be required and non-repeatable, so the run leader is what starts a tuple when nothing counts it.
- Runtime: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` gained one branch ahead of the counted path. When the group has run members and no `count_member`, a span starts wherever the run leader appears, takes consecutive runs (each one leader, then its non-decreasing optional members with the same order, repeat and payload-size checks the counted path uses, then the required-member check), and then consumes one of the group's own members, the `NAM1` that closes the model, and ends the span (see the bug entry at the end of this file). The counting branch is untouched, so INNR, NPC_ actor sounds and the CONT/FURN/TERM groups behave exactly as before.
- Mutation: `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:insert_record_subrecord_group` and `:remove_record_subrecord_group` throw `SubrecordGroupError` ("spans uncounted sub-runs") for such a group before touching the record; the run-level insert and remove already refused a group whose `count_member` is empty ("has no counted sub-run"). Nothing can add a run to a record where the model/run boundary is a convention rather than a stored count.
- Rows: the group carries the members only; `Radicle/schema/fallout4/fields.json:NOCM\Index` (INDX, u32 at 0, repeated) and `:NOCM\Model` (NAM1, string, repeated) stay ordinary repeated rows outside the group, the same way `INNR\RulesetCount` and `INNR\NameText` sit outside the INNR group. `DATA` and `INTV` stay unrowed: xEdit types them `wbUnknown`.
- Corpus, read-only scan of the seven official masters: one NOCM record, in `Fallout4.esm`, holding 87 spans, 197 runs, 1589 `DATA` and 87 `NAM1`. Every span carries exactly one `NAM1` (histogram of `NAM1` per span is `{1: 87}`), every span starts with `INDX` and ends with its `NAM1`, and every run starts with `INDX` and ends with `INTV`, so the declared shapes hold without exception. Runs per span range from 1 to 24, most commonly 1 (59 spans); `DATA` per run ranges from 0 to 45.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_nested_group_runs.cpp:NestedGroupRuns.NocmObstacleDescriptorNamesItsUncountedRuns` (descriptor, empty counts, member flags), `:NocmSpansGroupEveryUncountedRunUnderItsModel` (two spans, three runs, exact span and run offsets), `:NocmShapeFailuresFailClosed` (missing `INTV`, `DATA` after `INTV`, a missing `NAM1`, two `INTV`), `:NocmRunlessModelAfterRunModelIsItsOwnSpan` (`INDX INTV NAM1 NAM1` as two spans, the second with no runs) and `:NocmUncountedRunsRefuseWholeSpanMutations` (all four mutation entry points refuse and the plugin bytes are unchanged), plus `:NocmIndexRowReadsEachRunsIndex` for the row. `Radicle/tools/test_subrecord_group_codegen.py:test_subrecord_group_run_may_be_uncounted` pins the rendered `Signature{}` and `:test_subrecord_group_run_members_cannot_repeat_a_group_member` the shared-signature rejection. `Radicle/tests/test_world_misc_records_real.cpp:NavmeshObstacleReal.NocmRecordKeepsEveryUncountedRunUnderOneModel` asserts the corpus figures above and that every span and run starts and ends with the signature its declaration says it does. Regression caught: a model's runs were previously invisible as a structure, so nothing could tell a `NAM1` that closed a model from one that started the next, and a row on `INDX` could not validate the record it wrote.
- Unverified: the meaning of `DATA` and `INTV` (xEdit names them Unknown and Unknown Datas), and whether `INDX` is an index into anything; xEdit labels it `Index`, so the row only reads and writes the u32. The span boundary rule is taken from the declaration order plus the 87/87 one-model-per-span measurement, not from the engine. Nothing was compiled on this machine, so no C++ test above has run; the corpus figures come from a read-only Python walk of the masters.

## Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans — uncounted span closes on its NAM1 (#602 B-23, NOCM bug)

- Bug: the uncounted branch of `group_spans` ran its trailing-member loop with `last` starting at 0, which is also the index of `NAM1`, the only group member. The first `NAM1` after a model's runs therefore matched the "out of order or repeated" check and threw, so every NOCM span with runs was refused, not only the shape `INDX INTV NAM1 NAM1`. The real-data test `Radicle/tests/test_world_misc_records_real.cpp:NavmeshObstacleReal.NocmRecordKeepsEveryUncountedRunUnderOneModel` would have failed the same way; the synthetic tests in `Radicle/tests/test_nested_group_runs.cpp` did not run here.
- Fix: the uncounted branch takes at most one trailing group member and then closes the span, so a `NAM1` ends its model and the next `NAM1` starts a new span. The counted branch is untouched.
- Shapes after the fix: `INDX INTV NAM1` one span; `INDX INTV NAM1 NAM1` two spans, the second with no runs (the leader path in `Radicle/src/plugin/field_writer_containers.cpp:group_spans` already accepted a leading `NAM1` with no runs); `NAM1` alone a zero-run span, unchanged; `DATA` with no `INDX` still refused by the leader path as "count does not match its nested runs"; `INDX INTV NAM1 DATA` or `... NAM1 INTV` refused the same way because neither is a group member; `INDX DATA NAM1` without `INTV` still refused for the missing required run member; `INDX INTV` with no `NAM1` still refused for the missing required `NAM1`.
- Mutation: `insert_record_subrecord_group`, `remove_record_subrecord_group`, and the run-level entry points still refuse before reading spans for this group, so `NocmUncountedRunsRefuseWholeSpanMutations` is unaffected.
- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_nested_group_runs.cpp:NestedGroupRuns.NocmRunlessModelAfterRunModelIsItsOwnSpan` detects the regression where a model with no runs after a model with runs was refused. `NocmShapeFailuresFailClosed` no longer lists that shape as a refusal.
- Unverified: not compiled and not run on this machine; the reasoning is a line-by-line trace of the uncounted branch against the four `NocmShapeFailuresFailClosed` refusal cases and the `NocmSpansGroupEveryUncountedRunUnderItsModel` offsets.

## Radicle/tools/subrecord_group_render.py:render_subrecord_groups — C++ text for the subrecord group table

`Radicle/tools/subrecord_group_render.py:render_subrecord_groups` turns the parsed subrecord-group rows into C++ lines. For each group it writes a members array `k_subrecord_group_members_N`, an optional successors array `k_subrecord_group_successors_N` and, when the group has a run, a run members array `k_subrecord_group_run_members_N`. Then it writes one `k_subrecord_groups` array of `SubrecordGroupDescriptor` entries, or an empty `std::array` when there are no groups. `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:render` calls it and adds the lines to its output; the rows come from `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py:parse_subrecord_group`.

- `Radicle/tools/subrecord_group_render.py:render_group_members` writes one `SubrecordGroupMemberDescriptor` initializer per member. The subrecord is written with `cpp_signature`, then the required, repeatable and payload-size fields, then a span over the default bytes (or an empty span), then the localized, skippable and leading flags. A member with a default gets its own `constexpr std::uint8_t k_subrecord_group_default_N[]` array; the counter `N` is shared by every group in the table, so the names do not repeat.
- A run's counter is `Signature{}` when `run.count_member` is empty, which is the uncounted-run shape. A group's count subrecord is `Signature{}` when `count_subrecord` is empty. `requires_existing_count` is written as a C++ bool.
- Strings go through `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:cpp_string`, which JSON-escapes the value with ASCII-only output, and signatures go through `Radicle/tools/field_address_codegen.py:cpp_signature`. This module imports both and defines neither, so `Radicle/tools/schema_codegen.py` imports `cpp_string` from the same place.

## NIF writer (apply_edits, write_nif)

- Radicle/src/nif/write_model.cpp:load_model: splits a parsed NIF into the header fields, the string and type tables, the block payloads and the roots, keeping every field as read so a zero-edit write reproduces the input bytes. It throws parse_error when the bytes hold no header line, which covers empty and short input.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_model.cpp:serialize: writes the file back from the model. Block sizes come from the payloads, the endian byte is always 1 (the only value the reader accepts), and the footer is written last so the reader's end-of-file check holds.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_model.cpp:intern_string: reuses an existing string-table entry or appends a new one. Empty text maps to -1. max_string_length is raised only when it is non-zero, because zero means the reader does not check string lengths.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_edits.cpp:shader_block: maps a shape id to its BSLightingShaderProperty through the shape's shader ref at offset 92 + 4 * extra-data count, and accepts a shader id directly. A shader that more than one shape references (counted by `write_edits.cpp:shader_users`, which counts shapes, not shaders) is copied first, and only the edited shape's ref is repointed at the copy. The copy is made once per shape: later edits in the same batch see a shader with one user and write in place. An edit sent on a shader id writes that shader in place, so every shape sharing it changes; the tree has no shader block ids, so the editor does not send them. A material, tex or float edit on a shape whose shader is BSEffectShaderProperty fails in shader_block with "shape has no BSLightingShaderProperty", which aborts the whole batch. PluginEditTool/native/src/assets/NifRender.cpp:shapeTreeBlock puts material and tex0 to tex7 under the shape's block id, so the writer routes them from the shape.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_edits.cpp:apply_texture: writes a slot into the BSShaderTextureSet that the shader references at offset 40 + 4 * extra-data count. A set shared by more than one shader is copied first (copy-on-write), so the other shaders keep their textures. The current slots are parsed from the original set before the copy, so a malformed set throws before any block is appended. `write_edits.cpp:fail` reports offset 0 for a block this batch appended, since it has no file offset. A slot past the end extends the set with empty strings; how the engine treats empty slots is not verified.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_edits.cpp:apply_float_field: writes the k_float_fields entries. translation and scale are AV fields at 16 + 4c and 64 + 4c. Shader fields sit at their NIF.md offsets, 24 to 92 (uvOffset, uvScale, emissive, alpha, smoothness, specular).
- Radicle/src/nif/write_edits.cpp:apply_name: name writes the AV name at offset 0 for nodes and shapes, or the shader name at offset 4 for a shader. material writes the shader name at offset 4, which is the .bgsm path that Shape.material reads. A `name` edit sent to a shader id writes that shader's name, which is the same material path, in place, so every shape that shares the shader changes.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_edits.cpp:apply_edit: unsupported keys (shaderFlags, eff_*, layer, boxDimensions, boxRadius, alphaBlend, alphaTest, alphaThreshold, rotation and any other key) and read-only keys (verts, tris, shaderType) throw parse_error. Alpha keys are unsupported because NIF.md does not define the NiAlphaProperty layout.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_edits.cpp:apply_edits: applies the edits to a model and throws before serializing if any edit fails, so no partial bytes are returned. It ends with read_nif on the output as a self-check.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_edits.cpp:is_shape_type: a copy of the shape-type list in Radicle/src/nif/geometry.cpp, which keeps its list file-local. The copy keeps geometry.cpp untouched.
- Radicle/include/fo4/nif/nif_write.hpp:Edit: has no cat field. The editor sends cat, but the writer routes by block type.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:SharedShaderIsCopiedBeforeAShapeEdit: regression: a translation, float, texture or material edit on one shape changed the other shape that shares its shader. It asserts the other shape keeps its shader ref, its material, and the original shader and texture set blocks byte for byte.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:EditsFollowTheExtraDataCountOnShapeAndShader: regression: with two extra-data refs, a shape translation or shader glossiness or texture slot lands at the wrong offset. It asserts that every changed byte lies inside the field's range.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:ZeroEditRoundTripKeepsExportStringsGroupsAndMaxLength: regression: export strings, max string length or the group table is re-encoded differently, so a zero-edit save changes bytes.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:NameEditReusesAnExistingStringIndex: regression: a name already in the table appends a duplicate entry.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:NameEditAppendsToStringTable: also checks that the root node, which shared string index 0 with the shape, keeps its old name.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:RejectsEditsOnBrokenShapesAndShaders: its shared malformed texture set case is a regression for the copy made before the slots were parsed, which indexed past the file's block table.
- Radicle/tests/nif_fixture.hpp:build_nif: takes optional export strings, max string length and groups, and nif_fixture::shape_block and nif_fixture::lighting_shader_block take an extra-data count that defaults to 0.

## NIF import (import_obj)

- Radicle/src/nif/import_obj.cpp:read_obj: reads `v`, `vt`, `vn`, `f`, and the first `o` or `g` name, and merges every object into one shape. Negative indices count back from the end of their list. Faces are fan-triangulated from their first corner, so only convex faces come out right.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_obj.cpp:parse: rejects an index outside its list, a non-finite number, a zero-length `vn`, and a `vt` past the half-float limit of 65504, so every value that reaches the writer is representable.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_obj.cpp:axis_map: with `from_blender`, maps (x, y, z) to (x, -z, y), which undoes Blender's default OBJ export (Y-up, forward -Z). Not checked against a real Blender export.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_obj.cpp:read_obj: vertices are unique per (position, uv, normal) corner, numbered in first-seen order. A corner without `vn` takes the area-weighted normal of its faces (`smooth_normals`), and a corner without `vt` gets UV (0, 0).
- Radicle/src/nif/import_obj.cpp:add_tangent_frame: the tangent and bitangent are the per-triangle UV gradients averaged per vertex and made orthogonal to the normal. A degenerate UV falls back to a perpendicular axis.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_build.cpp:half_bits: encodes UVs as IEEE half floats, subnormals included.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_build.cpp:unit_byte: normal, tangent and bitangent Y and Z bytes use `round((v + 1) * 127.5)`, which the reader decodes as `b / 255 * 2 - 1`.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_build.cpp:shape_block: writes the AV prefix with flags 14, the bounding sphere, skin -1, shader ref 2, alpha -1, the descriptor `0x41B << 44 | 0x650400 | 7` (position, UV, normal, tangent, full precision, stride 28; the offset nibbles put UV at 16, normal at 20, tangent at 24, equal to the vanilla corpus descriptor 0x0041b00000650407 in `Radicle/docs/NIF.md`); `NifImport.QuadRoundTrips...` pins those eight bytes because the reader ignores the nibbles, the counts, the 28-byte vertices and u16 indices. The byte order follows `nif_fixture::shape_block`.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_build.cpp:shader_block: a 140-byte BSLightingShaderProperty with the defaults of `nif_fixture::lighting_shader_block`. The flags1 `0x80400201` and flags2 `0x21` are copied from `nif_fixture::full_nif`, not from a game file.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_build.cpp:texture_set_block: 10 slots, slot 0 diffuse and slot 1 normal, the rest empty. `Radicle/docs/NIF.md` gives 10 slots per texture set across the corpus.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_build.cpp:import_obj: refuses box collision because there is no collision writer, refuses more than 65535 unique vertices because the u16 indices would wrap, and reads its own output back with `read_nif` and `read_shapes`, throwing unless the result is one shape with no warning and the same vertex and index counts.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_build.cpp:import_obj: UV v is written as given. Blender and OBJ use a bottom-left origin and NIF uses top-left, so the textures may need the v flip until they are checked in game or against niftool.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:QuadRoundTripsNamesTexturesPositionsUvsNormalsAndTriangles: regression: a wrong vertex stride, UV or normal byte encode, fan split or texture slot order breaks the read-back.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:TangentFrameFollowsTheUvAxesWithSmoothedNormals: regression: a swapped or flipped tangent frame, or smoothed normals facing the wrong way, makes normal maps light the wrong way.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:BlenderYUpExportIsRestoredToZUp: regression: from_blender is ignored or its axes are mapped the wrong way.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:RejectsObjThatWouldWriteAWrongNif: regression: an OBJ with no faces, a bad index, an overflowing UV or a NaN position is written as garbage instead of failing.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:BoxCollisionIsRejectedInsteadOfDropped: regression: a box collision request is dropped, so the NIF has no collision the user asked for.
- Radicle/tests/test_nif_write.cpp:RejectsMoreVerticesThanAShapeCanIndex: regression: indices past 65535 wrap to 16 bits and the NIF reads back as a different mesh.
## Radicle/src/papyrus/resolver.cpp:Resolver::resolve (PET semantic layer, piece 2 of the Papyrus lift)

- What moved. PluginEditTool's native Type, Binding, Resolver, TypeChecker, ScriptIndex and Symbols are now `fo4::papyrus` in `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/type.hpp`, `binding.hpp`, `resolver.hpp`, `type_checker.hpp`, `script_index.hpp` and `symbols.hpp`, with definitions in `Radicle/src/papyrus/type.cpp`, `binding.cpp`, `resolver.cpp`, `type_checker.cpp`, `script_index.cpp` and `symbols.cpp`. `Radicle/src/papyrus/declaration_check.cpp:declarationCheck` is PET's `declarationCheck` function alone, lifted out of `CodeGenerator.cpp` (lines 216 to 293, section header dropped); the rest of CodeGenerator, the user-flag table, the compiler and the decompiler were lifted in later pieces (`Radicle/src/papyrus/code_generator.cpp`, `user_flags.cpp`, `compile_script.cpp`, `decompiler.cpp`). `Radicle/src/papyrus/file_walk.cpp:enumeratePapyrusFiles` is PET's `walkPapyrusFiles` body lifted out of `AnalysisService.cpp` with the two file-local helpers it uses (`iequals`, `lower`); PET's one-line forwarder is folded away. `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/script_names.hpp:safeScriptObjectName` is PET's `ScriptNames.hpp` at the same path, namespace changed. Nothing from PluginEditTool is included, no C ABI was added and `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is untouched. `fo4::psc` and `fo4::pex_analysis` declare none of these names, so the namespace does not clash with them.

- Byte-level fidelity was checked, not assumed. Each lifted header and source was compared with PET's after removing comment-only lines and blank lines and folding the namespace and include paths: zero differing lines for all twelve semantic files. `declarationCheck` matches PET's `CodeGenerator.cpp` lines 219 to 293 with zero differing lines. The walk differs from PET only by the dropped forwarder. Beyond namespace and includes the only edits are comment removal and the two lifetime constraint lines in `binding.hpp` and `script_index.hpp`.

- Comments removed from the source, and where their reasoning now lives. Each entry says what the removed comment established.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/type.hpp:TypeKind` is the port of PET's `PapyrusTypeKind`.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/type.hpp:Type` has value semantics with structural equality. The element type of an array is held through `std::shared_ptr`, because an array can hold any type including another array. Primitives are static singletons.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/type.hpp:Type::primitive` looks a primitive up case-insensitively and returns nullptr when the name is not a primitive.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/type.hpp:isImplicit` and `isExplicit` are the port of PET's `PapyrusConversions`. Their `inherits` argument is the caller's "child extends ancestor" predicate, and the default answers that nothing inherits, so a bare call never invents a subclass relation.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/binding.hpp:BindingKind` is the port of `PapyrusBindingKind`.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/binding.hpp:Binding` points its `declaration` and `owner` into a Script that the ScriptIndex cache owns, so the index must outlive any binding it produced. The constraint line above `Resolution` states the same rule.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/binding.hpp:Resolution` maps are keyed on node identity. Expression and statement nodes are heap-allocated and keep a stable address; declaration nodes are value members of the parsed Script and are stable once parsing has finished; TypeRefs are value members too and are keyed by address. A change in any of those storage choices silently breaks every lookup, which is why the key type is a pointer.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/resolver.hpp:Resolver` is the port of `PapyrusResolver`. It binds every identifier, member and call site to a declaration or keyword and computes the type of every expression. Diagnostics are gated on the base chain being complete: a missing parent or a missing import suppresses name reporting, mirroring the C# oracle, so "no errors" never means "could not tell". `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/binding.hpp:Resolution` carries that flag as `baseChainComplete`.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/resolver.hpp:Resolver::resolveTypeName` resolves a type name for both the resolver and the type checker: primitives, structs on the base chain, `Owner:Struct`, and scripts. It returns nullopt when the name cannot be resolved.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/resolver.hpp:Resolver::Context` keeps its scope stack keyed by lowercased name, because Papyrus is case-insensitive like the C# oracle. Its `ownedBindings` and `ownedTypes` are deques so that the pointers handed out by `lookupName`, `bindingFor` and `computeType` stay valid while more entries are appended.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/resolver.hpp:Resolver` (the private expression entry points) take `Node*` and downcast internally, because the AST stores expressions as `unique_ptr<Node>`.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/type_checker.hpp:TypeChecker` is the port of `PapyrusTypeChecker`. It consumes a `Resolution` and reports type mismatches, argument-count and argument-name problems, invalid casts, override mismatches and parameter-order errors. It reports nothing when the base chain is incomplete, for the same reason the resolver does.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/type_checker.hpp:TypeChecker::inherits` writes to `inheritsCache_`, so every member stays non-const, as in the C# oracle, which has no const methods either.

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/type_checker.cpp:visitChildExpressions` mirrors the C# `CheckExpression` default arm: it walks the children and re-checks any child expression. Call, Cast and Index are handled before the default arm reaches it.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/script_index.hpp:ScriptIndex` is the port of `PapyrusScriptIndex`. It walks its roots for `.psc` files, resolves a script name to a file (qualified name, then bare last segment), parses on demand through an `(size, mtime)`-keyed cache, and computes base chains. The index owns every parsed Script; the constraint line above the class states that the index must outlive the bindings and resolutions.

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/script_index.cpp:ScriptIndex::findFile` tries the qualified name first and falls back to the bare last segment. A name with no colon is its own bare name.

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/script_index.cpp:ScriptIndex::resolve` returns the parsed Script for a name, or nullptr when the name is on no root.

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/script_index.cpp:ScriptIndex::parseCached` returns nullptr on an I/O failure or on a parse that cannot produce a Script at all. Hazard, carried over from PET unchanged: when the file's size or mtime changes, the cache entry's `unique_ptr` is replaced, so a Script pointer returned before the edit is freed. Callers must not hold a `Script*` across an edit to the file.

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/script_index.cpp:ScriptIndex::baseChain` follows `Extends` into `[script, parent, grandparent, ...]` and is guarded against cycles. It is non-const because resolving a parent may populate the parse cache, as in the C#.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/script_index.hpp:ScriptIndex::byQualifiedName_` keys are lowercased and the values keep the canonical spelling. `Radicle/src/papyrus/script_index.cpp:ScriptIndex::scriptNames` returns the names sorted with an ordinal ignore-case comparison, mirroring the C# `ScriptNames`.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/script_index.hpp:ScriptIndex::parsed_` is keyed by the absolute path string.

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/script_index.cpp:qualifiedNameOf` recomputes the qualified name from the file's on-disk path so the returned names keep their original casing, as the C# does (it keys by `QualifiedNameFor` and exposes the keys as ScriptNames). If no root contains the path it falls back to the lowercased key; that should not happen.

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/script_index.cpp:ScriptIndex::addRoot` is a manual depth-first walk that mirrors `PapyrusFileWalk`: case-insensitive `.psc` match, and symlinked directories are skipped (the C# checks that `LinkTarget` is null). The `..` check is defensive because `Path.GetRelativePath` never yields `..` for a file under its root. Roots are de-duplicated ignoring case, and the first root to provide a qualified name keeps it.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/symbols.hpp:SymbolKind` is ordered the same as the C# enum so the names serialize identically.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/symbols.hpp:Symbol` is the port of `PapyrusSymbol`. `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/symbols.hpp:AstPathEntry` is one entry on the C# generic node path. TypeRefs are value members of the AST rather than nodes, so a path entry is either a node or a type reference.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/symbols.hpp:pathTo` returns the chain of ancestors of the innermost node whose span contains the offset, root first, including TypeRef entries where the C# tree carries a type-reference node. It is empty when nothing contains the offset.

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/symbols.cpp:childrenOf` lists a node's children in the C# enumeration order. Grouped properties sit under their group, as in the C# `Properties.Where(p => p.GroupName == null)`, and an IfBranch reports the same NodeKind as an if statement but carries a condition and a body instead of branches. `Radicle/src/papyrus/symbols.cpp:ChildRef` holds either a node or a type reference.

- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/symbols.hpp:Symbols` provides the document outline and name-based definition lookup (locals, parameters, this script's members, the Extends chain, imports, script names). It resolves by name only, with no type checker, so a member reached through an expression whose type is not written down cannot be resolved; it returns null rather than a guess.

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/symbols.cpp:resolveTypeName` honours `#` as well as `:` in qualified names, because PET's decompiler emits `Script#Struct` type names. The C# oracle rejects `#`; this is the same divergence noted for the front end above, carried over unchanged.

- Tests. `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_resolver.cpp`, `test_papyrus_type_checker.cpp` and `test_papyrus_symbols.cpp` are case-for-case ports of PET's `PapyrusResolverTests`, `PapyrusTypeCheckerTests` and `PapyrusSymbolsTests` (Catch2 to gtest, test names from the PET titles). Helper-level `REQUIRE` and `FAIL` became `throw std::runtime_error`, because a gtest `ASSERT_*` cannot return from a helper that returns a value. `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_script_index.cpp` and `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_declaration_check.cpp` are new focused unit tests: PET has no native unit test for `ScriptIndex`, `enumeratePapyrusFiles` or the duplicate check, only corpus sweeps. `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_semantic_real.cpp` holds the corpus gates: the symbols sweep (ported from PET's `PapyrusCorpusTests`), the duplicate-declaration sweep (ported, on `FO4RE_PSC_ROOTS`), and the new resolve and type-check gate over complete scripts on `FO4RE_PSC_CORPUS`, which asserts 7,832 complete scripts when the corpus has the documented 7,854 files.

- Not in this lift. PET's `ScriptIndex` has no in-memory overlay root; the graph's self-reference publish is a PET graph concern. Codegen, the compiler, user flags and the decompiler were lifted in later pieces (`Radicle/src/papyrus/compile_script.cpp:compileScript`, `Radicle/src/papyrus/decompiler.cpp:Decompiler::toSource`). Recursion depth in `Resolver`, `TypeChecker` and `childrenOf` is unbounded, as it is in PET; a hostile script could exhaust the stack, which is untested here.
## Radicle/src/f4se/emitter.cpp:F4SEEmitter (PET F4SE binding emitter, the F4SE lift)

- What moved and from where. PluginEditTool's native F4SE emit logic is now Radicle's: `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/binding_model.hpp`, `binding_validator.hpp`, `cpp_emitter.hpp`, `cpp_scanner.hpp`, `cross_check.hpp`, `emitter.hpp`, `native_oracle.hpp`, `papyrus_header_emitter.hpp`, `plugin_emitter.hpp`, `region_merge.hpp`, `registration_extractor.hpp`, `type_map.hpp` and `version_diff.hpp`, with the definitions in the matching `Radicle/src/f4se/*.cpp`. The namespace is `fo4::f4se` and the file names are snake_case. The lift is mechanical: the code changes are the namespace, the include paths, the graph diagnostic dependency and the removal of comment text. Every emitted string (including the `FO4IDE_BODY` markers and the README `git clone` lines) is unchanged from PET's. Radicle includes nothing from PluginEditTool, no C ABI export was added and `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` is untouched.
- The graph dependency. PET's `F4SEEmitter`, `BindingValidator` and their diagnostics used `fo4ide::graph::GraphDiagnostic`. Radicle's F4SE code now reaches the lifted graph types through `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/diagnostic.hpp:Diagnostic`, `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/diagnostic.hpp:DiagnosticSeverity`, `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/diagnostic.hpp:errorDiagnostic` and `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/diagnostic.hpp:codes`, which alias `fo4::graph::GraphDiagnostic`, `GraphSeverity`, `errorDiagnostic` and `fo4::graph::codes`. The nine F4SE code strings are unchanged: `kDuplicateVariableName` GRA0032, `kArgumentCount` GRA0034, `kDuplicateDeclaration` GRA0037, `kDuplicateNativeBinding` GRA0050, `kNativeArityUnsupported` GRA0051, `kUnmappedNativeType` GRA0052, `kInvalidBindingName` GRA0054, `kStructOwnerMismatch` GRA0055 and `kNoModules` GRA0056. They stay GRA-coded because they are the user-visible validation codes, and they now live in the graph's code table.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/emitter.cpp:F4SEEmitter::emit` runs validation, then emits every module's `.h`, `.cpp` and `.psc`, the registrations aggregator and the shell files, and finally merges preserved bodies from the previous emit. `F4SEEmitOptions` (`Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/emitter.hpp:F4SEEmitOptions`) carries the previous emit's files for body preservation and the escape hatch that emits even when validation reports errors. `F4SEEmitResult::errors` keeps only `DiagnosticSeverity::Error` items. `F4SEEmitResult::file` is a case-insensitive path lookup, mirroring the C# `File(relativePath)`. `F4SEEmitter::roundTrip` recovers the emitted `.cpp` registrations and cross-checks them against the emitted `.psc` declarations.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/binding_model.hpp:F4SETarget` is the two F4SE targets. The original target exports the query entry point and checks the runtime; the next generation target exports the version data instead. `NativeParameter`, `NativeBinding` (with `noWait`, `isLatent`, the C++ base type and function name), `StructMemberBinding`, `StructBinding` (qualified by `ownerScript`), `ModuleBinding` (one emitted module), `MessageSubscription` (a message name to a handler, emitted as a dispatch case) and `PluginBinding` are the model the emitter reads. `PluginBinding::allNatives` and `PluginBinding::allStructs` are flat views over every module. `EmittedFile` is one emitted file's relative path and text.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/binding_validator.cpp:BindingValidator::validateModules` refuses two modules writing the same script (case-insensitive). `BindingValidator::validateStructs` refuses duplicate struct names, case-sensitive, matching the C# `GroupBy` with `Ordinal`. `BindingValidator::validateNatives` refuses a duplicate (class, function) pair, case-insensitive, and a required parameter after an optional one. `BindingValidator::kMaximumArity` (10) is the template family limit. `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/binding_validator.hpp:BindingValidator` is the pre-emit validation pass that produces the GRA-coded diagnostics.
