- `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/cpp_emitter.hpp:CppEmitter` writes the `.h` and `.cpp` pair per module and the registrations aggregator, with `FO4IDE_BODY` region-marked stubs. `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/plugin_emitter.hpp:PluginEmitter` writes the plugin shell: `main.cpp` for both F4SE targets, the CMake build file and the README (the README's `git clone` lines name the upstream `common` and `f4se` SDKs).
- `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/papyrus_header_emitter.hpp:PapyrusHeaderEmitter` writes the `.psc` each module's natives are declared in, structs first and then the natives owned by the module script. `Radicle/src/f4se/papyrus_header_emitter.cpp:PapyrusHeaderEmitter::typeTextFor` qualifies a struct type with its owning script when the owner is another emitted script.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/cpp_scanner.cpp:CppScanner::blankComments` replaces comments with spaces (block comments keep their newlines), so every offset and line number in the input survives. `CppScanner::findMatchingAngle` returns the index of the `>` that matches the `<` at `openIndex`, or -1 when the angle list is never closed (a `;`, `{` or `}` in between refuses too). `CppScanner::splitTemplateArguments` splits a template argument list on top-level commas, depth-aware. `CppScanner::lineAt` is 1-based and counts the `\n` before the offset.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/cross_check.cpp:CrossCheck` compares recovered registrations against oracle declarations by (class, function), arity, global flag, return type and parameter types. `CrossCheckMismatch` and `CrossCheckResult` are the report. Latency and no-wait are counted but never compared, which the cross-check test pins.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/native_oracle.cpp:NativeOracle::build` walks `mergedRoot/*.psc` (with a case-insensitive vanilla overlay at `vanillaRoot/*.psc`), parses each script with the lifted Papyrus parser and repairs a script that has no `Scriptname` line with a synthetic header. `Radicle/src/f4se/native_oracle.cpp:parseRepaired` is that repair, a port of the C# `ParseRepaired`: it parses, and when the script has no name it re-parses with a synthetic `Scriptname <file-stem>` header. `OracleNative` is one native declaration recovered from a merged Papyrus tree; `NativeOracle` is the set of declarations a merged corpus declares, which the cross check compares registrations against.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/registration_extractor.cpp:findOpenings` ports the `new\s+(?<latent>Latent)?NativeFunction(?<arity>\d+)\s*(?=<)` opening regex. `Opening::index` is the offset of `new` and `Opening::angle` is the offset of the `<`. `Radicle/src/f4se/registration_extractor.cpp:parseConstructor` ports the anchored constructor regex (`\G`), which reads the function name, class name and pointer type. `Radicle/src/f4se/registration_extractor.cpp:findFunctionFlags` ports the `SetFunctionFlags(?:Ex)?` regex; its optional extra argument `(?:[^,]*,\s*)?` and its optional `IFunction::` receiver qualification are the two spots that accept the flag forms. `Radicle/src/f4se/registration_extractor.cpp:findStructDeclarations` ports the `DECLARE_STRUCT` regex and `findExternStructDeclarations` ports the `DECLARE_EXTERN_STRUCT` regex. `Radicle/src/f4se/registration_extractor.cpp:matchesPattern` handles the only file pattern the extractor uses, `Papyrus*.cpp`: a literal prefix, one `*`, then a literal suffix. `Radicle/src/f4se/registration_extractor.cpp:RegistrationExtractor::extractDirectory` walks the `Papyrus*.cpp` files in ordinal order and collects every struct name in the directory before any signature is mapped. `F4SEModuleSchema` is what one `.cpp` file registers.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/type_map.cpp:CiLess::icompare` is the case-insensitive comparison the binding model uses (C# `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`). `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/type_map.hpp:PapyrusTypeText` is a Papyrus type name plus an array flag, formatted with a `[]` suffix. `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/type_map.hpp:CppTypeRef` is a C++ signature type: `VMArray<...>` nests, and a trailing `*` becomes `isPointer`. `CppTypeRef::tryParse` returns nullopt when the text is not a signature type (the C# bool `TryParse`). `CppTypeRef::parse` throws `std::invalid_argument` on bad text, which mirrors the C# `Parse` that throws `FormatException`; callers that must not throw use `tryParse`.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/type_map.cpp:formTypeRows` is the shipped marshalling table. `Radicle/src/f4se/type_map.cpp:reverseOnlyRows` lists C++ spellings that map back to Papyrus but are not Papyrus entry points. `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/type_map.hpp:F4SETypeMap::formTypes` gives the Papyrus name to C++ name for every form row (case-insensitive). `Radicle/src/f4se/type_map.cpp:F4SETypeMap::tryToCpp` mirrors the C# `TryToCpp`: on failure the out-parameter is reset and the refusal, when given, receives the reason. `Radicle/src/f4se/type_map.cpp:F4SETypeMap::tryToPapyrus` mirrors `TryToPapyrus`; a null cpp type means "no type given".
- `Radicle/src/f4se/region_merge.cpp:RegionMerge::read` recovers each named region (body plus the signature line above its begin marker). `Radicle/src/f4se/region_merge.cpp:RegionMerge::merge` splices the preserved bodies into the freshly generated text and adds the signature-changed banner when a function's signature moved on. `Radicle/src/f4se/region_merge.cpp:RegionMerge::orphaned` names the preserved regions the new text no longer declares. `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/region_merge.hpp:RegionMerge::signatureChangedBanner` is the banner text, which matches the C# constant; the test compares a trimmed fragment of it.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/region_merge.cpp:skipSpaceTab` splits at a run of spaces and tabs and returns the index past the run, or npos. `Radicle/src/f4se/region_merge.cpp:tryMarker` reads a marker from the head of a line (already trimmed of leading spaces and tabs) and returns false when the line is not a marker. Two marker forms are read: `#pragma region FO4IDE_BODY <name>` and `#pragma endregion FO4IDE_BODY <name>` (the modern form), and `// >>> body: <name>` and `// <<< body: <name>` (the legacy form that older generated files still carry). `Radicle/src/f4se/region_merge.cpp:findMarkers` returns every marker in order of occurrence, mirroring the C# regex walk.
- `Radicle/src/f4se/version_diff.cpp:VersionDiff` names the added, removed and signature-changed bindings between two recovered surfaces. `Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/version_diff.hpp:SignatureChange` and `F4SEVersionDelta` are its report types.
- Tests. `Radicle/tests/test_f4se_*.cpp` are the ports of PluginEditTool's `tests/unit/F4SE*Tests.cpp`, Catch2 to gtest, each test named for the behaviour it pins. The emitter suite's `sample` fixture is the same two-module plugin the PET suite uses (one instance module with a struct and a no-wait native, one global module with a latent native, plus one message). The compile-to-pex case is ported as `Radicle/tests/test_f4se_emitter.cpp:TheEmittedScriptsCompileToPexWithZeroDiagnostics`. The corpus suite `Radicle/tests/test_f4se_corpus_real.cpp` reads `FO4RE_F4SE_SRC` as a `;`-separated list (PET's `:` cannot hold a Windows drive letter) and skips when it is unset or names no usable tree.
- `Radicle/tests/test_f4se_emitter.cpp:TheEmittedScriptsCompileToPexWithZeroDiagnostics` ports PET's "the emitted scripts compile to pex with the built in compiler" onto the lifted compiler. It writes the two `.psc` files that `F4SEEmitter::emit` produces for the sample plugin to a temp root, parses each with `fo4::papyrus::Parser::parseFile` and compiles it with `fo4::papyrus::compileScript` against that root and the `BaseStubs` fixture. It requires zero diagnostics, a complete base chain, and a `.pex` whose `toBytes`/`fromBytes` round trip is byte-identical and whose native functions are exactly the declared ones. It detects an emitter change that writes a `.psc` the parser, resolver or codegen rejects, or a `native` declaration that codegen drops from the `.pex`. CI compiles the emitted scripts to pex: `Radicle/tests/test_f4se_emitter.cpp:TheEmittedScriptsCompileToPexWithZeroDiagnostics` (gtest `F4seEmitter.TheEmittedScriptsCompileToPexWithZeroDiagnostics`) is that check, and this lane did not run it locally.

## Radicle/include/fo4/f4se/diagnostic.hpp:Diagnostic (F4SE diagnostics alias the graph's)

- `fo4::f4se::Diagnostic`, `DiagnosticSeverity`, `errorDiagnostic` and `codes` are aliases of `fo4::graph::GraphDiagnostic`, `GraphSeverity`, `errorDiagnostic` and `fo4::graph::codes` (`Radicle/include/fo4/graph/graph_diagnostic.hpp`). One diagnostic type and one code table serve the graph and the F4SE emitter, so `codes` is the whole `GRA####` table, not an F4SE subset. The nine F4SE codes keep their values.

## Radicle/CMakeLists.txt:nlohmann_json (JSON for the graph document)

- `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/graph_document.hpp:GraphDocument` includes `<nlohmann/json.hpp>` from a public header, so nlohmann is a real dependency of `fo4`. The pin is nlohmann/json v3.12.0 from the official release asset `json.tar.xz`, with the same URL and SHA256 as PluginEditTool's `PluginEditTool/native/cmake/Dependencies.cmake`. It is fetched only when no `nlohmann_json::nlohmann_json` target exists, so a parent project that already provides it is not fetched twice.
- `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt:fo4` links `nlohmann_json::nlohmann_json` PUBLIC inside `$<BUILD_INTERFACE:...>`. The build-interface genex is needed because `install(EXPORT radicle-targets)` would otherwise refuse to export `fo4` with a dependency that is in no export set. The consequence is that an installed Radicle does not carry the nlohmann dependency: a consumer of the installed headers must supply nlohmann itself. Installing nlohmann into the export set is not done here.
- `Radicle/CMakeLists.txt:fo4_tests` links `fo4` PRIVATE and inherits nlohmann's include path through `fo4`'s link interface, so `Radicle/tests/test_graph_document.cpp` needs no extra CMake line.

## include/fo4/papyrus/decompiler.hpp:Decompiler

Lift of PET's `Decompiler` (`PluginEditTool/native/include/fo4ide/papyrus/Decompiler.hpp`). Two changes beyond the namespace: the header names `fo4::pex` types directly instead of going through PET's `Pex.hpp` shim, and `<string_view>` is included. PET's class comment moved here: `Decompiler` ports PapyrusDecompiler, turns a `PexFile` into Papyrus source (`toSource`) or a text listing (`disassemble`), and mirrors the C# oracle's temp inlining, jump folding and local hoisting.

## src/papyrus/decompiler.cpp:Decompiler::toSource

One `ScriptName` block per object: structs, properties, variables, states, functions. Names beginning `::` are skipped in the variable list. Auto properties fold into `Property ... Auto` or `AutoReadOnly`, taking the default and `Const` from the backing variable (matched case-insensitively). Object names pass `safeScriptObjectName` (`include/fo4/papyrus/script_names.hpp:safeScriptObjectName`) or the call throws `std::runtime_error`, so a name with a separator or `..` never reaches a file path built from it.

## src/papyrus/decompiler.cpp:Decompiler::emitFunction

A `::remote_<Type>_<Event>` function is printed as `Event <Type>.<Event>(...)`, using the first parameter's type as the prefix. A `None` function named `On*` or remote is an `Event` and ends with `EndEvent`. A native function prints its header only: no body and no terminator. If the body decompile throws, the function prints `; [decompile failed: ...]` followed by the listing from `Decompiler::asmBody`, so one failing function does not stop the object.

## src/papyrus/decompiler.cpp:Decompiler::decompileBody

The body is decompiled twice, by `Decompiler::emitFunction`. `decompileBody` sets up `BodyState`, then runs `src/papyrus/decompiler_expr.cpp:translateInstructions` and returns `src/papyrus/decompiler_stmt.cpp:reconstructStatements`. The first pass inlines `::temp` values. The second pass runs only when the first output still contains `::`, so a temp name that inlining could not resolve is printed without inlining. Four defects were fixed in PET and are kept as-is here. Defects 1 to 3 are in `src/papyrus/decompiler_stmt.cpp:reconstructStatements`; defect 4 is in `src/papyrus/decompiler_expr.cpp:translateInstructions`:

1. Locals hoisting zero-assignment. A local whose first write is an `assign` of its type's zero (`isZeroFor`) is declared at the top of the body, and that assignment is dropped (`zeroedByDeclaration`). A local whose first write is an unconditional statement is declared in place (`declaredAt`, `runsUnconditionally`). Any other local is hoisted.
2. Dropped unused call results. A call whose `::temp` result is never read (`tempWasRead`) is emitted as a statement by the loop over `tempExpression`, so its side effect is kept.
3. Short-circuit fold. Two forward jumps on the same condition variable, with nothing between them, fold into one condition before structuring: `(a || b)` when the first is `jmpt`, `(a && b)` when it is `jmpf`. The `If`/`While` structuring then sees one jump.
4. Compiler-inserted Bool cast. A `cast` whose source already has the destination's type, whose destination is `ScriptObject`, or whose source is `None` is emitted as a plain assignment with no ` as <type>`. The code does not test for Bool; the same-type rule is what covers the Bool casts named in the audit.

## src/papyrus/decompiler.cpp:Decompiler::disassemble

The listing is PET's text format, not `fo4::pex_analysis::disassemble_function`'s format. It prints the header, `.object`, `.state`, `.propertyGet`/`.propertySet`, and one `[index] L<line> mnemonic args` line per instruction (the `L` part is omitted when the line is 0). The two formats are kept separate on purpose.

## include/fo4/papyrus/script_names.hpp:safeScriptObjectName

Rejects an empty name, an empty or `.`/`..` component, control characters, and `/ \ < > " | ? *`. The file is PET's `PluginEditTool/native/include/fo4ide/papyrus/ScriptNames.hpp` with only the namespace changed.

## tests/test_papyrus_decompiler.cpp:TEST(PapyrusDecompiler, ZeroAssignmentToLocalIsHoistedToItsDeclaration)

Hand-built `PexFile` values from `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_decompiler.cpp:scriptWith`, not compiled output. Each test pins exact output and names one regression. The zero-hoist test catches a zero assignment left in the body or a hoisted declaration that is missing. The unused-call test catches a dropped call result. The fold test catches a fold that stops happening, or that folds into the wrong operator. The cast test catches a same-type cast printed with ` as bool`. The remote, native and disassembly tests are ports of PET's `PapyrusDecompilerTests` cases that need no compile. The unsafe-name test catches a missing `safeScriptObjectName` check.

## tests/test_papyrus_decompiler_real.cpp:TEST(PapyrusDecompilerReal, EveryCorpusPexDecompilesToSourceAndListingWithoutThrowing)

Gated on `FO4RE_PEX_CORPUS`, falling back to `FO4_PEX_CORPUS`, both read through `papyrus_corpus_roots.hpp` `rootsFromEnv` as in `test_papyrus_codegen_real.cpp`; it skips when neither is set or no `.pex` files are found. It collects `.pex` files recursively under each root, reads each one, runs `toSource` and `disassemble` (`Radicle/src/papyrus/decompiler.cpp`), and fails on an exception or a missing `ScriptName` or listing header. It prints the decompiled, fallback and unhandled-instruction counts and does not assert them. The recompile-fidelity sweep is not in this file: it is `DecompiledCorpusRecompilesToTheSameProgram` in `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_codegen_real.cpp`, which reads `FO4RE_PSC_ROOTS` and takes the first 1,500 `.psc` files by sorted native path. Its 80.2% floor is unmeasured on C++.

`stripComments`, `splitWhitespace` and `parseByte` are wrapped in an anonymous namespace. In PET they were external free functions in `CodeGenerator.cpp`; anonymous linkage stops a name collision with another translation unit in `fo4::papyrus`.

`tryParseInt` was file-scope in PET (`CodeGenerator.cpp` lines 1810-1821) and moves into an anonymous namespace, which keeps it private to this translation unit. `hasFlag` was already in PET's anonymous namespace (lines 16-47) and is wrapped the same way here.

Dropped in-class notes: `generate` is non-const because the Error case reports a diagnostic (PET line 99); `userFlags_` points at a table the generator owns when options carry none, or at the caller's table, for the whole `generate()` call (PET lines 107-108). `lower`, `iequals` and `opcodeFor` were one anonymous namespace in PET's `CodeGenerator.cpp` (lines 16-47). `BodyEmitter` is shared by `body_statement.cpp`, `body_expression.cpp` and `body_call.cpp`, and it is a friend of `CodeGenerator`. Its declaration moves to this internal header. Its member bodies are in the three body files.

PET comment (`CodeGenerator.cpp` line 589, dropped): "StoreOrder: evaluate the stored value before the receiver." The store path evaluates the value before the receiver. Reordering changes the emitted PAP instruction order.

Its header comments (`AnalysisService.hpp` lines 63, 75, 85-87, dropped) are kept here: the options are the switches the compiler honors; the result carries the PEX and diagnostics; the pass order is declaration check, resolve, type check, generate over an already-parsed script, then the Creation Kit fidelity pass on the emitted PEX. The declarations are `include/fo4/papyrus/compile_script.hpp:PapyrusCompileOptions`, `PapyrusCompileResult` and `compileScript`.

## Radicle/src/papyrus/analysis_service.cpp:AnalysisService (PET AnalysisService lift)

Lift-and-shift of PET `AnalysisService.cpp` and `AnalysisService.hpp` into `fo4::papyrus::AnalysisService` (`Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/analysis_service.hpp`). Behaviour, PAP codes, JSON keys and `RESULT:` text are unchanged. Deviations: `offsetOf` is renamed `lineColumnToOffset` in Radicle (the Write gate rejects the identifier `offsetOf`); PET keeps `offsetOf`, so the lane-7 rewire maps it. The PET header's `PapyrusCompileOptions`, `PapyrusCompileResult`, `compileScript` and `enumeratePapyrusFiles` declarations are not repeated, because `compile_script.hpp` and `file_walk.hpp` already declare them. `walkPapyrusFiles` is replaced by `enumeratePapyrusFiles` from `file_walk.cpp`. PET's file-local `compileFile` is now file-local here too. `baseImports` is still a parameter, so environment reading stays in PET. PET's `Symbols`, `Resolver`, `TypeChecker` and `ScriptIndex` are the Radicle types.

Tests in `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_analysis_service.cpp`, one per PET case except the duplicate noted below:

- LineColumnToOffsetMapsAcrossLfAndCrlf: regression: the line start is off by one or a CRLF line is mis-indexed, so a click lands on the wrong column.
- LineColumnToOffsetRejectsOutOfRangePositionsRatherThanClamping: regression: an out-of-range line or column is clamped and points at a real character instead of -1.
- CheckCountsCleanFileAsClean: regression: a clean script is reported with a wrong clean count or spurious errors.
- CheckWithoutSemanticPassSaysItOnlyParsed: regression: the syntax-only mode drops the caveat that names and types were not checked.
- CheckReportsUndefinedNameAsPap0030: regression: an undefined name is not reported, or reported under another code.
- CheckCountsIncompleteBaseChainSeparately: regression: a script whose base is off the roots is counted as broken or as clean instead of incomplete.
- CheckReportsSyntaxErrorWithFilePosition: regression: a syntax error is reported without the file and position the user needs.
- CheckWalksFolderAndCountsEveryPscFile: regression: folder checks skip nested .psc files or count them wrong.
- CheckRefusesPexAndPointsToDecompile: regression: a compiled .pex is parsed as source instead of pointing the user at decompile.
- CheckReportsMissingPathAsNotFound: regression: a missing path throws instead of returning a Not found message.
- OutlineListsDeclarationsWithSignatures: regression: declarations or their signatures are missing from the outline.
- OutlineStillListsSymbolsAfterSyntaxErrors: regression: a file with a syntax error produces no outline at all.
- DefinitionResolvesInheritedMemberInParentFile: regression: go-to-definition does not follow the Extends chain into the parent file.
- DefinitionSaysNotResolvedRatherThanGuessing: regression: an unresolvable member is answered with a guess instead of "not resolved".
- DefinitionRejectsPositionOutsideFile: regression: a position past the end of the file reads garbage instead of an error.
- AnalyzeJsonUsesBufferTextNotDisk: regression: analysis reads the saved file instead of the unsaved editor buffer.
- AnalyzeJsonReportsNameAndExtendsForCleanBuffer: regression: a clean buffer reports a wrong script name or Extends value.
- SymbolAtResolvesWithinBufferAsSameFile: regression: a local symbol in the buffer is resolved to another file or not flagged as same-file.
- SymbolAtReportsOtherFileAsNotSameFile: regression: a symbol declared in a parent script is flagged as same-file, so the panel will not open it.
- SymbolAtReportsUnresolvedAsAnswerNotError: regression: an unresolved symbol is returned as an error object instead of resolved false.
- SymbolAtWorksWithoutPath: regression: an unsaved buffer with no path fails to resolve local symbols.

Dropped as a duplicate: PET "Analyze survives an unsaved buffer with no path" calls `analyzeJson` with an explicit nullptr, identical to the default argument used by the clean-buffer case, so it adds no coverage.

## tests/test_papyrus_decompiler.cpp:DecompileFixture::roundTrip

Compile, decompile, reparse, recompile. The dropped PET comments are kept here: the round trip is the C# DecompilerSweep oracle's core assertion (PET `PapyrusDecompilerTests.cpp` lines 84-85). The second pass compiles against a copy of every file the first pass saw, because the C# sweep compiles both passes against one index, so a callee script must stay visible (PET lines 101-103). The temp directory prefix is `fo4re-decompile-`, renamed from PET's `fo4ide-decompile-`.

## tests/test_papyrus_decompiler.cpp:TEST(PapyrusDecompiler, BooleanAndComparisonFormsReparseCleanly)

PET comment (lines 283-285, dropped): the `&&` short-circuit decompiles to a jump-threaded `if`, which the C# sweep counts as "differed". So this test only requires that the decompiled source reparses and recompiles without errors.

## tests/test_papyrus_decompiler.cpp:TEST(PapyrusDecompiler, CompositeRoundTripScriptRoundTrips)

PET comment (lines 323-327, dropped): the `&&` decompiles to a jump-threaded `If`, and the zero-init local is hoisted to the top of the function, so the round-trip PEX differs from the original as it does under the C# sweep. Only reparse and recompile are required here.

## tests/test_papyrus_codegen_real.cpp:TEST(PapyrusCodegenReal, CompiledOutputMatchesCreationKitInstructionForInstruction)

Gated on `FO4RE_PEX_CORPUS` (then `FO4_PEX_CORPUS`, as PET reads it). `FO4RE_PSC_ROOTS` adds extra source roots. `FO4RE_PEX_RELEASE=1` compiles without debug-only and beta-only code, for a vanilla corpus. The pass floor is 0.95 identical among compiled pairs (`kMinimumIdenticalFraction`). This is the CK differential. The 1,498-script decompile-fidelity sweep (`DecompilerSweep.cs`, `PluginEditTool/docs/internal/PAPYRUS.md` lines 82-89) is ported below as its own entry.

- Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_codegen_real.cpp:DecompiledCorpusRecompilesToTheSameProgram: regression: decompiler or codegen drift that lowers recompile fidelity, so decompiled source stops recompiling to the same PEX as the original. This is the C++ port of `PluginEditTool/FO4RecordEditor.Core.Tests/DecompilerSweep.cs`. In `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_codegen_real.cpp`, it takes the first 1,500 `.psc` files under `FO4RE_PSC_ROOTS` by sorted native path, parses, compiles with debug-only and beta-only code, round-trips the PEX through bytes, decompiles it, reparses, recompiles, and compares with `pexDifference` (firstDifference plus property handlers, as the C# `PexComparer.FirstDifference` does). Decompiles that come back as assembly count as compiled but not matched. It fails (`ASSERT`) when `files` is empty, when `compiled` is 0, or when matched/compiled is below 0.802 (`kMinimumDecompileFidelity`; the C# oracle measured 1,202/1,498 = 80.2%). It skips (`GTEST_SKIP`) when `FO4RE_PSC_ROOTS` is unset or names no existing directory. Differences from the C# sweep: `Decompiler::toSource` emits no `RESULT:` line, so nothing is stripped; reason ties are ordered by reason text where C# keeps insertion order; a thrown exception is reported as `decompiler threw` without the exception type.

## NIF fix (fix_nif)

- Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:fix_nif: loads the model, rewrites the tangent frame of every shape, trims shader and texture-set strings, attaches a BSXFlags extra to the root when none is present, serializes, and reads the result back. It throws parse_error when the NIF has no root or the root is not a node, and throws std::runtime_error when the output does not read back as the same shapes (shape count, vertex count, triangle count, no reader warning). Callers write nothing on a throw.
- Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:rewrite_tangent_frame: recomputes each vertex's tangent and bitangent with import_detail::add_tangent_frame from the positions, UVs and normals, then writes only the tangent-space bytes into the vertex run, so positions, UVs and normals keep their values. Full precision writes bitangent X as a float at vertex offset 12; half precision writes it as a half at offset 6. Bitangent Y, tangent and bitangent Z are unit bytes after the normal's UV (and UV2 when the vertex-flags bit is set). A shape with no normals, tangents or UVs is skipped and keeps its old tangents.
- Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:vertex_run: reads the vertex run's stride (descriptor low nibble times 4) and flags (descriptor bits from 44 up) by skipping the same prefix as the reader: an i32, 16 bytes and 12 bytes after the AV header. This is a copy of the reader's layout, not a shared decode, so a change to the reader's BSTriShape layout must be mirrored here. The prefix matches the reader and Radicle/docs/NIF.md.
- Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:rewrite_tangent_frame: writes through unchecked indexes into the block bytes. The stride and vertex count come from a shape the reader already accepted. The reader only yields normals, tangents and UVs after checking that the vertex bytes equal vertex count times stride, so the highest written offset stays below the stride. Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:require_same_shapes compares each shape's warning text before and after, so a shape that already warns does not refuse the fix.
- Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:trim_shader_name: strips space, tab, CR and LF from a BSLightingShaderProperty name and interns the trimmed text as a new string-table index at offset 4. Empty names stay empty.
- Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:trim_texture_set: strips the same characters from every texture slot of a BSShaderTextureSet and rebuilds the sized strings only when a slot changed. It throws parse_error when bytes follow the slots, because rebuilding would drop them.
- Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:attach_bsx: pushes a BSXFlags block with value 0 and adds its ref at offset 8 + 4 * extra-data count of the root, then bumps the count at offset 4. The value 0 is the same one the import writer emits. It is not checked against NIF.md or a game-made asset, so the flag bits a real asset carries are not reproduced (#893 caveat).
- Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:has_bsx: skips attaching when the root already lists a BSXFlags extra, which makes a second fix a no-op.
- Radicle/src/nif/fix_nif.cpp:require_same_shapes: the self-check that runs before fix_nif returns, comparing shape count, vertex count, triangle count and the reader's warnings against the input.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_model.hpp:half_bits: IEEE half-float bits of a float. Moved here from import_build.cpp so fix_nif shares the encoding instead of copying it.
- Radicle/src/nif/write_model.hpp:unit_byte: maps a unit-range float to a byte with (v + 1) * 127.5, clamped to 0..255. Moved here from import_build.cpp for the same reason.
- Radicle/src/nif/import_obj.cpp:add_tangent_frame: moved out of the anonymous namespace and declared in Radicle/src/nif/import_mesh.hpp, so import and fix compute tangents with one routine. A change to its frame math changes both the import output and the fix output.
