## Radicle/src/c_api_graph.cpp:radicle_graph_compile

Exposes `Radicle/include/fo4/graph/graph_tool_service.hpp:GraphToolService` (validate, compile, searchPalette, describeNode) as four C exports declared in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_graph.h`: `radicle_graph_validate`, `radicle_graph_compile`, `radicle_graph_palette_search` and `radicle_graph_describe_node`. Each returns the service's UTF-8 text unchanged through `out_text`/`out_size`, freed with `radicle_free_bytes`, so the tests can compare the export with the service byte for byte. A graph that will not load and an unknown node type are `RESULT: FAILED` text with status OK, not an error status. Argument refusals are `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT` with both out-parameters cleared first: a null graph path, query or node type, a null out pointer, a null base-import entry, and a NULL `base_imports` array with a non-zero count. A NULL or empty `output_path` maps to the service's nullptr output, so nothing is written and the generated source comes back as text. A non-empty `output_path` with a `..` segment is refused. That scan is hygiene, not containment: absolute, UNC and symlinked paths are accepted, because the callers are trusted hosts. The `..` check runs before `lexically_normal()`, because normalising first would fold `a/../b` into `b` and hide the segment. A `std::filesystem::filesystem_error` maps to `RADICLE_STATUS_IO_ERROR`. The `GraphToolServiceCApi*` cases in `Radicle/tests/test_graph_tool_service.cpp:GraphToolService` name their regressions: the equality cases catch a dropped imports, base-import, limit or node-type argument; the broken-graph case catches base imports that are ignored; the missing-graph case catches a load failure reported as an error status; the source-only case catches a dropped `source_only` flag; the empty-path case catches a null or empty `output_path` that writes `Fixture.psc` into the working directory or is refused instead of returning the source; the escape case compiles a real graph, so an unguarded `..` path creates the escaped folder and fails the test; the null-argument case catches a null pointer reaching the service and an out-parameter left holding a stale buffer; the null-entry case catches a null base entry reaching `utf8_path`; the NULL-array case catches a NULL `base_imports` with a non-zero count being read; the zero-limit case catches `Radicle/src/c_api_graph.cpp:radicle_graph_palette_search` returning other than the service default of 30 for a limit of 0 or below (it passes the limit through, so this detects a changed pass-through).
## src/c_api_papyrus_compiler.cpp:radicle_papyrus_compile_source

In-memory compile for the editor. The source is parsed with `fo4::papyrus::Parser::parse` under the caller's file name and never written to disk, then compiled by `fo4::papyrus::compileScript` against a `ScriptIndex` built from the `imports` roots (a `;`-separated list; missing directories are ignored by `ScriptIndex::addRoot`). The index has no in-memory overlay, so the script under compile is reachable only as the parsed `Script`. `release` maps to `emitDebugOnlyCode = emitBetaOnlyCode = false`, the mapping `tests/test_papyrus_codegen_real.cpp` uses for `FO4RE_PEX_RELEASE=1`. `no_debug_info` maps to `emitDebugInfo = false`. The option fields are named so that an all-zero struct is the `PapyrusCompileOptions` default, so a C caller that leaves them zero gets the default compile. Every diagnostic, warnings included, becomes a row `severity<TAB>code<TAB>line<TAB>column<TAB>message`, with `code` the `PAP....` string from `fo4::papyrus::codeString`. The handle is returned only when no row is an error, so a clean compile with warnings returns both. Messages pass through a copy of `src/c_api_papyrus_source.cpp:row_text` that turns tabs and newlines into spaces. An empty source is refused like the summary export refuses it, not returned as a parse-error row. The handle comes from `src/c_api_pex_internal.hpp:make_pex_handle`, which fills the `strings` index; `src/c_api_pex.cpp:radicle_pex_parse` calls the same helper, so the object-code and string readers work on a compiled handle as on a parsed one. The `copy_bytes` helper is copied from `src/c_api_pex.cpp` rather than shared. `src/c_api_papyrus_compiler.cpp:radicle_papyrus_decompile` calls `fo4::papyrus::Decompiler::toSource`, or `disassemble` when `assembly` is nonzero. `toSource` throws for an object name that is not a safe file name (`tests/test_papyrus_decompiler.cpp:ObjectNameThatIsNotASafeFileNameIsRefused`). Any `std::exception` from a malformed .pex maps to `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR`, the same mapping `radicle_pex_parse` uses for malformed input. No compiled script can carry such a name, so that mapping needs a hand-built .pex to test.

Tests (`Radicle/tests/test_c_api_papyrus_source.cpp`): `CApiPapyrusCompileTest.CompileSourceMatchesCompileScriptForTheSameInput` requires the handle's bytes to equal `compileScript` on the same source and roots, which catches an export that drops the imports or compiles with other defaults. `ImportRootsDecideWhetherAnImportedScriptResolves` compiles a `Debug.Trace` call with no imports and requires an error row and no handle, which catches imports silently ignored. `DebugAndReleaseFlagsReachTheCodeGenerator` compiles a whole-statement `Debug.Trace` call; `Debug` is `DebugOnly` in `testdata/graph/BaseStubs/Debug.psc`, so `release` drops that statement (`src/papyrus/code_generator.cpp:CodeGenerator::excludedBy`, reached from `src/papyrus/body_statement.cpp`), and the test requires the release bytes to differ from the debug bytes and to equal the `compileScript` reference for `emitDebugOnlyCode = false`. It also requires `no_debug_info` to match `emitDebugInfo = false`, which catches an inverted or dropped flag. `DecompiledSourceRecompilesToTheSameFunctions` compiles, decompiles to source, recompiles, and compares functions with `tests/papyrus_pex_comparer.hpp:firstDifference`; it also requires the assembly flag to print the `; Disassembly of Probe.psc` header, which catches swapped decompile modes or decompiler output that does not recompile. `SourceErrorsReturnRowsAndNoHandle` requires status OK, a NULL handle and the exact `PAP0004` row for a `@` at line 2 column 11 (`src/papyrus/lexer.cpp:Lexer` lexes `#` as `TokenKind::Hash`, a qualifier separator, so it is not an error there), which catches an error status (the editor cannot tell that from a broken library) or a handle returned on error. `RefusalsClearEveryOutputParameter` pre-fills each out-parameter with a sentinel and requires every refusal to clear it, which catches a stale handle or row array left behind by a refused call.

## Radicle/src/c_api_papyrus_analysis.cpp:radicle_papyrus_check

Exposes `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/analysis_service.hpp:AnalysisService` as eight C exports declared in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus_analysis.h`: `radicle_papyrus_line_column_to_offset`, `radicle_papyrus_check`, `radicle_papyrus_outline`, `radicle_papyrus_definition`, `radicle_papyrus_analyze_json`, `radicle_papyrus_symbol_at_json`, `radicle_papyrus_compile_path` and `radicle_papyrus_natural_roots`. The disk operations (check, outline, definition, compile_path) take a `.psc` path, or a folder for check and compile_path. The two JSON operations take the buffer bytes, so unsaved editor text is what gets analysed. Text results are the service's string unchanged, copied by `copy_bytes` into a `malloc` buffer and freed with `radicle_free_bytes`. The `all` parameter of `AnalysisService::check` is not exported because the service ignores it. `buildIndex` is not exported because it returns a C++ `ScriptIndex`. `naturalRootsFor` is exported as rows freed with `radicle_free_string_array`, since it returns paths. A service answer such as `Not found`, `No source given.` or the `.pas` refusal is text with status OK, because the service reports those as results. Error statuses come only from argument refusals (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, with out-parameters cleared first) and from exceptions mapped by the `guarded` wrapper copied from `src/c_api_graph.cpp`: `bad_alloc` to `OUT_OF_MEMORY`, `filesystem_error` to `IO_ERROR`, other `std::exception` to `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The service takes `std::string` paths and passes them to `std::filesystem::path` unchanged, so non-ASCII path handling belongs to the service; this has not been checked against a non-ASCII path.

## Radicle/src/c_api_papyrus_analysis.cpp:radicle_papyrus_line_column_to_offset

Byte offset of a 1-based line and column in UTF-8 text with LF or CRLF endings, from `AnalysisService::lineColumnToOffset`. A position outside the text is `*out_offset == -1` with status OK, because the service returns that sentinel and the export must not clamp it. `out_offset` is zeroed before the NULL checks, so a refused call leaves 0. `text` must not be NULL even when `size` is 0, so an empty buffer has to be passed as a non-NULL pointer to zero bytes. `radicle_papyrus_analyze_json` and `radicle_papyrus_symbol_at_json` use the same rule.

## Radicle/src/c_api_papyrus_analysis.cpp:radicle_papyrus_compile_path

Disk compile through `AnalysisService::compile`, which writes `<output>/<ScriptName with ':' turned into '/'>.pex` for each file that compiles. A NULL or empty `output_path` maps to the service's nullptr, so the `.pex` goes to the source's folder (the parent of a file, or the folder itself). `release != 0` maps to the service's `release`, and `no_debug_info == 0` maps to `debugInfo`. `flag_file` is passed as the service's `flagFile` pointer, NULL when absent. Compile failures are counted in the returned summary text, not in the status. The tests in `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_papyrus_analysis.cpp` cover these regressions: `LineColumnToOffsetMatchesServiceAndIsMinusOneOutsideText` catches swapped line and column arguments and clamping instead of -1; `CheckReportsUnresolvedNameAsPap0030AndMatchesService` catches a dropped or reformatted diagnostic row, since the export must equal the service text; `CheckWithSemanticOffSaysSyntaxOnly` catches a dropped `semantic` flag, which would report PAP0030 with semantics on; `CheckForwardsBaseImportsSoInheritedMembersResolve` catches `base_imports` being ignored, which turns the inherited call into the `not on the roots` case; `OutlineAndDefinitionMatchServiceAcrossInheritance` catches a wrong position or a lost base chain; `DefinitionRejectsPositionOutsideFileAsResultText` catches an out-of-range position reported as an error status; `AnalyzeJsonReadsBufferNotDiskAndReportsSyntaxErrors` catches the disk file being analysed instead of the buffer, and parse errors dropped from the payload; `SymbolAtResolvesBufferOffsetAndAnswersUnresolvedWithoutError` catches an offset that is not forwarded and an unresolved answer reported as an error; `CompilePathWritesPexToOutputFolderNotBesideSource` catches `output_path` being dropped, which writes the `.pex` beside the source; `NaturalRootsMatchServiceAndAddSourceUserFolder` catches reordered rows and a lost `Source/User` root; `NullRequiredArgumentsAreRefusedWithOutParamsCleared` catches a NULL reaching the service and an out-parameter left holding a stale value; `BaseImportsRefuseNullEntryAndMissingArray` catches a NULL base entry reaching `utf8_path` and a NULL array read with a non-zero count.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION (ABI 77)

ABI 76 to 77 is one bump for three header sets that merged in #916, #917 and #918, each of which deferred the number. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus_compiler.h` adds `radicle_papyrus_compile_source`, `radicle_papyrus_decompile` and the `radicle_papyrus_compile_options` struct. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_graph.h` adds `radicle_graph_validate`, `radicle_graph_compile`, `radicle_graph_palette_search` and `radicle_graph_describe_node`. `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_papyrus_analysis.h` adds `radicle_papyrus_line_column_to_offset`, `radicle_papyrus_check`, `radicle_papyrus_outline`, `radicle_papyrus_definition`, `radicle_papyrus_analyze_json`, `radicle_papyrus_symbol_at_json`, `radicle_papyrus_compile_path` and `radicle_papyrus_natural_roots`. The pin is now `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSeventySeven`.

The three headers are listed in `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py:HEADERS`. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py:SCALARS` gained `int` because `radicle_graph_compile` (`source_only`) and `radicle_graph_palette_search` (`limit`) take a plain C `int`, which the mapper otherwise refuses; on the Windows targets that is the same 32-bit width as `int32_t`. The generated `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` were regenerated by running the generator, and the probe gained the `PapyrusCompileOptions` layout lines.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PapyrusCompiler.cs:PapyrusCompiler.CompileSource

Managed wrapper over `radicle_papyrus_compile_source`. The handle is wrapped with `PexFile.Snapshot` only when the native call returned one, which the C ABI does only when no row is an error, so a failed compile yields `Pex == null` with the rows. Each row is `severity<TAB>code<TAB>line<TAB>column<TAB>message` (see `Radicle/src/c_api_papyrus_compiler.cpp:diagnostic_row`), split into at most five fields so a tab inside the message stays in it. The source span is pinned with a stack sentinel when empty, because the C ABI refuses a NULL source before it checks the size, which would turn the documented "source must not be empty" refusal into a different message. Covered by `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/PapyrusTests.cs:PapyrusTests.ALexerErrorIsReturnedAsADiagnosticRowWithoutAHandle` (row field order, and no handle on error) and `PapyrusTests.AnEmptySourceIsRefusedByItsOwnMessageNotByANullPointer` (empty-span pointer).

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PapyrusCompiler.cs:PapyrusCompiler.Decompile

Borrows the pex handle through `PexFile.Use` (the C export takes `const radicle_pex*`), so the `PexFile` stays owned by the caller. `assembly` selects the listing; the listing starts with `; Disassembly of <file>` as pinned by `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_papyrus_source.cpp`. Covered by `PapyrusTests.ACleanCompileHandleReadsBackAsTheScriptAndDecompilesToSourceThatCompilesAgain`, which catches a handle that does not wrap the compiled object and decompiled source that does not recompile.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PapyrusAnalysis.cs:PapyrusAnalysis.AnalyzeJson

`radicle_papyrus_analyze_json` takes the buffer bytes, not a path, so unsaved editor text is what gets analysed. Like `LineColumnToOffset` and `SymbolAtJson`, the text pointer must be non-NULL even for an empty buffer; the wrapper substitutes a stack sentinel for an empty span. Parse failures come back as an `{"error"}` JSON object with status OK, so the wrapper returns the JSON text unparsed. Covered by `PapyrusTests.AnalyzeJsonReadsTheBufferNotTheFileOnDiskAndAcceptsAnEmptyBuffer`, which catches the disk file being analysed instead of the buffer and an empty buffer refused as a NULL argument.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PapyrusAnalysis.cs:PapyrusAnalysis.LineColumnToOffset

Returns the export's `out_offset` unchanged, so a position outside the text is `-1` rather than a clamped offset. Covered by `PapyrusTests.LineColumnToOffsetCountsCrLfLineEndingsAndIsMinusOneOutsideTheText`, which catches swapped line and column arguments, a CRLF miscount, and clamping instead of `-1`.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PapyrusAnalysis.cs:PapyrusAnalysis.Check

`semantic` is forwarded as the export's int flag. With it off the report says it "does not resolve names or check types" and has no PAP0030 row. Covered by `PapyrusTests.CheckReportsAnUnresolvedNameAsPap0030OnlyWhenSemanticsAreOn`, which catches a dropped semantic flag and a check that reports nothing.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/GraphTools.cs:GraphTools.Validate

A graph that will not load is `RESULT: FAILED` text with status OK, so the wrapper returns the text and does not throw. Covered by `PapyrusTests.AMissingGraphIsResultTextNotAnErrorStatus`, which catches a load failure surfaced as an error status. `GraphTools.PaletteSearch` passes `limit` through unchanged, so 0 selects the service default of 30.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/Core.cs:NativeStrings.AddAll

Base-import roots are copied into `NativeStrings` and pinned with `fixed` in each wrapper. An empty list pins to NULL with a count of 0, which the C ABI accepts. The NULL-array-with-count refusal in `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_papyrus_analysis.cpp` cannot be reached from managed code, because the pinned array length always equals the count passed.

## Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/PexFile.cs:PexFile.Snapshot

Made `internal` so `PapyrusCompiler.CompileSource` can wrap a handle the native compiler returned. `PexFile.Use` is `internal` for the same reason, for `PapyrusCompiler.Decompile`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_ops.cpp:int_range_result (SWF interp gaps L8)

Generic AVM2 `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `negate`, `increment` and `decrement` (the non-`_i` opcodes) compute on doubles and return an int32 or uint32 only when the exact result is in that type's range; otherwise they return a Number. So `int.MAX_VALUE + 1` is the Number 2147483648, not a wrapped int. `uint_range_result` does the same for uint32, so `0u - 1u` is -1. The `_i` opcodes (`add_i`, `subtract_i`, `multiply_i`, `increment_i`, `decrement_i`, `inclocal_i`, `declocal_i`) still wrap to int32 on purpose. Covered by `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_ops.cpp:int_range_result` through `Avm2Interpreter.AddOfIntsPromotesToANumberOnOverflow`, `Avm2Interpreter.IncrementOfIntMaxPromotesToANumber`, `Avm2Interpreter.SubtractOfUintsPromotesToANumberBelowZero`, `Avm2Interpreter.AddOfUintsPromotesToANumberAboveUintMax` and `Avm2Interpreter.NegateOfIntMinPromotesToANumber`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_a.inc:k_inclocal and k_declocal (SWF interp gaps L8)

Generic `inclocal` (0x92) and `declocal` (0x94) were decoded but not dispatched, so `i++` on a Number or uint local returned NotImplemented. They now apply `increment_value` and `decrement_value` to the local, so the int32-range rule above applies. Covered by `Avm2Interpreter.IncrementsAndDecrementsANumberLocal`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_a.inc:k_negate_i (SWF interp gaps L8)

`negate_i` (0xC4) was decoded but not dispatched. It negates through uint32 so the result wraps to int32, as the `_i` family does. Covered by `Avm2Interpreter.NegatesAnIntWithNegateI`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_a.inc:k_inclocal_i (inclocal_i and declocal_i wrap)

`Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_a.inc:k_inclocal_i` handles `inclocal_i` (0xC2) and `declocal_i` (0xC3). It adds or subtracts 1 in uint32 and converts the result back to int32, so `INT_MAX` wraps to `INT_MIN` and `INT_MIN` to `INT_MAX` without signed overflow. Covered by `Avm2Interpreter.InclocalIWrapsIntMaxToIntMin` and `Avm2Interpreter.DeclocalIWrapsIntMinToIntMax`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/coercion.cpp:string_to_number (SWF interp gaps L8)

After the optional sign, the text must start with a digit or `.`, or it is NaN. `std::from_chars` otherwise accepts `inf`, `infinity` and a second sign, so `Number("inf")` was Infinity and `Number("--5")` was 5. The `Infinity` literal is still handled before this check. Covered by `Avm2Value.RejectsNonEcmaSignedAndInfinityText`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp:Runtime::install_builtins (SWF interp gaps L8)

`String.prototype.toLocaleUpperCase` and `toLocaleLowerCase` reuse the `toUpperCase` and `toLowerCase` native ids. They are ASCII-only, as those are. `Object.toLocaleString` and `Array.toLocaleString` are not added: Object's would give `[object Object]` for arrays. Covered by `Avm2Builtins.StringToLocaleUpperCaseRaisesAsciiLetters`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute_frame (SWF interp gaps L8, deferred opcodes)

Decoder-valid opcodes still returning NotImplemented, not implemented in L8: `hasnext` (0x1F, needs the key-list code of `hasnext2` factored out first), `pushnamespace` (0x31, needs a namespace Value kind), `getglobalslot` and `setglobalslot` (0x6E/0x6F, legacy), `setpropertylate` and `deletepropertylate` (0x69/0x6B), `finddef` (0x5F), and the `coerce_b/i/d/u/o` names (0x81/0x83/0x84/0x88/0x89, not confirmed against avmplus). E4X (`getdescendants`, `dxns`, `dxnslate`, `esc_xelem`, `esc_xattr`, `checkfilter`) is out of scope. Alchemy memory ops (`li8` through `sf64`, `sxi1` through `sxi16`) are not used by SWF UI code. Pinned avmplus sources were not found at `%TEMP%\abc-ref`, so the semantics above come from the AVM2 overview and not from the reference.
## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION (ABI 78)

ABI 77 to 78 is one bump for `radicle_runtime_open_movie_with_bgs` in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_runtime.h`, the only new export. The pin is now `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSeventyEight`. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` was regenerated, and it changed only `CompiledAbiVersion`, because `c_api_runtime.h` is not in `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py:HEADERS`. The runtime exports are hand-declared, so the new DllImport is `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RuntimeNative.cs:RadicleNative.RuntimeOpenMovieWithBgs`.

## Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:radicle_runtime_open_movie_with_bgs

This is the options-taking C open that the "Fake BGS host and acceptance harness (#807 R8 L4)" section names as the follow-up. Before it, the C ABI opened every movie with `SwfRuntimeOptions` at its defaults, so `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/swf_runtime.hpp:SwfRuntimeOptions` `bgs_host` could only be set from C++, and a C host got a `BGSCodeObj` with no functions. The new export passes `bgs_host != 0` into `open_movie_bytes`, which sets `options.bgs_host` before `SwfRuntime::create`. `radicle_runtime_open_movie` now delegates to it with 0, so existing callers see no change.

Every refusal clears `*out_movie` before any check: a NULL runtime or out_movie, NULL or unparsable bytes, and a failed create. `open_movie_bytes` writes `*out_movie` only after the movie exists. The flag is a plain `int`, the same style as `source_only` in `radicle_graph_compile`; the export never refuses a flag value.

A movie whose root has no `BGSCodeObj` opens with the bridge on and no functions installed. `Radicle/src/avm2/native_bgs.cpp:install_bgs_code_object` returns without error in that case, which matches the no-op for GJ_Defrag and TurretHack in the BGSCodeObj host call table section. The export does not refuse it.

`radicle_runtime_open_movie_from_ba2` still opens with the bridge off. A C host that needs the bridge on an archived movie calls `radicle_ba2_extract` and then this export.

Tests, both in `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime.cpp`: `BgsOpenInstallsTheCodeObjectFunctionsOnlyWhenRequested` runs a root `Play` method that applies `BGSCodeObj.playSound`. With the flag off the host sees no call. With it on the host sees `bgs.playSound`. This catches an open that drops the flag or ignores it. `BgsOpenClearsItsMovieOutputOnEveryRefusal` starts from a non-NULL sentinel in `out_movie` and checks that a NULL runtime, a NULL `out_movie` (no crash), NULL bytes and unparsable bytes each leave it NULL. This catches a refusal that keeps a stale handle.

## Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:apply_placement_state (placed ratio, blend, visible, cacheAsBitmap and filters)

The decoder already reads these flags, and this section covers what the runtime does with them. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp:decode_place_object2` reads the PlaceObject2 ratio (flag 0x10) and the PlaceObject3 flags3 bits for filters (0x01), blend mode (0x02), cacheAsBitmap (0x04) and visible (0x20). `SwfPlacement` keeps ratio, blend mode, bitmap cache and visible as optionals. Its `filters` vector cannot tell an absent filter flag from a flagged empty list, so `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfPlacement` carries `has_filter_list`, which `decode_place_object2` sets from the flag.

`Radicle/src/avm2/swf_movie_data.cpp:placement_row` copies each value into `SwfPlacementRow` with a `has_` flag. `Radicle/src/avm2/swf_runtime.cpp:apply_placement_state` applies them from `SwfTimelineClip::apply_frame_state`, after the clip depth. A present flag sets its value. An absent flag keeps the prior value on a modify-only row (`move` set). On any other placement row it resets to the SWF default: no ratio, blend 0 (normal), visible true, cache off and no placed filters. That is the rule the clip depth already follows.

Object state lives on `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/display.hpp:DisplayObject`. `ratio()`, `cache_as_bitmap()` and `placed_filters()` are new. `blend_mode()` and `visible()` already existed, but no placement set them before this change. The placed filters are kept apart from the AS3 `filters()` array, which holds AS3 values. A hidden object stays in the display list and in the snapshot; only hit testing skips it.

AS3 `blendMode` reads and writes through `Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:blend_mode_name` and `Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:blend_mode_from_value`. The 15 names are the AS3 BlendMode strings, indexed by the SWF blend number, so SWF 0 and 1 both read as "normal". A string that is not a BlendMode name writes 0. AS3 `visible` already writes `DisplayObject::set_visible` in `Radicle/src/avm2/display.cpp:write_display_property`.

`Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:make_entry` copies the ratio, the cache flag and the placed filters into `SnapshotEntry` (`Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/snapshot.hpp:SnapshotEntry`). `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:snapshot_hash` hashes all three, and `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:hash_filter` covers every field of each filter. The C ABI is unchanged. `Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:fill_entry` still fills only blend mode, visible and the AS3 `filter_count`, so a C host cannot see the ratio, the cache flag or the placed filters. Adding them there would be an ABI change, which this change does not make.

`Radicle/src/avm2/display_snapshot.cpp:append_node` prints `blend=N ratio=N|none filters=N` after `visible`, where `filters` is the placed filter count. The expected text in `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_display_snapshot.cpp:kExpectedText` was updated by hand to match, because nothing was built.

Not applied: filter rendering, morph tessellation (the ratio is stored but does not change any drawn shape), and bitmap caching. Placed filters are not converted into `flash.filters` objects, so an AS3 read of `filters` does not show them and `filter_count` still counts only the AS3 array.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_swf_runtime.cpp:MoveWithoutStateFlagsKeepsRatioBlendVisibleAndCache`, `MoveWithStateFlagsOverwritesRatioBlendVisibleAndCache`, `NonMovePlacementOverAnObjectResetsItsState`, `PlacedFilterListFollowsItsFlagOnModify` and `BlendModeAndVisibleReadAndWriteThroughTheDisplayState`. `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_snapshot.cpp:HiddenPlacementStaysInTheSnapshotFlagged` and `PlacedRatioFiltersAndCacheChangeTheSnapshotHash`. `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_display_snapshot.cpp:AChangedBlendVisibleOrRatioChangesTheHash`.
ABI 78 to 79 adds the SWF edit verbs declared in `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_swf_verbs.h` and implemented in `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_verbs.cpp`. The pin is now `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsSeventyNine`. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py:HEADERS` lists the header, so `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` regenerates the DllImports and structs. The managed side is `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/SwfVerbs.cs:SwfVerbs`, which reaches the handle through `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/SwfEditing.cs:SwfEditHistory.UseForVerbs`.

Every verb runs `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_verbs.cpp:commit_edit`. It edits a copy of the file, derives a top-level tag plan with `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_verbs.cpp:plan_between`, and sends that plan through `SwfEditHistory::apply`. Undo, redo and the revision therefore follow the existing history rules, and a refused edit moves nothing. `plan_between` keeps the common prefix and suffix, then walks the differing middle with a one-tag lookahead and no LCS. A tag that matches in order is left alone, so a long-header tag between two edits keeps its encoded bytes. A removal is chosen when the next old tag matches the current new tag, an insertion when the current old tag matches the next new tag, a payload replacement when the codes match, and otherwise a removal plus an insertion, which is how a code change is expressed because `SwfTagReplacement` carries only a payload. Before the plan is sent, `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_verbs.cpp:plan_reproduces` applies it to a copy and requires `same_tag` on every top-level tag against the candidate. `apply_tag_plan` already refuses every plan that cannot be expressed, so this guard is a second check, and no verb is known to trigger it. The regression test is `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_history.cpp:DepthReassignKeepsAnUnrelatedLongHeaderTagInTheMiddle`. This relies on replay being deterministic, so the same plan on the same state gives the same file.

`radicle_swf_frame_label_rows` and `radicle_swf_placement_list_json` take a timeline id. Id 0 is the root timeline and any other id is the DefineSprite that owns it. `radicle_swf_placement_list_json` lists top-level placements of that timeline only, with the tag index, depth, character id, matrix and filters.

`radicle_swf_reassign_instance_depth` and `radicle_swf_insert_instance_transform_keyframe` are root-timeline only, because the C++ `reassign_instance_depth` and `insert_instance_transform_keyframe` refuse sprite-internal instances. `radicle_swf_apply_instance_transforms` does reach sprite-internal instances, through `root_frame` and `instance_id`. Edit text is addressed by top-level tag index, so a DefineEditText inside a sprite is not reachable.

The set-placement-depth verb was skipped. The C++ offers only `replace_placement_depth`, a body splice with no collision or mask proof, so `radicle_swf_reassign_instance_depth` is the proven depth edit.

Not built or run locally. CI is the first compile and run.

## Radicle/src/avm1/decode.cpp:Decoder::record

A record with a code of 0x80 or higher has a u16 Length that covers only the fields in its own header. For DefineFunction (0x9B), DefineFunction2 (0x8E), With (0x94) and Try (0x8F), the body is not inside the Length. The body follows as separate records in the same stream, sized by `body_size`, `try_size`, `catch_size` and `finally_size`. `Decoder::body` checks each body against its block before it decodes it. The probe ran read-only over the three shipped GFx movies (RaceSex_menu.gfx, TutorialMenu.gfx, SafeZone.gfx). The header-only layout parsed all 148 DoAction and DoInitAction payloads (82 and 66). The body-inclusive layout failed 42 of them. The probe did not cover With, Try, GetURL, GotoFrame2 or Call, so their layouts come from the SWF spec, not from measurement.

A record with a code below 0x80 is one byte and has no Length, so `Decoder::record` sets its length to 1 and `unknown` from `action_mnemonic`. An unknown code of 0x80 or higher keeps its declared bytes in `Avm1Raw` (`Decoder::payload` default case) and sets `unknown`. The code table covers every code of 0x80 or higher that has a payload case, so a known opcode is never flagged unknown.

## Radicle/src/avm1/decode.cpp:Decoder::push_values

The Push value widths were checked against the probe, and every value type parsed at the expected width. Double is stored as two little-endian u32 words, high word first, then low word. That word order is the SWF spec reading and has not been checked against a decoded value. A Boolean byte other than 0 or 1 is refused with BadPushValue at the type byte, because the encoder writes only 0 or 1 and an accepted byte would break the exact re-encode.

## Radicle/src/avm1/decode.cpp:Decoder::resolve_branches

A Jump (0x99) or If (0x9D) target is the end of its own record plus the signed offset. A target outside 0 to the stream size is refused with BranchOutOfRange at the branch offset. A target inside a record is refused with BranchNotRecord, because a listing label must name a record start. The stream end is a valid target, and it is the only boundary that is not a record start.

## Radicle/src/avm1/decode.cpp:Decoder::run

Bytes after the first End record are kept in `Avm1Stream::trailing` and written back by `encode_actions`, so the re-encode returns every input byte. The disassembly prints a `trailing N bytes` line for them. Nothing is decoded from the trailing bytes.

## Radicle/include/fo4/avm1/avm1.hpp:decode_actions

Typed payloads cover the record codes listed in the payload switch of `Radicle/src/avm1/decode.cpp:Decoder::payload`. Those are Frame, GetURL, the one-byte records, ConstantPool, WaitForFrame, the two text records, DefineFunction and DefineFunction2, Try, With, Push, Jump and If, Call (no payload) and GotoFrame2. Every other record of 0x80 or higher, and every unknown code below 0x80, is raw-preserved in `Avm1Raw` or as a byte. A failed decode clears `actions`. The status and offset are still set, so the caller can report the refusal.

## Radicle/src/avm1/decode.cpp:Decoder::body

Each nested body recurses through `block`, `record` and `body`. An unbounded chain of With records, at 5 bytes per level, could overflow a 1 MB stack. `kMaxBodyDepth` is 64, and the 65th nested body is refused with `TooDeep` at the offset where its body would start. `depth_` is incremented around the `block` call and decremented on the way back. Every return path in `block` returns a bool, so the counter is restored on success and on failure. The limit does not depend on the byte count, so it bounds the stack for any input size.

The limit of 64 is a guess. The three shipped GFx movies were not measured for their maximum body depth, so a real file could in principle exceed it. Raise the constant if a real movie is refused.

## Radicle/src/avm1/decode.cpp:Decoder::payload

A ConstantPool count is checked against the bytes left in its record before `resize`. Each string needs at least one NUL byte, so a count larger than the bytes left cannot decode. `Decoder::function_header` does the same for the parameter count, which needs at least one byte per parameter. Without the check, a 65,535-string count allocates a large vector before the first string fails.

## Radicle/src/avm1/disassembly.cpp:quote

Quoted text escapes a quote and a backslash with a backslash. Control bytes below 0x20, and 0x7F, print as `\xNN`. This keeps one listing line on one line, because a raw newline in a Text value would otherwise split it.

## Radicle/src/avm1/encode.cpp:encode_actions

Re-encode writes each payload in the layout the decoder reads, and it writes Length from the payload size. Branch offsets and body sizes are rebuilt from the record list, not copied from the decoded values. A branch names its target record by `Avm1Branch::target`, which matches a record's `Avm1Action::offset`. When no surviving record has that offset, the branch retargets to the first surviving record with a larger offset, which is the next record in the original order. If no such record survives, it retargets to the stream end, which is after the trailing bytes. The rule is `std::map::lower_bound` over record start positions in `encode_actions`, so the fallback is the stream end when no start is found. Details for the emitter, body sizes, and the identity field are in the tail sections of this file.

Unverified in this change: the build, the unit tests, and the runner case. The runner case `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp:InterfaceGfxAvm1StreamsDecodeAndReencodeByteIdentically` depends on FO4_DATA_DIR and skips without it. Call's zero-length layout and the With, Try, GetURL and GotoFrame2 layouts are unmeasured.

Not built or run locally. CI is the first compile and run.
## Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_to_svg (SWF shape to SVG)

Fill rule is `nonzero`. `fill_edges` gives every edge its fill on the left: fill0 edges keep their direction and fill1 edges are reversed. With every region's boundary directed the same way, the winding number is positive inside a filled region and zero outside, so nonzero paints the union of the regions of one fill. Evenodd would cut holes where two regions of the same fill overlap, which the SWF fill model allows.

Edge reversal: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:reversed` swaps the start and end of an edge. A quadratic keeps its control point, so the reversed curve is the same curve.

Loop chaining: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:loops_text` joins the edges of one fill into closed loops by exact endpoint match and closes each with `Z`. Separate subpaths would each be closed by the fill with a chord, and those chords do not cancel when a boundary is split at a style change, so the fill would be wrong. A chain that never returns to its start is emitted open. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:index_by_start` buckets the edges by start point in a `std::map` keyed on the twip `Point` (the ordering is the defaulted `<=>`), with each bucket in ascending edge index. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:take_unused_from` takes the lowest unused edge in the bucket, marks it used and skips used entries lazily. That is the same edge the old linear scan picked, so the output is unchanged, and one fill chains in O(n log n).

Style state: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_shape.cpp:read_records` sets `has_fill0`, `has_fill1` and `has_line` on each style change from SHAPE flag bits 0x02, 0x04 and 0x08. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:trace_edges` then applies a flagged index even when it is 0, so an explicit 0 turns that side off for later edges, and leaves an unflagged index unchanged. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_write.cpp:write_style_change` writes a flag for the same condition, so a decoded glyph re-encodes with the original flags. A nonzero index counts as present even without its flag, which keeps hand-built records and the C ABI (`Radicle/src/c_api_swf_art.cpp`, which has no presence fields) writing and tracing as before. The C ABI therefore cannot carry an explicit 0 across the boundary; that needs an ABI change and is not made here.

Twip scaling: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:pixels` divides twips by 20. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:number` prints fixed notation with six decimals through `std::to_chars` (`std::chars_format::fixed`, precision 6), then trims trailing zeros. `to_chars` does not read the C locale, so a comma-decimal locale cannot change the output. Its 32-byte buffer holds every value (int32 fixed-point or twips divided by 20, at most 26 characters). The integer hex colour in `hex_color` still uses `snprintf`; `%x` is not locale-dependent. Gradient matrices: scale and skew are 16.16 fixed point (divided by 65536), and the translation is in twips (divided by 20). `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:matrix_text` maps SWF `x' = ScaleX*x + RotateSkew1*y + TranslateX`, `y' = RotateSkew0*x + ScaleY*y + TranslateY` onto SVG `matrix(a b c d e f)` with `a = ScaleX`, `b = RotateSkew0`, `c = RotateSkew1`, `d = ScaleY`. This matches the composition in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp`.

Gradient extent: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:gradient_text` uses `kGradientHalfPixels` (819.2 px, which is 16384 twips) for the linear span and the radial radius, in `userSpaceOnUse`. The focal point is `fx = focal / 256 * 819.2` (`focal_text`). Spread: 0 pad, 1 reflect, 2 repeat (`spread_name`). Unverified against the SWF spec; the local SWF reference folder was not present.

Placeholder fallback: a bitmap fill (types 0x40 to 0x43) whose bitmap is missing from the file's top level, or that `bitmap_to_png` refuses, exports as the flat placeholder `#808080` (`kPlaceholderColor`) with no pattern (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_images`). A stroke whose LineStyle2 fill is a gradient or bitmap also uses the placeholder (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:stroke_paint`). A solid stroke fill uses its colour.

Caps and joins: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:cap_name` reads the start cap from bits 15-14 of the LineStyle2 flags (0 round, 1 butt, 2 square). `join_name` reads the join from bits 13-12 (0 round, 1 bevel, 2 miter). The miter limit is 8.8 fixed point. SVG has one linecap, so the end cap (bits 1-0) and NoClose (bit 2) are ignored. A LineStyle1 has flags 0 and so exports round caps and joins. Width 0 (hairline) exports as 1 px in `stroke_attributes`. Unverified against the SWF spec bit order; the fixture in `Radicle/tests/swf_art_fixtures.hpp` (`define_shape_4_payload`) agrees with it.

Paint order: `shape_to_svg` writes every fill path first, in fill-style index order (`fill_paths`), then every stroke path in line-style order (`stroke_paths`). Interpolation mode (linearRGB) is not applied.

Closed strokes: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:stroke_text` records the first point of each contiguous run and appends `Z` when the run's last edge ends on that point, so a closed outline gets a closed join at its start corner (`closing_text`). An open run is unchanged. Fill paths are not touched, since `loops_text` already closed each loop.

Gradient ids: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:gradient_text` keeps the `fill<n>` ids. Each `shape_to_svg` call is one `<svg>` document, so ids collide only when a caller inlines two exported shapes into one page. A unique prefix needs a per-document value, which is a signature change, so it is not made here.

Tests: exact-string expectations in `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp` (including `ThousandsOfCollinearEdgesChainIntoOneClosedLoop` for the chaining and `ClosedStrokeLoopEndsInZ` for the stroke close), and the real-data well-formedness case `SwfRealData.ExportsEveryShapeToWellFormedSvg` in `Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp`. Not compiled or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.

## Radicle/src/c_api_swf_characters.cpp:radicle_swf_shape_svg (shape SVG by character id)

The C ABI exports `shape_to_svg` for one character. `radicle_swf_shape_svg` resolves the id through the same character model as `radicle_swf_character_by_id` (`Radicle/src/c_api_swf_characters.cpp:require_model`), so a refused model fails it with the same message. The character row carries a root tag index (`SwfCharacter::tag_index`), and the shape is read from `swf->file.tags[tag_index].shape`. An undefined id, an imported id and a non-shape kind all refuse with NOT_FOUND and the message "is not a decoded shape". NOT_FOUND mirrors `radicle_swf_shape_at` for a tag with no decoded shape; the brief did not fix a status for this case. Null arguments refuse with INVALID_ARGUMENT, and every output is cleared before any check. The text uses a local `copy_text` with the same trailing-NUL invariant as the copies in `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp` and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_abc_write.cpp`; the copies are not shared yet.

ABI: `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` moves 79 to 80 for this export. The pin is `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsEighty`. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` is the generator output for `RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` and the new `SwfShapeSvg` DllImport, and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/SwfFile.cs:SwfFile.ShapeSvg` is the managed wrapper, which follows `SwfFile.AbcText`.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_characters.cpp:CApiSwfCharacters.ExportsAFilledShapeAsSvg` (the `<svg` start and a `<path` for the shape 5 fixture, and the trailing NUL) and `CApiSwfCharacters.RefusesNonShapesAndNullArgumentsWithOutputsCleared` (edit text 11, undefined 99 and null arguments, with a non-null sentinel so a missed clear shows). Not compiled or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_actions

The first AVM1 interpreter slice. It runs the records that `decode_actions` already produced, one record at a time, on a per-call state: an operand stack, the constant pool from the last ConstantPool record, a global variable map and a trace vector. Function frames (see the function section at the tail) read the globals and their own locals; there are no host callbacks or timeline operations. The executed set is End, Pop, PushDuplicate, StackSwap, Push, ConstantPool, Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Equals (0x0E), Less (0x0F), Add2, Less2, Greater (0x67), Equals2, And, Or, Not, StringEquals, StringLength, StringExtract (0x15), StringAdd, CharToAscii (0x32), AsciiToChar (0x33), StringLess (0x29), StringGreater (0x68), Modulo (0x3F), TypeOf (0x44), ToInteger, ToNumber, ToString, Increment (0x50), Decrement (0x51), BitAnd, BitOr, BitXor (0x60 to 0x62), ShiftLeft, ShiftRight, ShiftUnsigned (0x63 to 0x65), GetVariable, SetVariable, Trace, Jump and If, the object records NewObject (0x40), InitArray (0x42), InitObject (0x43), GetMember (0x4E), SetMember (0x4F), Delete (0x3A) and Delete2 (0x3B) (`Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:object_ops`), the arms of `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action`. Less (0x0F) converts both operands to numbers, Greater is Less2 with its operands swapped, and `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:extract_string` pops the count, then the index, then the string, with the index counted from 1. MBStringLength (0x31) and MBStringExtract (0x35) execute by code point (see the `Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:unit_count (MBStringLength 0x31 and MBStringExtract 0x35)` section). MBCharToAscii (0x36) and MBAsciiToChar (0x37) execute by code point as well (see the `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action (MBCharToAscii 0x36 and MBAsciiToChar 0x37)` section at the tail). The function records (DefineFunction 0x9B, DefineFunction2 0x8E, CallFunction 0x3D, Return 0x3E, StoreRegister 0x87, DefineLocal 0x3C, DefineLocal2 0x41, CallMethod 0x52, NewMethod 0x53) and the register push run as described in `## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action (function opcodes; supersedes the refusal notes)`. Every other record is refused by `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action` with `Avm1RunStatus::Unsupported` and a message that names the opcode, so a missing operation never looks like a successful run.

A refused record stops the run at its offset. `Avm1Result::opcode` and `offset` name the refusing record, or the last record that ran when the run succeeds. A stream whose `ok()` is false is refused as InvalidStream before any record runs, because `decode_actions` clears `actions` on failure and an empty list would otherwise return Ok without running anything.

The step limit counts every record that runs, including End. Before a record runs, the count is compared with `max_steps`, and at the limit the run stops with StepLimit, so a run reports exactly `max_steps` steps. The default is 1,000,000. The step limit bounds loops and the operand stack, which can grow by at most one value per step. String length has its own bound in `push_result`.

A std::bad_alloc thrown while a record runs is reported as ResourceLimit with the message that the interpreter ran out of memory, and any other std::exception as InvalidStream with the exception's message. So `execute_actions` reports every failure as a status and does not throw.

Known ceilings of this slice, so that no one reads them as AS2 behavior. The optional `swf_version` of `Radicle/include/fo4/avm1/interpreter.hpp:execute_actions` (0 means unspecified) changes how null and undefined convert to a number, which reaches the arithmetic, comparison and ToNumber records, the text that undefined converts to from SWF 1 to 6 (see `## Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:to_text`), the units of StringLength (0x14) and StringExtract (0x15) (see `## Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:unit_count`), and the text of CharToAscii (0x32) and AsciiToChar (0x33). SWF 4 to 6 still differ in that a string's truthiness differs in If and Not, and And, Not, Equals (0x0E) and Less (0x0F) produce Booleans in `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action`, where the SWF 4 forms of these produce numeric results. StringLength (0x14) and StringExtract (0x15) count bytes before SWF 6 and UTF-8 code points from SWF 6 (`Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:unit_count`), while StringLess (0x29) and StringGreater (0x68) still compare bytes for every version. ToInteger (0x18) truncates toward zero as a double and does not reduce the result to a 32-bit integer, so a value past 2^31 keeps its magnitude. `parse_number` accepts whatever `std::strtod` accepts, including hex, `inf` and `nan`. None of these three points has been checked against the SWF spec v19 mirror. `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:extract_string` indexes from 1, the Flash 4 substring convention as this slice reads it, so an index of 0 or below starts at the first character. That is not ECMA `substr`, which is 0-based. `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:clamp_to_length` clamps a negative count to 0, so a negative count is empty; this is a ceiling, not a checked behaviour. The Modulo arm of `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action` follows C `fmod`. The mirror is not on this machine, so none of this is checked against it.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:jump_index

A Jump or If carries `Avm1Branch::target`, the byte offset of its destination record, and `jump_index` finds the record index by lower bound on the record offsets. A target that matches a record start runs from that record. A target past the last record start ends the run as a normal stop only when it equals the stream size, which is the end of the last record plus the `trailing` bytes. Any other target past the last record start, including one inside the trailing bytes, is refused with BadBranch, and so is a target that falls inside a record. `decode_actions` already refuses every such target, so BadBranch can only come from a stream built by hand. `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:JumpPastTheStreamEndIsRefusedUnlessItIsTheStreamSize` pins the exact-size stop and the one-byte-past refusal.

## Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:number_text

Numbers print in the ECMA-262 9.8.1 layout with two deliberate changes. The digits are rounded to 15 significant and trailing zeros are trimmed, so 0.1 + 0.2 prints 0.3, where the spec's shortest round-trip form prints 0.30000000000000004. The layout otherwise follows the spec: fixed form when the decimal exponent is from -6 to 20, and exponent form outside that range, written as `1e+21` or `1e-7` with no padding on the exponent. Integers up to 1e21 print as plain digits, so 1e20 prints as 100000000000000000000. NaN, Infinity and -Infinity print as their names, and zero, including -0, prints as 0. The 15-digit rounding is the AS2 display choice from memory and has not been checked against the SWF spec v19 mirror.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:push_result

`push_result` is the one place a binary or unary result is pushed. A String result longer than `kMaxStringBytes`, 16 MiB, is refused as ResourceLimit before it is pushed. That covers StringAdd (0x21), Add2 (0x47, when either operand is text) and ToString (0x4B), the only record paths that build text longer than their inputs. Without the cap, a loop of PushDuplicate and StringAdd doubles the string on every pass and would reach a bad_alloc or a length error long before the step limit. The check runs after the concatenation is built, so one transient allocation can reach twice the cap. `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:DoublingStringStopsAtTheResourceCap` stops on the 24th doubling, in well under 1,000 steps.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:parse_number

String to number trims the four ASCII whitespace bytes, returns 0 for an empty result, and then accepts whatever `std::strtod` accepts, so "inf", "nan" and hex forms parse. AS2 may refuse some of those, which is a known ceiling. Any text left after the number makes the result NaN.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:to_number

`to_number` takes the SWF version as its second argument. Version 0 is unspecified and keeps the rules the slice had before the version input: null is 0 and undefined is NaN. From SWF 7 both are NaN. Versions 1 to 6 make both 0. Every arithmetic, comparison and ToNumber arm passes the version, as do `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:less_than`, `add_values`, `loose_equal`, `to_uint32` and `extract_string`. Bitwise results do not change with the version, since NaN and 0 both give 0 in ToUint32. The SWF 7 split and undefined as 0 before it are from memory of Flash Player behavior and are not checked against the SWF spec v19 mirror, which is not on this machine. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:SwfSevenMakesNullNaN` and `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:UndefinedIsZeroBeforeSevenAndComparesFollow`. Not compiled or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.

## Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:first_code_point

`first_code_point` decodes the first UTF-8 sequence of a text for CharToAscii from SWF 6. The lead byte must be C2 to DF, E0 to EF or F0 to F4, every continuation byte must be 10xxxxxx, and the value must not be overlong or past U+10FFFF. Any failure, including a lead byte that cannot start a sequence and a sequence cut short by the end of the text, returns the lead byte. Surrogate values are accepted so that `Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:encode_code_unit` output decodes to the same value. That is a choice, not a checked behavior. Not checked against the spec mirror.

## Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:encode_code_unit

`encode_code_unit` writes a 16-bit unit as one, two or three UTF-8 bytes with no surrogate check, so a lone surrogate gets the three-byte form that strict UTF-8 refuses. AsciiToChar masks the unit to 16 bits first, so the four-byte form never arises here. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:SwfSixStringsAreUtf8CodePoints`, which pins chr(256) as U+0100 and the masked chr(65601) as A. Not checked against the spec mirror.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:to_uint32

ToUint32 follows ECMA-262 9.6 (cited from memory; no copy of the spec is on this machine): NaN and the infinities give 0, the value is truncated toward zero, reduced modulo 2^32 and read unsigned. `int32_value` reads the same bits as signed, which is ToInt32 of ECMA-262 9.5. So BitAnd, BitOr, BitXor, ShiftLeft and ShiftRight push numbers in -2^31 to 2^31-1, and ShiftUnsigned pushes its unsigned result. The shift count is the right operand's ToUint32 masked with 31, so a count of 32 is 0 and a count of 33 is 1. The file names 0x63 to 0x65 ShiftLeft, ShiftRight and ShiftUnsigned in `Radicle/src/avm1/opcodes.cpp:action_mnemonic`; the SWF spec calls them BitLShift, BitRShift and BitURShift. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:BitwiseOperatorsWrapTheirOperandsToInt32` and `ShiftCountsAreMaskedToFiveBits`.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:type_name

TypeOf returns "undefined", "null", "boolean", "number", "string" or "object" for the six `Avm1DataKind` values. An object and an array both return "object", as ECMA-262 gives for a plain object and an array. "null" is the AS2 result from memory, where ECMA-262 says "object"; not checked against the SWF spec v19 mirror. The slice has no function or movieclip value, so neither name is produced. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:TypeOfNamesEachDataKind`.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action

Equals (0x0E) is the SWF 4 numeric form, separate from Equals2 (0x49). Both operands go through `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:to_number` with the run's version, so null is 0 for version 0 and SWF 1 to 6 and NaN from SWF 7, undefined is NaN for version 0 and from SWF 7 and 0 for SWF 1 to 6, and non-numeric text is NaN; NaN equals nothing. It pushes a Boolean like Less (0x0F). Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:EqualsComparesNumbersAndNeverMatchesNaN` and `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:UndefinedIsZeroBeforeSevenAndComparesFollow`.

CharToAscii (0x32) and AsciiToChar (0x33) are byte-wise for version 0 and SWF 1 to 5. From SWF 6, CharToAscii reads the first UTF-8 sequence through `Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:first_code_point` and gives its code point, so an e-acute is 233 and empty text is 0; an invalid or cut-short sequence gives its lead byte. Before SWF 6, AsciiToChar keeps the low byte of the ToUint32 value of the number, so the value is taken modulo 256 and NaN gives a NUL byte. From SWF 6 it keeps the low 16 bits and encodes them as UTF-8 through `Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:encode_code_unit`, so chr(256) is U+0100. The byte-wise form is the version-0 behavior the slice had before. The SWF 6 rules are from memory and are not checked against the spec mirror. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:CharToAsciiAndAsciiToCharAreByteWise` (version 0) and `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:SwfSixStringsAreUtf8CodePoints`.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:loose_equal

Equals2 follows the ECMA-262 order: undefined equals null and nothing else, a Boolean compares as its number, and a string compares as a number against a number. Division by zero is IEEE division, so it gives Infinity or NaN, and Less2 with a NaN operand is false rather than undefined. Those three points, the Boolean-as-number rule and the ToBoolean rule for strings (empty is false, any other text is true) come from ECMA-262 and memory of AS2, and have not been checked against the SWF spec v19 mirror, because the mirror is not on this machine and was not downloaded.

## Radicle/include/fo4/avm1/interpreter.hpp:execute_actions

The runtime value `Avm1Data` is separate from the decoded Push record `Avm1Value`, so the decoder's type codes never reach the operand stack. Push Float and Double read the IEEE bit patterns that `Decoder::push_values` already stores in `float_bits` and `double_bits`. Push Constant8 and Constant16 read `Avm1Data` strings from the constant pool, and an index past the pool refuses as ConstantOutOfRange.

The third argument is `swf_version`, default 0, copied into `Avm1State::swf_version` and read by `execute_action` and `extract_string`. Only the tests pass a SWF version: no production caller does, and the C ABI has no execute entry point, so nothing outside `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp` runs a record with a known version. Version tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:SwfSixStringsAreUtf8CodePoints`, `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:SwfSevenMakesNullNaN` and `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:UndefinedIsZeroBeforeSevenAndComparesFollow`. Not compiled or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:ArithmeticResultIsTracedInOperandOrder`, `CountedLoopExitsThroughIfAndJump`, `SelfJumpStopsAtTheStepLimit`, `VariableRoundTripsThroughTheGlobalScope`, `UnsupportedOpcodeIsRefusedByName`, `DoublesTraceInTheEcmaScriptLayout`, `DoublingStringStopsAtTheResourceCap`, `JumpPastTheStreamEndIsRefusedUnlessItIsTheStreamSize` and `OperatorsConstantsAndRefusalsMatchTheTable`, plus `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:ComparisonOpcodesUseTheirOwnCoercion`, `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:SubstringReadsIndexThenCountAndClamps`, `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:ModuloAndIncrementDecrementMatchTheirTable` and `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:ObjectAndFunctionOpcodesStayRefusedByName`. The self-jump test has no independent failure mode: without the step check it never returns. Not compiled or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.

## Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:radicle_swf_detail::copy_text

`radicle_swf_detail::copy_text` replaces the four file-local copies in `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp`, `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_verbs.cpp`, `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_abc_write.cpp` and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_characters.cpp`. The copies were identical: malloc of size plus one, nullptr on allocation failure with `*out_size` untouched, empty text copies nothing, trailing NUL not counted in `*out_size`. Callers keep their own out-of-memory messages. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:copy_text` takes a `std::string_view`, so `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_abc_write.cpp:radicle_swf_abc_assemble` passes the serialized ABC bytes through a view with no extra copy; its former file-local `copy_bytes` had the same malloc, trailing-NUL and out_size behaviour and was deleted. `placement_json` emits `tag_index` as the flat pre-order index that `radicle_swf_tag_at` reports, not the position among top-level tags. `timeline_tags` also returns the timeline's base flat index (0 for id 0, the DefineSprite's flat index plus one for a sprite id), and `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_history.cpp:subtree_size` counts each row's descendants so the running index matches `Radicle/src/c_api_swf.cpp:flatten_tags`. Before this, a DefineSprite ahead of a placement made the root row report 1 where `radicle_swf_tag_at` reports 4. No in-repo consumer reads the field: `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/SwfVerbs.cs:PlacementListJson` has no caller, and PET reads `tagIndex` from the managed placement list (`PluginEditTool/FO4RecordEditor.Core/Services/SwfDocumentService.cs:Placements`), not from this JSON. ## Radicle/src/c_api_graph.cpp:radicle_graph_load_script

`radicle_graph_load_script` takes a script path, not bytes: `fo4::graph::GraphScriptLoader::load` only reads from disk, for `.psc` as source and for `.pex` by decompiling it through `papyrus::Decompiler`. The roots are the `imports` list and `base_imports` through `fo4::graph::graphIndexFor`, the same list the other graph exports build, and the loader adds the script's own folder. The output is `documentJson::serialize` (indented), with the trailing NUL not counted, freed by `radicle_free_bytes`. Every loader refusal is `RADICLE_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR`: a missing file, an extension other than `.psc` or `.pex`, a decompile failure, or a parse or lift error. `load_failure` gives the loader's failure text, or the error diagnostics joined with `"; "`, as the message. A missing file is therefore PARSE_ERROR and not `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`. The ABI moved from 80 to 81 for this export (`Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION`), pinned by `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsEightyOne`. The C# P/Invoke `GraphLoadScript` in `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs` came from `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py`, run with `python -I`. The ABI layout probe did not change. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_graph_tool_service.cpp:GraphToolService.GraphToolServiceCApiLoadScriptNamesTheEventAndFunctionNodesOfAPsc` loads a `.psc` that extends `ObjectReference` with one event and one function, and asserts the JSON has the `event:ObjectReference.OnLoad` node (the lifter names an override of a parent event after the parent that declares it) and a `function.entry` node named `Fire`. It detects an export that drops the imports roots, so `extends ObjectReference` does not resolve and the lift refuses, and an export that returns a document without the script's event and function nodes. Not compiled or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.

`radicle_swf_inspect_text` returns the text `fo4::swf::inspect_swf` renders for the handle's `SwfFile` with the default `SwfInspectionOptions`, so C# and C++ callers read one listing. The name is the caller's label for the `## name` heading, not a path. A NULL name is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT before any rendering, and every output is cleared first.

`radicle_swf_avm1_disassemble` takes a flat `radicle_swf_tag_at` index and decodes the `SwfTag::payload` bytes at `SwfTag::action` (offset and size), so a DoInitAction starts after its sprite id and a DoAction inside a DefineSprite is addressed like any other flat index. ## Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:radicle_swf_frames_open (display rows carry flat tag indexes)

A display row's `create_tag_index` and `transform_tag_index` are positions in the tag list of the row's own timeline, `instance.timeline_id`: top-level for timeline 0, the DefineSprite's children otherwise. `radicle_swf_frames_open` rewrites the handle's copy of the list through `to_flat_indices`, which resolves each row through the flat map of its own `timeline_id` and not the outer timeline, so each index becomes the flat pre-order index `radicle_swf_tag_at` reports. `radicle_swf_detail::timeline_flat_indices` in `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_history.cpp` produces the position-to-flat map, using the same `subtree_size` count as `top_level_position`. The maps are filled lazily and cached for one open. The conversion runs once at open, while the movie is still available; `radicle_swf_frames_instance_at` only copies. A row whose `timeline_id` does not resolve, or whose index is past its timeline, fails the open. Regression: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_edit.cpp:FramesOpenAddressesASpriteChildPastTheRootTagCount` places a sprite child at child index 4, past the root's four top-level tags; the outer-timeline mapping refused that open, and the child must read as flat index 5.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap.cpp:decode_bitmap_tag

`SwfBitmap::packed` keeps the zlib stream exactly as the tag carried it, so its size is bounded by the tag and it is the only pixel-related field a copied `SwfFile` carries. `decode_bitmap_tag` still inflates once through `Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:inflate_to` to validate the geometry, then discards the inflated bytes, so a malformed stream is refused as before. `bitmap_to_png` inflates `packed` again on demand with the same 64 MiB cap. `SwfBitmap::has_alpha` is set from DefineBitsLossless2 and the bitmap is moved into `out_tag.bitmap`, not copied. The C ABI does not expose either field: `radicle_swf_bitmap_at` copies only the scalar fields (`Radicle/src/c_api_swf_art.cpp:radicle_swf_bitmap_at`), so the ABI is unchanged. Regression: inflated pixels retained on every parsed bitmap, which multiplies in each `SwfFile` copy on edit and history snapshot, and a Lossless2 bitmap decoded without `has_alpha`, which would be encoded as opaque. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfBitmapPng.Lossless2UnpremultipliesAlphaIntoAnRgbaPng`.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap_png.cpp:bitmap_to_png

Encodes formats 3 (colour map) and 5 (32-bit ARGB) to an 8-bit RGBA PNG with filter 0 on every row and `compress2` at `Z_BEST_COMPRESSION`, so the output is byte-deterministic for a given zlib. It inflates `SwfBitmap::packed` through `inflate_to` to exactly the palette plus padded rows the geometry implies, so a width or height that no longer matches the stream returns nullopt, as does a palette index past the colour map. Format 4 (15-bit) is refused because its byte order is not verified against the spec or the C# oracle. Un-premultiply follows `BitmapArtwork.Png` in `E:\GardenEngine\GardenEngine\git\audit-pr277\tools\SwfTools\BitmapArtwork.cs`: `channel * 255 / alpha` rounded half-to-even (`std::nearbyint`, matching `Math.Round`), clamped to 255, and alpha 0 keeps the stored channel. The oracle handles only format 5; the palette un-premultiply for Lossless2 (RGBA entries) is an extension and is not checked against a reference. Regression: premultiplied colour left in the output (the 50% pixel would read 64 instead of 128), a half-up tie rule (a 4.5 channel would read 5), a 15-bit row read as ARGB, and a palette entry with alpha below 255 left premultiplied. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfBitmapPng.Lossless2UnpremultipliesAlphaIntoAnRgbaPng`, `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfBitmapPng.Lossless2ColourMapUnpremultipliesEachPaletteEntry`, `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfBitmapPng.ColourMappedRowsAreStridedAndLookedUpInThePalette`, `Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfBitmapPng.RefusesBitmapsThatCannotBeEncodedAsPng`.

## Radicle/tests/test_swf_art.cpp:SwfBitmapPng.RefusesBitmapsThatCannotBeEncodedAsPng

A JPEG-based DefineBitsJpeg2 tag never produces an `SwfBitmap`, so that refusal is structural: the test asserts the tag has no bitmap and does carry the JPEG. The other refusals go through `Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap_png.cpp:bitmap_to_png`: 15-bit (format 4), a width changed after decode so the packed stream no longer inflates to the geometry, and a palette index of 5 against a one-entry colour map. Regression: a JPEG blob reaching the lossless path, a 15-bit row read as ARGB, a short pixel buffer encoded as if complete, and an index read past the colour map.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:bitmap_pattern

A repeating bitmap fill (0x40 and 0x42, `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:is_tiled`) becomes a `<pattern>` whose `<image>` is the PNG that `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_images` encoded once per shape emission, via `Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap_png.cpp:bitmap_to_png`, in base64. The pattern is `patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` with `width`/`height` equal to the bitmap's pixel size and `patternTransform` from `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:bitmap_matrix_text`. The SWF bitmap fill matrix maps bitmap pixels to twips, so `bitmap_matrix_text` divides the linear part (scale_x, scale_y, skew0, skew1) and the translation by 20 twips per pixel. A scale of 20.0 is one stage pixel per bitmap pixel, and a scale of 2.0 with a 400 twip translation gives `matrix(0.1 0 0 0.1 20 0)`. This convention is from the SWF spec as recalled, unverified against real data. `matrix_text` keeps the gradient convention, where only the translation is divided by 20. Pattern ids are `<prefix>bmp<N>` (`fill_id`), so they never collide with gradient ids `<prefix><N>`.

Smoothing: 0x40 and 0x41 are smoothed and emit nothing extra; 0x42 and 0x43 add `image-rendering="pixelated"` on the `<image>`.

Clipped fills (0x41 and 0x43, `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:is_clipped`) are not patterns. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:clipped_bitmap` emits, for the fill's one path, a `<clipPath id="<fill id>clip">` holding that path's data and a `<g clip-path>` around a single `<image>` placed by `bitmap_matrix_text`, so the bitmap is drawn once instead of tiling. The clip id is `<prefix>bmp<N>clip` (for example `r3fbmp1clip` inside a frame), so it cannot collide with a mask id `r<index>clip`. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:fill_paths` emits the clip group only when `geometry_only` is false; `shape_fill_paths_to_svg`, which builds a mask's clipPath, keeps a plain path for every fill, because a `<g>` or `<image>` is not a valid clipPath child and the mask would clip everything out.

Approximation: outside the bitmap's own rectangle the clipped fill is transparent. SWF clamps edge pixels there and this export leaves them transparent, which differs from Flash. Not checked against the Flash player.

Fallback: a missing bitmap id, a bitmap tag that is not in the file's top level, a JPEG bitmap (DefineBits and DefineBitsJPEG tags never produce an `SwfBitmap`), or a format that `bitmap_to_png` refuses (format 4, 15-bit) gets no entry from `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_images`, so the fill keeps the old `#808080` placeholder and neither a pattern nor a clip group is emitted.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:fill_attributes

`fill_attributes` no longer encodes anything. It checks whether `SvgImages` from `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_images` has the fill's bitmap, and `fill_defs` builds the pattern from that same table, so each bitmap fill is encoded once per shape emission. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body` calls `shape_images` once per instance, so a frame with many instances of one bitmap-filled shape still encodes that PNG once per instance. Known cost, not measured. Upgrade path: cache the images per character id across the instances of one `frame_to_svg` call.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:index_bitmaps

`index_bitmaps` keys each top-level `SwfTag::bitmap` by its `character_id` and keeps the first tag for a duplicate id, the same first-wins rule `frame_to_svg` uses for shapes. Bitmaps nested inside a sprite's children are not indexed, so a bitmap fill inside a sprite-defined shape falls back to the placeholder when its bitmap lives in a sprite. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_to_svg` builds the index once per call and passes it to `frame_body`.

`shape_to_svg(shape)` (one argument) is `shape_to_svg(shape, SwfFile{})`, so it prints the placeholder for every bitmap fill and stays byte-identical to the older output. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_characters.cpp` (`radicle_swf_shape_svg`) now calls the two-argument overload, so a character export shows bitmap fills; the C ABI is unchanged.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:strict_equal (StrictEquals 0x66)

StrictEquals (0x66) pops two values and pushes true only when both have the same `Avm1DataKind` and the values are equal, with no ToNumber or ToString step. Undefined equals undefined and null equals null, NaN equals nothing because the comparison is a double `==`, and text compares by its bytes. The slice has no object, array or function kind, so the identity case does not arise. Under SWF 1 to 5 `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action` refuses the opcode through `unsupported`, the same refusal an unknown opcode gets, and the message names StrictEquals. Version 0 runs it: version 0 is unspecified and keeps the old rules, so it is not in the refused range. That choice is not checked against the SWF spec v19 mirror, which is not on this machine. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:StrictEqualsRequiresTheSameTypeAndValue` and `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:StrictEqualsIsRefusedBelowSwfSix`. Not compiled or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.

## Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:unit_count

StringLength (0x14) and StringExtract (0x15) count string units. From SWF 6 a unit is a UTF-8 code point. `unit_count` counts by stepping `decode_code_point`, the decoder that `first_code_point` also uses, so a sequence that is not valid UTF-8 steps one byte and every byte is counted once. Versions 0 to 5 count bytes, as these opcodes did before. `unit_offset` maps a unit index to a byte offset by the same rule, and `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:extract_string` uses both, so the index still counts from 1 and the count clamps to the units left. The multibyte forms MBStringLength (0x31) and MBStringExtract (0x35) count code points at every version; see the `Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:unit_count (MBStringLength 0x31 and MBStringExtract 0x35)` section at the tail. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:StringLengthAndExtractCountCodePointsFromSwfSix`. The SWF 6 unit rule is from memory and is not checked against the spec mirror.

## Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:to_text

`to_text` takes the run's SWF version with no default, so a call site that omits it does not compile. Undefined converts to the empty text for SWF 1 to 6 and to "undefined" for version 0 and SWF 7 and later. Null, Boolean, Number and text do not change. The rule reaches Add2 (0x47), StringAdd (0x21), StringEquals (0x13), StringLess (0x29), StringGreater (0x68), ToString (0x4B), StringLength (0x14), StringExtract (0x15), CharToAscii (0x32), Trace (0x26), and the names used by GetVariable (0x1C) and SetVariable (0x1D). Test: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:UndefinedIsEmptyTextFromSwfOneToSix`. The SWF 1 to 6 rule is from memory and is not checked against the spec mirror. Not compiled or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.
