## Radicle/src/c_api_swf_art.cpp:radicle_swf_bitmap_png (ABI 84, SWF bitmap PNG export)

ABI 84 is 83 plus the one export `radicle_swf_bitmap_png`, which hands `fo4::swf::bitmap_to_png` through the C ABI for the decoded bitmap of the flat tag `radicle_swf_tag_at` indexes, the same index space `radicle_swf_bitmap_at` uses. The pin is `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsEightyFour`, and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs:CompiledAbiVersion` was regenerated with `generate_interop.py`; `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` is unchanged because the export adds no struct layout. A tag with no decoded bitmap is `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, matching `radicle_swf_bitmap_at`; a bitmap `bitmap_to_png` refuses (15-bit, or a geometry the packed stream no longer matches) is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, because the ABI has no unsupported-format status and the refusal is about the request, not a parse failure. The PNG is copied into an exact-size `malloc` buffer with no trailing NUL, unlike the text exports that go through `radicle_swf_detail::copy_text`, because the bytes are binary and `radicle_swf_write_bytes` uses the same exact-size shape. Every refusal clears both outputs and a NULL argument is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The C# wrapper is `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/SwfFile.cs:SwfFile.BitmapPng`. Regression: a getter that returns bytes for a tag with no bitmap, an export that leaves a stale pointer on refusal, and a PNG that is not the one the C++ encoder produces for the same tag. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_display.cpp:CApiSwfBitmapPng.ExportsTheCppEncoderBytesForALossless2Bitmap`, `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_display.cpp:CApiSwfBitmapPng.RefusesNonBitmapAndUnencodableTagsWithOutputsCleared`, `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/SwfTests.cs:SwfTests.ExportsTheLossless2BitmapAsPngAndRefusesANonBitmapTag`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION (ABI 85, SWF frame SVG export)

ABI 85 is 84 plus the one export `radicle_swf_frame_svg` from `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:radicle_swf_frame_svg`. The pin is `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsEightyFive`, and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs:CompiledAbiVersion` was regenerated with `generate_interop.py`. The lane was written against 83 and took 84 in parallel with `radicle_swf_bitmap_png`; the merge renumbered it to 85.

## Radicle/src/c_api_swf_jpeg.cpp:radicle_swf_bitmap_jpeg (ABI 86)

ABI 86 is 85 plus the one export `radicle_swf_bitmap_jpeg`, which returns the JPEG stream of a DefineBits (tag 6) or DefineBitsJPEG2 (tag 21) at the flat tag `radicle_swf_tag_at` indexes, the same index space as `radicle_swf_bitmap_png`. The pin was `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsEightySix` until ABI 87 renamed it, `Radicle/include/fo4/c_api.h:RADICLE_ABI_VERSION` moved from 85 to 86, and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs:CompiledAbiVersion` was regenerated with `generate_interop.py`. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tests/abi_layout_probe.cpp` is unchanged because the export adds no struct layout.

The bytes are not stored on the decoded tag. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_bitmap.cpp:decode_jpeg_tag` keeps only `SwfJpeg::image_size`, so `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_jpeg.cpp:radicle_swf_bitmap_jpeg` reads the raw tag bytes from `SwfTag::payload` and skips the two-byte character id. The tables are the nearest tag 8 before the image in flat pre-order, found by `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_jpeg.cpp:nearest_jpeg_tables`. SWF requires the tables tag to precede the DefineBits it serves, so a tables tag after the image is ignored: `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/SwfTests.cs:SwfTests.ExportsTheDefineBitsImageAsJpegAndRefusesANonJpegTag` has its tables after the image and gets the bare image back.

The splice drops the tables' trailing EOI (FFD9) and the image's leading SOI (FFD8), then concatenates them, so the output is the tables stream followed by the image body. A DefineBits image with no preceding tables is returned as it is, and an empty tables payload counts as no tables. DefineBitsJPEG2 is self-contained and is never spliced.

An erroneous FFD9FFD8 pair at the head of the image data is removed first by `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_jpeg.cpp:without_leading_seam` for both tag 6 and tag 21, before the splice, so a seam left by a bad encoder does not reach the output. An image that is empty after the seam removal is `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`.

DefineBitsJPEG3 and DefineBitsJPEG4 (tags 35 and 90) carry a separate alpha plane. They decode as JPEGs, but `radicle_swf_bitmap_jpeg` refuses them with `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` until the lossless-PNG-of-alpha-composite lane lands; the refusal is by tag code, not by whether the alpha decodes. A non-JPEG tag or a tag with no decoded JPEG is also `RADICLE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, and every refusal clears both outputs. A NULL argument is `RADICLE_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The JPEG is copied into an exact-size `malloc` buffer, freed with `radicle_free_bytes`, as `radicle_swf_bitmap_png` does. The C# wrapper is `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/SwfFile.cs:SwfFile.BitmapJpeg`.

Regression: a DefineBits image returned without its tables, which does not decode; a leading FFD9FFD8 seam kept in the output; an alpha JPEG3 exported as if it were alpha-free; and a NULL output written through instead of refused. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_display.cpp:CApiSwfBitmapJpeg.SplicesTheJpegTablesOntoADefineBitsImage`, `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_display.cpp:CApiSwfBitmapJpeg.DropsAnErroneousLeadingSeamForTagSixAndTagTwentyOne`, `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_display.cpp:CApiSwfBitmapJpeg.RefusesNonJpegAndAlphaJpegTagsWithOutputsCleared`, `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_display.cpp:CApiSwfBitmapJpeg.RejectsNullArgumentsWithOutputsCleared`, and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/SwfTests.cs:SwfTests.ExportsTheDefineBitsImageAsJpegAndRefusesANonJpegTag`.

## Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp:svg_is_well_formed

`Radicle/tests/test_swf_real.cpp:svg_is_well_formed` rejects an export that contains the text "nan" or "inf", which catches a non-finite number printed into an attribute. Since bitmap fills embed a base64 PNG in `href`, the check runs on a copy with every `base64,` payload erased up to its closing quote, because a real PNG payload contains those three-letter runs by chance and would be reported as a malformed export. Detects a false "exports malformed SVG" failure on the Fallout 4 data runner.

## Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:unit_count (MBStringLength 0x31 and MBStringExtract 0x35)

MBStringLength (0x31) and MBStringExtract (0x35) come from the SWF 5 multibyte opcode set. This runtime stores text as UTF-8, and the slice has no movie codepage, so both count code points at every SWF version, the same unit that StringLength uses from SWF 6. This is a version-independent choice, not a version gate: a SWF 5 movie gets code points where the byte count of StringLength would apply. `Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.hpp:kCodePointVersion` (6) is passed to `unit_count` and `unit_offset` in `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action` for 0x31 and in `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:extract_string` for 0x35, while `to_text` and `to_number` still use the movie's own version, so an undefined operand keeps its SWF 5 meaning. MBCharToAscii (0x36) and MBAsciiToChar (0x37) use the same code point unit, see the tail section. Regression: a byte count for MBStringLength on SWF 5 traces 4 on the e-acute row instead of 3, and a byte-indexed MBStringExtract splits the e-acute. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:MultibyteStringOpcodesCountCodePointsAtEveryVersion`, `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:MultibyteCharOpcodesUseCodePointsAtEveryVersion`, and the two underflow rows for 0x36 and 0x37 in `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:NewOperatorsRefuseAShortStack`. The SWF 5 MB opcode set and the choice of code points are from memory and are not checked against the spec mirror.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:Expander::expand (row nesting level and world visibility)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:Expander::expand` stamps each `SwfFrameInstance` with `nesting_level`: 0 on the root timeline, one more for each enclosing sprite, passed down as `level + 1` on the recursive call. Each sprite's own timeline is expanded at level 0 too, so the scale matches the root. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body` scopes clip masks by that field. The old scope counted `/` in `path`, so a display name that contains `/` moved a row to the wrong level. `path` is still built from names and is no longer read for structure.

`world_visible` is the AND of the row's own PlaceObject3 visible flag and the parent's `world_visible`, so a hidden sprite hides its children as Flash is recalled to do, unverified against a source. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:replay` keeps the authored flag per depth the way it keeps the transform: a MOVE without a visible flag keeps the previous value, a fresh placement resets it to visible, and a flag-only update on a live depth changes it in place. The row stays in the display list with `world_visible` false, because the AVM2 runtime and other readers still need the object. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body` drops a hidden row only after the mask scope has been updated for it, so a hidden row still ends a scope and never opens a mask.

The C ABI is unchanged. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:radicle_swf_frames_instance_at` copies named fields only, so a C caller of the row query still sees a hidden row and has no `nesting_level` or `world_visible`; `radicle_swf_frame_svg` does skip it.

Test regressions, in `Radicle/tests/test_swf_display.cpp`: `SwfFrameSvg.ASlashInARowNameKeepsItsClipLevel` detects a slash in a row name pushing that row out of its mask range (depth 2 at clip depth 2 must stay clipped). `SwfFrameSvg.SkipsAHiddenRowAndTheChildrenOfAHiddenSprite` detects a PlaceObject3 row with its visible byte at 0 being painted, or a child of a hidden sprite being painted, and checks that a visible sibling still paints.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action (MBCharToAscii 0x36 and MBAsciiToChar 0x37)

MBCharToAscii (0x36) pops one value, converts it with `to_text` at the movie's version, and pushes `Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:first_code_point` of the result, so the whole first UTF-8 code point counts at every SWF version and empty text pushes 0. MBAsciiToChar (0x37) pops one value, takes `to_uint32` (truncation toward zero, wrap modulo 2^32, NaN and infinity as 0), keeps the low 16 bits and pushes `Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:encode_code_unit` of them, so the result is UTF-8 at every version. The code point read and the 16-bit wrap are from the SWF spec as recalled, unverified; no SWF spec mirror was available on the development machine to check them. Units 0xD800 to 0xDFFF encode as three-byte sequences, which is not valid UTF-8; this is a known gap, not checked against Flash. Regression: a byte read for 0x36 traces 240 on the U+1F600 row instead of 128512, and an unmasked 0x37 encodes 65601 as a malformed sequence instead of "A". Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:MultibyteCharOpcodesUseCodePointsAtEveryVersion` and the two underflow rows for 0x36 and 0x37 in `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:NewOperatorsRefuseAShortStack`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::call_indexed

callmethod (0x43) and callstatic (0x44) pop the argument count (second operand) and the receiver, box a primitive receiver, and fail with NullReference ("<mnemonic> needs an object receiver") for null. callmethod reads its first operand as a dispatch id and resolves it over the receiver's instance class and its super chain, through `Radicle/src/avm2/class.cpp:Class::resolve_dispatch_trait`, which never matches id 0. A missing trait is CannotCall "callmethod has no method N on this receiver". callstatic reads its first operand as a method_info index into `frame.file`'s method table and refuses an index past the end with MethodIndexOutOfRange "callstatic method index N is outside the M-entry method table". Otherwise it builds a FunctionObject for that method with no captured scope and runs it through invoke with the receiver as this and no scope override, so the callee sees the global scope only. Any object receiver is accepted; the class is not required. The callstatic operand meaning (method_info index, argc, receiver as this) is recalled from the AVM2 overview, not verified against avmplus, whose source was not available on this machine.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::outer_scope_value

getouterscope (0x67) reads the captured scope list held by Frame::outer_scope (set in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::invoke`), indexed directly, not through Frame::scopes. Index 0 being the global scope follows from newfunction capturing the whole scope stack (recalled from the AVM2 overview, unverified against avmplus). Only closures carry a captured scope, because newfunction is the only place it is recorded. A method with no captured scope (a class method, since newclass does not record one) returns NotImplemented "getouterscope needs a closure's captured outer scope; this method has none". Supporting that needs newclass to set captured_scope on every method FunctionObject and invoke's scope logic to change, a restructure outside this change, so it stays refused. An index at or past the captured size is ScopeUnderflow "getouterscope N is outside the M-entry captured outer scope". The NotImplemented message starts with "opcode ", so the real-data probe in `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_scripts_real.cpp:RunsEveryProgramsScriptInitializerWithoutUnimplementedOpcode` counts it as an unimplemented opcode; the ScopeUnderflow refusal is not counted.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::invoke

invoke sets `frame.outer_scope = &function.captured_scope()` next to owner_class. The pointer borrows the FunctionObject's vector; the frame is local to invoke and execute_frame returns before invoke does, and the caller holds the FunctionObject for the call, so the pointer is valid for the frame's life.

## Radicle/src/avm2/class.cpp:Class::resolve_dispatch_trait

Walks the class and its super chain and returns the first Method trait whose dispatch_id matches, so a subclass override shadows its base. Dispatch id 0 never matches: a compiler writes 0 for a method whose id it left for the VM to assign, and this runtime does not assign ids, so 0 names no method. Classes with no file are skipped (builtins and externals), because builtin traits are built with dispatch_id 0 in `Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp`, so matching them would make id 0 resolve to a builtin. Used by callmethod in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::call_indexed`. It matches dispatch ids, not method_info indices.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_body_opcodes

Decision: the verifier's rejection of callmethod in user bytecode is unchanged. Lines 343 to 346 of `verify_body_opcodes` still refuse it with "callmethod is not permitted in user bytecode". The interpreter does not run the verifier, so the callmethod case in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_b.inc` executes bytecode the verifier refuses; the verifier is not consulted at run time.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute_frame

Opcode census from a source scan (not compiled or run). Named opcodes with no case in `interpreter_dispatch_a.inc`, `interpreter_dispatch_b.inc`, `interpreter_dispatch_c.inc` or `interpreter_dispatch_d.inc` (all switch cases of `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute_frame`) fall to the default, which returns NotImplemented "opcode X is not implemented yet". Totals (`Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute_frame`): 169 named, 157 dispatched, 12 not dispatched (after the AVM2 domain-memory change; before it the count was 147 and 22, and before the more-ops change 138 and 31). The 12 are: dxns 0x06, dxnslate 0x07, pushnamespace 0x31, getdescendants 0x59, finddef 0x5F, setpropertylate 0x69, deletepropertylate 0x6B, getglobalslot 0x6E, setglobalslot 0x6F, esc_xelem 0x71, esc_xattr 0x72, checkfilter 0x78. The more-ops change (`Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute_frame`) dispatched hasnext 0x1F, sxi1 0x50, sxi8 0x51, sxi16 0x52, coerce_b 0x81, coerce_i 0x83, coerce_d 0x84, coerce_u 0x88 and coerce_o 0x89. The domain-memory change (`Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_memory.cpp:Interpreter::domain_memory_load` and `Interpreter::domain_memory_store`, dispatched from `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_d.inc`) dispatched li8 0x35, li16 0x36, li32 0x37, lf32 0x38, lf64 0x39, si8 0x3A, si16 0x3B, si32 0x3C, sf32 0x3D and sf64 0x3E, which read and write the current ApplicationDomain's domain memory ByteArray. dxns, dxnslate, pushnamespace, finddef, getdescendants and E4X were left out of that change. NotImplemented also comes from `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::outer_scope_value`, which returns it for a getouterscope in a method with no captured scope.

Detects callmethod resolving only the receiver's own class. Derived has no traits and extends Holder, so dispatch id 1 must reach Holder's scale trait through the super chain and return 4; an own-class-only lookup gives CannotCall.

Detects dispatch id 0, which compilers write as "VM assigns" (recalled, unverified against avmplus), matching a method whose dispatch_id is also 0. Detects getouterscope 1 in a closure failing to read the captured scope, or reading the wrong entry. The expected value is 7, the captured object at index 1. ## Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:object_ops

The object slice adds an object kind to the value type. `Radicle/include/fo4/avm1/interpreter.hpp:Avm1Data` has an `Object` kind and a `std::shared_ptr<Avm1Object>` handle, so an object is a reference: a copy of the value (through PushDuplicate, a variable or a property read) names the same `Avm1Object`. `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.hpp:Avm1Object` has no prototype or class. Its properties sit in a `std::map` for lookup and `order` keeps insertion order for a later enumerate record. `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:put` keeps the two in step and `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:erase_property` removes from both. The records `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:object_ops` runs are listed in `## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_actions`. CallFunction, CallMethod and NewMethod now run (see the function section at the tail); Enumerate, Enumerate2, InstanceOf and Extends stay refused by name.

An array is an `Avm1Object` with `is_array` set. `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:make_object` starts its `length` at 0 with no entry in `order`, and `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:put` raises `length` to the index plus one when the key is a canonical array index (decimal, no leading zero, at most 4294967294). A write never lowers `length`, and `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.hpp:Avm1Object` `order` never lists `length`, so an enumerate record built on `order` would skip it. Setting `length` on an array refuses with Unsupported, since truncation is not in this slice. Deleting `length` from an array pushes false, since ECMA-262 marks it non-configurable (from memory, not checked against a copy of the spec).

Opcodes. `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:new_object` creates an empty object only for `new Object` with a zero count; any other class or argument refuses. `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:init_array` pops a count and that many values, `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:init_object` pops a count and that many (name, value) pairs, and `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:get_member` and `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:set_member` take the name from the top of the stack with the object below it. `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:delete_member` and `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:delete_variable` push a Boolean for whether something was removed. A count that is not a Number, is not a whole number or is larger than the stack holds refuses with StackUnderflow, through `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:pop_count`.

Unverified against the SWF spec v19 mirror, which is not on this machine: the operand order. NewObject pops the name first and then the count. `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:init_array` takes element 0 from the value on top of the stack under the count, and element i from the value i places below that, so the value pushed last is element 0 (recalled, unverified). `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:init_object` takes each pair pushed as name then value, with the value on top, and reads the pairs from the deepest up, so the first pair pushed is the first property (recalled, unverified). GetMember and SetMember pop the name first and then the object. A GetMember on undefined or null pushes undefined, and a SetMember on undefined or null does nothing, both from memory of AS2. A member of a number, string or boolean refuses, because without prototypes `"abc".length` has no answer here. Delete of a missing property or variable pushes false, while ECMA-262 `delete` of a missing reference is true; the Flash result is not checked.

Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_objects.cpp:InitObjectThenGetMemberReadsEachPair`, `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_objects.cpp:SetMemberAndArrayLengthFollowTheWrittenKey`, `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_objects.cpp:InitArrayLengthAndElementOrder`, `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_objects.cpp:MemberAndConstructorRefusalsTraceNothing` and `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_objects.cpp:DeleteReturnsWhetherSomethingWasRemoved`. The TypeOf rows for object and array are in `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_ops.cpp:TypeOfNamesEachDataKind`. `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:ObjectAndFunctionOpcodesStayRefusedByName` now refuses Enumerate, InstanceOf and Extends; CallFunction, CallMethod and NewMethod were removed from it when the function slice made them run. Not compiled or run on the development machine; CI is the first compile and run.

## Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:Avm1Object::~Avm1Object

The destructor moves every child object onto a worklist and releases them from there, expanding a node's own children only when it is popped with `use_count` 1, so neither a chain nor a graph that shares children recurses once per link: the last holder to be popped always sees the count at 1. A child that another handle outside the worklist still holds stays alive, since that handle owns it. A cycle, an object that holds itself through a property, is never freed, because there is no collector; that is a known ceiling. `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_objects.cpp:DeepObjectChainTearsDownWithoutRecursion` builds a chain of 100000 objects and expects Ok after 2300010 steps. Not compiled or run on the development machine.

## Radicle/src/avm1/state.hpp:Avm1State

`Avm1State`, `kUnderflow` and `pop` moved out of the anonymous namespace of `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp` into this header, so `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp` pops operands from the same stack without a second copy. The records that `execute_action` already runs behave as before.

## Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:to_text

An object renders as `[object Object]`, which is the AS2 trace text of a plain object as recalled; not checked against the spec mirror. Arrays render the same way here. AS2 joins the elements with commas through Array.prototype.toString, which needs the prototype lane, so an array's text is a known gap. ToString (0x4B) and the text operands of StringAdd (0x21) and StringEquals (0x13) read this text.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:loose_equal

Two objects compare Equals2 equal only when they are the same `Avm1Object`, by pointer identity, and `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:strict_equal` uses the same identity. An object against a number or text converts to its text first, the ECMA-262 ToPrimitive path, so the object equals the text `[object Object]`. The ToPrimitive order is from ECMA-262 as recalled. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_objects.cpp:ObjectsConvertToTheObjectTextAndCompareByIdentity`.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:add_values

When either operand of Add2 (0x47) is an object, the result is text, because ToPrimitive gives an ordinary object its text and `+` then concatenates. So an object plus 1 traces `[object Object]1`, not NaN. From ECMA-262 as recalled; not checked against the spec mirror.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:to_number

ToNumber of an object is NaN, which is what ECMA-262 gives for the text `[object Object]`, since ToPrimitive then ToNumber of that text is NaN. `to_boolean` reads an object as true, as ECMA-262 does.

## Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:object_ops (ceilings of the object slice)

The object slice has these known gaps, so that none is read as AS2 behavior. Stored values are copied per step, since `Avm1Data` holds its text by value, and there is no byte budget for the properties of a run. A loop that stores a long string under many names can hold many copies up to the step limit; the operand stack has the same exposure through PushDuplicate, see `## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:push_result`. A per-run byte budget is the fix when a real movie needs one. `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:less_than` still compares an object as NaN, where ECMA-262 compares the object's text with a string. A count written as text (a String rather than a Number) refuses in `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:pop_count` rather than being converted. A cycle of objects leaks, see `## Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:Avm1Object::~Avm1Object`.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:pool_encodable (pool references, out-of-spec kinds and u30 fields)

`Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:pool_encodable` runs in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:AbcFile::serialize` after `detail::check_pool_indices` and before any byte is written. It applies the rules `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:parse_multiname_pool` and `parse_ns_set_pool` apply, so a model it accepts parses back. A QName `ns`, a Multiname `ns_set` and an ns_set member are compared with `>=` against their pool size with no index-0 exemption, because the parser does the same. A multiname `name` is checked only for the kinds that write it, and 0 is the "any" sentinel there. A TypeName `name` and each `params` entry must be below the entry's own index. Entries 1 and up are checked, because index 0 of each pool is the reserved slot that is never written. Namespace, multiname and value kinds are tested against the enum values in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:namespace_kind_known`, `multiname_kind_known` and `value_kind_known`, and return `AbcStatus::BadNamespaceKind`, `BadMultinameKind` and `BadValueKind`. Trait value kinds are read only on Slot and Const traits with a non-zero `value_index`, the only traits that write a kind byte. A trait kind above Const was already refused as `AbcStatus::InconsistentModel` by `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:traits_encodable`.

Hand-derived corruption: an unchecked writer emitted a QName with `ns` equal to the namespace count, which `parse_multiname_pool` reads back as `IndexOutOfRange`; an unknown multiname kind byte with no following fields, which shifts every later byte. The u30 rule is different. `Radicle/src/abc/byte_reader.cpp:ByteReader::u30` masks to 30 bits, so a value of 0x40000000 is written as the five bytes `80 80 80 80 04` and reads back as 0. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:fits_u30` refuses such fields with `InconsistentModel` in `model_encodable` and `traits_encodable`. Pool-index fields need no extra check, because a value of 2^30 or more is past every pool and `check_pool_indices` already refuses it. Namespace `name` is not a pool index, so it is covered by `fits_u30`.

- Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_write.cpp:RejectsPoolReferencesThatTheParserWouldRefuse` catches a dropped reference check in `multiname_refs_past_end`, one case per rule (QName ns at the namespace count, name at the string count, MultinameL ns_set past the set pool, an ns_set member at the namespace count, and a TypeName base and param that are not earlier). `Radicle/tests/test_abc_write.cpp:RejectsOutOfSpecKindValuesWithoutWritingBytes` catches a missing kind check, with namespace kind 0x09, multiname kind 0x08, trait and option value kind 0x09, and trait kind 7 (the last pins the existing `traits_encodable` refusal). `Radicle/tests/test_abc_write.cpp:RejectsU30FieldsPastTheMaskedRangeAndKeepsTheLargestValue` catches a u30 field at 0x40000000 written unmasked, and a too-strict bound that would also refuse 0x3FFFFFFF, which must still serialize and read back. Every refusal case expects an empty output buffer.
## Radicle/include/fo4/c_api_runtime.h:radicle_runtime_entry

ABI 87 appends `ratio` (uint16) and `cache_as_bitmap` (uint8) to `radicle_runtime_entry` after `filter_count`, so every earlier field keeps its offset. On LP64 the struct grows from 176 to 184 bytes: `filter_count` ends at 176, `ratio` sits at 176, `cache_as_bitmap` at 178, and the struct pads to 184. `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_quest.cpp:CApiQuest.AbiVersionIsEightySeven` pins the bump, and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RadicleNative.g.cs:RadicleNative.CompiledAbiVersion` is the regenerated constant. `Radicle/bindings/csharp/tools/generate_interop.py` does not read `fo4/c_api_runtime.h` (its HEADERS list omits it), so `RuntimeEntry` is hand-maintained in `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/RuntimeNative.cs` and no layout probe covers it; its layout was checked by hand against the header.

## Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:fill_entry

`ratio` is `SnapshotEntry::ratio` with an absent value written as 0, so a placement with no morph ratio and a placement with ratio 0 are indistinguishable through the C entry. The snapshot hash still tells them apart (`Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:snapshot_hash`). Whether a morph with no ratio draws the same frame as ratio 0 is UNVERIFIED against Flash; the C field is 0 in both cases, and a host that needs the distinction must add a presence flag, which would be another ABI bump. `cache_as_bitmap` is written as 0 or 1 from `SnapshotEntry::cache_as_bitmap`, the same convention `visible` uses in this function.

`blend_mode` and `visible` were already in `radicle_runtime_entry` and in the C# `RuntimeEntry` before ABI 87; this change did not add them. `filter_count` still counts the AS3 `filters` array (`Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:make_entry` takes it from `DisplayObject::filters`), not the PlaceObject3 filter list in `SnapshotEntry::placed_filters`. The placed filter list is not exposed through the C ABI: a `SwfFilter` carries gradient and matrix vectors, so exposing it needs per-entry storage and a new indexed export, which this change left out. Until that lands, a host that draws placed filters has no C-level data for them.

Regression: a C entry that drops the placed ratio or cache flag, or inverts `visible`, so a host draws the wrong morph frame or bitmap cache. Tests: `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime.cpp:SnapshotEntriesCarryAPlacementsRatioAndCacheFlag` (a PlaceObject3 with ratio 3, blend 8, visible off and cache on, read back through `radicle_runtime_snapshot_entry_at`, with the root keeping ratio 0, cache off, visible on) and `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop.Tests/RuntimeTests.cs:SnapshotEntriesCarryAPlacementsRatioAndCacheFlag` (the same movie through `Radicle/bindings/csharp/Radicle.Interop/Runtime.cs:RuntimeSnapshotEntry`, which gained `Ratio` and `CacheAsBitmap`).

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body (hidden and sprite mask rows)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body` reads a row's clip depth before its visibility, so a hidden shape row opens its mask and emits the `clipPath` geometry, but paints nothing for itself. This is recalled, unverified against Flash: Flash applies a mask whose visible flag is false. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.HiddenRowWithAClipDepthStillOpensItsMask` detects a hidden row that opens no mask (the visible row at depth 2 would then be drawn unclipped) or one that paints its own square.

A sprite row with a clip depth is a mask too. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:sprite_clip_to_svg` builds its `clipPath` from the descendant shape rows and static text rows (see `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:sprite_clip_to_svg`). `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:descendants_end` takes the contiguous rows after the sprite whose nesting level is deeper, which is exact because `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:build_display_list` pushes a sprite row before it expands that sprite's children straight after it at level plus one. Each child's fill paths carry that row's world transform as a `transform` attribute on each `<path>`: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:shape_fill_paths_to_svg` takes it as its fourth argument and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:fill_paths` writes it, and a shape mask passes nothing, so its output is unchanged. A sprite's `clipPath` has no transform of its own, because its children sit at different places. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body` moves the `mask_end` cursor past the descendants, so they paint nothing themselves. Test: `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.ASpriteMaskClipsWithItsShapeChildrenAndPaintsNothingItself` detects a sprite mask that draws its children unmasked, a clipPath built with no children, or a child path that drops its transform (the child at 20 px would print at the origin).

A sprite with no descendant shape rows gets an empty `<clipPath id="r<index>clip">`, which clips every later row out of its scope, the same as an empty shape mask. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:fill_paths` emits no path for a fill with no loops, so a shape with no filled loops also yields an empty clipPath.

Inside `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:sprite_clip_to_svg`, a descendant contributes only when its `world_visible` equals its sprite's. A hidden child of a visible sprite is left out, and the children of a hidden sprite all inherit the hidden flag and are all included, which keeps the hidden-mask rule above. Recalled, unverified against Flash.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:sprite_clip_to_svg` ignores a descendant's own clip depth, so a mask nested inside a sprite mask adds its geometry to the union. Unverified against Flash.

Ids: a sprite mask is `r<index>clip` for the sprite's row index, and its descendants' fill defs and paths use `r<child index>f`, which a painted row would use as well. Descendant rows are never painted, so each id is written once per document.

The two frame tests sit in `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp`, not `Radicle/tests/test_swf_display.cpp`, which was at 740 lines and whose movie builders are in its anonymous namespace. They build the `SwfFile` and `SwfDisplayList` by hand, so they check `frame_body` and not `build_display_list`; the nesting levels and visibility flags are written in by hand.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body (morph rows)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:replay` carries a placement's ratio the way it carries `clip_depth`: a MOVE with no ratio keeps the depth's previous ratio, a fresh placement takes its own, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:Expander::expand` copies it into `Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_display.hpp:SwfFrameInstance` as `ratio`, which stays absent for a row no placement gave one. `SwfFrameInstance::operator==` compares it. The C ABI is unchanged: `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:radicle_swf_frames_instance_at` copies named fields only, so a C caller of the row query sees no ratio, while `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:radicle_swf_frame_svg` now draws the morph rows.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:character_shape` (formerly row_shape) resolves a row's character in the shape tags first and then in the morph tags. For a morph it calls `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:interpolate_morph_shape` with `ratio / 65535`, an absent ratio being 0, and the returned `SwfShape` lives in the frame loop. `frame_body` and `sprite_clip_to_svg` then call the same `shape_defs_to_svg`, `shape_paths_to_svg` and `shape_fill_paths_to_svg` as a shape row, at the row's world transform, so visible, clip depth and sprite-mask handling are the shape rules unchanged.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:interpolate_morph_shape` builds that shape. Its records are `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:interpolate_morph_commands` unchanged, so the geometry rounding is the one that function already has. Each solid fill blends its start and end ARGB colour one byte at a time in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:blend_color`, using `blend_twips`, which rounds halves away from zero. Each line blends its width and colour the same way, keeps the start flags, and gets a miter limit only when both ends carry one. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:blend_rect` blends the bounds so a caller of the public function gets a usable viewBox; the frame path does not read them.

Refused, as before: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:interpolate_morph_shape` returns nullopt for any fill whose type is not 0x00 (linear and radial gradients 0x10 and 0x12, focal 0x13, bitmaps 0x40 to 0x43) and for any line with a fill, so such a row is not drawn. Gradient and bitmap interpolation (stop lists, gradient and bitmap matrices, focal points) is not written; it was left out to keep the lane small. A morph with a gradient fill refuses even when no record uses that fill.

Blend numbers, hand-derived for `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.MorphRowAtRatioHalfWayBlendsEdgesAndColour`: at ratio 32768 the factor is 32768/65535 = 0.5000076, so a 100 twip edge blends to 150 twips (7.5 px), and red `#ff0000` to blue `#0000ff` blends to `#7f0080` (red 127.498 rounds to 127, blue 127.502 to 128). Ratio 0 gives the start shape exactly and 65535 the end shape exactly.

Tests, all in `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp`:
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.MorphRowAtRatioZeroDrawsTheStartShape` detects a morph row at ratio 0 drawn as the end shape (10 px, blue) or not drawn at all.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.MorphRowAtFullRatioDrawsTheEndShape` detects a morph row at ratio 65535 drawn as the start shape (5 px, red), or a ratio clamped back to the start.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.MorphRowAtRatioHalfWayBlendsEdgesAndColour` detects a ratio that is ignored or read as a switch between the two shapes, since the midpoint must show a 7.5 px edge and `#7f0080`.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.MorphLineWidthBlendsIntoAStrokeAtHalfWay` detects a morph line that is not drawn, keeps its start width (`stroke-width` 1 instead of 1.5) or keeps its end width (2), since `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:blend_line_style` must blend 20 twips to 40 twips into 30 at ratio 32768.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.MorphWithAGradientFillDrawsNothing` detects a gradient morph drawn with its start solid colour or any approximation, since `Radicle/src/swf/swf_morph.cpp:interpolate_morph_shape` must refuse it and leave the body empty.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.PlaceObjectRatioIsKeptAcrossAMoveAndOverridden` runs a real movie through `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:build_display_list`: a PlaceObject2 ratio of 16384 must survive a MOVE with no ratio in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:replay`, a MOVE with ratio 65535 must override it, and a placement with no ratio (depth 2) must stay absent. It detects a replay that drops the ratio on a MOVE, one that does not overwrite it, or one that gives a ratio-less placement a value.

Unverified against Flash: that a morph interpolates line width and colour per ratio, that a morph row with a clip depth masks with its interpolated fill geometry (it takes the shape mask path, not tested), and the twip rounding of the blend. Nothing was compiled or run on the development machine for this change; the expected strings were derived by hand from the emitter and need CI.

## Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:Hasher (snapshot hash basis)

`Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:Hasher` now starts from the standard FNV-1a 64 offset basis 14695981039346656037, the same basis `Radicle/src/avm2/display_snapshot.cpp:fnv1a64` uses. The old basis 1469598103934665603 was one digit short, so every `Radicle/src/avm2/snapshot.cpp:snapshot_hash` value changed once, at this commit. No consumer should have persisted them: the hash is compared within a run (`Radicle/src/avm2/replay.cpp:replay`, `Radicle/src/c_api_runtime.cpp:radicle_runtime_snapshot_hash`), and the real-data pins in `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_runtime_real.cpp:kPinned` are all zero. A repo search found no persisted snapshot hash value.

## Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:invoke (user functions, calls and the depth limit)

A script-defined function is a `Function` value that holds a shared `Avm1FunctionBody` (`Radicle/src/avm1/state.hpp:Avm1FunctionBody`, `Radicle/include/fo4/avm1/interpreter.hpp:Avm1Data`), so copies of the value name one decoded body. `Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:invoke` gives each call a fresh `Avm1Call` (a locals map, a register file of the declared register count, and a return value), binds the preloads and the parameters, and runs the body through `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:run_block` on an `Avm1Block` whose `call` points at that frame. Every nested call runs through the same `Avm1Run`, so the step counter (`Avm1Result::steps`) and the depth counter (`Avm1Run::depth`) are shared across calls. `kMaxCallDepth` is 64: the 65th nested call is refused with `ResourceLimit` and the message "the call depth of 64 functions was reached". Recursion is native. An AVM1 call level is about four native frames (run_block, execute_action, call_function, invoke). The limit of 64 is chosen for a 1 MB Windows Debug stack, as the lead reports for CI; that stack use was not measured here.

Recalled, not verified against Flash: CallFunction pops the name, then the argument count, then the arguments, and the first argument popped is argument 1 (`Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:call_function`). CallMethod and NewMethod pop the method name, the object, the count and then the arguments (`Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:invoke_method`). DefineFunction2 flags 0x01 PreloadThis, 0x04 PreloadArguments, 0x10 PreloadSuper, 0x40 PreloadRoot, 0x80 PreloadParent and 0x100 PreloadGlobal, with preloads taking consecutive registers from 1 in the order this, arguments, super, root, parent, global (`Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:invoke`). The DefineFunction2 record fields are name, parameter count (UI16), register count (UI8), flags (UI16), each parameter as register (UI8) and name, then body size (UI16) (`Radicle/src/avm1/decode.cpp:Decoder::function_header`). StoreRegister does not pop (`Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:store_register`). DefineLocal pops the value and then the name, and DefineLocal2 pops the name only (`Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:define_local` and `define_local2`). The bytes in `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp` are built from these orders, so a wrong order fails the traces rather than passing.

Ceilings, each refused by name or documented here:
- The suppress flags (0x02, 0x08, 0x20) are read and ignored.
- There are no closures: a function sees the globals and its own locals and registers only. Function values compare equal per DefineFunction record (`Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:define_function` caches one body per record offset), so two evaluations of one literal are equal here but not in Flash.
- CallFunction runs with `this` undefined. `this` and `arguments` are reachable only as preload registers, not as names through GetVariable.
- A preload of super, _root, _parent or _global is refused at call time with "preloading super, _root, _parent or _global is not in this slice" (`Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:invoke`).
- NewMethod creates a plain object with no prototype. The function's return value replaces it only when that value is an object.
- A method on a value that is not an object, or a name that is not a script function, is refused with the name (`Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:invoke_method`).
- A top-level Jump or If that lands inside a function body is not refused. The top-level list is flat, so the branch runs the body records as top-level code. This is a known hole, not a tested behaviour.
- `Radicle/src/avm1/text_ops.cpp:to_text` renders a function as "[type Function]". That string is recalled, not verified.

## Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:define_function (body capture)

`Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:define_function` always moves the cursor past the records that follow the header in the same flat list, up to the offset `offset + length + body_size`, so a body never runs at definition time. The shared body is built once per DefineFunction record offset and kept in `Radicle/src/avm1/state.hpp:Avm1Run` (`functions`), so a DefineFunction executed again does not copy its records a second time. Regression detected by `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:DefineFunctionCallsWithArgsAndReturnsItsValue`: if the body records stayed in the top-level list, the trace would show their output before the call and the step count would not be 11. `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:DefineFunctionRunTwiceSkipsItsBodyAndReusesIt` detects a repeated definition that runs its nested body inline (the outer function would return 9, not 10) or that loses the body on the second run.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:run_block (step limit across calls and error labels)

`Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:run_block` checks the step limit before each record and counts a record when it starts, so a record the limit refuses is not counted, while a record that starts and then fails is. An error is labelled with the opcode, offset and message of the innermost record only. Outer frames return the status as it is, so a nested failure is never relabelled as the call that contained it. Tests:
- `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:RecursiveFactorialReturnsOneHundredTwentyInSeventyTwoSteps` detects a step counter reset per call, or one that does not count records inside a call. The total is 72 records: 5 at top level (DefineFunction, Push, CallFunction, Trace and the End record, which is a decoded action and counts as a step) plus 15 in each of the four frames for n of 5, 4, 3 and 2 plus 7 in the frame for n of 1. With a limit of 70 the refused record is the top-level Trace at steps 70, with an empty trace.
- `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:StepLimitRefusesTheReturnThatRunsPastTheLimitInsideNestedCalls` detects a limit that applies only at top level. With a limit of 69 the refused record is the Return of the outermost factorial frame (n of 5, opcode 0x3E at steps 69), which runs after four nested calls have returned.
- `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:UnboundedRecursionStopsAtTheCallDepthLimit` detects a missing depth check (a native stack overflow) or a check that fails to count the refused call. The 131 records are 3 at top level (DefineFunction, Push, CallFunction), then Push and CallFunction in each of the 64 accepted frames (3 + 2 * 64), and the refused CallFunction of the 65th call is record 131, at opcode 0x3D, which is counted. The message must name "call depth of 64".

Step counts are hand-derived from the flat record order and have not been run. CI is the first check.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action (function opcodes; supersedes the refusal notes)

This section supersedes the statements that CallFunction, CallMethod, NewMethod and a register push are refused, in `## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_actions` and `## Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:object_ops`. Those are now run. `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action` dispatches DefineFunction (0x9B) and DefineFunction2 (0x8E) to `function_ops::define_function`, CallFunction (0x3D), Return (0x3E), StoreRegister (0x87), DefineLocal (0x3C), DefineLocal2 (0x41), CallMethod (0x52) and NewMethod (0x53) to `Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp` (`function_ops` namespace). `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:push_values` pushes a register (type 4) through `function_ops::push_register`. A Return at top level ends the action list with status Ok. Still refused by name, as `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:ObjectAndFunctionOpcodesStayRefusedByName` pins: Enumerate (0x46), InstanceOf (0x54) and Extends (0x69). That test's refused list lost CallFunction, CallMethod and NewMethod in this change.

## Radicle/src/avm1/state.hpp:Avm1Block (the frame a record runs in)

`Radicle/src/avm1/state.hpp:Avm1Block` pairs the record list and its end offset with an optional `Avm1Call`. A null call is the top level: GetVariable, SetVariable and DefineLocal use the global map. A non-null call is a function frame: GetVariable reads the frame's locals before the globals, SetVariable writes a local only when the name is already one, and DefineLocal and DefineLocal2 always create a local, which shadows the global of the same name. Tests:
- `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:DefineLocalShadowsTheGlobalForOneCall` detects DefineLocal writing the global map (the top-level trace would show 2 for x, not 1, and `variables.at("x").number` would be 2), DefineLocal2 leaking y into the global map (`variables.count("y")` would be 1), and a local read that skips the frame (the trace inside the call would show 1, not 2). Its expected trace is "2", "undefined", "1", "undefined".
- `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:DefineFunction2PreloadsThisAndMapsParametersToRegisters` detects a this preload placed in the wrong register, or a parameter mapped to register 1 instead of its declared register 2. Either makes the result something other than 12 (5 read from this.k plus 7 read from parameter a). The 21 steps (13 top-level records before the call, 6 in the body, then Trace and End) pin the record count, including the SetMember and CallMethod records.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:Avm1Interpreter (the remaining function tests)

- `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:DefineFunctionCallsWithArgsAndReturnsItsValue` (trace "3", 11 steps) detects arguments bound in reverse (the subtraction would give -3), Return not delivering its value, and a body running at definition time (the step count would change).
- `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:DefineFunctionRunTwiceSkipsItsBodyAndReusesIt` (trace "10", "10") detects a repeated DefineFunction that runs its nested body inline or loses the body when the second run reuses the shared copy, since the inner body's Return would end the outer call with 9.
- `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_functions.cpp:FunctionRefusalsAreNamedAndTraceNothing` detects an unsupported path that runs silently, such as a CallFunction of a missing name that yields undefined without a refusal, a refusal that loses its name, a register outside a function read as a value, a preload past the declared register count writing out of bounds (InvalidStream is required), and a preloaded _root that runs. Its first row detects a top-level Return that is refused instead of ending the list.

Not compiled or run on the development machine for this change. The test file, the function model and these notes need CI to confirm the expected strings, step counts and status values.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_c.inc:execute_frame

hasnext (0x1F) pops the index, then the object, and pushes the next 1-based key index (index + 1) while keys remain, else 0. A non-object pushes 0. Its keys come from `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::enumeration_keys`, so hasnext, hasnext2, nextname and nextvalue read one list. sxi1 keeps only the low bit as -1 or 0. sxi8 and sxi16 sign-extend the low byte or low half of ToInt32. coerce_o pushes null for undefined and passes every other value through. The coerce_o and sxi semantics are recalled from the AVM2 overview, not verified against Flash. The verifier stack effects in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_stack.cpp:stack_effect` were already right for these opcodes (0x1F pops 2 and pushes 1; 0x50-0x52, 0x81-0x86 and 0x88-0x89 pop 1 and push 1), so the verifier is unchanged.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_a.inc:execute_frame

coerce_i, coerce_u, coerce_d and coerce_b share the convert_* branch and its to_int32, to_uint32, to_number and to_boolean conversions. The coerce-to-type behaviour for null and undefined (coerce_d of undefined is NaN and of null is 0; coerce_i and coerce_u give 0; coerce_b gives false) is recalled from the AVM2 overview, not verified. The convert_* opcodes were already dispatched, so no convert case was missing.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::enumeration_keys

Builds the key list for an object once per frame, keyed by object pointer in `Frame::iterator_keys`, and rebuilds only when that list is empty. Arrays enumerate index strings. Other objects enumerate own properties, which come from an unordered map so the order is hash order and not insertion order, then slot-like instance traits. This helper exists so hasnext and hasnext2 cannot disagree about the key list that nextname and nextvalue read. Known caveat, not changed here: the cache is never invalidated, so a second enumeration of the same object in the same frame reuses the first list and misses properties added between the two loops. This was already true for hasnext2.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_b.inc:execute_frame

hasnext2 now calls `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::enumeration_keys` instead of building the key list inline. Behaviour is unchanged. The test Hasnext2LoopAgreesWithNextnameAndNextvalue in `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp` covers it.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:SxiOneSignExtendsTheLowBit

Detects sxi1 (0x50) missing, or sign-extending as a mask that gives 1 or 0 instead of -1 or 0. Hand-derived: int 3 has low bit 1, so -1; int 2 has low bit 0, so 0.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:SxiEightSignExtendsTheLowByte

Detects sxi8 (0x51) missing, or zero-extending the low byte. Hand-derived: 0x1FF has low byte 0xFF, so -1; 0x180 has low byte 0x80, so -128 (zero-extension would give 128); 0x7F gives 127.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:SxiSixteenSignExtendsTheLowHalf

Detects sxi16 (0x52) missing, or zero-extending the low half. Hand-derived: 0x18000 has low half 0x8000, so -32768 (zero-extension would give 32768); 0x12345 has low half 0x2345, so 9029 (0x2345).

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:CoerceBMakesANonZeroIntABoolean

Detects coerce_b (0x81) missing, or returning the int 7 unchanged instead of the Boolean true.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:CoerceITruncatesADoubleToAnInt

Detects coerce_i (0x83) missing, or rounding 3.9 to 4 instead of truncating to 3.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:CoerceDMakesAnIntANumber

Detects coerce_d (0x84) missing, or leaving the int 7 as an int instead of a Number.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:CoerceUWrapsANegativeIntToAUint

Detects coerce_u (0x88) missing, or keeping int -1 instead of the uint 4294967295 (2^32 - 1).

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:CoerceOTurnsUndefinedIntoNullAndKeepsOtherValues

Detects coerce_o (0x89) missing, or leaving undefined in place instead of null. The second run checks that the int 5 passes through unchanged.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:HasnextReturnsOneBasedIndexThenZeroAtTheEnd

Detects hasnext (0x1F) missing, or returning a 0-based index, which would make the first key read as index 0 and end the loop. Hand-derived: hasnext(obj, 0) is 1 and hasnext(obj, 1) is 0 for a one-property object, so 1 * 10 + 0 = 10.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:HasnextOnANonObjectEnumeratesNothing

Detects hasnext enumerating a non-object, which would read keys from a number. The expected result is 0.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:HasnextRefusesAShortStackWithStackUnderflow

Detects hasnext reading a missing object as undefined on a one-item stack, instead of refusing with StackUnderflow. This is the only refusal path of hasnext; no wrong-type refusal exists because hasnext returns 0 for a non-object.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:HasnextLoopAgreesWithNextnameAndNextvalue

Detects hasnext, nextname or nextvalue disagreeing on the 1-based key index, so the loop reads no key or the wrong one. Hand-derived: a one-property object {value: 7} gives "" + "value" + 7 = "value7".

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:Hasnext2LoopAgreesWithNextnameAndNextvalue

Detects the shared key helper changing hasnext2's register loop, so it reads a different key than nextname and nextvalue. Hand-derived result "value7", the same as the hasnext loop.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:HasnextLoopVisitsEveryKeyOfAnObject

Detects a hasnext loop that stops after the first key of a two-key object. The check does not depend on key order, since the sum and the count are symmetric. Hand-derived: values 1 and 2 plus 100 per key give 1 + 100 + 2 + 100 = 203.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_more_ops.cpp:NewOpcodesRefuseAnEmptyStackWithStackUnderflow

Detects a new opcode that returns a value from an empty stack instead of refusing with StackUnderflow. Covers sxi1, sxi8, sxi16, coerce_b, coerce_i, coerce_d, coerce_u, coerce_o and hasnext. Before this change these opcodes returned NotImplemented.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:text_paths (static text rows)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:text_paths` draws a DefineText or DefineText2 row as glyph paths. Font, colour, height and the x and y position carry from one TEXTRECORD to the next, and a field a record omits keeps its previous value. Each glyph is `shape_fill_paths_to_svg` over its font's glyph records with one solid fill in the record colour. Its transform is `compose_transform(transform_from_matrix(text.matrix), glyph)`, where the glyph scale is height over 1024 for DefineFont and DefineFont2 and over 20480 for DefineFont3. The choice follows `define_font3`, not `units_per_em`, because the decoder only sets `units_per_em` for DefineFont3 when the font has a layout. The x cursor moves by each glyph's advance even when that glyph draws nothing. The whole row sits under its `world_transform` and takes the same colour filter as a shape row (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body`).

Draws nothing for: a glyph index outside the font's glyph shapes, a record with no known font, no height yet, a font with no glyph shapes, and a text row that carries a clip depth, which is a mask instead (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body`, see the static text clips section at the tail). A record that never sets a colour draws black, which is a guess at Flash's default and is unverified.

Out of scope: dynamic EditText (button up-state rows are now drawn, see the button rows section at the tail). Static text used as a mask and static text inside a clip sprite are drawn, see the static text clips section at the tail (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body`, `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:sprite_clip_to_svg`).

## Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfText (text MATRIX exposed)

`Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfText` gained `matrix`, which `Radicle/src/swf/swf_text.cpp:decode_text_tag` now fills in place of a local it used to drop. The MATRIX was already parsed by `read_matrix`; this only keeps it. No new parsing was added.

- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.StaticTextDrawsEachGlyphAtItsCursorInTheRecordColour` detects text rows dropped from the frame, a cursor that ignores advances or resets wrongly, a missing glyph index that stops the row instead of being skipped, and record colour, y offset or height that does not carry to the next record. It also pins DefineFont2 scale: a 1024-unit square at height 1024 is 51.2 px.
