- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:SwfFrameSvg.StaticTextAppliesItsMatrixAndSkipsFontsWithoutGlyphShapes` detects a DefineText MATRIX that is ignored, which would leave the glyph at `matrix(1 0 0 1 0 0)`, and a font with no glyph shapes that emits an empty group or indexes an empty glyph list.

Expected strings were derived by hand from `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:loops_text` and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_svg.cpp:fill_paths`. Nothing was compiled or run on the development machine for this change, so CI must confirm them.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:collect_frame_controls

The display list used to advance every nested sprite one frame per root tick and loop it at its length, so a movie clip whose frame-1 script calls `stop()` kept looping, and a root timeline with `stop()` or `gotoAndStop(n)` kept playing. `collect_frame_controls` reads the AVM1 `DoAction` tags of one timeline (the root from `file.tags`, a sprite from its `children`), splits them at each ShowFrame, and keeps only the frame-control records, one list per frame. It always returns at least one frame. A timeline with no control record therefore gets empty lists and plays linearly.

Recognised records: Stop (0x07), Play (0x06), NextFrame (0x04), PreviousFrame (0x05), GotoFrame (0x81), and GotoFrame2 (0x9F) only when the record directly before it is a Push whose top value is numeric (Float, Double or Integer, read as `Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:execute_action` reads them) and the record has no scene bias. GotoFrame's u16 is a 0-based index and becomes a jump followed by a Stop, because Ruffle 0.6.0 `action_goto_frame` calls goto with stop=true. GotoFrame2's number is 1-based and becomes a jump to `n - 1` followed by a Play or a Stop from flag bit 0. A number below 1, one that is not an integer, or one above 65535 records nothing (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:frame_number`). The below-1 case matches Ruffle `action_goto_frame_2`, where n<=0 is a no-op. Ruffle reads the number as u16, so a wrap is not copied here and an out-of-range number stays a no-op. A number above the frame count is clamped at landing, see `simulate_playhead`.

A DoAction that does not decode contributes nothing. A DoAction that contains SetTarget (0x8B), SetTarget2 (0x20), WaitForFrame (0x8A), WaitForFrame2 (0x8D), Jump (0x99), If (0x9D), DefineFunction (0x9B), DefineFunction2 (0x8E), With (0x94) or Try (0x8F) is skipped as a whole. Those records make the flat list lie about what runs. SetTarget2 is the one that retargets the following Stop to another clip. Skipping keeps such a clip on the linear playback it had before.

Known ceilings, so none of these reads as AS2 behaviour: GoToLabel (0x8C), Call (0x9E), CallFunction (0x3D), CallMethod (0x52) and DoInitAction (tag 59) are not modelled, so a Stop reached only through a function call still does not stop the clip. The GotoFrame2 flag bits (play = bit 0, scene bias = bit 1) and the 1-based GotoFrame2 number come from Ruffle 0.6.0 `activation.rs`, read in `E:\GardenEngine\GardenEngine-RE-Work\menu-reference\swf-runtime-01a0efb6\native-experiment\ruffle-0.6.0`. They are not measured against Flash. The clamp of a jump above the frame count follows Ruffle 0.6.0 `movie_clip.rs:run_goto`, which does `frame.min(frames_loaded)` (movie_clip.rs:1704) and advances `current_frame` to the clamped frame (movie_clip.rs:1709). The Double Push convention follows `interpreter.cpp`, not a measurement.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:simulate_playhead

`simulate_playhead(controls, ticks)` returns the playhead for ticks 0 to `ticks - 1`. The table is `Playhead::frame_at`, the displayed frame per tick, and `Playhead::entries`, the ascending ticks at which each frame was entered. Tick 0 lands on frame 0 and runs its controls. Each later tick, while the timeline is playing, lands on `(frame + 1) % count` and runs that frame's controls.

`land` runs one frame's controls in order. Stop sets playing false and Play sets it true. GotoFrame and GotoFrame2 record a jump to `min(index, count - 1)`, which is the clamp. NextFrame records a jump to `frame + 1` and stops only when `frame + 1 < count`. PreviousFrame records a jump to `frame - 1` and stops only when `frame > 0`. At an end, next and previous do nothing and do not stop, matching Ruffle `next_frame` (only when current < header frames) and `prev_frame` (only when current > 1). A pending jump runs the target's controls in the same tick, for at most `min(controls.size() + 1, 64)` landings (`kMaxHops`), and a jump still pending after that cap is dropped. The cap guarantees a goto loop returns.

The entry budget is `4 * ticks + 1024` (`kEntriesPerTick`, `kEntrySlack`), counted over the entries stored for this timeline, with the tick-0 entry counted. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:land` checks it before each frame change. Once the count reaches the budget, no further frame change is simulated and the playhead holds its frame. The next tick finds no movement and the loop breaks, so `frame_at` ends at that tick, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:displayed_frame` repeats its last entry for every later age. One forward jump can store up to `count` entries after the check, so the stored total can pass the budget by one jump's skipped frames.

`entries[f]` gets the landing tick whenever the playhead changes to frame `f`, at most once per tick: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:enter` skips a second landing on `f` in the same tick, so one tick's chain adds at most one entry per frame. A forward jump also records the landing tick for every frame it skips, so an instance created on a skipped frame ages from the landing tick and not from age 0. A landing on the frame already shown records nothing, so a goto to the current frame does not reset its children.

The loop stops early when a tick does not move the frame and does not change playing. Controls are deterministic from the frame, so every later tick repeats that tick and records nothing, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:displayed_frame` reads the last `frame_at` entry for every later age, so `frame_at` is not padded to `ticks`. Cost is at most `ticks * 64` hops per timeline, and each hop enters at most `count` frames. The table is built once per timeline in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:build_display_list`, which replaces the earlier O(age) replay per call.

The linear case stores no table. When every frame has an empty control list, `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:simulate_playhead` returns an empty `Playhead`, and `Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:displayed_frame` and `entry_age` compute the same values in closed form, with `count` the frame count: the displayed frame is `t % count`, and the entry tick is `t - t % count + f`, or 0 when `count` is 1. The closed form equals the table for every age the expansion reaches, because an instance on a frame is only in that frame's state when it was created at or before it. This avoids an O(ticks) table for each timeline without frame control. Default-off rows are meant to be unchanged; CI must confirm that.

Ceilings of `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:simulate_playhead`, none fixed here. (a) A legitimate sprite that enters more than 4 frames per tick on average (skipped frames count, so a gotoAndPlay of frame+5 on every frame does) spends the entry budget `4 * ticks + 1024` once `ticks` is large enough for the 1024 slack to run out, and then freezes permanently. (b) A controlled timeline, including a looping one, still costs O(ticks) for `frame_at` and up to the budget in entries, so memory is O(controlled timelines * ticks). (c) `ticks` is the ShowFrame count, bounded by `Radicle/src/swf/swf_internal.hpp:kMaxTags` (1 << 18 = 262144 tags), not by the 65535 frame count a header can state.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:enter

`enter` stores the landing tick on each frame it enters, once per tick, and counts each stored entry against the budget in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:simulate_playhead`.

Known ceiling: a rewind restarts a child. A child created on frame `f` ages from the newest landing on `f`, so when the playhead lands on `f` again, that child restarts at the landing tick. Ruffle `survives_rewind` (movie_clip.rs:1903) keeps a candidate child when a final placement exists at its depth (movie_clip.rs:1921-1925), so Ruffle keeps it. The playhead keeps no depth-level placement state, so this is not fixed here.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:displayed_frame and entry_age

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_display.cpp:displayed_frame` returns `timeline.playhead.frame_at[min(age, size - 1)]`, so ages past an early break read the last entry, or `age % count` when `frame_at` is empty (no frame control in the timeline). `entry_age` returns the last entry of `entries[frame]` at or before `age`, found by `std::upper_bound`, or 0 when there is none. When `frame_at` is empty it returns `age - age % count + frame`, or 0 when `count` is 1. `count` is `timeline.frames.size()` in both. `Expander::expand` uses both as before: `index` is the displayed frame, `born` is the entry tick of the instance's created frame, and the child age is `age - born`. The instance rows keep `timeline_frame = index`, which is the displayed frame.

`build_display_list` sets every timeline's `playhead` with one shared tick count, the longest timeline in the movie (root or sprite frame count), so every age the expansion asks for is in range. With `apply_frame_control` off, `controls_for` returns empty lists, so the display is the authored linear one. The consumers that index frames by authored position (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_edit.cpp:build_display_list` callers at lines 323 and 339, `Radicle/src/swf/swf_depth.cpp:build_display_list` at 418, `Radicle/src/swf/swf_keyframe.cpp:build_display_list` at 222) keep the default.

## Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf_display.hpp:SwfDisplayOptions

`apply_frame_control` (default false) turns on the frame-control playhead for the whole movie. `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:build_checked_display` sets it, because that is the build the C ABI frame and SVG handles render from. Other callers keep the authored frames unless they opt in.

## Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:build_checked_display

The C ABI frames and `frame_to_svg` now render the controlled playhead, so a clip whose script stops shows the held frame. The C ABI suites build with no frame-control DoAction, so their rows are unchanged. The one DoAction in `Radicle/tests/test_c_api_swf_text.cpp` is only disassembled and never builds frames.

Known ceiling: `Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:build_checked_display` switches control on for every caller, including `radicle_swf_frames_open` (`Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:120`) and `radicle_swf_frame_svg` (`Radicle/src/c_api_swf_display.cpp:216`). A stopped sprite's later authored frames therefore repeat the held frame in the frames handle, instead of showing their authored content.

## Tests in Radicle/tests/test_swf_frame_control.cpp:SwfFrameControl

Clip rows show the clip frame that `Art/Cell` (or `Art/Cell/Leaf`) displays at root ages 0 to 4, and `kMissing` where the row is absent. Each test detects the regression stated, and each expectation was derived by hand from the rules above. Nothing was compiled or run here, so CI must confirm them.

- `StopOnTheSecondFrameHoldsTheClipThere` detects a stop() that is ignored, which would show 0,1,2,0,1 instead of 0,1,1,1,1.
- `GotoFrameJumpsBackAndKeepsPlaying` detects a GotoFrame that is dropped, or that does not resume playing after its target. Frame 2 is GotoFrame 0 then Play: tick 2 lands on 0, then the clip advances, giving 0,1,0,1,0. A dropped goto would show 0,1,2,0,1.
- `BareGotoFrameStopsAtItsTarget` detects a GotoFrame that keeps playing after its jump. Frame 2 is GotoFrame 0 with no Play: tick 2 lands on 0 and stops, giving 0,1,0,0,0. Playing on would show 0,1,0,1,0.
- `GotoLoopEndsAtTheHopCap` detects a goto loop with no cap, which never returns. Frame 1 jumps to 2 and frame 2 jumps to 1, both with Play. Tick 1 lands 1,2,1,2 (four landings, `controls.size() + 1`) and stays on 2. Tick 3 repeats that. Expected 0,2,0,2,0. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:land` caps it at `min(4, 64)` here, and the budget is 1044 for five ticks, so neither changes the rows.
- `StopThenPlayOnTheSameFrameResumesThePlayhead` detects a Play ignored after a Stop on the same frame, which would show 0,1,1,1,1 instead of 0,1,2,0,1.
- `GotoFrame2TakesItsFrameFromThePrecedingPush` detects a 0-based frame read and an ignored play flag. Push 2 with flag 0 is frame 1, a self-jump that stops, giving 0,1,1,1,1. A 0-based read would show 0,2,2,2,2. Push 3 with flag 1 is frame 2 and plays, giving 0,2,0,2,0. A Stop there would show 0,2,2,2,2.
- `GotoFrame2ZeroIsNoOpAndAboveTheLastFrameClamps` detects a zero number that jumps or stops, and a number above the frame count that is dropped. Push 0 is a no-op, giving 0,1,2,0,1. Push 9 with flag 0 clamps to frame 2 and stops, giving 0,2,2,2,2. A dropped jump would show 0,1,2,0,1.
- `NextAndPreviousFrameStepOnceAndStop` detects a NextFrame or PreviousFrame that wraps, does not stop, or is ignored. Frame 1 next gives 0,2,2,2,2. Frame 2 previous gives 0,1,1,1,1.
- `NextAndPreviousAtTheEndsAreNoOps` detects a next at the last frame or a previous at the first that wraps and stops. Frame 0 previous and frame 2 next do nothing and the clip keeps playing, giving 0,1,2,0,1. The wrap-and-stop bug would show 0,1,0,0,0.
- `AStopAfterSetTarget2IsNotAppliedToTheClip` detects a SetTarget2 that is not in the flow set, which would apply the following Stop to this clip. The tag is skipped, giving 0,1,2,0,1. Applying the Stop would show 0,1,1,1,1.
- `ChildCreatedAfterAStopAgesFromItsFrameEntry` detects a child created on a frame after frame 0 that ages from the root start. Frame 1 places sprite 8 and stops, so frame 1 is entered at tick 1 and the child is born at age 1. Art/Cell is 1 for root ages 1 to 4, and Art/Cell/Leaf is kMissing,0,1,0,1. Ageing from the root start would show kMissing,1,0,1,0.
- `SkippedFrameChildAgesFromTheLandingTick` detects a frame skipped by a forward jump that never gets its entry, so it ages from 0. Frame 1 jumps to 3 and stops at tick 1, which skips frame 2. Frame 2 places the child, so the child is born at the landing tick 1. Art/Cell is 3 for root ages 1 to 4, and Art/Cell/Leaf is kMissing,0,1,0,1. Ageing from 0 would show kMissing,1,0,1,0.
- `StopOnTheRootTimelineHoldsTheRootFrame` detects a root timeline that ignores its own stop. With the option on, Marker is 0,1,1,1,1 and Late, placed on root frame 3, never appears. A root that ignores stop would show Marker 0,1,2,3,4 and Late at frames 3 and 4.
- `ByDefaultTheRootTimelineKeepsItsAuthoredFrames` detects the option leaking into the default display. With the default options Marker is 0,1,2,3,4 and Late is kMissing,kMissing,kMissing,3,4. Holding the root would show the controlled rows instead.
- `StoppedClipKeepsItsNestedClipPlaying` detects a child tied to its frozen parent's index. The parent stops at frame 1, giving Art/Cell 0,1,1,1,1, and the child keeps its own age, giving Art/Cell/Leaf 0,1,0,1,0. Tying the child to the parent index would show 0,1,1,1,1.
- `ASpriteWithOnlyNonControlActionsStillLoops` detects a DoAction whose records are not frame controls being read as frame controls, for example a Pop read as a Stop. It expects 0,1,2,0,1, and the bug would show 0,1,1,1,1.
- `AStopBehindABranchIsNotAppliedToTheClip` detects a flat extraction that applies a Stop behind a Jump. The tag is skipped, giving 0,1,2,0,1. Applying the Stop would show 0,1,1,1,1.
- `GotoChainStopsAtTheHopCapWithinOneTick` (`Radicle/tests/test_swf_frame_control.cpp:SwfFrameControl`) detects a hop cap that is missing or not `min(controls.size() + 1, 64)`, in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:land`. The sprite Art has 100 frames, so `ticks` is 100 and the cap is 64. Frame i (i < 99) is goto i+1 then Play, and frame 99 is goto 0 then Play. Tick 0 starts on 0 and hop 0 does not move. Hops 1 to 63 enter frames 1 to 63, so `frame_at[0]` is 63. Each later tick that starts on `s` enters `(s+1+k) % 100` for k from 0 to 63, so it ends on `(s+64) % 100`. That gives `(63 + 64t) % 100`: 63, 27, 91, 55 for t = 0 to 3. The uncapped `controls.size() + 1 = 101` hops would end tick 0 on frame 0, so row[0] would be 0 instead of 63. The budget for 100 ticks is 1424 and is reached in tick 22, after t = 3, so the asserted rows are unaffected.
- `EntryBudgetFreezesALongChainInsteadOfGrowing` (`Radicle/tests/test_swf_frame_control.cpp:SwfFrameControl`) detects an entry store with no budget in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:simulate_playhead`, which would keep moving and grow. It uses the same 100-frame cycle in a 1200-frame root, so `ticks` is 1200. Each tick enters 64 distinct frames, so it stores 64 entries. Tick 0 stores 64, counting the explicit tick-0 entry, so after tick t the count is 64(t+1). The budget is `4 * 1200 + 1024 = 5824`, which is reached after tick 90 (64 * 91). Tick 91 finds the budget spent, so it does not move, and the loop breaks with `frame_at[91]` equal to the tick-90 frame, `(63 + 64*90) % 100 = 23`. Expected Art/Marker is `(63 + 64t) % 100` for t from 0 to 90, and 23 for t from 91 to 1199. Without the budget the row keeps moving, and t = 91 would be `(63 + 64*91) % 100 = 87`.
- Dedup is not covered by a row test. A chain that revisits a frame inside one tick needs a short cycle, and in a 100-frame timeline such a cycle does not exhaust the budget within a test-sized run, so the dedup rule (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_control.cpp:enter`) is covered only by its code and notes.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_memory.cpp:Interpreter::domain_memory_load

Serves li8, li16, li32, lf32 and lf64 against `runtime_.current_domain()->domain_memory()`. The popped address goes through ToUint32, so a negative address becomes a large index and is refused. Bytes are gathered little-endian into a 64-bit accumulator, byte i at bit 8*i. li8 and li16 zero-extend because the accumulator holds only their width. li32 reads the low 32 bits as int32, so 0xFFFFFFFE reads as -2. lf32 bit-casts the low 32 bits to float and widens to double; lf64 bit-casts all 64 bits. The stack effect (pop 1, push 1) is already declared in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_stack.cpp` for 0x35 to 0x39.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_memory.cpp:Interpreter::domain_memory_store

Serves si8, si16, si32, sf32 and sf64. `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute_frame` pops the address first and the value below it, which matches the AVM2 operand order for si* and sf*. Integer stores take ToInt32 and write only the low width bytes, so si8 never touches the next byte. sf32 narrows to float before its bits are written; sf64 writes the double bits. The stack effect (pop 2, push 0) is declared in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_stack.cpp` for 0x3A to 0x3E.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_memory.cpp:check_domain_memory

Refusal kinds were chosen here, because the brief named no specific kind: no domain memory gives NullReference, since AS3 domainMemory is null; an access outside the byte array gives InvalidArgument. Both messages start with "domain memory". The bounds check is `index + width > length`, so an access ending exactly at the last byte is accepted and one starting at the length is refused. The index is widened to 64 bits before the width is added, so an address near 4294967295 cannot wrap.

## Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/domain.hpp:ApplicationDomainObject::set_domain_memory

domain_memory is a host-set reference, not an AS3 property. No native getter or setter for ApplicationDomain.domainMemory was added: the brief allowed skipping it, and a native pair needs two native ids, a setter trait that `Radicle/src/avm2/builtins.cpp` has no helper for, and a ByteArray cast in `Radicle/src/avm2/native_net.cpp`. Until one is added, AS3 code reading domainMemory gets undefined and cannot set it. The memory is looked up on `Runtime::current_domain`, so every frame uses the single current domain and not the domain of the loader that loaded its ABC. That is a simplification the lead should confirm.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute_frame (domain-memory cases)

The cases live in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_d.inc` and cover li8 through sf64 (0x35 to 0x3E). The opcode constants are in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_internal.hpp:op`. A short stack refuses with StackUnderflow from the same pop helper every other opcode uses, and the memory helper runs only after the operands are popped.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain_memory.cpp:SiThirtyTwoThenLiThirtyTwoRoundTripsANegativeInt

Detects si32 writing its bytes in the wrong order, the address and value being popped swapped, or li32 zero-extending a negative int. Hand-derived: -2 is 0xFFFFFFFE, so bytes 4 to 7 are FE FF FF FF, and li32 at 4 reads -2.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain_memory.cpp:StoresAreLittleEndianSoLiEightReadsTheBytesInOrder

Detects big-endian storage or a li8 or li16 reading the wrong offset. Hand-derived: 0x01020304 stores bytes 04 03 02 01 at offsets 0 to 3, so li8 at 0, 1, 2, 3 gives 4, 3, 2, 1; li16 at 0 gives 0x0304 (772) and at 2 gives 0x0102 (258).

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain_memory.cpp:SiEightAndSiSixteenStoreOnlyTheLowBytesAndLiZeroExtends

Detects si8 writing a second byte, si8 or si16 not masking to the low bits, and li8 or li16 sign-extending. Hand-derived: 0x1FF has low byte 0xFF, so byte 3 stays 0 and li8 at 2 gives 255, not -1. 0x12345 has low half 0x2345, stored as 45 23, so li16 at 0 gives 9029. si16 of -1 stores FF FF, so li16 at 4 gives 65535, not -1.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain_memory.cpp:SfThirtyTwoNarrowsToFloatAndLfThirtyTwoWidensItBack

Detects sf32 storing double bits, or lf32 reading eight bytes. Hand-derived: 0.1 as float is 13421773 times 2^-27, bits 0x3DCCCCCD, stored as CD CC CC 3D; lf32 reads back 0.100000001490116119384765625 exactly, and the test also asserts that this is not 0.1.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain_memory.cpp:SfSixtyFourThenLfSixtyFourRoundTripsADouble

Detects sf64 narrowing to float, or lf64 reading four bytes. Hand-derived: 0.1 as double has bits 0x3FB999999999999A, stored as 9A 99 99 99 99 99 B9 3F; lf64 gives 0.1.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain_memory.cpp:AccessOutsideTheDomainMemoryIsRefused

Detects an off-by-one bounds check (an access starting at the length accepted), a check on the first byte only, and a negative address that wraps. Hand-derived in a 4-byte memory: li8 at 4 is refused; li32 at 1 is refused because 1 + 4 > 4; li32 at 0 is accepted; li8 at -1 is refused because ToUint32(-1) is 4294967295; si32 at 1 is refused.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain_memory.cpp:AccessWithoutDomainMemoryIsRefused

Detects a null memory pointer being dereferenced, or a refusal with the wrong kind or a message not starting with "domain memory". With no memory set, li8 and si8 both refuse with NullReference.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_domain_memory.cpp:MemoryOpcodesRefuseAnEmptyStackWithStackUnderflow

Detects a memory opcode that continues with an undefined operand instead of refusing with StackUnderflow. All ten opcodes run on an empty stack with memory set, so the refusal can only come from the pop.

Nothing was compiled or run on the development machine for these tests, so CI must confirm them.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm1_objects.cpp:DiamondSharedChildTearsDownAfterItsLastParent

- `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_objects.cpp:DiamondSharedChildTearsDownAfterItsLastParent` builds a diamond: root A holds B and C, and both hold the shared child D, which holds a 2000-object chain. It detects a teardown that never takes a child, which leaks the chain, and a refcount error that keeps D alive after its last parent; it cannot observe a teardown that descends into D early, since D expires either way. Before the roots drop, D has two owners and the chain's top and bottom have one each. After A is released, D, the top and the bottom must all have expired. The guard that keeps this right is the `use_count() == 1` check in `Radicle/src/avm1/object_ops.cpp:Avm1Object::~Avm1Object`. `Avm1Object` is internal, so the test drives the graph through bytecode and reads only `Avm1Result::variables` through weak pointers. It therefore shows that the shared child is released, not a destructor count of exactly one.

## Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_text_matrix.cpp:TextRecordOffsetIsScaledByTheTextMatrix

- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_text_matrix.cpp:TextRecordOffsetIsScaledByTheTextMatrix` detects a TEXTRECORD x_offset that is placed without the DefineText MATRIX scale, which would emit `matrix(2 0 0 2 10 0)`, and an offset that is dropped, which would emit `matrix(2 0 0 2 0 0)`. Derivation: `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:text_paths` places the record at 200 twips / 20 = 10 px, then `compose_transform(text_transform, placed)` gives translate_x = 2 * 10 + 0 = 20 with scale 2, so the emitted transform is `matrix(2 0 0 2 20 0)`. The brief's expected `matrix(2 0 0 2 40 0)` needs a MATRIX translate of 400 twips or an x_offset of 400. Neither is in the brief's inputs, so the test uses the derived 20.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm2_call_indexed.cpp:callstatic argument order and primitive receiver

- `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_call_indexed.cpp:CallstaticConsumesItsArgumentsInPushOrder` detects an argument pop that reverses the order or drops one argument. `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::pop_arguments` fills the vector from the top of the stack, so the first pushed value is local 1. Pushing 10 then 3 and subtracting gives 7 through `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_ops.cpp:subtract_values`; reversed arguments would give -7.
- `Radicle/tests/test_avm2_call_indexed.cpp:CallstaticBoxesAnIntReceiverAsThis` detects a callstatic that refuses or unboxes a primitive receiver. `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::call_indexed` boxes an Int32 receiver with `Interpreter::box` into the builtin `int` class, which `Runtime::link` installs, so the method sees a boxed object holding 5 as `this`. A refusal would end in NullReference.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp:decode_button_tag (button decode)

`decode_button_tag` fills `SwfTag::button` for DefineButton (tag 7) and DefineButton2 (tag 34). Both start with the button's UI16 character id. Tag 34 then has a reserved byte and a UI16 action offset, which the decoder skips. Both tags then carry BUTTONRECORDs ended by a zero flags byte. Any bytes after that terminator are button actions and are not decoded.

A button whose records do not decode is left undecoded, and the file still loads. This is deliberate: `decode_tag_stream` refuses a whole file on any malformed payload, and `Radicle/tests/swf_character_fixtures.hpp:button_payload` is a 5-byte DefineButton2 with no record terminator that other tests load. Before this decoder existed a button only contributed its leading id, so refusing would have been a regression.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_placement.cpp:decode_button_records (record layout)

The record state byte holds 0x01 up, 0x02 over, 0x04 down and 0x08 hit test. For tag 34 only, 0x10 means a filter list follows and 0x20 means a blend-mode byte follows. These bit positions come from the SWF file format specification as recalled, not from a file in this environment. The Fallout 4 Interface archive holds 311 SWFs but no DefineButton or DefineButton2 tag in any of them, so no real record was available to check the layout against. CI with a real button is the first real check.

Each tag 34 record carries a CXFORMWITHALPHA. It is read with `read_color_transform` and kept as `SwfButtonRecord::color_transform`. The filter list is read with `decode_filter_list` and discarded, and the blend byte is skipped. The record therefore does not keep filters or blend mode, so a filtered or blended button draws without them. Tag 7 records have no colour transform, and their 0x10 and 0x20 bits are not parsed.

## Radicle/include/fo4/swf/swf.hpp:SwfButton

`SwfButton` and `SwfButtonRecord` are new, and `SwfTag::button` holds the decoded button. `SwfButton::character_id` is the button's own id, the key `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_to_svg` indexes it by. `Radicle/src/swf/swf.cpp:SwfTag::clear_decoded` resets the field along with the other decoded fields.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:button_group

A button row draws every record with the UP flag, sorted by PlaceDepth with `std::stable_sort`, so records at equal depth keep tag order. Each record's transform is `compose_transform(row.world_transform, transform_from_matrix(record.matrix))`. The record's character then goes through `character_group`, the same shape, morph and text path that a plain row uses. Each record gets the id prefix `r<row>u<k>`, which cannot collide with a row id `r<row>`. The record colour transform is ignored. The row's own colour filter still wraps the whole button, as it does for any row. Hit-only and over-only records draw nothing.

Out of scope: a record whose character is a sprite, a button or an edit-text draws nothing, and a button inside a clip sprite is not drawn, because `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:sprite_clip_to_svg` only collects shapes, morphs and static text (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:sprite_clip_to_svg`). A button row that carries a clip depth is also not drawn, which matches the text-row rule. This supersedes the "DefineButton rows" item in the static text note above.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body (button branch)

A non-mask button row takes the `button_group` branch. Otherwise content comes from `shape_group`, `button_group` or `text_group`, and empty content skips the row. The old per-branch text-empty check became that single check. `character_shape` replaces `row_shape`, and takes the character id and ratio, so a record can reuse it with no ratio.

## Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_buttons.cpp:SwfFrameSvgButtons tests

- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_buttons.cpp:SwfFrameSvgButtons.DefineButton2UpRecordDrawsItsShapeAtItsMatrix` detects a button row dropped from the frame, an UP record matrix that is ignored or not composed with the row, and a DefineButton2 record read from the wrong offset because the reserved or action bytes were not skipped.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_buttons.cpp:SwfFrameSvgButtons.HitOnlyRecordDrawsNothing` detects a hit-only record drawn as visible art, which would paint the hit area onto the stage.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_buttons.cpp:SwfFrameSvgButtons.UpRecordsDrawInDepthOrderAndIgnoreTheirColourTransforms` detects records drawn in tag order rather than depth, a record colour transform misread so the second record is lost, and a colour transform applied as a filter.
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_buttons.cpp:SwfFrameSvgButtons.DefineButtonRecordHasNoColourTransformBytes` detects a DefineButton (tag 7) decoder that reads the tag 34 colour transform, which would misplace the record.

Expected strings were derived by hand. The square path is the 1000-twip and 600-twip squares used by `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:kRedSquare` and `kBlueSquare`. Translations are twips divided by 20, as in `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:transform_from_matrix`. Nothing was compiled or run on the development machine for this change, so CI must confirm them.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body (static text clips)

A row whose character is a DefineText or DefineText2 with a clip depth opens a mask, the same way a shape row does. `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:frame_body` pushes the same `Mask` record and writes `<clipPath id="r<index>clip" transform="matrix(...)">` with the row's world transform as the attribute, and the glyph paths from `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:text_paths` with no outer transform as its content. The glyph paths carry their own text matrix and placement, so the clipPath content matches what the same text would draw. The index is the row's position in the flat frame row list, as for shape masks. A text row with a clip depth paints nothing for itself, and a hidden text row still opens its mask, the same as a hidden shape row. A text mask with no glyph paths gives an empty clipPath, which clips everything out, the same as a stroke-only shape mask. Unverified against Flash for the same reasons as the shape mask.

## Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:sprite_clip_to_svg (static text children)

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:sprite_clip_to_svg` adds a descendant text row's glyph paths to the sprite clipPath, after the same visibility check a shape child gets. The text row's world transform is passed to `Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:text_paths` as its outer transform, so each glyph path carries the composition of that transform, the text matrix and the glyph placement. A button child is still left out.

`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:text_paths` takes that outer transform as a third argument, defaulting to the identity, and composes it in front of the text matrix. Callers that pass nothing (`Radicle/src/swf/swf_frame_svg.cpp:text_group` and the text mask branch) get the composition `compose_transform(identity, matrix)`, which equals the matrix bit for bit for every matrix the decoder produces, because `Radicle/src/swf/swf_timeline.cpp:transform_from_matrix` never yields a negative zero. Their output is therefore unchanged.

## Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_text_clip.cpp:SwfFrameSvgTextClip tests

- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_text_clip.cpp:SwfFrameSvgTextClip.StaticTextMaskClipsTheRowsBelowItAtItsWorldTransform` detects a text row with a clip depth that opens no mask (the blue square would paint unclipped), a clipPath with no glyph paths, and a clipPath that drops the text row's world transform (the glyph at 20 px would print at the origin).
- `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg_text_clip.cpp:SwfFrameSvgTextClip.StaticTextInsideAClipSpriteJoinsTheSpriteMask` detects a text child left out of the sprite clipPath (the blue square would paint unclipped), and a glyph that ignores its child's world transform (it would print at the origin, not at 20 px).

Expected strings were derived by hand. The glyph is a 1000-twip square (50 px, the path of `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:kRedSquare` at its size), at a DefineText height of 1024, so the font scale is 1 and the text matrix is the identity. The blue square is the 600-twip one, `Radicle/tests/test_swf_svg.cpp:kBlueSquare`. The clipPath ids follow the shape-mask convention `r<index>clip`. Nothing was compiled or run on the development machine for this change, so CI must confirm them.

## Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:execute

Adds the AVM1 control and object opcodes 0x2A Throw, 0x2B CastOp, 0x46 Enumerate, 0x54 InstanceOf, 0x55 Enumerate2, 0x69 Extends, 0x8F Try and 0x94 With. This supersedes the older refusal notes for these opcodes; ImplementsOp 0x2C is implemented later by `Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:implements_op`. GetMember and SetMember on function prototypes stay deferred because there is no prototype model. Any other opcode still returns Unsupported.

## Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:try_regions

A Try record (0x8F) carries flags (bit0 catch, bit1 finally, bit2 catch-in-register), try_size, catch_size and finally_size, then a catch name string or a register byte. The record offsets body, catch_at, finally_at and after_at are resolved through jump_index. On Thrown the operand stack is cut back to its depth at the Try. A caught value binds to the catch name in block.call->locals or in the globals, or to a register through function_ops::store_register. A finally runs with the pending throw saved aside. If the finally jumps or returns, that overrides the pending throw. If it does not, the throw is restored and returns Thrown. Known limit: a Return inside a finally with a pending exception can still rethrow when the Try ends the body.

## Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:run_with

The With record (0x94) pops its object. A value that is not an object skips the body; this choice was made without a reference trace. An object is pushed onto block.scopes for the body, and scope_slot in function_ops.cpp consults it first for reads and writes. Try and With share one run-wide counter, run.regions, capped at kMaxNesting = 64 in control_ops.cpp. The 65th level returns ResourceLimit with "Try and With nesting reached the limit of 64 levels".

## Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:extends

Superclass links live in Avm1Run::superclasses, keyed by the subclass body pointer. InstanceOf and CastOp use the constructed_by body recorded by invoke_method in function_ops.cpp. This is a constructor-body class model, not prototype objects. A link that would create a cycle returns InvalidStream. A non-function operand returns Unsupported.

## Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:push_names

Enumerate and Enumerate2 push a null first, then the keys in insertion order, so the most recently added key is on top. Popping yields the keys most recently added first and ends on null. A non-object operand yields only null. Order is verified against Ruffle 0.6.0, not Flash: `E:\GardenEngine\GardenEngine-RE-Work\menu-reference\swf-runtime-01a0efb6\native-experiment\ruffle-0.6.0\core\src\avm1\activation.rs:action_enumerate` (line 1094) and `action_enumerate_2` (line 1111) push `get_keys` in reverse, and `core\src\avm1\object\script_object.rs:get_keys` lists own keys from `core\src\avm1\property_map.rs:PropertyMap::iter`, which yields the most recently added key first. Unverified: Ruffle's end sentinel is `Value::Undefined` (`activation.rs` line 1098), while this slice pushes null, and the Flash sentinel was not checked.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:run_range

Each record counts once against max_steps before it runs. Thrown overwrites result.opcode and result.offset but not result.status. The outer execute_actions turns an uncaught Thrown into the status Thrown with the message "the thrown value was not caught". On Ok the index is returned as resume so the enclosing Try or With can continue after its sub-range.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:jump_index

Known hole, not fixed: jump_index maps a target offset to an index in the flattened action vector and checks only that the target is a record start. A branch from top-level code into a DefineFunction or DefineFunction2 body is therefore accepted, and those records would run with block.call == nullptr. No test covers this path yet.

## Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:invoke

Ceilings: kMaxCallDepth = 64 functions, and the step limit is counted per record in run_range. Each call builds its own scopes vector for With bodies. The construct path in invoke_method sets instance.object->constructed_by before the constructor runs.

## Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:cast_op

The operand order is verified against Ruffle 0.6.0, the only oracle on disk: `E:\GardenEngine\GardenEngine-RE-Work\menu-reference\swf-runtime-01a0efb6\native-experiment\ruffle-0.6.0\core\src\avm1\activation.rs:action_cast_op` (line 905) pops the object first (line 906) and the constructor second (line 907), so the object is on top and the constructor is below. `activation.rs:action_instance_of` (line 1610) pops the constructor first, so CastOp and InstanceOf take their operands in opposite order. An earlier version of cast_op took the constructor from the top, the opposite of this oracle. Verified against Ruffle, not against Flash. No C# AVM1 interpreter was found under E:\GardenEngine: the .cs trees searched contain no CastOp or Enumerate2 implementation.

## Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:try_regions (Return inside a finally)

Test `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_control.cpp:ReturnInsideAFinallyDropsAPendingThrow` pins that a Return in a finally, after a pending Throw, ends the call with the returned value and drops the throw. The finally run leaves resume at the block end, which is not at[3], so try_regions returns Ok and the pending throw is dropped. The test body keeps a record after the Try. When the Try is the last record of the block, resume equals at[3] and the pending throw is restored, which is the known limit above and is not pinned. Regression detected: a finally that resumed the pending throw would return Thrown and trace nothing from the call.

## Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:run_with

Test `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_control.cpp:ThrowThatLeavesAWithPopsItsScope` detects a With whose scope stays on block.scopes when a Throw leaves the With. run_with pops the scope after run_range returns on every status, so a later read of x resolves to the global 10. A leaked scope would read the object's x, which is 1.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm1_control.cpp:NestedTryAndWithStopAtSixtyFourLevels

Decoder::body in `Radicle/src/avm1/decode.cpp` refuses a 65th nested body with TooDeep (kMaxBodyDepth = 64), so 65 static levels never reach the runtime guard in `Radicle/src/avm1/control_ops.cpp:run_try`. The test reaches the guard through recursion instead. Forty static Try levels, each with its body in the finally region, leave run.regions at 40. A function f whose body is a catch Try around a call to f adds one region per call. Call k runs its Try with regions at 40 + (k - 1), so call 25 is refused with "Try and With nesting reached the limit of 64 levels". Only 25 calls are live then, so run.depth stays below kMaxCallDepth = 64 in `Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:invoke` and the region budget is the cap that fires. The 64 static levels still run for both Try and With. Regression detected: a Try or With that did not count against the shared run.regions would recurse until the native stack overflows, and the test would see no ResourceLimit.

## Radicle/src/avm1/function_ops.cpp:invoke (Low: scope chain at definition)

A function defined inside a With body gets empty scopes when it is called, because DefineFunction does not capture the scope chain. invoke starts each call from a fresh `std::vector<Avm1Data> scopes`, and a call made inside a With does not pass the caller's scopes either. Flash keeps the definition-time chain, so names that the With object would supply resolve wrongly here. Not fixed in this slice.

## Radicle/src/avm1/interpreter.cpp:run_range (Low: opcode of an uncaught callee throw)

When a Throw in a callee is not caught, run_range overwrites result.opcode and result.offset at each enclosing frame, so the report names the outermost CallFunction or Try rather than the Throw. `Radicle/tests/test_avm1_control.cpp:FinallyRunsBeforeAnUncaughtThrowKeepsGoing` asserts opcode 0x8F, the outer Try, so it pins this Low; a fix must change that assertion. Not fixed in this slice.

## Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp (Low: stale test name in notes)

Radicle.md still cites `Radicle/tests/test_avm1.cpp:ObjectAndFunctionOpcodesStayRefusedByName` at lines 7693, 7937 and 8059. No file under Radicle/tests defines that name now, so those citations point at nothing. Not fixed in this slice.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute_frame (AVM2 late ops census)

Census from a source scan (not compiled or run): 169 named opcodes, 168 with a case in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_a.inc` through `interpreter_dispatch_e.inc`, and 1 without, `getdescendants` 0x59. This replaces the 12-opcode census above. The 11 added here are dxns 0x06, dxnslate 0x07, pushnamespace 0x31, finddef 0x5F, setpropertylate 0x69, deletepropertylate 0x6B, getglobalslot 0x6E, setglobalslot 0x6F, esc_xelem 0x71, esc_xattr 0x72 and checkfilter 0x78. All 11 new cases are in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_e.inc`, which `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter.cpp:Interpreter::execute_frame` includes.

getdescendants stays undispatched because this runtime has no XML or XMLList object model (see the R3 status note above), so there is no descendant set to return. It needs that model before a case can be added.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_e.inc:pushnamespace

pushnamespace pushes the namespace URI as a string Value, not a namespace Value kind. The Value variant has no namespace kind and no Namespace builtin exists. The only consumer of a namespace operand, `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::pop_runtime_operands`, reads it with to_string and builds a Package namespace, so a string gives the same result there. The cost is that `typeof` and `is Namespace` see a string. Add a namespace kind when a Namespace class is modelled. The public namespace has the empty URI, so it pushes "".

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_e.inc:setpropertylate

The late opcodes 0x69 and 0x6B have no constant pool operand, so the name is on the operand stack. The case builds a RuntimeName multiname in the public namespace and resolves the name with `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::pop_runtime_operands`. setpropertylate passes above=1 because the value is on top, and deletepropertylate passes above=0. The stack order is object, name, value for set and object, name for delete. There is no getpropertylate opcode: getproperty (0x66) already handles a runtime name through `resolve_runtime_multiname` in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_b.inc`.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_e.inc:getglobalslot

getglobalslot and setglobalslot address `frame.scopes.front()`, the object getglobalscope pushes. A read past the end of the slots is undefined, as getslot does. A write grows the slot vector, as setslot does. An empty scope list raises ScopeUnderflow.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_e.inc:dxns

dxns and dxnslate store the URI in `Radicle/include/fo4/avm2/interpreter.hpp:Interpreter` (the Frame field `default_xml_namespace`). Nothing reads it yet, because the default XML namespace only affects E4X, which is not modelled. The effect is storage only. The value is per frame and is not inherited by callees.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_xml_text.cpp:escape_xml_markup

PROVISIONAL: the escape sets in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_xml_text.cpp:escape_xml_markup` are unverified against ECMA-357, because no reference is available on this machine. The sets are the ones the change brief named: element content escapes `&`, `<` and `>`, and attribute values also escape `"` to `&quot;`. Open questions: whether `>` must also be escaped in attributes (this code escapes it in attributes, as it does in element content), and whether LF, CR and TAB become character references in attributes and CR in element content (this code escapes none of them). Behaviour is not changed by this note. The input is UTF-8 bytes; the escaped characters are ASCII, so multibyte sequences are never altered.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_e.inc:checkfilter

checkfilter refuses only null and undefined, with a TypeError status. Other values pass and stay on the stack. Because XML is not modelled, a non-XML value that the real opcode refuses passes here.

## Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_e.inc:finddef

finddef resolves its operand as a static multiname and calls `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_property.cpp:Interpreter::find_scope_binding` with create_on_global false, the same way the getlex case in `Radicle/src/avm2/interpreter_dispatch_b.inc` does. The verifier groups 0x5F with getlex and it has no runtime-multiname operands, so no runtime name is popped. It searches the scope chain and pushes the owning scope, or null when no scope holds the name. PROVISIONAL against avmplus: the scope-chain search and the null on a miss are not verified. The real finddef may search only the domain definitions, and may refuse a missing definition. The avmplus reference was not available here.

## Radicle/src/graph/graph_lifter.cpp:GraphLifter::liftAssign

- A compound assignment to a struct member (`s.X += v`) expands to `s.X = s.X + v`. The read is lifted through `liftExpression(*assign.target)`, which gives a `StructGet` for a struct member and the same `VariableGet` as before for an identifier. The target is lifted twice, so its receiver must be call-free; otherwise the lift is refused.
- A struct member compound whose value calls a function is refused. The Papyrus emitter reads the member before it evaluates the value (`Radicle/src/papyrus/body_statement.cpp:BodyEmitter::emitAssign`), but a lifted `Call` node runs earlier in the exec chain than a pure `StructGet`, so the read would move after the call.
- A plain struct member assignment lowers to a `StructSet` statement: config `member` holds the name, `target` holds the receiver and `value` holds the value. The value is lifted before the receiver, as the property and index paths already do.
- A non-compound `p.Y = p.X + Next()` has the same reordering as properties and variables, which is the existing model and is not covered by the refusal. The Papyrus emitter reads `p.X` before the call (`Radicle/src/papyrus/body_expression.cpp:BodyEmitter::emitBinary`), but the lifted `Call` node runs earlier in the exec chain, so the read moves after the call.

## Radicle/src/graph/graph_lifter_expr.cpp:GraphLifter::liftMember

- A struct member read lowers to a `StructGet` with config `member`, input `target` and output `value`, mirroring `PropertyGet`. It also carries config `type` set from the resolver type of the member, so `NodeDefinition::pinsFor` can make the output pin concrete. Without that, a binary over the read cannot bind its generic type.

## Radicle/src/graph/graph_lifter_expr.cpp:GraphLifter::liftExpression

- `new T` lowers to a `StructNew` with config `type` and output `ret`, mirroring `NewArray`. `GraphLinearizer::buildPure` reads config `type` to emit `new T`.

## Radicle/include/fo4/graph/node_definition.hpp:NodeDefinition::pinsFor

- `StructGet` shares the `StructNew` case, so its output data pin takes the concrete type from config `type`. Its `target` input stays `any`.

## Radicle/src/graph/graph_lifter.cpp:GraphLifter::liftStatement

- `Point p = new Point` is a known ceiling. The lifter declares `Point p` at the top of the function and emits `p = new Point`. The Papyrus emitter gives a declaration with no initializer an `assign p None` first (`Radicle/src/papyrus/body_statement.cpp:BodyEmitter`, DefineStatement case), while an initialised declaration emits only `struct_create`. So the lifted pex has one extra instruction. The tests therefore write `Point p` and `p = new Point` on separate lines. Locals with an initializer have the same ceiling.

## Radicle/src/graph/builtin_node_definitions.cpp:builtinDefinitions::all

- The struct nodes are palette entries because `GraphValidator::resolveDefinitions` refuses any node whose definition is not on the palette.
- `StructNew` and `StructGet` are pure. `GraphLinearizer::pull` refuses a value from a non-pure node (`kUseBeforeAssignment`), and a struct read has no exec pin to order it.

## Radicle/src/graph/graph_linearizer.cpp:GraphLinearizer::lowerSimple

- `StructSet` lowers to `member(target, config member) = value`, the same shape as `IndexSet`. Before this change `buildPure` had `StructNew` and `StructGet`, and nothing lowered `StructSet`.

## Radicle/tests/test_graph_lift.cpp:GraphLift.StructNewGetAndSetSurviveATripThroughTheGraph

- Detects a lifter that refuses `new T` or a struct member read, and a linearizer that drops `StructSet`. Each would leave the regenerated pex without its `struct_create`, `struct_get` or `struct_set`, and the pex comparer reports the first difference.
- Hand-derived original sequence: `assign p None`, `struct_create p`, `assign $a 3`, `struct_set p X $a`, `struct_get $c p X`, `iadd $b $c 4`, `struct_set p Y $b`. The regenerated source is the same text, so its sequence is the same.

## Radicle/tests/test_graph_lift.cpp:GraphLift.StructMemberCompoundAssignmentSurvivesATripThroughTheGraph

- Detects a struct member compound that is refused again, or expanded to read or write the wrong member. `p.Y -= p.X` uses both members, so a swapped read or write shows as a difference.
- Hand-derived original sequence: `assign p None`, `struct_create p`, `assign $a 1`, `struct_set p X $a`, `struct_get $d p X`, `iadd $e $d 2`, `struct_set p X $e`, `struct_get $f p Y`, `struct_get $g p X`, `isub $h $f $g`, `struct_set p Y $h`.
- The regenerated source is `p.X = p.X + 2` and `p.Y = p.Y - p.X`. Its sequence is `struct_get, iadd, struct_set` and `struct_get, struct_get, isub, struct_set`, which matches.

## Radicle/tests/test_graph_lift.cpp:GraphLift.StructMemberCompoundWithACallIsRefusedRatherThanReordered

- Detects a lifter that accepts a call in the value of a struct member compound. That would move the member read after the call and change behaviour with no diagnostic.
## Radicle/src/papyrus/quest_rules.cpp:bindVmadValues

- `Radicle/src/papyrus/quest_rules.cpp:bindShape` binds one shape from its declared type. Scalars keep their old rules. `array` goes to `bindArray` and `struct` goes to `bindStruct`. `variable` and unknown kinds stay unsupported with a reason.
- `Radicle/src/papyrus/quest_rules.cpp:bindArray` accepts only int, float, bool, string and object elements, and only when `elementCount` equals `elements.size()`. Otherwise the array is refused as not decoded yet. One element that fails to bind refuses the whole array, so no partial array is ever bound. A `Variable[]` shape carries elementType `Variable`, so it is refused as not a bindable scalar type.
- `Radicle/src/papyrus/quest_rules.cpp:bindStruct` keys members by the folded name, as `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/value.hpp:Struct` requires. A repeated member name refuses the struct instead of letting the map drop one. VMAD stores no struct type name, so `Struct::typeName` stays empty.
- `Radicle/include/fo4/papyrus/quest_rules.hpp:BoundProperty::isBound` now counts `Array` and `Struct`, so `Radicle/src/c_api_papyrus_quest.cpp:radicle_papyrus_bind_vmad_values` hands those values out. The C shape has no element or member fields, so C callers still get array and struct shapes refused. No ABI bump.
- Regression detected by `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_quest_rules.cpp:BindsIntAndObjectArraysAndAStructAndRefusesVariables`: a decoded array or struct reported as not decoded yet, a Variable or Variable[] property bound as a default, and a struct member lost to a duplicate name.

Expected values were derived by hand from `Radicle/src/papyrus/quest_rules.cpp:bindShape`.

## Radicle/src/papyrus/type_checker.cpp:TypeChecker::checkOverride

- The override check now compares parameter types and the return type with the nearest parent function of the same name (`index_.baseChain`, `ScriptIndex::findMemberOn`), after the existing parameter-count check, which still returns early. Each side resolves with `Resolver::resolveTypeName` relative to its own script, so the parent's types are read in the parent's scope. A pair is reported only when both sides resolve and differ; an unknown type name never yields this diagnostic. Void is a known type: a void override of a typed parent is a mismatch, and two void functions match. Only the first mismatch per override is reported (parameter count, then parameters in order, then return type). The code stays `OverrideMismatch` (PAP0044), the existing override code.
- Papyrus has no covariance, so an `Actor` parameter overriding a `Form` parameter is refused. The comparison is `Type::operator==`, which is case-insensitive on names, so `form` and `Form` match.
- False-positive risk: a parent that resolves to a different script than the engine would pick (for example a same-named type in another folder) would now be refused. The real-corpus gate `PapyrusSemanticReal.ResolvesAndTypeChecksEveryCompleteCorpusScriptClean` (`Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_semantic_real.cpp`) has to run on the Fallout 4 data runner before this is trusted; it was not run here.
- `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_type_checker.cpp:AnOverrideWithADifferentParameterTypeIsRejected` detects an override that keeps the parameter count but changes `int` to `float`, which the count-only check accepted. Expected: one `OverrideMismatch` whose message contains `whose parameter 1 is 'int', not 'float'`.
- `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_type_checker.cpp:AnOverrideWithADifferentReturnTypeIsRejected` detects an override that changes the return type from `int` to `string` with the same parameters. Expected: one `OverrideMismatch` whose message contains `which returns int, not string`. The body returns a string, so no other diagnostic appears. This is a fourth refusing case beyond the one the brief asked for, because return type is a named gap.
- `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_type_checker.cpp:AnOverrideWithTheSameParameterAndReturnTypesIsFine` is the accepting shape: `int Function Go(int a)` returning `a` in both scripts. It detects the new comparison refusing a correct override. Expected: no diagnostics.
- `Radicle/tests/test_papyrus_type_checker.cpp:AnOverrideMayNotNarrowAParameterToAChildObject` is the boundary: `Function Take(Actor)` overriding `Function Take(Form)`. It detects a covariant parameter accepted as an override. Expected: one `OverrideMismatch` with `whose parameter 1 is 'Form', not 'Actor'`.

- A missing `Return` is accepted, so `TypeChecker::checkCallable` reports nothing for a typed function that can reach its end. The Creation Kit compiles such functions: 36 shipped vanilla functions fall off the end, for example `DN151_MovableWater.psc` `ClearName` and `VitaleCodeMaster.psc` `checkForSolution`. A rule that refused them was removed, because the real-data gate `PapyrusSemanticReal` has zero tolerance for a refused vanilla script.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:type_name_expansion_too_large (ABC writer TypeName cap)

- Mirror: `Radicle/src/abc/constant_pool.cpp:parse_multiname_pool` refuses a TypeName (kind 0x1D) whose expansion passes `detail::kMaxTypeNameExpansion` (64, now declared in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_internal.hpp`, so the parser and the writer read one constant). The expansion of a TypeName is 1 + expansion(name) + the sum of expansion(param) over its params; every other multiname expands to 1. The parser checks the running total after each addend, which is the same as checking the final total because every addend is at least 1 and the total never falls.
- `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:pool_encodable` calls `type_name_expansion_too_large` after its reference loop, so every name and param index is already known to be below its TypeName. A model over the cap returns `AbcStatus::TypeNameTooLarge` and `AbcFile::serialize` leaves `out` empty, instead of writing bytes that `AbcFile::parse` rejects.
- Hand-derived boundary: a flat TypeName over QName 1 with 62 params expands to 64 and is accepted; with 63 params it expands to 65 and is refused. A chain of nested TypeNames, each with one param, expands to 2k + 1 at depth k: 31 levels give 63 (accepted), 32 levels give 65 (refused).
- Regressions: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_write.cpp:TypeNameExpansionCapIsInclusiveAtSixtyFourNodes` detects a writer with no cap at all, or an off-by-one `>=` that refuses 64. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_write.cpp:TypeNameExpansionCountsNestedParametersAcrossLevels` detects a writer that counts only direct params: each nested level has one param, so only the summed expansion refuses at 32 levels.
- This closes the "Known gap" bullet in the `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:AbcFile::serialize (#806 phase 1)` section above.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:put_trait (checked, no change)

- Correction to the "Remaining gap" bullet in the `Radicle/src/abc/abc_write.cpp:AbcFile::serialize (#806 phase 1)` section: `put_trait` does not write fields a kind does not use. Each kind writes only its own fields (Slot and Const: slot_id, type_name, value_index, and value_kind when value_index is non-zero; Class and Function: slot_id and class_index; Method, Getter and Setter: disp_id and method_index), plus metadata only when `has_metadata()`. The unused fields are never emitted, so there is no stray field to normalise.
- The one in-memory value that does not reach the file is `value_kind` on a Slot or Const whose `value_index` is 0. The format has no byte for it, `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp:parse_traits` leaves it at Undefined, and the bytes are canonical. It is not normalised, because a refusal would reject models that carry a default kind.
- The validity checks match the parser. `traits_values_known` tests `value_kind` only when `value_index` is non-zero, as `parse_traits` does, and `value_kind_known` lists the same kinds as `is_value_kind` in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_file.cpp`. A `has_metadata()` flag with an empty list writes a zero count, which the parser reads back.
- Checked by reading `put_trait` and `parse_traits` side by side. Nothing was compiled or run.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:BodyParser::parse_header (optional maxstack and local_count)

- `maxstack` and `local_count` are optional keywords in the body header. `Radicle/src/abc/abc_text_body.cpp:render_body` still always writes them, so the dump form is unchanged. `max_stack_given` and `local_count_given` record which keywords the text carried. The other header keywords (`method`, `init_scope`, `max_scope`, `code_bytes`) stay required and in order.
- A header that omits a keyword leaves that field at its default until `BodyParser::measure_omitted_limits` runs.
- Regressions: the optional-keyword path is exercised by the three `AbcAsm` cases listed under `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm.cpp:AbcAsm (omitted-limit cases)` below. A parser that still requires the keyword refuses every header from a stripped dump.

## Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:BodyParser::measure_omitted_limits (assembler limits)

- The body is pushed to `file.bodies` first, because `Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_method_flow` reads the body by index. It is popped again on refusal. The verifier is the only check on this path, so a body with an omitted limit is held to the same rules a body edit is.
- Omitted `local_count` is `1 + param_count + (1 if NEED_ARGUMENTS or NEED_REST)`, raised to `Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:required_local_count` of the decoded code. The parameter floor repeats the rule in `Radicle/src/abc/abc_verify.cpp:verify_method_context`, because `refresh_body_limits` only raises a count and would leave a method with parameters at 0. The verifier still checks the value, so a drift between the two shows up as a refusal.
- Omitted `max_stack` is measured by running `verify_method_flow` with `detail::kVerifierStackCeiling` (4096, shared with `Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:verify_and_commit`) and then set to `flow.observed_max_stack`, the deepest stack the walk reaches.
- Explicit values are never overwritten, even when the verifier would want a larger one. If any value is explicit the verifier runs with the explicit value in place, so an explicit `maxstack` below the observed depth makes assembly fail with `InconsistentModel` and the verifier's message. When both are explicit no verifier run happens, as before.
- Hand-derived values for the synthetic fixture (`Radicle/tests/abc_test_support.hpp:build_abc`): body 0 is the constructor, method 0 with no params, so local_count is 1. getlex (depth 1), pushstring (2), callpropvoid with argc 1 (pops 2) and returnvoid give observed depth 2. Body 1 is the listener, method 1 with one param, so local_count is 2. getlex (1), pushstring (2), getlex (3), callpropvoid with argc 2 (pops 3) give observed depth 3.
- Regressions: `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm.cpp:AbcAsm.ComputesAnOmittedMaxStackFromTheVerifierAndKeepsTheExplicitLocalCount` detects max_stack left at 0 (the verifier refuses depth 1 against 0) or a measured value that is not the observed depth. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm.cpp:AbcAsm.ComputesAnOmittedLocalCountFromTheParameterCountAndMaxStackFromTheCode` detects a local_count taken from the code alone (0 instead of 2), which the verifier refuses as too small for the parameter, and a max_stack that is not measured. `Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm.cpp:AbcAsm.KeepsAnExplicitMaxStackWhenOnlyLocalCountIsOmitted` detects an assembler that overwrites an explicit max_stack with the measured 3.
- For omitted values only, this supersedes the "Still open in phase 5/6" bullet of the `## ABC assembler: text back to a model (phase 5)` section above.

## Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:required_local_count (shared, moved)

- `required_local_count` moved out of the anonymous namespace in `Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp` into `detail`, and `Radicle/src/abc/abc_internal.hpp` declares it, so `Radicle/src/abc/abc_asm_code.cpp:BodyParser::measure_omitted_limits` uses the same rule as `Radicle/src/abc/edit.cpp:verify_and_commit`. The verifier ceiling `kVerifierStackCeiling` moved to the same header. No behaviour changed for edits.

## Radicle/tests/test_abc_asm.cpp:AbcAsm (omitted-limit cases)
